Source: https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/. JSON Schemas: https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/schema/index.json

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/getting-started/ai-assistance.html -->

# Getting AI Help

**An AI assistant can write LCARdS cards and whole dashboards for you; it just needs to know LCARdS first.**

- Out of the box, a chatbot has never seen LCARdS. It guesses, and guessed options are silently ignored.
- Give it the real list of LCARdS options and it stops guessing.
- Check what it wrote before you paste it into Home Assistant.

## With Claude (easiest)

**The LCARdS skill teaches Claude everything for your LCARdS version: every option, every built-in preset and colour, the docs, the gallery dashboards and the config checker.**

- It also knows [HA-LCARS](https://github.com/th3jesta/ha-lcars): its themes, its `--lcars-*` colour variables and its classes for stock cards.
- It knows the [UIX](https://github.com/Lint-Free-Technology/uix) styling HA-LCARS runs on too, so it can tell you which job belongs to an LCARdS option, the theme or UIX.

1. Add the skill to Claude:
   - **Claude Code:** install the LCARdS plugin. In a Claude Code session, run:

     ```
     /plugin marketplace add https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/marketplace.json
     /plugin install lcards@lcards
     ```

   - **claude.ai or the Claude apps:** download [`lcards-skill.zip`](/tools/lcards-skill.zip) and upload it as a custom skill in **Settings** (needs code execution turned on).
2. Ask. For example:
   - "Make me an LCARdS button for `light.kitchen` that turns red when it's on."
   - "Build an engineering dashboard with my `sensor.power_*` entities."

Claude uses your real entity ids instead of inventing them: give it them, or connect it to Home Assistant with [ha-mcp](#give-claude-your-home-s-context-ha-mcp). It also checks its own YAML before handing it over.

In Claude Code the plugin goes further:

- The config checker **runs by itself** every time Claude writes a YAML file with LCARdS cards in it, and Claude fixes whatever it reports before handing the file over.
- **`/lcards:check`** followed by a file or pasted YAML checks it and explains each problem.
- **`/lcards:dashboard`** builds a whole dashboard with you, one question at a time.

::: details Keeping the Claude Code plugin up to date
Each LCARdS release comes with a new version of the plugin. To get it, run `/plugin marketplace update lcards`, or open `/plugin`, go to **Marketplaces**, select **lcards** and turn on **Enable auto-update**. Run `/reload-plugins` (or start a new session) to load the new version.

- The plugin needs Claude Code 2.1.224 or newer.
- **Installed the skill by hand before?** Delete `~/.claude/skills/lcards/` first, so only the plugin copy loads.
- **Prefer a manual install?** Unzip [`lcards-skill.zip`](/tools/lcards-skill.zip) into `~/.claude/skills/`, so you have `~/.claude/skills/lcards/SKILL.md`. It won't update itself.
- **Running a dev build of LCARdS?** Use the dev channel instead, which follows the [dev docs](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/): `/plugin marketplace add https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/marketplace.json`, then `/plugin install lcards@lcards-dev`. Install one channel, not both.
:::

::: info Other tools that support skills
The LCARdS skill follows the open [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) standard, so any tool that supports Agent Skills can load the same zip. We build and test it with Claude.
:::

::: tip Claude can check YAML too
Already have a config, from you or from another tool? Paste it into Claude with the skill loaded and ask *"check this LCARdS config and fix it"*. Claude runs the same checker as the [Check Your Config](config-checker) page and explains each problem.
:::

::: tip Claude can restyle a dashboard you already have
Paste a whole dashboard and ask *"restyle this to the LCARS design rules"*. Claude keeps your entities, controls and labels, asks about anything the YAML doesn't settle (the look, how colours work, the schematic's leader style), rebuilds it with [Designing LCARS Screens](lcars-design) and the [patterns](lcars-patterns), then grades it against the guide's [Check a screen](lcars-design#check-a-screen) list and the config checker. You get the new YAML with each check marked met, fixed or left as is, and a short list of what changed.
:::

## Give Claude your home's context (ha-mcp)

**On its own, Claude doesn't know your Home Assistant: you tell it your entity ids.** The community [**ha-mcp**](https://github.com/homeassistant-ai/ha-mcp) server connects Claude to your Home Assistant, so together with the LCARdS skill Claude can look things up for itself:

- your **areas and floors**, to group a dashboard by room;
- your **entities** and their current **states**, so it uses your real entity ids;
- which devices are lights, sensors, switches and so on, to pick the right card for each.

Then ask, for example: *"Build an LCARdS engineering dashboard for the devices in my garage"* or *"Make a bridge view with a button for every light on the ground floor."*

::: warning ha-mcp is not part of LCARdS
ha-mcp is a separate community project; we don't make, support or take responsibility for it. It can also change your Home Assistant (automations, dashboards, settings and more). If you only want Claude to read your setup, turn on its **Read Only Mode**, or connect with its read-only URL (append `/readonly` to the server address). Install and set it up by following [its own instructions](https://github.com/homeassistant-ai/ha-mcp).
:::

## With other assistants

**If your assistant supports Agent Skills, use the skill above; otherwise attach the option list for your card.**

1. **Download the option list for your card**, for example [`lcards-button.json`](/schema/cards/lcards-button.json). Every card is listed in [`schema/index.json`](/schema/index.json).
2. **Attach it** to your chat and paste this first:

   ```
   I'm writing YAML for LCARdS, a custom Home Assistant card system. The
   attached JSON Schema lists every option. Only use options from the schema.
   If something I ask for isn't there, tell me instead of inventing a key.
   ```

3. **Describe the card you want.**

## Check what it wrote

**Check what an assistant wrote before it goes on a dashboard.**

- Paste the YAML into [Check Your Config](config-checker). It runs in your browser and points at each problem.
- Or ask Claude with the skill to check it (see the tip above).
- Prefer the command line? Download [`lcards-validate.mjs`](/tools/lcards-validate.mjs) and run `node lcards-validate.mjs my-dashboard.yaml` (Node.js 20 or newer).

## If it still makes things up

**Give the assistant the checker's results and the schema again.**

- Paste the checker's output back into the chat and ask it to fix exactly those lines.
- Remind it to re-read the attached schema and not to guess. Most assistants correct themselves once told.

## Additional Context

**More you can attach for a tool without the skill: the schemas, docs pages and a longer prompt.** Claude with the skill already has all of it.

::: details What else you can attach

**Schemas**

- **One card at a time (smallest):** the card's file from [`schema/index.json`](/schema/index.json), plus the shared files its entry lists under `uses` (rules, animations, background animations, state colours, filters). Card files are under 100 KB; attach only the shared files your request touches.
- **Everything in one file:** [`lcards-schema.json`](/lcards-schema.json) holds every card, the [Layout View](../cards/layout-view/) and the LCARS shell strategy. It is about 800 KB, so it suits tools with large context windows.
- Each GitHub release carries both (`lcards-schema.json`, `lcards-schema.zip`), plus the skill and the checker, matching that release exactly.

**Docs pages**

- [Common Properties](../cards/common) explains what the schema can't: entity references, the `theme:` prefix, `{{ }}` templates and actions.
- The card's own page (for example [Button](../cards/button/) or [Chart](../cards/chart/)) has worked examples.
- Tools that read [`llms.txt`](/llms.txt) find everything from there. [`llms-full.txt`](/llms-full.txt) is all the user docs in one file.

**MSD**

The MSD schema (`custom:lcards-msd-card`) is large and deeply nested. Attach [`lcards-msd-card.json`](/schema/cards/lcards-msd-card.json) with the shared files it uses, plus the [MSD Getting Started](../cards/msd/quick-start) or [Line Routing](../cards/msd/routing) page, and expect a few more rounds than for a single button.

**Longer prompt template**

```
I'm writing YAML configuration for LCARdS, a custom Home Assistant Lovelace
card system. I've attached its JSON Schema (from https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/schema/index.json)
and reference docs. Rules:
- Only use properties that appear in the schema for the card type I'm using
  (resolve "#/$defs/..." refs within the file, and "../shared/<name>.json" refs
  against the shared files I attached).
- Do not invent properties. If something I ask for isn't in the schema, tell
  me instead of guessing at a plausible-sounding key.
- Colour values must match the schema's colour pattern: hex, rgb()/rgba()/
  hsl()/hsla(), var(--name), or a theme:path token (e.g. theme:colors.ui.primary).
```

:::

# Building a Dashboard

**Go from single cards to a whole LCARS screen: pick the cards for each job, then lay them out on a layout view.** The [Dashboard Gallery](dashboard-gallery) shows what can be built.

- For the look (colour roles, frames, screen shapes and ready-made patterns) see [Designing LCARS Screens](lcars-design). The [AI skill](ai-assistance) follows the same guide.
- Before saving, paste the dashboard into [Check Your Config](config-checker).

## Pick the cards

**Each LCARS job has a card: elbows for the frame, buttons for blocks and labels, sliders for levels, and a layout view for the screen itself.**

| You want | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| The LCARS frame: corners, bars, headers | [Elbow](../cards/elbow/) | `header-left`/`footer-left` corners, `frame` for a full border; text labels sit on the bars |
| Buttons, labels, status pills | [Button](../cards/button/) | Presets for the classic shapes; `component: dpad` or `alert` for the D-pad and the alert symbol |
| A value you can set or read at a glance | [Slider](../cards/slider-card/) | Pills, gauges, shaped and Picard styles; read-only on sensors |
| Pick one of several options | [Select Menu](../cards/select-menu/) | One button per `input_select` option |
| Rows of readings | [Data Grid](../cards/data-grid/) | Entities, templates and data sources in a table; decorative mode for LCARS number blocks |
| History | [Chart](../cards/chart/) | Entity history, statistics or data sources |
| A ship or floor plan with live controls | [MSD](../cards/msd/) | Cards placed on an SVG, wired with routed lines |
| A full-screen alert | [Alert Overlay](../cards/alert-overlay/) | Shows over the view while an alert mode is active |
| The screen itself | [Layout View](../cards/layout-view/) | A CSS grid for the whole view; [Layout Card](../cards/layout-card/) for a grid inside one area |

::: info Using `custom:layout-card`?
LCARdS has its own [Layout Card](../cards/layout-card/) and [Layout View](../cards/layout-view/): the same grid keys, with a visual editor and more. LCARdS cards inside `custom:layout-card` can shrink and lose their margins, and moving over is a one-line change: see [Sizing inside `custom:layout-card`](../cards/common#inside-custom-layout-card).
:::

## Lay out the screen

**Build the view on a [Layout View](../cards/layout-view/): name the regions in `grid-template-areas`, then put each card in one with `view_layout.grid-area`.** The example is one view: in a dashboard's raw configuration it goes in the `views:` list.

- **Match the frame to the sidebar.** Give the header and footer elbows a `bar_width` equal to the sidebar column, so the bars line up with the buttons below.
- **Use `minmax(0, 1fr)`, not `1fr`,** for columns and rows that hold a chart, an MSD or a grid. A plain `1fr` can't shrink below its content, and the view overflows the screen.
- **Give button rows fixed heights** (`54px`), and the area that should take the rest a flexible track (`minmax(0, 1fr)`).

```yaml live
title: Bridge
path: bridge
type: custom:lcards-layout-view
layout:
  # fill the screen below Home Assistant's toolbar (the default)
  height: calc(100dvh - var(--header-height, 56px))
  padding: 12px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: 170px minmax(0, 1fr)
  grid-template-rows: 64px 54px 54px minmax(0, 1fr) 64px
  grid-template-areas: |
    "header header"
    "nav1   main"
    "nav2   main"
    "filler main"
    "footer footer"
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow:
      type: header-left
      segment:
        bar_width: 170 # the same width as the sidebar column
        bar_height: 22
    view_layout:
      grid-area: header
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: lozenge
    text:
      label:
        content: LIGHTS
        show: true
    view_layout:
      grid-area: nav1
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: lozenge
    text:
      label:
        content: DOORS
        show: true
    view_layout:
      grid-area: nav2
  # fill leftover space instead of leaving a hole in the frame
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-dark
    min_height: 0
    view_layout:
      grid-area: filler
  # the main area: a chart, an MSD or a data grid
  - type: custom:lcards-data-grid
    data_mode: decorative
    view_layout:
      grid-area: main
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow:
      type: footer-left
      segment:
        bar_width: 170
        bar_height: 22
    view_layout:
      grid-area: footer
```

::: details More about laying out cards
- **Some cards draw to their cell's height:** the D-pad, the alert symbol, Picard and shaped sliders. Give them a cell whose height suits them; a tall cell makes a D-pad wider than its column. `justify-self: center` in `view_layout` centres one in a wide area.
- **Data grids stretch their rows** to fill the area. Set `grid-auto-rows` (and `align-content: start`) under the card's `grid:` for a compact table.
- **Lozenge buttons hide their label** by design; set `text.label.show: true` when the button should say something. For a title on an elbow, set its `position` (for example `bottom-right`) and a `color`.
- **Fill leftover space** with a `panel-dark` button or a decorative data grid instead of leaving holes in the frame.
:::

## Recipes

### A status that changes colour at a threshold

**A rule on the card itself recolours it as a reading climbs: the card's `id` is the rule's target, and the higher `priority` wins when both rules match.** Drag the temperature under the card past 60 and then 80.

- See [Rules](../core/rules/) for other conditions (time ranges, templates, `all`/`any`) and for restyling other cards by tag.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
id: reactor_status
entity: sensor.reactor_temperature
preset: lozenge
text:
  label:
    content: "REACTOR {{ states('sensor.reactor_temperature') | int }} °C"
    show: true
rules:
  - id: reactor-hot
    priority: 20
    when:
      entity: sensor.reactor_temperature
      above: 80
    apply:
      overlays:
        reactor_status:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-alert-red)
  - id: reactor-warm
    priority: 10
    when:
      entity: sensor.reactor_temperature
      above: 60
    apply:
      overlays:
        reactor_status:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-alert-yellow)
```

### A smoothed live reading with its history

**A [data source](../core/datasources/) keeps an entity's recent values and runs processors over them: chart the raw and smoothed values together, and show the smoothed one in any text.**

- On the chart, each `sources` entry with `datasource:` plots the data source; `buffer` picks a processor's result instead of the raw values.
- Data source names are shared across the dashboard, so a button elsewhere can read the source the chart defines as `{ds:deck_temp.smoothed:.1f}`. `{ds:deck_temp}` without a format shows the raw value with its unit.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
data_sources:
  deck_temp:
    entity: sensor.deck_temperature
    history:
      hours: 6
    processing:
      smoothed:
        type: smooth
        method: exponential
        alpha: 0.3
sources:
  - datasource: deck_temp
    name: Raw
  - datasource: deck_temp
    buffer: smoothed
    name: Smoothed
```

This button reads the data source the chart defines, so it needs the chart on the same dashboard (it is a plain block for that reason):

```yaml
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: lozenge
text:
  label:
    content: "DECK {ds:deck_temp.smoothed:.1f} °C" # the data source defined on the chart
    show: true
```

### A screen that follows alert mode

**LCARdS cards already recolour themselves when an [alert mode](../core/alert-mode) is active; add buttons that raise and clear an alert, and an overlay for the full-screen effect.** The buttons run the `lcards.*` [actions](../configuration/ha-actions): tap RED ALERT here and this page goes to red alert.

- Automations can react to the alert level too: `input_select.lcards_alert_mode` always holds the current mode.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr
  grid-template-rows: 56px
  grid-gap: 6px
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: lozenge
    text:
      label:
        content: RED ALERT
        show: true
    tap_action:
      action: perform-action
      perform_action: lcards.red_alert
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: lozenge
    text:
      label:
        content: STAND DOWN
        show: true
    tap_action:
      action: perform-action
      perform_action: lcards.clear_alert
```

Add the [alert overlay](../cards/alert-overlay/) once to the view: it covers the screen with the alert symbol while an alert is active. Here it shows on a mock screen; pick a condition to see it.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
```

## Check it

**Before saving a dashboard, paste it into [Check Your Config](config-checker).** It reports keys LCARdS doesn't have and names that don't exist (a misspelt preset, animation or theme token), each at its path in the YAML.

Want help writing it? [Getting AI Help](ai-assistance) shows how to have Claude or another assistant write the YAML for you.

# Coming from CB-LCARS

**LCARdS grew out of, and supersedes, the [CB-LCARS](https://github.com/snootched/cb-lcars) project: most of its features are here, rebuilt, and the table below gives the LCARdS equivalent of each card.**

- CB-LCARS was based on [Custom Button Card](https://github.com/custom-cards/button-card); LCARdS is built from scratch with Lit and needs no other custom cards.

::: tip You can run both at once
CB-LCARS and LCARdS can coexist while you move over. New features and fixes go into LCARdS only.

The configuration formats differ, so card configs don't carry over directly.
:::

## Feature Comparison

**Each CB-LCARS card or feature and its LCARdS equivalent.**

✅ Present | ❌ Not present | ⚠️ Partial

| Feature | CB-LCARS | LCARdS | Notes |
|---|:---:|:---:|---|
| Buttons | ✅ `cb-lcars-button-card` | ✅ `lcards-button` | Built-in `preset` collection provides the standard LCARS button styles, which are completely configurable. |
| Multi-Segment Buttons | ❌ | ✅ `lcards-button` | Allows complex button designs (known as `component`) to be used as advanced multi-segment/multi-touch controls, configured via `segments`. |
| DPAD | ✅ `cb-lcars-dpad-card` | ✅ `lcards-button` | First advanced button to use the `component` feature of `lcards-button`. |
| ALERT | ⚠️ background animation | ✅ `lcards-button` | Promoted to a button card component: allows full interactive configuration. |
| Labels | ✅ `cb-lcars-label-card` | ✅ `lcards-button` | Label functionality is available via `lcards-button`. Additional presets available for text labels with or without decoration. |
| Elbows | ✅ `cb-lcars-elbow-card` | ✅ `lcards-elbow` | Equivalent in LCARdS: enhanced with more corner styles (e.g. straight cut with configurable angles). |
| Double Elbows | ✅ `cb-lcars-double-elbow-card` | ✅ `lcards-elbow` | Double Elbow functionality is now consolidated into a single unified `lcards-elbow` card. |
| Sliders | ✅ `cb-lcars-multimeter-card` | ✅ `lcards-slider` | Completely replacing the former multimeter card. Vastly improved: configurable direction, inversion, display min/max, control min/max, and more. |
| Cascade Data Grid | ⚠️ background animation | ✅ `lcards-data-grid` | CB-LCARS provided a decorative-only version as a background animation. `lcards-data-grid` is a full-featured grid that can show real entity data, text, etc. Decorative mode is still available. |
| Text | ✅ `cb-lcars-text-card` | ✅ `lcards-button` | Text-only button presets, or text fields on any card. |
| Picard-style controls | ✅ `cb-lcars-picard-card` | ✅ `lcards-elbow`, `lcards-slider` | Segmented (double) elbows and frames on `lcards-elbow`; the `picard` slider component with the `picard-gauge-vertical` preset; `filled` and `outline` button presets. |
| Layouts | ⚠️ `custom:layout-card` (separate install) | ✅ `lcards-layout-card`, `lcards-layout-view` | LCARdS has its own grid layouts with visual editors. Replace `custom:layout-card` with `lcards-layout-card`: change the `type` and remove `layout_type`; the `layout` and `view_layout` keys stay the same. See [Layout Card](../cards/layout-card/). |
| Select menu | ❌ | ✅ `lcards-select-menu` | A grid of buttons for an `input_select` or `select` entity. |
| card-mod | ⚠️ required | ✅ not needed | LCARdS needs no other custom cards or card-mod. |
| Charts / Graphs | ❌ | ✅ `lcards-chart` | Embedded ApexCharts library providing 15+ chart types to plot entity/data. |
| MSD (Master Systems Display) | ❌ | ✅ `lcards-msd-card` | Full MSD system in a card. Embed controls, connect routing lines, add animations to reflect statuses. |
| Background Animations | ✅ GRID, ALERT, GEO Array, Pulsewave | ⚠️ ✅ | Background animations split into stackable layers: mix and match building blocks. ✅ GRID (enhanced), ✅ ALERT (button component), ✅ Starfield & Nebula (enhanced). ⚠️ GEO Array, Pulsewave (pending). |
| Element Animations | ❌ | ✅ | Embedded Anime.js v4 enabling animation of any SVG element (cards, lines/stroke, text, etc.). |
| Symbiont (embedded cards) | ✅ | ✅ | In the [elbow card](../cards/elbow/symbiont): embeds any card and imprints the elbow's colours and font on it. `custom_style` adds your own CSS without UIX, and a `uix` block on the embedded card is passed through. |
| State-based Styling / Custom States | ✅ | ✅✅ | CB-LCARS has a limited set of states. LCARdS uses common state groupings (`default` \| `active` \| `inactive` \| `unavailable`) plus the ability to define ***any state*** for customised styling. Integrates with the core rules engine for hot-patching. |
| Sounds | ❌ | ✅ | Customisable sounds for many UI and card event types (tap, double tap, hold, hover, sidebar expand/collapse, and more). |
| Alert Overlay | ❌ | ✅ `lcards-alert-overlay` | Dashboard-level card that reacts to `input_select.lcards_alert_mode` and displays a full-screen configurable backdrop with an embedded content card. |

# Check Your Config

**Paste your YAML below to find what LCARdS won't understand: options that don't exist, misspelt names and values of the wrong kind.** A config LCARdS doesn't understand is mostly ignored without a word, so a typo often looks like a bug.

- **Works with** one card, a view, or a whole dashboard: it finds every LCARdS card in it, at any depth.
- **Private:** this page runs in your browser, and nothing is sent anywhere.

<ClientOnly>

</ClientOnly>

## Where to get your YAML

**Copy it from a card's code editor or from the dashboard's raw configuration.**

- **One card:** open the card editor and switch to its **YAML** tab, then copy everything.
- **A whole dashboard:** **Edit dashboard > ⋮ > Raw configuration editor**, then copy everything.

## Reading the results

**Errors are things LCARdS rejects or ignores; warnings are names it doesn't know and other likely mistakes.** Each result shows the option's path and line, and links to the docs for that option.

- **Errors:** invalid values, keys LCARdS doesn't have, an MSD with nothing to draw on. Fix these.
- **Warnings:** a preset, animation, sound or theme token LCARdS doesn't have, or a misspelt `var(--lcars-*)` or `var(--lcards-*)` colour, almost always a typo; the checker suggests the closest match. A name from a content pack of your own also shows as a warning, and is fine.
- A warning about an older chart or data grid format means the config still works but can be updated.
- **Missing animation params:** some animation presets do nothing without certain params, such as `color-shift` without `color_from` and `color_to`; the warning names the ones to add.
- **Cut-off values:** in YAML a `#` after a space starts a comment, so an unquoted `color: var(--lcars-alert-red, #cc0000)` reads as `var(--lcars-alert-red,`. A value that ends in a comma, or opens a CSS function it never closes, warns: put the whole value in quotes.

## Pasting into Home Assistant's code editor

**Home Assistant's own code editor reads a few unquoted words as `true` or `false`, so quote them there.** That is the editor in a card dialog's **Show code editor** and the raw configuration editor.

- `y`, `yes` and `on` become `true`, and `n`, `no` and `off` become `false`, in any case. So `y: 20` arrives as `true: 20`, and `label: N` as `label: false`.
- Quote them: `"y": 20`, `label: "N"`. The checker warns about each one (**Home Assistant's code editor reads...**).
- The LCARdS editor's own **YAML** tab reads them as written.

## Other ways to check

**The same checker runs in Claude, on the command line and in the card editors.**

- **Ask Claude:** with the [LCARdS skill](ai-assistance#with-claude-easiest) loaded, paste your YAML and ask *"check this LCARdS config and fix it"*. Claude runs this same checker, explains each problem and gives you the corrected YAML.
- **Command line:** download [`lcards-validate.mjs`](/tools/lcards-validate.mjs) and run `node lcards-validate.mjs my-dashboard.yaml` (Node.js 20 or newer). `--json` gives machine-readable output, `--strict` makes warnings fail too, and `-` reads the YAML from standard input. It also reads Home Assistant's `.storage/lovelace*` files.
- **In Home Assistant:** each LCARdS card editor shows schema problems at the top as you edit, and its **YAML** tab checks against the full schema, with lookups, as you type.

# Dashboard Gallery

**Sample screens that show LCARS layouts and the look, each a whole view built from LCARdS cards on a [Layout View](../cards/layout-view/).** Each was recorded in Home Assistant while its entities change (lights switch, levels move, alerts sound). Borrow layouts and sections from them; to build your own dashboard, the [LCARdS skill](ai-assistance) composes one for your entities.

- The dashboards use `lcards_test_*` helpers and one temperature sensor, `sensor.desk_sensor_temperature`. The [Live Demo](live-demo#in-your-own-home-assistant) page has the YAML that creates those helpers, if you want to try a dashboard unchanged first.

::: warning The colours are picked by hand
With test helpers there are no real states to colour by, so every block and button in these samples is given a theme role by hand, including its on and off colours. That shows the look, but it is not how a working dashboard is usually coloured: there, controls bound to your entities normally take the theme's state colours, and copying the hand-picked colours means removing them from every card later. Decide first; see [Colours by state or by hand](lcars-design#colours-by-state-or-by-hand).
:::

To use one:

1. Create a dashboard (**Settings > Dashboards > Add dashboard**), open it, then **Edit dashboard > Raw configuration editor**.
2. Paste the YAML and save.
3. Replace the `lcards_test_*` helpers and the sample temperature sensor with your own entities.
4. If something doesn't work, paste your version into [Check Your Config](config-checker).

# Getting Help

**Something not working? Work through these in order: most problems are a config typo or a setup issue, and both are quick to rule out.**

## 1. Check your config

**Paste your card YAML (or the whole dashboard) into [Check Your Config](config-checker), and fix what it reports first.** A config LCARdS doesn't understand is mostly ignored without a word, which often looks like a bug.

- It finds options that don't exist, misspelt preset, animation and colour names, and values of the wrong kind, each with its line and a suggestion.
- Using Claude with the [LCARdS skill](ai-assistance#with-claude-easiest)? Paste the YAML and ask it to check and fix it.

## 2. Run the health check

**Open the LCARdS Config panel in the sidebar, then Welcome > Support & system info.** Its checklist covers the most common causes of problems, each with a fix.

- The resource and `extra_module_url` checks need an **admin** user.

| Check | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Home Assistant version** | LCARdS requires Home Assistant **2026.11** or newer. |
| **Integration responding** | The cards loaded but the LCARdS integration did not answer. Add or repair it under **Settings > Devices & services**, then restart. |
| **Frontend = integration version** | If these differ, your browser is running a cached copy of an older LCARdS. Hard-refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R / Cmd+Shift+R), or clear the companion app's frontend cache. If you just updated, restart Home Assistant. |
| **Safe or recovery mode** | Home Assistant started in safe or recovery mode, so custom integrations may not load. Restart it normally. |
| **UI eXtension (UIX) / card-mod** | HA-LCARS styles Home Assistant through [UIX](https://github.com/Lint-Free-Technology/uix). **card-mod** no longer works with current Home Assistant and conflicts with UIX: uninstall it in HACS and remove its `extra_module_url` line from `configuration.yaml`. An HA-LCARS theme without UIX is flagged too. |
| **card-mod in `extra_module_url`** | A leftover `frontend: extra_module_url` entry still loads card-mod. Remove it and restart. |
| **custom:layout-card** | Shown when `custom:layout-card` is installed. LCARdS cards can shrink inside it; switch to the LCARdS [Layout Card](../cards/layout-card/). |
| **Lovelace resources** | LCARdS loads itself through the integration. An old manually added resource (e.g. `/hacsfiles/lcards/lcards.js`) or a duplicate loads it twice. Remove extras under **Settings > Dashboards > ⋮ > Resources**. |
| **HA-LCARS theme** | Shows whether an HA-LCARS theme is active. LCARdS works without it, but it is designed to pair with it. |

## 3. Common problems

**Most reports come down to one of these.**

- **Cards collapse or margins look wrong inside `custom:layout-card`:** use LCARdS's own [Layout Card](../cards/layout-card/) instead. Change the `type` to `custom:lcards-layout-card` and remove `layout_type`; the rest of the config stays the same. See [Sizing inside `custom:layout-card`](../cards/common#inside-custom-layout-card).
- **Cards look out of date after an update:** hard-refresh the page (Ctrl+Shift+R / Cmd+Shift+R) or clear the companion app's frontend cache.
- **Styling from card-mod stops working:** card-mod no longer works with current Home Assistant; HA-LCARS uses [UIX](https://github.com/Lint-Free-Technology/uix) instead. Remove card-mod.
- **Moving over from CB-LCARS?** See [Coming from CB-LCARS](cb-lcars-migration) for the equivalent of each card.

## 4. Report an issue

**Still stuck? Report an issue, in the same Support & system info section, opens a GitHub bug report with your versions and support info already filled in.** It also copies the full info to your clipboard. Review the form, describe the problem, add your card YAML, then submit: nothing is sent automatically.

- **Copy support info** copies the same information, to paste into an existing issue or a [Discussion](https://github.com/snootched/LCARdS/discussions).
- Tick **Include data-source names & entity IDs** only if the problem involves data sources.
- Expand **Preview what will be shared** to see exactly what is included: versions, browser, theme, UIX and card-mod status, integration options and the most recent LCARdS warnings. Those warnings can mention entity names, so review before sharing.

::: tip Please use the template
Issues need the bug report template so we have the versions and environment we need. Issues opened without it are labelled `needs-template`. Edit the issue to add the template sections, or use **Report an issue**.
:::

## Other ways to collect info

**Home Assistant's diagnostics file and the browser console give the same facts.**

- **Download diagnostics**, Home Assistant's standard diagnostics file: **Settings > Devices & services > LCARdS > ⋮ > Download diagnostics**. It contains the same backend facts plus Home Assistant's own system information.
- **Browser console** (F12, then Console): the calls below. Pass `{ includeConfig: true }` to the `support.*` calls to include data-source names and entity IDs.

```javascript
window.lcards.info()                    // quick summary
await window.lcards.support.copy()      // copy full support info to the clipboard
await window.lcards.support.openIssue() // copy + open a pre-filled bug report
await window.lcards.support.collect()   // raw support data (object)
```

# Installation

**Install LCARdS from the Home Assistant Marketplace, add the LCARdS integration, then create its helpers in the LCARdS Config panel.** There is nothing else to install: the integration loads the cards on every dashboard.

- **Needs Home Assistant 2026.11 or newer.** LCARdS relies on 2026.11's chip styling and dashboard card paths, and on 2026.10's dashboard visibility handling and validation library. The Marketplace doesn't offer it to older versions, and on an older version the integration logs an error and does not load.
- Something not working after installing? See [Getting Help](getting-help). The LCARdS Config panel's **Welcome** tab also has a health check for common installation problems.

::: tip Pair it with HA-LCARS
LCARdS is designed to pair with the [HA-LCARS themes](https://github.com/th3jesta/ha-lcars). HA-LCARS includes LCARdS theme profiles (**LCARS Picard [LCARdS Red Accent]** and **[LCARdS Blue Accent]**): choose one as your Home Assistant theme and Home Assistant's own screens match your LCARdS cards. See [HA-LCARS Theme Profiles](../configuration/ha-lcars-theme-profiles).
:::

## 1. Install from the Home Assistant Marketplace (HACS)

**Download LCARdS as a Marketplace integration, then restart Home Assistant.**

[![Open your Home Assistant instance and open a repository in the Marketplace.](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/marketplace_repository.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/marketplace_repository/?owner=snootched&repository=lcards&category=integrations)

1. Open **Marketplace** in Home Assistant.
2. Go to **Integrations** and search for **LCARdS**.
3. Click **Download** and confirm.
4. **Restart Home Assistant**, then [add the integration](#_2-add-the-integration).

::: details Manual installation (unmanaged updates)
1. Download `lcards.zip` from the [latest GitHub release](https://github.com/snootched/lcards/releases/latest).
2. Extract the contents into `config/custom_components/lcards/`. The folder should hold `manifest.json` and `__init__.py` directly, not a nested `lcards/lcards/` folder.
3. **Restart Home Assistant**, then [add the integration](#_2-add-the-integration).

Updates don't arrive by themselves this way: repeat these steps for each release.
:::

## 2. Add the integration

**Go to Settings > Devices & services > Add integration and pick LCARdS.** It asks no questions, and only one LCARdS entry can be added.

- The integration connects Home Assistant to the LCARdS cards, and adds the **LCARdS Config** panel to the sidebar.
- Its options are listed under [Integration options](#integration-options).

## 3. First setup

**Choose a theme, then create the helpers in the LCARdS Config panel.** The panel's **Welcome** tab walks you through the same steps.

1. **Choose your HA-LCARS theme** (recommended), ideally one of the LCARdS profiles HA-LCARS includes. See [HA-LCARS Theme Profiles](../configuration/ha-lcars-theme-profiles).
2. **Create the helpers.** Open **LCARdS Config** in the sidebar, go to the **Helpers** tab and click **Create All**. LCARdS keeps alert mode, sound and sizing settings in Home Assistant helpers, and several features (alert mode, the alert overlay, sounds) need them.
3. **Optional: customize your alert colours.** The **Alert Mode Lab** in **Theme Studio** sets how each alert mode recolours your dashboards. See [Alert Mode Lab](../configuration/alert-mode-lab).
4. **Optional: set up sounds.** The **Sounds** tab turns sounds on and picks a sound scheme you can customize. See [Sound Configuration](../configuration/sounds).
5. **Check the setup.** **Welcome > Support & system info** runs a health check (versions, browser cache, card-mod leftovers).

The [Configuration](../configuration/) section covers every panel tab in detail.

## Next steps

- **[Build a dashboard](building-dashboards)**: pick cards and lay out your first LCARS screen.
- **[Browse the gallery](dashboard-gallery)**: start from a complete dashboard.
- Stuck? See **[Getting Help](getting-help)**.

## Integration options

**Settings > Devices & services > LCARdS > Configure sets the sidebar entry, the log level and preview features.** Changes take effect when you save, with no restart; reload the browser page to pick up a new log level.

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| Show sidebar panel | On | Show the LCARdS Config entry in the sidebar. Turn it off for a cleaner sidebar: the integration stays active, every card keeps working, and you can turn it back on at any time |
| Sidebar title | `LCARdS Config` | The sidebar entry's label |
| Sidebar icon | `mdi:space-invaders` | The sidebar entry's icon |
| Log level | `warn` | How much LCARdS logs, in the browser console and in the Home Assistant log: `off`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug` or `trace`. `debug` and `trace` are very verbose: use them only for deep troubleshooting. `?lcards_log_level=debug` on a page's address overrides it for that page |
| Enable Preview Features | Off | Unlocks features still under active development. They may change; please give feedback, discuss or get help on GitHub Issues and Discussions |

# Designing LCARS Screens

**What makes a screen read as LCARS, written down as guidelines you can pick from.** They come from an automated analysis of hundreds of recognizable LCARS screens: the *Star Trek: Picard* season 3 consoles (as rebuilt by meWho's Titan.DS and LCARSlad London) and production panels from *The Next Generation*, *Deep Space Nine* and *Voyager*.

- A dashboard that follows just a few of these guidelines already looks more like LCARS than one that follows none: pick the ones that suit your screen and taste.
- [Building a Dashboard](building-dashboards) covers the mechanics (which card for which job, the layout view); this guide is about the look.
- The [Dashboard Gallery](dashboard-gallery#built-from-the-design-guide) has complete screens built from these guidelines.

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| This page | The two looks, colour roles, structure, scale and density (with a checklist), motion and alerts, and the screen archetypes to start from |
| [LCARS Patterns](lcars-patterns) | Over twenty building blocks, rendered live: code-block columns, sweeps and frames, pill grids, gauges, lists, tiles |

## Two looks

**LCARS comes in two broad looks: the thin, dark *Picard* screens and the thick, colourful classic ones.** Most of the guidelines below apply to both.

- The look mostly comes from the theme: the same layout reads as Picard in a Picard theme and as classic in a classic one.

| | Picard (*Picard* S3, Titan) | Classic (TNG, DS9, Voyager) |
|---|---|---|
| Structure | Thin frames in a few dark, muted tones | Thick blocks of colour |
| Colour | Mostly black and structure tones; a little accent | Several pastel colours at once |
| Buttons | Small square blocks with code numbers, pills at the edges | Grids of rounded pills, led by big numbers |
| Main display | Line-drawn schematic inside an open sweep | Content inside a bracket or sweep frame |
| Themes that suit it | `LCARS Picard [LCARdS Red/Blue Accent]`, `LCARS Picard I/II`, `LCARS 25C` | `LCARS Default`, `LCARS TNG`, `LCARS Classic`, `LCARS Nemesis Blue` |

## Colour comes from your theme

**Don't pick colours for an LCARS screen; pick roles, and let the theme supply the colour.** Then the screen follows when you switch themes, into light or dark mode, and into alert mode.

- **Prefer the `theme:` tokens.** They resolve to your [HA-LCARS](https://github.com/th3jesta/ha-lcars) theme's variable when it's installed and fall back to the LCARdS palette when it isn't, so the card always has a colour. A bare `var(--lcars-...)` is empty without HA-LCARS: give it a fallback, as in the table.
- **Keep accent colour sparse.** In the Picard references only about a tenth of the screen is accent colour; the rest is black and structure tones. A block stays a structure colour unless it means something.
- **Classic screens are more colourful:** several roles side by side, mixed freely. The classic themes already set their roles to the pastel set.
- HA-LCARS themes have one accent role, so the data colour is a deliberate pick from the palette: check it reads on your theme's structure colours.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 64px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr))
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
cards:
  # main structure
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: PRIMARY
    style:
      card:
        color:
          background:
            default: theme:colors.ui.primary
  # secondary structure
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: SECONDARY
    style:
      card:
        color:
          background:
            default: theme:colors.ui.secondary
  # dark structure, with its text partner
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: DARK
        color: var(--lcars-card-top-text, var(--lcards-gray-lightest))
    style:
      card:
        color:
          background:
            default: theme:colors.card.topColor
  # accent: used sparingly
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: ACCENT
    style:
      card:
        color:
          background:
            default: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
```

::: details More about colour
- **Light and dark mode belong to the theme.** If your theme has both, a screen built from roles works in both.
- **A view can choose its own theme:** `theme: LCARS Default` on a view shows that view in that theme, whatever the user's profile theme is. Handy for a classic screen on an otherwise Picard dashboard.
- **Every colour format:** [Colours](../core/colours) lists what a colour value can be and how theme tokens resolve.
:::

| Role | Use for | Token | HA-LCARS variable |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main structure | Sweeps, frame bars, the most important frame | `theme:colors.ui.primary` | `--lcars-ui-primary` |
| Secondary structure | Block columns, side bars | `theme:colors.ui.secondary`, `theme:colors.ui.quaternary` | `--lcars-ui-secondary`, `--lcars-ui-quaternary` |
| Dark structure | Inner frames, inactive blocks, tabs | `theme:colors.card.topColor`, `theme:colors.card.bottomColor` | `--lcars-card-top-color`, `--lcars-card-bottom-color` |
| Accent | What's on, selected or needs attention | `theme:colors.ui.tertiary`, `theme:colors.card.buttonOn` | `--lcars-ui-tertiary`, `--lcars-card-button-color` |
| Data | Readings, schematic lines, gauges | | a palette colour, e.g. `var(--lcars-blue, var(--lcards-blue-medium))` |
| Alert | Alert states | | `var(--lcars-alert-color, var(--lcards-orange-dark))` |
| Text on a role | Labels on a coloured block | | the role's text partner: `--lcars-ui-primary-text`, `--lcars-card-top-text`, ... |

## Colours by state or by hand

**Decide before you build whether a control's colour follows its entity's state or is picked by hand, because changing your mind later means editing every card.** The [gallery](dashboard-gallery) and the [patterns](lcars-patterns) pick by hand; a working dashboard usually shouldn't.

- **By state (the usual choice for your own dashboard):** leave the colour unset on a button bound to an entity, and its preset takes the theme's colours for on, off and unavailable. Every switch reads the same way, your theme and alert mode recolour it, and there is nothing to keep in step. Add a [state map](../core/colours/state-maps) only where one entity needs colours of its own.
- **By hand:** each control gets its own role for on and off (`active` and `inactive`), which gives the many-coloured canon look. Every bound card then carries its own colours, so moving to state colours later means cleaning up each one.
- **Mixed:** the decorative parts (sweeps, bars, code blocks, cascades) take roles picked by hand, which is where most of the look comes from, and the controls keep the theme's state colours.
- **Why the samples pick by hand:** their entities are test helpers, so hand-picked roles are the only way to show the look. Treat their colours as a picture of the style, not as how your switches should be coloured.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 48px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
cards:
  # decorative block: a role picked by hand
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    text:
      label:
        content: 03-118
    style:
      card:
        color:
          background: theme:colors.ui.secondary
  # bound control, by state: no colour set, the theme's on and off colours
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    entity: light.living_room
    text:
      label:
        content: LIGHTS
    tap_action:
      action: toggle
  # bound control, by hand: its own role for on and off
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    entity: light.living_room
    text:
      label:
        content: LIGHTS
    style:
      card:
        color:
          background:
            active: theme:colors.ui.primary
            inactive: theme:colors.card.bottomColor
    tap_action:
      action: toggle
```

## Structure

**An LCARS screen is black, framed by sweeps, and filled with structure rather than empty space.** These hold for both looks.

- **Black canvas.** Content sits on black inside frames, not on coloured blocks.
- **Sweeps make the frames.** A frame is a bar that turns 90° into another bar (an [elbow](../cards/elbow/)). Two sweeps facing each other (a header pair, or a left and a right sweep) is the signature LCARS shape; a lone elbow in a corner is rarer.
- **Frame the display with an open sweep.** On Picard screens the main display sits in one thin sweep that runs along the top, down the left and back along the bottom, open on the right ([display sweep](lcars-patterns#display-sweep)); classic ones put a thin sweep inside a thick one. A fully closed or double frame is rare: use it only when asked.
- **Break long bars into segments** of different lengths, separated by small black gaps. A segment can carry a small label or number.
- **One gap size everywhere.** The same gap between blocks, segments and frames on a screen (`grid-gap` on the layout view and layout cards). Blocks never touch.
- **Labels sit right-aligned**, usually at the bottom right of their block, in condensed capitals (the theme font). Numbers right-aligned in columns.
- **One title, top right**, large, in the accent colour or white; a dim subtitle at the bottom right if you need one. Classic titles often read `NAME • NUMBER`.
- **Numbers as texture.** Code-like numbers (`13-650`, `0099•06`) fill blocks and columns, and dense number cascades fill spare areas. Real readings and decorative numbers look alike; that's part of the look.
- **A sweep is at least as wide as what it frames.** If a sweep's vertical bar is narrower than the column above it, it looks detached; close a narrow column with a segmented bar instead.
- **Fill space with structure, not black.** If an area is empty, put blocks, a number cascade or a segmented bar in it.

## Scale and density

**An LCARS screen is many small parts of fixed size around one large part that takes the rest.** Measured on the reference screens, this matters more than colour. Generated screens most often look fan-made because their parts are too big and too few.

- **Small parts keep a fixed size.** Give their grid tracks a size in px (`64px`, `24px`) and leave `minmax(0, 1fr)` for the main display. With every track at `1fr`, blocks and pills grow with the screen and turn into large slabs. In a column or bar that must reach the screen edge, let one part (the last sidebar block, one long bar segment) take what is left.
- **Many parts.** A full screen carries about 50 to 90 small blocks, pills and bars, plus thin lines, ticks and number rows. A screen with fewer than about 30 reads as a web dashboard painted in LCARS colours.
- **No large empty patch.** About a sixth of the screen is plain black, spread out as gaps; no single empty region is larger than about a tenth of the screen. A chart or a short list alone in a big frame breaks this. Put readouts, a scale, or a column of blocks beside it.
- **Three or four size tiers, no medium-large.** One large display, one large title, small blocks and pills, and tiny labels, ticks and codes.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 192px
  grid-gap: 4px
  # fixed small columns; only the display grows
  grid-template-columns: 64px 64px minmax(0, 1fr)
  grid-template-rows: repeat(7, 24px)
cards:
  # a two-wide code-block column, each block 64 x 24 px
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: 63-934
        position: center-right
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: 13-650
        position: center-right
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-dark
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: 19-638
        position: center-right
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: 42-991
        position: center-right
    style:
      card:
        color:
          background:
            default: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: 28-130
        position: center-right
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-dark
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: 50-957
        position: center-right
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: 81-782
        position: center-right
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: 85-334
        position: center-right
  # the one part that grows: here a number cascade standing in for the main display
  - type: custom:lcards-data-grid
    data_mode: decorative
    format: digit
    view_layout:
      grid-column: "3"
      grid-row: 1 / -1
    grid:
      grid-template-columns: repeat(8, 44px)
      grid-template-rows: repeat(9, 18px)
      gap: 3
    style:
      font_size: 14
      color: theme:colors.ui.secondary
      align: right
```

::: details More about scale and density
- **Measured sizes.** Measured at 1600 px wide on Picard and classic references, the typical block is about 2.5% of the screen height and 4% of the width (about 64 x 24 px). Letters in a block are about half the block's height: `font_size` 13 to 14 in a 24 px block. The title's letters are 3 to 4% of the screen height (Picard) or 6 to 7% (classic). Take these as targets to aim near, not limits.
- **A starting grid.** For the display with side columns at 1600 px wide: `grid-template-columns: 116px 134px minmax(0, 1fr) 196px` (pills, a two-wide block column, the display, a readings column) and `grid-template-rows: 84px minmax(0, 1fr) 132px` (header, display, strip). For the classic data screen: `grid-template-columns: 168px 200px minmax(0, 1fr) 156px 156px` and `grid-template-rows: 84px 142px 18px 18px 90px minmax(0, 1fr)`, the first row sized for the title (about 1.3 times its `font_size`) and the two 18 px rows holding the upper and lower sweeps' bars. Classic pills are about 30 px tall at this size. Other archetypes keep the same idea: fixed px for every area but the display.
- **Overlap by lines, not areas.** Each named area must be one rectangle, or the browser drops the whole template (the [config checker](config-checker) reports it). Where a part sits inside a sweep's open corner (the classic number rows, a display tucked under a curve), place it with `view_layout` `grid-row` and `grid-column` instead of an area, with a left margin that clears the sweep's inner curve. Columns that must line up (a ruler of blocks beside its numbers) need the same row sizes.
- **Edge columns are narrow.** Picard block columns, gauge pairs and pill columns are each about 4 to 9% of the width and sit tight against the frame. A classic sidebar is thicker, about 8 to 12%.
- **Thin structure fills black without weight.** 1 to 3 px rules, leader lines from a block to what it labels, tick scales and [dot rows](lcars-patterns#dot-rows) are everywhere on the references.
- **Frames interlock.** A header bar runs into a sweep that becomes a column, and the column ends in another bar. Regions are divided by thin frames and small gaps, not by one large gap between equal boxes.
- **The main display is busy.** A schematic with labels and leader lines, or a chart with a scale and readouts beside it; not a chart alone.
- **Phones and portrait panels** hold fewer parts (about half), at the same small sizes.
:::

### Check a screen

**Before you call a screen done, run down this list.** Each item is a guideline from the references; a screen can break one on purpose.

| Check | Aim near |
|---|---|
| Small parts on fixed px tracks | Only the main display uses `1fr`, plus one filler part per edge column or bar |
| Small blocks, pills and bars on a full screen | 50 to 90 (a portrait panel about 600 px wide: 25 to 45) |
| Block size at 1600 px wide | About 64 x 24 px; a classic sidebar block is wider |
| Label text | Letters about half the block's height (`font_size` 13 to 14 in a 24 px block); one title at 36 to 48 (Picard) or 56 to 80 (classic), clear of everything round it |
| Largest empty region | Under about a tenth of the screen |
| Accent colour | About a tenth of the screen (Picard); classic carries more |
| Number cascades and readouts | On black, never in outlined or rounded boxes |
| Numbers that mean something | Most numbers are readings with a label; at most one decorative cascade filling an area, in a slot a reading can take (short groups inside a code-block column don't count) |
| Frames | Open sweeps that interlock; bars in two to four segments (a bracket screen's header may run on in many short coded segments); never one thick frame around a grid of equal boxes |
| Ends at the screen edge | Sweeps and bars that run off the screen end square; a short capped bar or a pill keeps its round cap |
| Leader lines | One style for the whole MSD; leave the label's side facing the part, at the text's mid-height; turn once, near the part, with a curve (broad on classic, tight on Picard), never a square corner; the bracket style runs straight, or turns sharply into one diagonal, in its bar's colour |

## Picard

**Picard screens are thin frames in dark tones, with columns of small blocks and a schematic in the middle.**

- **Columns of small number blocks** down one or both sides: mostly structure tones, a few in the accent, some dark (inactive). See [code-block column](lcars-patterns#code-block-column).
- **A utility column at the far edge:** a bracket frame open on the outer side, square-ended there, holding three to five small dark pills (zoom, settings, dimmer) with a red alert pill at the bottom. Every other button is a rectangular block. See [utility pills](lcars-patterns#utility-pills).
- **Concentric sweeps**: a thick sweep with a thin line running parallel inside it, for headers and corners. See [concentric sweep](lcars-patterns#concentric-sweep).
- **Controls inside a wide arm**: a thick frame whose black inset holds a group of blocks. See [controls inside a wide arm](lcars-patterns#controls-inside-a-wide-arm).
- **Vertical gauges with tick scales** beside the number columns ([Picard and gauge sliders](../cards/slider-card/)). See [gauge bank](lcars-patterns#gauge-bank).
- **The main display is a schematic**: a line drawing with leader lines to labels, small accent highlights for faults ([MSD](../cards/msd/)). A leader leaves its label from the side, runs out and turns once into the part with a tight curve, never a square corner. A screen keeps one style for every label: that one, a thin bar beside each label whose line leaves the bar's corner and runs straight (level with its part, or one sharp turn into a diagonal), or a short stub and an angled run. See [labelled schematic](lcars-patterns#labelled-schematic).
- **A strip of tabs and sliders along the bottom.** Tabs show their state as a line along the top ([toggle tab strip](lcars-patterns#toggle-tab-strip)).
- **Fixed chrome, changing centre.** Titan.DS keeps the same frame, columns and strips on every screen and swaps only the central display. In LCARdS: a layout view whose centre area holds several cards with [visibility conditions](../cards/layout-view/), one shown at a time.

## Classic (TNG, DS9, Voyager)

**Classic screens build their structure from thick blocks of colour, with grids of pills led by big numbers.**

- **The data screen is the classic shape.** An upper band about a quarter of the height carries a sweep, a [readings table](lcars-patterns#readings-table) of tiny labelled values (one or two colours a row), a few pills and the big title, which keeps clear of the readings. A thin band of two to four segments per bar divides it from the lower part. The lower part is a thick sidebar of stacked blocks beside one large line-art display (a grid, scan or schematic). See the [data screen archetype](#screen-archetypes).
- **Colour blocks are the structure.** Thick header blocks, often in several roles side by side.
- **Grids of rounded pills**, each with a small code label, in column groups that alternate two or three roles. See [pill grid](lcars-patterns#pill-grid-classic).
- **A column of big numbers** (`20`, `008`, `358`) leads each group of pills.
- **Bracket frames**: a top and a bottom bar with rounded ends, and a sidebar of stacked blocks with code numbers. See [bracket frame](lcars-patterns#bracket-frame-classic).
- **A split header**: two sweeps meeting across the top, with a thin segmented band in the gap between them. See [split header](lcars-patterns#split-header-classic).
- **Schematics list their labels in columns** beside the drawing, and each leader sweeps round into its part with a broad curve, like a small sweep. See [labelled schematic](lcars-patterns#labelled-schematic).
- **Segment the long arms.** A classic bar seldom runs unbroken across the screen: the sweep turns into a short bar, then segments of different lengths and roles carry labels. See [segmented bar](lcars-patterns#segmented-bar-classic-arms).

## Motion and alerts

**Keep an LCARS screen mostly still: small things move, and an alert changes everything at once.**

- **At rest, move small things only**: ticking numbers, a dot row, a scanning line. On the reference screens about one twentieth of the screen moves at a time. See [Animations](../core/animations) and [data grid cascades](../cards/data-grid/).
- **Animate entrances once** (`on_show` with `draw`, `cascade` or `text-reveal`), not continuously.
- **Alerts change the whole screen at once**: [alert mode](../core/alert-mode) recolours everything in place, and an [alert overlay](../cards/alert-overlay/) adds the alert symbol. Avoid making every card flash.
- **Show state by colour in place**, not by moving things: a block turns to the accent, a tab's line lights up.

## Screen archetypes

**Start a screen by picking its overall shape, then fill the areas with [patterns](lcars-patterns).** These are the layouts that recur across the reference screens, and each suits a different job.

- An archetype isn't tied to a look: any of them works as a Picard or a classic screen, whatever the table's examples name. The gallery's environmental screen is a data screen in the Picard look.
- Take groupings and sections from the [gallery](dashboard-gallery) and the references freely, but compose the screen for its own job rather than reproducing one whole.
- Two things vary a screen more than anything else: which archetype you start from, and which patterns you put in its areas. A screen that reuses one gallery screen's grid with new labels is the same screen; one that combines a different archetype with two or three patterns is a new one.

| Archetype | Good for | Shape (`grid-template-areas`) | In the gallery |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Display with side columns** | One main system (a ship, a floor plan, a chart) with controls around it; Titan.DS modules | `"pills top top top" "pills left main right" "pills left strip right"` | [Picard](dashboard-gallery#picard-display-with-side-columns) |
| **Display over controls** | A wide display with a dense control deck under it; Titan.DS ship screens | `"head head" "display display" "deck1 deck2"` | [Picard](dashboard-gallery#picard-display-over-controls) |
| **Wings** | Two related halves (port and starboard, upstairs and downstairs) around a shared centre | `"head head head" "lwing centre rwing"` | [Classic](dashboard-gallery#classic-wings) |
| **Switchable display** | Several systems on one screen, one at a time: a selector strip swaps the centre while the frame, columns and strips stay; Titan.DS modules | `"head head head" "left main right" "sel sel sel"` (several cards in `main`, each with a visibility condition) | [Picard](dashboard-gallery#operations) |
| **Master systems display** | One whole ship, house or floor as a schematic filling the screen, with routed callouts to readings and controls round its edges | `"head head head" "calll msd callr" "foot foot foot"` | [Picard](dashboard-gallery#engineering) |
| **Portrait panel** | Phones and wall tablets mounted upright | `"title" "main" "gauges" "controls"` | [Picard](dashboard-gallery#picard-portrait-panel) |
| **Tile wall** | Many similar things at once: cameras, rooms, sensors | `"head head head" "t1 t2 t3" "t4 t5 t6"` | [Picard](dashboard-gallery#picard-tile-wall) |
| **Data screen** | One large display (a scan, a map, a chart) with data rows above it | `"sweep data title" "side band band" "side display display"` | [Classic](dashboard-gallery#classic-data-screen) |
| **Sweep console** | A control panel: thick header sweep, sidebar, button groups; or two sweeps facing across the top, their arms running down the middle as stacked blocks | `"head head head" "side pills readout" "foot foot foot"` | [Classic](dashboard-gallery#classic-sweep-console) |
| **Bracket screen** | A readout or a document: capped top and bottom bars, a numbered sidebar | `"top top" "side main" "bottom bottom"` | [Classic](dashboard-gallery#classic-bracket-screen) |
| **List** | Rosters, schedules, logs: rows of text under a split header | `"head head" "list numbers" "pills pills"` | [Classic](dashboard-gallery#classic-list) |

## Putting it together

**A screen is a [layout view](../cards/layout-view/) shaped by one of the archetypes, with [patterns](lcars-patterns) in its areas.** For example: a facing-sweeps header across the top, a code-block column and utility pills down the left, a display sweep round an MSD or chart in the centre, and a toggle tab strip along the bottom. Or a portrait panel: a header bar with a title, a gauge bank, a selector strip.

The [Dashboard Gallery](dashboard-gallery#built-from-the-design-guide) has seven complete screens built this way, four in the Picard look and three classic, each laid out differently.

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/getting-started/lcars-patterns.html -->

# LCARS Patterns

**Building blocks to compose an LCARS screen from: each one is a card or a [layout card](../cards/layout-card/) you can drop into an area of a layout view, with every colour taken from a theme role.** Change the numbers, labels and entities to yours. [Designing LCARS Screens](lcars-design) explains what makes a screen read as LCARS, and its [archetypes](lcars-design#screen-archetypes) give the overall shapes to put these in.

- **Patterns are modules with slots.** A slot holds a decorative part or a control of the same size: a code block can toggle a light, a gauge can follow a real sensor, a number in a cascade can be a reading. Swap them freely; the module keeps its shape.
- **Small parts keep a fixed size.** The examples use the sizes measured on the reference screens (blocks about 64 x 24 px, letters about half the block height, `font_size` 13 to 14) on px tracks, so they keep that size on a full screen; only a main display takes `minmax(0, 1fr)`. See [Scale and density](lcars-design#scale-and-density).
- **Give the layout card's rows a size** (`grid-template-rows` or `grid-auto-rows` in px or `minmax(0, 1fr)`): rows left to size themselves squash the cards.
- **Keep a button's row at least as tall as the button:** 56 px by default. Small pills and blocks set a lower `min_height`, and bar labels size their text to it.
- Patterns marked *(classic)* come from TNG, DS9 and Voyager screens, and most of the others from the *Picard* references. The theme sets the colours, so most work in either look.
- The examples pick every colour by hand to show the look. Before you copy them onto controls bound to your entities, read [Colours by state or by hand](lcars-design#colours-by-state-or-by-hand).

| For | Patterns |
|---|---|
| Frames and headers | [Facing sweeps header](#facing-sweeps-header), [Concentric sweep](#concentric-sweep), [Display sweep](#display-sweep), [Header bar with a title](#header-bar-with-a-title), [Slanted bars](#slanted-bars), [Segmented bar](#segmented-bar-classic-arms), [Bracket frame](#bracket-frame-classic), [Split header](#split-header-classic) |
| Controls | [Code-block column](#code-block-column), [Utility pills](#utility-pills), [Controls inside a wide arm](#controls-inside-a-wide-arm), [Toggle tab strip](#toggle-tab-strip), [Selector strip](#selector-strip), [Flagged blocks](#flagged-blocks), [Pill grid](#pill-grid-classic) |
| Readings | [Labelled schematic](#labelled-schematic), [Status rows](#status-rows), [Readout rows](#readout-rows), [Gauge bank](#gauge-bank), [Tile wall](#tile-wall), [Fleet tiles](#fleet-tiles), [Brackets and scopes](#brackets-and-scopes), [List](#list) |
| Filling space | [Number cascade filler](#number-cascade-filler), [Dot rows](#dot-rows) |

## Code-block column

**The Picard side column: small blocks with code numbers, mostly in structure tones, one in the accent.** Use it down one or both sides of a screen.

- The blocks are panels (`panel-light`, `panel-dark`) with the label moved to the middle right and `min_height: 0`, on 64 x 24 px tracks. Two columns side by side is the usual Picard width.
- A panel with an entity shows the theme's accent while it's on and the dark structure tone while it's off: toggle the light under the card to see block 42-991 change.
- Leave out `text.label.content` and each block gets a random code.
- Picard columns often break the blocks with a short group of three or four rows of small numbers: a [number cascade](#number-cascade-filler) in the column's width.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 108px
  grid-gap: 4px
  grid-template-columns: 64px 64px
  grid-auto-rows: 24px
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: 63-934
        position: center-right
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: 13-650
        position: center-right
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: 19-638
        position: center-right
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 0
    entity: light.demo
    text:
      label:
        content: 42-991
        position: center-right
    tap_action:
      action: toggle
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: 28-130
        position: center-right
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: 50-957
        position: center-right
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: 81-782
        position: center-right
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: 85-334
        position: center-right
```

## Toggle tab strip

**A row of tabs whose state shows as a line along the top: dark when off, the accent when on.** The `toggle-tab` preset shows the entity's name in the middle; a tab without an entity takes its `text.name.content`.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 30px
  grid-gap: 4px
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 96px)
  grid-template-rows: 30px
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: toggle-tab
    min_height: 0
    entity: light.bridge
    tap_action:
      action: toggle
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: toggle-tab
    min_height: 0
    entity: switch.viewscreen
    tap_action:
      action: toggle
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: toggle-tab
    min_height: 0
    text:
      name:
        content: AUDIO
```

## Facing sweeps header

**Two sweeps meeting across the top, with the title in the black space between them.** The signature LCARS header: a `header-left` and a `header-right` elbow side by side, each in its own role.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 120px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) minmax(0, 1fr)
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow:
      type: header-left
      segment:
        bar_width: 120
        bar_height: 20
        color: theme:colors.ui.primary
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow:
      type: header-right
      segment:
        bar_width: 120
        bar_height: 20
        color: theme:colors.ui.secondary
    text:
      label:
        content: ENGINEERING
        position: center
        color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
```

## Display sweep

**The frame round a Picard main display: one sweep that runs along the top, turns down the left and back along the bottom, open on the right.** The top and bottom bars run on past the display as segments or dot rows; the display (an MSD, a chart) fills the black inside.

On a full screen the usual form is wider: the header bar turns down over a [code-block column](#code-block-column), the column is the display's left side, and a short sweep at its foot turns into the closing bar under the display. The frame below is the compact form for a display on its own.

- The bars end square on the open side, and thin bars keep one width round the corners: leave `inner_curve` unset.
- An elbow draws its inner curve only when its area is wider than its `bar_width` (and taller than its `bar_height`). When a header or foot sweep sits over a code column, give its area a gutter of about 40 px past the column, or it fills with a slab.
- Keep the bars thin (10 to 16 px) with a large outer curve; a code-block column often sits just left of the sweep.
- To run the bars on past the display, place the frame across the first columns of the area and the display over the rest, then put segments or a dot row in line with the top and bottom bars.
- One sweep per corner: the display sweep's top bar can be the header's bar. Don't stack a separate header corner right above the sweep's own corner, or the two curves read as a double ring.
- A closed frame on all four sides, or two nested rings (`style: segmented` with `segments.inner_frame`), is not seen on the reference screens; use it only when a screen asks for a boxed display.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-elbow
grid_options:
  rows: 4
elbow:
  type: frame
  segment:
    color: theme:colors.ui.secondary
  frame:
    bar_width: 14
    bar_height: 12
    outer_curve: 60
    right:
      enabled: false
```

## Labelled schematic

**The main display: a dimmed line drawing with small labels pointing at its parts.** It is an [MSD](../cards/msd/) whose labels are `text-only` buttons placed as controls, each joined to its part by a leader line.

- Widen `view_box` beyond the drawing to leave room for the labels, and place each label in that margin, well inside the `view_box` edge, with its proportions matching the display's area (otherwise the drawing is letterboxed and the margin moves).
- A leader leaves its label from the side that faces the part (`anchor_side: left` or `right`), at the text's mid-height. Align the text toward that side (`center-right` or `center-left`) and size the box close to the text, so the line starts at the text, not at empty box.
- Place the label so the part lies well past its end, above or below it: the line runs out, turns once near the part, and goes in. Leave top and bottom exits to a bar's corner.
- Sizes are in `view_box` units and scale with the drawing. Aim for labels that render at 12 to 14 px, lines at 2 to 3 px (Picard) or 1.5 to 2 px (classic), and bends that read as curves: value = px x `view_box` width / the display's width in px. Use one leader style for the whole MSD, with one corner size and line width; mix styles only when asked.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:enterprise-d-shuttlecraft15-anomaly
    filters:
      - mode: css
        type: grayscale
        value: 1
      - mode: css
        type: opacity
        value: 0.55
  view_box:
    - -60
    - -150
    - 1160
    - 800
  overlays:
    - id: lbl-tanks
      type: control
      attachment: top-left
      position:
        - -50
        - -120
      size:
        - 240
        - 40
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: text-only
        min_height: 0
        text:
          label:
            content: DEUTERIUM 1-3
            show: true
            position: center-right
            font_size: 28
            color: theme:colors.ui.secondary
    # every label the same way: out of the side, one tight bend into the part
    - id: ln-tanks
      type: line
      anchor: lbl-tanks
      attach_to:
        - 281
        - 60
      anchor_side: right
      anchor_gap: 8
      route: manhattan
      corner_radius: 22
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-card-top-color, var(--lcards-gray-medium))
        width: 5
    - id: lbl-cargo
      type: control
      attachment: top-left
      position:
        - -50
        - 570
      size:
        - 300
        - 40
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: text-only
        min_height: 0
        text:
          label:
            content: CARGO 4 · SEAL FAULT
            show: true
            position: center-right
            font_size: 28
            color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
    # the fault: the accent, the same style
    - id: ln-cargo
      type: line
      anchor: lbl-cargo
      attach_to:
        - 450
        - 440
      anchor_side: right
      anchor_gap: 8
      route: manhattan
      corner_radius: 22
      style:
        color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
        width: 5
    - id: lbl-seat
      type: control
      attachment: top-left
      position:
        - 880
        - 540
      size:
        - 170
        - 40
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: text-only
        min_height: 0
        text:
          label:
            content: FLIGHT DECK
            show: true
            position: center-left
            font_size: 28
            color: theme:colors.ui.secondary
    - id: ln-seat
      type: line
      anchor: lbl-seat
      attach_to:
        - 632
        - 227
      anchor_side: left
      anchor_gap: 8
      route: manhattan
      corner_radius: 22
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-card-top-color, var(--lcards-gray-medium))
        width: 5
```

::: details More about leader lines
- **Picard bends are tight but never square:** a small `corner_radius` (about 8 to 12 px rendered), never `corner_style: miter`. The bracket style is the exception: its lines are straight, or turn once at a sharp corner into a diagonal.
- **Picard styles, one per MSD:** straight out of the side with one tight bend (above); a thin bar beside every label, its line leaving the bar's top corner straight or into one diagonal (below); or a short stub and then a straight run at an angle (`route: angled`, `stub_length`; see [routing modes](../cards/msd/line-overlay#routing-modes)). A fault keeps the screen's style and takes the accent.
- **Gap:** the button's text `padding` (8 by default) plus `anchor_gap` keeps the line off the letters. A line leaving a bar or a filled block touches it.
- **End on a point:** `attach_to` as `[x, y]` on the drawing. A line that ends on an overlay (a shape or control) arrives at the side nearest its label, which adds a bend; give it `attach_side: center` to keep the one bend.
- **Faults** take the accent, the line too; everything else stays in structure tones.
- **A grid behind the drawing** (the `grid` background preset) suits it, but that preset scrolls by default: set its `config.scroll_speed_x` and `config.scroll_speed_y` to `0` so the screen stays still.
:::

**The bracket style gives every label a thin bar on the side its line leaves, and the line runs from the bar's top corner along its edge, then straight to the part.** The bar is the label's own border (`style.border.width.right` or `left`); `anchor_side: top-right` or `top-left` with `route_hint: xy` starts the line along the top, flush with the bar. Lay the labels out one of two ways: in columns beside the drawing, each level with its part so every line runs straight out; or above and below it, each line running a long stub (about 60 px) along the bar's edge before one sharp turn into a straight diagonal (`route: angled`, `stub_length`, `corner_style: miter`). No curves. The line takes the bar's colour.
