## Utility pills

**The Picard edge column: a bracket frame open on the outer side, a few small dark pills, and red alert at the bottom.** The frame and a layout card of pills share one grid area, and the inner layout card's padding keeps the pills inside the frame.

- The bracket's bars end square on the open side; only the corners where a bar turns are rounded. A frame does this by itself when a side is off.
- Pills are for the few utility controls only (zoom, settings, dimmer, red alert: three to five). Other buttons on a Picard screen are rectangular blocks.
- The empty `text-only` button takes up the flexible row, so the red alert pill sits at the bottom whatever the height. On a full screen that row is a slot: a gauge pair or a code-block column fits there.
- RED ALERT runs `lcards.red_alert`: tap it here and the page goes to red alert.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 300px
  grid-template-columns: 150px
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
  grid-template-areas: |
    "col"
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    view_layout:
      grid-area: col
    elbow:
      type: frame
      segment:
        color: theme:colors.ui.secondary
      frame:
        bar_width: 14
        bar_height: 36
        outer_curve: 36
        left:
          enabled: false
  - type: custom:lcards-layout-card
    view_layout:
      grid-area: col
    layout:
      padding: 46px 22px 46px 4px
      grid-gap: 8px
      grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)
      grid-template-rows: 26px 26px 26px minmax(0, 1fr) 26px
    cards:
      - type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        min_height: 26
        text:
          label:
            content: ZOOM
            show: true
            position: center
            color: theme:colors.ui.secondary
        style:
          card:
            color:
              background:
                default: theme:colors.card.topColor
      - type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        min_height: 26
        text:
          label:
            content: SETTINGS
            show: true
            position: center
            color: theme:colors.ui.secondary
        style:
          card:
            color:
              background:
                default: theme:colors.card.topColor
      - type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        min_height: 26
        text:
          label:
            content: DIMMER
            show: true
            position: center
            color: theme:colors.ui.secondary
        style:
          card:
            color:
              background:
                default: theme:colors.card.topColor
      - type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: text-only
        min_height: 0
      - type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        min_height: 26
        text:
          label:
            content: RED ALERT
            show: true
```

## Concentric sweep

**A thick sweep with a thin line running parallel inside it: the Picard header and corner shape.** It is a segmented elbow (`style: segmented`): `outer_segment` is the sweep and `inner_segment` the line.

- Leave the inner segment's curves unset: the line then stays concentric with the sweep and keeps one even width round the corner.
- Use it where nothing else turns the same corner: above a [display sweep](#display-sweep), let the display's own sweep make the corner instead.
- The line ends where the sweep's bar ends. When the bar carries on as segments in the next cards, end the elbow's area at the first gap, so the line stops at that gap with the bar.

- Keep the sweep's vertical part short: let the bar carry on as a segmented band beside a column of small blocks rather than as one tall block, or a wide inner block becomes a full-height slab.
- Swap the weights for the other common Picard form: a thin outer band with a large curve wrapped round a wide inner block. The [split screen](dashboard-gallery#picard-split-screen) uses `outer_segment` 40 by 14 with `outer_curve: 100` round an `inner_segment` 134 by 24 (as wide as a two-block column); the lcars-shell strategy's corners have the same form.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-elbow
grid_options:
  rows: 3
elbow:
  type: header-left
  style: segmented
  segments:
    gap: 6
    outer_segment:
      bar_width: 140
      bar_height: 24
      color: theme:colors.ui.secondary
    inner_segment:
      bar_width: 6
      bar_height: 4
      color: theme:colors.ui.primary
text:
  title:
    content: COURSE SELECT
    position: bottom-right
    color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
```

## Segmented bar (classic arms)

**Classic screens rarely run one unbroken bar across the screen: the sweep turns into a short bar, then continues as labelled segments of different lengths and roles.** Each segment is a panel in its own grid column.

- Keep the elbow's area just wider than its vertical bar, and put the segments in a row the same height as the bar (40 px here).
- Two to four segments per bar is plenty; more reads as a ruler. A bracket screen's header is the exception: its top bar runs on in many short coded segments.
- The same works for a Picard closing bar: thin segments (14 to 20 px) in structure tones, one in the accent.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
```

## Number cascade filler

**Fills a spare area with moving numbers instead of black.** A [data grid](../cards/data-grid/) in `decorative` mode needs no other keys; fixed px rows keep it dense.

- Use one small cascade on a screen at most, as a slot a [readings table](#readings-table) can take over later. Numbers that mean nothing read as noise once they fill more than a corner. Short groups of three or four rows between the blocks of a [code-block column](#code-block-column) are part of that column and don't count.
- Size the area to the rows: about `font_size` + 4 px per row (18 px rows at `font_size: 14`); smaller rows cut the text off.
- With rows left to `auto`, a tall area spreads the numbers far apart. Give `grid.grid-template-rows` a fixed row height (about 18 px with `font_size: 14`) and as many rows as fit the area, and the columns a fixed width (about 44 px for four digits) so the numbers stay in tight groups.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-data-grid
data_mode: decorative
format: digit
refresh_interval: 2000
refresh_cells: 0.1
grid:
  grid-template-columns: repeat(6, 44px)
  grid-template-rows: repeat(8, 18px)
  gap: 2
style:
  font_size: 14
  color: theme:colors.ui.secondary
  align: right
```

## Readings table

**Dense rows of short labels with live values, for the numbers on a screen that mean something.** A [data grid](../cards/data-grid/) in `data` mode: a code or short name, the entity's state as Home Assistant formats it, and a status word that follows the value.

- Keep it on black, with no header box: fixed px rows about `font_size` + 6 px, and fixed px columns sized to the longest value. Labels sit left and values right; `text_transform: uppercase` makes Home Assistant's states (`On`, `beta`) read as LCARS capitals.
- Colour by row (`rows[].style.color`) in one or two roles, and turn a value to the alert colour past a limit with a [state map](../cards/data-grid/data#conditional-colours).
- A classic data screen's upper band is a good home: three to six rows beside the sweep, in the slot a number cascade would fill.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-data-grid
data_mode: data
rows:
  - values:
      - 01-TMP
      - sensor.living_room_temperature
      - "{{ 'NOMINAL' if states('sensor.living_room_temperature') | float(0) < 24 else 'HIGH' }}"
    style:
      color: theme:colors.ui.secondary
  - values:
      - 02-HUM
      - sensor.living_room_humidity
      - NOMINAL
    style:
      color: theme:colors.ui.secondary
  - values:
      - 03-PWR
      - value: sensor.house_power
        style:
          color:
            default: theme:colors.ui.primary
            above:3000: var(--lcars-alert-color, var(--lcards-orange-dark))
      - DRAW
    style:
      color: theme:colors.ui.primary
# codes and status words left, values right
columns:
  - style:
      align: left
  - style:
      align: right
  - style:
      align: left
grid:
  grid-template-columns: 70px 70px 80px
  grid-template-rows: repeat(3, 20px)
  gap: 0px 10px
style:
  font_size: 14
  align: right
  text_transform: uppercase
```

## Header bar with a title

**A bar that carries the screen or section title, with a short cap before it.** Picard sections (*MISSION OPS*, *PROPULSION*) use this instead of a sweep.

- The title grows to fill the bar's height, so in a narrow area set a smaller `text.label.font_size` (or a shorter `min_height`) or it runs off the end.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
```

## Readout rows

**A label block and a horizontal gauge per line, for a set of levels read side by side.** Each line is a `panel-dark` button beside a slider with the `gauge-basic` preset; drag a level under the card to move its gauge.

- A slider keeps a minimum height of about 40 px so it stays easy to drag. A thin readout gauge in a shorter row sets `height` to the row (24 here); otherwise it spills into the next row.
- In rows this small, turn the gauge's scale labels off (`style.gauge.scale.labels.enabled: false`): at their default size they cover the fill. The ticks stay.
- On a full screen, a thin bar reads better than a full-height fill, which turns each row into a large accent slab: set `style.gauge.progress_bar.height` to about 8 with the ticks in a structure tone, as the `picard-gauge-column` preset does.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 80px
  grid-gap: 4px
  grid-template-columns: 110px minmax(0, 1fr)
  grid-template-rows: repeat(3, 24px)

    preset: panel-dark
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: PRIMARY
        position: center-right
  - type: custom:lcards-slider
    entity: input_number.primary_level
    preset: gauge-basic
    height: 24
    style:
      gauge:
        scale:
          labels:
            enabled: false
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-dark
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: SECONDARY
        position: center-right
  - type: custom:lcards-slider
    entity: input_number.secondary_level
    preset: gauge-basic
    height: 24
    style:
      gauge:
        scale:
          labels:
            enabled: false
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-dark
    min_height: 0
    text:
      label:
        content: RESERVE
        position: center-right
  - type: custom:lcards-slider
    entity: input_number.reserve_level
    preset: gauge-basic
    height: 24
    style:
      gauge:
        scale:
          labels:
            enabled: false
```

## Gauge bank

**A row of upright gauges, as on the Picard consoles: a number cap at each end, a thin value bar and a short ruler.** Good for several readings of the same kind: each is a slider with the `picard-gauge-column` preset, which shows the value in its top cap.

- The bottom cap shows the entity's name; give `text.name.content` a code or a short label instead when the name is too long for the cap.
- Keep the gauges narrow (about 60 px) and side by side; a bank of them sits beside a code-block column. Under about 56 px, turn the scale numbers off (`style.gauge.scale.labels.enabled: false`).
- The ticks are in the entity's units (a major tick every 10, a minor every 2). For another range, such as 10 to 35 °C, set `style.gauge.scale.tick_marks.major.interval` and `minor.interval` to suit.
- For the framed gauge with scanning lights, use the `picard-gauge-vertical` preset instead ([Picard component](../cards/slider-card/components#picard-component)).

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 420px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 60px)
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-slider
    preset: picard-gauge-column
    entity: sensor.demo_temperature
    text:
      name:
        content: "37-88"
  - type: custom:lcards-slider
    preset: picard-gauge-column
    entity: sensor.demo_humidity
    text:
      name:
        content: "51-80"
  - type: custom:lcards-slider
    preset: picard-gauge-column
    entity: sensor.demo_battery
    text:
      name:
        content: "21-10"
  - type: custom:lcards-slider
    preset: picard-gauge-column
    entity: input_number.demo_level
    text:
      name:
        content: "65-87"
```

## Fleet tiles

**A row of framed tiles, one per item, as in the Titan.DS fleet directory.** Each tile is a frame elbow with two text fields, the name and the class; its thicker top and bottom bars (`bar_height`) can carry a state colour.

- The two fields need about 90 px of tile height; in a shorter tile, put both on one line (`NCC-1701-A · CONSTITUTION`).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 150px
  grid-gap: 8px
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow:
      type: frame
      segment:
        color: theme:colors.card.topColor
      frame:
        bar_width: 4
        bar_height: 18
        outer_curve: 8
    text:
      label:
        content: NCC-1701-A
        position: top-center
        font_size: 14
        color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
      class:
        content: CONSTITUTION
        position: center
        font_size: 18
        color: theme:colors.ui.primary
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow:
      type: frame
      segment:
        color: theme:colors.ui.secondary
      frame:
        bar_width: 4
        bar_height: 18
        outer_curve: 8
    text:
      label:
        content: NCC-1701-C
        position: top-center
        font_size: 14
        color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
      class:
        content: AMBASSADOR
        position: center
        font_size: 18
        color: theme:colors.ui.primary
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow:
      type: frame
      segment:
        color: theme:colors.card.topColor
      frame:
        bar_width: 4
        bar_height: 18
        outer_curve: 8
    text:
      label:
        content: NCC-1701-E
        position: top-center
        font_size: 14
        color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
      class:
        content: SOVEREIGN
        position: center
        font_size: 18
        color: theme:colors.ui.primary
```

## Brackets and scopes

**Round displays framed by bracket arcs, and radar scopes (meWho's Titan.DS and Protostar screens).** They are the button's `brackets` and `radar` [components](../cards/button/components#brackets-and-radar), and both take their colours from the theme roles.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 300px
  grid-gap: 12px
  grid-template-columns: 300px 300px
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    component: brackets
    text:
      label:
        content: "88"
        show: true
        position: center
        font_size: 48
        color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    component: radar
```

# What is LCARdS?

<video class="doc-video" src="/img/lcards-banner.mp4" poster="/img/lcards-banner.webp" title="LCARdS: LCARS cards for Home Assistant. A wormhole opens in a live astrometrics scene beside the title, spins, and closes again." autoplay loop muted playsinline></video>

**LCARdS builds Star Trek LCARS-style dashboards in Home Assistant: a set of cards and services that work together as one system.** It includes buttons, elbows, sliders, charts, data grids, ship displays and more, designed to pair with the [HA-LCARS theme](https://github.com/th3jesta/ha-lcars).

## How it works

**Three layers, plus a small integration running inside Home Assistant.**

## What that gives you

**One system instead of separate cards, so the whole screen reacts together.**

- **Colours that follow state:** a button lights up when its light is on, a reading turns red past a threshold. No automations needed.
- **One look everywhere:** every card takes its colours, fonts and sizes from the same theme, so the whole screen matches.
- **Screen-wide reactions:** [rules](../core/rules/) restyle many cards at once, and [alert mode](../core/alert-mode) repaints the whole dashboard.
- **Live values anywhere:** put a sensor value, a smoothed reading or a [template](../core/templates/) in any label.
- **Motion and sound:** [animations](../core/animations) and LCARS [sounds](../core/sounds) on taps and state changes.
- **Control from automations:** [actions](../configuration/ha-actions) like `lcards.red_alert` work from scripts, automations and voice.

## Next steps

1. **[Install LCARdS](installation)**: from the Home Assistant Marketplace, then a quick setup.
2. **[Build a dashboard](building-dashboards)**: pick cards and lay out a screen.
3. **[Browse the gallery](dashboard-gallery)**: copy a complete dashboard and make it yours.
4. **[Get AI help](ai-assistance)**: let an assistant write the YAML for you.

::: info A hobby project
LCARdS is a fan-made hobby project, not a fully commissioned Starfleet product: expect the occasional tribble. If something in these docs doesn't match what you see, please [open an issue](https://github.com/snootched/lcards/issues).
:::

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/configuration/ -->

# Configuration

**The LCARdS Config Panel is the sidebar page where you set LCARdS up for the whole installation: its helpers, alert mode colours, sounds, the connection overlay, and the users and devices that have their own settings.** The integration adds it to the sidebar as **LCARdS Config**.

- Card settings live in each card's YAML or editor. The panel holds what is shared: the Home Assistant helpers LCARdS reads, and settings stored by the integration.
- Some settings can differ per user or per device (sounds, the connection overlay, theme token overrides). The panel's scope switches choose which level you are editing.
- Every tab has a **Docs** link at its top right that opens its page here.

::: tip New install?
Start with [First setup](../getting-started/installation#_3-first-setup): create the helpers, then tune alert modes and sounds.
:::

| Page | Covers |
|------|--------|
| [Persistent Helpers](./persistent-helpers) | Every helper LCARdS and HA-LCARS use, and how to create them by hand |
| [Users & Devices](./users-devices) | Device names and ids, and who has their own settings |
| [HA-LCARS Theme Profiles](./ha-lcars-theme-profiles) | The two LCARdS profiles HA-LCARS ships |
| [HA-LCARS Theme Lab](./ha-lcars-theme-lab) | Building your own HA-LCARS theme profile |
| [Alert Mode Lab](./alert-mode-lab) | How each alert mode recolours your dashboards |
| [Sound Configuration](./sounds) | Sound schemes, categories, per-event sounds, browser autoplay |
| [Home Assistant Actions](./ha-actions) | The `lcards.*` actions for automations and scripts |
| [Using browser_mod](./browser-mod) | LCARdS effects next to browser_mod popups |
| [Connectivity](./connectivity) | The overlay shown when the dashboard loses Home Assistant |

---

## Accessing the Panel

**Open LCARdS Config in the Home Assistant sidebar.** The integration registers it on install; there is nothing to add to your dashboards.

- If the entry is missing, open **Settings > Devices & services > LCARdS > Configure** and turn on **Show sidebar panel**. It appears at once, with no restart.
- The same screen sets the sidebar title and icon, the log level and preview features: see [Integration options](../getting-started/installation#integration-options).
- A link can open a tab directly: `/lcards-config?tab=theme`. The tab names are `welcome`, `helpers`, `theme`, `connectivity`, `sounds`, `users`, `packs` and `storage`.

---

## Panel Tabs

**The panel has a tab for each area.** Storage shows for Home Assistant administrators only.

### Welcome

**The first tab: a setup checklist, a guide to the other tabs, a health check of your installation and links.**

- **Get Started** lists the first steps: create the helpers, customize the alert modes in the Alert Lab, customize sounds.
- **Panel guide** describes each tab; a click on one opens it.
- **Support & system info** checks your setup and shows the LCARdS, integration, Home Assistant and frontend versions. **Report an issue** opens a pre-filled GitHub bug report for you to review (nothing is sent on its own), and **Copy support info** copies the same report.

### Helpers

**Lists every Home Assistant helper LCARdS uses, with its value and whether it exists, and creates the missing ones.**

- When any helper is missing, a banner says how many; **Create All** creates them all and gives each its default value. Each table row can also create one helper.
- The helpers are grouped into **Alert Lab Configuration**, **HA-LCARS Theme Settings** and **Sound System**. **Reset to Defaults** on a group sets its helpers back to their default values (the sound scheme choice is left alone).
- Helpers are ordinary `input_*` entities: they survive restarts and automations can read and change them. See [Persistent Helpers](./persistent-helpers).

::: tip First launch
Open the **Helpers** tab and click **Create All** before using anything else. This creates every helper LCARdS uses for alert mode, sounds and the alert colours, plus the HA-LCARS theme helpers, in one step.
:::

### Theme Studio

**The theme tools, one per tab: the two labs, the token and CSS variable browsers, and token overrides.**

- **LCARdS Alert Mode Lab**: tune how each alert mode recolours your dashboards, then save it to helpers. See [Alert Mode Lab](./alert-mode-lab).
- **HA-LCARS Theme Lab**: build your own HA-LCARS theme profile, with full palettes, LCARS chrome and state colours. See [HA-LCARS Theme Lab](./ha-lcars-theme-lab).
- **LCARdS Theme Tokens**, **LCARS CSS Variables** and **All CSS Variables** browse the active theme's tokens and the page's CSS variables: find the `theme:colors.ui.primary` path to use in card config, or the variable behind a colour.
- **Token Overrides** changes a token's value for everyone, for one user or for one device.

A card editor's **Main Engineering > Theme** tab lists the tokens that card uses and links here. See also [Alert Mode](../core/alert-mode) and [Themes](../core/themes/).

### Connectivity

**Sets up the full-screen overlay shown when a browser loses its connection to Home Assistant, so a kiosk never goes stale without anyone noticing.**

- The overlay can show styled text, any card, or the Borg assimilation, over effect layers you choose.
- It is off until you turn it on, and can be set for everyone, one user or one device.

See [Connectivity](./connectivity).

### Sounds

**Turns LCARS sounds on, picks the sound scheme and changes or mutes single events.**

- Sound categories (card interactions, UI navigation, alerts) switch groups of events on and off.
- Users and devices can have their own volume, scheme and event sounds without changing the defaults.

See [Sound Configuration](./sounds).

### Users & Devices

**Shows this browser's device name and id, and lets administrators see and tidy the users and devices that have their own settings.**

- Anyone can rename their own device here. Device names are what [targeted actions](./ha-actions#targeting) use.
- Administrators also see every user with stored settings and every registered device.

See [Users & Devices](./users-devices).

### Pack Explorer

**Browses every content pack loaded in LCARdS and what each one adds.**

- Packs are listed with their themes, style presets, components and their presets, animations, SVG assets, fonts, sounds, images and textures.
- Picking an item shows its details and, for themes, presets and SVG assets, a preview.

### Storage [advanced]

**Shows the raw key and value store the integration keeps for LCARdS settings that are not in helpers.** Visible to administrators only.

:::warning Advanced: use with caution
Editing or deleting a key here changes LCARdS settings directly, with no checks. Use it to inspect or repair stored settings.
:::

- Lists every stored key, with a JSON viewer and an editor for each value.
- Deletes one key, after a confirmation, or resets the whole store, after an explicit confirmation.
- Useful for debugging, recovering from a broken stored value, or seeing what per-user and per-device settings hold.

---

## HA-LCARS Theme Profiles

**[HA-LCARS](https://github.com/th3jesta/ha-lcars) includes two theme profiles made for LCARdS.** They map the LCARdS palette onto the HA-LCARS chrome and Home Assistant's own colour tokens, so stock Home Assistant screens, LCARdS cards and the HA-LCARS chrome share one palette, alert mode colour shifts included. Pick one as your Home Assistant theme; there is nothing to install separately. See [HA-LCARS Theme Profiles](./ha-lcars-theme-profiles).

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/configuration/alert-mode-lab.html -->

# Alert Mode Lab

**The Alert Mode Lab tunes how each alert mode recolours your dashboards, shows the result, and saves it to helpers so it lasts.** It is the first tab of **LCARdS Config > Theme Studio**.

- An alert mode turns every theme colour toward one hue and changes its saturation and lightness. Red, yellow and blue alert also pull colours into a hue band; black alert pushes dark colours darker and light ones lighter.
- Green alert is the baseline (the theme's own colours) and has nothing to tune.
- [Alert Mode](../core/alert-mode) explains what alert mode does and how to raise it.

::: tip Prerequisites
**Save to helpers** needs the Alert Mode Lab helpers. Click **Create All** in the [Helpers tab](./index.md#helpers) first.
:::

---

## Using the Lab

**Pick a mode, move the sliders, apply it to see it, then save.**

- **Alert mode** picks the mode to tune. With **Apply the mode when selected** on, choosing a mode also applies it.
- **Apply Live** applies the mode with the Lab's current values in this browser, so you can open a dashboard and look. It does not change `input_select.lcards_alert_mode` or other browsers.
- **Reset** puts the mode's sliders back to their built-in values. **Save to helpers** writes them to the mode's [helpers](./persistent-helpers#alert-mode-lab-parameters); every browser uses the saved values the next time that mode is raised.
- The right side has three views: **Live Preview** (key LCARS colours in the mode), **HSL Wheel** (how each colour moves; circles are green alert, squares the selected mode) and **Full Comparison** (every LCARS colour variable, before and after).

---

## Core Transform Parameters

**The four sliders every mode has: the hue colours turn toward, how far they turn, and how saturated and light they are.**

| Slider | Range | Description |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| **Hue Target** | 0 to 360° | The hue every colour is turned toward |
| **Hue Strength** | 0 to 1 | How far colours turn: `0` leaves hues alone, `1` turns them all the way |
| **Saturation** | 0 to 3× | Multiplies saturation: below 1 is more muted, above 1 more vivid |
| **Lightness** | 0 to 2× | Multiplies lightness: below 1 is darker, above 1 brighter |

## Hue Anchoring

**Red, yellow and blue alert also pull colours into a band of hues, so the whole palette reads as one colour family.** Colours already near the band move little; the rest are pulled in.

| Slider | Range | Description |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| **Center Hue** | 0 to 360° | Centre of the band |
| **Range** | 0 to 180° | How far the band reaches either side of the centre |
| **Pull Strength** | 0 to 1 | How strongly colours are pulled into the band |

## Contrast Enhancement

**Black alert splits colours at a lightness threshold: colours below it get darker and colours above it get lighter, which keeps text readable on a near-black screen.**

| Slider | Range | Description |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| **Threshold** | 0 to 100% | The lightness that splits dark colours from light ones |
| **Dark Multiplier** | 0 to 1 | Multiplies the lightness of colours below the threshold |
| **Light Multiplier** | 1 to 2 | Multiplies the lightness of colours above the threshold |

---

## Defaults

**The values each mode starts with: what its helpers are created with, and what LCARdS uses when they are missing.** Saturation and lightness are shown as multipliers here; the helpers store them as percentages (`1.4` is `140`).

| Mode | Hue Target | Hue Strength | Saturation | Lightness | Anchor (centre, range, strength) | Contrast (threshold, dark, light) |
|------|-----------|--------------|------------|-----------|----------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| Red | 0° | 0.8 | 1.4× | 0.9× | 0°, 60°, 0.9 | - |
| Yellow | 45° | 0.9 | 1.5× | 1.05× | 45°, 50°, 0.9 | - |
| Blue | 210° | 0.85 | 1.5× | 1.0× | 210°, 70°, 0.85 | - |
| Gray | 0° | 0 | 0× | 1.0× | - | - |
| Black | 0° | 0 | 0× | 0.7× | - | 69%, 0.6, 1.0 |

---

## Related

- [Alert Mode](../core/alert-mode): how alert mode works, how to raise it, and how cards respond
- [Persistent Helpers](./persistent-helpers#alert-mode-lab-parameters): the helper behind each slider
- [Sound Configuration](./sounds): the sound each alert mode plays

# Using LCARdS with browser_mod

**LCARdS and [browser_mod](https://github.com/thomasloven/hass-browser_mod) work side by side: LCARdS draws full-screen alerts, effects and colour changes, and browser_mod handles popups, navigation and browser sensors.** They don't get in each other's way.

- A typical pairing: browser_mod shows the popup with the buttons, LCARdS sets the mood behind it.
- Each tool has its own id for a browser: see [Pattern 3](#pattern-3-targeted-effect-on-one-device).

::: info No dependency
LCARdS works fully without browser_mod installed. Everything here is optional.
:::

---

## Integration Patterns

### Pattern 1: LCARdS effects alongside a browser_mod popup

**browser_mod shows the information and the buttons; an LCARdS screen effect darkens and tints the screen behind them.**

```yaml
actions:
  - action: browser_mod.popup
    data:
      title: Security Alert
      content:
        type: entities
        entities:
          - binary_sensor.front_door
          - binary_sensor.hallway_motion
      right_button: Acknowledge
      right_button_action:
        action: browser_mod.close_popup
  - action: lcards.trigger_effect
    data:
      duration: 10000
      layers:
        backdrop:
          preset: blur
          amount: 10px
        color:
          preset: color-tint
          color: alpha(var(--lcars-alert-red), 0.3)
        canvas:
          preset: static
          opacity: 0.25
```

---

### Pattern 2: Full LCARS alert with browser_mod acknowledgement button

**LCARdS holds the alert; browser_mod's popup clears it when someone acknowledges.**

```yaml
actions:
  - action: lcards.red_alert
  - action: browser_mod.popup
    data:
      title: CONDITION RED
      content:
        type: markdown
        content: Motion detected at **Front Entrance**. Acknowledge to clear.
      right_button: Acknowledge & Clear
      right_button_action:
        action: lcards.clear_alert
      left_button: Keep Active
      left_button_close: true
      dismissable: false
```

---

### Pattern 3: Targeted effect on one device

**Both tools can act on one browser, each by its own id.**

::: warning Independent device IDs
The LCARdS device name and browser_mod's `BrowserID` are separate. To give a tablet the same name in both, open it once with both URL parameters: `?lcards_device=kitchen-tablet&BrowserID=kitchen-tablet`.
:::

```yaml
actions:
  - action: lcards.trigger_effect
    data:
      duration: 15000
      target_device_names:
        - kitchen-tablet
      layers:
        backdrop:
          preset: blur
          amount: 8px
        color:
          preset: color-tint
          color: alpha(var(--lcars-alert-red), 0.35)
  - action: browser_mod.popup
    data:
      title: Kitchen Timer
      content: Timer expired - check the oven!
      timeout: 15000
    target:
      browser_id:
        - kitchen-tablet
```

---

### Pattern 4: browser_mod activity sensor gating an LCARdS effect

**browser_mod's sensors tell you whether a tablet is in use; play the effect only then.**

```yaml
conditions:
  - condition: state
    entity_id: binary_sensor.kitchen_tablet_browser
    state: "on"
actions:
  - action: lcards.trigger_effect
    data:
      duration: 5000
      target_device_names:
        - kitchen-tablet
      layers:
        canvas:
          preset: glitch
          intensity: 0.5
```

---

### Pattern 5: Trigger LCARdS effects from browser_mod JavaScript

**browser_mod can run LCARdS's browser console API directly, with no round trip to the server.**

- `window.lcards.screenEffect.play()` plays one effect for a while; `window.lcards.screenEffect.applySlot()` keeps one on a layer until it is cleared. See the [console API](/core/effects/screen-effects#console-api).

```yaml
action: browser_mod.javascript
data:
  code: "window.lcards?.screenEffect?.play('static', { duration: 2000, opacity: 0.4 })"
```

As a card's `tap_action` (browser_mod reads `service:` inside its own `browser_mod:` block; that is browser_mod's grammar, not a Home Assistant action):

```yaml
tap_action:
  action: fire-dom-event
  browser_mod:
    service: browser_mod.javascript
    data:
      code: "window.lcards?.screenEffect?.play('glitch', { duration: 1500 })"
```

An effect that stays until cleared:

```yaml
action: browser_mod.javascript
data:
  code: "window.lcards?.screenEffect?.applySlot('canvas', 'scanlines', { opacity: 0.2 })"
```

---

## Reference

### Service quick reference

**Which action to use for what.** The LCARdS ones are on the [Home Assistant Actions](./ha-actions) page.

| Intent | Action |
|---|---|
| Red alert everywhere | `lcards.red_alert` |
| Red alert on one device | `lcards.red_alert` with `target_device_names` |
| Screen blur, tint or canvas effect | `lcards.trigger_effect` |
| Clear screen effects | `lcards.clear_effect` |
| Clear the alert | `lcards.clear_alert` |
| A card over the whole screen | `lcards.show_portal_card` |
| A popup with buttons | `browser_mod.popup` |
| Navigate a browser | `browser_mod.navigate` |
| A toast notification | `browser_mod.notification` |
| Reload a browser | `lcards.reload` or `browser_mod.refresh` |
| Run JavaScript in a browser | `browser_mod.javascript` |
| Set a browser's Home Assistant theme | `browser_mod.set_theme` |

### Capability comparison

**What each tool can do.**

| | LCARdS | browser_mod |
|---|---|---|
| Full-screen visual overlay | Yes: backdrop, colour and canvas layers | Partly: a dialog, not a screen overlay |
| Recolouring the whole interface | Yes: alert modes shift every `--lcars-*` and `--lcards-*` colour | No |
| Backdrop filters and canvas animations | Yes | No |
| An alert state that lasts | Yes: `input_select.lcards_alert_mode` | No |
| Popup dialogs with buttons | Partly: an [alert overlay](../cards/alert-overlay/) card or [`lcards.show_portal_card`](./ha-actions#lcards-show-portal-card) can show any card | Yes |
| Browser navigation | No | Yes |
| Per-browser sensors | No | Yes: path, activity, battery, viewport and more |
| Screen on and off (Fully Kiosk) | No | Yes |
| Per-device and per-user targeting | Yes | Yes |
| Running JavaScript remotely | No | Yes: `browser_mod.javascript` |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/configuration/connectivity.html -->

# Connection Overlay

**The connection overlay covers the screen when a browser loses its connection to Home Assistant, and takes itself away when the connection is back.** On a wall tablet or kiosk you see at once that the dashboard is offline, instead of a screen quietly going stale.

- It is set up in the **Connectivity** tab of **LCARdS Config**, and is off until you turn it on.
- It can show styled text, any card, or the [Borg assimilation](/core/borg), over animated effect layers.
- Settings can be the same everywhere, or differ for one user or one device.

::: tip Try it
**Simulate Disconnect** at the bottom of the tab shows the overlay with your current settings, saved or not, while the dashboard keeps running.
:::

---

## How it works

**LCARdS watches each browser's connection to Home Assistant and shows the overlay when it drops.**

- After a drop it waits for the [disconnect tolerance](#general) (2.5 seconds by default) before showing the overlay, so short blips during a restart or a network handover pass unseen.
- When the connection is back, and has held for a second, the overlay goes. A short **Connection Restored** message can show first.
- The overlay covers everything on the page, Home Assistant's own sidebar and header included. It does not wait for the alert mode: during an alert it shows over the alert overlay, and its effect layers take the place of the alert's.

---

## Setting up

**Open LCARdS Config > Connectivity, change the settings, and click Save.**

- Nothing is live until you save. A banner says when there are unsaved changes; **Discard changes** goes back to the stored values.
- Pick the [scope](#scope-and-per-device-overrides) first (Global, User or Device): **Save** writes to that one.

---

## General

**Turns the overlay on, lets people close it, and sets how long a drop must last before it shows.**

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| **Enable connection overlay** | off | Show the overlay when the connection to Home Assistant is lost |
| **Allow user to dismiss** | on | A click on the overlay's backdrop closes it. It comes back at the next disconnect |
| **Disconnect tolerance (ms)** | `2500` | How long to wait after a drop before showing the overlay, `0` to `30000`. `0` shows it at once; 2000 to 5000 suits phones and shaky connections |

---

## Screen Overlay

**What the overlay shows when the connection is lost, and when it comes back.** The section is collapsed at first.

### Display style

**Display style picks one of three kinds of overlay.**

- **Simple text:** styled text over the effect layers. See [Simple text mode](#simple-text-mode).
- **Custom card (YAML):** any Home Assistant card, centred or placed where you like. See [Custom card mode](#custom-card-mode).
- **Resistance is Futile:** the Borg assimilation runs instead of an overlay. See [Borg mode](#borg-mode).

### Simple text mode

**Styled text, with its own font, size and colour, for the lost and the restored message.**

#### Connection Lost

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| **Message text** | `Connection Lost` | The text shown while disconnected |
| **Text colour** | `var(--error-color)` | Any CSS colour, CSS variable or theme token |
| **Font** | `Antonio` | Pick from the font list, or type a font name |
| **Size** | `42` px | Font size, `1` to `200` px |
| **Weight** | `400` | CSS font weight: `400`, `700`, `bold`, `lighter` ... |
| **Transform** | UPPERCASE | **UPPERCASE**, **Title Case** or **None** |

#### Connection Restored

**A short message when the connection is back, which goes by itself.**

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| **Show reconnect message** | on | Show the message on reconnect. Off: the overlay just goes |
| **Message text** | `Connection Established` | The text shown on reconnect |
| **Text colour** | `var(--primary-color)` | Any CSS colour, CSS variable or theme token |
| **Font**, **Size**, **Weight**, **Transform** | as for Connection Lost | Set separately from the lost message |
| **Auto-dismiss after (seconds)** | `3` | How long the message stays, `1` to `30` seconds |

The restored message shows only when the overlay itself was shown: a drop shorter than the tolerance shows neither.

### Custom card mode

**Any Home Assistant card as the disconnect screen: an LCARdS button, a picture, a markdown card, a whole stack.** Paste its YAML into the editor; it shows over the effect layers.

- Grids and stacks may need a width and height: CSS units such as `400px`, `30vw` or `auto`.

```yaml live
# A card to paste into Connection Lost Card
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: NO SIGNAL
    show: true
style:
  card:
    color:
      background: var(--lcars-alert-red)
```

#### Connection Lost Card

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| **YAML editor** | empty | The card's YAML, as in a dashboard |
| **Position** | centre | Where the card sits: one of nine places, from top left to bottom right |
| **Width** | `auto` | CSS width: `400px`, `40vw`, `auto` |
| **Height** | `auto` | CSS height: `300px`, `30vh`, `auto` |

#### Connection Restored Card

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| **YAML editor** | empty | A card shown on reconnect. Empty: the text reconnect message shows instead |
| **Show reconnect message** | on | Show the card (or text) on reconnect |
| **Auto-dismiss after (seconds)** | `3` | How long it stays, `1` to `30` seconds |

### Borg mode

**Resistance is Futile: on disconnect the [Borg assimilation](/core/borg) runs instead of an overlay, and reverses when the connection is back.** The dashboard turns Borg green, its font changes, and the assimilation intro plays over it.

- The assimilation starts once the [disconnect tolerance](#general) has passed, as the overlay does, so a short blip shows nothing. A click ends the intro; the Borg colours and effects stay until the connection returns, when the normal deassimilation plays.
- Messages, cards and the Effect Layers section are not used. Instead the mode has its own **Canvas Effect** (always the Borg intro, with its settings), **Backdrop Filter**, **Colour Tint**, **Palette Hue** and **Font Swap**.
- **Simulate Disconnect** runs the assimilation with these settings; **Simulate Reconnect** or **Clear Test** reverses it.

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| **Canvas Effect** | the Borg intro: 8 sites, 5 tendrils each, 600 px, 2 particles | The intro's settings: renderer, injection sites, tendrils, particles, colours, cube, signal corruption and overrun. See [intro.canvas](/core/borg#intro-canvas) |
| **Backdrop Filter** | `saturate` `200%` | A filter on the dashboard during the intro, or **None (disabled)** |
| **Colour Tint** | `color-tint`, a dark green | A colour over the dashboard during the intro, or **None (disabled)** |
| **Palette hue (degrees)** | `110` | The hue the dashboard colours turn toward, `0` to `359`: `0` red, `60` yellow, `110` Borg green, `180` cyan, `240` blue, `300` magenta |
| **Enable Borg font replacement** | on | Off: the dashboard keeps its font; everything else still runs |

---

## Effect Layers

**Three full-screen effect layers behind the message, each set on its own: an animated canvas, a colour overlay and a backdrop filter.** The section is collapsed at first, and is hidden in Borg mode.

| Layer | What it does | Default |
|-------|--------------|---------|
| **Canvas Effect** | An animation drawn over the page: static, pixelate, glitch, scanlines | `static` at 0.55 opacity |
| **Colour Overlay** | A colour over the page | `color-tint` with `rgba(0,0,0,0.55)` |
| **Backdrop Filter** | A CSS filter on everything behind it: blur, saturate, grayscale and more | **None (disabled)** |

### Configuring a slot

**Pick an Effect Preset for a layer; its settings appear under it.** The list holds the built-in [screen effects](/core/effects/screen-effects) and any a content pack adds. **None (disabled)** turns the layer off.

| Preset | Layer | Settings |
|--------|-------|----------|
| `static` | Canvas | Opacity, Grain Scale, Tint Color, Tint Strength |
| `pixelate` | Canvas | Pixel Size, Opacity, Light Variance, Base Lightness, Tint Color, Tint Strength |
| `glitch` | Canvas | Intensity, Max Shift, Band Height, Opacity, FPS |
| `scanlines` | Canvas | Line Height, Opacity, Scroll Speed |
| `color-tint` | Colour | Tint Color (any CSS colour; use `rgba()` for transparency) |
| `vignette` | Colour | Opacity |
| `blur` | Backdrop | Blur Amount (`8px`) |
| `saturate` | Backdrop | Amount (`200%`) |
| `grayscale` | Backdrop | Amount (`100%`) |
| `contrast` | Backdrop | Amount (`200%`) |
| `hue-rotate` | Backdrop | Angle (`180deg`) |

Mix them freely: a `grayscale` backdrop with a `color-tint` overlay and no canvas gives a washed-out, tinted page with no animation.

---

## Test Controls

**Preview the overlay with your current settings, saved or not.** The dashboard keeps running behind it; nothing is actually disconnected.

- **Simulate Disconnect** shows the overlay (and is greyed out while it shows).
- **Simulate Reconnect** plays what happens when the connection comes back, the restored message included.
- **Clear Test** removes it.

::: tip Workflow
Change a setting, click **Simulate Disconnect**, look, adjust, repeat. When it looks right, click **Save**.
:::

---

## Scope and per-device overrides

**Settings can be the same for everyone, or differ for one user or one browser.** A browser uses its device's setting first, then its user's, then the global one, then the built-in default.

```
Device  →  User  →  Global
```

| Scope | Who it applies to |
|-------|-------------------|
| **Global** | Every user and device |
| **User** | Your Home Assistant user, on any device |
| **Device** | This browser, whoever is logged in |

- Pick the scope with the switch at the top of the tab. Each setting shows a badge for where its value comes from; the clear button next to it removes the override at this scope.
- **Save (scope)** writes only the settings you changed, so the others keep coming from the scopes below.
- **Reset (scope)** removes every override stored at that scope, after a confirmation.

### Admin: editing another device or user

**Administrators can pick another user or device in the scope switch and save settings for it.** The browser it belongs to picks them up within seconds, with no reload.

- If you have the tab open on a device whose settings another administrator changes, and you have no unsaved edits, the tab refreshes itself.
- With unsaved edits, a banner says **Settings were updated from another device** with **Discard edits & refresh**; your edits stay until you choose.

### Broadcast buttons

**Two administrator buttons at the bottom act on every connected browser.**

| Button | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| **Push Live Config** | Every connected browser reads its overlay settings again, with no page reload. Use it for a device that was offline when you saved |
| **Reload All Clients** | Every connected browser reloads its page. A last resort |

---

## Upgrading: existing stored settings

**Settings saved before field-by-field saving existed may hold every field at one scope.** That is harmless: the values are right and the scopes still apply in order.

To keep only the overrides you meant at device scope:

1. Open **Connectivity**, pick the **Device** scope for that device and note which settings should differ from the user or global ones.
2. Click **Reset device** to remove all its device overrides.
3. Change and save only the settings you want to pin to the device.

Afterwards only those settings show a **device** badge.

# Home Assistant Actions

**LCARdS adds Home Assistant actions under the `lcards` domain, so automations, scripts, voice assistants and dashboard buttons can raise alerts, play effects and sounds, move an astrometrics camera and more.** They appear wherever Home Assistant lists actions: the automation and script editors, **Developer Tools > Actions**, and the REST and WebSocket APIs.

- Each action reaches every browser that has a dashboard open, or only the devices and users you [target](#targeting).
- The examples on this page are plain YAML for an automation's or script's actions (or **Developer Tools > Actions** in YAML mode): actions can't run as live cards on this site. A dashboard button runs one with `tap_action: action: perform-action`.
- Home Assistant checks every field before anything reaches a browser: a value out of range, or a missing required field, fails the action with an error.

| Group | Actions |
|-------|---------|
| [Alert Mode](#alert-mode-actions) | `lcards.set_alert_mode`, `lcards.red_alert`, `lcards.yellow_alert`, `lcards.blue_alert`, `lcards.gray_alert`, `lcards.black_alert`, `lcards.clear_alert` |
| [Screen Effects](#screen-effect-actions) | `lcards.trigger_effect`, `lcards.clear_effect` |
| [Sound](#sound-actions) | `lcards.play_sound` |
| [Astrometrics](#astrometrics-actions) | `lcards.fly_to`, `lcards.set_clock` |
| [Portal Overlay](#portal-overlay-actions) | `lcards.show_portal_card`, `lcards.clear_portal_card` |
| [Borg Assimilation](#borg-assimilation-actions) | `lcards.borg_assimilate`, `lcards.borg_deassimilate` |
| [Frontend Control](#frontend-control-actions) | `lcards.reload`, `lcards.set_log_level` |

---

## Targeting

**Four optional fields send an action to some devices or users only; without them it reaches every connected browser.** Every `lcards.*` action takes them, in any combination.

- A browser acts when its device or its user is in the lists. Device names and user names are matched in any case, and a name shared by several devices matches all of them.
- If the fields are set but match no device and no user (a typo in a name, say), the action fails with an error instead of reaching every browser. A list that matches only some of its names acts on the ones it matches.
- [Users & Devices](./users-devices) shows each browser's device name and id; `window.lcards.targeting.getMyIds()` in the browser console returns them too.

```yaml
# Red alert on the kitchen tablet only
action: lcards.red_alert
data:
  target_device_names:
    - Kitchen Tablet
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `target_device_ids` | list | every device | Browser device ids (the `lcards_device_id` each browser keeps in `localStorage`) |
| `target_device_names` | list | every device | Device display names, set in **LCARdS Config > Users & Devices** or with `?lcards_device=` |
| `target_user_ids` | list | every user | Home Assistant user ids |
| `target_user_names` | list | every user | Home Assistant user display names |

---

## Alert Mode Actions

**The alert actions change the [alert mode](../core/alert-mode): the colours, the alert sound and any [alert overlay](../cards/alert-overlay/) on the page.** Without targeting they set `input_select.lcards_alert_mode`, so every browser follows and the mode survives reloads.

- With [targeting](#targeting) the helper is not changed: only the matched browsers change their alert mode, until they reload or the helper changes.
- Without targeting the actions need the `input_select.lcards_alert_mode` helper: create it in **LCARdS Config > Helpers** (see [Persistent Helpers](./persistent-helpers#alert-mode)).

### lcards.set_alert_mode

**Sets any alert mode by name.** Use it when the mode comes from a template or a helper.

```yaml
action: lcards.set_alert_mode
data:
  mode: red_alert
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `mode` | string | required | `red_alert`, `yellow_alert`, `blue_alert`, `gray_alert`, `black_alert` or `green_alert` |
| [Targeting](#targeting) | - | every browser | `target_device_ids`, `target_device_names`, `target_user_ids`, `target_user_names` |

### Shortcut actions

**One action per alert mode, with no fields but the targeting ones.** `lcards.clear_alert` returns to normal.

| Action | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| `lcards.red_alert` | Red alert |
| `lcards.yellow_alert` | Yellow alert |
| `lcards.blue_alert` | Blue alert |
| `lcards.gray_alert` | Gray alert |
| `lcards.black_alert` | Black alert |
| `lcards.clear_alert` | Back to normal (`green_alert`) |

```yaml
action: lcards.red_alert
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| [Targeting](#targeting) | - | every browser | `target_device_ids`, `target_device_names`, `target_user_ids`, `target_user_names` |

---

## Screen Effect Actions

**Full-screen effects over the dashboard, in three independent layers: `backdrop` (a CSS filter on the page), `color` (a colour over it) and `canvas` (an animation).** [Screen Effects](/core/effects/screen-effects) describes every preset and its settings.

### lcards.trigger_effect

**Plays one or more screen effect layers, until cleared or for a set time.** Each layer in `layers` takes a `preset` and that preset's settings.

- A layer left out of `layers` keeps whatever it shows; a layer set to `null` is cleared.
- `duration` clears the layers this call set after that many milliseconds; each layer keeps its own timer, so a later call is never cut short by an earlier one. Without it the effect stays until [`lcards.clear_effect`](#lcards-clear-effect).
- An alert overlay, the connection overlay or a portal card with `layers` replaces only the layers it sets, and clears only its own when it closes, so an effect from this action on another layer keeps running.

```yaml
# A red-tinted blur, until cleared
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  layers:
    backdrop:
      preset: blur
      amount: 12px
    color:
      preset: color-tint
      color: alpha(var(--lcars-alert-red), 0.35)
```

```yaml
# TV static for 5 seconds
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  duration: 5000
  layers:
    canvas:
      preset: static
      opacity: 0.4
```

```yaml
# All three layers, on one device
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  target_device_names:
    - Kitchen Tablet
  layers:
    backdrop:
      preset: grayscale
      amount: 80%
    color:
      preset: vignette
      opacity: 0.5
    canvas:
      preset: scanlines
      opacity: 0.3
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `layers` | object | required | A map of layers: `backdrop`, `color` and `canvas`, each a `preset` with its settings, or `null` to clear it |
| `duration` | number | until cleared | Clear the layers this call sets after this many ms, at least `100` |
| [Targeting](#targeting) | - | every browser | `target_device_ids`, `target_device_names`, `target_user_ids`, `target_user_names` |

The presets for each layer, with their main settings:

| Layer | Preset | Main settings |
|-------|--------|---------------|
| `backdrop` | `blur` | `amount` (`8px`) |
| `backdrop` | `grayscale` | `amount` (`100%`) |
| `backdrop` | `saturate` | `amount` (`200%`) |
| `backdrop` | `contrast` | `amount` (`200%`) |
| `backdrop` | `hue-rotate` | `angle` (`180deg`) |
| `color` | `color-tint` | `color` |
| `color` | `vignette` | `opacity` (`0.7`) |
| `canvas` | `static` | `opacity`, `scale` |
| `canvas` | `pixelate` | `opacity`, `pixelSize` |
| `canvas` | `glitch` | `opacity`, `intensity` |
| `canvas` | `scanlines` | `opacity`, `lineHeight`, `scroll` |

### lcards.clear_effect

**Clears one screen effect layer, or all of them.**

```yaml
# Clear every layer on every browser
action: lcards.clear_effect
```

```yaml
# Clear only the backdrop layer, on one device
action: lcards.clear_effect
data:
  slot: backdrop
  target_device_names:
    - Kitchen Tablet
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `slot` | string | every layer | `backdrop`, `canvas` or `color` |
| [Targeting](#targeting) | - | every browser | `target_device_ids`, `target_device_names`, `target_user_ids`, `target_user_names` |

---

## Sound Actions

### lcards.play_sound

**Plays a sound, without changing the alert mode, the theme or the screen.** Use it for a soft chime when a kiosk tablet wakes, or a beep when a door opens.

- `event_type` plays the sound each browser has for that event (its own per-event sound, else its scheme's), and the event's [sound category](./sounds#enabling-sounds) switch applies.
- `asset_key` plays one exact sound whatever the scheme says: a sound asset key (**LCARdS Config > Sounds** lists them), a file URL such as `/local/sounds/chime.mp3`, or a `media-source://` id. Only the master switch applies.
- Give one of the two: a call with neither is refused. If both are given, `asset_key` wins. A browser whose master switch (`input_boolean.lcards_sound_enabled`) is off stays silent. [Sound Configuration](./sounds) has the schemes and the per-user and per-device settings.

```yaml
# The "notification" sound, as each browser has it set up
action: lcards.play_sound
data:
  event_type: notification
```

```yaml
# One exact sound on one tablet
action: lcards.play_sound
data:
  asset_key: lcards_default_system_ready
  target_device_names:
    - Kitchen Tablet
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `event_type` | string | - | One of the 27 event keys in [What Events Are Covered](./sounds#what-events-are-covered), such as `notification`, `card_tap` or `alert_red` |
| `asset_key` | string | - | A sound asset key, a file URL or a `media-source://` id |
| [Targeting](#targeting) | - | every browser | `target_device_ids`, `target_device_names`, `target_user_ids`, `target_user_names` |

---

## Astrometrics Actions

**Move the camera or set the clock of an [astrometrics card](/cards/astrometrics/) from an automation**, for example to show the front door on the wall panel when the doorbell rings. The card needs an `id`; every open dashboard showing that card follows, unless you target devices or users.

### lcards.fly_to

**Flies the card's camera to one of its named views or to one of its points.** Give a `view` or a `point`; with both, `point` wins, and with neither the action fails.

- From another LCARdS card on the same dashboard, the `fly-to` card action does the same without a round trip: see [Fly-to from other cards](/cards/astrometrics/data#fly-to-from-other-cards-and-automations).

```yaml
# Show the front door on every dashboard with the house map
action: lcards.fly_to
data:
  card_id: house_map
  point: front_door
```

```yaml
# The sector overview on the bridge tablet, slowly, with warp streaks
action: lcards.fly_to
data:
  card_id: galaxy
  view: sector
  duration: 4000
  warp: true
  target_device_names:
    - Bridge Tablet
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `card_id` | string | required | The astrometrics card's `id` |
| `view` | string | - | A named view of the card (`camera.views`) |
| `point` | string | - | A point id of the card; the camera flies to it as a tap on it would |
| `duration` | number | the card's `camera.fly_duration` | Flight time in ms, `0` to `60000` |
| `warp` | boolean | the view's `warp`, else the card's `camera.warp` | `true`: stars and dust streak on the way; `false`: they don't |
| [Targeting](#targeting) | - | every browser | `target_device_ids`, `target_device_names`, `target_user_ids`, `target_user_names` |

### lcards.set_clock

**Sets the card's [scene date](/cards/astrometrics/scale#the-scene-clock) and how fast it runs: where its real planets and moons are, and how they are turned.** Give a `date`, a `rate` or both (with neither the action fails); the one you leave out keeps running as it was.

- From another LCARdS card, the `set-clock` card action does the same: see [the scene clock](/cards/astrometrics/scale#the-scene-clock).

```yaml
# Show the planets on the date in a helper, held still
action: lcards.set_clock
data:
  card_id: sol
  date: "{{ states('input_datetime.lcards_test_date') }}"
  rate: 0
```

```yaml
# Back to now, running an hour a second
action: lcards.set_clock
data:
  card_id: sol
  date: now
  rate: 1 h/s
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `card_id` | string | required | The astrometrics card's `id` |
| `date` | string | keeps running | `now`, or an ISO date and time (`2026-10-30`, `2026-10-30T12:00:00Z`). A date and time helper's state works too (local time) |
| `rate` | string / number | unchanged | Days per second (`1` a day a second, `0` holds it, negative runs back), `live` for real time, or with a unit as the time slider shows it: `1 h/s`, `30 d/s`, `1 y/s` (units `s`, `min`, `h`, `d`, `w`, `mo`, `y`) |
| [Targeting](#targeting) | - | every browser | `target_device_ids`, `target_device_names`, `target_user_ids`, `target_user_names` |

---

## Portal Overlay Actions

**Show any Home Assistant card over the whole screen of the connected browsers, with screen effects behind it if you like.** The card has its own layer: it doesn't disturb an [alert overlay](../cards/alert-overlay/) or the [connection overlay](./connectivity), and they don't disturb it. For popups with buttons, see [Using browser_mod](./browser-mod).

### lcards.show_portal_card

**Shows a card in the portal overlay, until cleared, dismissed or for a set time.**

```yaml
# A light button over a blurred, darkened screen for 10 seconds
action: lcards.show_portal_card
data:
  content:
    type: custom:lcards-button
    entity: light.bridge
  position: center
  width: 360px
  duration: 10000
  layers:
    backdrop:
      preset: blur
      amount: 8px
    color:
      preset: color-tint
      color: alpha(var(--lcars-black), 0.5)
```

```yaml
# A markdown note on one device, until cleared
action: lcards.show_portal_card
data:
  content:
    type: markdown
    content: "# Alert!\nDoor opened."
  target_device_names:
    - Kitchen Tablet
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `content` | object | required | Any card config (`type: custom:lcards-button`, `type: entities` ...) |
| `layers` | object | none | Screen effect layers behind the card, as in [`lcards.trigger_effect`](#lcards-trigger-effect) |
| `position` | string | `center` | `center`, `top`, `top-left`, `top-right`, `bottom`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-right`, `left` or `right` |
| `width` | string | `auto` | CSS width of the card's box: `400px`, `40vw`, `auto` |
| `height` | string | `auto` | CSS height of the card's box: `300px`, `30vh`, `auto` |
| `duration` | number | until cleared | Close it after this many ms, at least `100` |
| `dismiss` | boolean | `true` | A click on the backdrop closes it |
| [Targeting](#targeting) | - | every browser | `target_device_ids`, `target_device_names`, `target_user_ids`, `target_user_names` |

### lcards.clear_portal_card

**Takes away the card shown by `lcards.show_portal_card`.** Alert and connection overlays stay.

```yaml
# Clear it on one device only
action: lcards.clear_portal_card
data:
  target_device_names:
    - Kitchen Tablet
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| [Targeting](#targeting) | - | every browser | `target_device_ids`, `target_device_names`, `target_user_ids`, `target_user_names` |

---

## Borg Assimilation Actions

**Start and end the [Borg assimilation](/core/borg) from automations.** It is not stored: a reload, or a browser opened later, shows the normal dashboard, so a reload also ends it. [Borg Actions](/core/borg-actions) has more examples.

### lcards.borg_assimilate

**Starts the assimilation; its fields tune the intro, the transition, the font, the sound and the effects left after the intro.** With no fields, the intro waits for a click and the default effects follow it.

- The flat intro fields (`site_count` to `overrun`) are shortcuts for `intro_layers.canvas`. When both are given, the keys in `intro_layers.canvas` win; they may be camelCase or snake_case.
- The Borg never writes `input_select.lcards_alert_mode`, targeted or not.

```yaml
# Every browser; the intro waits for a click
action: lcards.borg_assimilate
```

```yaml
# Auto-dismiss after 12 seconds, more and longer tendrils, palette and font only afterwards
action: lcards.borg_assimilate
data:
  intro_duration: 12000
  transition_style: fade_only
  site_count: 12
  tendrils_per_site: 14
  tendril_length: 900
  suppress_persistent: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `intro_duration` | number | wait for a click | End the intro after this many ms, `1000` to `60000`; a click still ends it earlier |
| `site_count` | number | `8` | Injection sites on the screen, `1` to `20` |
| `tendrils_per_site` | number | `5` | Tendrils per injection site, `1` to `20` |
| `tendril_length` | number | `600` | Longest tendril reach in pixels, `100` to `1200` |
| `particle_count` | number | `2` | Nano-probe particles per tendril, `0` to `6`; `0` turns them off |
| `renderer` | string | `auto` | `auto` or `webgl`: the WebGL intro where the browser supports it; `canvas`: the [classic intro](/core/borg#classic-intro) |
| `cube` | string | `detailed` | WebGL intro: `detailed` (solid cube with machinery), `classic` (wireframe) or `none` |
| `corruption` | number | `0.5` | WebGL intro: signal corruption strength, `0` to `1`; `0` turns it off |
| `overrun` | number | `0.65` | WebGL intro: darkness behind the assimilation front, `0` to `1` |
| `transition_style` | string | `blur_fade` | Palette transition: `blur_fade`, `flash`, `fade_only` or `off` |
| `font_swap` | boolean | `true` | `false` keeps the dashboard font; everything else still runs |
| `sound` | string | the `borg_assimilate` [sound event](/core/borg#sounds) | A file URL (`/local/sounds/borg.mp3`), a `media-source://` id or a sound asset key; `none` for silence |
| `suppress_persistent` | boolean | `false` | `true` leaves no effects after the intro. Ignored when `persistent_layers` is set |
| `intro_layers` | object | - | Layers for the intro, merged slot by slot with the defaults; see [Layers format](/core/borg#layers-format) |
| `persistent_layers` | object | - | Layers kept after the intro, replacing the defaults; `{}` keeps none. Wins over `suppress_persistent` |
| [Targeting](#targeting) | - | every browser | `target_device_ids`, `target_device_names`, `target_user_ids`, `target_user_names` |

### lcards.borg_deassimilate

**Restores the dashboard: a short glitch outro, then the normal colours, font and screen.** A browser that is not assimilated ignores it.

```yaml
# At once, with no outro
action: lcards.borg_deassimilate
data:
  with_outro: false
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `with_outro` | boolean | `true` | `false` restores at once, with no outro and no wait |
| `outro_layers` | object | glitch on `canvas` for 1200 ms | Outro layers, replacing the default. The longest `duration` in them sets the wait, at least 1200 ms |
| `revert_transition_style` | string | `fade_only` | Palette transition back to normal: `fade_only`, `flash`, `blur_fade` or `off` |
| `sound` | string | the `borg_deassimilate` [sound event](/core/borg#sounds) | A sound for this call, as for `lcards.borg_assimilate` |
| [Targeting](#targeting) | - | every browser | `target_device_ids`, `target_device_names`, `target_user_ids`, `target_user_names` |

---

## Frontend Control Actions

**Reload dashboards, or change how much LCARdS logs, from an automation.** Useful for troubleshooting and for kiosks nobody stands at.

### lcards.reload

**Reloads the page in every matched browser tab, at once.** Use it after updating LCARdS or changing a resource.

::: warning
The page reloads immediately: anyone using that dashboard loses what they were doing.
:::

```yaml
# Reload one device
action: lcards.reload
data:
  target_device_names:
    - Kitchen Tablet
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| [Targeting](#targeting) | - | every browser | `target_device_ids`, `target_device_names`, `target_user_ids`, `target_user_names` |

### lcards.set_log_level

**Changes how much LCARdS writes to the browser console and the Home Assistant log, at once and with no reload.** Use `debug` while chasing a problem, then go back to `warn`.

- The browser level changes in the matched tabs only. The Home Assistant log level is one for the whole server, so it changes whatever the targeting says.
- The level lasts until the page reloads; the integration's **Log level** option sets the lasting one (see [Integration options](../getting-started/installation#integration-options)).

```yaml
action: lcards.set_log_level
data:
  level: debug
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `level` | string | required | `off`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug` or `trace` |
| [Targeting](#targeting) | - | every browser | `target_device_ids`, `target_device_names`, `target_user_ids`, `target_user_names` |

---

## Automation Examples

### Red alert on motion

```yaml
alias: Red alert on motion
triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: binary_sensor.hallway_motion
    to: "on"
actions:
  - action: lcards.red_alert
```

### Set the alert mode from a helper

```yaml
# input_select.ship_condition is your own helper, with alert mode names as its options
alias: Alert mode from a helper
triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: input_select.ship_condition
actions:
  - action: lcards.set_alert_mode
    data:
      mode: "{{ states('input_select.ship_condition') }}"
```

### Debug logging while a dev mode switch is on

```yaml
alias: LCARdS debug on dev mode
triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: input_boolean.lcards_dev_mode
actions:
  - action: lcards.set_log_level
    data:
      level: "{{ 'debug' if is_state('input_boolean.lcards_dev_mode', 'on') else 'warn' }}"
```

### A soft chime when a kiosk tablet wakes

```yaml
alias: Tablet wake chime
triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: binary_sensor.hallway_motion
    to: "on"
actions:
  # your existing screen-wake action first
  - action: rest_command.fully_kiosk_wake_screen
  - action: lcards.play_sound
    data:
      event_type: notification
      target_device_names:
        - Kitchen Tablet
```

### Borg mode for 30 minutes

```yaml
alias: Borg mode
triggers:
  - trigger: time
    at: "20:00:00"
actions:
  - action: lcards.borg_assimilate
    data:
      intro_duration: 10000
  - delay:
      minutes: 30
  - action: lcards.borg_deassimilate
```

---

## From AI agents

**An AI agent connected to Home Assistant (through the Model Context Protocol server, a voice assistant, or the REST or WebSocket API) can drive LCARdS with the same actions.** They are ordinary `lcards.*` actions, so anything that can call a Home Assistant action can raise an alert, run a screen effect, play a sound or show a portal card.

- Every action and its fields is on this page; `services.yaml` in the integration carries the same descriptions, so agents that read the action list see them too.
- Without [targeting](#targeting) fields an action reaches every connected browser. Agents should target a device or user when the request is about one screen.
- To change what a dashboard looks like (rather than trigger something on it), an agent edits dashboard YAML instead. Point it at the [JSON Schemas and the config checker](/getting-started/ai-assistance) so it only writes keys LCARdS has.

# HA-LCARS Theme Lab

**The HA-LCARS Theme Lab builds your own theme profile for [HA-LCARS](https://github.com/th3jesta/ha-lcars), the same kind as the [LCARdS profiles](./ha-lcars-theme-profiles) HA-LCARS ships.** Start from any HA-LCARS theme, change its colours, check the result, and copy the YAML into HA-LCARS.

- **Five full palettes:** the colour roles Home Assistant's own screens use (primary, neutral, warning, danger, success), each an 11-tone scale, with separate light and dark versions if you want them.
- **Readable by design:** button text colours are checked for contrast and corrected automatically.
- **Everything else in one place:** the LCARS chrome (sidebar, header, status bars), legacy Home Assistant colours and the colour of every entity state.

::: tip Try it
Open it from the LCARdS panel: **LCARdS Config > Theme Studio > HA-LCARS Theme Lab**.
:::

![The HA-LCARS Theme Lab: the Start section with a theme to load, below the Configuration and Preview & Export switch](/img/theme-lab/start.webp)

## 1. Start from a theme

**Load a theme to start from, or paste one, and give yours a name.**

- **Load from HA-LCARS:** pick a theme. Ones installed on your Home Assistant are marked *installed*; the others are reference copies bundled with LCARdS. A good start is one of the LCARdS profiles, **LCARS Picard [LCARdS Red Accent]** or **[LCARdS Blue Accent]**.
- **Paste theme YAML:** bring in a theme you already have, including one you made here earlier.
- Give your theme a **Theme Name**. That is the name you'll pick in Home Assistant later.

## 2. Palette Seed: the five colour roles

![Palette Seed: the Primary role with its 11-tone light and dark scales, button badges and contrast notes, and the other four roles below](/img/theme-lab/palette-seed.webp)

**Each colour role (Primary, Neutral, Orange (Warning), Red (Danger), Green (Success)) gets a full scale of 11 tones, from darkest to lightest.** For each role, choose where its tones come from:

- **None:** leave it to Home Assistant's own default.
- **LCARdS Palettes:** use one of the LCARdS colour families (orange, gray, blue, green, yellow).
- **Custom:** set the tones yourself.
- **Imported:** keep the scale of the theme you loaded.

While you set the tones:

- Turn on separate **dark mode** tones for a role when light and dark mode should look different.
- The small **A**, **F**, **T** and **O** badges show which tone becomes a button's background or text (open *The A/F/T/O badges* for details).
- When a tone wouldn't be readable as button text, the lab picks a readable one on export and explains it under the role.

## 3. The other sections

**The LCARS chrome, the older Home Assistant colours, the state colours and any other variable.**

- **HA-LCARS & Legacy Home Assistant Semantic Colours:** the LCARS chrome (sidebar, header, status bars, buttons) and the older Home Assistant colour variables. Anything you leave unset keeps HA-LCARS's or Home Assistant's default.
- **Domain & State Colours:** the colour of an entity's icon in each state, per domain (lights, locks, climate and more), with a global fallback.
- **Advanced / Raw Overrides:** any other theme variable, by name.

## 4. Preview and export

**Switch to Preview & Export to check the theme in Light and Dark, then copy its YAML.** The preview shows the full palettes, a mock-up of the LCARS chrome, and real Home Assistant controls (buttons, switches, inputs) drawn with your colours.

![Preview & Export: the five palettes in dark mode with their button badges](/img/theme-lab/preview.webp)

At the bottom, **Copy YAML** copies the finished theme.

![Generated Theme YAML: the instructions and the Copy YAML button above the theme's YAML](/img/theme-lab/export.webp)

## 5. Add it to HA-LCARS

**Paste the YAML at the end of HA-LCARS's theme file and reload themes.** The theme builds on HA-LCARS's shared settings (its fonts, chrome and styling), so it goes into HA-LCARS's own theme file, as HA-LCARS's guide to [making your own colour themes](https://github.com/th3jesta/ha-lcars#make-your-own-color-themes) describes:

1. Open HA-LCARS's theme file, `lcars.yaml`, in the `themes` folder of your Home Assistant configuration.
2. Paste the YAML at the very end of the file.
3. Reload themes: **Developer tools > YAML > Themes**, or the `frontend.reload_themes` action.
4. Pick your theme in your **Profile** (or set it as the default theme).

::: warning Keep a copy of your theme
Updating HA-LCARS (for example through HACS) replaces `lcars.yaml`, and your theme with it. Keep the YAML somewhere safe and paste it back after an update. To change it later, load it again with **Paste theme YAML**.
:::

# LCARdS Theme Profiles for HA-LCARS

**[HA-LCARS](https://github.com/th3jesta/ha-lcars) includes two themes made for LCARdS: LCARS Picard [LCARdS Red Accent] and LCARS Picard [LCARdS Blue Accent].** Pick one, and Home Assistant's own screens, the HA-LCARS chrome and your LCARdS cards all share one palette.

- They use the LCARdS colour palette (the `--lcards-*` variables), which the integration provides.
- Home Assistant's core colour tokens (`--ha-color-*`), used by stock Home Assistant components, are mapped onto LCARdS palette colours, so the whole interface looks of a piece.
- Every colour points at a palette variable rather than a fixed value, so alert mode colour shifts and the switch between light and dark mode reach everything.

---

## Using a profile

**Install or update HA-LCARS, then pick one of the profiles as your theme.** There is nothing to copy into `themes.yaml`.

1. Install or update [HA-LCARS](https://github.com/th3jesta/ha-lcars): the LCARdS profiles are part of its theme file, so update it if you don't see them.
2. In Home Assistant, open your **Profile** and pick **LCARS Picard [LCARdS Red Accent]** or **LCARS Picard [LCARdS Blue Accent]** as the theme.

To make your own profile, use the [HA-LCARS Theme Lab](./ha-lcars-theme-lab) in LCARdS Config: start from one of these profiles, change its palettes, and add the result to HA-LCARS.

---

## Available Profiles

**Two profiles, differing in the accent colour Home Assistant's own buttons and controls use.**

| Profile name | Accent colour | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `LCARS Picard [LCARdS Red Accent]` | Orange and red (`--lcards-orange-*`) | Home Assistant's primary colour is the LCARdS orange family |
| `LCARS Picard [LCARdS Blue Accent]` | Blue (`--lcards-blue-*`) | Home Assistant's primary colour is the LCARdS blue family |

Both profiles have separate **light** and **dark** mode sections. They cover all 11 shades of Home Assistant's core colour tokens, and Home Assistant's `on-*`, `fill-*`, `border-*` and `surface-*` colours (the ones behind buttons, chips, form fields and dialogs).

---

## How the Colour Mapping Works

### Home Assistant Core Colour Tokens

**Home Assistant's frontend has an 11-shade scale (05 to 95) for five colour families: `primary`, `neutral`, `orange`, `red` and `green`.** Stock Home Assistant components use them.

- The profiles map each Home Assistant shade one to one onto the matching stop of the [LCARdS 11-stop palette](../core/themes/index.md#lcards-css-colour-palette).
- The LCARdS palette grew from its original 7 canon stops to 11 for exactly this, so no two Home Assistant shades have to share one colour.

The family mapping differs per profile:

| Home Assistant family | Red Accent profile | Blue Accent profile |
|---|---|---|
| `primary` | `--lcards-orange-*` | `--lcards-blue-*` |
| `neutral` | `--lcards-gray-*` | `--lcards-gray-*` |
| `orange` | `--lcards-yellow-*` | `--lcards-yellow-*` |
| `red` | `--lcards-orange-*` | `--lcards-orange-*` |
| `green` | `--lcards-green-*` | `--lcards-green-*` |

### Semantic Tokens (text-on-fill contrast)

**Both profiles also set Home Assistant's text and fill colours themselves, so button and chip text stays readable.**

- Home Assistant picks the text colour of buttons, chips and form fields (`--ha-color-on-*`) as a fixed tone of the same palette, such as "tone 40 of whatever primary is", assuming any colour a theme puts there still reads well at that tone.
- That doesn't hold equally for every hue: the LCARdS orange family has a narrower readable range of lightness than the blue one, so the Red Accent profile would otherwise get low-contrast button text.
- The profiles therefore set the whole `on-*`, `fill-*`, `border-*` and `surface-*` layer, with every text and background pair checked against WCAG contrast and corrected where Home Assistant's default would fail. See [ha-css-vars.md](../development/ha-css-vars.md#layer-2-semantic-colour-tokens) for the technical detail.

---
