# Persistent Helpers

**LCARdS keeps its shared settings in ordinary Home Assistant helpers: the alert mode, the sound switches and volume, each alert mode's colours, and the HA-LCARS sizes.** They survive restarts, show up as entities, and automations can read and change them.

- LCARdS works without them, with built-in defaults; a feature whose helper is missing simply can't be changed or saved.
- Settings that are not helpers (per-user and per-device settings, per-event sounds, the connection overlay) are kept by the integration: see [Users & Devices](./users-devices).

::: tip Create helpers from the Config Panel
Open **LCARdS Config > Helpers** and click **Create All**: every missing helper is created and given its default value. See [the Helpers tab](./index.md#helpers).
:::

---

## Helper Reference

### Alert Mode

**The alert mode itself, and how it behaves.** Shown in the Helpers tab under **Alert Lab Configuration**.

| Helper | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `input_select.lcards_alert_mode` | `input_select` | `green_alert` | The active alert mode: `green_alert`, `red_alert`, `yellow_alert`, `blue_alert`, `gray_alert` or `black_alert`. See [Alert Mode](../core/alert-mode) |
| `input_boolean.lcards_alert_mode_auto_switch` | `input_boolean` | off | On: a dashboard that opens during an alert shows it from the start. Changes to the alert mode always apply |
| `input_text.lcards_alert_message` | `input_text` | empty | A message an alert overlay can show, up to 255 characters: see [A message from a helper](../cards/alert-overlay/symbol#a-message-from-a-helper) |
| `input_select.lcards_alert_transition_style` | `input_select` | `off` | The screen transition when the alert mode changes: `off`, `blur_fade`, `fade_only`, `flash`, `color_bleed`, `flicker`, `static` or `wipe` |

### Sound

**The master sound switch, the three sound categories, the volume and the sound scheme.** Shown under **Sound System**. See [Sound Configuration](./sounds).

| Helper | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `input_boolean.lcards_sound_enabled` | `input_boolean` | off | Master switch: no LCARdS sound plays while it is off or missing |
| `input_boolean.lcards_sound_cards` | `input_boolean` | on | Card sounds: taps, holds, sliders, toggles |
| `input_boolean.lcards_sound_ui` | `input_boolean` | on | Home Assistant navigation sounds: sidebar, views, dialogs, edit mode |
| `input_boolean.lcards_sound_alerts` | `input_boolean` | on | Alert mode and system sounds |
| `input_number.lcards_sound_volume` | `input_number` | `0.5` | Volume for every sound, `0` to `1` |
| `input_select.lcards_sound_scheme` | `input_select` | `none` | The active sound scheme. Its options fill in as sound packs load |

### HA-LCARS Theme Helpers (optional)

**Sizes and switches the [HA-LCARS](https://github.com/th3jesta/ha-lcars) theme reads.** Only useful with an HA-LCARS theme. Shown under **HA-LCARS Theme Settings**.

| Helper | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `input_number.lcars_horizontal` | `input_number` | `30` | Width of the horizontal borders, `6` to `60` |
| `input_number.lcars_vertical` | `input_number` | `40` | Width of the vertical borders, `26` to `60` |
| `input_number.lcars_elbow_angle` | `input_number` | `45` | The diagonal cut angle of elbow corners, `1` to `89` degrees. Elbow segments set to **Theme Binding** follow it live |
| `input_number.lcars_menu_font` | `input_number` | `14` | Sidebar menu font size, `8` to `24` px |
| `input_boolean.lcars_sound` | `input_boolean` | off | HA-LCARS's own button and tap sounds |
| `input_boolean.lcars_texture` | `input_boolean` | off | HA-LCARS's grain pattern and backlight effect |
| `sensor.lcars_header` | template sensor | - | Text in the clock area of the HA-LCARS header. Can't be created from the panel: add the template sensor below to `configuration.yaml` |

### Alert Mode Lab Parameters

**How each alert mode recolours the dashboard: one set of `input_number` helpers per mode, named `input_number.lcards_alert_lab_<mode>_<parameter>`.** The [Alert Mode Lab](./alert-mode-lab) writes them with **Save to helpers**; **Create All** in the Helpers tab creates them first (saving fails while they are missing). Shown under **Alert Lab Configuration**.

- `<mode>` is `red`, `yellow`, `blue`, `gray` or `black`: for example `input_number.lcards_alert_lab_red_hue`.
- Saturation and lightness are stored as percentages: `140` is 1.4 times.

| Parameter | Modes | Range | Description |
|-----------|-------|-------|-------------|
| `hue` | all | `0` to `360` | The hue colours are turned toward, degrees |
| `hue_strength` | all | `0` to `1` | How far colours turn toward `hue` |
| `saturation` | all | `0` to `300` (`200` for gray and black) | Saturation, percent |
| `lightness` | all | `0` to `200` | Lightness, percent |
| `center_hue` | red, yellow, blue | `0` to `360` | Centre of the hue band colours are pulled into, degrees |
| `range` | red, yellow, blue | `0` to `180` | Half-width of that band, degrees |
| `strength` | red, yellow, blue | `0` to `1` | How strongly colours are pulled into the band |
| `threshold` | black | `0` to `100` | The lightness that splits dark colours from light ones |
| `dark_multiplier` | black | `0` to `2` | Multiplies the lightness of colours below the threshold |
| `light_multiplier` | black | `0` to `2` | Multiplies the lightness of colours above the threshold |

The defaults for each mode are on the [Alert Mode Lab](./alert-mode-lab#defaults) page.

---

## Manual YAML Setup

**You can define the helpers in `configuration.yaml` instead of creating them from the panel.** Use the same entity ids; restart Home Assistant (or reload the helpers) afterwards.

- Without an `initial` value Home Assistant starts an `input_boolean` off and an `input_number` at its minimum; the YAML below gives each helper the panel's default, so the sound categories start on and the volume at half.
- The Alert Mode Lab helpers are easiest to create with **Create All**.

### Alert Mode

```yaml
input_select:
  lcards_alert_mode:
    name: LCARdS Alert Mode
    options:
      - green_alert
      - red_alert
      - yellow_alert
      - blue_alert
      - gray_alert
      - black_alert
    initial: green_alert
    icon: mdi:alarm-light
  lcards_alert_transition_style:
    name: LCARdS Alert Transition Style
    options:
      - "off"
      - blur_fade
      - fade_only
      - flash
      - color_bleed
      - flicker
      - static
      - wipe
    initial: "off"
    icon: mdi:transition

input_boolean:
  lcards_alert_mode_auto_switch:
    name: LCARdS Auto Alert Switch
    initial: false
    icon: mdi:auto-mode

input_text:
  lcards_alert_message:
    name: LCARdS Alert Message
    max: 255
    icon: mdi:message-alert
```

### HA-LCARS Theme

```yaml
input_number:
  lcars_elbow_angle:
    name: LCARS Elbow Angle
    min: 1
    max: 89
    step: 1
    mode: slider
    unit_of_measurement: "°"
    initial: 45
    icon: mdi:angle-acute
  lcars_vertical:
    name: LCARS Vertical
    min: 26
    max: 60
    step: 1
    mode: slider
    icon: mdi:arrow-expand-vertical
  lcars_horizontal:
    name: LCARS Horizontal
    min: 6
    max: 60
    step: 1
    mode: slider
    icon: mdi:arrow-expand-horizontal
  lcars_menu_font:
    name: LCARS Menu Font
    min: 8
    max: 24
    step: 1
    mode: slider
    unit_of_measurement: "px"
    icon: mdi:format-font-size-increase

input_boolean:
  lcars_sound:
    name: LCARS Sound
    icon: mdi:volume-high
  lcars_texture:
    name: LCARS Texture
    icon: mdi:texture

template:
  - sensor:
      - name: LCARS Header
        state: >-
          {{ "LCARS " + states("sensor.time") }}
        icon: mdi:text-box
```

### Sound

```yaml
input_boolean:
  lcards_sound_enabled:
    name: LCARdS Sound Effects Enabled
    initial: false
    icon: mdi:volume-high
  lcards_sound_cards:
    name: LCARdS Card Interaction Sounds
    initial: true
    icon: mdi:gesture-tap
  lcards_sound_ui:
    name: LCARdS UI Navigation Sounds
    initial: true
    icon: mdi:navigation
  lcards_sound_alerts:
    name: LCARdS Alert & System Sounds
    initial: true
    icon: mdi:alert-circle

input_number:
  lcards_sound_volume:
    name: LCARdS Sound Volume
    min: 0
    max: 1
    step: 0.05
    initial: 0.5
    mode: slider
    icon: mdi:volume-medium

input_select:
  lcards_sound_scheme:
    name: LCARdS Sound Scheme
    options:
      - none
    icon: mdi:music-box-multiple
```

LCARdS adds the installed schemes to `lcards_sound_scheme`'s options by itself, so the list needs no editing when you add a sound pack.

---

## Using Helpers in Automations

**Because LCARdS reads these helpers live, any automation can change LCARdS, and any automation can react to it.**

- Changing `input_select.lcards_alert_mode` is the same as calling [`lcards.set_alert_mode`](./ha-actions#lcards-set-alert-mode); the `lcards.*` alert actions also work on single devices.
- See [Alert Mode](../core/alert-mode) for everything that happens when the alert mode changes.

```yaml
# Raise red alert from an automation
actions:
  - action: input_select.select_option
    target:
      entity_id: input_select.lcards_alert_mode
    data:
      option: red_alert
```

```yaml
# Run something when red alert starts
triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: input_select.lcards_alert_mode
    to: red_alert
```

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/configuration/sounds.html -->

# Sound Configuration

**LCARdS can play LCARS sounds when you tap cards, move around Home Assistant, open dialogs and change the alert mode.** The **Sounds** tab of **LCARdS Config** turns them on, picks the sound scheme and changes single events.

- Sounds are off until you create the sound helpers and turn on the master switch.
- A new installation's scheme is **None (silent)**: pick **lcards_default** (or another scheme) in **Sound Scheme** to hear the built-in sounds.
- A card can mute itself or play other sounds: see [Card Sounds](../core/sounds).

---

## Setup

**Create the sound helpers once: LCARdS Config > Helpers > Create All.** They hold the master switch, the three category switches, the volume and the scheme. See [Persistent Helpers](./persistent-helpers#sound).

## Enabling Sounds

**No sound plays until `input_boolean.lcards_sound_enabled` is on.** Turn it on with **Sound effects enabled** in the Sounds tab's **Master Controls**, from a dashboard, or from an automation.

- **Volume** sets the volume of every sound, `0` to `1` (default `0.5`). There is no volume per event.
- **Sound Categories** switch groups of events: **Card interaction sounds** (`lcards_sound_cards`), **UI navigation sounds** (`lcards_sound_ui`) and **Alert and system sounds** (`lcards_sound_alerts`). They are on by default, and a missing category helper counts as on.
- The category switches are the same for everyone; the master switch, volume and scheme can also be set per user or device (see [below](#per-user-per-device-overrides)).

## Sound Schemes

**A scheme gives every event its sound.** Pick it in the Sounds tab's **Sound Scheme** section, or set `input_select.lcards_sound_scheme`. **Preview** plays a sample.

- **lcards_default** is built in and covers every event with LCARS beeps and tones, except **Slider Value Change** (silent, so dragging a slider doesn't beep on every step) and the two Borg events. Sound packs add more schemes; the helper's options update by themselves.
- **None (silent)** is an empty scheme: nothing plays except the events you give a sound below. To turn every sound off, use the master switch instead.
- **Save as new scheme…** (under Per-Event Overrides) saves the current per-event sounds as a scheme of your own, listed as *name (custom)*. With a custom scheme active, per-event edits change that scheme directly; **Delete** removes it permanently.

## Per-Event Overrides

**Give any single event another sound, or mute it, whatever the scheme says.** Open **Per-Event Overrides** inside the Sound Scheme section and pick a sound for the event.

- Each event offers **(Use scheme default)**, **Mute this event**, **Browse Home Assistant Media…** (a sound from the media library) and every sound asset from the loaded packs. The play button next to it previews the result.
- Click **Save** to keep your changes, or **Discard**. **Reset to scheme defaults** clears every override at once.
- Overrides made here are global: they apply to every user and device that has no override of its own. They are stored by the integration (see the Storage tab), not in helpers.

---

## Per-User / Per-Device Overrides

**Your own sound settings, for your Home Assistant user on any device, or for this one browser, without changing everyone else's.** The section is at the bottom of the Sounds tab.

### Scope selector

**The User and Device switches choose which one you are editing.**

- **User:** applies to your Home Assistant user on every device.
- **Device:** applies to this browser, whoever is logged in.
- Each setting shows where its current value comes from; the clear button next to an override removes it, and the next level takes over.

### What can be overridden per-user / per-device

| Setting | User | Device |
|---------|------|--------|
| Sound effects enabled | yes | yes |
| Volume | yes | yes |
| Sound scheme | yes | yes |
| Per-event overrides | yes | yes |
| Sound categories | no | no |

### Resolution order

**Each setting takes the first value it finds, in this order.**

```
Card sounds → Device → User → Global → Scheme
```

| Level | What it is |
|-------|------------|
| **Card sounds** | A card's own [`sounds`](../core/sounds) block, for that card's events only |
| **Device** | Set in the Device scope for this browser |
| **User** | Set in the User scope for your Home Assistant user |
| **Global** | The helpers and the global per-event overrides |
| **Scheme** | The active scheme's sound for the event |

### Admin: editing other users / devices

**Home Assistant administrators can edit another user's or device's settings.** **Edit as admin** in each scope lists the users or devices; pick one to see and change its overrides. The change applies the next time that user or device plays a sound.

---

## What Events Are Covered

**Every event that can play a sound, with the key that card `sounds` blocks and [`lcards.play_sound`](./ha-actions#lcards-play-sound) use.**

### Card Interactions

| Event | Key | When |
|-------|-----|------|
| Card Tap | `card_tap` | A tap on an LCARdS card, or a click on a standard Home Assistant card |
| Card Hold | `card_hold` | A hold action |
| Card Double-Tap | `card_double_tap` | A double-tap action |
| Card Hover (Desktop) | `card_hover` | The mouse pointer moving onto a card |
| Toggle → On / Off | `toggle_on`, `toggle_off` | A toggle action turning an entity on or off |
| Slider Grab / Release | `slider_drag_start`, `slider_drag_end` | Grabbing or letting go of a slider |
| Slider Value Change | `slider_change` | Each step while a slider moves |
| More Info Open | `more_info_open` | A more-info dialog opening |

### Home Assistant UI Navigation

| Event | Key | When |
|-------|-----|------|
| Sidebar Menu Expand / Collapse | `menu_expand` | The sidebar menu button |
| Page / View Navigation | `nav_page` | Moving between views and sidebar pages |
| Dialog Open | `dialog_open` | Any Home Assistant dialog opening |
| Dialog Close | `dialog_close` | Any Home Assistant dialog closing |
| Dashboard Edit Start | `dashboard_edit_start` | Entering dashboard edit mode |
| Dashboard Edit Save / Done | `dashboard_edit_save` | Leaving dashboard edit mode |

### Alerts & System

| Event | Key | When |
|-------|-----|------|
| Red Alert | `alert_red` | The alert mode changes to `red_alert` |
| Yellow Alert | `alert_yellow` | The alert mode changes to `yellow_alert` |
| Blue Alert | `alert_blue` | The alert mode changes to `blue_alert` |
| Gray Alert | `alert_gray` | The alert mode changes to `gray_alert` |
| Black Alert | `alert_black` | The alert mode changes to `black_alert` |
| Alert Cleared (Green Alert) | `alert_clear` | The alert mode returns to `green_alert` |
| System Ready | `system_ready` | LCARdS has finished starting |
| System Error | `error` | LCARdS fails to start |
| Notification | `notification` | A Home Assistant notification appears |
| Borg assimilation | `borg_assimilate` | The [Borg assimilation](/core/borg#sounds) starts (silent until you give it a sound) |
| Borg deassimilation | `borg_deassimilate` | The Borg deassimilation starts (silent until you give it a sound) |

---

## Triggering from Automations

**[`lcards.play_sound`](./ha-actions#lcards-play-sound) plays a sound from an automation**, for example a soft chime when a kiosk tablet wakes, without changing the alert mode or the screen.

- With `event_type` it plays that event's sound as the browser has it set up (its overrides and scheme), and that event's category switch applies.
- With `asset_key` it plays one exact sound: an asset key, a file URL such as `/local/sounds/chime.mp3` (a file in the `www` folder of your Home Assistant configuration) or a `media-source://` id. Only the master switch applies.
- Like the other `lcards.*` actions, it can [target](./ha-actions#targeting) devices or users.

```yaml
action: lcards.play_sound
data:
  event_type: notification
```

---

## Browser Audio Policy

**Browsers block sound until you have clicked, tapped or pressed a key on the page.** For almost every LCARdS sound that is no trouble: your first tap is the interaction, and sounds play from then on.

The **System Ready** sound is the exception: it plays as soon as LCARdS has started, before you have touched the page, so the browser blocks it unless your Home Assistant address may play sound on its own. The Sounds tab shows the same notice with a link here.

:::: tabs
=== Chrome / Edge

1. Open **Settings > Privacy and security > Site settings > Additional content settings > Sound**.
2. Under **Allowed to play sound**, click **Add** and enter your Home Assistant address (for example `http://homeassistant.local:8123`).
3. Hard-refresh your dashboard: the startup sound now plays on page load.

Or click the site icon at the left of the address bar on your Home Assistant page, open **Site settings** and set **Sound** to **Allow**.

=== Firefox

1. Open **Settings > Privacy & Security**, scroll to **Permissions**, and click **Settings...** next to **Autoplay**.
2. Enter your Home Assistant address, set it to **Allow Audio and Video** and click **Save Changes**.
3. Hard-refresh your dashboard.

Or, when Firefox shows the autoplay-blocked icon in the address bar, click it and choose **Allow Audio and Video**.

::::

::: tip
If you don't use the System Ready sound, no browser change is needed.
:::

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/configuration/users-devices.html -->

# Users & Devices

**The Users & Devices tab of LCARdS Config shows who this browser is to LCARdS, and lets administrators see and tidy every user and device that has its own settings.**

- Every browser gets a device record: a stable id and a display name. Device names are what [targeted actions](./ha-actions#targeting) and per-device settings use.
- Everyone sees **This Session**. Home Assistant administrators also see **Users with Scoped Settings** and **Registered Devices**.
- The settings themselves are changed in their own tabs (Sounds, Connectivity, Theme Studio > Token Overrides); this tab manages the records.

---

## This Session

**Your logged-in user and this browser's device record.** Use it to name the browser, or to find its id for an action.

- Click the pencil next to **Display Name** to rename this device; Enter saves.
- A new device is named after its browser and system (`Chrome-Android`, `Safari-iPhone`) until you rename it.
- A device can be named from its address: add `?lcards_device=<name>`, for example `http://homeassistant.local:8123/?lcards_device=Kitchen%20Tablet`. The name applies on every load with it, over a name set before. Handy for kiosk bookmarks.
- `window.lcards.targeting.getMyIds()` in the browser console returns this device's id and your user id.

| Detail | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Logged-in User** | Your Home Assistant user's name |
| **User ID** | Your Home Assistant user id, as `target_user_ids` takes it |
| **Device ID** | A stable id kept in this browser's `localStorage` (`lcards_device_id`). It survives reloads and logins in the same browser profile; clearing the site's data gives a new one |
| **Display Name** | The name for this browser. Editable by any user |
| **Last Seen** | When this device last checked in with the integration |
| **User Agent** | The browser and system string recorded for it |

---

## Users with Scoped Settings

**Administrators only: every Home Assistant user with at least one setting of their own.**

- Each row shows the user's name (from Home Assistant), their id and the stored keys.
- **Clear all overrides for this user** deletes that user's own settings after a confirmation; they then get the device or global values. Device records and global settings are not touched.

---

## Registered Devices

**Administrators only: every browser that has registered with the integration, with its name, id and last check-in.**

- **Rename device** edits the display name in place.
- **Remove device record** deletes the record and the settings stored for that device, after a confirmation. A browser that opens Home Assistant again registers again, with the same id.

---

## How scoped settings work

**A setting that can differ per user or device takes the first value it finds: the device's, then the user's, then the global one.**

```
Device  →  User  →  Global  →  Built-in default (or the helper)
```

- **Device** settings apply to whoever is logged in on that browser.
- **User** settings apply to one Home Assistant user on every device.
- **Global** is the installation-wide value everyone shares.
- Today these settings can be scoped: [sounds](./sounds#per-user-per-device-overrides) (master switch, volume, scheme and per-event sounds), the [connection overlay](./connectivity#scope-and-per-device-overrides), and theme token overrides (Theme Studio > Token Overrides).

---

- [Home Assistant Actions: targeting](./ha-actions#targeting): send an `lcards.*` action to some devices or users only

- [Connectivity](./connectivity): per-user and per-device connection overlay settings
- [Scoped Settings Service](../architecture/subsystems/scoped-settings): developer reference for the storage behind this tab

All standard LCARS buttons, plus advanced multi-segment controls.

Classic LCARS corner designs.

![Elbow Card](/img/lcards-elbow.png)

Interactive sliders for display and control.

![Slider Card](/img/lcards-slider.gif)

- Horizontal and vertical orientations with independent fill and control inversion

- Fully customizable layout with CSS grid

# Alert Overlay Card

`custom:lcards-alert-overlay`

**The alert overlay shows the alert symbol over the whole screen while an alert mode is raised, and hides it when the alert clears.** It follows the `input_select.lcards_alert_mode` helper, so one automation or button raises the alert on every dashboard that has the card.

<video class="doc-video" src="/gallery/alert.webm" poster="/img/cards/alert-overlay.webp" title="Alert overlay: red alert covers a dashboard with a blurred backdrop and the red alert symbol, then yellow alert with the yellow one" autoplay loop muted playsinline></video>

- Add one alert overlay to every dashboard that should show alerts. It takes no room on the dashboard; in edit mode it shows an info box so you can find it.
- The overlay draws in a layer over the whole page, not in its grid cell, so where you put the card doesn't change where the alert shows.
- Each condition (red, yellow, blue, black, gray) shows the symbol in its own colours by default.
- The overlay covers the whole screen, so the live examples on these pages show it as the [Alert Studio](#alert-studio) does: on a mock screen with a stand-in dashboard behind it, one condition at a time.

::: tip Try it
The card editor's **Open Alert Studio** button opens a studio with a mock screen that shows each condition as it will look, without raising an alert. See [Alert Studio](#alert-studio).
:::

| Page | Covers |
|------|--------|
| [Position and Screen Effects](./overlay) | Where the symbol sits, its size, and the blur, tint and canvas effects behind it |
| [Alert Band](./band) | `display: band`: a row of dashes across the screen that leaves the dashboard usable |
| [Symbol and Content](./symbol) | Changing the symbol's text and colours, a message from a helper, or your own card |
| [Per-Condition Settings](./conditions) | Different settings for red, yellow, blue, black and gray alert |
| [Raising and Dismissing](./raising) | The `lcards.*` actions, tap to dismiss or reset, timers, and transition effects |

---

## Prerequisites

**The card needs the `input_select.lcards_alert_mode` helper.** Create it from the LCARdS Config Panel, or by hand with the options `green_alert`, `red_alert`, `yellow_alert`, `blue_alert`, `black_alert` and `gray_alert` (see [Helpers](/configuration/persistent-helpers)).

- The optional `input_select.lcards_alert_transition_style` helper adds a screen transition whenever the alert mode changes; see [Transition effects](./raising#transition-effects). It can also be created from the Config Panel.

## Quick start

**The card works with no settings: each alert shows the LCARS alert symbol in that condition's colours, with its animation, over an 8px blur.** The symbol is sized to 60% of the screen's width and 50% of its height, so it fits wide, tall and phone screens alike.

```yaml live
# Add this to every dashboard that should react to alert modes
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
```

## Placement

**Put the card anywhere in the view; the end of the view keeps it out of the way.** When an alert is up, the card shows it in a layer attached to the page rather than in its card slot, so it always covers the full screen.

```yaml
views:
  - cards:
      - type: custom:lcards-button
        # ... your other cards ...
      - type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay # the last card in the view
        dismiss_mode: reset
```

## Alert Studio

**The Alert Studio is where the alert overlay is set up: the card editor's Open Alert Studio button opens it.** The card editor itself has only that button, the Docs link and the YAML tab.

- The settings are on the left (Config, Backdrop, Conditions, YAML); on the right a mock screen shows the condition picked in the toolbar above it, or on the Conditions tab.
- The mock screen is laid out at your screen's size and scaled down, so sizes in %, px, `vw` and `vh` look as they will on the dashboard. It shows the screen effect layers, the symbol (or your content card) at its position and size, or the alert band.
- Settings that don't apply are hidden: overlay position and size for a condition shown as a band, and the band settings when no condition uses one.

::: details More about the Alert Studio
- **Only a preview:** the alert mode doesn't change and nothing shows on your dashboards. Click the backdrop (overlay) or the symbol (band) to try a dismiss, and **Replay** to show it again.
- **The symbol:** on the Config tab, **Alert symbol** changes the symbol for every condition. On the Conditions tab each condition picks **Alert symbol** (as it is), **Customise the symbol** (the symbol's own button editor, saving only what you change) or **Your own card** (any card, edited in place with its own editor). See [Symbol and Content](./symbol).
- **Guides:** the info guides (How the overlay works, How the band works, How condition overrides work) explain the settings with a diagram each.
- **Saving:** Save keeps the changes; Cancel leaves the card as it was.
:::

## Limitations

**One alert overlay is active per dashboard, and the card is not a normal LCARdS card.**

- Only the first instance on the page becomes active. Any others have no visual presence, and in edit mode they show a "Duplicate · inactive" warning; remove them. The preview in the card editor is not a duplicate: it shows a plain info box.
- While the dashboard is in edit mode the overlay stays hidden. An alert raised meanwhile shows when you leave edit mode, and its auto-dismiss countdown starts then.
- The rules engine can't target the overlay: it has no card id or tags. An `lcards-*` content card inside it does support rules.
- `band.phase` locks to the built-in symbol's bar sweep. With `band.emblem: false` or a custom `content` card there is nothing to lock to, and the band runs on its own.

## Card options

**The keys set on the card apply to every condition; [`conditions`](./conditions) changes them for one.**

- The card has none of the [common card options](/cards/common): no `height` or `width` for its grid cell, `id`, `tags`, `grid_options`, actions, text fields or animations. It sits in the grid as an empty element, and its `width` and `height` size the symbol on the screen.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
dismiss_mode: reset # a tap clears the alert everywhere
width: 50%
layers:
  backdrop:
    preset: blur
    amount: 12px
conditions:
  yellow_alert:
    display: band # a band across the screen; taps reach the dashboard
```

::: details More about the card options
- **From the card picker:** a card added from the picker starts with `dismiss_mode: dismiss`, `width: 50%`, `height: 33%`, `position: center` and an 8px blur, rather than the defaults below.
- **Older configs:** a card-level `backdrop` (`blur`, `opacity`, `color`) from older versions is still read when `layers` is not set; see [Layers](./overlay#layers).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `type` | string | required | `custom:lcards-alert-overlay` |
| `dismiss_mode` | string | `dismiss` | What a dismiss does: `dismiss`, `reset`, `auto-dismiss` or `auto-reset`. See [Dismiss](./raising#dismiss) |
| `auto_dismiss_seconds` | number | - | Seconds before an `auto-dismiss` or `auto-reset` hides the alert, at least 1 |
| `display` | string | `overlay` | `overlay`: the symbol over a backdrop, the dashboard blocked until dismissed. `band`: see [Alert Band](./band) |
| `band` | object | - | Band settings for `display: band`; see [Alert Band](./band) |
| `position` | string | `center` | Where the symbol sits on the screen; see [Position](./overlay#position) |
| `width` | string | `60%` | Symbol width (CSS length; % is of the screen) |
| `height` | string | `50%` for the symbol, else `auto` | Symbol height (CSS length); see [Size](./overlay#size) |
| `alert_button` | object | - | Changes to the built-in symbol for every condition; see [alert_button](./symbol#alert-button) |
| `layers` | object | an 8px blur | Screen effects behind the symbol; see [Layers](./overlay#layers) |
| `conditions` | object | - | Settings for one condition; see [Per-Condition Settings](./conditions) |

> **Using LCARdS with browser_mod?** See [Using LCARdS with browser_mod](/configuration/browser-mod), including patterns for stacking browser_mod popups with LCARdS screen effects, combined targeting, and driving LCARdS effects from browser_mod JavaScript.

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/alert-overlay/band.html -->

# Alert Band

`display: band` shows the alert the way the Titan.DS screens do: a row of short dashes in the condition colour across the whole screen, with the alert symbol in the middle.

## band

**`display: band` shows the alert as a band across the screen instead of a backdrop, so the dashboard stays readable and usable while the alert is on.** Pair it with an alert-aware theme so the rest of the screen changes colour too.

- Clicks reach the cards under the band. Clicking the symbol (or Enter or Space on it) dismisses the band, following `dismiss_mode`.
- The symbol is the same alert button as the overlay's, so [`alert_button`](./symbol#alert-button) changes and a [content card](./symbol#content-cards) apply here too.
- Backdrop [layers](./overlay#layers) are off in band mode unless you set them.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
display: band
dismiss_mode: reset
band:
  position: 70% # band centre at 70% of the screen height
  height: 48px
  emblem_scale: 3 # the symbol three times the band height
```

::: details More about the band
- **On screen:** `top` and `bottom` keep the symbol 16px from the edge, and a percentage is held so the symbol (or the dashes at their tallest) stays on screen.
- **Without the symbol:** with `emblem: false` there is nothing to click, so only auto-dismiss or the alert mode changing hides the band.
- **A content card** sits in a box the shape of the alert symbol (about 1.36 wide for 1 high), `emblem_scale` times the band height.
- **Colour:** the dashes take the condition's alert colour from the theme (`colors.alert.red` and so on). A `color` you set may be a theme token or a CSS variable, so it follows alert mode palette changes.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `display` | string | `overlay` | `band` to show the band |
| `band.position` | string | `center` | `top`, `center`, `bottom`, or a percentage of the screen height for the band's centre (`75%`) |
| `band.height` | string | `clamp(24px, 4vh, 64px)` | Dash height (CSS length) |
| `band.emblem` | boolean | `true` | The alert symbol (or the content card) in the middle |
| `band.emblem_scale` | number | `4` | Symbol height as a multiple of the band height, 1 to 10 |
| `band.color` | colour | the condition colour | Dash colour |

## Dashes

**The dash keys set the width, spacing and corners of the dashes.** Dashes run outward from the symbol to both screen edges, so the spacing sets how many there are.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
display: band
band:
  dash_width: 12
  dash_gap: 8
  dash_radius: pill # rounded ends
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `band.dash_width` | number | `8` | Dash width in px, at least 1 |
| `band.dash_gap` | number | `12` | Space between dashes in px |
| `band.dash_radius` | number or `pill` | `0` | Corner radius in px, at most half the dash width or height; `pill` rounds the ends fully |

## Animation

**The band's animation runs a flash along the dashes, or pulses them all together, and can swell them as it passes.** The device's reduced motion setting turns it off.

- `sweep` runs a flash outward from the symbol (or inward from the screen edges with `direction: inward`); `flash` pulses every dash together; `none` keeps the band still.
- `speed` also sets the symbol's bar sweep, so the two keep step, unless `alert_button.speed` sets the symbol's own speed.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
display: band
band:
  animation: sweep
  direction: inward
  speed: 1.5 # 1.5 times as fast, the symbol's bars too
  grow: 1.6 # dashes swell as the sweep passes
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `band.animation` | string | `sweep` | `sweep`, `flash` or `none` |
| `band.direction` | string | `outward` | Sweep direction: `outward` from the symbol, or `inward` from the screen edges |
| `band.speed` | number | `1` | Speed multiplier, 0.25 to 4 (`2` is twice as fast, `0.5` half speed) |
| `band.grow` | number | `1` | Peak dash height as a multiple of the band height, 1 to 4: the dashes swell as the sweep passes, or all together with `flash`. `1` is no growth |

## band.phase

**`phase` locks the band's animation to the symbol's bar sweep, so the two read as one movement.** The symbol's bars light from the outside in, reaching the middle at 150 degrees; at `180` an outward sweep starts as the symbol's finishes, so it runs from the core out to the edges like a warp core.

- It needs the built-in symbol and the same speed for both: leave `alert_button.speed` unset. With `emblem: false` or a custom `content` card there is nothing to lock to, and the band runs on its own.

```yaml live
# A warp-core band across the lower third; red alert takes the whole screen instead
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
display: band
dismiss_mode: reset
band:
  position: 70%
  dash_radius: pill
  grow: 1.6
  phase: 180
  speed: 0.75
conditions:
  red_alert:
    display: overlay
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `band.phase` | number | - | Degrees after the symbol's bar sweep, 0 to 360. Unset: not locked. No effect with `animation: none` |

## Per-condition band

**`display` and `band` can be set per condition, so one alert takes the whole screen while the others show a band.** A condition's `band` is merged over the card's, key by key.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
display: band
conditions:
  red_alert:
    display: overlay # red alert still takes over the screen
  yellow_alert:
    band:
      animation: flash
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `conditions.<key>.display` | string | the card's `display` | `overlay` or `band` for this condition |
| `conditions.<key>.band` | object | the card's `band` | Band keys for this condition, over the card's |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/alert-overlay/conditions.html -->

# Per-Condition Settings

`conditions` gives one alert condition its own settings: its own message, effects, size or display.

## Condition keys

**Under `conditions`, each alert condition (`red_alert`, `yellow_alert`, `blue_alert`, `black_alert`, `gray_alert`) can override any of the card's settings for that alert.** All keys are optional: set only what you want to change.

- A condition you leave out, or list with no keys, uses the card's settings and the built-in symbol in its own colours.
- `dismiss_mode` is set on the card only; a condition can change only its `auto_dismiss_seconds`.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
dismiss_mode: auto-reset
auto_dismiss_seconds: 60
conditions:
  red_alert:
    auto_dismiss_seconds: 15 # red alerts time out faster
    position: center
    width: 500px
    alert_button:
      text:
        sub_text:
          content: CONDITION RED - ALL HANDS TO BATTLE STATIONS
  yellow_alert:
    display: band
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `content` | object | - | A card to show instead of the symbol; overrides `alert_button` entirely. See [Content cards](./symbol#content-cards) |
| `alert_button` | object | - | Changes to the symbol, merged over the card's `alert_button`. Ignored when `content` is set. See [alert_button](./symbol#alert-button) |
| `layers` | object | the card's `layers` | Effect slots for this condition, over the card's; see [Layers per condition](#layers-per-condition) |
| `display` | string | the card's `display` | `overlay` or `band` for this condition; see [Alert Band](./band#per-condition-band) |
| `band` | object | the card's `band` | Band keys, merged over the card's `band` |
| `position` | string | the card's `position` | Where the symbol sits; see [Position](./overlay#position) |
| `width` | string | the card's `width` | Symbol or content width. SVG component cards (such as the built-in symbol) take their height from it |
| `height` | string | the card's `height` | Height, for a content card that can't size itself from its width |
| `auto_dismiss_seconds` | number | the card's value | Timeout for this condition, at least 1. Only used when the card's `dismiss_mode` is `auto-dismiss` or `auto-reset` |

## Layers per condition

**A condition's `layers` changes only the slots it lists; the others come from the card's `layers`.** Set a slot to `null` to turn it off for that condition.

- **Older configs:** a condition's own `backdrop` (`blur`, `opacity`, `color`, from older versions) sets that condition's `backdrop` and `color` slots, read as the card-level one is ([Layers](./overlay#layers)); its `canvas` still comes from the card. Slots in the condition's `layers` win over it, and the Alert Studio converts it to `layers` when you change a layer.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
layers:
  backdrop:
    preset: blur
    amount: 8px
  canvas:
    preset: scanlines
conditions:
  red_alert:
    layers:
      # a red tint on top of the card's blur
      color:
        preset: color-tint
        color: alpha(theme:colors.alert.red, 0.35)
      # no scanlines for red alert
      canvas: null
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `layers.backdrop` | object or `null` | the card's | The [backdrop filter](./overlay#layers-backdrop) for this condition |
| `layers.color` | object or `null` | the card's | The [colour layer](./overlay#layers-color) for this condition |
| `layers.canvas` | object or `null` | the card's | The [canvas animation](./overlay#layers-canvas) for this condition |

## Putting it together

**A full setup: a blur and dark tint for every condition, and red, yellow and black alert each with their own message, width and effects.**

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
dismiss_mode: reset
position: center
layers:
  backdrop:
    preset: blur
    amount: 8px
  color:
    preset: color-tint
    color: alpha(var(--primary-background-color), 0.5)
conditions:
  # red: a heavier blur and a red tint
  red_alert:
    width: 500px
    layers:
      backdrop:
        preset: blur
        amount: 16px
      color:
        preset: color-tint
        color: alpha(theme:colors.alert.red, 0.35)
    content:
      type: custom:lcards-button
      component: alert
      preset: condition_red
      text:
        alert_text:
          content: ALERT
        sub_text:
          content: CONDITION RED - ALL HANDS TO BATTLE STATIONS
  # yellow: the card's blur, a yellow tint
  yellow_alert:
    width: 500px
    layers:
      color:
        preset: color-tint
        color: alpha(theme:colors.alert.yellow, 0.3)
    content:
      type: custom:lcards-button
      component: alert
      preset: condition_yellow
      text:
        alert_text:
          content: ALERT
        sub_text:
          content: CONDITION YELLOW
  # black: a heavy blur, nearly dark
  black_alert:
    width: 500px
    layers:
      backdrop:
        preset: blur
        amount: 20px
      color:
        preset: color-tint
        color: alpha(var(--primary-background-color), 0.7)
    content:
      type: custom:lcards-button
      component: alert
      preset: condition_black
      text:
        alert_text:
          content: ALERT
        sub_text:
          content: CONDITION BLACK - SILENT RUNNING
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| [Condition keys](#condition-keys) | | | `content`, `alert_button`, `layers`, `display`, `band`, `position`, `width`, `height`, `auto_dismiss_seconds` |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/alert-overlay/overlay.html -->

# Position and Screen Effects

Where the alert symbol sits on the screen, how big it is, and the effects drawn over the dashboard behind it. These settings apply to `display: overlay`; the [band](./band) has its own.

## Position

**`position` places the symbol (or your content card) on the screen: in the middle, along an edge or in a corner.** A corner keeps the middle of the dashboard in view while the alert is up.

- The backdrop still covers the whole screen wherever the symbol sits, and a tap anywhere outside the symbol's box (its `width` by `height`) dismisses the alert ([Dismiss](./raising#dismiss)).

```yaml live
# A small notification in the top right corner
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
position: top-right
width: 380px
conditions:
  red_alert:
    content:
      type: custom:lcards-button
      preset: lozenge
      text:
        name:
          content: RED ALERT
          show: true
      style:
        card:
          color:
            background:
              default: var(--lcards-orange-dark)
```

| Value | Where |
|-------|-------|
| `center` | In the middle of the screen (the default) |
| `top`, `top-center` | Centred, at the top |
| `bottom`, `bottom-center` | Centred, at the bottom |
| `left`, `left-center`, `center-left` | Centred top to bottom, at the left edge |
| `right`, `right-center`, `center-right` | Centred top to bottom, at the right edge |
| `top-left`, `top-right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-right` | In that corner |

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `position` | string | `center` | One of the values above. A condition can set its own |

## Size

**`width` and `height` size the symbol, or your content card, on the screen.** Percentages are of the screen, so `60%` is 60% of the screen's width.

- For the built-in symbol and other SVG component cards a width alone is enough: the height follows from the shape.
- With neither set, the symbol gets 60% of the width and 50% of the height of the screen and scales to fit inside, so it suits wide, tall and phone screens alike.
- Set a `height` for a custom content card that can't size itself from its width.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
width: 500px # the height follows from the symbol's shape
conditions:
  black_alert:
    width: 40%
    height: 30%
```

::: details More about size
- **The default height:** `50%` applies only to the built-in symbol (or a `content` card that is itself `component: alert`) when no `width` is set either. Set a `width` without a `height`, or use another content card, and the height is `auto`: the content sizes itself.
- **Per condition:** `conditions.<key>.width` and `conditions.<key>.height` fall back to the card's values, then to these defaults.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `width` | string | `60%` | Width as a CSS length (`400px`, `50%`, `50vw`) |
| `height` | string | `50%` for the symbol with no `width`, else `auto` | Height as a CSS length. `auto`: the content sizes itself |

## layers

**`layers` sets the screen effects drawn over the dashboard behind the symbol: a filter on the dashboard, an animated canvas over it, and a colour on top.** Without `layers` the overlay shows an 8px blur and nothing else.

- There are three slots, each with its own presets: [`backdrop`](#layers-backdrop) filters the dashboard behind the overlay, [`color`](#layers-color) lays a colour over it, and [`canvas`](#layers-canvas) draws an animation between the two (the colour lies over it).
- Set only the slots you want. Once `layers` is set, a slot you leave out stays off, so `layers` with only `color` has no blur.
- `layers: null` turns every layer off: the symbol shows over the dashboard as it is.
- A condition can change one slot and keep the others, or turn a slot off with `null`; see [Per-Condition Settings](./conditions#condition-keys).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
dismiss_mode: reset
layers:
  # blur the dashboard
  backdrop:
    preset: blur
    amount: 12px
  # dim it with a red tint
  color:
    preset: color-tint
    color: alpha(theme:colors.alert.red, 0.35)
  # TV static, under the tint
  canvas:
    preset: static
    opacity: 0.3
```

::: details More about layers
- **Colours:** the colour settings (`color-tint`'s `color`, and `color` on the `static` and `pixelate` canvas presets) take any LCARdS colour: `rgb()`/`rgba()`, `var(--css-variable)`, theme tokens (`theme:palette.moonlight`), CSS colour names and computed expressions (`alpha(theme:colors.ui.primary, 0.4)`). For colours that follow the alert mode use `var(--lcards-*)` or `var(--lcars-*)` variables.
- **Older configs:** a card-level `backdrop` with `blur`, `opacity` and `color` (from older versions) is still read when `layers` is not set: `blur` becomes a blur layer and `color` a `color-tint`, with `opacity` (default `0.6`) multiplied into the colour's alpha. The Alert Studio converts it to `layers` when you change a layer.
- **The band:** in `display: band` the layers are off unless you set them; see [Alert Band](./band).
- **Effects from actions:** the overlay only replaces the layers it sets and, when it closes, clears only its own. A screen effect started with [`lcards.trigger_effect`](/configuration/ha-actions#lcards-trigger-effect) on a layer the overlay leaves out keeps running, and so does one started on any layer after the overlay appeared.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `layers` | object or `null` | - | The screen effects; `null` turns them all off |
| `layers.backdrop` | object | an 8px blur when `layers` is not set | The [backdrop filter](#layers-backdrop) |
| `layers.color` | object | - | The [colour layer](#layers-color) |
| `layers.canvas` | object | - | The [canvas animation](#layers-canvas) |

### layers.backdrop

**The backdrop slot filters the dashboard behind the overlay: blur it, take the colour out, or shift its hues.** It is a CSS `backdrop-filter`, so the dashboard shows through, changed.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
layers:
  backdrop:
    preset: grayscale
    amount: 80%
```

| Preset | What it does | Setting |
|--------|--------------|---------|
| `blur` | Blurs the dashboard | `amount`, default `8px` |
| `grayscale` | Takes out the colour | `amount`, default `100%` |
| `saturate` | Makes colours stronger | `amount`, default `200%` |
| `contrast` | Raises the contrast | `amount`, default `200%` |
| `hue-rotate` | Shifts every hue round the colour wheel | `angle`, default `180deg` |

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `preset` | string | required | One of the presets above |
| `amount` | string | by preset | CSS value for `blur` (`4px` subtle, `20px` heavy), `grayscale`, `saturate` and `contrast` |
| `angle` | string | `180deg` | `hue-rotate` only: the angle (`90deg`, `270deg`) |

### layers.color

**The colour slot lays a colour over the dashboard, on top of the backdrop filter and the canvas: a flat tint, or a vignette that darkens the edges.**

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
layers:
  color:
    preset: vignette
    opacity: 0.8
```

| Preset | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `color-tint` | A flat colour over the whole screen; use a colour with alpha so the dashboard shows through |
| `vignette` | A dark fade from clear in the middle to dark at the edges |

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `preset` | string | required | `color-tint` or `vignette` |
| `color` | colour | `rgba(0,0,0,0.5)` | `color-tint` only: the tint, any colour (alpha sets how much shows through) |
| `opacity` | number | `0.7` | `vignette` only: how dark the edges get, 0 to 1 |

### layers.canvas

**The canvas slot draws an animation over the dashboard, between the backdrop filter and the colour layer: TV static, a mosaic, glitch bands or scanlines.**

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
layers:
  canvas:
    preset: scanlines
    lineHeight: 3
    opacity: 0.3
    scroll: 2
```

| Preset | What it does | Settings |
|--------|--------------|----------|
| `static` | TV static noise | `opacity`, `scale`, `color`, `tintStrength` |
| `pixelate` | Mosaic blocks | `pixelSize`, `opacity`, `variance`, `baseLight`, `color`, `tintStrength` |
| `glitch` | Bands shifted sideways | `intensity`, `maxShift`, `bandHeight`, `opacity`, `fps` |
| `scanlines` | CRT lines across the screen | `lineHeight`, `opacity`, `scroll` |

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `preset` | string | required | One of the presets above |
| `opacity` | number | `0.55` static, `0.75` pixelate, `0.85` glitch, `0.25` scanlines | How strong the effect is, 0 to 1 |
| `scale` | number | `4` | `static`: grain size, 1 to 16; larger is chunkier |
| `pixelSize` | number | `8` | `pixelate`: block size in px, 2 to 64 |
| `variance` | number | `0.35` | `pixelate`: brightness difference between blocks, 0 to 1 (`0` is even) |
| `baseLight` | number | `80` | `pixelate`: base grey level, 0 (black) to 255 (white) |
| `color` | colour | `#ffffff` static, `#8c9aa6` pixelate | `static` and `pixelate`: the colour blended in, by `tintStrength` |
| `tintStrength` | number | `0` | `static` and `pixelate`: how far to blend toward `color`, 0 to 1 (`0` is white noise or a grey mosaic) |
| `intensity` | number | `0.08` | `glitch`: share of lines shifted each frame, 0.01 to 0.5 |
| `maxShift` | number | `40` | `glitch`: largest sideways shift in px |
| `bandHeight` | number | `4` | `glitch`: height of each band in px |
| `fps` | number | `20` | `glitch`: frames per second, 1 to 60 |
| `lineHeight` | number | `4` | `scanlines`: height of each line in px, 1 to 20 |
| `scroll` | number | `0` | `scanlines`: scroll speed, 0 to 10 (`0` is still) |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/alert-overlay/raising.html -->

# Raising and Dismissing

How an alert starts and ends: the actions that raise it, what a tap on the overlay does, timers that clear it, and the transition played when the alert mode changes.

## Triggering alert modes

**The `lcards.*` alert actions raise and clear alerts from automations, scripts and dashboard buttons.** Without targeting they set `input_select.lcards_alert_mode`, so every dashboard with an alert overlay shows the alert.

- `lcards.red_alert`, `lcards.yellow_alert`, `lcards.blue_alert`, `lcards.black_alert` and `lcards.gray_alert` raise that alert; `lcards.clear_alert` returns to `green_alert`; `lcards.set_alert_mode` takes the mode as `mode`.
- With a targeting field the alert is local to the matching devices or users, and the global helper is not changed: the alert overlay on those devices shows it, the others don't. [Users & Devices](/configuration/users-devices) explains broadcast and targeted alerts in full.
- You can also set the helper with Home Assistant's own `input_select.select_option` action.

```yaml live
# A dashboard button that raises red alert
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: RED ALERT
    show: true
style:
  card:
    color:
      background:
        default: var(--lcars-alert-red)
tap_action:
  action: perform-action
  perform_action: lcards.red_alert
```

```yaml
# In an automation or script: every dashboard
action: lcards.red_alert
```

```yaml
# Only on the kitchen tablet; the global helper is not changed
action: lcards.red_alert
data:
  target_device_names:
    - Kitchen tablet
```

```yaml
# The helper directly: red_alert, yellow_alert, blue_alert, black_alert, gray_alert or green_alert
action: input_select.select_option
target:
  entity_id: input_select.lcards_alert_mode
data:
  option: red_alert
```

::: details More about triggering
- **From the browser console:** `window.lcards.setAlertMode('red_alert')` or `window.lcards.redAlert()` sets an alert, and `window.lcards.setAlertMode('green_alert')` or `window.lcards.greenAlert()` clears it. There are also `yellowAlert()`, `blueAlert()`, `grayAlert()` and `blackAlert()`. With the helper in place they write it, so every dashboard follows; without it the alert shows in this browser only.
- **The same mode again:** setting the mode that is already active changes nothing, so a dismissed alert comes back only when the mode changes.
- **More:** the [Alert Mode](/core/alert-mode) page covers what else an alert changes (theme colours, sounds), and [Actions](/configuration/ha-actions) lists every `lcards.*` action.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `mode` | string | required | `lcards.set_alert_mode` only: `red_alert`, `yellow_alert`, `blue_alert`, `gray_alert`, `black_alert` or `green_alert` |
| `target_device_ids` | list | all devices | Browser device ids (the `lcards_device_id` each browser stores) |
| `target_device_names` | list | all devices | Device display names, set in the LCARdS Config Panel or with `?lcards_device=`. A name shared by several devices matches all of them |
| `target_user_ids` | list | all users | Home Assistant user ids |
| `target_user_names` | list | all users | Home Assistant user display names, any case |

## Dismiss

**`dismiss_mode` sets what happens when someone taps outside the symbol: hide the alert on this screen, or clear it everywhere.** The auto modes do the same on a timer.

- `dismiss` and `auto-dismiss` hide the overlay on this dashboard only: the alert mode stays active, other dashboards still show it, and it shows again when the mode changes.
- `reset` and `auto-reset` also set `lcards_alert_mode` back to `green_alert`, clearing the alert everywhere. A targeted alert (on this device only) is cleared on this device.
- With an auto mode the user can still tap to dismiss early. In `display: band` the tap is on the symbol.

```yaml live
# Hides after 30 seconds and clears the alert; red alerts after 15
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
dismiss_mode: auto-reset
auto_dismiss_seconds: 30
conditions:
  red_alert:
    auto_dismiss_seconds: 15
```

::: details More about dismiss
- **The timer:** the countdown starts when the overlay shows (for an alert raised in edit mode, when you leave edit mode). A dismiss cancels it. If the alert changes to another condition while it runs, it starts again for that condition.
- **Without a time:** an auto mode with no `auto_dismiss_seconds` starts no timer, and the alert stays until it is dismissed or the mode changes.
- **Where to tap:** the whole screen outside the symbol's box (its `width` by `height`) dismisses, whether or not there are screen effects. A tap inside the box goes to the symbol or content card.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `dismiss_mode` | string | `dismiss` | `dismiss`, `reset`, `auto-dismiss` or `auto-reset` |
| `auto_dismiss_seconds` | number | - | Seconds before an auto mode hides the alert, at least 1. Needed for `auto-dismiss` and `auto-reset`; a condition can set its own |

## Transition effects

**A transition effect plays over the whole screen while the new alert colours are applied, whenever the alert mode changes.** The `input_select.lcards_alert_transition_style` helper picks it.

- The helper is optional. Without it, or with it set to `off`, the colours change at once with no effect.
- Create it from the **LCARdS Config Panel** (Alert System section), or in Home Assistant with that entity id and the values below. Once it exists, change the effect at any time from the Config Panel, a dashboard dropdown or an automation.
- The effect plays on the whole page on every alert mode change, whichever dashboard or device raised it; it is not part of any one alert overlay.

```yaml
# Pick the effect from an automation
action: input_select.select_option
target:
  entity_id: input_select.lcards_alert_transition_style
data:
  option: blur_fade
```

| Value | Effect |
|-------|--------|
| `off` | No transition: the colours change at once (the default) |
| `blur_fade` | The view blurs and dims, the colours change, then it sharpens again |
| `fade_only` | The view fades to near black, the colours change, then it fades back in |
| `flash` | A full-screen flash in the alert colour fades in and out over the change |
| `color_bleed` | The hues turn a full 360° and the brightness dips while the colours change |
| `flicker` | The view flickers in uneven steps, changing colour part way through |
| `static` | Pixelated noise, tinted to the alert colour, plays over the change |
| `wipe` | A see-through panel in the alert colour wipes across the screen and back |

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `input_select.lcards_alert_transition_style` | helper | `off` | One of the values above |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/alert-overlay/symbol.html -->

# Symbol and Content

What the alert shows in the middle: the built-in alert symbol, changed as little or as much as you like, or a card of your own.

## alert_button

**`alert_button` changes the built-in alert symbol without replacing it: set only what you want to change, and it is merged over the symbol.** Use it for your own message, a different text colour or size, or a faster bar sweep.

- Without a `content` card each condition shows the built-in symbol: an `lcards-button` with the `alert` component, its condition's preset for the colours, and the text `ALERT` over `CONDITION: RED` (and so on).
- `alert_button` on the card changes the symbol for every condition; `conditions.<key>.alert_button` changes it for one condition, merged over the card's; `conditions.<key>.content` replaces the symbol entirely, and `alert_button` is ignored for that condition.
- Any `lcards-button` key can be changed: text fields (`content`, `color`, `font_size`, ...), `style`, `animations`, `sounds` and the rest. `type`, `component` and `preset` stay fixed, so each condition keeps its own colours.

```text
built-in symbol (the condition's preset and text)
  ← alert_button                    (every condition)
    ← conditions.<key>.alert_button (this condition)
conditions.<key>.content            (replaces all of it)
```

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
alert_button:
  text:
    sub_text:
      content: ALL HANDS TO BATTLE STATIONS
  alert:
    color:
      shape: var(--lcars-orange)
```

::: details More about alert_button
- **Merging:** objects merge key by key, so a text field keeps the settings you don't change. A list (such as `animations`) in a condition's `alert_button` replaces the card's list rather than adding to it.
- **In the Alert Studio:** the Config tab's **Alert symbol** section edits the card's `alert_button`, and each condition picks **Alert symbol** (as it is), **Customise the symbol** (its `alert_button`, in the symbol's own button editor) or **Your own card** (`content`). The studio saves only what you change.
- **More keys:** the [alert component](/cards/button/components#alert) lists the symbol's own settings and text fields.
:::

| Condition | Preset | Text |
|-----------|--------|------|
| `red_alert` | `condition_red` | `ALERT`, `CONDITION: RED` |
| `yellow_alert` | `condition_yellow` | `ALERT`, `CONDITION: YELLOW` |
| `blue_alert` | `condition_blue` | `ALERT`, `CONDITION: BLUE` |
| `black_alert` | `condition_black` | `ALERT`, `CONDITION: BLACK` |
| `gray_alert` | `condition_gray` | `ALERT`, `CONDITION: GRAY` |

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `alert_button` | object | - | Changes to the symbol for every condition: any `lcards-button` key except `type`, `component` and `preset` |
| `alert_button.text.alert_text` | object | `content: ALERT` | The top label: `content` and any text field setting (`color`, `font_size`, ...) |
| `alert_button.text.sub_text` | object | `content: CONDITION: RED` and so on | The message: `content` (static text or a template) and any text field setting |
| `alert_button.alert.color.shape` | colour | the condition colour | Fill of the shield |
| `alert_button.alert.color.bars` | colour | the condition colour | Colour of the bars |
| `alert_button.speed` | number | `1` | Bar sweep speed, 0.25 to 4 (`2` is twice as fast). In band mode it follows `band.speed` unless set |
| `conditions.<key>.alert_button` | object | - | Changes for one condition, over the card's `alert_button`. Ignored when the condition has `content` |

### One message for every condition

**Set the message once in the card's `alert_button`, and override it for a condition that needs its own.** Every condition shows the message in its own colours.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
alert_button:
  text:
    sub_text:
      content: ALL HANDS TO BATTLE STATIONS
      font_size: 22
conditions:
  blue_alert:
    alert_button:
      text:
        sub_text:
          content: SECURITY LOCKDOWN IN PROGRESS
```

Blue alert shows its own message, still at size 22, because the condition's `sub_text` is merged over the card's.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| [alert_button keys](#alert-button) | | | `text.sub_text`, `text.alert_text`, `alert`, `speed` |

### A message from a helper

**Point the message at the `input_text.lcards_alert_message` helper, so an automation can set the words when it raises the alert.** Create the helper from the LCARdS Config Panel ([Helpers](/configuration/persistent-helpers)).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
conditions:
  blue_alert:
    alert_button:
      text:
        sub_text:
          content: "{{ states('input_text.lcards_alert_message') }}"
```

Set the message in an automation or script before raising the alert:

```yaml
action: input_text.set_value
target:
  entity_id: input_text.lcards_alert_message
data:
  value: SECURITY LOCKDOWN IN PROGRESS
```

A JavaScript template can fall back to the usual text when the message is empty:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
conditions:
  blue_alert:
    alert_button:
      text:
        sub_text:
          content: '[[[
            const msg = hass.states["input_text.lcards_alert_message"]?.state;
            return msg?.trim() || "CONDITION: BLUE";
          ]]]'
```

::: details More about messages
- **When templates are read:** a Jinja template (`{{ }}` or `{% %}`) is worked out by Home Assistant once, when the alert shows. A JavaScript template (`[[[ ]]]`) or a token (`{entity.state}`) is worked out by the button itself, so it follows the helper while the alert is up.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| [alert_button keys](#alert-button) | | | `text.sub_text.content` takes static text or a template |

## Content cards

**`conditions.<key>.content` shows a card of your own for that condition instead of the symbol.** Any card type works: it is created and mounted as it would be on a dashboard, and LCARdS cards keep their templates, entities, actions and animations.

- The alert symbol as content (`component: alert`) is sized like the built-in one; any other card keeps its own height unless you set `height` ([Size](./overlay#size)).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
conditions:
  red_alert:
    content:
      type: custom:lcards-button
      component: alert
      preset: condition_red
      text:
        alert_text:
          content: INTRUDER ALERT
        sub_text:
          content: SECURITY TEAM TO MAIN BRIDGE
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `conditions.<key>.content` | object | the built-in symbol | A full card config (`type` required) shown for this condition. Replaces the symbol and its `alert_button` |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/astrometrics/ -->

# Astrometrics

`custom:lcards-astrometrics-card`

![Astrometrics card: a galaxy disc with bearing labels round its rim, the galactic core glowing yellow, Federation space as a blue see-through sector, Borg space as a green one, crossing beams and a small blue planet with its orbits](/img/cards/astrometrics.webp)

**A 3D scene in the style of the astrometrics lab and stellar cartography: a lettered sector map, a galaxy disc with territories, a planet with an away team on it, or the sky over your home with the sun and moon where they are now.** Drag to orbit, scroll or pinch to zoom, and tap a point to fly to it.

- **Objects** draw the scene (grids, planets, territories, routes, nebulas, ships), and **points** are the named places on it that labels, routes and the camera refer to by id.
- The camera orbits a target, and named views let a tap fly it from the galaxy to a planet and back.
- The scene draws only when something moves, so an idle card costs nothing, and every astrometrics card and WebGL background on a page shares one WebGL context.

::: tip Try it
- The card editor opens the [Astrometrics Studio](./start#the-studio): a full-screen editor with the live scene, where you tap, drag and place points, edit every object in a form, capture camera views and start from a starter.
- [Getting Started](./start) has a first card to copy and every starter with its picture.
:::

## How a scene is sized

**One card holds one scene, and every position, size and distance in it is in scene units: your own, or real ones you name.** Most scenes are built to fit; a true-scale scene uses the real numbers and can reach from a galaxy down to a station.

- **Scene units** are yours to pick: a disc of radius 100, planets 5 across. Nothing is to scale, and everything shows at once. This is the easy way, and most starters work like this.
- **Named units** (`units: ly`, `pc`, `au`, `km` or `m` on the card) say what one unit is, so real numbers come out right: a galaxy 100,000 light years across, a planet at its real distance, a model at its real size (a model's `length` is in metres and is converted to the scene's units).
- **A star system** (a `system` object placed at one of the scene's points) is a scene inside the scene, with units of its own: a galaxy in light years holds a solar system in km. As the camera flies close it switches to the system's units, so one card spans the whole range.
- **Screen sizes** (line widths, dashes, label and marker sizes) are in px, the same at any zoom. Every other length (`radius`, `size`, `line_spacing`, positions) is in scene units.

[Scale](./scale) has the details: units, star systems, the real Solar System and the scene clock.

## Where to start

**Pick the starter closest to what you want and change it; it is quicker than an empty scene.** The Studio's Starters tab adds one with a few settings, and [Getting Started](./start#starters) shows them all with pictures.

| You want | Start with |
|---|---|
| A galaxy map with territories | [Galaxy with territories](./starters#galaxy-with-territories) (scene units), [Federation map](./starters#federation-map) (scene units), [Star Trek galaxy](./starters#star-trek-galaxy) (ly) |
| A sector map or tactical grid | [Sector map](./starters#sector-map) (scene units) |
| Planets and orbits | [Solar system](./starters#solar-system) (scene units), [Solar system (real positions)](./starters#solar-system-real-positions) (km, the planets where they are on the scene clock's date) |
| The sky over your home | [Sky dome: the sun and moon](./starters#sky-dome-the-sun-and-moon) (scene units; the sun and moon where they are now, from your Home Assistant location) |
| A ship or starbase close up | [Starbase approach](./starters#starbase-approach), [Deep Space 9](./starters#deep-space-9), [Utopia Planitia yards](./starters#utopia-planitia-yards), [Borg encounter](./starters#borg-encounter) (scene units) |
| From a galaxy down to a station | [Galaxy to station at true scale](./starters#galaxy-to-station-at-true-scale) (ly, with a solar system in km inside) |
| Something of your own | The [quick start](./start#quick-start): a grid and a few points (scene units) |

## Pages

| Page | Covers |
|------|--------|
| [Getting Started](./start) | A first card, the starters with pictures, and the card's own options |
| [Starters](./starters) | Every ready-made scene and part as a live card with its YAML |
