# Camera and Views

**The camera orbits a target, and named views let a tap fly it from one place in the scene to another.** Four numbers place it: `yaw` (the way it faces: `0` faces north), `tilt` (how high above the target), `distance` and `fov` (the field of view).

- Bearings are degrees clockwise from north, as on a compass seen from above, and north is away from the camera in the default view: `yaw: 0` looks north, `yaw: 90` looks east.
- Fly between views with a `tap_action` on a point or object (`action: fly-to`, see [Points: actions](./points#actions)), or from other cards and automations ([Live data: fly-to](./data#fly-to-from-other-cards-and-automations)).
- In the [Astrometrics Studio](./start#the-studio)'s Camera tab, move the preview's camera and select **Capture view** to write a view where the camera is.

## camera.views

**Named views of the scene, and the one the card opens on.** A view is a target and the numbers that place the camera round it; `camera.view` names the view shown first.

- `target` is a point id or `[x, y, z]`. When the target is a point that moves, the camera [follows it](#following-a-point).
- The view the card opens on faces north at a tilt of 35 when it leaves out `yaw` and `tilt`, and frames the whole scene when it leaves out `distance`. A view flown to later keeps the camera's current numbers for any key it leaves out.
- With no views at all, the camera frames the whole scene from a bearing of 20 and a tilt of 35.
- `projection: orthographic` removes the perspective, for a flat map; `distance` then sets the zoom.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 340
camera:
  view: galaxy
  views:
    galaxy:
      target: core
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 35
      distance: 260
    # straight down, without perspective
    map:
      target: core
      tilt: 90
      distance: 300
      projection: orthographic
backdrop:
  stars: true
points:
  - id: core
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    label: GALACTIC CORE
    style: title
  - id: to_map
    polar: [45, 300]
    marker: reticle
    label: MAP VIEW
    tap_action:
      action: fly-to
      view: map
  - id: to_galaxy
    polar: [45, 120]
    marker: reticle
    label: GALAXY VIEW
    tap_action:
      action: fly-to
      view: galaxy
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 100
    pattern: polar
    line_spacing: 10
    spoke_count: 36
```

::: details More about views
- **Wide cards:** on a card wider than 2:1 the field of view narrows, so the view is never wider than on a 2:1 card; a very wide angle would stretch planets near the sides out of shape. A wide, short card therefore shows the scene closer: move `distance` back to fit more in.
- **Distances in a system:** a view's `distance` is in its target's units, so a view of a station inside a [star system](./scale#star-systems) in km is a few km away. A view with an `[x, y, z]` target is in scene units.
- **A guided tour:** `camera.view` can follow an entity instead of naming a view, so a slider or a select flies the camera from stop to stop. See [Live data: a guided tour](./data#a-guided-tour).
- **In the Studio:** a captured view writes the target as a point's id when the camera looks at a point (after flying to it), else as coordinates. Each view flies, renames (actions that fly to it follow the new name), reorders and becomes the start view with **Start here**.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `camera.view` | string / object | the first view | The view the card opens on. Or a [guided tour](./data#a-guided-tour): `entity` and its stops |
| `camera.views` | object | - | Your views, by name |
| `camera.views.<name>.target` | id / `[x, y, z]` | the scene's centre | What the camera looks at. A view flown to later keeps the current target when it leaves this out |
| `camera.views.<name>.yaw` | number | `0` | The way the camera faces, degrees: `0` faces north, `90` east |
| `camera.views.<name>.tilt` | number | `35` | The camera's height angle, degrees: `0` level with the target, `90` straight down. `-90` to `90` |
| `camera.views.<name>.distance` | number | frames the scene | Distance from the target, in the target's units. With `projection: orthographic`, the zoom |
| `camera.views.<name>.fov` | number | `40` | Vertical field of view, degrees, perspective only. Held between `5` and `150` |
| `camera.views.<name>.projection` | string | `perspective` | `perspective`: far things look smaller. `orthographic`: no perspective, a flat map |
| `camera.views.<name>.warp` | boolean | `camera.warp` | Stars and dust streak while the camera flies here ([warp](./effects#warp-and-dust)) |

## Controls

**Drag to orbit, pan and zoom with a mouse, a touchpad, a touch screen or the keys.** These keys change what each gesture does, or turn the controls off.

| To | Mouse | Touchpad | Touch screen | Keys (card focused) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Orbit round the target | Drag | Click and drag, or shift + two-finger swipe | Drag one finger | Shift + arrows |
| Pan | Shift-drag, right-drag or middle-drag | Two-finger swipe | Two fingers | Arrows |
| Zoom | Wheel, toward the pointer | Pinch, toward the pointer | Pinch | `+` / `-` |
| Fly forward or back (camera and target together, so you travel through the scene; slower near a planet, model or cube, so you never fly into it) | | | | `W` / `S`, `Page Up` / `Page Down` |
| Draw small models larger, or at their [real size](./objects/ships#real-size) again | | | | `V` |
| Fly in toward a spot | Double-click blank space (shift: out) | Double-tap blank space | Double-tap blank space | |
| Fly to a point and follow it | Click the point or its label | Tap the point or its label | Tap the point or its label | |
| Fly in close to what stands at a point (a station, a ship, a planet) | Double-click the point or its label | Double-tap it | Double-tap it | |
| Let go of a followed point | Click blank space | Tap blank space | Tap blank space | |
| Back to the start view | | | | `Home` |

- `drag: pan` swaps orbit and pan for a one-finger or left-button drag. With `limits.tilt` locked to one value (`[90, 90]`), a drag always pans, as on a map.
- Pan moves along the screen by default, so a side view pans up and down and a top view pans across the map. `pan: ground` keeps the target at its height.
- `controls: false` turns off dragging, zooming, double-tap and keys, and leaves the camera to fly-to actions, `auto_rotate` and the [on-card buttons](#camera-buttons).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 300
camera:
  # a one-finger drag moves across the map
  drag: pan
  pan: ground
  # each zoom step is a smaller change
  zoom_step: 1.5
  double_tap: none
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 0
      tilt: 55
      distance: 220
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: plane
    size: 200
    line_spacing: 20
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
  - type: ring
    radius: 40
    color: var(--lcars-orange)
```

::: details More about controls
- **Touchpad or mouse wheel:** both send the same wheel events, so the card tells them apart by the events (a wheel moves in whole steps, a two-finger swipe in small ones and sideways too). A swipe pans, a mouse wheel zooms, and a pinch always zooms. If your mouse has a smooth wheel that pans instead, set `wheel: zoom`; `wheel: pan` makes every wheel event pan.
- **Double-tap on a point:** on a point without a `tap_action` of its own, or with a `fly-to`, a double-tap flies in close: to a few times the size of the largest object standing at the point, or much closer than now when nothing stands there. A station a few km across seen from the far side of its planet is a double-tap away.
- **Taps on points and objects** whose `tap_action` is another action run it on each tap; `double_tap` never changes that.
- **The on-card buttons** do the same as the keys; press and hold keeps moving.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `camera.controls` | boolean | `true` | Drag, zoom, double-tap and keys. `false`: the camera moves only by fly-to, `auto_rotate` and the buttons |
| `camera.drag` | string | `orbit` | What a one-finger or left-button drag does: `orbit` (shift or the right button pans) or `pan` (shift or the right button orbits). A middle-button drag always pans |
| `camera.pan` | string | `screen` | `screen`: pan along the screen. `ground`: across the ground plane, the target keeps its height |
| `camera.wheel` | string | `auto` | `auto`: a mouse wheel zooms and a touchpad swipe pans. `zoom`: every wheel event zooms. `pan`: every wheel event pans |
| `camera.zoom_to` | string | `cursor` | Where the wheel and pinch zoom toward: `cursor` (the spot under the pointer stays put) or `target` (straight in and out) |
| `camera.zoom_step` | number | `2` | Distance factor of one zoom step (double-tap, zoom buttons, `+` and `-`). `2` halves the distance. More than `1` |
| `camera.double_tap` | string | `zoom` | `zoom`: a double-tap flies in toward the spot, or close to a point. `none`: nothing |

## Following a point

**After the camera flies to a point, it stays on the point while the point moves:** a ship on its orbit, a planet round its star, a phone placed from its entity.

- Any fly-to that lands on a point starts it: a tap on the point, a `fly-to` action, a view whose `target` is the point, a fly-to from another card or an automation.
- Orbit and zoom work round the point as usual, and the wheel and pinch zoom straight in on it rather than toward the pointer. A pan or a fly forward or back keeps following, offset from the point, so a planet on a fast [scene clock](./scale#the-scene-clock) does not race out of view.
- A double-tap, a tap on blank space or a fly-to somewhere else lets go, and the point is no longer highlighted.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 320
camera:
  follow: true
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 35
      distance: 140
points:
  - id: sun
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    label: SUN
    style: major
  # tap the ship: the camera flies to it and rides along
  - id: ship
    polar: [45, 0]
    object: orbit
    marker: dot
    label: TAP TO FOLLOW
objects:
  - type: glow
    at: sun
    size: 30
    color: var(--lcars-yellow)
  - type: ring
    id: orbit
    radius: 45
    spin: 15
    width: 1
    opacity: 0.4
```

::: details More about following
- **Objects on a moving point:** a fly-to an object standing on a moving point (`at: <point id>`: a comet on its orbit, a ship model on a moving point) flies to the point and follows it the same way, in the card and in the Studio's preview. Dragging a point in the Studio lets go first.
- **Points that stand still** are not affected.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `camera.follow` | boolean | `true` | Keep a point at the centre while it moves, after a fly-to lands on it. `false`: the camera stays where it landed |

## camera.buttons

**An LCARdS D-pad on the card that moves the camera, with a time slider under it.** It does what the keys do, so a touch screen without a keyboard can pan, zoom and fly forward too.

- The arms pan, the centre flies back to the start view, the left corners zoom in (top) and out (bottom), and the right corners fly forward (top) and back (bottom). Press and hold keeps moving.
- It takes the D-pad colours of your theme (the `components.dpad` theme tokens, as on a button with `component: dpad`), so it follows HA-LCARS and alert modes.
- The buttons fade out after three seconds without input on the card and come back when the pointer moves over it, on a touch or a key (`hide: idle`).
- `buttons: true` shows all of them in the bottom right.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 360
camera:
  buttons:
    position: bottom-right
    size: 150
    hide: never
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 35
      distance: 150
backdrop:
  stars: true
points:
  - id: sun
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    label: SUN
    style: major
objects:
  - type: glow
    at: sun
    size: 30
    color: var(--lcars-yellow)
  - type: ring
    radius: 50
    spin: 10
    dash: [6, 8]
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
```

::: details More about the buttons
- **The time slider** slows the scene's motion (orbits, spins, drift) down to a tenth, holds it, or speeds it up to four times, so a fast ship is easy to tap. It changes the view only; `time_scale` on the card sets the speed it starts at ([Scene and Looks](./scene#units-and-motion)).
- **The date slider:** on a card with a [clock](./scale#the-scene-clock), the slider can set the scene date's rate instead: a year, a month or a day a second backward, paused, live, then an hour, a day, a month or a year a second forward, with the date above it and NOW to go back to today. The clock button beside it switches between the two sliders.
- **The size button** shows under the pad while a model is drawn at its [real size](./objects/ships#real-size): REAL SIZE keeps models in proportion, VISIBLE SIZE draws each small one at least 40 px across (the `V` key does the same). It changes the view only.
- **Off parts:** `pan`, `zoom`, `travel` or `reset: false` dims those parts of the pad and turns them off.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `camera.buttons` | boolean / object | off | `true` for every button in the bottom right, or the keys below |
| `camera.buttons.position` | string | `bottom-right` | Where they sit: `top-left`, `top-center`, `top-right`, `center-left`, `center`, `center-right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-center` or `bottom-right` |
| `camera.buttons.size` | number | `180` | How big the D-pad is, px across, `64` to `320` |
| `camera.buttons.pan` | boolean | `true` | The arms pan. `false`: dimmed and off |
| `camera.buttons.zoom` | boolean | `true` | The left corners zoom. `false`: dimmed and off |
| `camera.buttons.travel` | boolean | `true` | The right corners fly forward and back, as `W` and `S`. `false`: dimmed and off |
| `camera.buttons.reset` | boolean | `true` | The centre flies back to the start view. `false`: dimmed and off |
| `camera.buttons.scale` | boolean | `true` | The model size button, shown while a model is at its real size. `false` hides it |
| `camera.buttons.time` | boolean / string | `true` | The time slider. `speed`: the motion's speed. `date`: the scene clock's rate. `both`: either, with a switch. `true`: both on a card with a `clock`, else speed. `false` hides it |
| `camera.buttons.hide` | string | `idle` | `idle`: fade out after three seconds without input. `never`: always shown. `toggle`: a small button folds them away and back |

## camera.limits

**Where drag and zoom stop: how low and high the camera may tilt, how near and far it may go, and where the point it looks at may wander.**

- A tilt range of one value (`[90, 90]`) locks the tilt, and a one-finger drag then pans, as on a map.
- The point the camera looks at stays inside a sphere 1.5 times the size of the scene, so panning cannot lose it. Set your own sphere (`radius`, optional `center`) or box (`x`, `y`, `z` ranges; an axis left out is free), or `false` for none.
- Limits are in scene units, also while the camera is inside a [star system](./scale#star-systems).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 300
camera:
  # a flat map: straight down, panning stays over the grid
  limits:
    tilt: [90, 90]
    distance: [80, 400]
    target:
      x: [-100, 100]
      z: [-100, 100]
  views:
    map:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      tilt: 90
      distance: 260
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: plane
    size: 200
    line_spacing: 20
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `camera.limits.tilt` | `[min, max]` | `[-90, 90]` | Lowest and highest tilt, degrees |
| `camera.limits.distance` | `[min, max]` | `[1, 100000]` | Nearest and farthest distance, scene units. A scene at true scale widens it: down to half its smallest object, out to 20 times its size |
| `camera.limits.yaw` | `[min, max]` | no limit | Yaw range, degrees |
| `camera.limits.target` | object / `false` | a sphere 1.5 times the scene | Where the point the camera looks at may go. `false`: anywhere |
| `camera.limits.target.radius` | number | - | A sphere this big, scene units |
| `camera.limits.target.center` | `[x, y, z]` | the scene's centre | The sphere's centre |
| `camera.limits.target.x` | `[min, max]` | free | A box: its x range. Also `y` and `z` |

## Flying and turning

**How long a fly-to takes, how it eases, whether the stars streak on the way, and a camera that turns on its own.**

- A fly-to over a long zoom moves evenly in log distance, so each factor of ten takes the same time ([Scale](./scale#one-scene-in-real-units)).
- `camera.warp` streaks the stars and dust on every fly-to; a view's own `warp` wins. The card's `warp` key is different: it holds the scene at warp ([Effects: going to warp](./effects#going-to-warp)).
- `auto_rotate` pauses while you drag. Under reduced motion it stops, and a fly-to jumps instead of flying, without streaks.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 320
camera:
  auto_rotate: 4
  fly_duration: 2500
  ease: outQuad
  warp: true
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 30
      distance: 200
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 2500
points:
  - id: core
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    label: CORE
    style: major
  - id: outpost
    polar: [70, 120]
    marker: diamond
    label: TAP TO FLY
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 90
    pattern: polar
    line_spacing: 15
    spoke_count: 24
  - type: glow
    at: core
    size: 40
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `camera.fly_duration` | number | `1600` | How long a fly-to takes, ms |
| `camera.ease` | string | `inOutCubic` | The fly-to's easing: an anime.js easing name such as `inOutCubic`, `outQuad` or `linear` |
| `camera.warp` | boolean / object | `false` | Every fly-to streaks the stars and dust. Or `entity` (and `attribute`): fly-tos streak while it is on (`on`, `true` or a number above 0) |
| `camera.auto_rotate` | number | `0` | Turn round the target, degrees per second; negative turns the other way. `0` is off |

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/astrometrics/data.html -->

# Live Data

Points take their text, colour and even their position from Home Assistant, and rules change points and objects as entities change. None of it rebuilds the scene: a label or a colour changes in place, a point moves on the next frame.

## A point's entity

**`entity` on a point is that point's own entity: its label templates read it, its colour maps follow its state, and its actions act on it.** Use it for a point that stands for a device: a light, a switch, a phone.

- Label [templates](#templates) read it as `entity` (`{entity.state}`, `{entity.attributes.friendly_name}`).
- Colour [state maps](/core/colours) on the point and its text fields follow its state, with the card's `state_classification`.
- `more-info` and `toggle` actions without an `entity` act on it, and a [position](#positions-from-entities) can come from its attributes.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 280
camera:
  views:
    top:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      tilt: 70
      distance: 120
points:
  - id: lamp
    entity: switch.demo_switch
    xyz: [-20, 0, 0]
    marker: square
    style: major
    # follows the switch: tap to toggle it
    color:
      active: var(--lcars-orange)
      inactive: var(--lcars-blue)
    text:
      label:
        content: "{entity.attributes.friendly_name}"
      state:
        content: "{entity.state}"
        position: bottom-right
        font_size: 11
    tap_action:
      action: toggle
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: plane
    size: 100
    line_spacing: 10
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | string | - | The point's entity: templates read it, state colour maps follow it, `more-info` and `toggle` act on it, positions can come from it |
| `color` | colour / state map | by style | The point's colour, a state map by this entity: see [Markers](./points#markers) |

## Positions from entities

**`xyz`, `polar`, `latlon` and `altaz` take numbers, or `entity` to read them from an entity's attributes: a phone on a globe, the sun on a sky dome.** The point moves when they change, and paths, rings and beams that use it follow.

- The entity defaults to the point's own `entity`.
- Each form reads attributes by default names: `latitude` and `longitude` (a person, a device tracker, a zone), `azimuth` and `elevation` (`sun.sun`), `x`, `y` and `z`, or `distance` and `bearing`. Change them with the form's own keys; `state` as a name reads the entity's state.
- A point is hidden while one of its numbers is missing or not a number.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 320
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 10, 0]
      yaw: 160
      tilt: 20
      distance: 190
points:
  # the sun from sun.sun's azimuth and elevation, on the dome
  - id: sun
    altaz:
      entity: sun.sun
    object: sky
    marker: dot
    color: var(--lcars-yellow)
    label: SOL
  # home from zone.home's latitude and longitude, on the globe
  - id: home
    latlon:
      entity: zone.home
    object: earth
    marker: reticle
    label: HOME
objects:
  - type: grid
    id: sky
    shape: dome
    radius: 80
    line_spacing_deg: 15
  - type: sphere
    id: earth
    at: [0, 20, 0]
    radius: 15
    image: builtin:earth_blue_marble
```

::: details More about positions from entities
- **A probe from a sensor's attributes:** a point with `entity: sensor.probe_track` and `polar: { attributes: [range, heading] }` reads its distance from the sensor's `range` attribute and its bearing from `heading`.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `latlon.entity` | string | the point's `entity` | The entity to read: a person, a device tracker, a zone |
| `latlon.latitude` | string | `latitude` | The attribute holding the latitude |
| `latlon.longitude` | string | `longitude` | The attribute holding the longitude |
| `altaz.entity` | string | the point's `entity` | The entity to read, such as `sun.sun` |
| `altaz.azimuth` | string | `azimuth` | The attribute holding the azimuth |
| `altaz.altitude` | string | `elevation` | The attribute holding the altitude |
| `xyz.entity` | string | the point's `entity` | The entity to read |
| `xyz.attributes` | list | `[x, y, z]` | The three attributes holding x, y and z |
| `polar.entity` | string | the point's `entity` | The entity to read |
| `polar.attributes` | list | `[distance, bearing]` | The two attributes holding the distance and the bearing |

## Templates

**Label `content` takes the four [template types](/core/templates/) as on every card: `{entity.state}` tokens, `[[[ JavaScript ]]]`, `{{ Jinja2 }}` (evaluated by Home Assistant) and `{ds:name}` [data sources](/core/datasources/).** Besides `entity`, `states`, `config`, `variables` and `theme`, label templates can read the sun and moon (`sky`) and the point's own config (`point`).

- A template is evaluated again only when something it reads changes: its entities, a data source, or the sky.
- The sky values update every minute, and work in all four types: `{sky.moon.illumination}`, `[[[ return Math.round(sky.sun.altitude) ]]]`, `{{ sky.moon.illumination }}`.
- The angles have one decimal; for whole degrees, round in JavaScript: `[[[ return 'SOL ' + Math.round(sky.sun.altitude) + '°' ]]]`.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 300
camera:
  views:
    sky:
      target: [0, 20, 0]
      yaw: 180
      tilt: 20
      distance: 190
points:
  - id: sun
    sky: sun
    object: dome
    marker: dot
    label: "SOL {sky.sun.altitude}°"
    color: var(--lcars-yellow)
  - id: moon
    sky: moon
    object: dome
    marker: moon_phase
    label: "LUNA {sky.moon.illumination}%"
objects:
  - type: grid
    id: dome
    shape: dome
    radius: 80
    line_spacing_deg: 15
```

::: details More about templates
- **JavaScript templates** may read any state, so they run again on every change the card tracks.
- **Template off:** `template: false` on a field shows its `content` as written.
:::

| Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `sky.sun.azimuth` | number | The sun now, degrees to one decimal (from `sun.sun` when it exists) |
| `sky.sun.altitude` | number | The sun's height above the horizon, degrees to one decimal |
| `sky.moon.azimuth` | number | The moon now, degrees to one decimal (computed from the time and your location) |
| `sky.moon.altitude` | number | The moon's height above the horizon, degrees to one decimal |
| `sky.moon.illumination` | number | How much of the moon is lit, whole percent |
| `sky.moon.waxing` | boolean | `true` while it grows |
| `point` | object | The point's own config (`{point.id}`) |

## Settings from entities

**Any number on a point or object can follow an entity instead of holding still: a shield bubble's opacity follows the shields, a glow's size follows the power.** Write the key as `entity` with an `input` range and an `output` range, the same words as `map_range` in [animations](/core/animations) and the rules' `map_range_cond`.

- A value outside `input` stays at the end of `output`, unless `clamp: false`. No value (unavailable, not a number) gives the key's default.
- Templates work too: `spin: "[[[ return states['input_number.lcards_test_power'].state / 10 ]]]"`, or `{{ }}` and `{entity.state}`.
- An object's `opacity`, `radius`, `size` and `spin` ease to their new value without rebuilding anything; most other keys rebuild that one object or point, at most four times a second, and step.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 300
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 20
      distance: 160
objects:
  - type: sphere
    id: shields
    at: [-35, 0, 0]
    radius: 30
    fill:
      color: var(--lcars-blue)
    # shields 0 to 100 % gives an opacity of 0 to 0.6
    opacity:
      entity: input_number.lcards_test_shields
      output: [0, 0.6]
  - type: glow
    id: core
    at: [40, 0, 0]
    color: var(--lcars-orange)
    # power 0 to 100 % gives a glow 10 to 60 across, easing over 1 s
    size:
      entity: input_number.lcards_test_power
      input: [0, 100]
      output: [10, 60]
      smooth: 1000
```

::: details More about settings from entities
- **What else changes in place:** some types take more keys of their own that ease without a rebuild: a belt's `radius` (each side too), `thickness` and `count` (the band widens or thins round the same rocks); a comet's `nucleus.size`, `coma.size`, `tail.length` and `glow`; a nebula's `drift` (each side too: the clouds speed up or slow down from where they are) and `density`; a crystalline entity's `glow` and `opacity`. A colour of any object crossfades to its new value (see [Colours from entities](#colours-from-entities)). Any other key (a deformation's `amplitude`, a galaxy's `arms.count`, a point's `alt`) rebuilds that one object or point.
- **A bound belt `count`** builds for the top of its `output` and draws fewer, so keep `output` no higher than you need.
- **Pairs:** a setting that takes `[a, b]` (a belt's `[inner, outer]` radius and `[smallest, largest]` rock size, a grid's or image's `[w, d]` size, a ring's ellipse, a nebula's drift) can have either side follow an entity of its own: `radius: [{ entity: input_number.lcards_test_shields, output: [40, 70] }, 90]`. A whole `radius` bound to one entity gives one number (for a belt, the outer edge with the inner at 0.8 of it) and scales in place; a bound side rebuilds the object, except a belt's radius and a nebula's drift, which ease. In the Astrometrics Studio each box of a pair has its own link button.
- **Whole numbers:** how-many settings (a belt's `count`, a galaxy's `arms.count` and `stars.count`, a nebula's `count`, a lightning object's `branches`, a wobble's `lobes`, a polar grid's `spoke_count`, `num_octaves`, `major.row_interval` and `major.col_interval`) take the mapped value rounded, so `count: { entity: input_number.lcards_test_power, output: [100, 500] }` gives 233 rocks at 33.3 %, and the object rebuilds only when the whole number changes.
- **Not bound:** lists of three (`[x, y, z]`, `rotation`) do not follow entities, and a `seed` takes only a plain number (a new pattern would rebuild the object).
- **On the card:** `time_scale`, `warp_factor`, `clock.rate` and `clock.date` follow entities the same way (`clock: { date: { entity: input_datetime.lcards_test_date } }` shows the planets on the date in a helper). Positions follow entities their own way: see [Positions from entities](#positions-from-entities).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | string | required | The entity to follow |
| `attribute` | string | - | Read this attribute instead of the state |
| `input` | `[low, high]` | the entity's `min` and `max`, else `[0, 100]` | The range of the entity's value. `min` and `max` are an `input_number`'s attributes |
| `output` | `[low, high]` | - | The range of the setting the input maps to. Left out: the entity's number as it is |
| `clamp` | boolean | `true` | `false`: a value outside `input` carries on past the ends of `output` |
| `smooth` | number | `600` | How long a change eases, ms, for a key that changes in place. `0` steps |

### Colours from entities

**Any colour on an object can follow an entity or a template too: its `color`, a part's `color` (such as `edges.color` or `core.color`), each colour in a `colors` list, and the colours of a `fill.effect`.** Write it as a [state map](/core/colours) with the entity it reads, using the same state words as the other cards.

- With no key matching, a value that is itself a colour is used, so `color: { entity: light.desk, attribute: rgb_color }` follows a light's colour.
- A colour change crossfades that object to the new colour in place over a moment, with no rebuild: its motion carries on.
- A point's colour already follows the point's own entity: see [A point's entity](#a-point-s-entity).

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 320
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 35
      distance: 220
objects:
  - type: grid
    id: deck
    shape: plane
    size: 120
    # the lines turn orange while the toggle is on
    color:
      entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
      active: var(--lcars-orange)
      inactive: var(--lcars-gray)
    # the frame turns red above 80 % power
    edges:
      color:
        entity: input_number.lcards_test_power
        "above:80": var(--lcars-red)
        default: var(--lcars-blue)
  - type: nebula
    id: cloud
    at: [0, 25, 0]
    radius: 50
    # two clouds placed by hand take the colours in order:
    # the first stays blue, the second follows the mode
    clouds:
      - xyz: [-28, 0, 0]
        radius: 24
      - xyz: [28, 0, 0]
        radius: 24
    colors:
      - var(--lcars-blue)
      - entity: input_select.lcards_test_mode
        alpha: var(--lcars-violet)
        beta: var(--lcars-orange)
        default: var(--lcars-red)
```

::: details More about colours from entities
- **Templates:** `color: "[[[ return states['input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle'].state === 'on' ? 'var(--lcars-red)' : 'var(--lcars-blue)' ]]]"`, or `{{ }}`. The result is a colour (`[r, g, b]` works too).
- **Nothing matching**, and no `default`: the colour the key has when it is left out.
- **How often:** a colour change crossfades at most four times a second; under reduced motion it changes at once. A model, whose look comes from its file, is built again instead.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | string | required | The entity to follow |
| `attribute` | string | - | Match this attribute's value instead of the state |
| `<state>` | colour | - | The colour for that exact state or attribute value (`heat`, `alpha`) |
| `active` | colour | - | The colour while the entity is on, with the card's `state_classification` |
| `inactive` | colour | - | The colour while the entity is off |
| `unavailable` | colour | - | The colour while the entity is unavailable or unknown |
| `zero` | colour | - | The colour when the value is the number 0 |
| `non_zero` | colour | - | The colour when the value is any other number |
| `above:N` | colour | - | The colour when the value is above N |
| `below:N` | colour | - | The colour when the value is below N |
| `between:A:B` | colour | - | The colour when the value is between A and B |
| `default` | colour | - | The colour when nothing else matches |

### A guided tour

**`camera.view` can follow an entity: the camera flies to `views[n]` when the entity's value is `n` (counting from 0), or to the view an `input_select`'s option names.** Step the number from an automation, a script or buttons (`input_number.increment`), and the card flies from stop to stop.

- A number is rounded and held to the list, so a value past the last stop stays on the last.
- A stop can set the [scene clock](./scale#the-scene-clock) too: `view`, with `date` and `rate`.
- Leave `views` out when the entity's state is the view's name.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 320
camera:
  view:
    entity: input_number.lcards_test_stage
    views:
      - wide
      - planet
      - moon
  views:
    wide:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 35
      distance: 170
    planet:
      target: planet
      yaw: 40
      tilt: 20
      distance: 60
    moon:
      target: moon
      yaw: 200
      tilt: 15
      distance: 25
points:
  # each tap sets the stage, and the camera follows it
  - id: home
    xyz: [-50, 0, 0]
    marker: diamond
    label: STAGE 0 (TAP)
    tap_action:
      action: perform-action
      perform_action: input_number.set_value
      target:
        entity_id: input_number.lcards_test_stage
      data:
        value: 0
  - id: planet
    xyz: [20, 0, 0]
    label: STAGE 1 (TAP)
    tap_action:
      action: perform-action
      perform_action: input_number.set_value
      target:
        entity_id: input_number.lcards_test_stage
      data:
        value: 1
  - id: moon
    xyz: [45, 4, 10]
    label: STAGE 2 (TAP)
    tap_action:
      action: perform-action
      perform_action: input_number.set_value
      target:
        entity_id: input_number.lcards_test_stage
      data:
        value: 2
objects:
  - type: sphere
    at: planet
    radius: 12
    fill:
      effect:
        preset: gas_giant
  - type: sphere
    at: moon
    radius: 3
    color: var(--lcars-gray)
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 70
    pattern: polar
    line_spacing: 10
    spoke_count: 12
    opacity: 0.4
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `camera.view.entity` | string | required | The entity whose value picks the view |
| `camera.view.attribute` | string | - | Read this attribute instead of the state |
| `camera.view.views` | list | - | The stops in order: a view name, or `view` with `date` and `rate` |
| `camera.view.views[].view` | string | required | The named view to fly to |
| `camera.view.views[].date` | string | - | Set the scene date there: `now` or an ISO date |
| `camera.view.views[].rate` | number / string | - | Set the date's rate there: `live`, days per second, or with a unit (`1 h/s`, `30 d/s`, `1 y/s`) |

## Rules

**Points and objects with an `id` are [rule](/core/rules/) targets, as MSD overlays are: a rule's `apply.overlays` patches them with their own keys.** Use it to recolour, relabel, hide or move points and objects while an entity is in some state.

- When the rule stops matching, the point or object goes back to its config.
- A patched point label is rebuilt on its own; the rest of the scene stays. An object whose patch changes only colours crossfades in place, and other keys build that object again, nothing else.
- Ids are page-wide: two cards with a point `sol` both match a rule on `sol`. Use distinct ids, or tags, when a dashboard has several astrometrics or MSD cards.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 300
camera:
  views:
    top:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      tilt: 70
      distance: 130
labels:
  styles:
    hostile:
      font_size: 16
      font_weight: bold
      color: var(--lcars-alert-red)
points:
  # tap to toggle the alert
  - id: alert_switch
    xyz: [-35, 0, 25]
    marker: square
    label: RED ALERT (TAP)
    tap_action:
      action: toggle
      entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
  - id: warbird
    xyz: [20, 0, -10]
    marker: triangle
    label: CONTACT
  - id: escort
    xyz: [-10, 0, -20]
    marker: dot
    tags:
      - patrol
    label: ESCORT
objects:
  - type: ring
    id: neutral_zone
    radius: 45
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
rules:
  - id: red_alert_contacts
    when:
      entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
      state: "on"
    apply:
      overlays:
        # a point
        warbird:
          style: hostile
          label: HOSTILE CONTACT
        # every point or object tagged patrol
        "tag:patrol":
          color: var(--lcars-alert-red)
        # an object
        neutral_zone:
          visible: false
```

::: details More about rules
- **Selectors:** an id, `tag:<name>` (points and objects take `tags`), `type:astrometrics-point` or `type:astrometrics-object`, `pattern:<regex>`, `all`.
- **Point keys a rule can patch:** `label`, `text`, `style`, `color`, `marker`, `priority`, `overlap`, `visible`, `opacity`, the distance keys (`fade`, `min_distance`, `max_distance`), `tap_action`, `card` and the placement forms (a rule can move a point).
- **Object keys:** any of their keys. `visible` and the distance keys change it without a rebuild.
- **MSD-style patches:** `style: { color: var(--lcars-red) }` patches the colour. A plain string `style` is the label style.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rules` | list | - | The card's [rules](/core/rules/) |
| `apply.overlays` | object | - | Patches by selector: a point or object id, `tag:<name>`, `type:astrometrics-point`, `type:astrometrics-object`, `pattern:<regex>` or `all` |
| `tags` | list | - | On a point or object: names for `tag:<name>` selectors |

## Fly-to from other cards and automations

**Give the astrometrics card an `id`, then any LCARdS card can fly its camera with a `fly-to` action naming it in `card`, with a `view` or a `point`.** From an automation, the [`lcards.fly_to`](/configuration/ha-actions#lcards-fly-to) action does the same on every open dashboard (or only the devices and users you target).

- The camera of every open card with that id flies, in the same browser.
- The two examples below work together: the button flies the camera of the card above it.

```yaml live
# the card to fly: its id is galaxy
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
id: galaxy
height: 280
camera:
  views:
    wide:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 40
      distance: 170
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 2000
points:
  - id: earth
    polar: [45, 120]
    marker: dot
    label: EARTH
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 70
    pattern: polar
    line_spacing: 10
    spoke_count: 12
```

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: EARTH
    show: true
style:
  card:
    color:
      background:
        default: var(--lcars-orange)
tap_action:
  action: fly-to
  card: galaxy          # the astrometrics card's id
  point: earth          # or view: <a camera view>
  duration: 2500        # optional, ms
  warp: true            # optional: streak the stars on the way (false: never)
```

::: details More about flying from outside
- **Browser console:** `window.lcards.cards.astrometrics` has `getAll()`, `get(id)` and `flyTo(id, view or { point }, { duration, warp })`.
- **The scene date:** `set-clock` takes `card` the same way: see [Scene actions](./points#scene-actions).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | - | On the astrometrics card: the name other cards and automations use |
| `card` | string | required | On the action: the astrometrics card's `id` |
| `point` | string | - | A point id to fly to. Wins over `view` |
| `view` | string | - | A named view (`camera.views`) to fly to |
| `duration` | number | `camera.fly_duration` | How long the flight takes, ms |
| `warp` | boolean | the view's `warp`, else `camera.warp` | `true` streaks the stars on the way, `false` never |
