<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/astrometrics/effects.html -->

# Effects

The [background animation](/core/effects/background-animations) presets, rebuilt as parts of the 3D scene: they sit in space and move with the camera instead of being a flat layer behind it. Every effect is still unless you give it a speed, so a scene with nothing moving draws nothing; under reduced motion (the system setting) they all hold still.

## Nebula

**`type: nebula` puts clouds of gas in the scene, in the look of the [nebula](/core/effects/background-animations/preset-reference#nebula) preset with `volumetric: true`.** Use it for a nebula on a star map, a gas cloud round a station, or a storm to fly into.

- Each cloud is a few soft puffs facing the camera at slightly different depths, so as you turn the camera the clouds shift against each other and against the grids.
- A cloud fades as you fly into it, and a planet hides the clouds behind it.
- Every key of the object is in the [nebula](./objects/space#nebula) table; the sections below show what the volume, shapes, dust and presets do.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 340
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 25
      distance: 300
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 2000
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 100
    pattern: polar
    line_spacing: 10
    spoke_count: 36
  - type: nebula
    size: [220, 50, 220]
    count: 8
    seed: 5
    drift: 3
    colors: [var(--lcars-violet), var(--lcars-blue), var(--lcars-red)]
```

::: details More about nebulae
- **Never tappable:** clouds never catch a tap, so they never get in the way of points behind them. A label for a cloud is a [point](./points) at the same place.
- **The seed:** `count` clouds are placed by `seed` inside the region; the same seed always places the same clouds, and picks each cloud's colour from `colors`.
- **Entities:** `drift` (and with `render: volume`, `density`) can [follow an entity](./data#settings-from-entities); it eases to each new value.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `radius` | number | `100` | The clouds fill a ball this big round `at`, scene units |
| `size` | number / `[w, h, d]` | - | Or a box, scene units (one number for a cube). Wins over `radius` |
| `count` | number | `4` | How many clouds the seed places, 1 to 10 |
| `seed` | number | `1` | The same seed always places the same clouds |
| `colors` | colour / list | `var(--lcars-violet)` | One colour, or a list the seed picks from per cloud |
| `drift` | number / `[x, y]` | `0` | How fast the gas churns, scene units per second. `[x, y]` gives a direction. `0` is still |
| [Nebula keys](./objects/space#nebula) | | | `clouds`, `color`, `min_radius`, `max_radius`, `brightness`, `turbulence`, `noise_scale`, `blend` and the rest |

### Gas you can fly into

**`render: volume` draws the same clouds (the same seed, colours and brightness) as one body of gas filling the region, instead of puffs.** Fly into it and there is gas all round you, which puffs facing the camera cannot give.

- The gas fades out toward the edges of the region, so its box or ball never shows.
- A planet, model or other solid object inside the gas hides the gas behind it, and the gas in front of it still shows.
- `turbulence` erodes the clouds into wisps and holes (0 gives smooth blobs), and `density` makes the gas thicker or thinner.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 340
camera:
  view: outside
  views:
    outside:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 20
      distance: 300
    inside:
      target: [40, 0, 10]
      yaw: 200
      tilt: 6
      distance: 30
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 2000
points:
  # tap the labels to fly in and out
  - id: fly_in
    xyz: [40, 0, 10]
    label: FLY INSIDE
    tap_action:
      action: fly-to
      view: inside
  - id: fly_out
    xyz: [-90, 0, 0]
    label: BACK OUT
    tap_action:
      action: fly-to
      view: outside
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 100
    pattern: polar
    line_spacing: 10
    spoke_count: 36
  - type: sphere
    at: [30, 0, -20]
    radius: 14
    fill:
      color: var(--lcars-orange)
  - type: nebula
    render: volume
    size: [220, 60, 220]
    count: 7
    seed: 5
    drift: 2
    colors: [var(--lcars-violet), var(--lcars-blue)]
```

::: details More about volume gas
- **Bigger clouds:** with `render: volume`, the clouds' default sizes are 0.25 and 0.55 of the region (`min_radius`, `max_radius`), so the gas fills it.
- **Resolution:** a volume is drawn at half the screen's resolution, which soft gas does not show.
- **Volume only:** `shape`, `dust`, `density` and `lightning` work only with `render: volume`.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `render` | string | `puffs` | `puffs`: soft puffs facing the camera. `volume`: one body of gas you can fly into |
| `density` | number | `1` | `render: volume`: how thick the gas is (`2` is twice as thick) |
| `turbulence` | number | `0.5` | How ragged the edges are, `0` to `1` |

### Shapes, dust and colour

**With `render: volume`, `shape` gives the gas a form, after the real nebulae: a hollow shell, an hourglass, long filaments, a cavity.** The clouds still give the clumps and the colours inside the form, so `count`, `seed` and `colors` keep working; turn the form with `rotation`.

- `stretch` draws each seeded cloud out (0 round to 1 long and flat), each turned its own way. The same seed with or without `stretch` places the same clouds.
- `core.color` colours the gas deep inside a cloud (in a shape: near its middle), running out to the cloud colours at the edges, as in the Hubble pictures.
- Dust is dark gas that hides the gas behind it: see [Dust lanes](#dust-lanes).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 360
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 0
      tilt: 10
      distance: 420
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 2000
objects:
  # the Ring nebula
  - type: nebula
    render: volume
    shape: shell
    at: [-150, 60, 0]
    radius: 55
    count: 8
    colors: [var(--lcars-ice), var(--lcars-violet)]
  # the Butterfly
  - type: nebula
    render: volume
    shape: bipolar
    at: [-50, 60, 0]
    radius: 55
    count: 8
    colors: [var(--lcars-orange), var(--lcars-red)]
    core:
      color: var(--lcards-moonlight)
  # the Veil
  - type: nebula
    render: volume
    shape: filaments
    at: [50, 60, 0]
    radius: 55
    count: 8
    stretch: 0.5
    colors: [var(--lcars-red), var(--lcars-ice)]
  # a blister, as in Orion
  - type: nebula
    render: volume
    shape: cavity
    at: [150, 60, 0]
    radius: 55
    count: 8
    colors: [var(--lcars-red), var(--lcars-orange)]
    core:
      color: var(--lcars-ice)
  # stretched clouds with dust across them
  - type: nebula
    render: volume
    at: [0, -70, 0]
    size: [300, 60, 80]
    count: 8
    stretch: 0.7
    dust:
      count: 3
    colors: [var(--lcars-violet), var(--lcars-blue)]
    core:
      color: var(--lcars-ice)
```

::: details More about the shapes
- **`clouds`** (the default): the clouds themselves.
- **`shell`:** a thin hollow sphere, a ring with a dark middle from any side (the Ring nebula).
- **`bipolar`:** an hourglass along the object's y axis, two hollow lobes joined at a narrow waist, the gas streaked outward (the Butterfly, the Hourglass).
- **`filaments`:** long thin strands running along the object's x axis (the Veil).
- **`cavity`:** a thick cup round a hollow that opens on the object's +z side: a bright bowl seen from there, a crescent from the side (a blister, as in Orion).
- **`layers`:** a floor and a ceiling of gas across a box with a gap between: see [the Badlands](#the-badlands-layers-columns-and-lightning).
- **`wake`:** a bright ribbon waving along the object's x axis and a sheet of gas trailing it: see [the Nexus](#the-nexus-a-ribbon-and-its-wake).
- **Hand-placed clouds** take `size` and `rotation` instead of `stretch`: see [Dust lanes](#dust-lanes).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shape` | string | `clouds` | `render: volume`: the form of the gas: `clouds`, `shell`, `bipolar`, `filaments`, `cavity`, `layers` or `wake` |
| `stretch` | number | `0` | How drawn out each seeded cloud is, `0` (round) to `1` (long and flat) |
| `core.color` | colour | - | A colour deep in the gas, running out to the cloud colours at the edges. Left out: the cloud colours throughout |

### Dust lanes

**Dust is dark gas in a volume nebula that hides the gas behind it: lay a few dark clouds across the gas with `dust.count`, or place one by hand with `dust: true`.** A lane placed by hand through a bright cloud reads most clearly.

- With `blend: add` (the default) the dust darkens only this nebula's own gas, so the stars behind still show through; with `blend: normal` it hides what is behind the nebula too.
- Dust clouds the seed lays have a seed of their own, so adding dust moves no gas cloud.
- `clouds` places clouds by hand, instead of `count` and the seed: up to 10 gas clouds and 4 dust clouds.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 300
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 0
      tilt: 0
      distance: 400
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 2000
objects:
  - type: nebula
    render: volume
    radius: 130
    colors: [var(--lcars-orange)]
    clouds:
      # a bright cloud
      - xyz: [0, 0, 0]
        radius: 100
        opacity: 0.9
      # a long dark lane across it
      - xyz: [0, 0, 40]
        size: [200, 20, 30]
        rotation: [0, 0, 20]
        dust: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dust.count` | number | `0` | Dark dust clouds the seed lays across the gas clouds, 0 to 4 |
| `dust.amount` | number | `0.8` | How dark the dust is, `0` to `1` |
| `dust.color` | colour | black | The dust's colour |
| `clouds` | list | - | Clouds placed by hand, instead of `count` and the seed |
| `clouds[].xyz` | `[x, y, z]` | `[0, 0, 0]` | Where the cloud sits, scene units from the object |
| `clouds[].radius` | number | halfway between `min_radius` and `max_radius` | Cloud radius, scene units |
| `clouds[].size` | `[w, h, d]` | - | Or an ellipsoid, scene units. Replaces `radius` |
| `clouds[].rotation` | `[x, y, z]` | - | Turns the ellipsoid, degrees, as an object's `rotation` |
| `clouds[].color` | colour | the next of `colors` | This cloud's colour. Without it, the clouds take `colors` in order |
| `clouds[].opacity` | number | the middle of `brightness` | Opacity, `0` to `1` |
| `clouds[].dust` | boolean | `false` | `render: volume`: a dark dust cloud (`dust.amount`, `dust.color`) instead of glowing gas |

### The Badlands: layers, columns and lightning

**The Badlands, the plasma storms of Deep Space Nine and Voyager, start from a preset: `preset: badlands` (Deep Space Nine) or `preset: badlands_voyager` (Voyager).** Fly the camera into the gap between the sheets.

- `badlands`: liquid fire in yellow, orange and red, an orange band glowing between the sheets, fire columns thick and thin.
- `badlands_voyager`: peach and mauve layers, held pink lightning columns, strikes that light the gas.
- Every key you set wins over the preset's; in `band`, `columns` and `lightning` key by key, so `columns: { count: 3 }` keeps the preset's kind and colour.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 360
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 30
      tilt: 3
      distance: 110
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 2000
objects:
  - type: nebula
    preset: badlands
```

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 360
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 200
      tilt: 3
      distance: 160
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 2000
objects:
  - type: nebula
    preset: badlands_voyager
```

::: details More about the Badlands
- **What the presets are:** both are `render: volume` with `shape: layers` in a `size: [500, 140, 500]` box (Voyager's 160 high): a floor and a ceiling of gas with their surfaces rolled into ridges, `colors` running from each sheet's surface into its depth.
- **Deep Space Nine's** sets `veins: 0.8`, a narrower `gap` of `0.4`, a brighter band and eight fire columns from `1` to `3` times the usual width.
- **Voyager's** sets seven lightning columns, a butter-coloured band and strikes in the gas.
- **Your own box:** the preset's box is 500 across; with a `size` (or `radius`) of your own, its `drift` scales with it, so the gas churns as fast for its size. A drift you set stays as you wrote it.
- **Turning parts off:** `band: false` or `lightning: false` drops that part of the preset; `true` keeps the preset's settings.
- **Lightning anywhere:** `lightning` works on any volume nebula, not only `layers`, and a [lightning object](./objects/lines#lightning) striking inside any volume nebula lights its gas too. The strikes take the nebula's `seed` unless you give them one.
- **Reduced motion:** the columns stand still and no strike shows.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `preset` | string | - | `badlands`, `badlands_voyager` (or `nexus`, [below](#the-nexus-a-ribbon-and-its-wake)): a named nebula to start from |
| `gap` | number | `0.56` | `shape: layers`: how much of the height is open between the sheets, `0` (they touch) to `0.9` |
| `veins` | number | `0` | `shape: layers`: bright fine veins in the sheets' surfaces with darker gas between (liquid fire), `0` to `1` |
| `band` | boolean / object | `false` | `shape: layers`: light glowing in the gap, brightest in a thin sheet at its middle |
| `band.brightness` | number | `1` | How bright, `0` to `3` |
| `band.width` | number | `0.08` | How far the glow reaches from the middle, a fraction of half the height |
| `band.color` | colour | `var(--lcards-moonlight)` | The band's colour |
| `columns` | object | - | `shape: layers`: columns from the floor to the ceiling: see [Columns](#columns) |
| `lightning` | boolean / object | `false` | Strikes inside the gas that light it: `true`, or the [lightning object's](./objects/lines#lightning) `rate`, `flash`, `color`, `glow`, `width`, `jaggedness`, `branches`, `brightness` and `seed` |

### Columns

**`columns` stands fire, vortices or held lightning from the floor to the ceiling of a `layers` nebula, spread over the region.** A field of vortices, with the funnels joined into columns, is a storm of its own.

- `fire` is rising flame, wide at the foot with a splash ring on the floor; its white-hot heart takes `columns.color` and its edge the sheets' surface colour.
- `vortex` is a twisting funnel, narrow at its middle (`waist`) and dark at its rim.
- `lightning` is a held, crawling bolt that lights the gas round it.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 360
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 200
      tilt: 4
      distance: 150
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 2000
objects:
  - type: nebula
    render: volume
    shape: layers
    size: [500, 160, 500]
    count: 6
    seed: 8
    drift: [3, 0]
    colors: [var(--lcars-violet-creme), var(--lcars-violet), var(--lcars-blue)]
    band:
      brightness: 0.8
      color: var(--lcars-violet-creme)
    columns:
      count: 6
      kind: vortex
      waist: 0.4
      width: 1.5
      color: var(--lcars-violet-creme)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `columns.kind` | string | `fire` | `fire`, `vortex` or `lightning` |
| `columns.count` | number | `4` | How many, 1 to 10, spread over the region |
| `columns.width` | number / `[min, max]` | `1` | `fire` and `vortex`: how thick, times the usual. A pair gives each column its own width between them, so thick columns and thin strands stand together |
| `columns.waist` | number | `0.2` | `vortex`: how wide the middle is against the ends, `0.05` (two funnels meeting at a point) to `1` (one straight column) |
| `columns.speed` | number | `1` | `lightning`: how fast the bolts crawl and flicker. `0.5` is half as fast, `0` still |
| `columns.color` | colour | `var(--lcards-moonlight)` | The fire's white-hot heart, the vortex, or the bolt |
| `columns.glow.color` | colour | the column colour | `lightning`: the glow round the bolts |

### The Nexus: a ribbon and its wake

**The Nexus, the ribbon of energy in Star Trek Generations, starts from `preset: nexus`: a white-hot ribbon waving across a long box, a wake of pink and red gas streaming out behind it, and small discharges crawling off it and lighting the gas.**

- The preset is `render: volume` with `shape: wake` in a `size: [2000, 500, 500]` box: the ribbon waves along the object's x axis near the bottom of the region and the gas trails up from it, `colors` running from the ribbon out, white-hot right at it.
- Every key you set wins over the preset's; in `ribbon`, `wake` and `lightning` key by key.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 360
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, -60, 0]
      yaw: 8
      tilt: 6
      distance: 1500
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 3000
objects:
  - type: nebula
    preset: nexus
```

::: details More about the Nexus
- **Your own box:** with a `size` (or `radius`) of your own, the ribbon's `speed` scales with its length, so the waves run as fast for its size. A speed you set stays as you wrote it.
- **Discharges:** `lightning.mode: crawl` (the preset's) puts short bolts and small loops on the ribbon that flicker and jump along it, in place of strikes. It works only with `shape: wake`.
- **The glow's colour** defaults to the first of `colors`.
- **Reduced motion:** the ribbon holds still, and the discharges stand still and dim.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ribbon` | boolean / object | `true` | `shape: wake`: the bright line and the curve it follows. `false`: the gas only |
| `ribbon.waves` | number | `2.5` | How many waves along it, end to end |
| `ribbon.amplitude` | number | `0.2` | How far it waves, a fraction of half the region's height (a little less in depth), up to `0.5` |
| `ribbon.speed` | number | `0` (the preset: `40`) | How fast the waves run along it, scene units a second; the wake streams out from it as fast. Negative runs the other way |
| `ribbon.width` | number | `6` (the preset: `4`) | The line's width, px |
| `ribbon.color` | colour | `var(--lcards-moonlight)` | The line's colour, and the gas right at it |
| `ribbon.glow` | boolean / object | `true` | The glow round the line and in the gas near it |
| `ribbon.glow.color` | colour | the first of `colors` | The glow's colour |
| `ribbon.glow.width` | number | `8` | How wide the outer glow is, times the line's width |
| `wake.side` | string | `up` | Which way the gas trails: `up`, or `down` (the ribbon near the top). Turn the object with `rotation` to trail it another way |
| `wake.lean` | number | `0` | How far the gas leans along the ribbon as it goes out, `-1` to `1`: a fan trailing to one side, seen from afar |
| `lightning.mode` | string | `strike` (the preset: `crawl`) | `crawl`: discharges crawling off the ribbon. `strike`: bolts in the gas |
| `lightning.count` | number | `6` | `crawl`: how many at once, 1 to 40 |
| `lightning.reach` | number | `0.35` | `crawl`: how far they stand off the ribbon, a fraction of half the height |
| `lightning.speed` | number | `1` | `crawl`: how fast they flicker, reshape and jump |

### A travelling Nexus

**To send the Nexus travelling, put it `at:` a moving point with `face: motion`.** Facing turns the object's +z along the travel, so `rotation: [-90, 0, 0]` turns the wake (its +y) to trail behind.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 360
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 0
      tilt: 35
      distance: 7000
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 3000
points:
  - id: nexus
    polar: [2500, 0]
    object: track
    label: NEXUS
objects:
  # the point rides this spinning ring
  - type: ring
    id: track
    radius: 2500
    spin: 3
    width: 0.5
    opacity: 0.15
  - type: nebula
    preset: nexus
    at: nexus
    size: [1500, 400, 400]
    face: motion
    rotation: [-90, 0, 0]
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Keys every object takes](./objects#keys-every-object-takes) | | | `at`, `face` and `rotation`; see [Facing the way it goes](./objects#facing-the-way-it-goes) |

## Scan bands

**`scan` on a `grid`, `sphere`, `volume` or `model` sends a bright band across its lines, as the background grid's `scan_period` does.** Use it for a sensor sweep across a map, a planet being scanned, or a ship's hologram.

- A sphere sweeps from pole to pole, a dome from the top to its rim, a cylinder top to bottom, and a plane runs south to north.
- A polar disc rings out from its centre like a sensor ping, and a volume sweeps down its walls.
- On a [model](./objects/ships#model) the band runs along its longest side, in the hologram look.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 320
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 10, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 25
      distance: 260
objects:
  # a ping ringing out from the centre
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 100
    pattern: polar
    line_spacing: 10
    spoke_count: 36
    scan:
      period: 6
      color: var(--lcars-yellow)
  # pole to pole
  - type: sphere
    at: [-50, 25, 0]
    radius: 22
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
    scan:
      period: 5
  # down the walls
  - type: volume
    shape: sector
    radius: [55, 95]
    angle: [100, 170]
    height: [0, 30]
    color: var(--lcars-green)
    scan:
      period: 4
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scan.period` | number | `0` | Seconds per sweep. `0`: none. Stops under reduced motion |
| `scan.color` | colour | `var(--lcards-moonlight)` | The band's colour |

## Moving dashes and pulses

**A dashed line can move its dashes along it, and any line can send bright pulses along it, as the [flow](/core/effects/background-animations/preset-reference#flow) preset's streaks do.** Use it for traffic on a route, power along a conduit, or a ring that turns.

- `dash` with `pattern` and `speed` moves the dashes on a `ring`, `path` or `trail`, `speed` px per second (negative runs backwards). Dashes keep their px size at any distance, so they move at the same speed on screen near or far.
- `pulse` works on a `ring`, `path`, `trail` and `beam`. Pulses add light, so on a coloured line they burn toward white.
- With `dash.speed` set, the pulses move at that speed too; else at `pulse.speed`.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 340
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 40
      distance: 320
points:
  - id: hub
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    marker: diamond
    label: HUB
    style: major
  - id: alpha
    polar: [70, 30]
    marker: dot
    label: ALPHA
  - id: beta
    polar: [60, 150]
    marker: dot
    label: BETA
  - id: gamma
    polar: [80, 260]
    marker: dot
    label: GAMMA
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 100
    pattern: polar
    line_spacing: 20
    spoke_count: 12
    opacity: 0.5
  # pulses with the defaults
  - type: path
    from: hub
    to: alpha
    arc: 10
    color: var(--lcars-orange)
    pulse: true
  # moving dashes
  - type: path
    from: hub
    to: beta
    arc: 10
    color: var(--lcars-orange)
    dash:
      pattern: [8, 6]
      speed: 30
  # longer, rarer yellow pulses
  - type: path
    from: hub
    to: gamma
    arc: 10
    width: 2
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
    pulse:
      length: 24
      gap: 120
      color: var(--lcars-yellow)
  # a ring whose dashes turn
  - type: ring
    radius: 100
    width: 2
    dash:
      pattern: [12, 8]
      speed: 20
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dash.pattern` | list | solid | Dashes as `[on, off]` in px (more pairs repeat) |
| `dash.speed` | number | `0` | Move the dashes (and pulses) along the line, px per second; negative runs backwards |
| `pulse` | boolean / object | off | Bright pulses moving along the line: `true`, or their settings |
| [Line keys](./objects/lines#line-keys) | | | `pulse.length` (`14`), `pulse.gap` (`90`), `pulse.width`, `pulse.color` (`var(--lcards-moonlight)`) and `pulse.speed` (`80`) |

## Animated surface fills

**`fill.effect` paints an animated pattern on a `sphere`'s body or under a `grid`'s lines: a star's surface, a gas giant's bands, an ocean, a density map.** The types are the [plasma](/core/effects/background-animations/preset-reference#plasma), [fluid](/core/effects/background-animations/preset-reference#fluid) and [contour-field](/core/effects/background-animations/preset-reference#contour-field) presets, plus `bands` (belts round the latitude, a gas giant) and `swirl` (gas spiralling in, [below](#swirls)).

- The pattern is drawn in 3D, so it has no seam round a sphere and no pinch at its poles, and it turns with `spin`.
- On a sphere it is painted over `fill.color` in place of `image`, and the body still hides what is behind it.
- `preset` starts from a [planet type](#planet-types); the keys you set win over it.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 320
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 10, 0]
      yaw: 15
      tilt: 30
      distance: 230
objects:
  # contour bands under a grid's lines
  - type: grid
    shape: plane
    size: [220, 140]
    line_spacing: 20
    opacity: 0.6
    fill:
      effect:
        type: contour
        colors: [var(--lcars-blue), var(--lcars-green), var(--lcars-yellow), var(--lcars-orange)]
        num_bands: 6
        fill_level: 0.3
        opacity: 0.5
  # a star's surface
  - type: sphere
    at: [-60, 30, 0]
    radius: 24
    line_spacing_deg: 30
    opacity: 0.4
    fill:
      effect:
        type: plasma
        color_a: var(--lcars-orange)
        color_b: var(--lcars-yellow)
        speed: 2
  - type: sphere
    at: [10, 30, -10]
    radius: 20
    opacity: 0.3
    spin: 4
    fill:
      effect:
        type: contour
        colors: [var(--lcars-orange), var(--lcars-yellow), var(--lcars-red)]
        num_bands: 8
  # an ocean
  - type: sphere
    at: [70, 25, 10]
    radius: 18
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
    fill:
      effect:
        type: fluid
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
```

::: details More about fills
- **Detail:** `base_frequency` is features per scene unit, about 3 across the object's radius by default; `num_octaves` adds layers of finer detail.
- **Motion:** with `speed` above 0 the pattern flows through the object; under reduced motion it holds still.
- **Entities:** the fill's numbers and colours can follow entities, as on any object: see [Live data](./data#settings-from-entities).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fill.effect.preset` | string | - | A [planet type](#planet-types) to start from |
| `fill.effect.type` | string | the preset's, else `plasma` | `plasma` (two-colour bands), `fluid` (a one-colour wash), `contour` (stepped topographic bands), `bands` (belts round the latitude) or `swirl` (gas spiralling in) |
| `fill.effect.color_a` | colour | `var(--lcars-blue)` | `plasma`: the first colour |
| `fill.effect.color_b` | colour | `var(--lcars-orange)` | `plasma`: the second colour |
| `fill.effect.color` | colour | `var(--lcars-blue)` | `fluid`: the wash colour; its alpha is how strong the wash is |
| `fill.effect.colors` | colour / list | blue to orange | `contour`: stops from low to high. `bands`: the belt colours, repeated from the south pole to the north. `swirl`: stops from the middle out to the rim |
| `fill.effect.num_bands` | number | `5` | `contour`: how many bands. `bands`: how many belts pole to pole. `2` to `64` |
| `fill.effect.fill_level` | number | `0` | `contour`: flood the lowest bands, `0` to `0.95` |
| `fill.effect.fill_color` | colour | see-through | `contour`: the colour over the flooded bands |
| `fill.effect.blend_colors` | boolean | `true` | `contour` and `bands`: colours fade between bands. `false`: hard edges |
| `fill.effect.turbulence` | number | `0.3` | `bands`: how much the belt edges swirl, `0` (straight) to `1` (stormy). `swirl`: how much the gas clumps and how ragged its edge is |
| `fill.effect.base_frequency` | number | about 3 across the radius | Detail: features per scene unit. Lower is larger features |
| `fill.effect.num_octaves` | number | `2` contour, `3` plasma, `4` the others | Layers of finer detail, `1` (smooth) to `8` (rough) |
| `fill.effect.speed` | number | `0` | How fast the pattern flows through the object, scene units per second. `swirl`: how fast the gas turns at the rim |
| `fill.effect.opacity` | number | `1` | The fill's opacity, `0` to `1` |

### Swirls

**`type: swirl` is gas spiralling in round the object's y axis: a whirlpool, an accretion disc, a wormhole's mouth.** On a `well` grid the gas pours down the funnel; on a `disc` it lies flat.

- It turns faster toward the middle and is streaked along the spiral, with dark lanes of thinner gas between the streaks, a rippled heart and a ragged outer edge that trails off in wisps (`turbulence`).
- `colors` run from the heart out to the rim, and `speed` is how fast it turns at the rim.
- Set `line_width: 0` and `edges: false` on the grid to show the gas alone.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 340
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, -2, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 40
      distance: 34
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: well
    well:
      throat: 0.07
    radius: 15
    depth: 5
    line_width: 0
    edges: false
    fill:
      effect:
        type: swirl
        colors: [var(--lcards-moonlight), var(--lcards-orange-lightest), var(--lcars-violet), var(--lcards-blue-medium), var(--lcars-violet), var(--lcards-blue-dark)]
        speed: 3
        turbulence: 0.8
        num_octaves: 5
  - type: glow
    at: [0, 3, 0]
    size: 10
    color: var(--lcards-orange-lightest)
```

::: details More about swirls
- **A whole wormhole:** the [Bajoran wormhole starter](./starters#bajoran-wormhole) builds a mouth from a swirl, with a shaft of light, sparkling stars and wisps of gas.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Fill keys](#animated-surface-fills) | | | `type: swirl` with `colors`, `speed`, `turbulence` and the detail keys |

### Planet types

**`preset` starts a fill from a planet type: its type, colours (from the LCARdS palette, so they follow the theme) and detail.** Anything you set on top wins, so `preset: gas_giant` with `num_bands: 9` is a gas giant with fewer belts.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 340
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 0
      tilt: 10
      distance: 130
objects:
  - type: sphere
    at: [-48, 14, 0]
    radius: 10
    line_width: 0.5
    spin: 8
    fill:
      effect:
        preset: gas_giant
  - type: sphere
    at: [-16, 14, 0]
    radius: 10
    line_width: 0.5
    spin: 8
    fill:
      effect:
        preset: ringed_giant
  - type: sphere
    at: [16, 14, 0]
    radius: 10
    line_width: 0.5
    spin: 8
    fill:
      effect:
        preset: ice_giant
  - type: sphere
    at: [48, 14, 0]
    radius: 10
    line_width: 0.5
    spin: 8
    fill:
      effect:
        preset: storm_giant
  - type: sphere
    at: [-48, -14, 0]
    radius: 10
    line_width: 0.5
    spin: 8
    fill:
      effect:
        preset: clouds
  - type: sphere
    at: [-16, -14, 0]
    radius: 10
    line_width: 0.5
    spin: 8
    fill:
      effect:
        preset: lava
  - type: sphere
    at: [16, -14, 0]
    radius: 10
    line_width: 0.5
    spin: 8
    fill:
      effect:
        preset: ice
  - type: sphere
    at: [48, -14, 0]
    radius: 10
    line_width: 0.5
    spin: 8
    fill:
      effect:
        preset: terran
```

| `preset` | Looks like | Built on |
|---|---|---|
| `gas_giant` | Jupiter: orange and cream belts, stormy edges | `bands` |
| `ringed_giant` | Saturn: pale gold belts, calm | `bands` |
| `ice_giant` | Uranus: pale blue, faint belts | `bands` |
| `storm_giant` | Neptune: deep blue belts, streaked | `bands` |
| `clouds` | Venus from space: a cream cloud deck, slowly churning | `bands` |
| `lava` | Dark crust with glowing cracks | `contour` |
| `ice` | White and pale blue ice | `contour` |
| `rocky` | Grey highlands and plains | `contour` |
| `terran` | Oceans, land and ice caps | `contour` |

## Warp and dust

**A fly-to with `warp` streaks the stars past the camera, and `backdrop.dust` fills the space round the camera with faint particles that show depth on every move.** The streaks grow with the camera's speed and shrink back to stars as it lands.

- Turn warp on for every fly-to with `camera.warp: true`, for one view with `warp: true` in that view (a point's or object's `view` takes it too), or for one action with `warp: true` on its `fly-to` (or the [`lcards.fly_to`](/configuration/ha-actions#lcards-fly-to) action); `false` there turns it off.
- The streaks follow how fast the camera moves for its distance from what it looks at, so a hop between planets streaks as a jump across the galaxy does.
- The dust stays put as the camera moves, unlike the stars at infinity, and streaks in a warp too. It has no edge: particles fade out at `radius` from the camera and new ones fade in ahead as it travels, and coming back to a place shows the same dust.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 340
camera:
  view: far
  fly_duration: 2400
  views:
    far:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 20
      distance: 600
    near:
      target: [40, 5, 30]
      yaw: 30
      tilt: 10
      distance: 25
      warp: true
  buttons: true
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 4000
    max_radius: 1.4
    spectrum: true
  dust:
    count: 1500
points:
  # tap the label to warp in
  - id: core
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    label: GALACTIC CORE
    style: title
    tap_action:
      action: fly-to
      view: near
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 100
    pattern: polar
    line_spacing: 10
    spoke_count: 36
    opacity: 0.6
  # tap the glow to fly back out
  - type: glow
    at: core
    size: 50
    color: var(--lcars-yellow)
    tap_action:
      action: fly-to
      view: far
```

::: details More about warp and dust
- **Following a toggle:** `camera.warp` with an `entity` makes fly-tos streak while it is on (`on`, `true`, `yes`, `engaged`, `open`, `home`, or a number above 0), such as an `input_boolean`.
- **Spectrum:** `backdrop.stars.spectrum: true` splits each streak into colour, as a Doppler shift of the star's own colour: violet toward the tail (nearer the direction of flight) and red toward the head. White stars show the whole rainbow; a blue star streaks green to violet, its tail fading as it shifts past violet, and a red star the other way. `spectrum.direction: reverse` puts violet at the head instead.
- **Denser dust:** a smaller `radius` is denser and shows depth on smaller moves.
- **Reduced motion:** nothing streaks.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `camera.warp` | boolean / object | `false` | Every fly-to streaks the stars and dust; a view's own `warp` wins |
| `camera.warp.entity` | string | - | Fly-tos streak while this entity is on |
| `camera.warp.attribute` | string | - | Read this attribute instead of the state |
| `camera.views.<name>.warp` | boolean | `camera.warp` | Streak on the way to this view |
| `backdrop.stars.streak` | number | `1` | How long the streaks are, a multiple of the usual length. `0`: never |
| `backdrop.stars.spectrum` | boolean / object | off | Split each streak into colour |
| `backdrop.stars.spectrum.direction` | string | `doppler` | `doppler`: violet toward the tail. `reverse`: violet toward the head |
| `backdrop.dust` | boolean / object | off | Depth dust round the camera: `true`, or the keys below |
| `backdrop.dust.count` | number | `800` | How many particles (about half are within reach of the camera at any time) |
| `backdrop.dust.radius` | number | 1.5 times the scene's radius | How far round the camera the dust reaches, scene units |
| `backdrop.dust.min_radius` | number | `0.4` | Smallest particle radius, px |
| `backdrop.dust.max_radius` | number | `1` | Largest particle radius, px |
| `backdrop.dust.brightness` | `[min, max]` | `[0.35, 1]` | Each particle's brightness is picked between these |
| `backdrop.dust.color` | colour | `var(--lcards-moonlight)` | Particle colour |
| `backdrop.dust.colors` | list | - | Several colours, picked per particle. Wins over `color` |
| `backdrop.dust.opacity` | number | `1` | Fades the whole dust layer, `0` to `1` |
| `backdrop.dust.seed` | number | `7` | The same seed places the same dust |
| `backdrop.dust.spectrum` | boolean / object | off | Split the dust's streaks into colour, as on the stars |

### Going to warp

**`warp` on the card sends the ship to warp where it is: the scene's own backdrop stars and dust streak along the view, and the [warp starfield](/core/effects/background-animations/preset-reference#warp-starfield) streams past behind the scene.** `false` drops out of warp again; both `warp` and `warp_factor` can follow entities, so a toggle and a slider make an ENGAGE button and a warp factor control.

- `warp` reads `on`, `true`, `yes`, `engaged`, `open`, `home` or a number above 0 as engaged.
- Going to warp takes about two seconds, dropping out a little less; a change of warp factor eases too.
- `camera.warp` is different: it streaks the stars only while a fly-to moves the camera.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 320
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 0
      tilt: 10
      distance: 120
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 3000
    spectrum: true
  dust:
    count: 1500
# at warp while the toggle is on: tap ENGAGE
warp:
  entity: input_boolean.demo_toggle
# the warp factor from a slider, 1 to 9.9
warp_factor:
  entity: input_number.lcards_test_power
  output: [1, 9.9]
points:
  - id: engage
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    marker: square
    style: major
    label: ENGAGE (TAP)
    tap_action:
      action: toggle
      entity: input_boolean.demo_toggle
```

::: details More about going to warp
- **With spectrum:** with `backdrop.stars.spectrum`, the backdrop streaks are in colour.
- **Reduced motion:** nothing streams.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `warp` | boolean / object | `false` | Go to warp. `false` drops out |
| `warp.entity` | string | - | At warp while this entity is on |
| `warp.attribute` | string | - | Read this attribute instead of the state |
| `warp_factor` | number | `6` | How long the streaks grow and how fast they stream, `1` to `9.9`. Can [follow an entity](./data#settings-from-entities) |

## Cost

**A still effect costs nothing between frames, because a still scene draws nothing; an effect that moves costs a little on every frame.** Most scenes stay well inside the time a smooth frame allows.

- A volume nebula costs more than puffs, and a little more again seen from inside the gas. A `shape`, `stretch`, `core.color` or dust adds a little on top.
- The Badlands are the costliest effect, most of all from inside with columns and `veins`; their lightning adds little.
- The Nexus costs little more than a plain volume nebula.
- The nebula and fill shaders load in a small extra download the first time a card uses one.

# Your Own Models

**Any ship, station or other object can come from a glTF file of your own (`.glb` or `.gltf`), drawn by the [model](./objects/ships#model) object.** LCARdS also ships a few [built-in models](./objects/ships#built-in-models): the Constitution-class and Galaxy-class starships, Deep Space 9, Earth Spacedock and a Utopia Planitia drydock.

In short:

1. Get a `.glb` file (see [where models come from](#where-models-come-from)).
2. Copy it into `/config/www/lcards/models/` (the [My models folder](#the-my-models-folder)).
3. In the [Astrometrics Studio](./start#the-studio), add a model object, set **Src** to **Browse Home Assistant media**, and pick it under **LCARdS**, **My models**.
4. Set its `size`, and `rotation` if it faces the wrong way ([make it fit](#make-it-fit)).

## Where models come from

**Download one from a community site, or make your own in a 3D tool that exports glTF.**

- **Community sites** such as Sketchfab have many fan-made ship and station models, some free to download. Pick **GLB** when the site offers it; a **glTF** download is a folder (a `.gltf` file with a `.bin` file and textures) that works too, kept together.
- **Your own** models can be made in Blender or any 3D tool that exports glTF.
- **Check the license before you use a model.** Fan-made models of ships from films and series are fan art of designs their studios own, and some uploads are taken from games without permission even when the page shows an open license. LCARdS does not ship, link to or download third-party models; what you load on your own dashboard is your call.

## The My models folder

**LCARdS keeps your models in `/config/www/lcards/models/` and shows that folder in the Home Assistant media browser as LCARdS, My models.**

- `/config/www/lcards/` is the LCARdS user folder; `models/` in it is for your models (other kinds of files may get folders beside it later).
- LCARdS creates the folder when it starts. **Updating LCARdS never touches it**: updates replace `custom_components/lcards/`, not `www/`. It is in your Home Assistant backups like the rest of `/config`.
- Copy files in with the File editor or Studio Code Server add-on, a Samba share, or any way you reach `/config`. Subfolders are fine (`ships/odyssey.glb`). Keep a `.gltf` and its `.bin` and texture files together in one folder.

::: details More about the folder
- **Not private:** like everything in `/config/www`, the files can be fetched without logging in (on `/lcards-user/...` and on `/local/lcards/...`) by anyone who can reach your Home Assistant and knows their names. Keep only models there.
- **What it lists:** the media browser lists `.glb` and `.gltf` files only.
- **No uploads:** uploading through the media browser does not work here. Home Assistant's own media folder only takes audio, video and images, which is why LCARdS has its own.
:::

## Pick it

**In the Studio, a model's Src (and every image field: a planet's texture, an image object) has three sources.**

| Source | What it sets | For |
|---|---|---|
| **Asset library** | `builtin:<name>` | The models (or images) LCARdS ships |
| **Custom path** | `/local/...` or an `https://` URL | A file anywhere in `/config/www` (it is `/local/...`), or on a web server that allows it |
| **Browse Home Assistant media** | `media-source://...` | My models (and, for images, your Home Assistant media) |

- A file from another web server only loads if that server allows it (CORS); download the file instead when in doubt. A page that offers a download does not count: the link has to be the file itself.
- The same in YAML is below. The files are your own, so this example is not live:

```yaml
objects:
  # from My models, as the media browser picks it
  - type: model
    id: odyssey
    src: media-source://lcards/my_models/odyssey.glb
    size: 60
  # any file in /config/www
  - type: model
    id: runabout
    src: /local/models/runabout.glb
    size: 8
```

## Make it fit

**A model from elsewhere comes in its maker's units, facing their way, with their part names.** These keys size it, turn it and read its units.

- `size` scales the model so its largest extent fits, whatever units the file uses. To keep models in proportion instead, leave `size` out in a scene with `units`: each is drawn at its [real size](./objects/ships#real-size).
- LCARdS models face +z (bow forward). A model that comes in sideways or nose-up needs a quarter turn, such as `rotation: [0, 90, 0]` or `[-90, 0, 0]`.
- glTF files are in metres unless their maker got it wrong: if a model comes out a hundred times too large, try `file_units: cm`; at an odd scale, give its `length` instead.
```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 320
units: km
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 150
      tilt: 20
      distance: 1.6
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 1500
objects:
  # no size: drawn at its real length, 0.64 km
  - type: model
    src: builtin:galaxy_class
    at: [-0.35, 0, 0]
  # turned a quarter round, its own colours
  - type: model
    src: builtin:constitution_class_refit
    at: [0.35, 0, 0]
    rotation: [0, 90, 0]
    material: original
```

::: details More about fitting
- **Labels on its parts:** `part:` on a point puts it on a named part (a node in the file). Names in downloaded files are often like `Object_12`; in the Studio's Points tab the part list fills in from the file once it has loaded, so you can try them. See [points on a model](./objects/ships#points-on-a-model).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | number | real size | Its largest extent, scene units. Left out: its real size in a scene with `units`, else 50 scene units |
| `length` | number | - | Its real length in metres, for a file not at its true scale: drawn that long at its real size, whatever the file measures |
| `file_units` | string | `m` | The units the file was made in, for its real size: `m`, `cm`, `mm`, `km`, `ft` or `in` |
| `rotation` | `[x, y, z]` | `[0, 0, 0]` | Turn it, degrees |
| `material` | string | `hologram` | `hologram` works on any model: glow, rim, scanlines, edges. `original` shows the file's own colours and textures, lit |
| `face` | string | - | `motion`: on a moving point, the model turns to face where it is going. Or a point id to face. See [Facing the way it goes](./objects#facing-the-way-it-goes) |

## Make it light

**The model is drawn on every frame the scene moves, and downloaded with the dashboard, so a smaller file is better on every device.** The built-in models have 10,000 to 20,000 triangles each, in files of 220 to 410 KB; models made for games or renders can have 100,000 or more, and tens of MB of textures.

- **Any size loads**, but every device that shows the dashboard downloads the whole file and holds it in memory: a 100 MB model is slow to appear on a phone and may not load on a small tablet.
- **Compress and simplify** with [glTF Transform](https://gltf-transform.dev/) (needs Node.js), as below. Blender's Decimate modifier also reduces triangles before export.
- **Draco** compression is not supported (the loader is not shipped); `meshopt` below writes a file the card reads.
- A hologram ignores textures, so a model you only show as a hologram can be exported without them.

```sh
npx @gltf-transform/cli inspect ship.glb                     # triangles, textures, sizes
npx @gltf-transform/cli simplify ship.glb ship-small.glb --ratio 0.25
npx @gltf-transform/cli resize ship-small.glb ship-small.glb --width 1024 --height 1024
npx @gltf-transform/cli meshopt ship-small.glb ship-small.glb
```

::: details More about heavy models
- **Feature edges** are off by default on a model over 250,000 triangles: working them out takes seconds on a model that dense (2.5 million triangles froze the page for 11 seconds), and they would be noise anyway. `edges: true` draws them.
:::

## When it does not show

**A dim stand-in box shows while the file loads, and stays if it fails.** The browser console (filter on `Astrometrics`) says why:

- **not found / could not resolve:** the path or the picked file is gone; pick it again.
- **slow to appear, or the tab runs out of memory:** the file is too big for that device; see [make it light](#make-it-light).
- **Draco-compressed:** convert it with `meshopt` as above.
- **blocked (CORS):** the file is on a server that does not allow it; copy it into My models.
- **has no part:** the name is not in the file; the message lists the names it has.

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/astrometrics/objects/lines.html -->

# Lines and Light

Lines through the scene and lights in it: routes, beams, trails behind moving points, lightning and glows. The keys every object takes (`id`, `at`, `rotation`, `opacity`, `visible` ...) are on the [Objects](../objects#keys-every-object-takes) page.

## path

**A line through a list of points, or from one point to another.** Use it for a route between places, a supply line, or an outline drawn in the scene.

- List the places in `points` (point ids or `[x, y, z]`), or give just `from` and `to`. A path through point ids moves when those points move.
- `arc` bends each leg upward into a curve, so a route between two places on a map reads as a flight path rather than a straight line.
- A path with `at` is a shape drawn round that point: each `[x, y, z]` is measured from `at`, so the shape moves and turns with it.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 300
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 40
      distance: 170
points:
  - id: star
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    marker: reticle
    label: STAR
  - id: outpost
    polar: [60, 250]
    marker: dot
    label: OUTPOST
  - id: relay
    polar: [55, 60]
    marker: dot
    label: RELAY
objects:
  - type: ring
    at: star
    radius: 30
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
  # a route from the outpost past the star to the relay
  - type: path
    points: [outpost, star, relay]
    arc: 15
    width: 2
    colors: [var(--lcars-orange), var(--lcars-yellow)]
    glow: true
  # a pipe drawn round the star, with pulses running along it
  - type: path
    at: star
    points:
      - [-40, -25, 0]
      - [0, -32, 0]
      - [40, -25, 0]
    arc: 6
    width: 8
    line_look: tube
    pulse: true
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
```

::: details More about path
- **Ids and offsets together:** with `at`, a point id in `points` still means that point, wherever it is; only the `[x, y, z]` entries are measured from `at`.
- **The track of the sun or moon:** `sky: sun` (or `moon`) with `object: <dome grid id>` draws today's track across the sky on that dome, split where it goes under the horizon. `points`, `from` and `to` are not used then.
- **Looks:** a path is part of the diagram look; the realistic [look](../scene#looks-diagram-and-realistic) hides it unless the path sets `look: all`.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `points` | list | - | The places the line passes through, in order: point ids or `[x, y, z]`. With `at`, each `[x, y, z]` is an offset from `at` |
| `from` | id / `[x, y, z]` | - | Start, instead of `points` |
| `to` | id / `[x, y, z]` | - | End, instead of `points` |
| `arc` | number | `0` | Lift each leg into a curve this high at its middle, scene units. `0` is straight |
| `sky` | string | - | `sun` or `moon`: draw today's track of that body on the dome in `object` |
| `object` | string | - | With `sky`: the id of the dome grid to draw on |
| `alt` | number | `0` | With `sky`: height above the dome, scene units |
| `color` | colour | `var(--lcars-orange)` | Line colour |
| [Line keys](#line-keys) | | | `width`, `dash`, `colors`, `glow`, `line_look`, `blend` and `pulse` |

### Line keys

**How a line is drawn: its width, dashes, colours, glow and pulses.** The same keys work on a `path`, a [ring](./surfaces#ring) and (all but `glow` and `line_look`) a [trail](#trail).

- Widths, dashes and pulses are measured in screen pixels, so a line keeps its thickness however close the camera is.
- `pulse` sends bright dashes along the line, like data moving down a conduit. Moving dashes and pulses are explained with more examples on the [Effects](../effects#moving-dashes-and-pulses) page.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 260
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 0
      tilt: 50
      distance: 150
objects:
  # dashed
  - type: path
    from: [-60, 0, -30]
    to: [60, 0, -30]
    width: 2
    dash: [8, 6]
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
  # a colour fade with a glow under it
  - type: path
    from: [-60, 0, 0]
    to: [60, 0, 0]
    width: 3
    colors: [var(--lcars-orange), var(--lcars-yellow)]
    glow: true
  # a lit pipe with pulses
  - type: path
    from: [-60, 0, 30]
    to: [60, 0, 30]
    width: 10
    line_look: tube
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
    pulse:
      color: var(--lcars-yellow)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | number | `1.5` | Line width, px |
| `dash` | list / object | solid | Dashes as `[on, off]` in px (more pairs repeat). Or `pattern: [on, off]` with `speed` (px per second; negative runs backwards) to move them |
| `color` | colour | per type | Line colour |
| `colors` | `[from, to]` | - | Fade from the first colour to the second along the line. Wins over `color` |
| `glow` | boolean / number | off | A soft halo under the line: `true` is 4 times the line's width, or give the factor (at least 1) |
| `line_look` | string | `flat` | `flat`: one brightness. `tube`: shaded like a lit pipe (dark edges, a bright stripe); reads best from about 6 px wide |
| `blend` | string | `normal` | `add`: light adds up where lines cross, so they glow |
| `pulse` | boolean / object | off | Bright pulses moving along the line. `true`, or the keys below |
| `pulse.length` | number | `14` | Pulse length, px |
| `pulse.gap` | number | `90` | Space between pulses, px |
| `pulse.width` | number | line width + 1 | Pulse width, px |
| `pulse.color` | colour | `var(--lcards-moonlight)` | Pulse colour. Pulses add light, so they look whiter than this on a bright line |
| `pulse.speed` | number | `80` | px per second, when `dash.speed` is not set |

Moving dashes and pulses stop under reduced motion.

## beam

**A glowing straight line between two places: a tractor beam, a phaser, a transporter lock.** It is drawn as a wide, soft haze round a thin bright core, so it reads as light rather than a drawn line.

- `from` and `to` take point ids or `[x, y, z]`. A beam between points follows them when they move.
- `width` sets the haze; the bright core stays thin whatever the width.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 280
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 25
      tilt: 20
      distance: 140
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 1500
points:
  - id: station
    xyz: [-45, 0, 0]
    marker: reticle
    label: STATION
  - id: ship
    xyz: [45, 10, 0]
    marker: dot
    label: SHIP
objects:
  - type: beam
    from: station
    to: ship
    width: 14
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
    pulse: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | id / `[x, y, z]` | - | One end |
| `to` | id / `[x, y, z]` | - | The other end |
| `width` | number | `12` | Width of the haze, px. The core stays thin |
| `color` | colour | `theme:colors.ui.secondary` | Beam colour |
| `pulse` | boolean / object | off | Pulses moving along the beam, as on a [line](#line-keys) |

## trail

**A line behind a moving point, showing where it has been: a ship's wake, the last stretch of a planet's orbit.**

- The point must move: ride a spinning ring, stand on a model part during an animation, or be placed from an entity's state. A point that stands still leaves no trail.
- The trail starts empty when the card opens and grows as the point moves, up to `length` seconds of travel.
- The tail fades to black, which is the background in space. Over a bright planet, set `fade_tail: false`.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 320
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 35
      distance: 120
points:
  - id: sun
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
  - id: ship
    polar: [40, 0]
    object: orbit
    marker: dot
    label: SHIP
    style: minor
  - id: probe
    polar: [22, 180]
    object: inner
    marker: dot
    label: PROBE
    style: tiny
objects:
  - type: glow
    at: sun
    size: 30
    color: var(--lcars-yellow)
  # the points ride these two spinning rings
  - type: ring
    id: orbit
    radius: 40
    spin: 20
    width: 0.5
    opacity: 0.2
    rotation: [12, 0, 0]
  - type: ring
    id: inner
    radius: 22
    spin: -45
    width: 0.5
    opacity: 0.2
  - type: trail
    point: ship
    length: 6
    width: 3
  - type: trail
    point: probe
    length: 3
    width: 2
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
```

::: details More about trail
- **Drawn where the point stands:** a moon on a ring round a planet that is itself on an orbit leaves its trail round the planet, riding along with it, not the looping track it makes through the scene.
- **Entities:** a point placed from an entity leaves a line through the positions it reported since the card opened.
- **Reduced motion:** a point on a ring holds still, so its trail stops growing. A point that jumps with an entity still leaves its line.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `point` | string | required | The id of the point to follow |
| `length` | number | `10` | How far back the trail reaches, in seconds of the point's travel |
| `fade_tail` | boolean | `true` | Fade from the colour at the point to black at the tail. `false`: one colour all along |
| `color` | colour | `var(--lcars-orange)` | Colour at the point |
| `width`, `dash`, `blend`, `pulse` | | | As the [line keys](#line-keys) |

## lightning

**Jagged, forked bolts of lightning: quick strikes at random places, or columns that stay lit.** Put it inside a volume nebula and each bolt lights the gas round it, as in a storm.

- `mode: strike` (the default) flashes a bolt now and then somewhere in the region, mostly from high to low.
- `mode: column` holds `count` bolts from the region's floor to its ceiling, crawling and flickering.
- The region is a ball (`radius`) or a box (`size`) round the object's place (`at`).
- Under reduced motion no strikes show, and columns stand still and dim.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 360
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 30
      tilt: 6
      distance: 300
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 2000
objects:
  - type: nebula
    render: volume
    size: [400, 220, 400]
    count: 10
    colors: [var(--lcars-orange), var(--lcars-red)]
    seed: 5
    density: 1.6
    max_radius: 160
  - type: lightning
    size: [260, 170, 260]
    rate: 2
    color: var(--lcars-space-white)
    glow:
      color: var(--lcars-lavender)
    branches: 4
    seed: 4
```

::: details More about lightning
- **A strike** is a quick rise, a fade and a weaker second stroke, then a pause of about `1 / rate` seconds (the pauses vary).
- **Lighting the gas:** a bolt lights any [volume nebula](../effects#gas-you-can-fly-into) it falls in, in its own colour, without linking the two. `lights: false` turns that off.
- **Lightning on a nebula itself:** a volume nebula can also have strikes of its own (`lightning:` on the nebula, see [the Badlands](../effects#the-badlands-layers-columns-and-lightning)), or discharges crawling along its ribbon (`mode: crawl`, see [the Nexus](../effects#the-nexus-a-ribbon-and-its-wake)).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `strike` | `strike`: bolts that flash and go. `column`: bolts held from floor to ceiling |
| `radius` | number | `50` | The region as a ball round `at`, scene units |
| `size` | number / `[w, h, d]` | - | The region as a box, scene units. Wins over `radius` |
| `rate` | number | `0.5` | `strike`: about how many strikes a second. `0`: none. Can [follow an entity](../data#settings-from-entities) |
| `flash` | number | `150` | `strike`: how long a strike shows, ms |
| `count` | number | `1` | `column`: how many columns (1 to 10), spread over the region |
| `speed` | number | `1` | `column`: how fast the bolts crawl and flicker. `0.5` is half as fast, `0` still. Can follow an entity |
| `color` | colour | `var(--lcards-moonlight)` | The bolt's bright core |
| `glow` | boolean / object | `true` | The soft glow round the bolt. `false` for none, or `color` and `width` (times the bolt's width, default 6) |
| `width` | number | `2` | The bolt's width, px. Branches are about half as wide |
| `jaggedness` | number | `0.5` strike, `0.25` column | How far the bolt zigzags, from `0` (straight) to `1` |
| `branches` | number | `3` strike, `1` column | Forks off the bolt; each may fork once more |
| `brightness` | number | `1` | How strongly a bolt lights the gas, `0` to `2`. Can follow an entity |
| `lights` | boolean | `true` | Light the gas of a volume nebula the bolt is in |
| `seed` | number | `1` | Where the strikes fall and how the bolts are shaped; the same seed gives the same storm |

## glow

**A soft round light that always faces the camera: a star, a galactic core, a beacon.** It is a light, not a solid: it brightens what is behind it and has no edge.

- Place it with `at` (a point id or `[x, y, z]`); `size` is its diameter in scene units.
- `falloff` shapes it: a low value is a wide, even haze, a high value a small bright core with a faint halo.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 260
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 0
      tilt: 15
      distance: 160
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 1500
objects:
  # a wide, even haze
  - type: glow
    at: [-45, 0, 0]
    size: 60
    falloff: 0.5
    color: var(--lcars-orange)
  # the default
  - type: glow
    at: [0, 0, 0]
    size: 60
    color: var(--lcars-yellow)
  # a tight bright core
  - type: glow
    at: [45, 0, 0]
    size: 60
    falloff: 6
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | number | `60` | Diameter, scene units |
| `color` | colour | `var(--lcards-moonlight)` | Colour of the light |
| `opacity` | number | `0.9` | Strength, `0` to `1` |
| `falloff` | number | `2` | How fast it fades from the middle: higher is a tighter, brighter core. At least `0.25` |
| `blend` | string | `add` | `add`: light adds up with what is behind. `normal`: drawn over it |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/astrometrics/objects/ships.html -->

# Ships and Stations

Ships, stations and other made things: 3D models (the built-in ships and starbases, or your own glTF files) and the Borg cube. The keys every object takes (`id`, `at`, `rotation`, `opacity`, `visible` ...) are on the [Objects](../objects#keys-every-object-takes) page.

## model

**A 3D model from a glTF file (`.glb` or `.gltf`): a starship, a station, or anything else made as a model.** It is drawn as a hologram by default: a glow with a bright rim, scanlines and its feature edges.

- `material: original` shows the file's own materials instead, lit.
- Leave out `size` to draw the model at its [real size](#real-size); give `size` to scale it to fit.
- Your own file goes in `/config/www/` and is `/local/...` in `src`. Where to put it, how to pick it and how to keep it light are on [Your own models](../models).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 340
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 150
      tilt: 20
      distance: 130
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 1500
objects:
  # a hologram with a scan band and its animation looping
  - type: model
    id: refit
    src: builtin:constitution_class_refit
    at: [-30, 0, 0]
    size: 55
    scan:
      period: 5
    animation: all
  # the file's own materials, lit
  - type: model
    id: galaxy
    src: builtin:galaxy_class
    at: [30, 0, 0]
    size: 55
    material: original
```

::: details More about model
- **While it loads:** a stand-in box shows until the file is in.
- **Compression:** files compressed with meshopt load. Draco-compressed files do not load; the browser console says why.
- **Big models:** feature edges are left off on a model over 250,000 triangles, because working them out freezes the page for seconds. `edges: true` draws them anyway. See [make it light](../models#make-it-light).
- **Labels behind it:** a model hides labels and cards behind it by its real shape, not by a bounding sphere. See [Points on a model](#points-on-a-model).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src` | string | required | The file. `builtin:<name>` is a model shipped with LCARdS (see [built-in models](#built-in-models)); your own is `/local/...` |
| `size` | number | real size | Its largest extent, scene units: the file is scaled and centred to fit. Left out: its [real size](#real-size) |
| `length` | number | - | Its real length in metres (its largest extent), for a file not made at its true scale. See [real size](#real-size) |
| `file_units` | string | `m` | The units the file was made in, for its real size: `m`, `cm`, `mm`, `km`, `ft` or `in` |
| `material` | string | `hologram` | `hologram`: a glow with a bright rim and scanlines. `original`: the file's own materials, lit |
| `color` | colour | `var(--lcars-blue)` | The hologram's body colour |
| `rim.color` | colour | `var(--lcards-moonlight)` | The hologram's rim colour |
| `opacity` | number | `0.85` | The hologram's brightness, `0` to `1` |
| `scanlines` | number | `0.5` | Scanline strength, `0` (none) to `1` |
| `solid` | boolean | `true` | `true`: the hologram hides its own far side. `false`: see-through |
| `blend` | string | `add` | The hologram's blending: `add` or `normal` |
| `scan.period` | number | `0` | A bright band sweeping along the model, seconds per sweep. `0`: none. Stops under reduced motion |
| `scan.color` | colour | `var(--lcards-moonlight)` | The scan band's colour |
| `edges` | boolean / object | on for a hologram | Feature edges as lines. Off with `material: original`, and on a model over 250,000 triangles |
| `edges.angle` | number | `30` | Draw an edge where faces meet at more than this angle, degrees |
| `edges.color` | colour | the rim colour | Edge colour |
| `animation` | string / list | - | Clips to loop: `all`, a clip name or a list of names. Both built-in ships have one clip, `bussards` |
| `occlude` | boolean | `true` | Hide labels and cards behind it |

### Points on a model

**A point with `object:` set to a model's id stands on that model: a label on the bridge, a marker on a nacelle.** The point moves and turns with the model.

- `xyz` is then in the file's own coordinates, so changing `size` never moves the points.
- `part:` puts a point on a named part of the file (a node), so it follows that part when an animation moves it. With `part`, `xyz` is an offset from the part.
- Labels on the far side of the model hide behind it: drag to turn the ship below until the port nacelle is behind the hull, and its label goes.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 380
camera:
  view: three
  views:
    three:
      target: [0, -6, 0]
      yaw: 145
      tilt: 22
      distance: 105
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 1500
points:
  - id: bridge
    object: ship
    part: bridge
    label: BRIDGE
    marker: dot
    style: major
  - id: deflector
    object: ship
    part: deflector
    label: DEFLECTOR
    marker: dot
  - id: port
    object: ship
    part: nacelle_port
    label: PORT NACELLE
    marker: dot
  - id: starboard
    object: ship
    part: nacelle_starboard
    label: STARBOARD NACELLE
    marker: dot
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 70
    pattern: polar
    line_spacing: 10
    spoke_count: 24
    at: [0, -25, 0]
  - type: model
    id: ship
    src: builtin:constitution_class_refit
    size: 70
    scan:
      period: 5
    animation: all
```

::: details More about points on a model
- **In the Astrometrics Studio:** **Pick on preview** places a point on the model's surface, and the part list fills in from the file.
- **How models hide labels:** by their real shape, from a small depth image of the scene that is taken only when the camera or the model moves.
- **More placement forms** for points are on the [Points](../points#placement-forms) page.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string | - | On the point: the id of the model it stands on |
| `xyz` | `[x, y, z]` | - | On the point: where it sits, in the file's own coordinates (with `part`: an offset from the part) |
| `part` | string | - | On the point: the name of a part (node) of the model; the point follows it. A model's parts are listed under [built-in models](#built-in-models) |

### Real size

**A model without `size`, in a scene with `units`, is drawn at its real size.** Ships and stations then sit in proportion to each other and to the planets.

- The scene needs `units` (or the model must be in a [star system](../scale#star-systems) that has them). Without `units`, a model without `size` is drawn 50 scene units across.
- The file is read in `file_units`: metres by default, as glTF files and the built-in models are.
- For a file not made at its true scale, give its real `length` in metres and it is drawn that long, whatever the file measures. `size` wins over both; set it to draw a model larger on purpose.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 340
units: km
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 30
      tilt: 20
      distance: 2.6
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 1500
points:
  - id: ds9
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
  - id: ship
    xyz: [0.9, 0.2, 0.6]
    label: NCC-1701-A
    style: minor
objects:
  # Deep Space 9, 1.45 km across
  - type: model
    id: station
    src: builtin:deep_space_nine
    at: ds9
    material: original
  # the refit Constitution-class ship, 0.305 km long
  - type: model
    id: ship
    src: builtin:constitution_class_refit
    at: ship
```

::: details More about real size
- **In proportion:** the Constitution-class ship is 0.305 km long beside Deep Space 9's 1.45 km, round a planet 12,742 km across.
- **Downloaded models:** many are not made at their true scale. A Star Trek Online Odyssey-class ship from Sketchfab measures 53 units long, so read as metres it would be drawn 53 m long. Give it its real `length` in metres (the Odyssey is 1,061 m).
- **Any units:** `length` stays right in any scene units, where a `size` would need changing with them.
- **Your own files,** with a file made in feet and one at an odd scale:

  ```yaml
  objects:
    # a download made in feet
    - type: model
      id: runabout
      src: /local/models/runabout.glb
      at: [1, 0, -1]
      file_units: ft
    # a download at an odd scale: its real length in metres
    - type: model
      id: odyssey
      src: /local/models/odyssey.glb
      at: [-3, 0, 2]
      length: 1061
  ```

- **In the Astrometrics Studio:** the model's form shows what its file measures and how it is drawn. A file read at its own measurements says to set **Length (m)** when it is not at its true scale. **Show** flies the preview to the model, **Fit to view** sets a size about a fifth of the preview's view, **File size** sets its largest extent as the size (for a file made in the scene's units) and **Real size** clears `size`.
- **New models:** a new model in a scene with units starts at its real size, and the preview flies to it once its file is in (and again when you pick another file), so a real-size ship is never a lost speck.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `units` | string | - | On the card: what one scene unit is (`m`, `km`, `au`, `ly` or `pc`). See [Scale](../scale#units) |
| `size` | number | - | Wins over the real size: its largest extent, scene units |
| `length` | number | - | Its real length in metres. Wins over `file_units` |
| `file_units` | string | `m` | The units the file was made in: `m`, `cm`, `mm`, `km`, `ft` or `in` |

### Visible size

**At its real size a ship is a speck in a view of a whole star system. `model_scale: visible` on the card draws it large enough to see.**

- Each model is drawn at least 40 px across, scaled about its centre, and at its real size again once you are close enough for that to be larger.
- Only real-size models grow: a model with its own `size` is left as it is. Points on a model grow with it.
- You can switch it on screen with the size button under the [camera buttons](../camera#camera-buttons), the `V` key, a `set-model-scale` action or the Astrometrics Studio's toolbar. That is not saved.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 340
units: km
model_scale: visible
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [15, 0, 5]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 30
      distance: 90
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 1500
points:
  - id: ds9
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    label: DEEP SPACE 9
    style: minor
  - id: ship
    xyz: [30, 0, 10]
    label: NCC-1701-A
    style: minor
objects:
  - type: model
    id: station
    src: builtin:deep_space_nine
    at: ds9
    material: original
  - type: model
    id: ship
    src: builtin:constitution_class_refit
    at: ship
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_scale` | string | `real` | On the card: how real-size models start. `real`: in proportion, however small. `visible`: at least 40 px across |
| `camera.buttons.scale` | boolean | `true` | The size button beside the camera buttons, shown only when a model is drawn at its real size. `false` hides it |
| `model_scale` (action) | string | `toggle` | On a `set-model-scale` action: `real`, `visible` or `toggle`. See [actions](../points#actions) |

### Built-in models

**Ships and stations shipped with LCARdS: fan art made in code (no third-party model), recreating the designs seen on screen.** Use one in `src` as `builtin:<name>`.

- All of them are in metres, with Y up, so they come in at their [real size](#real-size).
- `material: original` shows their own colours and lit windows.
- Both ships use one set of part names, so a scene that labels `bridge` or `nacelle_port` works with either.
- Rings, rims and round hulls put their part point on the front face (+z), so a label sits on the structure rather than in the middle of the station.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 420
camera:
  view: station
  views:
    station:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 30
      tilt: 10
      distance: 170
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 1500
points:
  - id: ops
    object: ds9
    part: ops
    label: OPS
    marker: dot
    style: major
  - id: promenade
    object: ds9
    part: promenade
    label: PROMENADE
    marker: dot
  - id: pylon
    object: ds9
    part: upper_pylon_1
    label: UPPER PYLON 1
    marker: dot
objects:
  - type: model
    id: ds9
    src: builtin:deep_space_nine
    size: 90
    material: original
```

::: details More about the built-in models
- **Parts on the front face:** the rings, rims and round hulls with their point on the front face are `habitat_ring`, `docking_ring`, `cap`, `promenade`, `underdish`, `neck` and `hull`.
- **Your own files:** for the My models folder, picking a file, sizing and turning it, and keeping a big model light, see [Your own models](../models).
:::

| `src` | What it is | Parts (`part:`) |
|---|---|---|
| `builtin:constitution_class_refit` | The refit Constitution-class starship of the films (USS Enterprise NCC-1701-A): 305 m long, 144.5 m across the saucer, the bow toward +z. One animation clip, `bussards` (the collectors pulse). | `saucer`, `bridge`, `sensor_dome`, `impulse`, `impulse_exhaust`, `neck`, `torpedo_launcher`, `secondary_hull`, `deflector`, `shuttle_bay`, `pylon_port`, `pylon_starboard`, `nacelle_port`, `nacelle_starboard`, `bussard_port`, `bussard_starboard`, `grille_port`, `grille_starboard`, `windows` |
| `builtin:galaxy_class` | The Galaxy-class starship of The Next Generation (USS Enterprise NCC-1701-D): 642.5 m long, about 470 m across the saucer, the bow toward +z. One animation clip, `bussards`. | the same names as the Constitution, without `sensor_dome` |
| `builtin:deep_space_nine` | Deep Space 9 (Terok Nor), the Cardassian station of Deep Space Nine: 1452 m across, the docking pylons 969 m tip to tip. | `ops`, `upper_core`, `promenade`, `lower_core` (its bottom tip), `sail_towers`, `spokes` (three thin ones, between the bridges), `habitat_ring`, `docking_ring`, `crossover_bridges` (three), `docking_ports`, `windows`, `upper_pylon_1` to `upper_pylon_3` and `lower_pylon_1` to `lower_pylon_3` (their tips) |
| `builtin:earth_spacedock` | Earth Spacedock, from Star Trek III: The Search for Spock onward: 3800 m across and about 5480 m tall. | `antennas` (the top), `cap`, `space_doors` (the front door), `underdish`, `neck`, `hull`, `stem`, `base` (the sphere), `towers` (their tips, the bottom), `panels`, `windows` |
| `builtin:utopia_planitia_drydock` | A drydock of the Utopia Planitia Fleet Yards over Mars, sized for a Galaxy-class ship: about 760 m long, the bow end toward +z. Place several for the yards. | `frame` (ribs and rails), `deck`, `keel`, `lights`, `berth` (where a ship sits), `bow`, `stern` |

## cube

**A Borg cube, the same one as the [Borg screen effect](/core/borg) draws, or a plain shaded box.** It has machinery carved into every face, a rail lattice over it, green light from the recesses and glow spots pulsing deep inside.

- It sits in the scene like any object: it turns with `rotation` and `spin`, other objects pass into its recesses, and labels behind it hide.
- For the cube's green halo, put a `glow` at the same point.
- For many cubes or a slow tablet, use `detail: false`.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 380
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [8, 0, 0]
      yaw: 35
      tilt: 20
      distance: 75
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 1500
points:
  - id: cube
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
  - id: name
    at: cube
    offset: [0, 18, 0]
    label: BORG CUBE
    style: major
objects:
  # the Borg cube with a glow behind it for its halo
  - type: glow
    at: cube
    size: 60
    color: var(--lcards-green-medium)
    opacity: 0.5
  - type: cube
    at: cube
    size: 20
    spin: 5
  # a plain box
  - type: cube
    shape: box
    at: [30, -5, 0]
    size: [8, 4, 12]
```

::: details More about the cube
- **Reduced motion:** the glow spots pulse on the scene clock, so they hold still under reduced motion.
- **Cost:** the carved cube costs about as much as the screen effect's cube for the pixels it covers. One cube filling the card is fine on a laptop.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shape` | string | `borg` | `borg`: the Borg cube. `box`: a shaded box with its edges |
| `size` | number / `[x, y, z]` | `20` | Scene units: one number for a cube, or `[x, y, z]` for a box |
| `color` | colour | `var(--lcards-green-medium)` (borg), `var(--lcards-gray-medium)` (box) | `borg`: the light from inside and the hull's tint. `box`: the box |
| `glow.color` | colour | `var(--lcards-green-lightest)` | `borg`: the glow spots |
| `detail` | boolean | `true` | `borg`: `true` carves the machinery into the faces; `false` draws flat faces with the lattice, for slow graphics hardware |
| `seed` | number | `1` | `borg`: where the glow spots sit. A different number moves them |
| `edges` | boolean / object | `true` | `box`: draw its edges |
| `edges.color` | colour | `theme:colors.ui.secondary` | `box`: the edge colour |
| `opacity` | number | `1` | `box`: how see-through it is, `0` to `1`. A Borg cube ignores it |
| `occlude` | boolean | `true` | Hide labels and cards behind it |
