# Objects

**`objects` is the list of what the scene draws: planets, grids, routes, nebulas, ships.** Each object has a `type`, and its other keys depend on the type.

- Pick a type in [Which type for what](#which-type-for-what); each links to its keys on one of the four pages below.
- Positions, sizes and distances are in scene units, set by the card's `units` ([Scale](./scale#units)). Line widths and dashes are in px.

| Page | Types |
|---|---|
| [Grids, Spheres and Volumes](./objects/surfaces) | grid, volume, sphere, ring, image |
| [Lines and Light](./objects/lines) | path, beam, trail, lightning, glow |
| [Space Phenomena](./objects/space) | nebula, belt, asteroid, comet, galaxy, crystalline |
| [Ships and Stations](./objects/ships) | model, cube |

## Which type for what

**The type to use for each thing you might want in the scene.** Each name links to its keys.

| You want | Use |
|---|---|
| A planet, moon or globe (solid, hides what is behind it, can wear a map) | [`sphere`](./objects/surfaces#sphere) |
| A wireframe: a sector map, a galaxy disc, a sky dome, a see-through ball, a tube, a gravity well | [`grid`](./objects/surfaces#grid) |
| A territory or region of space (see-through cells: a box, a pie slice or any outline) | [`volume`](./objects/surfaces#volume) |
| An orbit, a range ring, a rim | [`ring`](./objects/surfaces#ring) |
| A route through points, an arched route, the sun's track | [`path`](./objects/lines#path) |
| A weapon, transporter or sensor beam (a glowing straight line) | [`beam`](./objects/lines#beam) |
| Where a moving point has been (a fading line behind a ship or planet) | [`trail`](./objects/lines#trail) |
| A star, a galactic core, a beacon (a soft light) | [`glow`](./objects/lines#glow) |
| Clouds of gas | [`nebula`](./objects/space#nebula) |
| An asteroid belt (a band of rocks round a centre) | [`belt`](./objects/space#belt) |
| One asteroid up close (a tumbling rock, lit from its star) | [`asteroid`](./objects/space#asteroid) |
| A comet (a nucleus, a glowing coma and tails pointing away from its star) | [`comet`](./objects/space#comet) |
| A spiral galaxy (stars, arms, a bar and dust; the Milky Way by default) | [`galaxy`](./objects/space#galaxy) |
| Your own picture on the plane | [`image`](./objects/surfaces#image) |
| A ship, a station, any 3D model | [`model`](./objects/ships#model) |
| A Borg cube (or a plain shaded box) | [`cube`](./objects/ships#cube) |
| The Crystalline Entity (a glowing crystal spine and branches round a starburst core) | [`crystalline`](./objects/space#crystalline) |
| Lightning: bolts that flash and go, or held flickering columns (lights the gas of a volume nebula it strikes in) | [`lightning`](./objects/lines#lightning) |
| A star system at true scale inside a larger scene (its own points and objects, in units of its own) | [`system`](./scale#the-system-object) |

## Keys every object takes

**These keys work on every type: where the object sits, how it is turned, when it shows and what a tap does.**

- Colours take theme tokens (`theme:colors.ui.primary`), CSS variables (`var(--lcars-blue)`) or plain colours.
- Under reduced motion, moving parts (spin, pulses, drifting gas, strikes) stop; each type says what it shows instead. Moving effects are on the [Effects](./effects) page.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 280
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 30
      distance: 110
points:
  - id: planet
    xyz: [25, 0, 0]
    label: PLANET
    style: minor
objects:
  - type: sphere
    at: planet
    radius: 6
  # sits at a point, tipped over and spinning
  - type: ring
    id: rings
    at: planet
    radius: 14
    rotation: [30, 0, 0]
    spin: 30
    color: var(--lcars-orange)
  # half see-through, with a tag for rules
  - type: grid
    shape: sphere
    at: [-25, 0, 0]
    radius: 15
    opacity: 0.5
    tags: [survey]
```

::: details More about keys every object takes
- **Looks:** an object without `look` shows in every look, and one with a diagram form switches its parts with the look: a mapped sphere, a filled grid, a glow, cube, asteroid, belt, comet, galaxy, crystalline entity or volume nebula shows its wireframe in the diagram look, and a model with its own materials shows as a hologram. A ring drawn as a line, and a path, hide in the realistic look. `look: all` shows it in every look, as configured.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | `type#n` | A name for points standing on it (`object`), rules and fly-to. The first grid is `grid#1` |
| `at` | id / `[x, y, z]` | the origin | Where it sits: a point id (it follows the point) or `[x, y, z]` |
| `rotation` | `[x, y, z]` | `[0, 0, 0]` | Turns it, degrees: y is a bearing, x tips it toward the camera, z rolls it |
| `spin` | number | `0` | Turns it round its own vertical axis, degrees per second. Points on it turn with it |
| `face` | string | - | `motion`: [face the way it goes](#facing-the-way-it-goes). A point id: [face that point](#facing-a-point) |
| `look` | string | every look | `diagram`, `realistic` or `all`: which [look](./scene#looks-diagram-and-realistic) of the card shows it (`mixed` shows both) |
| `opacity` | number | `1` | `0` to `1`. Some types start lower (a model `0.85`, a glow `0.9`) |
| `visible` | boolean | `true` | `false` hides it; its points still work |
| `max_distance`, `min_distance`, `fade` | | | Shown only within a camera distance: see [Distance](#distance) |
| `hide_in_systems` | boolean / list | `false` | `true` hides it while the camera is inside a [star system](./scale#star-systems), so galaxy-scale volumes and lines step aside in the close-ups. A list of system ids hides it in those only |
| `tags` | list | - | Tags for [rules](./data#rules): a rule on `tag:<name>` changes every object with the tag |
| `tap_action`, `hold_action` | action | - | What a tap or a hold does, as on [points](./points#actions). An object without a `tap_action` is not tappable |
| `view` | object | - | Where the camera lands when it flies to the object: `distance`, `tilt`, `yaw`, `warp`. Keys left out keep the current ones; the distance defaults to a close-up |

### Facing the way it goes

**`face: motion` turns an object to face where its point is going: a ship rides its orbit nose first.**

- The object needs `at:` a moving point. Without `face`, the object slides along keeping its own turn.
- The bow is +z on every built-in model. A model file with its bow along +x needs `rotation: [0, 90, 0]`.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 320
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 35
      distance: 120
points:
  - id: ship
    polar: [40, 90]
    object: orbit
    label: ENTERPRISE
    style: tiny
objects:
  - type: ring
    id: orbit
    radius: 40
    spin: 12
    width: 0.5
    opacity: 0.4
  - type: model
    at: ship
    src: builtin:constitution_class_refit
    size: 8
    face: motion
  - type: trail
    point: ship
    length: 4
    width: 2
```

::: details More about facing the way it goes
- **Level flight:** the object's top stays up, so a ship stays level. `rotation` applies on top, in the object's own frame.
- **Where the heading comes from:** the point's movement however it moves (a spinning ring, an entity, a rule), measured on the object the point stands on. A ship on a ring round a planet that is itself on an orbit faces round the planet, not along the planet's way.
- **Before it moves:** before the point first moves, and under reduced motion (which holds spin), a point on a spinning object faces along the spin. Anything else keeps its `rotation` until the point moves.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `face` | string | - | `motion`: turn the object's +z toward where its point is going, top up |

### Facing a point

**`face: <point id>` keeps an object turned toward a point, wherever it is (another star system, across the galaxy), as either moves.**

- Most objects turn their +z to the point, top up. Objects round an axis (a grid other than a plane, a ring, a belt, a galaxy) point their axis at it instead, so a ring lies face-on to it.
- A [well](./objects/surfaces#wells-and-wormholes)'s narrow end leads to the point it faces, and a wormhole is two wells facing each other.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 300
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 30
      distance: 130
points:
  - id: beacon
    polar: [45, 0]
    object: track
    marker: reticle
    label: BEACON
objects:
  - type: ring
    id: track
    radius: 45
    spin: 20
    opacity: 0.3
  # turns its +z (the bow) to the beacon
  - type: model
    src: builtin:constitution_class_refit
    size: 30
    face: beacon
  # turns its axis to the beacon, so it lies face-on to it
  - type: ring
    at: [0, 22, 0]
    radius: 8
    face: beacon
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `face` | string | - | A point id: turn toward that point. `rotation` applies on top |

## Distance

**Show an object only within a range of camera distances: planets that appear as you zoom in.** Zoom into the star below: its planet and orbit appear as you close in, and the disc gives way.

- The distance is measured to the object's nearest edge, so a large grid does not vanish while you fly through it.
- To swap a model for a marker far away, give the model `max_distance: 60` and give a point with `marker: ship` (or `starbase`) `min_distance: 60`. Touching ranges cross-fade, so one stands in for the other.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 320
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 35
      distance: 420
points:
  - id: star
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    marker: dot
    label: SOL
    style: major
    min_distance: 140
  - id: earth
    polar: [30, 60]
    object: orbit
    label: EARTH
    style: minor
    max_distance: 150
objects:
  - type: glow
    size: 24
    color: var(--lcars-yellow)
  - type: ring
    id: orbit
    radius: 30
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
    spin: 6
    max_distance: 120
  - type: sphere
    at: earth
    radius: 2.5
    image: builtin:earth_blue_marble
    line_width: 0
    max_distance: 120
  # gives way as you close in
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 90
    line_spacing: 30
    opacity: 0.6
    min_distance: 120
```

::: details More about distance
- **Points:** the keys are the same as on [points](./points#visibility).
- **Inside and above:** the distance is 0 when the camera is inside the object. A flat grid (`shape: plane` or `disc`, not deformed) is measured to its surface: above a galactic disc the distance is your height over it, so `min_distance` can hide the disc once you dive into a star system.
- **Out of range:** an object out of range is not drawn and cannot be tapped; its points keep their own ranges.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_distance` | number | - | Hidden when the camera is farther than this. It fades out over the next 10% of that distance |
| `min_distance` | number | - | Hidden when the camera is closer than this. It fades in over the 10% of that distance before it |
| `fade` | `[start, end]` | - | Fully shown nearer than `start`, gone past `end` |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/astrometrics/points.html -->

# Points

**A point is a named place in the scene: placed once, then referred to by its `id` from paths, rings, beams, object positions and camera views.** With a `label` or a `marker` it also shows on the scene, and with a `tap_action` or a `card` it becomes something to tap.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 260
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 45
      distance: 140
points:
  - id: vega                 # a unique name
    polar: [40, 120]         # where: exactly one placement form
    label: Vega              # text shown at the point
    marker: triangle         # a marker
    style: major             # the label style
    tap_action:
      action: fly-to         # a tap flies the camera there
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 60
    pattern: polar
    line_spacing: 10
    spoke_count: 12
```

## In the Astrometrics Studio

**The card editor opens the [Astrometrics Studio](./start#the-studio), a full-screen editor with the live scene, and its Points tab lists every point.** Add, duplicate, reorder and remove points there, and set each one's placement, the object it stands on, entity, label, style, marker, colour and the main label text keys. Other keys stay as they are; edit them in the YAML tab.

- **Pick on preview** (the crosshair on a row) places a point with a tap: the preview shows "TAP TO PLACE ..." and the next tap writes the point's numbers, in its own form. `xyz` and `polar` land on the ground (y = 0), or on the surface of the object in `object`; `latlon` lands on a sphere, `altaz` on a dome, `cell` on a plane grid's cell. Drag to turn the view first if you need to; Escape or Cancel stops picking.
- **On the scene**, tap a point to open its row, drag it to move it, or add one with **Place a point** in the toolbar. See [The Studio](./start#the-studio).
- **A part of a model** puts a point on a named part of a model object: the part list comes from the built-in model, or from the preview once it has loaded your file. The offset moves the point from the part's origin.
- **The Card section** pins a Lovelace card to the point: **Add card** opens Home Assistant's card picker, and the card's own editor opens below, as in a stack card. Show, position and width set how it appears.

::: details More about the Studio and points
- **Points that cannot be picked:** points placed by `sky`, `at` or an entity are not picked on the preview.
- **On a model:** a picked `xyz` lands on the model's surface, in the model file's own coordinates. See [model](./objects/ships#model).
- **Card picker not ready:** if the picker says it is not ready, select **Add card** on any dashboard once (you can cancel it) and try again.
:::

## Placement forms

**Each point takes exactly one placement form: scene coordinates, a bearing on the plane, a place on a globe or a dome, the sun or moon, a real planet, a sector map cell, another point, or a part of a model.** `offset: [x, y, z]` then moves any of them by scene units.

- `object` names the object the point stands on. `latlon`, `altaz`, `sky`, `cell` and `part` need it; with `xyz` or `polar` it is optional, and the point then moves and spins with that object.
- A point can sit on a point that sits on an object that sits on a point: the planet orbits the star, the away team stands on the planet. A reference that loops back on itself is refused (and logged).
- `xyz`, `polar`, `latlon` and `altaz` can also read their numbers from an entity: see [Positions from entities](./data#positions-from-entities).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 340
camera:
  views:
    side:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 30
      tilt: 25
      distance: 120
points:
  # scene coordinates
  - id: origin
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    marker: dot
    label: XYZ
  # distance and bearing on the plane
  - id: bearing
    polar: [35, 90]
    marker: diamond
    label: POLAR 35 AT 90
  # another point, moved up
  - id: lifted
    at: bearing
    offset: [0, 15, 0]
    marker: triangle
    label: AT + OFFSET
  # on the globe, lifted off its surface
  - id: lander
    latlon: [20, 0]
    object: globe
    alt: 0.5
    marker: reticle
    label: LATLON 20 0
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 50
    pattern: polar
    line_spacing: 10
    spoke_count: 12
  - type: sphere
    id: globe
    at: [-30, 12, 0]
    radius: 10
    spin: 10
```

::: details More about placement
- **Longitude 0** on a sphere faces the default camera, with east to the right. A `latlon` point turns with the sphere's `spin`.
- **The sun and moon** with `sky` are placed from the time and your Home Assistant location (`sun.sun` when it exists), updated every minute; with a [clock](./scale#the-scene-clock) on the card, at the scene date instead of now.
- **Real bodies** with `body` sit where that Sun, planet, dwarf planet or moon is at the scene date, in the scene's or system's units. See [The real Solar System](./scale#the-real-solar-system).
- **A model part** with `part`: the point follows the part as it moves, and `xyz` is then an offset in the part's coordinates. See [model](./objects/ships#model).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | required | Unique name of the point, used by `at`, `target`, `from`, `to`, `points` and views |
| `xyz` | `[x, y, z]` | - | Scene coordinates; y is up. With `object`: local to that object (on a model, in the file's coordinates) |
| `polar` | `[distance, bearing]` | - | On the scene plane: distance from the centre, scene units, and a bearing in degrees (0 north, clockwise seen from above) |
| `latlon` | `[lat, lon]` | - | Latitude and longitude, degrees, on the sphere in `object` |
| `altaz` | `[azimuth, altitude]` | - | On the sky dome in `object`: azimuth clockwise from north, altitude up from the horizon, degrees |
| `sky` | string | - | `sun` or `moon`: that body on the dome in `object`, now or at the scene date |
| `body` | string | - | A real Sun, planet, dwarf planet or moon (`mars`), at the scene date |
| `center` | string | - | With `body`: measure from this body instead of the Sun (`jupiter`) |
| `cell` | string | - | The centre of a sector map cell (`AF3`) on the plane grid in `object`, which needs `axis_labels` |
| `at` | string | - | At another point, by id |
| `part` | string | - | On a named part of the [model](./objects/ships#model) in `object`; it follows the part |
| `object` | string | - | The object the point stands on, by id |
| `alt` | number | `0` | Height above the surface (`latlon`, `altaz`, `sky`) or the plane (`polar`), scene units |
| `offset` | `[x, y, z]` | - | Moves the point by these scene units from where its form puts it |

## Labels

**A point's label is LCARdS text, with the same [text-field keys](/core/text-fields) as the button, elbow and slider cards: font, size, weight, case, letter spacing, colour (a state map too), a background box, templates.** `label: Vega` is short for one field called `label`; `text:` gives a point as many fields as you like, each placed round the point.

- Fields with the same `position` stack. Without a `position`, a field sits right of the marker (`center-right`), or on the point when there is no marker (`center`).
- `text.default` holds keys every field of this point inherits; it is not drawn itself.
- Text-field keys that place text in a card's zones (`zone`, `x`, `y`, `x_percent`, `y_percent`, `anchor`, `baseline`, `stretch`, `font_size_percent`, `cap_height_ratio`) mean nothing round a point; the checker reports them as unknown.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 260
camera:
  views:
    top:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      tilt: 70
      distance: 110
points:
  - id: switch
    entity: switch.demo_switch
    xyz: [-15, 0, 0]
    marker: reticle
    text:
      # every field of this point
      default:
        font_size: 14
      label:
        content: "{entity.attributes.friendly_name}"
        color:
          default: var(--lcards-moonlight)
          "off": var(--lcars-orange)
      # under the label, right of the point
      status:
        content: "{entity.state}"
        position: bottom-right
        font_size: 11
        color: var(--lcars-black)
        # the LCARS bar-break box
        background:
          default: var(--lcars-orange)
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: plane
    size: 100
    line_spacing: 10
```

::: details More about label text
- **Templates** in `content` are evaluated with the point's `entity`, and with `sky` and `point` as well: see [Live data: templates](./data#templates).
- **Fonts:** `font_family` takes the LCARdS fonts (`lcards_eurostile`, `lcards_microgramma`, ...), loaded when used. The default is the theme's LCARS font (Antonio).
- **Selected points:** a `selected` key in a `color` map colours the field while the point is selected. Without one, a selected point's label takes the theme's alert colour.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | string / number | - | Text shown at the point: short for `text.label.content` |
| `text` | object | - | Text fields by name (`label` is the main one) |
| `text.default` | object | - | Keys every text field of this point inherits |
| `content` | string | - | A field's text. [Templates](/core/templates/) are evaluated |
| `template` | boolean | `true` | `false` shows `content` as written |
| `show` | boolean | `true` | `false` hides the field |
| `display_format` | string | - | As on every card: see [Display format](/core/text-fields-content#display-format) |
| `position` | string | `center-right` with a marker, else `center` | Where the field sits round the point: `center`, `center-right`, `top-left`, `bottom-center` and the other six. `right`, `left`, `top` and `bottom` are short for the middle ones |
| `font_size` | number / string | by style | px (a number) or a CSS size |
| `font_weight` | string / number | - | As on every card |
| `font_family` | string | the theme's LCARS font | A font name or one of the LCARdS fonts |
| `text_transform` | string | - | `uppercase`, `lowercase`, `capitalize` |
| `letter_spacing` | number / string | - | px (a number) or a CSS length |
| `color` | colour / state map | by style | A colour, or a [state map](/core/colours) by the point's entity; a `selected` key colours it while the point is selected |
| `background` | colour / state map | - | A box behind the text, as on the [bar-label buttons](/core/text-fields-style#text-background) |
| `background_padding` | number | `8` | Space between the text and the sides of its box, px |
| `background_radius` | number | `4` | Corner radius of the box, px |
| `background_width` | number | - | A fixed box width, px |
| `background_min_width` | number | - | A smallest box width, px |
| `padding` | number / object | - | Moves the field, px: a number, or `top`, `right`, `bottom` and `left` |
| `rotation` | number | - | Turns the field, degrees |

### Styles and defaults

**`style` picks a label style, which sets the size, the colour and the rank when labels overlap.** The four built-ins are `title` (34 px), `major` (20 px), `minor` (13 px, the default) and `tiny` (10 px); `labels.styles` changes them or adds your own, and `labels.default` sets keys for every label on the card.

- A field takes its keys from, lowest first: the built-in style, `labels.default`, `labels.styles.<style>`, the point's `color`, the point's `text.default`, the field.
- Ring and axis labels of a grid take a `style` and a `text.default` the same way.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 300
camera:
  views:
    top:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      tilt: 70
      distance: 140
labels:
  default:
    text_transform: uppercase
    letter_spacing: 1
  styles:
    # a style of your own
    hostile:
      font_size: 16
      font_weight: bold
      color: var(--lcars-alert-red)
      priority: 90
points:
  - id: base
    xyz: [-30, 0, 10]
    marker: square
    style: major
    label: Starbase 12
  - id: warbird
    xyz: [25, 0, -15]
    marker: triangle
    style: hostile
    text:
      label:
        content: Warbird
      class:
        content: D'deridex class
        position: bottom-right
        font_size: 10
        font_weight: normal
        color: var(--lcards-moonlight)
  - id: buoy
    xyz: [20, 0, 25]
    marker: dot
    text:
      label:
        content: Buoy 7
        color: var(--lcars-black)
        background: var(--lcars-orange)
        background_radius: 8
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: plane
    size: 120
    line_spacing: 10
```

::: details More about the built-in styles
- **The four styles:**

  | Style | Size | Priority | Colour |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `title` | 34 px, letter spacing 1 | `100` | `var(--lcards-moonlight)` |
  | `major` | 20 px | `80` | `var(--lcards-moonlight)` |
  | `minor` | 13 px | `40` | the theme's text colour |
  | `tiny` | 10 px | `10` | the theme's text colour |

- **Changing a built-in:** `labels.styles.major` with only `font_size: 22` keeps the rest of `major` (its colour and priority).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style` | string | `minor` | The point's label style: `title`, `major`, `minor`, `tiny` or one of yours. An unknown name is drawn as `minor` |
| `labels.default` | object | - | Text keys every label on the card inherits (`font_family`, `text_transform`, `letter_spacing`, ...), over the built-in styles |
| `labels.styles` | object | - | Label styles by name: change a built-in or add your own |
| `labels.styles.<name>` | object | - | A style: text keys plus `priority` and `overlap` |
| `labels.snap` | boolean | `false` | Round label positions to whole px: crisper text on a weak device, steppier in fast motion |

### Priority and placement

**When a label would overlap another one, or run off the card, it first tries the other side of its point; only when no side is free is it hidden, and the higher `priority` wins.**

- A label that moved keeps its new side while the scene turns, and goes back once its own side is clear.
- Between two labels of the same priority, the nearer one wins.
- `overlap: true` keeps a label from ever being hidden: it still moves to a free side when it can, else it shows over the other label. It suits a scene with few labels that must always show (compass letters, your home); in a busy galaxy, hiding the lower-priority labels keeps it readable.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 260
camera:
  views:
    top:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      tilt: 70
      distance: 120
labels:
  # every label on this card
  overlap: true
  styles:
    # except the small ones
    tiny:
      overlap: false
points:
  - id: home
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    marker: square
    style: major
    label: HOME
  # close to home: moves to a free side, or shows over it
  - id: shed
    xyz: [4, 0, 1]
    marker: dot
    label: SHED
  # tiny, and in the way: hidden
  - id: gate
    xyz: [2, 0, -1]
    marker: dot
    style: tiny
    label: GATE
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: plane
    size: 100
    line_spacing: 10
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `priority` | number | by style | Which label wins when two overlap: higher wins. Overrides its style's |
| `overlap` | boolean | the style's, else `labels.overlap` | Never hide this label when labels overlap |
| `labels.overlap` | boolean | `false` | The same for every label on the card |
| `labels.styles.<name>.priority` | number | - | The priority of labels in this style |
| `labels.styles.<name>.overlap` | boolean | - | Labels in this style are never hidden |

### Labels on ships and planets

**When a model, a globe or a cube sits at a point (its `at:` names the point), the point's label stands off the object's edge on screen, with a thin leader line back to it, so it never sits on the hull.**

- The gap follows the object's size as the camera moves in and out.
- The object never hides its own point's label, and a tap on the object (or the label) selects the point and flies to it, as on a marker.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 300
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 30
      distance: 200
points:
  - id: enterprise
    polar: [70, 0]
    object: patrol
    label: ENTERPRISE
  # no leader line
  - id: base
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    label: STARBASE 11
    leader: false
objects:
  - type: ring
    id: patrol
    radius: 70
    spin: 4
  - type: model
    src: builtin:constitution_class_refit
    at: enterprise
    size: 16
    face: motion
  - type: sphere
    at: base
    radius: 12
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `leader` | boolean | `true` | With a model, globe or cube at the point: `false` leaves out the line from the object's edge to the label |

## Markers

**`marker` draws a shape at the point: a dot, a triangle, a diamond, a square, a reticle, a starship or a starbase seen from above, or the moon's lit part.** A point with a marker can be tapped.

- `color` on the point colours the marker, and is the default for its text fields; a state map follows the point's entity. A field's own `color` colours only that text.
- `ship` and `starbase` stand in for a model far away: see [Distance](./objects#distance).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 240
camera:
  views:
    top:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      tilt: 70
      distance: 110
points:
  - id: patrol
    xyz: [-25, 0, 0]
    marker: ship
    color: var(--lcars-orange)
    label: PATROL
  - id: station
    xyz: [20, 0, 0]
    marker: starbase
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
    label: STATION
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: plane
    size: 100
    line_spacing: 10
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `marker` | string | `none` | `dot`, `triangle`, `diamond`, `square`, `reticle` (a target ring), `ship`, `starbase`, `moon_phase` (the moon's lit part, from the sky) or `none` |
| `color` | colour / state map | by style | The marker's colour, and the default for the text fields. A state map by the point's entity; a `selected` key while it is selected. Built-in styles: `var(--lcards-moonlight)` for `title` and `major`, the theme's text colour for `minor` and `tiny` |

## Visibility

**A point can hide its label and marker, show them only in one look of the card, fade them, or show them only within a range of camera distances.** Distance ranges show detail as you zoom in, and hide it again as you zoom out.

- A hidden point still places the things that use it. [Rules](./data#rules) use `visible` to hide and show points.
- Labels behind a planet, a model, an asteroid or a cube are hidden; the see-through volumes and grids hide nothing.
- Objects take the same three distance keys, measured to their nearest edge: see [Distance](./objects#distance).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 280
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 40
      distance: 160
points:
  - id: sector
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    marker: reticle
    style: major
    label: SECTOR 001
  # hidden from where the camera starts: zoom in to see it
  - id: detail
    xyz: [15, 0, 10]
    marker: dot
    label: OUTPOST (ZOOM IN)
    max_distance: 120
  # half see-through
  - id: faint
    xyz: [-25, 0, -10]
    marker: dot
    label: FAINT
    opacity: 0.4
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 50
    pattern: polar
    line_spacing: 10
    spoke_count: 12
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `visible` | boolean | `true` | `false` hides the label, marker and card; the point still places other things |
| `look` | string | - | `diagram` or `realistic`: the label and marker show only in that [look](./scene#looks-diagram-and-realistic) of the card (and in `mixed`) |
| `opacity` | number | `1` | Opacity of the label and marker, `0` to `1` |
| `max_distance` | number | - | Hidden when the camera is farther than this, scene units |
| `min_distance` | number | - | Hidden when the camera is closer than this, scene units |
| `fade` | `[start, end]` | - | Fully shown nearer than `start`, gone past `end`, scene units from the camera |
| `below_horizon` | string | `dim` for `sky`, `show` for `altaz` | Sky points under the horizon: `dim`, `hide` or `show` |
| `hide_in_systems` | boolean / list | - | Hide the label and marker while the camera is inside a [star system](./scale#star-systems); a list of system ids hides it in those only |

## Actions

**`tap_action` and `hold_action` take any card action (`more-info`, `toggle`, `perform-action`, `navigate`, `url`, `none`), plus `fly-to`, which flies the camera to the point.**

- A point with no `tap_action` and a marker (or a model or globe sitting at it) selects on a tap: its label turns the alert colour (or the `selected` colour of its colour map), and the camera flies to it.
- `more-info` and `toggle` without an `entity` act on the point's `entity`, else the card's.
- A point's own `view` sets where the camera lands when it flies to that point.
- A drag never fires a tap (a press that moves more than 6 px is a drag), and a hold (half a second) fires `hold_action`, not `tap_action`.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 340
camera:
  view: wide
  views:
    wide:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 40
      distance: 160
points:
  # tap to toggle the light, hold for its dialog
  - id: lamp
    xyz: [-30, 0, 0]
    marker: square
    label: LIGHT
    tap_action:
      action: toggle
      entity: light.demo
    hold_action:
      action: more-info
      entity: light.demo
  # tap to fly in close, with a low camera
  - id: probe
    xyz: [30, 0, 10]
    marker: diamond
    label: PROBE
    view:
      distance: 30
      tilt: 15
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: plane
    size: 120
    line_spacing: 10
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tap_action` | action | select and fly-to, with a marker | Action on a tap. A point with a marker, a `tap_action` or a `card` can be tapped |
| `hold_action` | action | - | Action on a hold of half a second |
| `view.distance` | number | a close-up | Where the camera lands when it flies to this point: distance from it, scene units |
| `view.tilt` | number | the current tilt | Camera height angle on landing, degrees: `0` level, `90` straight down |
| `view.yaw` | number | the current yaw | The way the camera faces on landing, degrees |
| `view.warp` | boolean | `camera.warp` | Stars and dust streak on the way here (see [Warp and dust](./effects#warp-and-dust)) |
| [Scene action keys](#scene-actions) | | | `fly-to`, `set-clock` and `set-model-scale` |

### Scene actions

**Three actions belong to the astrometrics card: `fly-to` moves the camera, `set-clock` sets the scene date, and `set-model-scale` switches the models between their real size and visible size.** On the card's own points and objects they act on this card; from any other LCARdS card, `card` names the astrometrics card (its `id`).

- `action: fly-to` alone flies to the point (on an object: to its middle). With `view`, it flies to that named view instead; with `point`, to that point.
- `duration` and `warp` on the action win over the card's `camera.fly_duration` and `camera.warp` and the view's own `warp`.
- Flying from other cards and from automations is on [Live data](./data#fly-to-from-other-cards-and-automations).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 300
camera:
  view: wide
  views:
    wide:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 40
      distance: 160
    map:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      tilt: 90
      distance: 120
points:
  # fly to the named view, slowly
  - id: overview
    xyz: [-30, 0, 0]
    marker: diamond
    label: MAP VIEW (TAP)
    tap_action:
      action: fly-to
      view: map
      duration: 3000
  # back to the start, streaking the stars
  - id: back
    xyz: [30, 0, 0]
    marker: diamond
    label: WIDE VIEW (TAP)
    tap_action:
      action: fly-to
      view: wide
      warp: true
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 2000
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: plane
    size: 120
    line_spacing: 10
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | string | - | `fly-to`, `set-clock` or `set-model-scale` (or any other card action) |
| `card` | string | this card | The astrometrics card to act on, by its `id`. Needed from any other LCARdS card |
| `view` | string | - | `fly-to`: a named view (`camera.views`) to fly to instead of the point |
| `point` | string | - | `fly-to`: a point id to fly to. Wins over `view` |
| `duration` | number | `camera.fly_duration` | `fly-to`: how long the flight takes, ms |
| `warp` | boolean | the view's `warp`, else `camera.warp` | `fly-to`: `true` streaks the stars on the way, `false` never |
| `date` | string | - | `set-clock`: the [scene date](./scale#the-scene-clock), `now` or an ISO date |
| `rate` | number / string | - | `set-clock`: days per second, or `live` |
| `model_scale` | string | `toggle` | `set-model-scale`: `real`, `visible` or `toggle`, as in [visible size](./objects/ships#visible-size). Not saved |

## Cards on points

**`card` pins any Lovelace card to the point: a tile, an entities card, an LCARdS button.** It follows the point as the camera moves, and hides when the point is off screen, behind a planet or a model, or out of its `max_distance` range.

- `show: tap` (the default): a tap on the point opens its card and selects the point; a tap anywhere else, another point or Escape closes it. One card is open at a time. A `tap_action` then runs only when it is `fly-to` (the card opens and the camera flies).
- `show: always`: the card is always shown, a small control panel standing in the scene.
- A point with a card needs no label or marker: the card is what shows. Its visibility conditions work as on a dashboard.
- A rule can patch `card` like any other point key; only that card is built again.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 360
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 25
      tilt: 30
      distance: 110
points:
  # always shown
  - id: relay
    xyz: [-25, 0, 0]
    marker: diamond
    label: RELAY
    card:
      show: always
      position: top-left
      width: 150
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: input_boolean.demo_toggle
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          name:
            content: RELAY POWER
            show: true
  # opens on a tap
  - id: outpost
    xyz: [25, 0, 10]
    marker: dot
    label: OUTPOST (TAP)
    card:
      position: top-right
      width: 170
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: switch.demo_switch
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          name:
            content: SHIELDS
            show: true
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 50
    pattern: polar
    line_spacing: 10
    spoke_count: 12
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card.card` | object | required | The card config, as on a dashboard (`type` and its own keys) |
| `card.show` | string | `tap` | `tap`: opens on a tap on the point. `always`: always shown |
| `card.position` | string | `center-right` | Where the card sits round the point, with the label position names. It stays inside the scene |
| `card.offset` | `[x, y]` | `[0, 0]` | Moves the card from where `position` puts it, px |
| `card.width` | number | `280` | Card width, px (at least `80`); the height follows the card |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/astrometrics/scale.html -->

# Scale

**An [Astrometrics card](./) can be drawn to look right or to be right.** Both are the same card with the same keys.

- **Built to fit** (most [starters](./starters)): sizes and distances picked so everything shows at once. Planets are big enough to see from across their system, a station is a sizeable part of its planet. Easy to read, nothing to tune, and not to scale.
- **True scale:** the real numbers, so what you see is how it is: a solar system in km where planets are dots from across it, a galaxy in light years with a station 1.5 km across inside it. The close views are where it shines; you pick what shows from afar with the [distance](./objects#distance) keys.
- The **Solar system (real positions)** and **Galaxy to station at true scale** [starters](./starters) are ready-made true-scale scenes.

## Units

**`units` on the card names what one scene unit is, for real data: `m`, `km`, `au`, `ly` or `pc`.** Positions, sizes and distances are all in scene units; without a name they are your own.

- The name tells the card how a [star system](#star-systems) inside relates to the scene, draws a [model](./objects/ships#real-size) at its real size, places real bodies (`body:` points) at their real distances and gives a galaxy the Milky Way's radius in those units.
- It does not rescale what is already there: naming the units of a scene built in scene units only says what its numbers mean.
- Screen sizes (line widths, label sizes, marker sizes) are in px whatever the units, and a model's `length` is in metres. Every other length is in the units of the frame it is in: the scene's, or its [system's](#star-systems).
- In the [Studio](./start#the-studio) it is the **Units** section of the Scene tab, and the Studio shows the unit beside each length field (`units` when the scene names none).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 300
# one unit is a km: the Earth below is 6,371 km in radius
units: km
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: earth
      yaw: 200
      tilt: 15
      distance: 140000
backdrop:
  stars: true
points:
  - id: earth
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    label: EARTH
    style: major
objects:
  - type: sphere
    at: earth
    radius: 6371
    image: builtin:earth_blue_marble
  # a geostationary orbit, 42,164 km from Earth's centre
  - type: ring
    radius: 42164
    width: 1
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
```

::: details More about units
- **Each starter is in one set of units:**

| Starters | Units |
|---|---|
| Solar system (real positions) | km |
| Star Trek galaxy (and its Star Trek parts), Galaxy to station at true scale | ly (the station's system inside in km) |
| Every other scene | Scene units, built to fit |

- **Named units:** a part added to a scene (a planet, a belt, a comet, a nebula field, territories, the Badlands, the Nexus, the wormhole) starts at its real size: an Earth-sized planet one au out, the Badlands 10 ly across, the Nexus 1 ly long, the wormhole 40 km long, a comet 0.6 to 35 au from its star (Halley's). None of the three has a size on screen, so 10 ly, 1 ly and 40 km are plausible sizes, not canon.
- **Scene units, with something in the scene:** a part is sized to fit: about a quarter of the scene's size (a belt about half, out among the planets). The Nexus added to the Solar system starter is about 80 long, where Neptune's orbit is 160.
- **An empty scene:** a part keeps its own sizes.
- **Starbases and asteroids:** a starbase and a single asteroid keep their sizes in scene units (a model is drawn larger when it would be too small to see, [`model_scale`](./objects/ships#real-size)). What you type always wins.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `units` | string | - | What one scene unit is: `m` (metres), `km`, `au` (149,597,870.7 km), `ly` (light years) or `pc` (parsecs, 3.26 ly). Left out: scene units of your own |

## One scene in real units

**Build a scene with the real numbers and the card holds the whole range, from the whole system down to a station in front of Earth.** This one opens on Deep Space 9 4 km away, with Earth 42,000 km behind it and the Sun 150 million km further.

- **Depth:** the near station, Earth and the Sun draw in the right order. When one depth range cannot hold the view, the card draws it in slices, far to near; a scene built to fit draws in one pass.
- **Distance limits** follow the scene: you can zoom in to half its smallest object and out to 20 times its size (a scene built to fit keeps 1 to 100,000). [`camera.limits.distance`](./camera#camera-limits) sets your own.
- **Fly-to** over a long zoom moves evenly in log distance, so each factor of ten takes the same time, and zooming in the camera lines up on its target early instead of sweeping past it close up.
- **What to expect:** at true scale, planets are dots from across their system (Earth is 1/23,000 of its orbit), so give them markers and labels. The [distance](./objects#distance) keys still pick what shows when.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 360
units: km
camera:
  view: station
  views:
    system:
      target: sun
      yaw: 40
      tilt: 35
      distance: 2100000000
    earth:
      target: earth
      yaw: 225
      tilt: 12
      distance: 70000
    station:
      target: ds9
      yaw: 330
      tilt: 6
      distance: 4
points:
  - id: sun
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    label: SOL
    style: major
    tap_action:
      action: fly-to
      view: system
  - id: earth
    polar: [149597870.7, 30]
    marker: dot
    label: EARTH
    tap_action:
      action: fly-to
      view: earth
  - id: ds9
    at: earth
    offset: [-21082, 0, 36515]
    label: DEEP SPACE 9
    style: tiny
objects:
  - type: glow
    at: sun
    size: 9000000
    color: var(--lcars-yellow)
  - type: sphere
    at: sun
    radius: 696340
    fill:
      color: var(--lcars-yellow)
  - type: ring
    radius: 149597870.7
    width: 1
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
  - type: sphere
    at: earth
    radius: 6371
    image: builtin:earth_blue_marble
  - type: model
    at: ds9
    src: builtin:deep_space_nine
    size: 1.452
    material: original
```

::: details More about real units
- **Orbit rings** add segments near the camera, so an orbit 150 million km across still passes through its planet seen from 70,000 km (an `orbit` ring adds them round its body).
:::

## Star systems

**A `system` object holds points and objects in units of their own, at a point of the scene: the galaxy in light years, Sol in km.** One set of units cannot hold a galaxy and a station: at 26,000 light years from the galactic core, numbers in light years are only good to about 30 km.

- Write each part with the numbers as published: star positions in ly or pc, orbits in AU or km, sizes in km.
- **Ids are card-wide:** views, `fly-to`, rules, templates and paths name a system's points and objects like any others.
- **Distances are in the owner's units:** a view's `distance` is in its target's units (the `station` view below is 4 km, the `galaxy` view 140,000 ly), and so are a point's or object's `fade`, `min_distance` and `max_distance`. A view with an `[x, y, z]` target, and `camera.limits`, are in scene units.
- **The camera follows:** within a few times its size of a system, the camera works in the system's units, so a station a few km across holds steady; further out it works in the scene's. Nothing on screen moves at the change, and a fly-to from the galaxy lands exactly on its target inside.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 380
units: ly
camera:
  view: galaxy
  views:
    galaxy:
      target: core
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 35
      distance: 140000
    earth:
      target: earth
      yaw: 225
      tilt: 12
      distance: 70000
    station:
      target: ds9
      yaw: 330
      tilt: 6
      distance: 4
points:
  - id: core
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    label: GALACTIC CORE
    style: title
  # tap SOL to dive from the galaxy to Earth
  - id: sol
    polar: [26000, 200]
    alt: 60
    marker: dot
    label: SOL
    style: major
    tap_action:
      action: fly-to
      view: earth
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 50000
    pattern: polar
    line_spacing: 5000
    spoke_count: 36
    min_distance: 20
  - type: glow
    at: core
    size: 30000
  # Sol, in km
  - type: system
    id: sol_system
    at: sol
    units: km
    points:
      - id: sun
        xyz: [0, 0, 0]
      - id: earth
        polar: [149597870.7, 30]
        marker: dot
        label: EARTH
        max_distance: 3000000000
      - id: ds9
        at: earth
        offset: [-21082, 0, 36515]
        label: DEEP SPACE 9
        style: tiny
        max_distance: 3000000
        tap_action:
          action: fly-to
          view: station
    objects:
      - type: glow
        at: sun
        size: 9000000
        color: var(--lcars-yellow)
      - type: sphere
        at: sun
        radius: 696340
        fill:
          color: var(--lcars-yellow)
      - type: ring
        radius: 149597870.7
        width: 1
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
      - type: sphere
        at: earth
        radius: 6371
        image: builtin:earth_blue_marble
      - type: model
        at: ds9
        src: builtin:deep_space_nine
        size: 1.452
        material: original
```

::: details More about star systems
- **Galaxy-scale things in the close-ups:** a region's walls or a quadrant line thousands of light years long would cross a close-up of a planet. `hide_in_systems: true` on a point or object hides it while the camera is inside any system (within a few times its size, where it works in the system's units); outside every system it shows as usual. A list of system ids (`hide_in_systems: [sol_system]`) hides it inside those systems only. The [Star Trek galaxy](./starters#star-trek-galaxy) starter sets it on its regions, lines and names.
- **One level:** a system cannot hold another system (it reaches from a galaxy down to a station already).
- **Not rotated:** a system's axes are the scene's.
- **The disc above:** Sol sits 60 ly above the disc, and `min_distance: 20` on the grid hides the disc once the camera is inside the system ([Distances](#distances)).
:::

### The system object

**`type: system` draws nothing itself: it holds `points` and `objects` written in its own units, at a point of the scene.**

- `units` inside a system needs the card's own `units`, so the card knows how the two relate. For units without a name, give `scale` instead: how many scene units one unit inside is.
- A system's objects can be any type but another `system`.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 280
units: au
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: star
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 35
      distance: 4
points:
  - id: star
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    label: STAR
    style: major
objects:
  - type: glow
    at: star
    size: 0.4
    color: var(--lcars-yellow)
  - type: ring
    radius: 1.5
    width: 1
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
  # a planet in km, 1.5 au out
  - type: system
    id: planet_system
    at: [0, 0, 1.5]
    units: km
    points:
      - id: planet
        xyz: [0, 0, 0]
        marker: dot
        label: PLANET
    objects:
      - type: sphere
        at: planet
        radius: 6000
        fill:
          color: var(--lcars-orange)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | `system#n` | Its name |
| `at` | id / `[x, y, z]` | the origin | Where its origin sits: a point of the scene (it stays there), or `[x, y, z]` in scene units |
| `units` | string | the scene's | What one unit inside is: `m`, `km`, `au`, `ly` or `pc`. Needs the card's own `units` |
| `scale` | number | - | Scene units per unit inside, for units without a name. Wins over `units` |
| `points` | list | - | Its points, in its units ([Points](./points)) |
| `objects` | list | - | Its objects, in its units: any type but another `system` |
| `visible` | boolean | `true` | `false` hides everything in it (its points still work) |

## The real Solar System

**A point with `body: mars` sits where Mars really is at the scene date, on its real tilted, elliptical orbit.** A sphere with `body: mars` turns as Mars really does, and a ring with `orbit: mars` draws the real orbit. All three follow the [scene clock](#the-scene-clock).

- **Where:** the Sun sits at the origin of the point's frame (the scene, or its [system](#star-systems)), in that frame's units: set `units` (km or au; without it au is assumed, with a warning). A moon is placed from the Sun too (its planet plus its own orbit), so it sits by its planet's point. `center: jupiter` measures from another body instead, for a scene centred on a planet.
- **Axes:** y is up toward ecliptic north, and bearing 0 (away from the default camera) is ecliptic longitude 90°, so the planets go round anticlockwise seen from above, as from the north.
- **Spheres and rings:** on a sphere, `body` replaces `spin` and `rotation`: its axis is tilted where the real pole points, it turns in the real sidereal day, and its map's longitude 0 is where the prime meridian is. Put the sphere at the body's point (`at: mars`) with its real radius. A ring with `body: saturn` lies in Saturn's equator (its rings). An `orbit` ring for a moon goes at its planet's point (`orbit: io`, `at: jupiter`); a planet's needs no `at`.
- **True sizes:** at true scale the planets are dots from across the system, so give their points markers and labels, and fly in to see the bodies.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 400
units: au
clock:
  date: now
  rate: 10
camera:
  buttons: true
  view: inner
  views:
    inner:
      target: sun
      yaw: 30
      tilt: 40
      distance: 4.5
points:
  - id: sun
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    label: SOL
    style: major
  - id: mercury
    body: mercury
    marker: dot
    label: MERCURY
    style: tiny
  - id: venus
    body: venus
    marker: dot
    label: VENUS
    style: tiny
  - id: earth
    body: earth
    marker: dot
    label: EARTH
  - id: mars
    body: mars
    marker: dot
    label: MARS
objects:
  - type: glow
    at: sun
    size: 0.25
    color: var(--lcars-yellow)
  - type: ring
    orbit: mercury
    width: 1
    opacity: 0.5
  - type: ring
    orbit: venus
    width: 1
    opacity: 0.5
  - type: ring
    orbit: earth
    width: 1
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
  - type: ring
    orbit: mars
    width: 1
    opacity: 0.5
```

::: details More about the real Solar System
- **Bodies:** `sun`, the planets, `pluto` and `ceres`, and the moons `moon` (Luna), `phobos`, `deimos`, `io`, `europa`, `ganymede`, `callisto`, `titan`, `triton` and `charon`. The [Solar system (real positions)](./starters#solar-system-real-positions) starter has them all, with their maps and the asteroid and Kuiper belts.
- **Accuracy:** planets from JPL's approximate elements (Standish), within a few hundredths of a degree for the inner planets and a few tenths for the giants, 3000 BC to 3000 AD; outside that they keep going, less exactly. Pluto and Ceres from JPL's small-body elements: a fraction of a degree for Pluto, a degree or two for Ceres outside 2000 to 2050. The Moon from the same series as the sky. The other moons from JPL's mean elements, within a degree from 2000 to 2026 and a few degrees out to 1950 and 2100 (Titan and Phobos up to 15). Rotation from the IAU models. Good for a picture of the sky, not for navigation.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `body` (point) | string | - | Place the point where this real body is at the scene date |
| `center` (point) | string | `sun` | With `body`: measure from this body instead, so it sits at the origin |
| `body` (sphere) | string | - | Turn the sphere as this body is turned. `spin` and `rotation` do not apply |
| `body` (ring) | string | - | Lay the ring in this body's equator (Saturn's rings) |
| `orbit` (ring) | string | - | Draw this body's real orbit. Put a moon's at its planet's point |

### The scene clock

**`clock` on the card sets the scene date: where the real bodies are, how they are turned, and the [sky dome](./objects/surfaces#grid) (`sky: sun | moon` points and paths) once it is set.** It starts at `date` and runs on at `rate`.

- `rate` is days per second as a number (`1` a day a second, `30` a month, `365.25` a year), or with a unit as the time slider shows it: `1 h/s`, `30 d/s`, `1 y/s`, `-1 d/s` (units `s`, `min`, `h`, `d`, `w`, `mo`, `y`). `live` is real time, `0` holds it, and a negative rate runs back.
- **On screen:** the [time slider](./camera#camera-buttons) gets a date mode on a card with a clock: the date, its rate from a year a second backward to a year a second forward, and NOW. What it sets stays until the card's `clock` changes.
- **Separate from `time_scale`:** the clock moves the real bodies; `time_scale` and the speed slider run decorative motion (degree spins, scans, drift, moving dashes). Holding one does not hold the other.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 320
units: au
clock:
  # the Apollo 11 landing, an hour a second
  date: "1969-07-20T20:17:00Z"
  rate: 1 h/s
camera:
  buttons: true
  views:
    v:
      target: sun
      yaw: 30
      tilt: 40
      distance: 3.5
points:
  - id: sun
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    label: SOL
    style: major
  - id: earth
    body: earth
    marker: dot
    label: EARTH
  - id: venus
    body: venus
    marker: dot
    label: VENUS
    style: tiny
objects:
  - type: glow
    at: sun
    size: 0.25
    color: var(--lcars-yellow)
  - type: ring
    orbit: earth
    width: 1
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
  - type: ring
    orbit: venus
    width: 1
    opacity: 0.5
```

::: details More about the clock
- **From other cards:** `tap_action` with `action: set-clock`, `card: sol` (the astrometrics card's `id`), `date: now` and `rate: 30` on any LCARdS card; leave out `card` on the astrometrics card itself.
- **From automations:** the [`lcards.set_clock`](/configuration/ha-actions#lcards-set-clock) action, with `card_id`, `date` and or `rate`; `date` can be a date and time helper's state.
- **From an entity:** `date` and `rate` can follow an entity (`date` an `input_datetime`), or a template ([Settings from entities](./data#settings-from-entities)).
- **Spins follow the clock exactly,** however fast it runs: at a year a second a planet turns hundreds of times a second and looks still or slow (the wagon-wheel effect). Slow the date down to watch it turn.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clock.date` | string | `now` | The date the scene starts at: `now`, or an ISO date or date and time (`2026-10-30`, `1969-07-20T20:17:00Z`; a date alone is midnight UTC) |
| `clock.rate` | number / string | `live` | How fast the date runs: `live`, days per second, or with a unit (`1 h/s`) |

## Distances

**Every distance is in the units of what it belongs to.** An object's distance is to its nearest edge.

- A flat grid (`shape: plane` or `disc`, not deformed) is measured to its surface, so a galactic disc can hide once you dive into a star system above it: Sol sits 60 ly above the disc in the [star systems](#star-systems) example, and `min_distance: 20` on the grid hides it there.

| Distance | Units |
|---|---|
| A view's `distance` | Its target point's: the `station` view above is 4 km, the `galaxy` view 140,000 ly |
| A view with an `[x, y, z]` target | The scene's |
| `camera.limits` | The scene's |
| A point's or object's `fade`, `min_distance`, `max_distance` | Its own system's (the scene's outside one) |

## In the Studio

**The [Studio](./start#the-studio) edits a system's points and objects in the same Points and Objects tabs: select Open on the system's row.** The tabs then show that system's lists, in its units, with a bar naming it and **Back to the scene**. Tapping a point or object on the preview opens the list it is in.

- **Place** and **Pick on preview** put points on the system's own ground plane, in its units, and **drag** moves a point on its system's plane.
- **Capture** a view while the camera looks at a point (after a fly-to it does): the view names the point, with the distance in its units. New ids are checked against the whole card, since ids are card-wide.
- **Starters** adds parts into the system. A part with sizes starts at real sizes in the system's units (an Earth-sized planet one au out in a km system), or sized to fit the system when it has no named units ([Units](#units)); a part in other units than the system's goes to the scene instead.

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/astrometrics/scene.html -->

# Scene and Looks

**The settings for the whole scene: its units and motion, how it looks, what is behind it and how its labels are drawn.** What the scene holds is on the [Objects](./objects) and [Points](./points) pages; the camera is on [Camera and Views](./camera).

## Units and motion

**Scene units are yours to pick, and every moving key works in the same units: degrees or scene units per second.**

- Sizes, distances and positions are in scene units: a galaxy disc of radius 100, a planet of radius 10. Line widths, dashes, label sizes and card offsets are in px, so they hold their size at any zoom.
- For real data, name the units with `units` (`km`, `au`, `ly` ...): a solar system in km, a galaxy in light years with Sol inside it in km. The card holds the whole range, from a galaxy down to a station 1.5 km across. See [Scale](./scale).
- Motion is off until you set it. Turning is in degrees per second (`spin`, `camera.auto_rotate`); travel is in its own units per second (`dash.speed` in px, a fill's `speed` and a nebula's or noise's `drift` in scene units); repeating cycles are a `period` in seconds (`scan.period`, a deformation's `period`). Fly-to times are in ms, as everywhere in LCARdS.
- `time_scale` runs all that motion slower or faster. The sky, the [scene clock](./scale#the-scene-clock) and the camera are not affected.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 280
# everything turns at half the speed it is set to
time_scale: 0.5
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 25
      distance: 130
objects:
  # 20 degrees a second, so 10 at this time scale
  - type: sphere
    radius: 25
    spin: 20
    line_spacing_deg: 15
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
  - type: ring
    radius: 40
    spin: -30
    dash: [6, 8]
    color: var(--lcars-orange)
```

::: details More about motion
- **Bearings** are degrees clockwise from north (north is away from the default camera), as on a compass seen from above.
- **On screen:** the time slider under the [camera buttons](./camera#camera-buttons) changes the speed without changing the config. A new `time_scale` in the config wins over it.
- **Reduced motion:** spins, scans, drift and moving dashes stop whatever `time_scale` is ([Performance and motion](#performance-and-motion)).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `units` | string | - | What one scene unit is: `m`, `km`, `au`, `ly` or `pc`. Optional. See [Scale: units](./scale#units) |
| `time_scale` | number | `1` | Speed of the scene's motion (orbits, spins, drift, scans, trails): `0.5` half speed, `2` twice as fast, `0` holds it. Can [follow an entity](./data#settings-from-entities) |

## Looks: diagram and realistic

**One scene can be an LCARS diagram, a realistic view, or both.** Give an object or point `look: diagram` or `look: realistic`, and the card's `look` picks what shows.

- `diagram` shows what has `look: diagram`, `realistic` what has `look: realistic`, and `mixed` (the default) shows both. Anything without a `look` shows in every look, except orbits and routes (below).
- An object without a `look` that has a diagram part and a realistic part switches them by itself: a mapped planet is a wire globe in the diagram look and a photograph in the realistic one, with nothing extra to write. `look: all` keeps an object as configured in every look.
- Orbits and routes (a `ring` drawn as a line, a `path`) are part of the diagram: they show in the diagram and mixed looks and hide in the realistic one.
- Switching crossfades in place, without a rebuild.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 300
look: mixed
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 20
      distance: 150
points:
  - id: name
    xyz: [0, 38, 0]
    label: MARS
    style: minor
objects:
  # a wire globe in the diagram look, the map in the realistic one
  - type: sphere
    radius: 30
    image: builtin:mars_viking
    spin: 4
    line_spacing_deg: 15
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
  # diagram only
  - type: ring
    radius: 45
    dash: [6, 8]
    look: diagram
```

::: details More about looks
**What each object switches** when it has no `look`:

| Object | Diagram look | Realistic look |
|---|---|---|
| `sphere` with an `image` or a `fill.effect` | Its lines over a plain body (its `fill.color`) | The bare map or painted surface |
| `grid` with a `fill.effect` | Its lines | Its fill |
| `model` with `material: original` | A hologram | Its own materials |
| `glow` | A ring marker with four ticks, facing the camera | The glow |
| `cube` | Its edges and a grid on each face | The Borg cube or shaded box |
| `asteroid` | A wireframe of its rock | The lit rock |
| `belt` | Its inner and outer edges | The rocks |
| `comet` | Its nucleus as a wireframe, a ring round the coma, each tail as a line | Nucleus, coma and tails |
| `galaxy` | Each arm's spiral, the rim, a ring round the bulge and the bar | Stars, glow and dust |
| `crystalline` | Its spine and branches as lines, a ring round the core | The crystal and its core |
| `nebula` with `render: volume` | Its outline: a ball's three rings, a box's edges | The gas (and its lightning) |
| `ring` drawn as a line, `path` | The line | Hidden: orbits and routes are part of the diagram |

- **Mixed:** shows every object as configured. The wireframes (from `glow` down in the table) are drawn in the object's own colours and show in the diagram look only, so `mixed` draws those objects as configured, without the extra wireframe.
- **Rings with a band:** a ring with a `band` image (a planet's rings) is part of the realistic picture and shows in every look.
- **Far away:** an asteroid, belt or crystalline entity is a dot in every look.
- **No realistic form:** for what has none, such as a wormhole's wire funnel and its glowing vortex, give each part its own `look`.
- **From an entity:** `look` can follow an entity whose state (or `attribute`) names the look, in any case. An `input_select` with the options `DIAGRAM`, `REALISTIC` and `MIXED`, shown as a [select menu](../select-menu/) next to the card, makes a quick switch. The docs have no such helper, so this example is not live:

```yaml
look:
  entity: input_select.astro_look
```
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `look` | string / object | `mixed` | `diagram`, `realistic` or `mixed`: which objects and points show. Or the keys below |
| `look.entity` | string | - | An entity whose state names the look |
| `look.attribute` | string | - | Read this attribute instead of the state |
| `look` on an object or point | string | - | `diagram` or `realistic`; on an object also `all` (every look, as configured). See [Keys every object takes](./objects#keys-every-object-takes) |

## Backdrop

**Stars at infinity behind the scene: they turn with the camera and never move when it pans.** `stars: true` uses the defaults.

- Each star gets a random size between `min_radius` and `max_radius` and a random brightness within `brightness`; `seed` picks the same ones every time.
- `opacity` fades the whole layer, so the stars can sit quietly behind a busy scene.
- `backdrop.dust` adds depth dust: particles round the camera that stay put as it moves, so every move shows depth. It and the star streaks of a warp fly-to are on [Effects: warp and dust](./effects#warp-and-dust).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 260
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 0
      tilt: 10
      distance: 150
backdrop:
  stars:
    count: 2500
    min_radius: 0.4
    max_radius: 1.4
    brightness: [0.3, 1]
    colors: [var(--lcards-moonlight), var(--lcars-blue)]
    seed: 7
objects:
  - type: glow
    at: [0, 0, 0]
    size: 40
    color: var(--lcars-yellow)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `backdrop.stars` | boolean / object | off | Stars at infinity. `true` for the defaults, or the keys below |
| `backdrop.stars.count` | number | `2000` | How many stars, `0` to `50000` |
| `backdrop.stars.min_radius` | number | `0.4` | Smallest star radius, px |
| `backdrop.stars.max_radius` | number | `1.2` | Largest star radius, px |
| `backdrop.stars.brightness` | `[low, high]` | `[0.35, 1]` | Each star's brightness is picked between these, `0` to `1` |
| `backdrop.stars.color` | colour | `var(--lcards-moonlight)` | Star colour |
| `backdrop.stars.colors` | list | - | Several colours, picked at random per star. Wins over `color` |
| `backdrop.stars.opacity` | number | `1` | Fades the whole layer, `0` to `1` |
| `backdrop.stars.seed` | number | `7` | The same seed places the same stars |
| `backdrop.stars.streak` | number | `1` | How long stars and dust streak in a warp fly-to, times the usual length. `0`: never. See [Effects](./effects#warp-and-dust) |
| `backdrop.stars.spectrum` | boolean / object | off | Streaks split into colour. See [Effects](./effects#warp-and-dust) |
| `backdrop.dust` | boolean / object | off | Depth dust round the camera. See [Effects: warp and dust](./effects#warp-and-dust) |

## background_animation

**A flat background effect behind the scene: a nebula, a warp starfield, a grid.** It takes any [background animation](/core/effects/background-animations), as on the MSD card.

- It does not turn with the camera: it is a picture behind the 3D scene. For clouds in the scene itself, use a [nebula object](./effects#nebula).
- It takes a list, so several effects can be layered behind the scene.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 280
background_animation:
  - preset: nebula
    config:
      volumetric: true
      cloud_count: 4
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 30
      distance: 150
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 60
    pattern: polar
    line_spacing: 10
    spoke_count: 24
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `background_animation` | list | - | Background effects behind the scene. See [Background animations](/core/effects/background-animations) |
| `background_animation[].preset` | string | required | The effect: `nebula`, `starfield`, `grid` ... |
| `background_animation[].config` | object | the preset's | The effect's own settings |

## Labels

**How every label on the card is drawn: the text keys they all start from, the label styles, overlap and pixel snapping.** Point labels are LCARdS text, with the [text-field keys](/core/text-fields) of the other cards: fonts, sizes, weights, colours with state maps, background boxes, templates.

- `labels.default` sets keys for every label. `labels.styles` changes the built-in styles (`title`, `major`, `minor`, `tiny`) or adds your own, which starts from `minor`; a point picks one with `style`. A style's keys win over `labels.default`, which wins over the built-in style.
- When two labels overlap, the higher priority wins (the larger style), then the nearer one. `overlap: true` keeps them all shown; each still moves to a free side of its point when it can.
- Labels move by sub-pixel steps, which looks smooth while the scene turns. On a weak device, `snap: true` rounds them to whole px.
- What a label says, and its fields round the point, are on [Points: labels](./points#labels).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 280
labels:
  default:
    text_transform: uppercase
    letter_spacing: 1
  styles:
    # change a built-in style
    major:
      color: var(--lcars-orange)
    # add your own
    alert:
      font_size: 16
      color: var(--lcars-red)
      priority: 90
camera:
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 0
      tilt: 40
      distance: 160
points:
  - id: home
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    marker: reticle
    label: Starbase
    style: major
  - id: contact
    polar: [50, 60]
    marker: triangle
    label: Unknown contact
    style: alert
  - id: buoy
    polar: [45, 220]
    marker: dot
    label: Buoy
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 70
    pattern: polar
    line_spacing: 10
    spoke_count: 24
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `labels.default` | object | - | Text keys every label on the card starts from (`font_family`, `text_transform`, `letter_spacing` ...), over the built-in styles |
| `labels.styles` | object | - | Label styles by name: a built-in (`title`, `major`, `minor`, `tiny`) to change, or your own. See [Points: styles and defaults](./points#styles-and-defaults) |
| `labels.styles.<name>.priority` | number | by style | Which label wins when two overlap: higher wins. Built in: `title` 100, `major` 80, `minor` 40, `tiny` 10 |
| `labels.styles.<name>.overlap` | boolean | `labels.overlap` | Labels of this style are never hidden by another label |
| `labels.overlap` | boolean | `false` | Never hide a label when labels overlap. `false` hides the lower-priority one, which keeps busy scenes readable |
| `labels.snap` | boolean | `false` | Round label positions to whole px: crisper text on weak devices, steppier fast motion |

## A header bar

**The card is the scene only: for an LCARS frame round it, put it in a Layout Card.** An elbow or a bar-label button above the scene makes an "ALPHA QUADRANT" header.

- The [Layout Card](../layout-card/) places the astrometrics card and its frame together, so they move and size as one.

## Performance and motion

**The scene draws only when something moves, so an idle card costs nothing.** Every astrometrics card and WebGL background on a page shares one WebGL context.

- The scene draws when the camera moves, a fly-to runs, an object spins or an [effect](./effects) moves, the sky timer ticks or the theme changes. A still scene draws nothing, and off screen or in a hidden tab nothing draws.
- Under reduced motion (the system setting), spin, `auto_rotate`, [deformations](./objects/surfaces#deformed-grids) and every [effect](./effects) (drift, scans, moving dashes, fills) stop, and a fly-to jumps instead of flying (no warp streaks).
- Alert modes recolour the scene in place: every object crossfades to the alert palette over a moment (at once under reduced motion), the camera and motion carry on, and labels follow the palette at once.

::: details More about drawing
- **The scene clock:** a [scene clock](./scale#the-scene-clock) faster than a minute a second draws every frame; at a minute a second or slower it draws once a second. Under reduced motion the clock keeps running (it is data, like the sky) but moves things once a second.
- **Models:** labels behind a model are hidden with a small depth image, made only while something moves. See [model](./objects/ships#model).
- **Alert modes and models:** a model is built again in its new colours.
:::

## When the 3D view is unavailable

**The card shows 3D VIEW UNAVAILABLE, with the reason, when it cannot draw the scene.** That happens when the browser has no WebGL, or when the graphics context was lost (a GPU reset, too many WebGL pages).

- Reloading the page starts the view again.
