# Getting Started

**Start from the quick start below or from a starter, then open the card in the [Astrometrics Studio](#the-studio) to change it on the live scene.** Not sure which? [Where to start](./#where-to-start) matches what you want to a starter.

## Quick start

**A galaxy disc with three named stars: drag to turn it, scroll or pinch to zoom.** Tap **Vega** to fly to it; tap **MAP VIEW** to fly to the view named `map`.

- Scene units are yours to choose: here the disc has a radius of 100. Line widths, dashes and label sizes are in px, so they look the same at any zoom.
- Bearings are in degrees: **0 is north** (away from the camera in the default view), **clockwise** seen from above. `polar: [64, 160]` is 64 units out on a bearing of 160.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 360
camera:
  view: galaxy
  views:
    galaxy:
      target: core
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 35
      distance: 260
    map:
      target: core
      tilt: 90
      distance: 300
backdrop:
  stars: true
points:
  - id: core
    xyz: [0, 0, 0]
    label: GALACTIC CORE
    style: title
  - id: vega
    polar: [64, 160]
    marker: triangle
    label: Vega
  - id: rigel
    polar: [88, 95]
    marker: diamond
    label: Rigel
  - id: home
    polar: [45, 300]
    marker: reticle
    label: MAP VIEW
    tap_action:
      action: fly-to
      view: map
objects:
  - type: grid
    shape: disc
    radius: 100
    pattern: polar
    line_spacing: 10
    spoke_count: 36
    ring_labels:
      step: 30
  - type: ring
    radius: 100
    width: 2
  - type: glow
    at: core
    size: 50
```

## Starters

**A starter is a ready-made scene or part: add one, then change anything, since nothing refers back to it.** In the [Studio](#the-studio) the Starters tab adds one with a few settings and shows its YAML first; the [Starters](./starters) page has each one as a live card with its YAML to copy.

- **A scene** is a whole card: its camera views, points and objects. In the Studio, **Use this scene** replaces yours and **Merge into the scene** adds its points, objects and views to yours.
- **A part** adds itself to the scene you have, next to what is there: a planet with moons, a belt, a nebula field. Its ids start with its name (`planet_body`), so two of the same part need two names.
- A part is sized for where it goes: at its real size when the scene names its units, sized to fit when it is in scene units (see [How a scene is sized](./#how-a-scene-is-sized)). At its real size a planet is a dot in a light-year scene, so add it inside an open star system, in that system's units.

**Scenes:**

**Parts:**

## The Studio

**The card editor opens the Astrometrics Studio: a full-screen editor beside the live scene, where you build the card in forms and on the scene itself.** In the dashboard's edit mode, edit the card and select **Open Astrometrics Studio**.

![The Astrometrics Studio: the Objects tab on the left with a grid and a sphere in the list, the live scene on the right with a box round the selected planet](/img/cards/astrometrics-studio.webp)

- It works on a copy: **Save** writes it to the card, **Cancel** leaves the card as it was. Every change can be undone (Ctrl+Z, Cmd+Z on a Mac).
- The preview is the real card with your entities, so what you see is what the dashboard shows. Taps on it select instead of running actions.
- The Studio writes the same YAML you would write by hand and keeps keys it has no field for, so anything can be finished in its YAML tab.

| Tab | What you do there |
|---|---|
| **Starters** | Try a scene or part in the preview, then keep it. The Studio opens here for a new card |
| **Scene** | Units, look, the scene date, warp, stars, background and label styles |
| **Objects** | Add objects from a gallery of every type, and edit each in a form |
| **Points** | Place points and give them labels, markers, entities and actions |
| **Camera** | Capture views, pick the start view, and set the controls, buttons and limits |
| **YAML** | The whole config, with completion from the card's schema |

::: details More about the Studio
- **On the scene:** tap a point or object to open its row; drag a point to move it (it slides along the object it stands on); **Place a point** in the toolbar adds one where you tap next.
- **Capture a view:** move the preview's camera where you want it and select **Capture view** in the Camera tab: its target, yaw, tilt and distance become a new named view.
- **Star systems:** a `system` row in the Objects tab has an **Open** button. The preview flies to it, and the Points, Objects and Starters tabs then edit the system, in its own units.
- **Following an entity:** a field with a link button can follow an entity instead of holding a number (see [Settings from entities](./data#settings-from-entities)).
- **Measure and units:** the toolbar can measure between two places, and the units of the open scene or system, with a scale bar, sit at the bottom right of the preview.
- **Prisms:** a prism's outline can be drawn and dragged on the preview.
:::

## Card options

**The astrometrics card's own top-level keys.** Each block has its own page; this table links to it.

- The card also takes the keys every LCARdS card takes (`id`, `tags`, `sounds`, `grid_options`, `width`, `min_height`, `max_height` ...): see [Common card properties](../common).
- Any number on a point or object can follow an entity (`opacity` from a sensor, say): see [Settings from entities](./data#settings-from-entities).
- The [config checker](/getting-started/config-checker) also checks what the schema cannot: that each point has exactly one position, and that every id a point, path, ring, beam or view names exists.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 300
look: diagram
time_scale: 0.5
camera:
  buttons: true
  views:
    v:
      target: [0, 0, 0]
      yaw: 20
      tilt: 30
      distance: 140
backdrop:
  stars: true
objects:
  - type: sphere
    radius: 25
    image: builtin:earth_blue_marble
    spin: 10
    line_spacing_deg: 15
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
  - type: ring
    radius: 45
    dash: [6, 8]
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `height` | number / string | `400` | Card height, px or CSS. The scene fills the card. On a sections view the card takes the grid rows its height needs, so it never runs into the card below (`grid_options.rows` overrides) |
| `camera` | object | frames the scene | Views, controls, buttons, limits and fly-to timing: see [Camera and Views](./camera) |
| `points` | list | - | Named points with labels and markers: see [Points](./points) |
| `objects` | list | - | What is drawn: see [Objects](./objects) and [Effects](./effects) |
| `look` | string / object | `mixed` | `diagram`, `realistic` or `mixed`, or an entity naming one: see [Looks](./scene#looks-diagram-and-realistic) |
| `units` | string | - | What one scene unit is: `m`, `km`, `au`, `ly` or `pc`. See [Scale: units](./scale#units) |
| `clock` | object | - | The scene date and how fast it runs, for the real Solar System and the sky: see [The scene clock](./scale#the-scene-clock) |
| `time_scale` | number | `1` | How fast the scene's motion runs: `0.5` half speed, `0` still. See [Units and motion](./scene#units-and-motion) |
| `model_scale` | string | `real` | `real` or `visible`: how models at their real size start. See [Visible size](./objects/ships#visible-size) |
| `warp` | boolean / object | off | Go to warp: the stars stream past behind the scene. `true`, or an entity. See [Going to warp](./effects#going-to-warp) |
| `warp_factor` | number | `6` | How fast the stars stream at warp, `1` to `9.9` |
| `backdrop` | object | - | `stars` and `dust`: see [Backdrop](./scene#backdrop) and [Effects: warp and dust](./effects#warp-and-dust) |
| `background_animation` | list | - | Flat background effects behind the scene: see [background_animation](./scene#background-animation) |
| `labels` | object | - | `default`, `styles`, `overlap` and `snap` for every label: see [Labels](./scene#labels) |
| `rules` | list | - | Rules on the card, its points and its objects: see [Live data: rules](./data#rules) |
| `state_classification`, `triggers_update`, `data_sources` | | | For point entities and label templates: see [Live data](./data) |
| `variables` | object | - | Your own named values, for templates as `variables.<name>` |

# Starters

Ready-made scenes and parts for the [Astrometrics card](./). Copy one into your card and change anything: nothing refers back to the starter.

- In the [Astrometrics Studio](./start#the-studio), the **Starters** tab adds them with a few settings (a part's name, its centre, its size) and shows the YAML first. A scene replaces the card's scene or merges into it; a part adds itself next to what is there.
- Here, each one is a live card with its default settings. Copy its YAML into a card, or into the YAML tab of the Studio.

A part is sized for where it goes: at its real size when the scene names its units (km, au, ly), sized to fit the scene when it is in scene units ([Scale: Units](./scale#units)). The live cards here show each part on its own, at its own sizes.

A part's ids start with its name and an underscore (`planet_body`, `planet_orbit`), so two of the same part need two names. Its centre is a point of your scene (`sun`) or coordinates (`0, 0, 0`); with coordinates, the part adds a point of its own there (`planet_centre`).

<!-- starters:begin (generated by npm run docs:astro-starters, do not edit) -->

### Bajoran wormhole

The Bajoran wormhole as the station displays draw it: the mouth (a swirl of gas round a warm heart in the realistic look, an entrance disc and funnel in the diagram) and, diagram only, its inside: the pipeline, the negative CTL region, the ring singularity, the positive CTL region, the point singularity and the verteron membrane. Switch the card's look to see one or the other. Tap a name to fly to it. With a power entity (0 to 100) the mouth opens and the regions wobble with it.

| Setting | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Power entity (optional) | `` | A number from 0 to 100: the mouth opens with it. |

```yaml live collapsed
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 400
points:
  - { id: mouth, xyz: [0, 0, 0] }
  - id: name
    at: mouth
```

### Utopia Planitia yards

Three drydocks of the Utopia Planitia Fleet Yards in orbit over Mars (its USGS Viking map), a Galaxy-class starship in the first. Tap a drydock to fly to it.

```yaml live collapsed
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 400
points:
  - { id: mars, xyz: [0, -200, 0] }
  - { id: mars_name, at: mars, offset: [0, 40, 200], label: MARS, style: major }
  - { id: dock1, xyz: [-70, 30, 20] }
  - id: dock1_name
    at: dock1
    offset: [0, 14, 0]
    marker: reticle
    label: DRYDOCK 1
    style: minor
    tap_action: { action: fly-to, view: dock1 }
  - { id: dock2, xyz: [0, 38, 0] }
  - id: dock2_name
    at: dock2
    offset: [0, 14, 0]
    marker: reticle
    label: DRYDOCK 2
    style: minor
    tap_action: { action: fly-to, view: dock2 }
  - { id: dock3, xyz: [70, 30, -20] }
  - id: dock3_name
    at: dock3
    offset: [0, 14, 0]
    marker: reticle
    label: DRYDOCK 3
    style: minor
    tap_action: { action: fly-to, view: dock3 }
```

### Borg encounter

A Borg cube with its green halo bearing down on the built-in Galaxy-class starship, its tractor beam locked on. Tap a name to fly to it.

```yaml live collapsed
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card

  - { id: cube, xyz: [0, 0, -20] }

  - { id: ship, xyz: [0, 4, 70] }
  - id: ship_name
    at: ship
    offset: [0, 10, 0]
    label: USS ENTERPRISE
    style: minor
    tap_action: { action: fly-to, view: ship }
  - { id: emitter, xyz: [0, 2, 0] }
objects:
  - { type: glow, at: cube, size: 110, color: var(--lcards-green-medium), opacity: 0.45 }
  - { type: cube, id: borg, at: cube, size: 40, spin: 3, rotation: [8, 25, 0] }
  - { type: model, id: hull, src: builtin:galaxy_class, at: ship, size: 22, rotation: [0, 160, 0], scan: { period: 5 } }
  - { type: beam, from: emitter, to: ship, width: 10, color: var(--lcards-green-medium), pulse: true }
camera:
  view: encounter
  views:
    encounter: { target: [0, 0, 20], yaw: 120, tilt: 15, distance: 170 }

    ship: { target: ship, yaw: 150, tilt: 20, distance: 45 }
backdrop: { stars: { count: 2500 } }
```

### Galaxy to station at true scale

A galaxy in light years with the Sol system in km inside it, 26,000 light years from the core: tap SOL and dive from the galaxy to the planets, Earth and Deep Space 9, all at their real sizes and distances, with the planets where they are today.

### Star Trek galaxy

The Milky Way in light years cut into the four quadrants (the Alpha/Beta line runs from Sol to the core), with the Federation, the Klingon, Romulan and Cardassian empires, the Dominion and the Borg, the Bajoran wormhole to the Gamma Quadrant, Voyager's route home from Ocampa and the Great Barrier. Fly in to Sol for Federation space: Vulcan, Andoria and Tellar at their real stars (40 Eridani, Procyon, 61 Cygni), the Klingon, Romulan and Cardassian capitals at the distances the reference charts give. The galaxy view sizes the empires to be seen, so the two scales do not overlay exactly.

## Parts

Each part on its own card, at its default centre. In the Studio, give it a point of your scene as its centre.

### Planet with moons

A planet orbiting a centre point on its own ring, with up to four moons going round it. Tap the planet to fly to it.

Its ids start with its name (default `planet_`).

| Setting | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Label | `PLANET` |  |
| Orbits round | `0, 0, 0` | A point id (a star) or x, y, z. |
| Orbit radius | `40` |  |
| Planet radius | `3` |  |
| Moons (0 to 4) | `2` |  |
| Surface | `rocky` | A planet type (gas_giant, ringed_giant, ice_giant, storm_giant, clouds, lava, ice, rocky, terran), a map (builtin:mars_viking) or your own picture (/local/planet.jpg). |

```yaml live collapsed
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card

    polar: [40, 0]

    tap_action: { action: fly-to }

  - { id: planet_moon2, polar: [9.6, 110], object: planet_moon2_orbit, marker: dot, label: MOON2, style: tiny, max_distance: 120 }

    id: planet_orbit

    fill: { effect: { preset: rocky } }
    line_spacing_deg: 30

  - type: ring
```

### Comet

A comet on an orbit centred off its star, so it swings in close and out far. Its tails point away from the star and it grows and brightens near it (activity.mode: distance). Tap it to fly to it.

Its ids start with its name (default `comet_`).

| Setting | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Label | `COMET` |  |
| Star | `0, 0, 0` | A point id (a star) or x, y, z. |
| Closest to the star | `25` |  |
| Farthest from the star | `175` |  |
| Seconds per orbit | `36` |  |

```yaml live collapsed
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card

points:

    id: comet_orbit

    spin: 10
```


### Sector volume set

Three territories side by side round a centre, each a see-through volume of cells in its own colour with its name above it. Tap one to fly to it.

Its ids start with its name (default `zone_`).

| Setting | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Centre | `0, 0, 0` | A point id or x, y, z. |
| Inner radius | `30` |  |
| Outer radius | `80` |  |

```yaml live collapsed
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 400
points:
  - { id: zone_centre, xyz: [0, 0, 0] }
  - { id: zone_a, at: zone_centre, offset: [27.5, 16, -47.6], label: TERRITORY A, style: major, color: var(--lcars-blue) }
  - { id: zone_b, at: zone_centre, offset: [54.2, 16, 9.6], label: TERRITORY B, style: major, color: var(--lcars-red) }
  - { id: zone_c, at: zone_centre, offset: [9.6, 16, 54.2], label: TERRITORY C, style: major, color: var(--lcars-green) }
objects:
  - type: volume
    id: zone_a_space
    at: zone_centre
    shape: sector
    radius: [30, 80]
    angle: [0, 60]
    height: [-4, 10]
    cells: { ring: 10, angle: 10, layer: 7 }
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
    tap_action: { action: fly-to }
  - type: volume
    id: zone_b_space
    at: zone_centre

    angle: [70, 130]
    height: [-4, 10]
    cells: { ring: 10, angle: 10, layer: 7 }

    tap_action: { action: fly-to }
  - type: volume

    height: [-4, 10]
    cells: { ring: 10, angle: 10, layer: 7 }

```

### Starbase

A built-in starbase model (Deep Space 9, Earth Spacedock or a Utopia Planitia drydock) at a point, with its name and main parts labelled; far away a starbase marker stands in for it. Tap the name to fly to it.

Its ids start with its name (default `starbase_`).

| Setting | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Label | `DEEP SPACE 9` |  |
| Model | `deep_space_nine` | deep_space_nine, earth_spacedock or utopia_planitia_drydock. |
| At | `0, 0, 0` | A point id or x, y, z. |
| Size (its largest extent) | `60` |  |

```yaml live collapsed
type: custom:lcards-astrometrics-card
height: 400
points:
  - { id: starbase_centre, xyz: [0, 0, 0] }
  - id: starbase_name
    at: starbase_centre
    offset: [0, 42, 0]
    label: DEEP SPACE 9
    style: minor
    tap_action: { action: fly-to, view: starbase_view }
  - { id: starbase_ops, object: starbase_station, part: ops, marker: dot, label: OPS, style: tiny, max_distance: 360 }
  - id: starbase_promenade
    object: starbase_station
    part: promenade
    marker: dot
    label: PROMENADE
    style: tiny
    max_distance: 360
  - id: starbase_docking_ring
    object: starbase_station
    part: docking_ring
    marker: dot
    label: DOCKING RING
    style: tiny
    max_distance: 360
  - id: starbase_far
    at: starbase_centre
    marker: starbase
    min_distance: 720
    tap_action: { action: fly-to, view: starbase_view }
objects:
  - type: model
    id: starbase_station
    src: builtin:deep_space_nine
    at: starbase_centre
    size: 60
    material: original
    max_distance: 720
camera: { views: { starbase_view: { target: starbase_centre, yaw: 30, tilt: 15, distance: 120 } } }
```

## Where the Star Trek galaxy's places come from

The [Star Trek galaxy](#star-trek-galaxy) and its parts follow what is recorded: what was said on screen, the published reference charts (*Star Trek: Star Charts* and *Stellar Cartography: The Starfleet Reference Library*, as summarised on Memory Alpha), and the star charts seen on screen that were drawn from them.

- **Quadrants:** two lines through the galactic core, one of them through Sol. Alpha is the half of Sol's side at galactic longitude 0 to 180 degrees (left of the line from Sol to the core, seen from above), Beta the other half; Gamma and Delta lie across the core.
- **Homeworlds at real stars** sit at those stars' real positions: Vulcan at 40 Eridani (16 ly, in Beta), Andoria at Procyon (11 ly, Beta), Tellar at 61 Cygni (11 ly, Alpha). Alpha Centauri, Wolf 359, Vega and Altair are there as well.
- **Other worlds** sit within the distances on record: Qo'noS over 100 ly from Sol in Beta, Romulus in Beta past the Neutral Zone, Bajor 5.25 ly from Cardassia in Alpha, Ferenginar 55 ly from Cardassia and 60 from Bajor, the far end of the Bajoran wormhole 4.72 ly from Idran, Idran about 70,000 ly from Bajor and Ocampa about 70,000 ly from Earth, the Dominion 40,000 to 50,000 ly from the core, the Great Barrier about 15,000 ly across. Sol is 26,000 ly from the core.
- **Two scales:** the galaxy view draws the empires as regions sized after the Federation's 8,000 light years, so they can be seen; the capitals are all within about 120 ly of Sol, so they appear only in the close-ups (FEDERATION, SOL NEIGHBOURS). The two do not overlay exactly. Region outlines and the places without a recorded position are our own.

# Button Card

`custom:lcards-button`

**The LCARS building block: a toggle button, a label, a panel or a section header, or a D-pad, alert symbol or round display.** Most buttons need only an `entity` and a `preset`.

- A button is drawn one of three ways: a `preset` shape, a `component` (a D-pad, the alert symbol, bracket arcs or a radar scope), or your own `svg`.
- The [Elbow card](../elbow/) is built on the button, so most of these pages apply to elbows too.

::: tip Try it
- The card editor's tabs cover the options on these pages, with a live preview.
- The [Playground](./playground) lets you edit button YAML here in the docs and see the result.
:::

| Page | Covers |
|------|--------|
| [Style, Text and Hover](./styles) | Background and border colours, text, hover and cursor, filters |
| [Icons](./icons) | The icon, its area beside the text, per-state icons, the divider |
| [Textures and Backgrounds](./textures) | Moving textures inside the shape and animated backgrounds |
| [D-pads, Alerts and Scopes](./components) | The D-pad, Voyager D-pad, alert symbol, brackets and radar |
| [Custom SVG](./custom-svg) | Your own SVG with tappable parts |
| [Playground](./playground) | Edit YAML and see the button live |

---

## Quick start

**Two examples to start from: a light you toggle, and a section header.**

- Presets hide their text until you ask for it: `text.name.show: true` shows the entity's name.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
tap_action:
  action: toggle
```

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: bar-label-left
interactive: false
text:
  label:
    content: NAVIGATION
```

## Presets

**`preset` picks the shape and the text layout.** Any `style`, `text` or icon key you set overrides the preset.

### Standard Buttons

**Filled, outlined and text-only buttons with rounded, half-rounded or square ends.** The `-right` versions put the icon area on the right.

- The `toggle-tab` line is the tab's top border, so it can go on any side at any thickness: `style.border.width.left: 6` with `top: 0` moves it to the left edge.

| Preset | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `lozenge` | Rounded at both ends, icon area on the left |
| `lozenge-right` | Rounded at both ends, icon shown on the right |
| `bullet` | Flat left end, rounded right end, icon area on the left |
| `bullet-right` | Rounded left end, flat right end, icon shown on the right |
| `capped` | Rounded left end, flat right end, icon area on the left |
| `capped-right` | Flat left end, rounded right end, icon shown on the right |
| `barrel` | Square corners, no border, icon area on the left |
| `barrel-right` | Square corners, no border, icon area on the right |
| `filled` | Square filled block with the name on the right |
| `filled-right` | Square filled block with the name on the left |
| `outline` | Transparent background with a border (Picard style) |
| `outline-right` | Like `outline`, icon area on the right |
| `icon` | Square icon-only button with rounded corners |
| `text-only` | No background or border: text alone |
| `toggle-tab` | Dark square tab with a centred name; a coloured line along the top shows the state |

### Panels

**Square-cornered blocks with a code label, for number columns and fillers.** With an entity they show the theme accent when on and the dark structure tone when off.

- Panels are decorative: they set `interactive: false`, so they don't change colour on hover.

| Preset | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `panel-light` | Light structure block with a code label |
| `panel-dark` | Dark structure block with a code label |
| `panel-flagged` | Dark code block with a thin accent flag on its left edge |

### Bar Labels

**Horizontal bars whose text sits on a black background that breaks the bar: the classic LCARS header.** The text grows with the card's height.

- A bar label is 56 px tall (one sections-view row) unless you set `height`.

| Preset | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `bar-label-base` | Bar label foundation: filled bar, text that scales with the height, centred |
| `bar-label-left` | Text on the left |
| `bar-label-center` | Text centred |
| `bar-label-right` | Text on the right |
| `bar-label-square` | Square corners |
| `bar-label-lozenge` | Rounded at both ends |
| `bar-label-bullet-left` | Flat left end, rounded right end |
| `bar-label-bullet-right` | Rounded left end, flat right end |
| `bar-label-capped-left` | Rounded left end, flat right end |
| `bar-label-capped-right` | Flat left end, rounded right end |

## Card options

**The button's own top-level keys.** Each block has its own page; this table links to it.

- The button also takes the keys every LCARdS card takes (`height`, `width`, `grid_options`, `id`, `tags`, `tap_action`, `hold_action`, `double_tap_action`, `animations`, `sounds`, `data_sources`, `rules` ...): see [Common card properties](../common).
- Set one of `preset`, `component` or `svg`. With `component`, `preset` names the component's own preset (such as `condition_red` on the alert).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge-right
icon: mdi:sofa
text:
  name:
    show: true
tap_action:
  action: toggle
hold_action:
  action: more-info
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `type` | string | required | `custom:lcards-button` |
| `entity` | string | - | The entity the button shows and acts on |
| `preset` | string | - | The shape: see [Presets](#presets). With `component`, the component's preset |
| `component` | string | - | `dpad`, `dpad_voyager`, `alert`, `brackets` or `radar`: see [D-pads, Alerts and Scopes](./components) |
| `svg` | object | - | Your own SVG: see [Custom SVG](./custom-svg) |
| `style` | object | from the preset | Background, border, cursor and text defaults: see [Style, Text and Hover](./styles) |
| `text` | object | from the preset | Text on the card: see [Text fields](./styles#text-fields) |
| `interactive` | boolean | `true` with an action or a switchable entity, else `false` | `false`: no hover colour or hover animations. See [interactive](./styles#interactive) |
| `filters` | list | - | CSS and SVG filters: see [filters](./styles#filters) |
| `show_icon` | boolean | `false`, `true` on some presets | Show the icon: see [Icons](./icons#icon) |
| `icon` | string | the entity's icon | The icon: see [Icons](./icons#icon) |
| `icon_area` | string | `left` | Where the icon's area sits: see [Icons](./icons#icon) |
| `icon_area_size` | number | fits the icon | Width (or height) of the icon area: see [Icons](./icons#icon) |
| `icon_area_background` | colour / state map | - | Background of the icon area: see [Icons](./icons#icon) |
| `icon_style` | object | - | Icon colour, size, position: see [icon_style](./icons#icon-style) |
| `divider` | object | from the preset | The line between icon and text: see [divider](./icons#divider) |
| `shape_texture` | object | - | A texture inside the shape: see [shape_texture](./textures#shape-texture) |
| `background_animation` | list | - | An animated background: see [background_animation](./textures#background-animation) |
| `dpad` | object | - | D-pad segments: see [dpad](./components#dpad) |
| `dpad_voyager` | object | - | Voyager D-pad segments: see [dpad_voyager](./components#dpad-voyager) |
| `brackets` | object | - | Bracket segments: see [Brackets and Radar](./components#brackets-and-radar) |
| `radar` | object | - | Radar segments: see [Brackets and Radar](./components#brackets-and-radar) |
| `alert` | object | - | Alert colours and presets: see [alert](./components#alert) |
| `ranges` | list | - | Switch the component's preset by value: see [ranges](./components#ranges) |
| `ranges_attribute` | string | the state | The attribute that [range colours](/core/colours/attributes#ranges-attribute) and `ranges` compare |
| `state_attribute` | string | - | The attribute whose value picks [exact-match colours](/core/colours/attributes#state-attribute) |
| `state_classification` | object | - | Which states count as active or inactive: see [state_classification](/core/colours/attributes#state-classification) |

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/button/components.html -->

# D-pads, Alerts and Scopes

`component` swaps the button's shape for a ready-made drawing whose parts (segments) each take their own colours and actions: a D-pad, the Voyager D-pad, the alert symbol, bracket arcs and a radar scope.

- A component draws to the height of its grid cell and keeps its proportions. In a sections view it asks for 6 columns and 5 rows (`alert` 4 rows, `dpad_voyager` 6); `grid_options` in your config changes that.
- Text fields go into the component's zones with `zone` (such as `center`); every component also has a `full` zone covering the whole drawing. See [Zones](/core/text-fields-zones).

## dpad

**`component: dpad` draws a nine-part direction pad, each part with its own action.** Use it for a TV remote, a camera mount or a media player.

- The segments are `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, `center` and the corners `up-left`, `up-right`, `down-left`, `down-right`. `default` sets keys for every segment at once.
- A segment without a `tap_action` does nothing when tapped; the card's own `tap_action` doesn't run for it.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
component: dpad
dpad:
  segments:
    # every segment: gray, and a hold opens the TV's dialog
    default:
      style:
        fill: var(--lcars-gray)
      hold_action:
        action: more-info
    center:
      entity: media_player.tv
      style:
        fill:
          default: var(--lcars-orange)
          hover: var(--lcars-yellow)
      tap_action:
        action: perform-action
        perform_action: media_player.media_play_pause
        target:
          entity_id: media_player.tv
    up:
      style:
        fill: var(--lcars-blue)
      tap_action:
        action: perform-action
        perform_action: media_player.volume_up
        target:
          entity_id: media_player.tv
    down:
      style:
        fill: var(--lcars-blue)
      tap_action:
        action: perform-action
        perform_action: media_player.volume_down
        target:
          entity_id: media_player.tv
```

::: details More about dpad
- **Zones:** text zones use underscores (`up_left`, `down_right`), while the segments use hyphens (`up-left`). A text field without `zone` goes into the first zone, `up`.
- **Order:** the theme's D-pad colours, then `segments.default`, then the segment's own keys, so a segment's own `style` wins over `default` and `default` over the theme. The same holds on every component.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `dpad.segments.default` | object | - | [Segment keys](#segment-keys) for every segment |
| `dpad.segments.<id>` | object | the theme's D-pad colours | [Segment keys](#segment-keys) for one segment: `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, `center`, `up-left`, `up-right`, `down-left`, `down-right` |

### Segment keys

**The keys a segment takes, on every component and in [custom SVG](./custom-svg).** A style colour can be a state map, with `hover` and `pressed` keys for the pointer.

- A segment follows the card's `entity` unless it sets its own, so one D-pad can show several devices.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
component: dpad
dpad:
  segments:
    center:
      entity: light.living_room
      tap_action:
        action: toggle
      hold_action:
        action: more-info
      style:
        fill:
          active: var(--lcars-yellow)
          inactive: var(--lcars-gray)
        stroke: var(--lcars-orange)
        stroke-width: 2
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `entity` | string | the card's `entity` | The entity this segment shows and acts on |
| `tap_action` | object | - | What a tap on the segment does: see [Actions](/core/actions) |
| `hold_action` | object | - | What a hold does |
| `double_tap_action` | object | - | What a double tap does |
| `style.fill` | colour / state map | from the component | Fill colour |
| `style.stroke` | colour / state map | from the component | Outline colour |
| `style.stroke-width` | number / string / state map | from the component | Outline width in px (0 to 50), or a CSS length |
| `style.opacity` | number / state map | - | Opacity, 0 to 1 |
| `text` | string | - | Text written into the segment's element, for an SVG `<text>` element. May be a template |
| `animations` | list | - | Animations on this segment only: the same entries as the card's [animations](/core/animations) |
| `selector` | string | `#<segment id>` | CSS selector for the part of the drawing, to target several elements at once |

## dpad_voyager

**`component: dpad_voyager` draws the D-pad as on Voyager's consoles, with every shape of the artwork a segment of its own.** It has 56 segments; configure them under `dpad_voyager.segments` with the same [segment keys](#segment-keys).

- The main segments are `center`, `up_arrow`, `down_arrow`, `left_arrow`, `right_arrow` and the corners `up_left`, `up_right`, `down_left`, `down_right`.
- Each arm also has `<arm>_shaft`, `<arm>_outer` and `<arm>_ring` (and the up arm `up_inner` and `up_seam`). The decorative band round them is `ring_<direction>_<n>` (such as `ring_up_1` or `ring_upright_2`), `ring_down`, `ring_downright`, `top_bar_1` to `top_bar_7` and `accent_1` to `accent_6`.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
component: dpad_voyager
dpad_voyager:
  segments:
    center:
      entity: light.demo
      tap_action:
        action: toggle
      style:
        fill:
          active: var(--lcards-orange)
          inactive: var(--lcards-gray)
    up_arrow:
      tap_action:
        action: perform-action
        perform_action: media_player.volume_up
        target:
          entity_id: media_player.tv
    down_arrow:
      tap_action:
        action: perform-action
        perform_action: media_player.volume_down
        target:
          entity_id: media_player.tv
```

::: details More about dpad_voyager
- **Zones:** every segment is also a text zone of the same name, so a label can sit on any part. A text field without `zone` goes into `up_left`.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `dpad_voyager.segments.default` | object | - | [Segment keys](#segment-keys) for every segment |
| `dpad_voyager.segments.<id>` | object | the theme's D-pad colours | [Segment keys](#segment-keys) for one segment |

## Brackets and Radar

**Two decorative round components: `brackets` frames a reading between two arcs, `radar` draws a scope.** Put a number or label in the `center` zone with a text field.

- `brackets` has the segments `left` and `right`, and the zones `center`, `left` and `right`.
- `radar` has the segments `rim`, `rings`, `inner-ring`, `cross` and `sweep` (the wedge), and the zone `center`. Their colours come from the theme's primary and secondary colours.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
component: brackets
text:
  label:
    content: "88"
    position: center
    font_size: 48
    color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
```

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
component: radar
radar:
  segments:
    sweep:
      style:
        fill: var(--lcars-orange)
    rim:
      style:
        stroke: var(--lcars-blue)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `brackets.segments.default` | object | - | [Segment keys](#segment-keys) for both arcs |
| `brackets.segments.<id>` | object | the theme's secondary colour | [Segment keys](#segment-keys) for `left` or `right` |
| `radar.segments.default` | object | - | [Segment keys](#segment-keys) for every part |
| `radar.segments.<id>` | object | the theme's colours | [Segment keys](#segment-keys) for `sweep`, `rings`, `inner-ring`, `cross` or `rim` |

## alert

**`component: alert` draws the Starfleet alert symbol: a shield with bars that sweep in light, and two lines of text.** `preset` picks the condition, and [`ranges`](#ranges) can switch it by a sensor's value.

- The presets are `default`, `condition_red`, `condition_yellow`, `condition_blue`, `condition_green`, `condition_gray` and `condition_black`. Each sets the shield and bar colours, the sweep colours and the text (`ALERT` over `CONDITION: RED` ...).
- The text fields are `alert_text` (zone `alert_line`) and `sub_text` (zone `sub_line`); set `text.alert_text.content` to change the words.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
component: alert
preset: condition_yellow
alert:
  color:
    shape: var(--lcars-orange)
text:
  sub_text:
    content: "DECK 7"
```

::: details More about alert
- **Your own presets:** `alert.custom_presets` adds presets or changes built-in ones, keyed by name. A preset with the name of a built-in one is merged over it, so you give only what changes. Each takes `segments.shape.style.fill`, `segments.bars.style.stroke` and `text.<field>.content` / `text.<field>.color`, and `extends: <preset>` builds on another preset.
- **Order:** the component's colours, then the preset's, then `alert.color`, then `alert.segments`; a matching range's `color` wins over all of them while it matches.
- **The sweep:** the bars' light sweep is two looping `on_load` animations with the ids `bars-top-sweep` and `bars-bottom-sweep`. An entry in `animations` with the same `id` changes it.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `preset` | string | `default` | The condition: `default`, `condition_red`, `condition_yellow`, `condition_blue`, `condition_green`, `condition_gray`, `condition_black`, or one of your `custom_presets` |
| `alert.color.shape` | colour | from the preset | Fill of the shield |
| `alert.color.bars` | colour | from the preset | Colour of the bars |
| `alert.segments.shape.style.fill` | colour | from the preset | Fill of the shield, as a segment style |
| `alert.segments.bars.style.stroke` | colour | from the preset | Colour of the bars, as a segment style |
| `alert.custom_presets` | object | - | Your own or changed presets, keyed by name |

### ranges

**`ranges` switches the component's preset by the entity's value: red alert above 80, yellow from 50.** The first entry that matches wins; when none matches, the card's `preset` (or `default`) is used.

- `above` and `below` are strict (`>` and `<`); `at_least` and `at_most` include the value itself. Combine one of each for a band, as in the example, so neighbouring bands meet without a gap.
- The value is the entity's state, or the attribute in `ranges_attribute` (or the entry's own `attribute`). `brightness_pct` is a light's brightness as 0 to 100.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
component: alert
entity: sensor.threat_level
ranges:
  - preset: condition_red
    at_least: 80 # 80 and up
  - preset: condition_yellow
    at_least: 50 # 50 up to 80
    below: 80
  - preset: default
    below: 50
```

::: details More about ranges
- **Text values:** `equals` compares as text, so it also matches states such as `"on"` or `"armed_away"`. An entry with `equals` ignores its number keys.
- **Changed meaning:** `above` used to include the value itself here (`>=`). A range that relied on a value landing exactly on an `above` boundary now needs `at_least`.
- **Attributes:** ranges are checked on every update, so a range on an attribute (a light's brightness) switches even when the state stays `on`.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `ranges[].preset` | string | required | The component preset to use while this entry matches |
| `ranges[].above` | number | - | Matches when the value is greater than this |
| `ranges[].at_least` | number | - | Matches when the value is this or greater |
| `ranges[].below` | number | - | Matches when the value is less than this |
| `ranges[].at_most` | number | - | Matches when the value is this or less |
| `ranges[].equals` | string / number / boolean | - | Matches when the value is exactly this, compared as text |
| `ranges[].attribute` | string | `ranges_attribute` | The attribute this entry compares |
| `ranges[].color.shape` | colour | - | Shield fill while this entry matches |
| `ranges[].color.bars` | colour | - | Bar colour while this entry matches |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/button/custom-svg.html -->

# Custom SVG

Your own drawing as a button: inline SVG markup or an SVG file, with parts you can tap.

## svg

**`svg` draws the button from your own SVG, and elements with an `id` become segments with their own entity, colours and actions.** Use it for a floor plan of switches, a ship schematic or any control the presets and components don't cover.

- Configure a segment under `svg.segments.<id>` with the same [segment keys](./components#segment-keys) as a component. With a `default` entry, every element that has an `id` becomes a segment; without one, only the ids you list do.
- The SVG is drawn to fit the card, keeping its proportions (`xMidYMid meet`), from its own `viewBox` (or `0 0 100 100` when it has none).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
svg:
  content: |
    <svg viewBox="0 0 200 100">
      <rect id="btn-a" x="10" y="10" width="80" height="80" rx="8"/>
      <rect id="btn-b" x="110" y="10" width="80" height="80" rx="8"/>
    </svg>
  segments:
    default:
      style:
        fill:
          active: var(--lcars-orange)
          inactive: var(--lcars-gray)
          hover: var(--lcars-yellow)
    btn-a:
      entity: light.zone_a
      tap_action:
        action: toggle
    btn-b:
      entity: light.zone_b
      tap_action:
        action: toggle
grid_options:
  rows: 2
```

::: details More about svg
- **Tokens in the markup:** `{{entity.state}}` and `{{entity.attributes.<name>}}` are replaced with the card entity's values, `{{entity.state == 'on' ? 'a' : 'b'}}` picks one of two words, and `theme:<token path>` is replaced with the theme's value. `enable_tokens: false` turns this off.
- **Colours in the markup:** CSS variables in an SVG `fill` attribute are not read the same way in every browser. Colours set in a segment's `style` always work, because the card resolves them.
- **Scripts:** `<script>`, `<iframe>`, `<embed>` and `<object>` elements are removed unless `allow_scripts: true`. Event attributes (`onclick` ...) and `javascript:` or `data:` links are always removed.
- **Text:** `<text>` elements in the SVG let taps through to the segment beneath them.
- **Files:** `src` takes a URL, such as a file under `/local/`, or a `data:` URI.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `svg.content` | string | - | Inline SVG markup |
| `svg.src` | string | - | URL of an SVG file, instead of `content` |
| `svg.viewBox` | string | the SVG's own, else `0 0 100 100` | The drawing's coordinate box |
| `svg.preserveAspectRatio` | string | `xMidYMid meet` | How the drawing fits the card |
| `svg.enable_tokens` | boolean | `true` | Replace `{{entity...}}` and `theme:` tokens in the markup |
| `svg.allow_scripts` | boolean | `false` | Keep `<script>` elements in the SVG |
| `svg.segments.default` | object | - | [Segment keys](./components#segment-keys) for every element with an `id` |
| `svg.segments.<id>` | object | - | [Segment keys](./components#segment-keys) for the element with that `id` |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/button/icons.html -->

# Icons

The icon on a button: which one, where its area sits, how it is coloured and placed, a different icon per state, and the divider line between the icon and the text.

## icon

**`show_icon: true` shows an icon in an area of its own beside the text.** The icon is `icon`, or the entity's own icon when you leave `icon` out.

- Most presets hide the icon, so setting `icon` alone is not enough: add `show_icon: true`. The `icon` preset and the `-right` lozenge, bullet and capped presets show it already.
- `icon_area` puts the area on the `left`, `right`, `top` or `bottom` edge, and the text fills the rest. `none` reserves no area: the icon sits over the button like a text field, placed by [`icon_style.position`](#icon-style).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge
show_icon: true
icon: mdi:sofa
icon_area_background:
  active: var(--lcars-yellow)
  inactive: var(--lcars-gray)
text:
  name:
    show: true
tap_action:
  action: toggle
```

::: details More about icon
- **Icon names:** `mdi:` for Material Design Icons, `si:` for Simple Icons, `entity` for the entity's own icon. Other installed icon sets (such as `hue:`) work too.
- **Area size:** without `icon_area_size` the area is as wide as the icon plus a little space each side and the divider. A larger area leaves the icon centred in it, so it reads as a coloured cap.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `show_icon` | boolean | `false`, `true` on `icon` and the `-right` lozenge, bullet and capped presets | Show the icon |
| `icon` | string | the entity's icon | `mdi:...`, `si:...` or `entity` |
| `icon_area` | string | `left`, or the preset's | `left`, `right`, `top`, `bottom` or `none` |
| `icon_area_size` | number | fits the icon | Width of a left or right area (height of a top or bottom one), 20 to 500 px |
| `icon_area_background` | colour / state map | - | Fill of the icon area, clipped to the button's shape |

## icon_style

**`icon_style` sets the icon's colour, size, position and rotation.** The colour can follow the entity's state like any other colour.

- The icon shrinks to fit the button's height, keeping `spacing` clear above and below it.
- `position` places the icon inside its area (`center`, `top-left`, `bottom-right` ...). With `icon_area: none` it places the icon on the whole button, `padding` away from the edges.
- `x` and `y` (or `x_percent` and `y_percent`) place the icon's top-left corner anywhere on the button. Set both of a pair; the icon then has no area of its own.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: sensor.temperature
preset: barrel
show_icon: true
icon: mdi:thermometer
icon_area: none
icon_style:
  position: top-right
  padding: 10
  size: 32
  rotation: -15
  color: var(--lcards-moonlight) # a plain colour: every state
text:
  name:
    show: true
    position: bottom-left
    color: var(--lcards-moonlight)
grid_options:
  rows: 2
```

::: details More about icon_style
- **Nudging inside the area:** `padding` as an object (`top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left`) moves the icon within its area away from that edge. `padding_left`, `padding_right`, `padding_top` and `padding_bottom` set one side on their own: each is the same as that side of the object and wins over it, and the other sides keep their values.
- **Colour fallback:** without `icon_style.color` the icon takes the preset's icon colour, then the theme's, then the button's text colour.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `icon_style.color` | colour / state map | the preset's icon colour | Icon colour |
| `icon_style.icon` | string / state map | - | Icon per state, instead of `icon`: see [Per-State Icons](#per-state-icons) |
| `icon_style.size` | number | `24` | Icon size, 8 to 200 px |
| `icon_style.position` | string | `center` | Where the icon sits in its area, or on the button with `icon_area: none` |
| `icon_style.x` | number | - | Left edge of the icon from the button's left, px. Needs `y` |
| `icon_style.y` | number | - | Top edge of the icon from the button's top, px. Needs `x` |
| `icon_style.x_percent` | number | - | Left edge as a percentage of the button's width (0 to 100). Needs `y_percent` |
| `icon_style.y_percent` | number | - | Top edge as a percentage of the button's height (0 to 100). Needs `x_percent` |
| `icon_style.rotation` | number | `0` | Rotation in degrees, -360 to 360 |
| `icon_style.padding` | number / object | `8` | A number: space from the button's edges with `icon_area: none`. An object: nudges the icon inside its area |
| `icon_style.padding.top` | number | `0` | Move the icon down from the top of its area, px |
| `icon_style.padding.right` | number | `0` | Move the icon in from the right of its area, px |
| `icon_style.padding.bottom` | number | `0` | Move the icon up from the bottom of its area, px |
| `icon_style.padding.left` | number | `0` | Move the icon in from the left of its area, px |
| `icon_style.padding_top` | number | `0` | One side of `padding`: the same as `padding.top`, and wins over it. 0 to 200 px |
| `icon_style.padding_right` | number | `0` | The same as `padding.right`, and wins over it. 0 to 200 px |
| `icon_style.padding_bottom` | number | `0` | The same as `padding.bottom`, and wins over it. 0 to 200 px |
| `icon_style.padding_left` | number | `0` | The same as `padding.left`, and wins over it. 0 to 200 px |
| `icon_style.spacing` | number | `8` | Space kept round the icon in its area, 0 to 100 px |

### Per-State Icons

**`icon_style.icon` as a state map swaps the icon by state, including value ranges.** Use it for a bulb that changes with brightness or a lock that shows open and closed.

- The icon is picked in the same order as [state colours](/core/colours/state-maps#resolution-order): the exact state, `zero`, ranges, `non_zero`, active or inactive, `default`, and last the top-level `icon`.
- [`ranges_attribute`](/core/colours/attributes#ranges-attribute) makes the range keys compare an attribute; `brightness_pct` is a light's brightness as 0 to 100.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.tv
preset: lozenge
show_icon: true
ranges_attribute: brightness_pct # ranges compare brightness, 0 to 100
icon: mdi:lightbulb # used when nothing below matches
icon_style:
  icon:
    above:90: mdi:lightbulb-alert
    below:20: mdi:lightbulb-outline
    active: mdi:lightbulb
    inactive: mdi:lightbulb-off
text:
  name:
    show: true
tap_action:
  action: toggle
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `icon_style.icon` | string / state map | - | One icon, or an icon per state key (`active`, `inactive`, `unavailable`, an exact state, `above:N`, `below:N` ...). A string may be a template |

## divider

**The line between the icon area and the text.** Set `width: 0` to hide it.

- The divider is only drawn when the icon shows in a `left`, `right`, `top` or `bottom` area.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge
show_icon: true
divider:
  color: var(--lcars-orange)
  width: 2
text:
  name:
    show: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `divider.width` | number | `5` with a preset, `6` without | Thickness in px, 0 to 200. `0` hides it |
| `divider.color` | colour | the theme's button text colour (black) | Divider colour. One colour, not a state map |

# Button Playground

Edit the YAML and the card redraws as you type. Pick a starting point (a lozenge toggle, state colours, a bar-label header or a sensor readout), then change the preset, label or colours.

**You don't need to know the YAML to start:**

- **Quick settings** above the editor change the most common options for you.
- **Type in the editor** and it suggests the options that fit where your cursor is, with a short description. Press **Ctrl+Space** to see suggestions anywhere, and hover over a key to read what it does.
- **Options here** (under the editor) lists everything you can add at the cursor. **Insert** adds it at the right indent, and **Docs** opens its section in a new tab.

<ClientOnly>

</ClientOnly>

## How the preview works

The preview is the real button card, the same code your dashboard runs. The docs site has no Home Assistant, so:

- **Entities get sample values.** The entities listed under the preview are always there, and any other entity id in your YAML gets a plausible value for its domain (lights and switches are on, sensors get a number with a unit).
- **Taps that toggle** switch the sample entity, so state colours change as on a dashboard. **More info**, **navigate** and other actions say what they would do instead.
- **Jinja2 templates** (`{{ ... }}`) need Home Assistant and render empty here; `{entity.state}` tokens and `[[[ JavaScript ]]]` templates work.
- **Icons** aren't drawn (Home Assistant provides them), and sounds are off.

Messages under the card show schema warnings for your YAML.

When it looks right, **Copy YAML** and paste it into your card's YAML editor, then swap in your own entities.

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/button/styles.html -->

# Style, Text and Hover

How a button looks and reacts: its background and border, the text on it, what happens when the pointer is over it, and filters. Colours take a plain colour or a [state map](/core/colours/state-maps) (`default`, `active`, `inactive`, `unavailable`, `hover`, `pressed`, exact states and ranges).

## style.card

**`style.card.color.background` is the button's fill colour, one colour or one per state.** Use it to light a button when its entity is on and dim it when off.

- `hover` and `pressed` keys colour the button while the pointer is over it or it is pressed. They have no effect when [`interactive`](#interactive) is `false`.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
style:
  card:
    color:
      background:
        active: var(--lcars-orange)
        inactive: var(--lcars-gray)
        hover: var(--lcars-yellow)
tap_action:
  action: toggle
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.card.color.background` | colour / state map | from the preset (theme button colours) | The button's fill |

## style.border

**The border's colour, width and corner radius.** Rounded presets set the radius for you; set it yourself for a custom shape.

- `width` and `radius` take one number for every side or corner, or an object with one key per side (`top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left`) or corner (`top_left`, `top_right`, `bottom_right`, `bottom_left`). The sides or corners an object leaves out keep the preset's value.
- A radius larger than half the button's height (or width) is made smaller to fit, so a tall button keeps its shape.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: outline
text:
  name:
    show: true
style:
  border:
    width: 3
    color:
      active: var(--lcars-orange)
      inactive: var(--lcars-gray)
    radius:
      top_left: 24
      bottom_right: 24
tap_action:
  action: toggle
```

::: details More about style.border
- **Rounded presets:** `lozenge`, `bullet` and `capped` take their round ends from the Home Assistant theme's card radius (`--ha-card-border-radius`, 34 px in HA-LCARS), not from the button's height.
- **Theme values:** `width` and `radius` also take a theme token or a CSS variable, such as `theme:components.button.radius.large` or `var(--ha-border-radius-lg)`.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.border.color` | colour / state map | the button's own colour (theme button colours) | Border colour. It matches the fill by default, so on a filled preset set a different colour to see the border |
| `style.border.width` | number / string / object | from the preset: `0` on most | Border width in px, a token, or one per side |
| `style.border.width.top` | number / string | from the preset | Top border width |
| `style.border.width.right` | number / string | from the preset | Right border width |
| `style.border.width.bottom` | number / string | from the preset | Bottom border width |
| `style.border.width.left` | number / string | from the preset | Left border width |
| `style.border.radius` | number / string / object | from the preset | Corner radius in px (0 to 100), a token, or one per corner |
| `style.border.radius.top_left` | number / string | from the preset | Top-left corner radius |
| `style.border.radius.top_right` | number / string | from the preset | Top-right corner radius |
| `style.border.radius.bottom_right` | number / string | from the preset | Bottom-right corner radius |
| `style.border.radius.bottom_left` | number / string | from the preset | Bottom-left corner radius |

## Text Fields

**`text` puts any number of labels on the button, each placed and styled on its own.** The full reference is the [Text Fields](/core/text-fields) page.

- Every preset already has three fields: `name` (the entity's name), `state` (its state) and `label` (a random code). Most presets hide them until you set `show: true`; fields with any other name show by default.
- `text.default` sets the font, size and colour for every field on the card, and `style.text.default` does the same at a lower priority.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: sensor.temperature
preset: barrel
text:
  default:
    font_family: "Antonio, sans-serif"
    color: var(--lcards-moonlight)
  name:
    content: TEMPERATURE
    show: true
    position: top-left
    font_size: 11
  value:
    content: "{entity.state}"
    position: center
    font_size: 28
    font_weight: bold
    color:
      default: var(--lcards-moonlight)
      unavailable: var(--lcars-alert-red)
grid_options:
  rows: 2
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `text` | object | from the preset | The fields, keyed by any name you choose: see [Text Fields](/core/text-fields) |
| `text.default` | object | - | Font, size and colour for every field |
| `style.text.default.color` | colour / state map | the theme's button text colour | Text colour for every field, below `text.default` |
| `style.text.default.font_size` | number / string | from the preset | Font size for every field |
| `style.text.default.font_weight` | string / number | from the preset | Font weight for every field |
| `style.text.default.font_family` | string | from the preset | Font for every field |
| `style.text.default.letter_spacing` | number / string | `normal` | Space between letters for every field: px as a number, or a CSS value (`0.1em`) |
| `style.text.default.text_transform` | string | from the preset | Case for every field: `none`, `uppercase`, `lowercase` or `capitalize` |

## interactive

**`interactive: false` makes a button decorative: no hand cursor, no hover colour, no hover animations.** Use it for panels, headers and fillers that shouldn't look tappable.

- A button with no action and no entity a tap can toggle (a title, a dot row, a filler, a sensor readout) is decorative already; set `interactive: true` to give it hover effects anyway.
- A label bound to a light, switch or input boolean only for its text or colour still toggles it on a tap; give it `tap_action: { action: none }` and it is decorative too.
- Taps and holds still run their actions, so a decorative button can still do something.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.corridor
preset: lozenge
interactive: false # no hand cursor or hover colour
text:
  name:
    show: true
tap_action:
  action: toggle # still works
```

::: details More about interactive
- **What changes:** with `interactive: true` the cursor is a hand (`pointer`), the background changes to the hover colour from the preset or `style`, and hover animations run. With `false` the cursor is the arrow (`default`), the colour stays, and hover animations don't run.
- **Presets:** the panel presets set `interactive: false` for you.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `interactive` | boolean | `true` with an action or a switchable entity, else `false` (`false` on panel presets) | `false`: no hand cursor, hover colour or hover animations. Actions still run |

## style.cursor

**`style.cursor` sets the mouse cursor over the button, whatever `interactive` says.** Use it to keep the hover effects but show a different cursor.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: lozenge
text:
  label:
    content: TARGET
    show: true
style:
  cursor: crosshair
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.cursor` | string | `pointer`, or `default` when `interactive: false` | Any CSS cursor: `pointer`, `default`, `none`, `not-allowed`, `crosshair`, `grab`, `zoom-in`, `help`, `wait`, `progress`, `move`, `copy`, `text` ... |

## filters

**`filters` runs CSS or SVG filters over the whole button: blur, brightness, colour shifts, glows.** They apply in order, the first innermost. The [Filters](/core/effects/filters) page lists every type and its value.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
filters:
  - type: brightness
    value: 0.8
  - type: saturate
    value: 0.5
  - type: blur
    value: 1px
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `filters[].mode` | string | `css` | `css` for CSS filter functions, `svg` for SVG filter primitives |
| `filters[].type` | string | required | A CSS filter (`blur`, `brightness`, `contrast`, `saturate`, `drop-shadow` ...) or an SVG primitive |
| `filters[].value` | string / number / object | - | The filter's value: its form depends on the type (`blur` takes a length such as `4px`) |

## Annotated Example

**A lozenge with state colours, a templated value, an icon, actions and two animations.** Each part is labelled.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.workbench
preset: lozenge
grid_options:
  rows: 2
# text: a small name at the top left, the brightness in the middle
text:
  default:
    font_family: "Antonio, sans-serif"
  label:
    content: Workbench
    show: true
    position: top-left
    font_size: 14
    text_transform: uppercase
    color: var(--lcards-moonlight)
  value:
    content: "[[[return entity.state === 'on' ? Math.round(entity.attributes.brightness / 255 * 100) + '%' : 'Off']]]"
    position: center
    font_size: 26
    font_weight: bold
    color:
      default: var(--lcards-moonlight)
      inactive: var(--lcards-gray)
# icon: grey when off, orange when on
show_icon: true
icon: mdi:desk-lamp
icon_area: left
icon_style:
  color:
    default: var(--lcards-gray)
    active: var(--lcards-orange)
  size: 28
# border: orange when on
style:
  border:
    color:
      default: var(--lcards-gray)
      active: var(--lcards-orange)
    width: 2
# actions
tap_action:
  action: toggle
hold_action:
  action: more-info
# animations: a bounce on tap, a glow while the light is on
animations:
  - trigger: on_tap
    preset: bounce
    params:
      scale_max: 1.05
      bounces: 2
    duration: 400
  - trigger: on_entity_change
    entity: light.workbench
    to_state: "on"
    check_on_load: true
    preset: glow
    params:
      color: var(--lcards-orange)
      blur_max: 12
    loop: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `animations` | list | - | Animations on triggers such as `on_tap` and `on_entity_change`: see [Animations](/core/animations) |
| `tap_action` | object | - | What a tap does: see [Actions](/core/actions) |
| `hold_action` | object | - | What a hold does |
| `double_tap_action` | object | - | What a double tap does |

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/button/textures.html -->

# Textures and Backgrounds

Movement and pattern on a button: a texture drawn inside the button's own shape, or an animated background behind the whole card.

## shape_texture

**`shape_texture` draws a pattern or a moving effect inside the button's fill, clipped to its shape.** Use it for a grid on a panel, a shimmer across a lozenge, or a level that rises with a sensor.

- It works on preset buttons (and on [elbows](../elbow/)), not with a `component` or your own `svg`.
- `opacity`, `speed` and every colour in `config` can follow the entity's state with a state map. Numbers and colours in `config` can also follow a value with `map_range` or a template.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
shape_texture:
  preset: grid
  opacity:
    active: 0.6
    inactive: 0.1
  mix_blend_mode: screen
  speed: 0.5
  config:
    line_spacing: 12
    color: var(--lcards-moonlight)
```

::: details More about shape_texture
- **Speed:** `speed` multiplies the preset's own scroll or sweep speed; `0` holds it still.
- **Following a value:** any number or colour in `config` can be `{ map_range: { entity, attribute, input, output, clamp } }`, the same keys as `map_range` in [animations](/core/animations). With two colours as `output` the colour is blended between them; each can be any colour LCARdS accepts (a hex of any length, a named colour, `rgb()` or `hsl()`, a CSS variable, a `theme:` token or a computed colour such as `alpha()`). `entity` defaults to the card's entity, `attribute` to its state, and `clamp` is on unless set to `false` (`entity_id`, the older name for `entity`, still works).
- **Full parameter reference:** every preset's keys and defaults are in [Shape Texture System](/architecture/internals/shape-texture-system).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `shape_texture.preset` | string | required | The texture: see [Available Presets](#available-presets) |
| `shape_texture.opacity` | number / state map | `0.3` | Texture opacity, 0 to 1 |
| `shape_texture.mix_blend_mode` | string | `normal` | How the texture mixes with the fill: `normal`, `multiply`, `screen`, `overlay`, `hard-light`, `soft-light`, `color-burn` or `color-dodge` |
| `shape_texture.speed` | number / state map | `1` | Speed multiplier; `0` is still |
| `shape_texture.config` | object | the preset's defaults | The preset's own keys: see the table below |

### Available Presets

**The textures `shape_texture.preset` takes, and the main keys of each.** Every `color` key takes a CSS variable, a theme token, `rgba()`, hex or a state map.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: sensor.battery
preset: capped
text:
  name:
    content: BATTERY
    show: true
shape_texture:
  preset: level
  opacity: 0.8
  config:
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
    fill_pct: "[[[return Number(entity.state)]]]"
    wave_height: 3
```

| Preset | What it draws | Main `config` keys |
|--------|---------------|--------------------|
| `grid` | Scrolling grid lines | `line_spacing`, `pattern` (`both`, `horizontal`, `vertical`) |
| `diagonal` | Scrolling diagonal hatching | `line_spacing` |
| `hexagonal` | Scrolling hexagonal grid | `hex_radius` |
| `dots` | Scrolling dot grid | `dot_radius`, `spacing` |
| `fluid` | Swirling noise, an organic wash of colour | `base_frequency`, `num_octaves` |
| `plasma` | Two-colour turbulent bands | `color_a`, `color_b`, `base_frequency` |
| `shimmer` | A band of light sweeping across | `angle`, `highlight_width`, `speed` |
| `flow` | Streaks streaming one way | `wave_scale`, `scroll_speed_x` |
| `level` | A fill bar with a wave on top | `fill_pct`, `direction`, `wave_height`, `color` (the fill), `color_b` (a tint at the leading edge) |
| `pulse` | A radial glow breathing in and out | `color`, `speed` (pulses per second), `radius`, `min_size` |
| `scanlines` | CRT-style scan lines | `line_spacing`, `direction` |
| `image` | Your image, clipped to the shape | `source`, `size`, `position`, `repeat` |

## background_animation

**`background_animation` draws animated layers (grids, starfields, nebulae, a data cascade) behind the button's content.** The [Background Animations](/core/effects/background-animations) page has every preset and its keys.

- The background sits behind the button's fill, so it shows best on a button with a transparent fill, such as the `outline` preset.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: outline
text:
  name:
    content: SENSOR GRID
    show: true
grid_options:
  rows: 2
background_animation:
  - preset: grid
    config:
      line_spacing: 20
      color: alpha(var(--lcars-orange), 0.3)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `background_animation` | list / object | - | A list of effects (bottom layer first), or `inset` plus `effects`: see [Background Animations](/core/effects/background-animations#canvas-options) |
| `background_animation[].preset` | string | required | The effect: see [Available Presets](/core/effects/background-animations#available-presets) |
| `background_animation[].config` | object | the preset's defaults | The effect's own keys |

# Chart Card

`custom:lcards-chart`

![Chart card: a 24-hour temperature history as an orange area with a gradient fill, a blue smoothed line from a data source, and a dashed comfort threshold](/img/cards/chart.webp)

**A chart of your Home Assistant sensors over time: lines, areas, columns, gauges, range bands, candlesticks and more.** It picks up your LCARS theme's colours and fonts, so most charts need nothing more than a list of entities.

- Each entry under `sources` is one series: an entity's history, Home Assistant's long-term statistics, or an LCARdS data source.
- The card is built on [ApexCharts](https://apexcharts.com/). You don't need to know ApexCharts to use it: these pages cover everything LCARdS sets up for you.

::: tip Try it
- In the card editor, **Open Configuration Studio** gives you a live preview while you add series, pick a chart type and adjust colours.
- The [Playground](./playground) lets you edit chart YAML here in the docs and see the result.
:::

The charts on these pages are drawn by the card's own code from generated sample data.

| Page | Covers |
|------|--------|
| [Series and Time](./series) | Where the data comes from, series options, the time window, grouping, Y axes |
| [Chart Types](./types) | Every chart type with an example, gauges, range charts, mixing types in one chart |
| [Styling](./styling) | Colours, lines, fills, markers, grid, fonts, theme, animation, raw ApexCharts options |
| [Axes and Labels](./labels) | Reference lines, legend, value labels, axes, formatters, tooltip and toolbar |
| [Examples](./examples) | Complete charts to copy |
| [Playground](./playground) | Edit YAML and see the chart live |
| [Upgrading](./upgrading) | Older chart configs, and coming from apexcharts-card |

---

## Quick start

**Three charts to start from: one sensor, two sensors as areas, and a week of daily energy from long-term statistics.**

- Without `graph_span` a chart shows the last 24 hours, and it moves along as time passes.
- Statistics suit long spans: see [Long-term statistics](./series#long-term-statistics).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
sources:
  - entity: sensor.living_room_temperature
```

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: area
sources:
  - entity: sensor.living_room_temperature
    name: Living room
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
style:
  legend:
    show: true
```

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: column
graph_span: 7d
sources:
  - entity: sensor.energy_consumption
    name: Energy per day
    statistics:
      type: change
      period: day
```

## Chart types

**`chart_type` picks how the series are drawn.** Time charts plot each series over the time window; the round charts, the radar and the treemap show each series' latest value.

- A series can override the chart type with its own `type`, so one chart can show columns and a line together: see [Mixing chart types](./types#mixing-chart-types).
- Every type is shown with an example on [Chart Types](./types).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: radialBar
sources:
  - entity: sensor.phone_battery
    name: Phone
  - entity: sensor.living_room_humidity
    name: Humidity
```

| Type | Shows | Data |
|------|-------|------|
| `line` | Values over time as lines | Any series |
| `area` | Lines with the area below filled | Any series |
| `column` | Vertical bars | Any series; works well with [grouping](./series#grouping) |
| `bar` | Horizontal bars, one per point, labelled with its time | Any series; group it so there are only a few bars |
| `scatter` | Individual points | Any series |
| `heatmap` | One row per series, colour by value | Any series; works well with grouping |
| `radialBar` | Circular gauges, one per series | The latest value of each series (0 to 100 works best) |
| `pie`, `donut` | Slices of a whole | The latest value of each series (use two or more) |
| `polarArea` | Slices sized by value | The latest value of each series |
| `radar` | Values around a polygon | The latest value of each series |
| `treemap` | Rectangles sized by value | The latest value of each series |
| `rangeArea` | A shaded band from low to high | See [Range charts](./types#range-charts) |
| `boxPlot` | Spread of values per time bucket | See [Range charts](./types#range-charts) |
| `candlestick` | Open, high, low and close per time bucket | See [Range charts](./types#range-charts) |
| `rangeBar` | Timeline bars from a start to an end time | Not offered in the Chart Studio: the card can't build its data yet; see [Range charts](./types#range-charts) |

## Card options

**The chart's own top-level keys.** Each block has its own page; this table links to it.

- The chart also takes the keys every LCARdS card takes (`height`, `width`, `id`, `tags`, `grid_options`, `data_sources` ...): see [Common card properties](../common). Rules can restyle a chart through its `id` and `tags`: see the [Rules Engine](../../core/rules/).
- In a sections view the chart takes 6 columns and 4 rows unless `grid_options` says otherwise, and can't be made smaller than 4 by 2.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: area
graph_span: 12h
yaxis:
  - id: temperature
    min: -10
    max: 30
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `type` | string | required | `custom:lcards-chart` |
| `sources` | list | - | The series: see [Series and Time](./series#where-the-data-comes-from) and [Series options](./series#series-options) |
| `chart_type` | string | `line` | How the series are drawn: see [Chart types](#chart-types) |
| `graph_span` | string | `24h` | How much time the chart shows: see [Time window](./series#time-window) |
| `span` | object | - | Line the window up with the calendar, or move it back: see [Time window](./series#time-window) |
| `yaxis` | list | one shared axis | Several Y axes: see [Y axes](./series#y-axes) |
| `xaxis_type` | string | `category` for `bar`, else `datetime` | `datetime`, `category` or `numeric` |
| `data_sources` | object | - | LCARdS data sources the series can plot: see [Data Sources](../../core/datasources/) |
| `style` | object | your theme's chart style | Colours, lines, labels and more: see [Styling](./styling) and [Axes and Labels](./labels) |

Older options (`source`, `series_names`, `history_hours`, ...) still work: see [Upgrading](./upgrading).

# Examples

Complete charts that combine the options from the other pages. Copy one, then swap in your own entities.

## Weather panel

**Outdoor temperature as a filled area with humidity on its own axis, frost and warm lines, and a tooltip that reads naturally.** Two days, averaged every 30 minutes.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: area
graph_span: 48h
yaxis:
  - id: temperature
  - id: humidity
    opposite: true
    min: 0
    max: 100
    decimals: 0
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Temperature
    unit: °C
    float_precision: 1
    opacity: 0.35
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 30min
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_humidity
    name: Humidity
    type: line
    yaxis_id: humidity
    stroke_dash: 4
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 30min
style:
  colors:
    series:
      - var(--lcars-orange)
      - var(--lcars-blue)
  thresholds:
    - value: 0
      label: Frost
      color: var(--lcars-blue)
      dash: true
    - value: 20
      label: Warm
      color: var(--lcars-red)
  legend:
    show: true
    position: top
  formatters:
    xaxis_label: ddd HH:mm
    tooltip: "{seriesName}, {x|ddd [at] HH:mm}: {y}"
```

## Energy fortnight

**Daily energy use from long-term statistics, with each column labelled and a line for the daily target.** The window ends at midnight tonight, so today is the last column.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: column
graph_span: 14d
span:
  end: day
sources:
  - entity: sensor.energy_consumption
    name: Energy per day
    unit: kWh
    float_precision: 1
    statistics:
      type: change
      period: day
style:
  colors:
    series:
      - var(--lcars-yellow)
  data_labels:
    show: true
    font_size: 10
  yaxis:
    decimals: 0
  thresholds:
    - value: 5
      label: Target
      color: var(--lcars-green)
  chart_options:
    plotOptions:
      bar:
        borderRadius: 4
```

## Power monitor

**The last six hours of a busy power sensor: the 10-minute average as an area, and the 10-minute peak as a thin line above it.** The toolbar lets you zoom in on a spike.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 6h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Average
    type: area
    opacity: 0.35
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 10min
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Peak
    stroke_width: 1
    curve: stepline
    group_by:
      func: max
      duration: 10min
style:
  legend:
    show: true
  thresholds:
    - value: 2000
      label: High load
      color: var(--lcars-red)
      dash: true
  display:
    toolbar: true
```

## Smoothed temperature

**A living room temperature smoothed by an LCARdS data source, with humidity on a second axis and a warm line.** In these docs the smoothing doesn't run (processors only run on a real dashboard), so the preview plots the raw temperature.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: area
graph_span: 24h
sources:
  - datasource: living_room
    buffer: smoothed
    name: Temperature
    unit: °C
    float_precision: 1
    opacity: 0.35
  - entity: sensor.living_room_humidity
    name: Humidity
    yaxis_id: humidity
    type: line
data_sources:
  living_room:
    entity: sensor.living_room_temperature
    history:
      hours: 24
    processing:
      smoothed:
        type: smooth
        method: exponential
        alpha: 0.2
yaxis:
  - id: temperature
  - id: humidity
    opposite: true
    min: 0
    max: 100
style:
  colors:
    series:
      - var(--lcars-orange)
      - var(--lcars-blue)
  legend:
    show: true
  thresholds:
    - value: 22
      label: Warm
      color: var(--lcars-red)
  animation:
    preset: lcars_standard
```
