<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/chart/labels.html -->

# Axes and Labels

Everything on a chart that reads as text or marks a value: reference lines, the legend, value labels, the axes, formatters, the tooltip and the toolbar. Several Y axes are on [Series and Time](./series#y-axes).

## Reference lines

**`style.thresholds` draws horizontal lines at fixed values, such as a target, a limit or a comfort band, and `style.zero_line` draws one at 0.** A line with a `label` names itself on the right.

- The label is drawn in dark text on a tab of the line's colour.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
style:
  zero_line: true
  thresholds:
    - value: 18
      label: Warm
      color: var(--lcars-red)
    - value: 8
      label: Cold
      color: var(--lcars-blue)
      dash: true
```

::: details More about reference lines
- **The zero line** is a thin dashed line at half opacity, labelled "Zero".
- **Per series:** reference lines belong to the chart, not to a series; with several [Y axes](./series#y-axes) they are measured on the first.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.zero_line` | boolean | `false` | Draw a line at 0 |
| `style.zero_line_color` | colour | `var(--lcars-gray)` | The zero line's colour |
| `style.thresholds` | list | - | Lines at fixed values, each with the keys below |
| `style.thresholds[].value` | number | required | Where the line goes, on the Y axis |
| `style.thresholds[].label` | string | - | Text on the line |
| `style.thresholds[].color` | colour | `var(--lcars-red)` | Line and label colour |
| `style.thresholds[].width` | number | `2` | Line width, px |
| `style.thresholds[].dash` | boolean | `false` | Dashed line |
| `style.thresholds[].opacity` | number | `0.7` | Line opacity, 0 to 1 |

## style.legend

**`style.legend` shows the series names and colours, and sets where they go.** It is off on most charts and on for pie, donut, polar area and gauge charts, because there it names the slices.

- A gauge chart's legend also shows each gauge's value.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
sources:
  - entity: sensor.attic_temperature
    name: Attic
  - entity: sensor.kitchen_temperature
    name: Kitchen
  - entity: sensor.office_temperature
    name: Office
style:
  legend:
    show: true
    position: right
    font_size: 13
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.legend.show` | boolean | `false` (`true` for `pie`, `donut`, `polarArea` and `radialBar`) | Show the legend |
| `style.legend.position` | string | `bottom` (`top` on scatter) | `top`, `bottom`, `left` or `right` |
| `style.legend.horizontalAlign` | string | `center` | `left`, `center` or `right` |
| `style.legend.font_size` | number | font size + 2 (`12` on scatter and polar area) | Legend font size, px (8 to 24) |

The legend's text colours are [`style.colors.legend`](./styling#colours).

## style.data_labels

**`style.data_labels` writes each value on the chart, on its column or point.** It suits a chart with few values, such as a week of daily columns.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: column
graph_span: 7d
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Daily high
    statistics:
      type: max
      period: day
style:
  data_labels:
    show: true
    font_size: 11
  yaxis:
    decimals: 0
```

::: details More about value labels
- **Decimals:** `style.yaxis.decimals` rounds the labels too.
- **Treemaps** show their labels (the series names) unless `show` is `false`.
- **Colours** are [`style.colors.data_labels`](./styling#colours).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.data_labels.show` | boolean | `false` | Show value labels |
| `style.data_labels.offsetY` | number | `0` | Move the labels down (or up, negative), px (-50 to 50) |
| `style.data_labels.font_size` | number | the base font size | Label font size, px (8 to 24) |

## style.xaxis and style.yaxis

**`style.xaxis` and `style.yaxis` show or hide each axis's labels, line and tick marks, and `style.yaxis.decimals` rounds the values.** The X axis shows time by default.

- `style.yaxis.decimals` rounds the Y axis labels, the tooltip and the value labels together. Without it labels show up to two decimal places.
- Set `xaxis_type: category` or `xaxis_type: numeric` at the top level for other kinds of X values. For several Y axes, use [`yaxis`](./series#y-axes); `style.yaxis` styles them all.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 48h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
style:
  xaxis:
    border:
      show: true
    ticks:
      show: true
  yaxis:
    decimals: 1
    border:
      show: true
```

::: details More about axes
- **Time labels:** the X axis picks its own time format to suit the window. Times show in the time zone and clock (12 or 24 hour) set in your Home Assistant profile, the same zone the [time window](./series#time-window) uses; the tooltip time too. Set your own format with [`style.formatters.xaxis_label`](#formatters).
- **Rotating labels** works on category axes only; time axes don't rotate.
- **Colours** are [`style.colors.axis`](./styling#colours).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.xaxis.labels.show` | boolean | `true` | Show the X axis labels |
| `style.xaxis.labels.rotate` | number | `0` | Label rotation, degrees (-90 to 90) |
| `style.xaxis.border.show` | boolean | `false` | Show the X axis line |
| `style.xaxis.ticks.show` | boolean | `false` | Show the X axis tick marks |
| `style.yaxis.labels.show` | boolean | `true` | Show the Y axis labels |
| `style.yaxis.decimals` | number | up to 2 places | Decimal places for the labels, the tooltip and value labels (0 to 10) |
| `style.yaxis.border.show` | boolean | `false` | Show the Y axis line |
| `style.yaxis.ticks.show` | boolean | `false` | Show the Y axis tick marks |

## Formatters

**`style.formatters` sets the text of the axis labels and the tooltip with short format strings.** They use a small chart-only syntax; they are not LCARdS templates.

- An X axis format without `{` is a date format: `HH:mm`, `MMM DD`, `ddd HH:mm`. A Y axis format puts the value into text: `{value}°C`.
- A tooltip format replaces the whole tooltip: `{seriesName}: {y}`, or `{x|MMM DD HH:mm}: {y}°C` to format the time.
- Units and decimal places usually need no formatter: set `unit` and `float_precision` on the [series](./series#units-and-decimals).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
style:
  formatters:
    xaxis_label: ddd HH:mm
    yaxis_label: "{value}°"
    tooltip: "{x|ddd [at] HH:mm}: {y}°C"
```

::: details More about formatters
- **Date tokens:** `YYYY`, `YY`, `MMMM` (October), `MMM` (Oct), `MM`, `M`, `dddd` (Tuesday), `ddd` (Tue), `DD`, `D`, `HH`, `H`, `hh`, `h`, `mm`, `m`, `ss`, `s`, `A` (PM), `a` (pm). Month and day names follow your Home Assistant language. Put literal text in square brackets: `[at] HH:mm`.
- **Time zone:** date formats show times in the time zone set in your Home Assistant profile, like the axis.
- **Values:** `{value}` in axis labels; `{y}`, `{x}`, `{x|format}` and `{seriesName}` in tooltips. `{value}` and `{y}` show up to one decimal place, and a plain `{x}` reads like `Oct 07 14:30`.
- **Quote** a format that starts with `{`, or YAML reads it as a map.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.formatters.xaxis_label` | string | a time format to suit the window | X axis labels: a date format, or text with `{value}` |
| `style.formatters.yaxis_label` | string | - | Y axis labels: text with `{value}`. Applies to every axis in [`yaxis`](./series#y-axes) |
| `style.formatters.tooltip` | string | the standard tooltip | The tooltip's whole text, with `{x}`, `{x\|format}`, `{y}` and `{seriesName}` |

## style.display

**`style.display` turns the hover tooltip and the ApexCharts toolbar (zoom, pan, download) on or off.** The toolbar is off, because most dashboards don't need it.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 6h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Power
style:
  display:
    toolbar: true
    tooltip:
      theme: light
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.display.toolbar` | boolean | `false` | Show the zoom, pan and download toolbar |
| `style.display.tooltip.show` | boolean | `true` | Show the tooltip on hover |
| `style.display.tooltip.theme` | string | `dark` | `dark` or `light` |

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/chart/playground.html -->

# Chart Playground

Edit the YAML and the chart redraws as you type. Pick a starting point from the list, or paste a chart from your own dashboard.

**You don't need to know the YAML to start:**

- **Quick settings** above the editor change the most common options for you.
- **Type in the editor** and it suggests the options that fit where your cursor is, with a short description. Press **Ctrl+Space** to see suggestions anywhere, and hover over a key to read what it does.
- **Options here** (under the editor) lists everything you can add at the cursor. **Insert** adds it at the right indent, and **Docs** opens its section in a new tab.

<ClientOnly>

</ClientOnly>

## How the preview works

The preview uses the chart card's own code: the same option handling, grouping, time window, theme colours and validation as on your dashboard. The docs site has no Home Assistant, so:

- **Entities get generated sample data.** Names containing `temperature`, `humidity`, `power`, `energy` or `battery` get a realistic signal, and `light.*`/`switch.*`/`binary_sensor.*` entities switch on and off. Any other entity gets a generic wave. Helpers (`input_number.*`, `input_boolean.*`, `input_select.*`) hold their value until something changes it, as at home.
- **Long-term statistics** are computed from the same sample signal.
- **Data source series** plot their entity's sample signal. Processors (smoothing, rates, ...) only run on a real dashboard.
- **`theme:` tokens** resolve on a real dashboard; the preview shows their fallback colours.

Messages under the chart show schema warnings, and explain how an [older format](./upgrading) would be converted.

When it looks right, **Copy YAML** and paste it into your card's YAML editor, then swap in your own entities.

# Series and Time

What each series plots and where its data comes from, how much time the chart shows, how to combine points into time buckets, and how to give series their own Y axes. Chart types and mixing them are on [Chart Types](./types).

## Where the data comes from

**Each entry under `sources` is one series (one line, area or set of columns), and it gets its data from one of three places.** Start with entity history; the table below helps you pick.

- **Entity history** is the simplest and shows exactly what Home Assistant recorded.
- **Long-term statistics** suit charts that span more than a few days, or sensors that change so often that history gets slow. They also last beyond the recorder's history limit.
- **An LCARdS data source** plots a processed value (a smoothed line, a rate of change, a converted unit), or shares one live value between several cards. Data sources keep a limited number of recent points (up to 1,000), so they suit short windows.

| | Entity history | Long-term statistics | LCARdS data source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Write it as** | `entity: sensor.x` | `entity: sensor.x` plus `statistics:` | `datasource: name` |
| **What it is** | Every state change Home Assistant recorded | Home Assistant's own 5-minute and hourly summaries (mean, min, max, sum) | A live buffer LCARdS keeps in your browser, with optional processing |
| **Stored by** | Home Assistant's recorder database | Home Assistant's recorder database | Your browser, while the dashboard is open |
| **How far back** | As long as the recorder keeps history (10 days by default) | Hourly summaries are kept indefinitely | What was preloaded (6 hours by default, up to 7 days) plus what arrived since the page loaded |
| **Live updates** | Yes | Refreshed every 5 minutes (hourly for daily and longer periods) | Yes |
| **Works for** | Any entity with numeric (or on/off) values | Sensors with a `state_class` (most energy, power and climate sensors) | Any entity |
| **Best for** | Hours to days of detail | Weeks, months, years | Processed values: smoothing, rates, unit conversion, statistics |

## Entity history

**`entity` plots what Home Assistant recorded for that entity over the time window, and keeps the line live as new states arrive.** Add `attribute` to plot one of its attributes instead of its state.

- Charts plot numbers. The states `on`/`off`, `open`/`closed`, `true`/`false` and `active`/`inactive` plot as 1 and 0; `curve: stepline` draws them as steps.
- Other text states (`heat`, `home`, `docked` ...) don't plot. Pick a numeric attribute instead, or use a [data source](#data-sources) with `enum_mapping` to turn each state into a number. Chart Studio warns you when a series won't plot.

```yaml live
# an attribute instead of the state
type: custom:lcards-chart
sources:
  - entity: climate.living_room
    attribute: current_temperature
    name: Thermostat reading
```

```yaml live
# an on/off entity drawn as steps
type: custom:lcards-chart
sources:
  - entity: light.living_room
    name: Living room light
    curve: stepline
    type: area
    opacity: 0.4
```

::: details More about entity history
- **Edges of the window:** the last value before the window is drawn from its left edge, and the latest value is carried on to now, so a value that hasn't changed in the window still draws a line (as Home Assistant's history graph does).
- **Units:** the series takes the entity's `unit_of_measurement`, except when it plots an attribute; set `unit` on the series then.
- **Reconnects:** when the connection to Home Assistant drops and comes back, the chart loads the window again.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `entity` | string | required | The entity to plot |
| `attribute` | string | the state | Plot this attribute instead of the state |

## Long-term statistics

**`statistics` plots Home Assistant's own summaries of a sensor instead of every state change: the average, low or high of each period, or how much a meter went up.** It works for sensors with a `state_class`, and suits charts of weeks, months or years.

- `type` picks which summary to plot. Three series of the same sensor can show each day's low, average and high.
- The chart fetches the statistics again every 5 minutes for `5minute` and `hour` periods, and every hour for `day`, `week` and `month`.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 14d
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Low
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
    stroke_dash: 4
    statistics:
      type: min
      period: day
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Average
    color: var(--lcars-orange)
    stroke_width: 3
    statistics:
      type: mean
      period: day
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: High
    color: var(--lcars-red)
    stroke_dash: 4
    statistics:
      type: max
      period: day
style:
  legend:
    show: true
```

| `type` | Each period shows | Typical sensors |
|--------|-------------------|-----------------|
| `mean`, `min`, `max` | The average, lowest or highest value | Temperature, humidity, power (`state_class: measurement`) |
| `change` | How much a meter increased | Energy, water, gas (`total` / `total_increasing`) |
| `sum`, `state` | The meter's running total, or its reading at the end of the period | Same |

::: details More about statistics
- **Grouping or statistics:** for long spans of a sensor with a `state_class`, statistics are usually better: Home Assistant has already done the summarising. [Grouping](#grouping) works on any series, including entity history and data sources.
- **Range areas:** on a `rangeArea` chart, a statistics series without `group_by` plots each period's minimum to maximum as a band, whatever its `type`: see [Range charts](./types#range-charts).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `statistics.type` | string | `mean` | `mean`, `min`, `max`, `sum`, `state` or `change` |
| `statistics.period` | string | `hour` | `5minute`, `hour`, `day`, `week` or `month` |

## Data sources

**`datasource` plots an LCARdS data source: a live buffer in your browser that can smooth, convert or otherwise process an entity's values.** Use it to plot a processed value, or to share one value between several cards.

- `buffer` picks one of the data source's processors to plot instead of its raw values.
- Data sources are created when the dashboard loads, preload some history, then follow live changes. See [Data Sources](../../core/datasources/) for the keys and processors.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
sources:
  - datasource: living_room
    buffer: smoothed
    name: Smoothed
data_sources:
  living_room:
    entity: sensor.living_room_temperature
    processing:
      smoothed:
        type: smooth
        method: exponential
        alpha: 0.3
```

::: details More about data source series
- **In these docs:** the previews plot the data source's entity; processors only run on a real dashboard.
- **Sources from other cards:** a series can name a data source another card defines. If it doesn't exist yet, the chart tries again after 2 seconds.
- **A missing buffer:** when the data source has no processor called `buffer`, the series plots the raw values and logs a warning.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `datasource` | string | required | The name of a data source, in this card's `data_sources` or defined by another card |
| `buffer` | string | the raw values | The processor whose values to plot |

## Series options

**Every series, whatever its data, takes the same keys for its name, colour, line, units and axis.** Set them on the series when one series should look different; `style` sets them for the whole chart.

- `name` is shown in the legend and the tooltip. Without it the series takes the entity's friendly name.
- `type` draws this series as another chart type than the chart's, for a chart of columns and lines: see [Mixing chart types](./types#mixing-chart-types).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Power
    color: var(--lcars-orange)
    stroke_width: 3
  - entity: sensor.solar_power
    name: Solar
    type: area
    opacity: 0.3
    curve: straight
style:
  legend:
    show: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `name` | string | the entity's friendly name | Name in the legend and tooltip. A data source series is named after the data source (and its buffer) |
| `type` | string | `chart_type` | `line`, `area`, `column` or `scatter`: draw this series differently from the chart |
| `yaxis_id` | string | the first axis | The `id` of the [Y axis](#y-axes) this series uses |
| `group_by` | object | - | Combine points into time buckets: see [Grouping](#grouping) |
| [Line styles](#line-styles) | | | `color`, `curve`, `stroke_width`, `stroke_dash` and `opacity` |
| [Units and decimals](#units-and-decimals) | | | `unit` and `float_precision` |

### Line styles

**`curve`, `stroke_width`, `stroke_dash`, `color` and `opacity` style one series' line or fill.** They win over the chart-wide [`style.stroke`](./styling#style-stroke), [`style.fill`](./styling#style-fill) and [`style.colors.series`](./styling#colours) for that series.

```yaml live
# each series averaged over 30 minutes, so the lines are easy to tell apart
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 12h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.attic_temperature
    name: smooth
    curve: smooth
    group_by:
      duration: 30min
  - entity: sensor.kitchen_temperature
    name: straight, dashed
    curve: straight
    stroke_dash: 6
    group_by:
      duration: 30min
  - entity: sensor.office_temperature
    name: stepline, thick
    curve: stepline
    stroke_width: 4
    group_by:
      duration: 30min
style:
  legend:
    show: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `color` | colour | the next colour in `style.colors.series` | Series colour: any colour, `var(--lcars-...)` or `theme:` token |
| `curve` | string | `style.stroke.curve` | `smooth`, `straight`, `stepline` or `monotoneCubic` |
| `stroke_width` | number | `style.stroke.width` | Line width, px (0 to 20) |
| `stroke_dash` | number | `style.stroke.dash_array` | Dash length, px; `0` is a solid line (0 to 20) |
| `opacity` | number | `style.fill.opacity` | Fill opacity for areas and columns, 0 to 1 |

### Units and decimals

**`unit` and `float_precision` set how a series' values read in the tooltip (hover the chart).** Without them the entity's own unit is used, and values show up to two decimal places.

- An axis label shows the unit too, when every series on that axis has the same unit.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Power
    unit: watts
    float_precision: 0
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
    float_precision: 2
    yaxis_id: temperature
yaxis:
  - id: power
  - id: temperature
    opposite: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `unit` | string | the entity's unit | Unit in tooltips and axis labels. Not taken from the entity when the series plots an attribute |
| `float_precision` | number | up to 2 places | Decimal places in the tooltip (0 to 6). Without it, `style.yaxis.decimals` applies when set |

## Time window

**`graph_span` sets how much time the chart shows, and `span` lines that window up with the calendar or moves it back in time.** Without `span` the window ends now and moves along as time passes.

- `span.start: day` starts the window at midnight today. With a `24h` span it shows today so far: the window runs to midnight, so the line stops at now.
- `span.offset` moves the window, so `start: day` with `offset: -1d` shows all of yesterday.
- The calendar follows your Home Assistant profile: days start at midnight in the time zone it uses (the server's or your device's), and weeks start on its first weekday.

```yaml live
# all of yesterday
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 24h
span:
  start: day
  offset: -1d
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Yesterday
```

```yaml live
# this week so far, from daily statistics
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: column
graph_span: 7d
span:
  start: week
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Daily high
    statistics:
      type: max
      period: day
```

::: details More about the time window
- **Durations:** a number and a unit: `s`, `min` (or `m`), `h`, `d`, `w`, `mo` or `y`. Spelled out (`hour`, `day`, `week`, `month`, `year`) and plurals (`2days`) work too, and so do decimals (`1.5h`). A month is 30 days and a year 365 days.
- **Time zone:** days, weeks, months and years line up in the time zone set in your Home Assistant profile (Settings > Profile > Time zone): the server's zone (Settings > System > General) or your device's. A browser in another zone than Home Assistant still shows the same "today", and the axis labels and tooltip times use the same zone.
- **Weeks** start on the first weekday set in your profile: "Language" takes it from your language (Sunday for `en`, Monday for `de` or `en-GB`), or pick a day. Without a profile setting, weeks start on Monday.
- **Hours** line up with the hour in that zone too, so in a zone such as India's (UTC+5:30) `start: hour` begins at half past the UTC hour.
- **Rolling over:** an aligned window (`start` or `end`) is checked every minute; when it rolls over (at midnight for `day`), the chart loads the new window.
- **Both start and end:** when both are set, `start` is used.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `graph_span` | string | `24h` | How much time the chart shows, such as `30min`, `6h`, `2d`, `1w`, `1mo`, `1y` |
| `span.start` | string | - | Start the window at the beginning of the current `minute`, `hour`, `day`, `week`, `month` or `year`; it lasts `graph_span` |
| `span.end` | string | - | End the window at the end of the current unit (same units); it starts `graph_span` earlier |
| `span.offset` | string | - | Move the window, with a sign: `-1d` (a day earlier) or `+2h` |

## Grouping

**`group_by` combines the points in each time bucket into one value.** Use it to smooth out a busy sensor, to show hourly averages over a week, or to turn a meter's readings into totals per hour.

- `func` decides how each bucket is combined; the table below lists them. `minmax`, `box` and `ohlc` build the data the [range charts](./types#range-charts) need.
- `delta` is how much a meter went up within each bucket, so a meter that only counts up gives energy per hour.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 12h
sources:
  # the raw readings
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Raw
    stroke_width: 1
    color: var(--lcars-gray)
  # the same sensor, averaged over 30 minutes
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: 30 min average
    stroke_width: 3
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 30min
style:
  legend:
    show: true
```

```yaml live
# energy per hour from a meter that only counts up
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: column
graph_span: 24h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.energy_consumption
    name: kWh per hour
    group_by:
      func: delta
      duration: 1h
      fill: zero
```

| `func` | Each bucket shows |
|--------|-------------------|
| `avg` | The average |
| `min`, `max`, `median` | The lowest, highest or middle value |
| `sum` | The total |
| `first`, `last` | The first or last reading |
| `delta` | How much the value changed within the bucket |
| `diff` | How much the value changed since the previous bucket (useful for meters) |
| `minmax` | The low and high value, for [range areas](./types#range-charts) |
| `box` | Min, quartiles, median and max, for [box plots](./types#range-charts) |
| `ohlc` | Open, high, low and close, for [candlesticks](./types#range-charts) |

::: details More about grouping
- **Buckets** start at the window's start, one every `duration`, and stop at now; each value is drawn at the start of its bucket.
- **Empty buckets with `fill: last`:** `delta`, `diff` and `sum` give `0` (nothing changed); the other functions repeat the last reading.
- **`diff` in the first bucket** compares with the last reading before the window, and is `0` when there is none.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `group_by.duration` | string | required | Bucket length, such as `10min`, `1h` or `1d` |
| `group_by.func` | string | `avg` | How each bucket is combined: see the table above |
| `group_by.fill` | string | `last` | Buckets with no readings: `last` (repeat the last value), `null` (leave a gap) or `zero` |

## Y axes

**`yaxis` gives series their own Y axes, for series with very different ranges such as temperature and humidity.** Without it all series share one axis that scales itself.

- Each series picks an axis by its `id` with `yaxis_id`. Series without one use the first axis.
- `min` and `max` fix the range, so the scale stays steady as values change; leave them out to scale automatically.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
yaxis:
  - id: temperature
  # drawn on the right, pinned to 0 to 100
  - id: humidity
    opposite: true
    min: 0
    max: 100
    decimals: 0
sources:
  - entity: sensor.living_room_temperature
    name: Temperature
  - entity: sensor.living_room_humidity
    name: Humidity
    yaxis_id: humidity
```

::: details More about Y axes
- **Labels:** an axis shows the series' unit when every series on it has the same unit. Without `decimals` it uses [`style.yaxis.decimals`](./labels#style-xaxis-and-style-yaxis), or up to two decimal places.
- **Styling** (label visibility, axis line, ticks) is in [`style.yaxis`](./labels#style-xaxis-and-style-yaxis), and applies to every axis.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `yaxis[].id` | string | required | The name series use in `yaxis_id` |
| `yaxis[].show` | boolean | `true` | Show the axis |
| `yaxis[].opposite` | boolean | `false` | Draw it on the right |
| `yaxis[].min` | number | automatic | Fixed lowest value |
| `yaxis[].max` | number | automatic | Fixed highest value |
| `yaxis[].decimals` | number | up to 2 places | Decimal places in the labels (0 to 6) |
| `yaxis_id` | string | the first axis | On a series: the axis it uses |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/chart/styling.html -->

# Styling

Colours, lines, fills, markers, the grid, fonts and animation for the whole chart. Charts use your theme's colours and fonts without any `style` at all, so everything on this page is optional. The legend, axes, labels and reference lines are on [Axes and Labels](./labels).

For one series' colour and line, the [series options](./series#line-styles) (`color`, `stroke_width`, `curve` ...) are usually simpler than the lists below. Colours accept every format in [Colours](../../core/colours): `var(--lcars-*)`, `theme:` tokens, computed colours like `alpha()`, hex and rgba.

## Colours

**`style.colors` sets the colours of everything on the chart: the series, lines and fills, the background, the text, the grid, the axes and the legend.** The lists (`series`, `stroke`, `fill` ...) give one colour per series, in order.

- Without `style.colors` the chart uses your theme's chart colours: LCARS orange, blue, yellow and green for the series, grey for the grid.
- A series' own `color` wins over `style.colors.series` for that series.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: area
sources:
  - entity: sensor.attic_temperature
    name: Attic
  - entity: sensor.office_temperature
    name: Office
style:
  colors:
    series:
      - var(--lcars-yellow)
      - var(--lcars-violet)
    grid: var(--lcars-gray)
  fill:
    type: gradient
    gradient:
      opacityFrom: 0.5
      opacityTo: 0.05
  legend:
    show: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.colors.series` | list | your theme's chart colours | Series colours, used in order |
| `style.colors.stroke` | list | the series colours (black on polar area, the axis colour on box plots) | Line and outline colours |
| `style.colors.fill` | list | the series colours | Area and column fill colours |
| `style.colors.background` | colour | `transparent` | Chart background |
| `style.colors.foreground` | colour | `var(--lcars-text-light)` | Default text and label colour |
| `style.colors.grid` | colour | your theme's grid colour | Grid line colour |
| `style.colors.marker.fill` | list | the series colours | Point fill colours |
| `style.colors.marker.stroke` | list | the foreground colour | Point outline colours |
| `style.colors.axis.x` | colour | your theme's axis colour | X axis label colour |
| `style.colors.axis.y` | colour | your theme's axis colour | Y axis label colour |
| `style.colors.axis.border` | colour | the grid colour | Axis line colour |
| `style.colors.axis.ticks` | colour | the grid colour | Tick mark colour |
| `style.colors.legend.default` | colour | the foreground colour | Legend text colour |
| `style.colors.legend.items` | list | - | Legend text colour for each series, in order |
| `style.colors.data_labels` | list | the foreground colour | Value label colours |

## style.stroke

**`style.stroke` sets how every line is drawn: its width, its curve and its dashes.** It also draws the outline of columns and slices.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 12h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
style:
  stroke:
    width: 3
    dash_array: 8
    curve: straight
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.stroke.width` | number | `2` | Line width, px (0 to 10) |
| `style.stroke.curve` | string | `smooth` | `smooth`, `straight`, `stepline` or `monotoneCubic` |
| `style.stroke.dash_array` | number | `0` | Dash length, px; `0` is solid (0 to 20) |

## style.fill

**`style.fill` sets how areas and columns are filled: solid, a gradient, or a pattern.** A gradient that fades out towards the bottom is the classic look for an area chart.

- A gradient's `opacityFrom` and `opacityTo` fade the fill from the line down to the axis.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: area
graph_span: 12h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
style:
  fill:
    type: gradient
    gradient:
      shade: dark
      type: vertical
      opacityFrom: 0.7
      opacityTo: 0.05
```

::: details More about fills
- **Pattern and image:** `pattern` draws ApexCharts' default stripes. `image` needs the image in [`style.chart_options`](#raw-apexcharts-options) (`fill.image.src`).
- **Per series:** a series' own `opacity` wins over `style.fill.opacity` for that series.
- **Chart types with their own fill:** range areas use opacity `0.35` and polar area charts `0.8` unless `style.fill.opacity` is set.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.fill.type` | string | `solid` | `solid`, `gradient`, `pattern` or `image` |
| `style.fill.opacity` | number | `0.7` | Fill opacity, 0 to 1 |
| `style.fill.gradient.shade` | string | - | `light` or `dark` |
| `style.fill.gradient.type` | string | - | `horizontal`, `vertical`, `diagonal1` or `diagonal2` |
| `style.fill.gradient.shadeIntensity` | number | - | How strong the shading is, 0 to 1 |
| `style.fill.gradient.opacityFrom` | number | - | Opacity where the gradient starts, 0 to 1 |
| `style.fill.gradient.opacityTo` | number | - | Opacity where the gradient ends, 0 to 1 |

## style.markers

**`style.markers` draws a point on each value.** Points are off on line and area charts; they help on a grouped series with few values.

- Points take the series colours unless [`style.colors.marker`](#colours) says otherwise.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 12h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 1h
style:
  markers:
    size: 6
    shape: diamond
    stroke:
      width: 1
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.markers.size` | number | `0` (`6` on scatter) | Point size, px (0 to 20); `0` hides them |
| `style.markers.shape` | string | `circle` | `circle`, `square`, `rect`, `diamond`, `triangle`, `star`, `cross`, `plus` or `line` |
| `style.markers.stroke.width` | number | `2` (`0` on scatter) | Point outline width, px (0 to 10) |

## style.grid

**`style.grid` draws the dashed lines behind the chart, and can shade alternate rows or columns.** Its colour is [`style.colors.grid`](#colours).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: column
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Power
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 2h
style:
  grid:
    stroke_dash_array: 0
    row_colors:
      - var(--lcars-gray)
      - transparent
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.grid.show` | boolean | `true` | Show the grid lines |
| `style.grid.stroke_dash_array` | number | `4` | Dash length, px; `0` is solid (0 to 20) |
| `style.grid.row_colors` | list | - | Background colours for alternate rows, repeated in turn |
| `style.grid.column_colors` | list | - | Background colours for alternate columns, repeated in turn |

## style.typography

**`style.typography` sets the font and base size of all the chart's text.** Without it the chart uses your theme's LCARS font at 12 px.

- The legend is 2 px larger than the base size, and reference line labels 2 px smaller.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
style:
  typography:
    font_size: 16
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.typography.font_family` | string | your theme's font | Font for all chart text |
| `style.typography.font_size` | number | `12` | Base font size, px (8 to 24) |

## style.theme

**`style.theme` passes ApexCharts' own theme options: light or dark mode, and a monochrome palette made from shades of one colour.** Explicit colours take priority.

- Monochrome suits a donut or pie of several parts that belong together.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: donut
sources:
  - entity: sensor.kitchen_power
    name: Kitchen
  - entity: sensor.office_power
    name: Office
  - entity: sensor.garage_power
    name: Garage
  - entity: sensor.laundry_power
    name: Laundry
style:
  theme:
    monochrome:
      enabled: true
      color: var(--lcars-orange)
      shade_to: dark
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.theme.mode` | string | `dark` | `dark` or `light` |
| `style.theme.monochrome.enabled` | boolean | `false` | Colour the series in shades of one colour |
| `style.theme.monochrome.color` | colour | the first series colour | The base colour |
| `style.theme.monochrome.shade_to` | string | `dark` | `dark` or `light` |
| `style.theme.monochrome.shade_intensity` | number | `0.65` | How far the shades spread, 0 to 1 |

## Animation

**`style.animation.preset` picks how the chart animates in when it first draws, and how it moves when new values arrive.** Without a preset charts animate like `lcars_standard`.

The chart below uses `lcars_dramatic`; reload the page to see it again.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: column
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Power
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 1h
style:
  animation:
    preset: lcars_dramatic
```

| Preset | Entrance | Updates |
|--------|----------|---------|
| `lcars_standard` | Smooth, 800 ms, series one after another | 350 ms |
| `lcars_dramatic` | Slower and more theatrical, 1200 ms | 500 ms |
| `lcars_minimal` | Quick and subtle, 400 ms, all at once | 200 ms |
| `lcars_realtime` | None | 100 ms, for live data |
| `lcars_alert` | Fast, 600 ms, for alert displays | 250 ms |
| `none` | None | None |

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.animation.preset` | string | - | One of the presets above |

## Raw ApexCharts options

**`style.chart_options` passes options straight to ApexCharts, for anything LCARdS doesn't cover.** It overrides everything else on these pages: see the [ApexCharts options reference](https://apexcharts.com/docs/options/).

- Only plain values work here; ApexCharts options that expect JavaScript functions can't be written in YAML.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: column
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Power
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 2h
style:
  chart_options:
    plotOptions:
      bar:
        borderRadius: 6
        columnWidth: 60%
```

::: details More about raw options
- **Chart type:** `chart.type` here can't switch the chart to a type LCARdS doesn't support; use `chart_type`.
- **Series data** always comes from `sources`; a `series` list here is replaced.
- **Colours** here can be `var(--lcars-*)` names and `theme:` tokens too: they are resolved before ApexCharts sees them.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.chart_options` | object | - | ApexCharts options, deep-merged over everything LCARdS sets |

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/chart/types.html -->

# Chart Types

Every chart type with an example, the options some of them have, and how to mix types in one chart. `chart_type` sets the type for the whole chart; the full list is on the [Overview](./#chart-types).

## Time charts

**Line, area, column, bar, scatter and heatmap charts plot each series over the time window.** Use them for history: how a value moved over hours, days or weeks.

- Columns and heatmaps read best with [grouping](./series#grouping), one column or cell per bucket.
- A horizontal `bar` chart draws one bar per point, labelled with its time on the vertical axis, and puts the values along the bottom; group it so there are only a few bars.

```yaml live
# columns of hourly averages
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: column
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Power
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 1h
```

```yaml live
# a heatmap of several sensors, one row each
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: heatmap
sources:
  - entity: sensor.kitchen_temperature
    name: Kitchen
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 2h
  - entity: sensor.bedroom_temperature
    name: Bedroom
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 2h
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 2h
```

```yaml live
# individual readings as points
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: scatter
graph_span: 6h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Power readings
```

::: details More about time charts
- **Scatter points** are 6 px unless `style.markers.size` says otherwise, and the legend sits at the top unless `style.legend.position` says otherwise.
- **The X axis** shows time. For other kinds of X values set `xaxis_type: category` or `numeric`.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `chart_type` | string | `line` | `line`, `area`, `column`, `bar`, `scatter` or `heatmap` for a time chart |
| `xaxis_type` | string | `category` for `bar`, else `datetime` | `datetime`, `category` or `numeric` |

## Current-value charts

**Gauges (`radialBar`), `pie`, `donut`, `polarArea`, `radar` and `treemap` show the latest value of each series, not its history.** Use them for "right now": battery levels, where the power is going, rooms compared.

- Each series becomes one gauge, slice, spoke or rectangle, named after the series. Pie, donut, polar area and gauge charts show their legend unless `style.legend.show` is `false`, because it names the slices.
- Several series read better than one: a pie of one value is a full circle.

```yaml live
# a donut of current values
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: donut
sources:
  - entity: sensor.kitchen_power
    name: Kitchen
  - entity: sensor.office_power
    name: Office
  - entity: sensor.garage_power
    name: Garage
```

```yaml live
# room temperatures compared on a radar
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: radar
sources:
  - entity: sensor.kitchen_temperature
    name: Kitchen
  - entity: sensor.bedroom_temperature
    name: Bedroom
  - entity: sensor.office_temperature
    name: Office
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
  - entity: sensor.garage_temperature
    name: Garage
```

```yaml live
# where the power is going right now, as a treemap
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: treemap
sources:
  - entity: sensor.kitchen_power
    name: Kitchen
  - entity: sensor.office_power
    name: Office
  - entity: sensor.garage_power
    name: Garage
  - entity: sensor.laundry_power
    name: Laundry
```

```yaml live
# the same four values as polar areas
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: polarArea
sources:
  - entity: sensor.kitchen_power
    name: Kitchen
  - entity: sensor.office_power
    name: Office
  - entity: sensor.garage_power
    name: Garage
  - entity: sensor.laundry_power
    name: Laundry
```

::: details More about current-value charts
- **Radar:** the web is sized to fill the card (with room for the axis names) and centred, so a three-axis triangle doesn't leave the bottom empty. There is no line-chart grid behind it. To place it yourself, set `plotOptions.radar.size` (radius in px) and `offsetY` in [`style.chart_options`](./styling#raw-apexcharts-options).
- **Polar area:** the ring values are hidden, because they sit on the vertical spoke. `style.yaxis.labels.show: true` brings them back.
- **Treemap:** each rectangle carries its series name.
- **Resizing:** these layouts follow the card when it changes size; raw options still override them.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `chart_type` | string | `line` | `radialBar`, `pie`, `donut`, `polarArea`, `radar` or `treemap` for a current-value chart |
| `style.legend.show` | boolean | on for `pie`, `donut`, `polarArea` and `radialBar` | Show the legend: see [style.legend](./labels#style-legend) |

## Gauges

**A `radialBar` chart draws one gauge per series, and a few `style` keys shape the arc and the numbers.** Values from 0 to 100 fill the arc, so it suits percentages such as batteries and humidity.

- The legend shows each gauge's value, because several gauges only show their values on hover.
- A half-circle gauge (start and end angles within -90 to 90, the default) fills the card's height instead of reserving room for the missing lower half.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: radialBar
sources:
  - entity: sensor.phone_battery
    name: Phone
  - entity: sensor.tablet_battery
    name: Tablet
style:
  gauge_start_angle: -135
  gauge_end_angle: 135
  value_format: percent
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.gauge_start_angle` | number | `-90` | Where the arc starts, degrees (-360 to 360; `0` is the top) |
| `style.gauge_end_angle` | number | `90` | Where the arc ends, degrees |
| `style.gauge_total` | boolean | `false` | Show the sum of all gauges in the centre |
| `style.value_format` | string | - | `percent` adds a % sign to the values and rounds them |

## Range charts

**`rangeArea`, `boxPlot` and `candlestick` charts draw several values per point: a low and a high, the spread, or open, high, low and close.** `group_by` builds them from any series, one per time bucket.

- Set the series' `group_by.func` to what the chart needs (table below). Without it, the card shows a message saying which `func` to use.
- A `rangeArea` can also come straight from [long-term statistics](./series#long-term-statistics), with no grouping: the band runs from each period's minimum to maximum.

```yaml live
# open, high, low and close every 3 hours
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: candlestick
graph_span: 2d
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
    group_by:
      func: ohlc
      duration: 3h
```

```yaml live
# the spread of a busy sensor each day
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: boxPlot
graph_span: 7d
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Power spread per day
    group_by:
      func: box
      duration: 1d
```

```yaml live
# a daily low-to-high band from statistics
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: rangeArea
graph_span: 14d
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Daily range
    statistics:
      type: mean
      period: day
```

| Chart type | Set the series' `group_by.func` to |
|------------|-----------------------------------|
| `rangeArea` | `minmax`. Or use long-term statistics without `group_by` |
| `boxPlot` | `box` |
| `candlestick` | `ohlc` |
| `rangeBar` | Nothing yet: the card can't build timeline data, and shows a message instead |

::: details More about range charts
- **Candlestick colours:** one series draws green candles for up and red for down. Two or more series draw each series' candles in its own colour (full for up, darker for down), so they match the legend and stay apart. Set `plotOptions.candlestick.colors.upward` and `downward` in [`style.chart_options`](./styling#raw-apexcharts-options) to choose.
- **Range areas** draw straight edges and a light fill (opacity `0.35`) unless `style.stroke.curve` or `style.fill.opacity` say otherwise.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `group_by.func` | string | `avg` | On each series: `minmax`, `box` or `ohlc` for these charts. See [Grouping](./series#grouping) |
| `style.group_rows` | boolean | `true` | `rangeBar`: put bars with the same label on one row |
| `style.show_labels` | boolean | `true` | `rangeBar`: show labels on the bars |
| `style.color` | colour | the theme's accent colour | `boxPlot`: colour of the boxes |

## Mixing chart types

**A series' `type` overrides the chart type, so one chart can show columns and lines together.** Give the line its own [Y axis](./series#y-axes) when the two have different units.

- In a mixed chart, columns are sized by the closest pair of points in any series. If the line has a reading every few minutes, the columns become thin lines: group the line to the same bucket length as the columns (here `1h`).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: line
sources:
  - entity: sensor.energy_consumption
    name: Energy per hour
    type: column
    unit: kWh
    group_by:
      func: delta
      duration: 1h
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
    yaxis_id: temperature
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 1h
yaxis:
  - id: energy
  - id: temperature
    opposite: true
```

::: details More about mixed charts
- **Scatter series** in a mixed chart get 6 px points unless `style.markers.size` is set.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `type` | string | `chart_type` | On a series: `line`, `area`, `column` or `scatter` |

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/chart/upgrading.html -->

# Upgrading

How older chart configs keep working and get converted, and how to move a chart over from apexcharts-card.

## Older chart configs

**Earlier versions of the chart card used a different layout for series (`source`, `series_names`, numbered `series_1` data sources, and so on), and those charts keep working as they are.** You don't need to change anything.

- **On your dashboard** an older chart is read in the old layout and drawn exactly as before. Nothing is saved or changed.
- **When you open it in the card editor**, the editor converts it to the current layout and shows a notice saying so; the YAML tab shows the new layout. Press **Save** to keep the converted version, or **Cancel** to leave your config exactly as it was.
- **If you type the old layout by hand** in the YAML editor, it still works. The editor shows a warning naming the current option to use, and doesn't rewrite your text while you type.
- To see a conversion explained step by step, pick **Older format (converted)** in the [Playground](./playground).

```yaml no-validate
# Before: a chart made with the old Chart Studio
type: custom:lcards-chart
sources: [series_1]
series_names: [Living room]
data_sources:
  series_1:
    entity: sensor.living_room_temperature
    attribute: state
    history:
      preload: true
      hours: 48
```

```yaml live
# After
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 48h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.living_room_temperature
    name: Living room
```

### What changes

**Each older key maps to a current one; the editor makes these changes for you.**

- LCARdS data sources you named yourself (anything other than the old editor's `series_1`, `series_2`, ...) are never moved or removed, because other cards may use them too.

| Older layout | Current layout |
|--------------|----------------|
| `source: sensor.x` with `attribute: a` | `sources: [{ entity: sensor.x, attribute: a }]` |
| `data_source: x` (one name or a list) | the same as `source` / `sources` |
| `sources: [sensor.x, sensor.y]` | `sources: [{ entity: sensor.x }, { entity: sensor.y }]` |
| `sources: [my_source]` (an LCARdS data source) | `sources: [{ datasource: my_source }]` |
| `series_1`, `series_2`, ... entries the old editor added to `data_sources` | moved into the series as `{ entity: ..., name: ... }` |
| `{ datasource: x, buffer: transformation, key: smooth }` | `{ datasource: x, buffer: smooth }` |
| `series_names: [A, B]` | `name:` on each series |
| `history_hours: 12` (or `history.hours` on a `series_N`) | `graph_span: 12h` |
| `show_legend: true` | `style.legend.show: true` |
| `yaxis` on a series | removed: it never had an effect. Use [`yaxis_id`](./series#y-axes) |
| `max_points` | removed: it never had an effect. Use [`group_by`](./series#grouping) |
| `style.grid.opacity` | not an ApexCharts option and never had an effect; use a semi-transparent `style.colors.grid` |

## Coming from apexcharts-card

**Many options have the same names as in the popular [apexcharts-card](https://github.com/RomRider/apexcharts-card), so most charts move over by renaming `series` to `sources`.** JavaScript transforms become LCARdS data sources.

```yaml no-validate
# apexcharts-card
type: custom:apexcharts-card
graph_span: 7d
series:
  - entity: sensor.energy_consumption
    statistics:
      type: change
      period: day
```

```yaml live
# lcards-chart
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: column
graph_span: 7d
sources:
  - entity: sensor.energy_consumption
    statistics:
      type: change
      period: day
```

| apexcharts-card | lcards-chart |
|-----------------|--------------|
| `graph_span` | `graph_span` |
| `span.start`, `span.end`, `span.offset` | `span.start`, `span.end`, `span.offset` |
| `series:` | `sources:` |
| `series[].entity`, `attribute` | `sources[].entity`, `attribute` |
| `series[].statistics.type`, `period` | `sources[].statistics.type`, `period` |
| `series[].group_by.func`, `duration`, `fill` | `sources[].group_by.func`, `duration`, `fill` |
| `yaxis[]`, `series[].yaxis_id` | `yaxis[]`, `sources[].yaxis_id` |
| `series[].name`, `unit`, `float_precision`, `curve`, `stroke_width`, `color`, `opacity`, `type` | the same names on `sources[]` |
| `apex_config` | `style.chart_options` |
| `transform`, `data_generator` (JavaScript) | an [LCARdS data source](../../core/datasources/) with processors |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/common.html -->

# Common Card Properties

**Every LCARdS card takes the same set of card-level options: an `id` and `tags` for the rules engine, `variables` for templates, size overrides and `grid_options`.** They sit at the top level of the card's YAML, next to `type`.

- Most cards need none of them: a card fills the cell Home Assistant gives it, and `grid_options` sets how big that cell is.
- The size overrides (`height`, `width` and their minimum and maximum) change how big the card draws inside its cell, for a card outside a sections grid or one that must keep a fixed size.
- The alert overlay is the exception: it takes none of these, see its [card options](/cards/alert-overlay/#card-options).

## id and tags

**`id` names one card and `tags` put it in groups, so [rules](/core/rules/) can restyle that card or every card in a group.** Neither changes how the card looks on its own; they also label the card in debug logs.

- Under a rule's `apply.overlays`, a card's id is the key that targets it (`kitchen-light-btn:`) and `tag:<name>` targets a group (`tag:lights:`).

```yaml live
# A rule on this card turns it blue while the kitchen light is on (tap to toggle)
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.kitchen
preset: lozenge
id: kitchen-light-btn
tags:
  - kitchen
  - lights
text:
  name:
    content: KITCHEN
    show: true
rules:
  - id: kitchen-on
    when:
      entity: light.kitchen
      state: "on"
    apply:
      overlays:
        kitchen-light-btn:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcards-blue)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | - | This card's name for rules (the key under `apply.overlays`) and logs |
| `tags` | list | - | Group names for rules (`tag:<name>`), such as `[nav, lights]` |

## variables

**`variables` holds your own named values, so a value used in several places on a card is set once.** Templates read them: `{variables.<name>}` in a token template and `variables.<name>` inside a `[[[ JavaScript ]]]` template.

- A variable can hold anything YAML can: text, a number, a colour, a list. See [Templates](/core/templates/) for where templates work.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.kitchen
preset: lozenge
variables:
  accent: var(--lcards-orange)
  room: Kitchen
text:
  label:
    content: "{variables.room}"
    show: true
style:
  card:
    color:
      background:
        active: "[[[ return variables.accent ]]]"
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `variables` | object | - | Your own named values: `variables.<name>` in JavaScript templates, `{variables.<name>}` in token templates |

## Sizing

**`height` and `width` set the card's own size, overriding the cell it sits in.** By default a card is as big as its cell and its drawing scales to fit, so you only need these for a fixed size or for a card outside a sections grid.

- A number is pixels (`200` is `200px`); a string takes any CSS length: `px`, `%`, `vh` and `vw`, `em` and `rem`, or `calc()`.
- In a sections view Home Assistant still sizes the cell from `grid_options` (or the card's own row count), so a card taller than its cell overlaps the cards below it. Set `grid_options.rows` to match.
- A pixel `height` also sets the rows the card reports in a masonry view: the height divided by 50, rounded up.

```yaml live
# A fixed 120 px tall button, half the width of its cell (two rows, so it fits)
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.kitchen
preset: lozenge
height: 120
width: 50%
grid_options:
  rows: 2
text:
  name:
    content: FIXED SIZE
    show: true
```

::: details More about sizing
- **Where it helps:** a card in a horizontal stack or another container that doesn't use the sections grid, a chart or MSD at an exact pixel height, or a pair of `height` and `width` that keeps proportions.
- **Relative units:** `vh`, `%` and other relative heights can't be turned into rows before the card draws, so the card reports its usual row count for them.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `height` | number / string | the cell's height | Card height: a number is px, or any CSS length (`200px`, `50vh`, `calc(100% - 8px)`) |
| `width` | number / string | the cell's width | Card width: a number is px, or any CSS length (`300px`, `100%`) |

### Minimum and maximum size

**`min_height`, `min_width`, `max_height` and `max_width` keep a card that sizes itself between a floor and a ceiling.** The card still fills its cell, but never shrinks below the minimum or grows past the maximum.

- A `height` or `width` wins over the minimum on the same side: the card is exactly that size.
- A button (and an elbow or slider) has a floor already: its presets set `min_height` to the theme's button height (56 px with the LCARdS theme), and without one it keeps `--lcards-button-min-height` (40 px unless your theme sets it). In a [Layout Card](/cards/layout-card/) or [layout view](/cards/layout-view/) cell of a fixed height it follows the cell instead; elsewhere set `min_height: 0` to let it follow a shorter cell.

```yaml live
# A two-row cell, but never taller than 80 px or wider than 300 px
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.kitchen
preset: lozenge
max_height: 80
max_width: 300
grid_options:
  rows: 2
text:
  name:
    content: CEILING
    show: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `min_height` | number / string | the button's preset: the theme's button height; others none | Smallest height (a number is px). Cleared when `height` is set; the preset's gives way in a layout cell of a fixed height |
| `min_width` | number / string | - | Smallest width (a number is px). Cleared when `width` is set |
| `max_height` | number / string | - | Largest height (a number is px, or any CSS length) |
| `max_width` | number / string | - | Largest width (a number is px, or any CSS length) |

## overflow

**`overflow` sets what happens to content that doesn't fit inside the card: it can spill out, be cut off, or scroll.** `overflow_x` and `overflow_y` set one direction each and win over `overflow` for that direction.

- The values are CSS's: `visible` (spills out), `hidden` (cut off), `clip` (cut off, and no scrolling from code either), `scroll` (always a scrollbar) and `auto` (a scrollbar only when needed).

```yaml live
# Cut off anything drawn outside the card, such as a glow
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.kitchen
preset: lozenge
overflow: hidden
text:
  name:
    content: CLIPPED
    show: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `overflow` | string | - | Both directions: `visible`, `hidden`, `clip`, `scroll` or `auto` |
| `overflow_x` | string | - | Left to right only, over `overflow` |
| `overflow_y` | string | - | Top to bottom only, over `overflow` |

## z_index

**`z_index` sets which card is drawn on top where cards overlap.** A higher number is in front of a lower one; cards that set none share the default stacking order.

- It only orders cards that overlap in the same container, such as cards placed over each other in a [Layout Card](/cards/layout-card/).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.kitchen
preset: lozenge
z_index: 10
text:
  name:
    content: IN FRONT
    show: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `z_index` | integer | - | Stacking order, higher in front. The card editor offers -999 to 9999 |

## grid_options

**`grid_options` is Home Assistant's own setting for how many columns and rows of a sections view the card takes.** It sizes the cell; the card then fills it.

- A section is 12 columns wide, and each row is 56 px with an 8 px gap. Without `grid_options` each card asks for its own size: a button is one row, a d-pad five.
- `grid_options` sizes the cell and `height` / `width` size the card in it; in a sections view `grid_options` is usually all you need.

```yaml live
# Half the section's width, two rows tall
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.kitchen
preset: lozenge
grid_options:
  columns: 6
  rows: 2
text:
  name:
    content: TWO ROWS
    show: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `grid_options.columns` | number / string | the card's own | Columns of 12 to span, or `full` |
| `grid_options.rows` | number / string | the card's own | Rows to take, or `auto` |

## Inside custom:layout-card

**Use the LCARdS [Layout Card](/cards/layout-card/) rather than `custom:layout-card` to arrange LCARdS cards in a grid.** Inside `custom:layout-card`'s grid, LCARdS cards shrink to their minimum height (its rows are `auto` high) and `card_margin` is ignored; the LCARdS Layout Card has neither problem and adds the Layout Studio.

- Moving over is one line: set `type: custom:lcards-layout-card` and remove `layout_type`. The `layout` keys and each card's `view_layout` stay the same.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr)
  grid-template-rows: 1fr
  height: 120px
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: lozenge
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: lozenge
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: lozenge
```

::: details Staying on custom:layout-card?
Add this to the layout card itself (not the LCARdS card) so its rows fill their height. `card_margin` stays ignored there; the LCARdS Layout Card is the fix.

```yaml
type: custom:layout-card
layout_type: custom:grid-layout
card_mod:
  style: |
    grid-layout {
      --layout-height: 100% !important;
    }
```
:::

## More options on every card

**Most cards also take these options, each with its own page.**

| Option | Covers |
|--------|--------|
| [`text`](/core/text-fields) | Text fields with templates, per-field styling and zones |
| [`tap_action`, `hold_action`, `double_tap_action`](/core/actions) | Any Home Assistant action |
| [`preset`](/core/presets) | Style presets (button, elbow, slider; select menu options) |
| [`rules`](/core/rules/) | Restyle this or other cards when conditions match |
| [`animations`](/core/animations) | Animations on load, tap, state change and more |
| [`background_animation`](/core/effects/background-animations) | Animated canvas backgrounds (button, elbow, slider) |
| [`filters`](/core/effects/filters) | CSS and SVG filters on the card |
| [`sounds`](/core/sounds) | Per-card sound overrides, or `enabled: false` |
| [`data_sources`](/core/datasources/) | Named entity subscriptions with history and processing |
| [`triggers_update`](/core/templates/#manual-tracking-with-triggers-update) | Extra entities that re-evaluate templates |
| [`zones`, `debug_zones`](/core/text-fields-zones) | Your own named text zones, and outlines for every zone |
| [`state_attribute`, `ranges_attribute`, `state_classification`](/core/colours) | State colours from an attribute or your own state buckets |
| [Themes](/core/themes/) | The design tokens cards read (colours, fonts, sizes) |
