# MSD Card

`custom:lcards-msd-card`

<video class="doc-video" src="/img/cards/msd-motion.webm" poster="/img/cards/msd.webp" title="MSD card: a starship blueprint inside shield arcs that turn orange, then red, as shield strength drops, with three controls joined to the ship by routed lines" autoplay loop muted playsinline></video>

**A Master Systems Display: a ship blueprint, deck plan or floor plan with live Home Assistant cards placed on it, joined to the drawing by lines that find their own way round it.** Shapes add rooms, zones and conduits, and rules and animations bring the whole display to life.

- The drawing is an SVG: one of the built-in blueprints, your own file, or a blank canvas. Every position on the card is measured in the drawing's own units, so the display scales as one.
- **Overlays** sit on the drawing: controls (any card), lines and shapes. A line runs between two named points (anchors), and routes round the controls and the ship by itself.
- Lines and shapes can follow entities: colours by state, animations, and rules that restyle several overlays at once.

::: tip Try it
- The card editor's **Open Configuration Studio** opens the MSD Studio: a full-screen editor where you pick the blueprint, draw controls and shapes on the canvas and connect lines with a click.
- [Getting Started](./quick-start) builds a first display in the Studio, step by step.
:::

| Page | Covers |
|------|--------|
| [Getting Started](./quick-start) | A first display in the MSD Studio, and a complete example to copy |
| [Background and Anchors](./background) | The `msd` block, the blueprint, the view box, anchors and an animated background |
| [Control Overlay](./control-overlay) | Any card placed on the drawing |
| [Line Overlay](./line-overlay) | Lines between anchors and overlays: sides, gaps, colours, markers |
| [Shape Overlay](./shape-overlay) | Rooms, zones and conduits: rectangles, circles and polylines |
| [Line Routing](./routing) | How lines find their way, bundling, crossings, channels and the routing settings |
| [Manual Routing](./manual-routing) | Lines through waypoints you place |
| [Animations and Rules](./animations) | Animations on the blueprint and on groups of overlays, and rules that restyle overlays |
| [Base SVG Filters](./base-svg-filters) | Dim, blur or tint the blueprint so the overlays stand out |

## Quick start

**A blueprint, two controls in its empty corners, and a line from each control to a point on the ship.**

- `br` and `wc` are markers built into this blueprint (its bridge and warp core): see [Automatic anchors](./background#automatic-anchors).
- `attachment: top-left` makes `position` the control's top-left corner. Without it, `position` is the control's centre.
- `route: auto` draws each line around the ship, not through it.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue
  overlays:
    - id: bridge-ctl
      type: control
      attachment: top-left
      position: [60, 60]
      size: [360, 100]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: light.bridge
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          label:
            content: BRIDGE
            show: true
            font_size: 30
    - id: core-ctl
      type: control
      attachment: top-left
      position: [60, 1040]
      size: [360, 100]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: switch.warp_core
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          label:
            content: WARP CORE
            show: true
            font_size: 30
    - id: bridge-line
      type: line
      anchor: bridge-ctl
      attach_to: br
      route: auto
    - id: core-line
      type: line
      anchor: core-ctl
      attach_to: wc
      route: auto
```

## Overlay types

**Everything on the drawing is one of three overlay types, listed under `msd.overlays`.** Each has an `id` (required, and what lines and rules use to find it) and a `type`.

- Overlays paint in `z_index` order, higher in front. Unset, controls paint over lines and lines over shapes.
- A button, chart or slider on the drawing is a normal card inside a control overlay; the MSD has no widgets of its own.

| Type | Draws | Placed with | `z_index` default | Page |
|------|-------|-------------|-------------------|------|
| `control` | Any Home Assistant or LCARdS card | `position`, `size`, `attachment` | `200` | [Control Overlay](./control-overlay) |
| `line` | A line from one anchor or overlay to another | `anchor`, `attach_to`, `route` | `100` | [Line Overlay](./line-overlay) |
| `shape` | A rectangle, circle or polyline | `kind`, then `position` and `size`, or `points` | `50` | [Shape Overlay](./shape-overlay) |

## Card options

**The card's own top-level keys: the `msd` block holds the display, the rest are the keys every LCARdS card takes.** Each links to its page.

- Rules restyle overlays through their ids and the card's `id` and `tags`: see [Rules](./animations#rules).
- In a sections view the card takes the full width and 8 rows unless `grid_options` says otherwise, and can't be made smaller than 2 by 4.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
id: bridge-display
tags:
  - ship-displays
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 5
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue
  view_box: [180, 270, 1600, 720]
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `type` | string | required | `custom:lcards-msd-card` |
| `msd` | object | required | The display: blueprint, view box, anchors, overlays, routing, animations. See [msd](./background#msd) |
| `id` | string | - | This card's name for rules and logs: see [id and tags](../common#id-and-tags) |
| `tags` | list | - | Group names for rules: see [id and tags](../common#id-and-tags) |
| `rules` | list | - | Rules that restyle overlays and play animations: see [Rules](./animations#rules) and the [Rules Engine](../../core/rules/) |
| `data_sources` | object | - | Named entity subscriptions with history and processing: see [Data Sources](../../core/datasources/) |
| `height` | number / string | the cell's height | Card height: see [Sizing](../common#sizing) |
| `width` | number / string | the cell's width | Card width: see [Sizing](../common#sizing) |
| `min_height` | number / string | - | Smallest height: see [Minimum and maximum size](../common#minimum-and-maximum-size) |
| `min_width` | number / string | - | Smallest width: see [Minimum and maximum size](../common#minimum-and-maximum-size) |
| `max_height` | number / string | - | Largest height: see [Minimum and maximum size](../common#minimum-and-maximum-size) |
| `max_width` | number / string | - | Largest width: see [Minimum and maximum size](../common#minimum-and-maximum-size) |
| `overflow` | string | - | What happens to content outside the card: see [overflow](../common#overflow) |
| `overflow_x` | string | - | Left to right only, over `overflow` |
| `overflow_y` | string | - | Top to bottom only, over `overflow` |
| `z_index` | integer | - | The card's stacking order on the dashboard: see [z_index](../common#z-index) |
| `grid_options` | object | full width, 8 rows | Home Assistant's cell size in a sections view: see [grid_options](../common#grid-options) |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/msd/animations.html -->

# Animations and Rules

An MSD can animate in four places, all with the same animation keys as every LCARdS card ([Animations](../../core/animations)), and rules can restyle its overlays while a condition holds.

| Where | Animates | Page |
|-------|----------|------|
| `animations` on a line, shape or control | That overlay | [Line Overlay](./line-overlay), [Shape Overlay](./shape-overlay), [Control Overlay](./control-overlay) |
| `msd.base_svg.animations` | Parts of the blueprint, by id or class | [base_svg.animations](#base-svg-animations) |
| `msd.animations` | A group of overlays, by selector | [msd.animations](#msd-animations) |
| `rules[].apply.animations` | Overlays, while a rule matches | [Rules](#rules) |

None of them play in the MSD Studio's preview while you edit; check the effect on the dashboard.

## base_svg.animations

**Animations on parts of the blueprint itself: a marker that blinks, a deck that glows, a conduit that draws in.** Each one names the element to animate with `target` (or several with `targets`), a CSS selector such as `#br` (an id in the SVG) or `.deck` (a class).

- The selector is looked for inside the blueprint only, never in the overlays.
- Open the SVG in a text editor or the browser's inspector to find its ids; the MSD Studio's animation editor lists them for you on the Base SVG tab.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 5
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue
    # the bridge marker (a circle with id br) blinks
    animations:
      - trigger: on_load
        preset: blink
        target: "#br"
        loop: true
  view_box: [180, 270, 1600, 720]
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `base_svg.animations` | list | - | Animations, each with the [animation keys](../../core/animations#animation-options); `target` or `targets` picks the part of the blueprint |

## msd.animations

**One animation for a whole group of overlays, picked by a CSS selector, instead of the same entry on every overlay.** Use it for a set of shields that draw in together, every line on the card, or all the controls.

- The selector runs over all the overlays at once, so it works the same on shapes, lines and controls. Each overlay carries `data-overlay-id` (its id) and `data-overlay-type` (`line`, `shape` or `control`) to select by.
- On a line or shape, aim at the drawn part inside it by adding `[data-animatable="true"]`, as below. A selector that matches only the overlay's wrapper still fades, moves and scales it, but colour animations (stroke, fill) show nothing there.
- On a control, the selector reaches the frame the card sits in, not the card inside it: fades, movement and glows work, but the card's own parts can't be animated from here.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 4
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 800, 300]
  # every overlay whose id starts with conduit_ draws in, then out again
  animations:
    - trigger: on_load
      preset: draw
      target: '[data-overlay-id^="conduit_"] [data-animatable="true"]'
      duration: 1500
      loop: true
      alternate: true
  overlays:
    - id: conduit_upper
      type: shape
      kind: polyline
      points:
        - [60, 80]
        - [400, 80]
        - [400, 150]
        - [740, 150]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 6
    - id: conduit_lower
      type: shape
      kind: polyline
      points:
        - [60, 220]
        - [400, 220]
        - [400, 150]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 6
```

::: details More about msd.animations
- **The selector, picked for you:** in the MSD Studio, the target picker offers **All Shapes overlays**, **All Lines overlays** and **All Controls overlays**, and an **All "prefix_*" overlays** entry for every two or more overlays whose ids share the text before their first underscore (`shield_fore`, `shield_aft` ... give **All "shield_*" overlays**). They already aim at the drawn part, so prefer them over writing the selector by hand.
- **Why the wrapper isn't enough for colours:** each line or shape is a `<g data-overlay-id="...">` round the element that is actually drawn, and that element sets its own stroke and fill (from `style.color` and `style.fill`). A colour animated on the wrapper is inherited only where nothing closer sets it, so it never shows.
- **Other cards in a control:** for a Home Assistant card that isn't an LCARdS card, the control's frame is all an animation can reach.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `msd.animations` | list | - | Animations, each with the [animation keys](../../core/animations#animation-options); `target` or `targets` is a selector over all the overlays |

## Rules

**Rules change the display while a condition holds: they restyle overlays, play animations on them and tint the blueprint.** The rule sits in the card's `rules` list and works like a rule on any card ([Rules Engine](../../core/rules/)); this section covers what it can do on an MSD.

- Under `apply.overlays`, name an overlay by its `id` and give the style to use. A line or shape takes its `style` keys (`color`, `width`, `opacity`, `dash_array`, `fill`); the [Rules Engine](../../core/rules/) also has selectors for groups (`tag:`, `type:`, `pattern:`, `all`).
- Animations under `apply.animations` start when the rule matches and stop when it no longer does. Name the overlay with `overlay:` (its id), or a group with `tag:`, `type:` or `pattern:`.
- `apply.base_svg` crossfades the blueprint to other [filters](./base-svg-filters), such as a red tint on alert; `filters: []` clears them.
- For an animation with no condition (these all draw in on load), use [msd.animations](#msd-animations) instead.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 5
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue
  view_box: [180, 270, 1600, 720]
  overlays:
    - id: reactor-ctl
      type: control
      attachment: top-left
      position: [190, 886]
      size: [340, 96]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
        text:
          name:
            content: REACTOR
            show: true
            font_size: 30
    - id: reactor-line
      type: line
      anchor: reactor-ctl
      attach_to: wc
      route: auto
      corner_style: round
      style:
        color: var(--lcards-gray-medium-light)
        width: 4
# while the toggle is on: the line turns red and blinks, and the ship takes a red tint
rules:
  - id: msd-reactor-alert
    when:
      entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
      state: "on"
    apply:
      overlays:
        reactor-line:
          style:
            color: var(--lcars-alert-red)
      animations:
        - overlay: reactor-line
          preset: blink
          loop: true
      base_svg:
        filters:
          - mode: svg
            type: tint
            value:
              color: alpha(var(--lcars-alert-red), 0.35)
        transition: 500
```

::: details More about rules on an MSD
- **Rule ids are shared:** every card's rules run in one engine, keyed by `id`, so give each rule a name no other card uses.
- **The highest priority wins** when two matching rules both set `base_svg`.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `apply.overlays.<id>` | object | - | The overlay's new `style` while the rule matches. Also takes the Rules Engine's group selectors |
| `apply.animations` | list | - | Animations played while the rule matches: `overlay` (an id), `tag`, `type` or `pattern`, with `preset`, `duration`, `loop`, `params` ... |
| `apply.base_svg.filters` | list | - | The blueprint's [filters](./base-svg-filters) while the rule matches. `[]` clears them |
| `apply.base_svg.transition` | number | `1000` | How long the crossfade to the new filters takes, ms |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/msd/background.html -->

# Background and Anchors

The drawing an MSD is built on, and the named points on it that overlays and lines use. The overlays themselves have their own pages: [Control Overlay](./control-overlay), [Line Overlay](./line-overlay) and [Shape Overlay](./shape-overlay).

## msd

**Everything the display shows lives under the card's `msd` key: the blueprint, the view box, the anchors, the overlays and how lines are routed.** The other top-level keys (`id`, `rules`, sizing) are on the [overview](./#card-options).

- An `msd` needs a blueprint (`base_svg.source`) or a `view_box`. A `view_box` with no blueprint is a [blank canvas](#a-blank-canvas).
- Every position, size and distance under `msd` is in the drawing's own units (its view box), not pixels, so the whole display scales with the card.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 5
msd:
  # the blueprint, and the part of it to show
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue
  view_box: [180, 270, 1600, 720]
  # a card on the drawing, and a line from it to the bridge marker (br)
  overlays:
    - id: bridge-ctl
      type: control
      attachment: top-left
      position: [190, 278]
      size: [340, 96]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_lights
        text:
          name:
            content: BRIDGE
            show: true
            font_size: 30
    - id: bridge-line
      type: line
      anchor: bridge-ctl
      attach_to: br
      route: auto
      corner_style: round
      style:
        color: var(--lcards-gray-medium-light)
        width: 3
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `msd.base_svg` | object | - | The blueprint: see [base_svg](#base-svg). Not needed for a blank canvas |
| `msd.view_box` | `auto` / list | `auto` | The part of the drawing shown, `[min_x, min_y, width, height]`: see [view_box](#view-box) |
| `msd.anchors` | object | - | Your own named points: see [anchors](#anchors) |
| `msd.overlays` | list | - | The controls, lines and shapes: see [Overlay types](./#overlay-types) |
| `msd.routing` | object | - | Card-wide line routing settings: see [Line Routing](./routing#routing) |
| `msd.channels` | object | - | Named corridors that guide lines: see [Line Routing](./routing#channels) |
| `msd.animations` | list | - | One animation for a group of overlays: see [msd.animations](./animations#msd-animations) |
| `msd.background_animation` | list / object | - | An animated canvas behind the drawing: see [background_animation](#background-animation) |
| `msd.triggers_update` | string | - | `all`: every control gets every Home Assistant update. Slower; prefer `triggers_update` on the one control that needs it ([Control Overlay](./control-overlay)) |

## base_svg

**The blueprint the display is drawn on: a built-in ship, your own SVG file, or none.** Its markers and outline also give you [anchors](#automatic-anchors) to attach lines to without placing any yourself.

- `source` takes `builtin:<name>` (see [Built-in blueprints](#built-in-blueprints)), a file in your `/config/www` folder as `/local/<file>.svg`, a full `https://` URL (the site must allow it), or an SVG from the Home Assistant media library as `media-source://...`.
- In the MSD Studio's Base SVG tab, **Asset library** lists the built-in blueprints, **Custom path** takes a `/local/` path or a URL, and **Browse Home Assistant media** picks an SVG from the media library (it lists only SVG files).
- `render_visual: false` hides the blueprint but still reads its anchors: use it with an [animated or image background](#background-animation) and anchors placed on that instead.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 6
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-kelvin
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `base_svg.source` | string | required | `builtin:<name>`, `/local/<file>.svg`, an `https://` URL, `media-source://...`, or `none` for a [blank canvas](#a-blank-canvas) |
| `base_svg.filters` | list | - | Dim, blur or tint the blueprint: see [Base SVG Filters](./base-svg-filters) |
| `base_svg.render_visual` | boolean | `true` | `false`: don't draw the blueprint, only read its anchors and view box |
| `base_svg.harvest_landmarks` | boolean | `true` | Work out anchors from the blueprint's outline: see [Automatic anchors](#automatic-anchors) |
| `base_svg.harvest_svg_elements` | boolean | `true` | Use the blueprint's own named markers as anchors: see [Automatic anchors](#automatic-anchors) |
| `base_svg.animations` | list | - | Animations on parts of the blueprint, by id or class: see [base_svg.animations](./animations#base-svg-animations) |

### Built-in blueprints

**The blueprints that come with LCARdS, for `source: builtin:<name>`.** The MSD Studio's Asset library lists the same ones.

| Source | Blueprint |
|--------|-----------|
| `builtin:ncc-1701-a` | USS Enterprise NCC-1701-A (Constitution class refit), the master systems display |
| `builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue` | The same ship in blue, with markers for the bridge (`br`), warp core (`wc`) and shuttle bay (`sb`) |
| `builtin:ncc-1701-kelvin` | USS Enterprise NCC-1701 of the Kelvin timeline films |
| `builtin:enterprise-d-shuttlecraft15-anomaly` | Shuttlecraft 15, a type-6 shuttle of the Enterprise-D, with anomaly markers |

## view_box

**Which part of the drawing the card shows, and the coordinates every position on it uses.** By default it is the blueprint's own view box, so the whole drawing fits the card.

- Give `[min_x, min_y, width, height]` to show only part of the blueprint: the card crops to it and keeps its shape (width to height).
- Overlay positions stay in the blueprint's coordinates whatever the view box: cropping moves the window, not the overlays.
- In the MSD Studio, the Base SVG tab's ViewBox section switches between **Auto-detect from SVG** and a custom view box.

```yaml live
# Only the ship's middle, cropped from the 1920 by 1200 blueprint
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 5
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue
  view_box: [180, 270, 1600, 720]
```

::: details More about view_box
- **No view box in the SVG:** with `auto`, an SVG file that has no `viewBox` of its own is read as `[0, 0, 400, 200]`. Give `view_box` for such a file.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `view_box` | `auto` / list | `auto` | `auto`: the blueprint's own view box. Or `[min_x, min_y, width, height]` in the blueprint's units; required for a blank canvas |

### A blank canvas

**A display with no blueprint: give a `view_box` and draw everything with overlays.** Use it for a panel of controls wired together, or a floor plan drawn from shapes.

- A `view_box` with no `base_svg` is a blank canvas; `base_svg.source: none` says the same thing and needs a `view_box` too.
- With no blueprint there are no automatic anchors: place overlays by `[x, y]` or by your own [anchors](#anchors).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 4
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 800, 300]
  overlays:
    - id: deck
      type: shape
      kind: rect
      position: [40, 40]
      size: [720, 220]
      corner_style: round
      corner_radius: 24
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 3
        fill: alpha(var(--lcars-orange), 0.1)
    - id: lights-ctl
      type: control
      position: [400, 150]
      size: [260, 80]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_lights
        text:
          name:
            content: DECK LIGHTS
            show: true
```

## anchors

**Your own named points on the drawing, for placing controls and for the ends of lines.** A control's `position`, a line's `anchor` or `attach_to`, and a shape's `position` or `points` can all name an anchor instead of giving `[x, y]`.

- Each anchor is `[x, y]` in the drawing's units. Either value may be a percentage of the view box instead (`"40%"`), measured from its top-left corner.
- An anchor you name here wins over an [automatic anchor](#automatic-anchors) of the same name, so you can move a blueprint's marker without editing the file.
- In the MSD Studio, the Anchors tab adds anchors with **Add Anchor** or by clicking **Place on Canvas**.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 4
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 800, 300]
  anchors:
    port: [150, 120]
    starboard: ["80%", "40%"]
    relay: ["50%", "85%"]
  overlays:
    # controls centred on two anchors
    - id: port-ctl
      type: control
      position: port
      size: [200, 70]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_lights
        text:
          name:
            content: PORT
            show: true
    - id: starboard-ctl
      type: control
      position: starboard
      size: [200, 70]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_doors
        text:
          name:
            content: STARBOARD
            show: true
    # lines from each control to the relay anchor
    - id: port-line
      type: line
      anchor: port-ctl
      attach_to: relay
      route: auto
      corner_style: round
    - id: starboard-line
      type: line
      anchor: starboard-ctl
      attach_to: relay
      route: auto
      corner_style: round
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `anchors.<name>` | `[x, y]` | - | A named point in the drawing's units. Each value may be a percentage of the view box, as `"40%"` |

## Automatic anchors

**A blueprint gives you anchors of its own, so lines can attach to it before you place any: its named markers, and landmarks worked out from its outline.** Both are on by default.

- **Landmarks** (`harvest_landmarks`) come from the blueprint's silhouette: `hull_center` (its middle), `extremity_bow` and `extremity_stern` (the right-most and left-most points), `extremity_top` and `extremity_bottom`, and on a twin-hulled shape such as a ship with nacelles, `lateral_a` and `lateral_b` (the tips of the two hulls).
- **Markers** (`harvest_svg_elements`): every `<circle>`, `<ellipse>`, `<text>` and `<rect>` in the SVG with an `id` is an anchor of that name (a rectangle by its centre). The built-in `ncc-1701-a-blue` has `br`, `wc` and `sb` this way.
- When names collide, your [anchors](#anchors) win over markers, and markers over landmarks.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue
  overlays:
    - id: top-ctl
      type: control
      attachment: top-left
      position: [60, 60]
      size: [360, 100]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_lights
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          name:
            content: TOP
            show: true
            font_size: 30
    - id: centre-ctl
      type: control
      attachment: top-left
      position: [60, 1040]
      size: [360, 100]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          name:
            content: CENTRE
            show: true
            font_size: 30
    # a landmark from the outline, and one from the middle of the ship
    - id: top-line
      type: line
      anchor: top-ctl
      attach_to: extremity_top
      route: auto
    - id: centre-line
      type: line
      anchor: centre-ctl
      attach_to: hull_center
      route: auto
```

::: details More about automatic anchors
- **Facing:** `extremity_bow` is the right-most point, so it is the bow only on a blueprint that faces right.
- **Landmarks that share a spot:** a landmark that lands on the same place as one before it is left out. On a ship whose nacelles reach furthest, `lateral_a` and `lateral_b` take that spot and `extremity_bow` or `extremity_stern` may not exist.
- **Ids from a drawing program:** marker names come from the SVG as exported, so they can be numbered (`g293`) rather than meaningful. Ids that start with `__` or `msd-internal-` are skipped.
- **In the MSD Studio:** the Anchors tab lists both kinds read-only, as **Base SVG: Computed** (landmarks) and **Base SVG: Harvested** (markers), with a search box. **Promote to User Anchor** opens the Add Anchor form at that point, so you can give a `g293` a proper name under `anchors`; **Promote All** does it for every entry the search matches.
- **Turning them off:** set `harvest_landmarks: false` or `harvest_svg_elements: false` to drop either kind, for example a long list of numbered markers. Turning landmarks off also saves the work of reading the outline when the card loads.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `base_svg.harvest_landmarks` | boolean | `true` | Landmarks from the blueprint's outline: `hull_center`, `extremity_bow`, `extremity_stern`, `extremity_top`, `extremity_bottom`, `lateral_a`, `lateral_b` |
| `base_svg.harvest_svg_elements` | boolean | `true` | The blueprint's named `<circle>`, `<ellipse>`, `<text>` and `<rect>` elements, by their `id` |

## background_animation

**An animated canvas behind the drawing: a starfield, a grid, a nebula, or a still image.** It is the same background the button and elbow cards use, with every preset of [Background Animations](../../core/effects/background-animations).

- It draws behind the blueprint and every overlay, whatever their `z_index`.
- To use a picture instead of a blueprint, set `base_svg.render_visual: false` and add the `image` preset: the blueprint's anchors and view box still apply, so you can keep its markers or place your own anchors on the picture.
- In the MSD Studio it is the Base SVG tab's **Background Effects** section; the Studio's preview doesn't draw it.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 5
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue
  view_box: [180, 270, 1600, 720]
  # stars drifting behind the ship
  background_animation:
    - preset: starfield
      config:
        count: 200
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `background_animation` | list / object | - | A list of effects (`preset` and `config`), or `inset` and `effects`: see [Background Animations](../../core/effects/background-animations) |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/msd/base-svg-filters.html -->

# Base SVG Filters

Filters change how the blueprint looks: dimmer, softer, grey or tinted, so the controls and lines on it stand out. They apply to the blueprint only; overlays stay sharp. The same filters work on the button and data grid cards ([Filters](../../core/effects/filters)).

## filters

**`base_svg.filters` is a list of filters applied to the blueprint, one after another.** Each entry names a `type` and gives its `value`; `mode: svg` marks the SVG filter primitives, and CSS filters need no `mode`.

- CSS filters (`opacity`, `blur`, `grayscale` ...) are quick and cover most needs. SVG filters (`tint`, `feColorMatrix` ...) do what CSS can't, such as a real colour tint.
- The CSS filters run first, in list order, then the SVG filters, chained in list order: each one works on the result of the one before.
- `filters: []` clears them. A [rule](./animations#rules) can crossfade the blueprint to other filters while a condition holds, such as a red tint on alert.
- In the MSD Studio, the Base SVG tab's **Filters (base_svg)** section adds and edits them, with a guide to each type.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 5
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue
    # faded and darker, with a blue tint over it
    filters:
      - type: opacity
        value: 0.6
      - type: brightness
        value: 0.8
      - mode: svg
        type: tint
        value:
          color: alpha(var(--lcars-blue), 0.2)
  view_box: [180, 270, 1600, 720]
```

::: details More about filters
- **Older configs** wrote `filters` as one map (`opacity: 0.5`, `blur: 3px`). Write a list of entries instead, as on this page.
- **Live values:** filter values are fixed; templates and entity bindings don't work in them. Use a [rule](./animations#rules) to change them with an entity.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `filters[].type` | string | required | The filter: one of the [CSS filters](#css-filters) or [SVG filters](#svg-filters) below |
| `filters[].value` | number / string / object | per type | A number or string for a CSS filter, the keys listed below for the others |
| `filters[].mode` | string | `css` | `css` or `svg`. Set `svg` for the SVG filters |

## CSS filters

**The browser's own CSS filters: fade, blur, brighten, desaturate and shift the colours of the blueprint.** Most take one number as `value`; `blur` and `hue-rotate` take a length or an angle as a string.

- Stack several to combine them: a faded, slightly blurred blueprint is two entries.
- Each type below has a playground: move the sliders to see it on a sample shape, and copy the YAML it prints.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 5
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue
    # grey, softened and faded
    filters:
      - type: grayscale
        value: 1
      - type: blur
        value: 2px
      - type: opacity
        value: 0.6
  view_box: [180, 270, 1600, 720]
```

### opacity

**How see-through the blueprint is, from `0` (invisible) to `1` (solid).** The usual way to push a busy blueprint into the background.

```yaml
filters:
  - type: opacity
    value: 0.5
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | number | `1` | `0` to `1`. Above `1` changes nothing |

### blur

**A soft focus over the blueprint, as a length in px.** It gives a sense of depth and hides fine detail.

```yaml
filters:
  - type: blur
    value: 3px
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | string | `0px` | Blur radius in px, such as `"3px"` |

### brightness

**Darker or brighter: `1` is unchanged, lower is darker, higher is brighter.**

```yaml
filters:
  - type: brightness
    value: 0.7
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | number | `1` | `0` is black. No upper limit; the Studio goes to `3` |

### contrast

**Less or more contrast: `1` is unchanged, lower softens hard edges and mutes colours.**

```yaml
filters:
  - type: contrast
    value: 0.8
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | number | `1` | `0` is flat grey. No upper limit; the Studio goes to `3` |

### grayscale

**Takes the colour out: `0` is full colour, `1` completely grey.** For a monochrome display, or to give the blueprint less weight.

```yaml
filters:
  - type: grayscale
    value: 0.5
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | number | `0` | `0` to `1` |

### sepia

**A warm brown tone, from `0` (none) to `1` (full).**

```yaml
filters:
  - type: sepia
    value: 0.3
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | number | `0` | `0` to `1` |

### hue-rotate

**Turns every colour round the colour wheel by an angle.** A quick way to recolour a blueprint, or to mark an alert state.

```yaml
filters:
  - type: hue-rotate
    value: 45deg
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | string | `0deg` | An angle in deg, such as `"45deg"`. `0deg` to `360deg` covers the wheel; larger values wrap round |

### saturate

**Less or more colour: `1` is unchanged, lower mutes the colours, higher makes them stronger.**

```yaml
filters:
  - type: saturate
    value: 0.6
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | number | `1` | `0` is grey. No upper limit; the Studio goes to `3` |

### invert

**Inverts the colours, from `0` (normal) to `1` (fully inverted).** For a light blueprint on a dark display, or special effects.

```yaml
filters:
  - type: invert
    value: 0.2
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | number | `0` | `0` to `1` |

### drop-shadow

**A shadow behind the blueprint's lines, for depth or emphasis.**

```yaml
filters:
  - type: drop-shadow
    value:
      x: 2
      "y": 2
      blur: 4px
      color: var(--lcars-black)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value.x` | number | `0` | Shadow offset to the right, px |
| `value.y` | number | `0` | Shadow offset down, px |
| `value.blur` | string | `0px` | Shadow blur radius, such as `"4px"` |
| `value.color` | colour | black | Shadow colour |

## SVG filters

**SVG filter primitives, for effects the CSS filters can't give: a real colour tint, colour matrices, glows, outlines and distortion.** Each entry needs `mode: svg`, and its `value` is a set of keys.

- They chain: each primitive works on the result of the one before it in the list, so a blur followed by a blend makes a glow.
- `tint` is the friendly one: a single entry for a colour wash. The others are the browser's SVG primitives, named as in SVG (`feGaussianBlur` ...).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 5
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue
    # a soft glow: blur the blueprint, then blend the blur back over it
    filters:
      - mode: svg
        type: feGaussianBlur
        value:
          stdDeviation: 6
      - mode: svg
        type: feBlend
        value:
          mode: screen
  view_box: [180, 270, 1600, 720]
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `mode` | string | `css` | Must be `svg` for these |
| `value` | object | per type | See each type below |

### feGaussianBlur

**A blur that chains with the other SVG filters, smoother than the CSS blur.** The base for glows and soft shadows.

```yaml
filters:
  - mode: svg
    type: feGaussianBlur
    value:
      stdDeviation: 4
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value.stdDeviation` | number | `0` | How much to blur: `0` is none |

### feColorMatrix

**Changes colours with a colour matrix: saturation, a hue turn, transparency from brightness, or a custom 4 by 5 matrix.** For colour changes beyond the CSS `saturate` and `hue-rotate`.

```yaml
filters:
  - mode: svg
    type: feColorMatrix
    value:
      type: saturate
      values: 1.5
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value.type` | string | `saturate` | `saturate`, `hueRotate`, `luminanceToAlpha` (darker parts become see-through) or `matrix` |
| `value.values` | number / string / list | `1` for `saturate`, `0` for `hueRotate` | The saturation factor, the hue angle in degrees, or 20 numbers for `matrix` (a list or a string). Not used by `luminanceToAlpha` |

### feOffset

**Moves the result by `dx` and `dy` px.** With a blur and a blend, it makes a shadow of your own.

```yaml
filters:
  - mode: svg
    type: feOffset
    value:
      dx: 3
      dy: 3
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value.dx` | number | `0` | Move right (negative: left), px |
| `value.dy` | number | `0` | Move down (negative: up), px |

### feBlend

**Blends the result so far back over the original blueprint with a blend mode.** After a blur, `screen` or `lighten` gives a glow.

```yaml
filters:
  - mode: svg
    type: feBlend
    value:
      mode: screen
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value.mode` | string | `normal` | Any of the 16 CSS blend modes: `normal`, `multiply`, `screen`, `darken`, `lighten`, `overlay`, `color-dodge`, `color-burn`, `hard-light`, `soft-light`, `difference`, `exclusion`, `hue`, `saturation`, `color`, `luminosity` |

### feComposite

**Combines the result so far with the original blueprint by a compositing operator, or a formula of your own.** For layering beyond the blend modes.

```yaml
filters:
  - mode: svg
    type: feComposite
    value:
      operator: over
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value.operator` | string | `over` | `over`, `in`, `out`, `atop`, `xor` or `arithmetic` |
| `value.k1` | number | `0` | `arithmetic` only: the result is `k1 * a * b + k2 * a + k3 * b + k4` (a: the result so far, b: the blueprint) |
| `value.k2` | number | `0` | `arithmetic` only |
| `value.k3` | number | `0` | `arithmetic` only |
| `value.k4` | number | `0` | `arithmetic` only |

### feMorphology

**Thins (`erode`) or thickens (`dilate`) the blueprint's lines.** For outlines, or heavier strokes on a fine drawing.

```yaml
filters:
  - mode: svg
    type: feMorphology
    value:
      operator: dilate
      radius: 2
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value.operator` | string | `erode` | `erode` thins, `dilate` thickens |
| `value.radius` | number | `1` | How far to thin or thicken |

### feTurbulence

**Noise for organic textures, usually followed by `feDisplacementMap` to warp the blueprint.** On its own it draws only the noise, in place of the blueprint.

```yaml
filters:
  - mode: svg
    type: feTurbulence
    value:
      baseFrequency: 0.02
      numOctaves: 3
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value.type` | string | `turbulence` | `turbulence` (cloudy) or `fractalNoise` (softer) |
| `value.baseFrequency` | number | `0.05` | `0` to `1`: lower is larger features |
| `value.numOctaves` | integer | `1` | `1` to `10` layers of detail |
| `value.seed` | number | `0` | Change it for a different pattern |

### feDisplacementMap

**Warps the image by the colours of the result before it: wavy, liquid or turbulent distortion.** Put an `feTurbulence` right before it to give it something to warp by.

```yaml
filters:
  - mode: svg
    type: feTurbulence
    value:
      baseFrequency: 0.02
      numOctaves: 3
  - mode: svg
    type: feDisplacementMap
    value:
      scale: 20
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value.scale` | number | `10` | How strong the distortion is |
| `value.xChannelSelector` | string | `R` | The colour channel that moves pixels across: `R`, `G`, `B` or `A` |
| `value.yChannelSelector` | string | `G` | The colour channel that moves pixels up and down |

### tint

**A flat colour wash over the blueprint, from one entry: the alert tint.** The colour's alpha sets how much of the blueprint shows through.

- It covers the blueprint's whole area, background included, not only its lines.

```yaml
filters:
  - mode: svg
    type: tint
    value:
      color: alpha(var(--lcars-alert-red), 0.35)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value.color` | colour | black at 50% | The wash colour, with its alpha, such as `alpha(var(--lcars-alert-red), 0.35)` |

## Recipes

**Filter lists to copy for the usual looks.** Each is a `base_svg.filters` value; change the numbers to taste.

### Dimmed

**Lower opacity and brightness: a quieter blueprint that still shows its detail.** A good default.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 4
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue
    filters:
      - type: opacity
        value: 0.5
      - type: brightness
        value: 0.8
  view_box: [180, 270, 1600, 720]
```

### Subtle

**A light fade with a slight blur and a little less colour: the detail stays, the weight goes.**

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 4
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue
    filters:
      - type: opacity
        value: 0.6
      - type: blur
        value: 1px
      - type: grayscale
        value: 0.2
  view_box: [180, 270, 1600, 720]
```

### Backdrop

**Strong dimming with a blur, for displays full of data where the overlays carry everything.**

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 4
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue
    filters:
      - type: opacity
        value: 0.3
      - type: blur
        value: 3px
      - type: brightness
        value: 0.6
  view_box: [180, 270, 1600, 720]
```

### Faded

**Less colour and contrast with a fade: a muted, minimal look.**

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 4
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue
    filters:
      - type: opacity
        value: 0.4
      - type: grayscale
        value: 0.5
      - type: contrast
        value: 0.7
  view_box: [180, 270, 1600, 720]
```

### Red wash

**A real red tint with the SVG `tint` filter, for alert states.** Put it in a [rule](./animations#rules) to show it only during an alert.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 4
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue
    filters:
      - mode: svg
        type: tint
        value:
          color: alpha(var(--lcars-alert-red), 0.35)
  view_box: [180, 270, 1600, 720]
```

### Monochrome

**Fully grey with lower contrast, so only the overlays carry colour.**

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 4
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue
    filters:
      - type: opacity
        value: 0.6
      - type: grayscale
        value: 1
      - type: contrast
        value: 0.8
  view_box: [180, 270, 1600, 720]
```

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/msd/control-overlay.html -->

# Control Overlay

`type: control`

**A control puts a real card on the MSD canvas: an LCARdS button, a Home Assistant thermostat, a custom card.** The card works as it does anywhere else (taps, more-info, live states); the control decides where it sits and how big it is, and gives lines nine points to connect to.

- Sizes and positions are in viewBox units, the same coordinates as the background, so a control stays on its part of the blueprint however wide the card is drawn.
- Controls are drawn over lines and shapes, so a line can run under a card and seem to stop at its edge.

## card

**`card` is the embedded card's own config, exactly as you would write it on a dashboard.** `id` names the control, so lines, rules and other controls can refer to it.

- Any card works: LCARdS cards, Home Assistant's own cards (`thermostat`, `entities`, `sensor`) and custom cards from HACS. The card fills the control's `size`.
- The card's own `entity`, actions and styles stay on the card. The control itself has no entity.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 200]
  overlays:
    - id: warp_control
      type: control
      position: [160, 100]
      size: [240, 70]
      tags: [engineering]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: switch.warp_drive
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          label:
            content: WARP DRIVE
            show: true
        tap_action:
          action: toggle
    - id: impulse_control
      type: control
      position: [440, 100]
      size: [240, 70]
      tags: [engineering]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: light.impulse_deck
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          label:
            content: IMPULSE
            show: true
        tap_action:
          action: toggle
```

::: details More about card
- **Home Assistant and custom cards:** they render on a dashboard but not in these docs (the docs have no Home Assistant frontend), so here is one as plain YAML:

  ```yaml
  - id: climate_control
    type: control
    position: sickbay
    size: [220, 130]
    card:
      type: thermostat
      entity: climate.sickbay
  ```

- **Entities the control cannot see:** a control updates its card when an entity named in `card` changes. If the card depends on others (a card that finds its entities by itself), list them in [`triggers_update`](#triggers-update).
- **Animations** on a control animate its frame; see [Animations and Rules](./animations).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | required | Unique id: the name lines, rules and other controls use |
| `type` | string | required | `control` |
| `card` | object | required | The embedded card's config |
| `tags` | list | - | Tags for rules: the selector `tag:<name>` matches every overlay with that tag |
| `z_index` | number | `200` | Stacking order among overlays; higher is in front. Lines default to `100` and shapes to `50`, so controls cover both |
| `locked` | boolean | `false` | MSD Studio only: the control can't be dragged or resized on the canvas (it stays editable in the list). No effect on the dashboard |
| `animations` | list | - | Animations on the control's frame; see [Animations and Rules](./animations) |

## position

**`position` says where the control goes and `attachment` says which point of the control lands there.** By default the control's centre sits on its position.

- `position` takes `[x, y]`, the name of an anchor (see [Background and Anchors](./background#anchors)), or another control's `id`.
- `attachment: top-left` makes `position` the control's top-left corner, which is easier when you line controls up in a column. Any of the nine [attachment points](#attachment-points) works.
- Placed on another control, a control centres on it. `position_side` picks a different point of that control, for example `right` to start beside it.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 220]
  anchors:
    bridge: [150, 110]
  overlays:
    # centred on a named anchor
    - id: bridge_ctl
      type: control
      position: bridge
      size: [200, 60]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: light.bridge
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          label:
            content: BRIDGE
            show: true
    # its left edge on the bridge control's right edge
    - id: helm_ctl
      type: control
      position: bridge_ctl
      position_side: right
      attachment: left
      size: [160, 60]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: light.helm
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          label:
            content: HELM
            show: true
    # top-left corner at [400, 150]
    - id: ops_ctl
      type: control
      position: [400, 150]
      attachment: top-left
      size: [180, 50]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: light.ops
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          label:
            content: OPS
            show: true
```

::: details More about position
- **`anchor` on a control** is an older name for `position`. It still works, but `position` wins when both are set; use `position`.
- **Order matters for `position_side`:** the control you place against must come earlier in `overlays`. If it isn't ready yet, the control falls back to that control's centre.
- **No size:** a control without `size` is drawn 100 by 100.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `position` | `[x, y]` / string | required | Where the control goes: `[x, y]` in viewBox units, an anchor name, or another control's `id` |
| `size` | `[width, height]` | `[100, 100]` | Size in viewBox units |
| `attachment` | string | `center` | Which point of this control sits on `position`: one of the nine [attachment points](#attachment-points) |
| `position_side` | string | `center` | When `position` is another control's `id`: which of that control's nine points to use. Ignored for an anchor or `[x, y]` |

## Attachment Points

**Every control has nine named points that lines connect to: the middle of each edge, each corner and the centre.** A line names the control in `anchor` or `attach_to` and picks the point with `anchor_side` or `attach_side`.

- Left out, the side is the one nearest the line's other end. Set it when you want a particular side.
- The [line overlay](./line-overlay#attachment-points) page covers sides, gaps and how a side also sets the direction a line leaves in.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 260]
  overlays:
    - id: sensor_card
      type: control
      position: [150, 60]
      size: [200, 60]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: sensor.warp_speed
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          label:
            content: WARP SPEED
            show: true
    - id: graph_card
      type: control
      position: [450, 200]
      size: [200, 60]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: sensor.shield_strength
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          label:
            content: SHIELDS
            show: true
    # from the bottom of one control to the left of the other
    - id: link
      type: line
      anchor: sensor_card
      anchor_side: bottom
      attach_to: graph_card
      attach_side: left
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 4
```

| Point | Where |
|---|---|
| `top` | Middle of the top edge |
| `bottom` | Middle of the bottom edge |
| `left` | Middle of the left edge |
| `right` | Middle of the right edge |
| `center` | The centre |
| `top-left` | Top-left corner |
| `top-right` | Top-right corner |
| `bottom-left` | Bottom-left corner |
| `bottom-right` | Bottom-right corner |

## obstacle

**`obstacle: true` makes routed lines go round the control instead of across it.** Use it for a card that sits between two things a line joins.

- Only lines routed `auto` (the default), `smart` or `grid` avoid obstacles; `direct`, `angled`, `manhattan` and `manual` lines keep their shape. See [Line Routing](./routing#obstacles).
- `clearance` on the line, or in [`routing`](./routing#routing), keeps lines a set distance from the box.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 240]
  anchors:
    west: [40, 120]
    east: [560, 120]
  overlays:
    - id: core_status
      type: control
      position: [300, 120]
      size: [200, 70]
      obstacle: true
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: switch.warp_core
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          label:
            content: WARP CORE
            show: true
    - id: bypass
      type: line
      anchor: west
      attach_to: east
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 4
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `obstacle` | boolean | `false` | Lines routed `auto`, `smart` or `grid` go round this control's box |

## triggers_update

**`triggers_update` lists entities the embedded card depends on that LCARdS can't see in its config.** A control only refreshes its card when an entity it knows about changes, which keeps a busy MSD fast.

- LCARdS finds the entities named in `card` by itself. You only need this for a card that picks its entities another way, such as an alert card that finds every entity of a device class.
- `triggers_update: all` refreshes this control on every Home Assistant update. Use it only when the entities can't be listed. `msd.triggers_update: all` does the same for every control on the card and is best avoided.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 160]
  overlays:
    - id: alerts
      type: control
      position: [300, 80]
      size: [300, 70]
      triggers_update:
        - binary_sensor.hull_breach
        - binary_sensor.core_breach
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: switch.red_alert
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          label:
            content: ALERTS
            show: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `triggers_update` | list / `all` | - | Extra entity ids that refresh this control, or `all` for every update |

## Rules Engine Integration

**Rules can change a control while a condition holds: dim it, hide it, flag it.** Name the control by `id` (or every control with a tag, `tag:<name>`) under the rule's `apply.overlays`.

- A rule's `style` on a control is set as CSS on the control's frame, so frame-wide properties such as `opacity` work. The embedded card keeps its own colours.
- Change the switch under the card to see the rule apply. [Animations and Rules](./animations#rules) has the full story, including animations a rule starts and stops.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 160]
  overlays:
    - id: warp_core
      type: control
      position: [300, 80]
      size: [260, 70]
      tags: [engineering]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          label:
            content: WARP CORE
            show: true
rules:
  - id: warp-offline
    when:
      entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
      state: "off"
    apply:
      overlays:
        warp_core:
          style:
            opacity: 0.3
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rules` | list | - | Card-level rules; each `apply.overlays` entry names a control by `id` or `tag:<name>`. See [Rules Engine](../../core/rules/) |
| [`id` and `tags`](#card) | | | How a rule finds the control |
