<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/msd/line-overlay.html -->

# Line Overlay

`type: line`

**A line joins two places on the MSD canvas: a control to a point on the ship, one control to another, a shape's corner to an anchor.** You give the two ends; the router draws the path between them, round obstacles and alongside other lines.

- Ends can be a control, a [shape](./shape-overlay), an anchor name or `[x, y]`. A line to a control or shape follows it when it moves.
- How the router picks a path, bundles lines and avoids crossings is on [Line Routing](./routing). [Manual Routing](./manual-routing) draws a line through points you choose.

## anchor and attach_to

**`anchor` is where the line starts and `attach_to` is where it ends.** Each takes an overlay `id`, the name of an anchor, or `[x, y]` in viewBox units.

- Both ends are needed. Point at a control or shape, and pick the point on it with a [side](#attachment-points).
- Lines are drawn under controls and over shapes (`z_index` `100`), and the background is always behind them.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 240]
  anchors:
    hull: [520, 200]
  overlays:
    - id: bridge_ctl
      type: control
      position: [130, 60]
      size: [200, 60]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: light.bridge
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          label:
            content: BRIDGE
            show: true
    # from the control's right edge to a named anchor
    - id: bridge_line
      type: line
      anchor: bridge_ctl
      anchor_side: right
      attach_to: hull
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 4
    # between two coordinates
    - id: plain_line
      type: line
      anchor: [40, 200]
      attach_to: [300, 200]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 4
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | required | Unique id, for rules and the Studio |
| `anchor` | string / `[x, y]` | required | Start: an overlay `id`, an anchor name or `[x, y]` |
| `attach_to` | string / `[x, y]` | required | End: an overlay `id`, an anchor name or `[x, y]` |
| `tags` | list | - | Tags for rules: the selector `tag:<name>` matches every overlay with that tag |
| `z_index` | number | `100` | Stacking order among overlays; higher is in front. Controls default to `200`, shapes to `50` |
| `animations` | list | - | Animations on the line (draw it in, march its dashes); see [Animations and Rules](./animations) |

## Attachment Points

**`anchor_side` and `attach_side` pick the point of a control or shape where the line starts or ends.** There are nine on a control or a `rect`/`circle` shape, and one per corner point on a `polyline` shape.

- On an end that is a control or shape, a side you leave out is the one nearest the other end, and the line starts out at right angles to it. Set `center` to run to the middle.
- A side also sets the direction the line leaves or arrives in: `left` and `right` make that end horizontal, `top` and `bottom` vertical. This works on an anchor or `[x, y]` end too, which has no edge to sit on.
- A corner side with a `route_hint` (`route_hint_last` at the end) runs the line along that edge, inside it: the line's outer edge is flush with the box, and it starts half its width inside the corner. A label with a border on one side and a line from that side's top corner make one clean L.
- In MSD Studio's Connect mode these points show as dots on every control (orange), shape (green) and anchor (cyan): click a start and an end to draw a line with the sides filled in. Dragging a line's end near a point snaps it on.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 260]
  overlays:
    - id: card_a
      type: control
      position: [130, 70]
      size: [180, 60]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: light.port
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          label:
            content: PORT
            show: true
    - id: card_b
      type: control
      position: [470, 190]
      size: [180, 60]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: light.starboard
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          label:
            content: STARBOARD
            show: true
    # right edge to left edge
    - id: h_connection
      type: line
      anchor: card_a
      anchor_side: right
      attach_to: card_b
      attach_side: left
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 4
    # bottom edge to bottom edge
    - id: v_connection
      type: line
      anchor: card_a
      anchor_side: bottom
      attach_to: card_b
      attach_side: bottom
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 4
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anchor_side` | string | nearest side | Where on the start overlay the line begins: `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, `center`, `top-left`, `top-right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-right`, or `vertex0`, `vertex1` ... on a polyline shape |
| `attach_side` | string | nearest side | Where on the end overlay the line arrives; same values |

## Gap System

**A gap leaves a space between the overlay's edge and the end of the line.** Use it so a line stops short of a card instead of touching it.

- The gap moves the end straight out from the side: left from `left`, up from `top`, and out on both axes from a corner.
- A gap needs a side on an overlay end. An anchor or `[x, y]` end has no edge to step out from.
- `attach_gap_x` and `attach_gap_y` set the two directions of the end's gap separately, for a corner.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 160]
  overlays:
    - id: card_a
      type: control
      position: [130, 80]
      size: [180, 60]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: light.port
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          label:
            content: PORT
            show: true
    - id: card_b
      type: control
      position: [470, 80]
      size: [180, 60]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        entity: light.starboard
        preset: lozenge
        text:
          label:
            content: STARBOARD
            show: true
    - id: gap_line
      type: line
      anchor: card_a
      anchor_side: right
      # 20 out from card_a's right edge
      anchor_gap: 20
      attach_to: card_b
      attach_side: left
      # 20 out from card_b's left edge
      attach_gap: 20
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 4
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anchor_gap` | number | `0` | Space between the start overlay's side and the line, viewBox units |
| `attach_gap` | number | `0` | Space between the end overlay's side and the line, viewBox units |
| `attach_gap_x` | number | `attach_gap` | The end's gap across, for a corner or `left`/`right` side |
| `attach_gap_y` | number | `attach_gap` | The end's gap up or down, for a corner or `top`/`bottom` side |

## Routing Modes

**`route` picks how the path is drawn: found round obstacles and other lines (`auto`), straight, one bend, a side stub and then straight, or through your own points.** Leave it out for `auto`, which suits almost every line.

- `auto`, `smart` and `grid` lines bundle with nearby lines and avoid crossing them; see [Line Routing](./routing). `direct`, `angled`, `manhattan` and `manual` lines keep their shape, though other lines still bundle beside them and avoid crossing them.
- `route_hint` and `route_hint_last` set which way the first and last stretch run, for every mode except `direct`, `angled` and `manual`. A side (`anchor_side`, `attach_side`) sets them for you when you leave them out.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 380]
  anchors:
    a1: [40, 40]
    b1: [560, 120]
    a2: [40, 160]
    b2: [560, 280]
    a3: [40, 360]
    b3: [460, 290]
  overlays:
    # straight
    - id: direct_line
      type: line
      anchor: a1
      attach_to: b1
      route: direct
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 3
    # one bend, vertical first
    - id: manhattan_line
      type: line
      anchor: a1
      attach_to: b1
      route: manhattan
      route_hint: yx
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 3
    # through two points of your own
    - id: manual_line
      type: line
      anchor: a2
      attach_to: b2
      route: manual
      waypoints:
        - [300, 160]
        - [300, 280]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-green)
        width: 3
    # a stub out of the right side, then straight at an angle
    - id: angled_line
      type: line
      anchor: a3
      attach_to: b3
      route: angled
      anchor_side: right
      stub_length: 120
      corner_radius: 12
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-yellow)
        width: 3
```

| Mode | What it draws |
|---|---|
| `auto` | The default: full pathfinding with obstacle avoidance, bundling and crossing avoidance. The same as `smart` |
| `direct` | A straight line between the ends. Never pathfinds |
| `angled` | A straight stub out of `anchor_side` (and into `attach_side` when set), then one straight run at any angle. `stub_length` sets the stub. Never pathfinds |
| `manhattan` | One bend (or a few, to leave and arrive on the sides you set). No pathfinding, bundling or crossing avoidance |
| `smart` | Pathfinding plus a refinement pass that nudges bends for room and clearance |
| `grid` | Pathfinding, bundling and crossing avoidance, without the refinement pass |
| `manual` | Straight runs through your `waypoints`; see [Manual Routing](./manual-routing) |

::: details More about route hints
- **Values:** `xy` and `yx` name the order of the two directions. On `route_hint`, `xy` starts horizontal and `yx` starts vertical. On `route_hint_last`, `xy` ends vertical and `yx` ends horizontal.
- **From sides:** with no hint set, `anchor_side: left` or `right` starts the line horizontal and `top` or `bottom` vertical; `attach_side` does the same for the end. A corner or `center` side doesn't set a direction.
- **Neither:** the line starts along whichever axis is longer between the two ends, and ends the same way it started.
- **Order:** a hint you set wins over a side, and a side wins over the distance rule.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `route` | string | `auto` | `auto`, `direct`, `angled`, `manhattan`, `smart`, `grid` or `manual` |
| `route_hint` | string | from `anchor_side` | First stretch: `xy` horizontal, `yx` vertical |
| `route_hint_last` | string | from `attach_side` | Last stretch: `xy` vertical, `yx` horizontal |
| `waypoints` | list | - | `manual` only: the points to pass through, in order: `[x, y]`, `[x, y, radius]` or an anchor name. See [Manual Routing](./manual-routing#per-waypoint-corner-radius) |
| `route_channels` | list | - | Channel ids this line routes through; see [channels](./routing#channels) |
| `clearance` | number | `routing.clearance` | Space kept round obstacles for this line, viewBox units |

## Corners

**`corner_style` and `corner_radius` shape every bend: rounded (the default), square, or cut off diagonally.** The radius is a target; a bend between two short runs gets a smaller one so it fits.

- `bevel` cuts the corner off; `corner_angle` tilts the cut toward the run going in (`0`) or coming out (`90`).
- `corner_radius_mode: forced` keeps room for the full radius at every bend, at the cost of more detours and crossings; [Corner Size](./routing#corner-size-target-vs-forced) explains when that helps.
- `smoothing_mode: chaikin` softens the whole path into curves. Set `smoothing_iterations` too: with `0` nothing changes.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 240]
  anchors:
    s1: [40, 40]
    end_1: [200, 200]
    s2: [220, 40]
    end_2: [380, 200]
    s3: [400, 40]
    end_3: [560, 200]
  overlays:
    # rounded, radius 34 (the default)
    - id: round_line
      type: line
      anchor: s1
      attach_to: end_1
      route: manhattan
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 6
    # square
    - id: miter_line
      type: line
      anchor: s2
      attach_to: end_2
      route: manhattan
      corner_style: miter
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 6
    # cut diagonally
    - id: bevel_line
      type: line
      anchor: s3
      attach_to: end_3
      route: manhattan
      corner_style: bevel
      corner_radius: 40
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-green)
        width: 6
```

::: details More about corners
- **Fitting:** a bend's radius is at most half the shorter run either side of it, and shrinks near another line so the two strokes don't touch. A wider stroke gets a slightly smaller radius for the same reason.
- **The first run:** routed lines keep a short straight run at each end before turning. `stub_length` sets it for one line; leave it unset unless a line turns later than it should, and check what the router chose first in the [debugger](./routing#debugging).
- **Corner room:** `corner_room_weight` (on `smart` and `auto` lines) lets the router move a bend a little to give a squeezed corner its full radius. `0` turns it off for this line.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `corner_style` | string | `round` | `round`, `miter` (square) or `bevel` (cut off) |
| `corner_radius` | number | `34` | Arc radius (`round`) or size of the cut (`bevel`), viewBox units. On a `manual` line one corner can differ: `[x, y, radius]` |
| `corner_radius_mode` | string | `auto` | `auto`: the radius shrinks where room is short. `forced`: room for the full radius is kept at every bend |
| `corner_angle` | number | `45` | `bevel` only: angle of the cut, `0` to `90` degrees |
| `stub_length` | number | the router's | Straight run at each end before the first turn, viewBox units |
| `corner_room_weight` | number | `routing.corner_room_weight` (`4`) | How hard the router works to give a squeezed corner its full radius. `0` turns it off |
| `smoothing_mode` | string | `none` | `none` or `chaikin` |
| `smoothing_iterations` | number | `0` | Smoothing passes, `0` to `5` |

## Styling

**`style` sets how the line is drawn: colour, width, opacity and the shape of its ends.** The same `style` works on [shapes](./shape-overlay#styling).

- `width` is in viewBox units, so a line gets thicker as the card is drawn bigger, like everything else on the canvas.
- `color` takes a colour or a map of states; see [Dynamic Styling](#dynamic-styling).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 160]
  anchors:
    a: [40, 50]
    b: [560, 50]
    c: [40, 110]
    d: [560, 110]
  overlays:
    - id: thick_line
      type: line
      anchor: a
      attach_to: b
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 10
        line_cap: round
    - id: faint_line
      type: line
      anchor: c
      attach_to: d
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 4
        opacity: 0.5
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style.color` | colour / state map | `theme:colors.ui.tertiary` | Line colour. `style.stroke` is an older name |
| `style.width` | number | `2` | Width, viewBox units. `style.stroke_width` is an older name |
| `style.opacity` | number | `1` | `0` to `1`. Markers fade with the line |
| `style.line_cap` | string | `butt` | `butt`, `round` or `square`: the ends of the line and of every dash |
| `style.line_join` | string | the line's `corner_style`, else `miter` | `miter`, `round` or `bevel`: how the stroke turns at a sharp corner |
| `style.miter_limit` | number | `4` | With `line_join: miter`: how far a sharp join may stick out |
| `style.animatable` | boolean | `true` | `false`: animations skip this line |
| [Dashes](#dash-patterns), [fill](#fill), [gradients and patterns](#gradients-and-patterns), [markers](#markers) | | | The other `style` keys |

### Dash Patterns

**`style.dash_array` breaks the line into dashes or dots.** Give dash and gap lengths, as `"5,5"` or `[5, 5]`.

- `line_cap: round` rounds every dash. For round dots use a dash of length `0`: `dash_array: "0,8"` with `line_cap: round` draws circles as wide as the line.
- A short dash with round caps (`"2,2"`) draws pills, not dots. MSD Studio's Dotted and Dash-Dot patterns use zero-length dashes for you; for other spacing pick Custom with a dash length of `0`.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 160]
  anchors:
    a: [40, 50]
    b: [560, 50]
    c: [40, 110]
    d: [560, 110]
  overlays:
    # dashes
    - id: dashed_line
      type: line
      anchor: a
      attach_to: b
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 4
        dash_array: "20,10"
    # round dots
    - id: dotted_line
      type: line
      anchor: c
      attach_to: d
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 8
        dash_array: "0,16"
        line_cap: round
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style.dash_array` | string / list | solid | Dash and gap lengths, `"5,5"` or `[5, 5]` |
| `style.dash_offset` | number | `0` | Where along the pattern the line starts |

### Fill

**`style.fill` fills the area a path encloses.** It matters most on [shapes](./shape-overlay) (rooms, zones); a line only encloses an area where its path crosses itself.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 220]
  anchors:
    a: [100, 40]
    b: [500, 40]
  overlays:
    # an open U: the fill closes it from end to start
    - id: loop_line
      type: line
      anchor: a
      attach_to: b
      route: manual
      corner_style: miter
      waypoints:
        - [100, 180]
        - [500, 180]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 3
        fill: var(--lcars-blue)
        fill_opacity: 0.3
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style.fill` | colour / state map | `none` | Fill colour |
| `style.fill_opacity` | number | `1` | `0` to `1` |

### Gradients and Patterns

**`style.gradient` fades the line from one colour to another; `style.pattern` draws it in dots.** Either one replaces `color`.

- A gradient always runs left to right. `type` and `direction` are accepted but not used yet.
- A pattern is always dots: small circles `size` apart. Other pattern types are accepted but drawn as dots.
- The short form `gradient: "var(--lcars-blue)-to-var(--lcars-orange)"` is two stops.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 160]
  anchors:
    a: [40, 50]
    b: [560, 50]
    c: [40, 110]
    d: [560, 110]
  overlays:
    - id: gradient_line
      type: line
      anchor: a
      attach_to: b
      style:
        width: 10
        gradient:
          stops:
            - offset: 0%
              color: var(--lcars-blue)
            - offset: 100%
              color: var(--lcars-orange)
    - id: pattern_line
      type: line
      anchor: c
      attach_to: d
      style:
        width: 10
        pattern:
          color: var(--lcars-orange)
          size: 8
          opacity: 0.8
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style.gradient` | object / string | - | A left-to-right gradient |
| `style.gradient.stops` | list | - | Each stop has `offset` (`0%` to `100%`) and `color` |
| `style.pattern` | object | - | A dot pattern along the line |
| `style.pattern.color` | colour | the text colour | Dot colour |
| `style.pattern.size` | number | `8` | Spacing of the dots, viewBox units |
| `style.pattern.opacity` | number | `0.5` | Dot opacity |

### Markers

**Markers put a shape on the ends of a line or on each bend: arrows, dots, diamonds, ticks.** `marker_end` is the end at `attach_to`, `marker_start` the end at `anchor`, `marker_mid` every bend.

- A start marker points away from the line, so `arrow` at both ends gives a two-headed arrow.
- `align: edge` puts the back of an arrow or diamond on the end instead of its middle, so the tip is the outermost point and a thick line can't poke past it.
- `fill: match_line` (or `stroke: match_line`) keeps the marker the line's colour as it changes with an entity. Without a `fill` the marker takes the line's colour when drawn.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 200]
  anchors:
    a: [60, 50]
    b: [540, 50]
    c: [60, 150]
    d: [540, 150]
  overlays:
    - id: arrow_line
      type: line
      anchor: a
      attach_to: b
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 4
        marker_start:
          type: dot
          size: 16
        marker_end:
          type: arrow
          size: 20
          align: edge
    - id: diamond_line
      type: line
      anchor: c
      attach_to: d
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 4
        marker_end:
          type: diamond
          size: 24
          fill: var(--lcars-yellow)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style.marker_start` | object | - | Marker at the `anchor` end; the same keys as `marker_end` |
| `style.marker_mid` | object | - | Marker on every bend; the same keys as `marker_end` |
| `style.marker_end` | object | - | Marker at the `attach_to` end; keys below |
| `style.marker_end.type` | string | required | `arrow`, `dot`, `diamond`, `line` (a tick across the line) or `rect`. `triangle` and `square` are older names; an unknown type draws a dot |
| `style.marker_end.size` | number | `10` | Size in viewBox units; it doesn't change with the line's width |
| `style.marker_end.fill` | colour | the line's colour | Fill, or `match_line` |
| `style.marker_end.stroke` | colour | `none` | Outline, or `match_line` |
| `style.marker_end.stroke_width` | number | `0` | Outline width |
| `style.marker_end.align` | string | `center` | `center` or `edge` (see above) |
| `style.marker_end.width` | number | `size` | `rect` only: its width |
| `style.marker_end.height` | number | `size` | `rect` only: its height |
| `style.marker_end.filled` | boolean | `false` (`true` for `square`) | `rect` only: filled, or drawn as an outline |

## Dynamic Styling

**A line can take its colour from an entity: green while a link is up, red when it drops.** Give the line its own `entity` and make `style.color` (or `style.fill`) a map of states.

- The keys are the same as on a button: `active`, `inactive`, `unavailable`, `default`, a state name, or a range such as `above:90`. `state_attribute` matches an attribute instead of the state, and `ranges_attribute` compares an attribute against the range keys.
- `style.color` also takes a Jinja2 (`{{ }}`) or JavaScript (`[[[ ]]]`) template, which can read any entity.
- Change the toggles under the card to see both lines follow.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 160]
  anchors:
    a: [40, 50]
    b: [560, 50]
    c: [40, 110]
    d: [560, 110]
  overlays:
    # a map of states, on the line's own entity
    - id: status_line
      type: line
      anchor: a
      attach_to: b
      entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
      style:
        width: 6
        color:
          active: var(--lcars-green)
          inactive: var(--lcars-red)
        marker_end:
          type: arrow
          size: 20
          fill: match_line
    # a template
    - id: template_line
      type: line
      anchor: c
      attach_to: d
      style:
        width: 6
        color: "{{ 'var(--lcars-blue)' if is_state('input_boolean.lcards_test_doors', 'on') else 'var(--lcars-orange)' }}"
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | string | - | The entity a state map in `style.color` or `style.fill` follows |
| `state_attribute` | string | - | Match this attribute's value against the state keys instead of the state |
| `ranges_attribute` | string | - | Compare this attribute against `above:`, `below:` and `between:` keys |

## Rules Engine Integration

**Rules restyle lines while a condition holds, across many lines at once.** Name a line by `id`, or every line with a tag (`tag:<name>`), under a rule's `apply.overlays`.

- A rule's `style` changes the line in place, without redrawing the card, so running animations carry on. The keys it can change this way are `color`, `width`, `opacity`, `dash_array`, `line_cap` and `fill`.
- Change the toggle under the card to see the rule apply. [Animations and Rules](./animations#rules) has the full story.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 160]
  anchors:
    a: [40, 50]
    b: [560, 50]
    c: [40, 110]
    d: [560, 110]
  overlays:
    - id: power_a
      type: line
      anchor: a
      attach_to: b
      tags: [power]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 6
    - id: power_b
      type: line
      anchor: c
      attach_to: d
      tags: [power]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 6
rules:
  - id: power-alert
    when:
      entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
      state: "on"
    apply:
      overlays:
        tag:power:
          style:
            color: var(--lcars-alert-red)
            dash_array: "12,6"
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rules` | list | - | Card-level rules; each `apply.overlays` entry names a line by `id` or `tag:<name>`. See [Rules Engine](../../core/rules/) |
| [`id` and `tags`](#anchor-and-attach-to) | | | How a rule finds the line |

# Manual Routing

**`route: manual` draws a line exactly where you say: from its start, through each waypoint in order, to its end.** Use it when a line must follow a set path on the blueprint, or for a decorative line.

- A manual line doesn't pathfind, bundle or avoid crossings. Other lines still see it: they avoid crossing it and can bundle beside it.
- For lines that should adapt when the layout changes, the automatic modes and [channels](./routing#channels) are usually the better tool; see [When to Use Manual Routing](#when-to-use-manual-routing).

## waypoints

**`waypoints` lists the points the line passes through, between `anchor` and `attach_to`.** A waypoint is `[x, y]` in viewBox units or the name of an anchor.

- The line runs `anchor`, then each waypoint in turn, then `attach_to`, with a straight run between each pair. A waypoint that isn't level with the one before gives a diagonal run.
- Each bend is rounded with the line's `corner_radius` (or cut with `corner_style: bevel`), shrinking to fit between short runs.
- `waypoints` only work with `route: manual`; on any other route they are ignored.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 500]
  anchors:
    start_point: [40, 60]
    nav_anchor: [200, 300]
    end_point: [560, 440]
  overlays:
    - type: line
      id: my_line
      anchor: start_point
      attach_to: end_point
      route: manual
      waypoints:
        # first a coordinate
        - [100, 200]
        # then a named anchor
        - nav_anchor
        # then another coordinate, then on to attach_to
        - [300, 400]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 3
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `route` | string | `auto` | `manual` to draw through `waypoints` |
| `waypoints` | list | - | The points to pass through, in order: `[x, y]`, `[x, y, radius]` or an anchor name |
| [Corner keys](./line-overlay#corners) | | | `corner_style`, `corner_radius`, `corner_angle`, `smoothing_mode`, `smoothing_iterations`, as on any line |

## Named Anchor Waypoints

**A waypoint can be an anchor's name instead of a coordinate, so the line passes through wherever that anchor is.** Move the anchor and every line through it follows.

- The name is looked up when the card draws. A name that matches no anchor is skipped, and the line goes straight to the next point.
- Named waypoints keep the layout readable and easy to change: `engineering_junction` says more than `[412, 318]`.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 240]
  anchors:
    start: [40, 200]
    junction: [300, 40]
    finish: [560, 200]
  overlays:
    - id: junction_mark
      type: shape
      kind: circle
      position: [290, 30]
      size: [20, 20]
      style:
        color: var(--lcards-moonlight)
        fill: var(--lcards-moonlight)
    - id: via_junction
      type: line
      anchor: start
      attach_to: finish
      route: manual
      waypoints:
        - [40, 40]
        - junction
        - [560, 40]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 4
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `waypoints` | list | - | An entry that is a string is an anchor name |

## Per-Waypoint Corner Radius

**A coordinate waypoint can carry a third number, the radius of its own corner: `[x, y, radius]`.** Other corners keep the line's `corner_radius`.

- With `corner_style: bevel` the third number is the size of that corner's cut.
- Like `corner_radius`, it is a target: a corner between short runs still gets a smaller one so it fits.
- An anchor-name waypoint is a string and can't carry a radius; its corner always uses the line's `corner_radius`.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 300]
  anchors:
    a: [40, 40]
    b: [560, 260]
  overlays:
    - id: mixed_corners
      type: line
      anchor: a
      attach_to: b
      route: manual
      corner_style: round
      corner_radius: 34
      waypoints:
        # tighter corner
        - [200, 40, 8]
        # the line's 34
        - [200, 260]
        # wider corner
        - [400, 260, 60]
        - [400, 40]
        - [560, 40]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 4
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `waypoints` | list | - | `[x, y, radius]`: this corner's radius (or bevel size), viewBox units |
| `corner_radius` | number | `34` | The radius of every other corner |

## Waypoint Order Matters

**Waypoints are used strictly in the order you list them: `anchor`, then the first, the second ..., then `attach_to`.** Swap two and the line doubles back on itself.

- Sketch the path first (start, waypoint 1, waypoint 2, end), and list points so the line keeps moving one way: left to right, or top to bottom.
- Many waypoints to steer a line round things is a sign a [channel](./routing#channels) or an [obstacle](./routing#obstacles) would do the job with less upkeep.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 300]
  anchors:
    a1: [40, 60]
    b1: [280, 260]
    a2: [320, 60]
    b2: [560, 260]
  overlays:
    # right, then down: a clean L
    - id: in_order
      type: line
      anchor: a1
      attach_to: b1
      route: manual
      waypoints:
        - [280, 60]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 4
    # down past the end, then back up: it doubles back
    - id: doubles_back
      type: line
      anchor: a2
      attach_to: b2
      route: manual
      corner_style: miter
      waypoints:
        - [320, 290]
        - [560, 290]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 4
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `waypoints` | list | - | Used in list order, first to last |

## Waypoints in MSD Studio

**In MSD Studio, select a line and use the Add Waypoint tool to place waypoints on the canvas.**

- Click the canvas to add a coordinate waypoint at the end of the list; click an anchor's marker to add it by name. Adding a waypoint switches the line to `route: manual`.
- Each waypoint shows as a numbered marker. Drag a marker to move it, and drag a corner's radius handle to set that corner's own radius.
- Click empty canvas to leave the tool.

## When to Use Manual Routing

**Manual routing suits a path that must be exact; the automatic modes suit a layout that will change.**

- **Use `manual`** when the path must follow the blueprint or a design rule, to steer round channels or obstacles in a way the router won't, for decorative paths, or to check what an automatic line ought to look like.
- **Use `auto`** (or `smart`, `grid`) when the path should adapt as controls move, when many lines share similar routes, when [channels](./routing#channels) mark clear routing zones, or when you want less to maintain.

## Troubleshooting

**Most manual-line problems are a missing `route: manual` or waypoints in the wrong order.**

- **The line ignores its waypoints and goes straight to the end:** `route` isn't `manual`. Waypoints are only used on a manual line.
- **The line crosses itself or zigzags:** the waypoint order makes it go back. Reorder them so the path keeps moving one way; the Studio's numbered markers show the order.
- **No numbered markers in the Studio:** select the line first (click the line itself, not the empty canvas next to it). A line with no waypoints yet has no markers; add some with the Add Waypoint tool.

# Getting Started

**Build a first Master Systems Display in the MSD Studio, the card's full-screen editor, without writing any YAML.** The MSD is more a small canvas editor than a single card, so this page shows which buttons and panels to use, in order.

- The other pages cover every option and the YAML underneath: [Background and Anchors](./background), [Control Overlay](./control-overlay), [Line Overlay](./line-overlay), [Shape Overlay](./shape-overlay) and [Line Routing](./routing).
- [Putting it together](#putting-it-together) at the end is a complete display to copy.

## What you're building

**An MSD is four layers on top of each other, all arranged in the MSD Studio.**

| Layer | What it is |
|-------|------------|
| **Base SVG** | The drawing underneath: a starship blueprint, a deck plan, a floor plan, or nothing at all (an empty view box) |
| **Controls** | Any Home Assistant or LCARdS card (a button, a slider, a sensor), placed on the drawing |
| **Lines** | Connections between controls and points on the drawing, routed automatically like circuit traces |
| **Shapes** | Rooms, zones and conduits drawn on top |

## Step 1: Add the card

**In a dashboard in edit mode, click Add Card and search for LCARdS MSD.**

![Screenshot: Home Assistant "Add Card" dialog with "LCARdS MSD" typed in the search box](/img/msd-quickstart-01-add-card.png)

**On the card editor's Configuration tab, click Open Configuration Studio.**

![Screenshot: MSD card editor's Configuration tab, showing the "Open Configuration Studio" button](/img/msd-quickstart-02-open-studio.png)

**The MSD Studio opens full screen: the canvas on one side, the settings on the other, and tabs across the top.** The tabs are Base SVG, Anchors, Controls, Lines, Shapes, Routing and YAML; a first display needs only the first four.

![Screenshot: MSD Studio full-screen dialog, empty canvas, tab bar visible across the top](/img/msd-quickstart-03-studio-overview.png)

## Step 2: Choose a background

**On the Base SVG tab, pick where the drawing comes from.** For a first display, pick a ship from the Asset library.

- **Asset library:** the ship blueprints built into LCARdS, the easiest start.
- **Browse Home Assistant media:** an SVG you uploaded to the Home Assistant media library.
- **Custom path:** a `/local/...` path to your own SVG.
- **None (ViewBox Only):** a blank canvas with no drawing.

::: tip Free anchors
Built-in ships, and most SVGs, come with anchor points worked out from the drawing's own outline (`hull_center`, `extremity_top` and others), so your first lines can attach to the ship before you place a single anchor yourself: see [Automatic anchors](./background#automatic-anchors).
:::

![Screenshot: Base SVG tab, Asset Library source mode, a ship selected and visible on the canvas](/img/msd-quickstart-04-base-svg.png)

## Step 3: Place your first control

**On the Controls tab, click Place on Canvas and draw a box for the control on the canvas.** When you let go, the Add Control form opens. You can also click **Add Control** and type the position and size into the form.

![Screenshot: Controls tab, empty state, "Add Control" button highlighted](/img/msd-quickstart-05-add-control.png)

**In the form, give the control an ID, pick its card on the Card tab, and save.**

- The card is any Home Assistant or LCARdS card (a button, a slider, a sensor tile), set up exactly as anywhere else on a dashboard.
- The control then appears on the canvas, on top of the background.

![Screenshot: Add Control form, Card tab, a button card configured inside it](/img/msd-quickstart-06-control-card-tab.png)

## Step 4: Connect the control to the ship with a line

**On the Lines tab, draw a line from your control to a point on the ship.** There are two ways.

- **Add Line** opens a form where you pick the start (**Anchor**) and the end (**Attach To**) from every control and anchor on the canvas, and which side of each the line leaves and arrives at.
- The **Connect Line** tool in the toolbar above the canvas: click a connection point of your control (an orange dot), then another control's connection point or an anchor (a blue dot).

![Screenshot: canvas toolbar with "Connect Line" mode active, a line being drawn between two controls](/img/msd-quickstart-07-connect-line.png)

**The Add Line form opens: give the line an ID or keep the one it suggests, leave the rest as it is, and click Save.** The line finds the best route by itself and appears on the canvas.

![Screenshot: two controls connected by a routed line on the canvas](/img/msd-quickstart-08-line-routed.png)

## Step 5: Save

**Click Save in the Studio's footer, then save the card and the dashboard as usual.** That is a complete display: a background, a live control, and a line from the control to the ship.

- Shapes and Routing are optional. Shapes add rooms, zones and conduits when you want the drawing to feel like a real schematic; Routing holds card-wide settings worth changing only once you notice something you want different ([Line Routing](./routing) explains how lines find their way).

![Screenshot: finished MSD card rendered on a dashboard, background + two controls + connecting line](/img/msd-quickstart-09-final-result.png)

## Putting it together

**A complete display to copy: a dimmed blueprint, three controls joined to its markers, a room drawn as a shape, and a rule that turns the warp core line red.** Tap the controls, or change the entities under the card.

- The blueprint's filters fade it so the controls stand out ([Base SVG Filters](./base-svg-filters)); `br`, `wc` and `sb` are markers in the blueprint itself ([Automatic anchors](./background#automatic-anchors)).
- The rule recolours the line and blinks it while the toggle helper is on ([Rules](./animations#rules)).

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-msd-card

      type: control
      attachment: top-left
      position: [190, 278]
      size: [340, 96]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge

          name:
            content: BRIDGE
            show: true
            font_size: 30
    - id: core-ctl
      type: control
      attachment: top-left
      position: [190, 886]
      size: [340, 96]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
        text:
          name:
            content: WARP CORE
            show: true
            font_size: 30
    - id: shuttle-ctl
      type: control
      attachment: top-left
      position: [1430, 886]
      size: [340, 96]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: filled
        entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_doors
        text:
          name:
            content: SHUTTLE BAY
            show: true
            font_size: 30
    - id: bridge-line
      type: line
      anchor: bridge-ctl
      attach_to: br
      route: auto
      corner_style: round
      style:
        color: var(--lcards-gray-medium-light)
        width: 3
    - id: core-line
```

# Line Routing

**MSD lines route themselves like cables in a raceway: they find their way round obstacles, bundle with lines going the same way, and avoid cutting across each other when a small detour is cheap.** This page explains how the router decides a path, then lists every routing setting.

- The settings on each line (`route`, `route_hint`, sides, `waypoints`) are on [Line Overlay](./line-overlay#routing-modes). This page covers the router and the card-wide `routing` and `channels` settings.
- The order you list lines in never changes the result: the router routes every line until the arrangement settles, before anything is drawn.

## How a Line Finds Its Path

**For every line, every time the card draws, the router works through the same steps.**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Line needs a route] --> B{route mode?}
    B -->|direct / manhattan / manual| C[Fixed shape<br/>no pathfinding]
    B -->|auto, smart, or grid| D{Obstacle<br/>in the way?}
    D -->|yes| E[Detour around it]
    D -->|no| F{Force channel<br/>referenced?}
    E --> F
    F -->|yes| G[Must route through it]
    F -->|no| H{Nearby trunk or channel<br/>worth joining?}
    H -->|yes, cheaper overall| I[Bundle into a shared lane]
    H -->|no, or not worth it| J[Route independently]
    G --> K{Would this cross<br/>another line's path?}
    I --> K
    J --> K
    K -->|yes, small detour avoids it| L[Step around the crossing]
    K -->|no, or detour too costly| M[Final path]
    L --> M
    C --> M
    M --> N[Registered<br/>other lines can now discover and bundle with this one]
```

- Bundling and crossing avoidance are cost comparisons, never hard rules: a line joins a bundle or takes a detour only when that is cheaper than the alternative.
- `direct`, `angled`, `manhattan` and `manual` lines keep their shape, but they are still registered: other lines avoid crossing them and can bundle beside them. That makes a `direct` line a good fixed backbone or wall.

## Obstacles

**An obstacle is a control or shape that routed lines go round instead of through.** Set `obstacle: true` on it; no setting is needed on the lines.

- Lines routed `auto` (the default), `smart` or `grid` avoid obstacles. `clearance` keeps them a set distance from the box: card-wide in [`routing`](#routing), or on one line.
- A `rect` or `circle` shape can be an obstacle as well as a control; see [Control Overlay](./control-overlay#obstacle).

![A line detouring around an obstacle box](/img/msd-routing-obstacle-avoidance.svg)

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 240]
  routing:
    clearance: 10
  overlays:
    - id: reactor
      type: control
      position: [300, 120]
      size: [120, 100]
      obstacle: true
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: panel-dark
        interactive: false
        text:
          label:
            content: REACTOR
    - id: sensors
      type: control
      position: [70, 120]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: SENSORS
            show: true
    - id: core
      type: control
      position: [530, 120]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: CORE
            show: true
    - id: coolant_line
      type: line
      anchor: sensors
      attach_to: core
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 4
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `obstacle` | boolean | `false` | On a control or a `rect`/`circle` shape: routed lines go round its box |
| `clearance` | number | `routing.clearance` (`0`) | On a line: space kept round obstacles, viewBox units |

## Bundling

**Lines that run close and side by side merge into one corridor, on evenly spaced lanes, and branch apart where their ends differ.** It happens on its own: no channel, no setting, just lines going the same way.

- The first line's path becomes the trunk's centre line and stays put. Lines that join take lanes either side of it, `trunk_line_spacing` apart.
- A line joins only when that is cheaper than going its own way. Which side of the centre a line rides follows where it comes from, never its id, and stays the same along a chain of trunks.
- Only `auto`, `smart` and `grid` lines join a bundle; `direct`, `angled`, `manhattan` and `manual` lines can still have others bundle beside them.

![Three lines merging into a shared lane-separated corridor, then branching apart at their destinations](/img/msd-routing-trunk-bundling.svg)

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 300]
  routing:
    trunk_line_spacing: 12
    clearance: 8
  overlays:
    # two bulkheads with a gap between them
    - id: bulkhead_top
      type: control
      position: [300, 55]
      size: [100, 110]
      obstacle: true
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: panel-dark
        interactive: false
        text:
          label:
            content: DECK 4
    - id: bulkhead_bottom
      type: control
      position: [300, 245]
      size: [100, 110]
      obstacle: true
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: panel-dark
        interactive: false
        text:
          label:
            content: DECK 6
    - id: a
      type: control
      position: [70, 40]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: A
            show: true
    - id: b
      type: control
      position: [70, 150]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: B
            show: true
    - id: c
      type: control
      position: [70, 260]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: C
            show: true
    - id: d
      type: control
      position: [530, 40]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: D
            show: true
    - id: e
      type: control
      position: [530, 150]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: E
            show: true
    - id: f
      type: control
      position: [530, 260]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: F
            show: true
    - id: a_d
      type: line
      anchor: a
      attach_to: d
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 3
    - id: b_e
      type: line
      anchor: b
      attach_to: e
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 3
    - id: c_f
      type: line
      anchor: c
      attach_to: f
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 3
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `routing.trunk_bundling_enabled` | boolean | `true` | Lines bundle on their own. `false` turns it off for the card |
| `routing.trunk_line_spacing` | number | `8` | Gap between lanes, viewBox units. It also limits how round the small bends are where lines step onto their lanes; see [Corner Size](#corner-size-target-vs-forced) |
| `routing.trunk_proximity` | number | `32` | How close a line must run to a trunk to join it, viewBox units |
| `routing.trunk_bundle_weight` | number | `0.5` | How strongly joining is rewarded: higher pulls lines in from further away |
| [Advanced bundling settings](#advanced-routing-settings) | | | `trunk_min_length`, `trunk_min_overlap`, `trunk_max_join_candidates`, `trunk_bundle_discount_cap`, `trunk_discovery_max_passes` |

## channels

**A channel is a corridor you draw: lines are rewarded for running through it, kept out of it, or made to use it.** Where bundling only happens between lines already close together, a channel can pull a line off the path it would take.

- `channels` sits directly under `msd:`, not under `msd.routing:`.
- A line opts in with `route_channels: [main_bus]`. A `force` channel must be used, in the order the line lists them; `prefer` is taken when it is cheaper overall; `avoid` costs extra to enter.
- A channel is also a ready-made trunk: lines bundle through it on lanes, as in [Bundling](#bundling). Any `auto`, `smart` or `grid` line passing near it may join, even one that doesn't list it; `discoverable: false` keeps it to the lines that do.

![A line bending off its natural path to ride through an authored prefer channel](/img/msd-routing-channel-prefer.svg)

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 300]
  channels:
    main_bus:
      bounds: [200, 130, 200, 40]
      mode: force
      direction: horizontal
      line_spacing: 16
  overlays:
    # the channel drawn as a shape, so you can see it
    - id: bus
      type: shape
      kind: rect
      position: [200, 130]
      size: [200, 40]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 1
        fill: var(--lcars-orange)
        fill_opacity: 0.2
    - id: a
      type: control
      position: [70, 50]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: A
            show: true
    - id: b
      type: control
      position: [70, 250]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: B
            show: true
    - id: c
      type: control
      position: [530, 50]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: C
            show: true
    - id: d
      type: control
      position: [530, 250]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: D
            show: true
    - id: a_c
      type: line
      anchor: a
      attach_to: c
      route_channels: [main_bus]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 3
    - id: b_d
      type: line
      anchor: b
      attach_to: d
      route_channels: [main_bus]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 3
```

::: details More about channels
- **Lanes:** lines through one channel get their own lanes, centred: one line rides the middle, two ride `line_spacing / 2` either side, three ride `-line_spacing`, `0` and `+line_spacing`, and so on. Lanes stay inside `bounds`, so make the channel at least `line_spacing` times the number of lines across.
- **Invisible:** a channel guides lines but draws nothing. Draw a shape on the same box (as above) if you want to see it; the Studio's Channels toggle shows them while you edit.
- **Older name:** `type` (`bundling`, `avoiding`, `waypoint`) is the old name for `mode` (`prefer`, `avoid`, `force`).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `channels.<id>.bounds` | `[x, y, width, height]` | required | The channel's box, viewBox units |
| `channels.<id>.mode` | string | `prefer` | `prefer`, `avoid` or `force` |
| `channels.<id>.direction` | string | `auto` | `horizontal`, `vertical`, or `auto`: wide boxes run horizontal, tall ones vertical |
| `channels.<id>.weight` | number | `0.5` | How strongly it pulls (`prefer`) or pushes (`avoid`), `0` to `1` |
| `channels.<id>.line_spacing` | number | `8` | Gap between lanes inside it, viewBox units, `0` to `100` |
| `channels.<id>.discoverable` | boolean | `true` | `false`: only lines that list it in `route_channels` use it |
| `route_channels` | list | - | On a line: the channel ids it routes through, in order |

## Crossing Avoidance

**A line is steered away from cutting across another line, unless the detour would be long.** It is a deterrent, not a wall: when stepping round is cheap the router steps round; otherwise the line crosses cleanly.

- Running side by side is never penalised: lines in a bundle don't push each other apart, and a line crossing the inner lanes of a bundle to reach its own outer lane does so freely, as in a real raceway.
- Raise `crossing_avoid_bias` to accept longer detours rather than cross.

![A line stepping around another line's path instead of crossing straight through it](/img/msd-routing-crossing-avoidance.svg)

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 260]
  routing:
    crossing_avoid_bias: 8
  overlays:
    - id: port
      type: control
      position: [70, 130]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: PORT
            show: true
    - id: aft
      type: control
      position: [330, 130]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: AFT
            show: true
    - id: helm
      type: control
      position: [200, 30]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: HELM
            show: true
    - id: sickbay
      type: control
      position: [530, 230]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: SICKBAY
            show: true
    # a fixed power bus: the blue line goes round its end rather than across it
    - id: power_bus
      type: line
      anchor: port
      attach_to: aft
      route: direct
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 4
    - id: helm_line
      type: line
      anchor: helm
      attach_to: sickbay
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 3
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `routing.crossing_avoid_enabled` | boolean | `true` | Lines avoid crossing each other. `false` turns it off for the card |
| `routing.crossing_avoid_bias` | number | `4` | The cost of a crossing: higher accepts longer detours to avoid one |
| `routing.crossing_min_length` | number | `12` | The shortest straight run other lines still avoid crossing, viewBox units |

## Routing Modes

**Each line's `route` picks whether the router finds its path or draws a fixed shape.** Leave it out for `auto`.

- `auto` always means full pathfinding, with or without obstacles or channels on the card. `routing.default_mode` changes what `auto` means for the whole card; a line's own `route` still wins.
- For a line that should not bundle or avoid crossings, choose `manhattan` (fixed shape) or `grid` (pathfinding without the refinement pass) on purpose.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 380]
  overlays:
    - id: direct_from
      type: control
      position: [70, 40]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: DIRECT
            show: true
    - id: direct_to
      type: control
      position: [530, 80]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: END
            show: true
    - id: direct_line
      type: line
      anchor: direct_from
      attach_to: direct_to
      route: direct
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 3
    - id: manhattan_from
      type: control
      position: [70, 130]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: MANHATTAN
            show: true
    - id: manhattan_to
      type: control
      position: [530, 170]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: END
            show: true
    - id: manhattan_line
      type: line
      anchor: manhattan_from
      attach_to: manhattan_to
      route: manhattan
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 3
    - id: auto_from
      type: control
      position: [70, 220]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: AUTO
            show: true
    - id: auto_to
      type: control
      position: [530, 260]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: END
            show: true
    - id: auto_line
      type: line
      anchor: auto_from
      attach_to: auto_to
      route: auto
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 3
    - id: manual_from
      type: control
      position: [70, 310]
      size: [100, 34]

        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge

            content: MANUAL
            show: true

      type: control
      position: [530, 350]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: END
            show: true
    - id: manual_line
      type: line
      anchor: manual_from

        - [350, 330]

        width: 3
```

| Mode | What it does |
|---|---|
| `auto` | The default: full pathfinding with obstacle avoidance, bundling and crossing avoidance. Resolves to `smart`, or to `routing.default_mode` |
| `direct` | A straight line. Never pathfinds or detours |
| `angled` | A straight stub out of `anchor_side` (and into `attach_side` when set), then one straight run at any angle. Never pathfinds or detours |
| `manhattan` | One bend (more only to leave and arrive on the sides set). No pathfinding, no bundling, no crossing avoidance |
| `smart` | Pathfinding plus a refinement pass that nudges bends for clearance and corner room |
| `grid` | Like `smart` (pathfinding, bundling, crossing avoidance) without the refinement pass |
| `manual` | Straight runs through `waypoints`; see [Manual Routing](./manual-routing) |

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `route` | string | `auto` | On a line: the mode, from the table above |
| `routing.default_mode` | string | `auto` | What `auto` means on this card: `auto` or `smart` (the same), `grid` or `manhattan`. A line's own `route` wins |

## Corner Size: Target vs. Forced

**A rounded corner needs room: a straight run either side of the bend.** `corner_radius_mode`, on each line, says where that room comes from.

- `auto` (the default): `corner_radius` is a target. The router picks the path it prefers for crossings and bundling, and each corner gets the full radius where the path leaves room, a smaller one where it doesn't.
- `forced`: `corner_radius` is a requirement. The line keeps a straight run of twice the radius at each end before routing, so the full radius always fits, but the router can't steer that stretch round crossings. It can cause detours or crossings near tight geometry; use it only where one line's corners must be exact.
- Lines with a large `corner_radius` and sides set that cross where they needn't are the `forced` trade-off in action: `auto` is the fix.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 300]
  overlays:
    - id: auto_from
      type: control
      position: [60, 50]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: AUTO
            show: true
    - id: auto_to
      type: control
      position: [240, 250]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: END
            show: true
    - id: forced_from
      type: control
      position: [360, 50]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: FORCED
            show: true
    - id: forced_to
      type: control
      position: [540, 250]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: END
            show: true
    # auto: the corners shrink to fit
    - id: target_line
      type: line
      anchor: auto_from
      attach_to: auto_to
      anchor_side: right
      attach_side: left
      corner_radius: 60
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 4
    # forced: the full radius, with the room it needs
    - id: forced_line
      type: line
      anchor: forced_from
      attach_to: forced_to
      anchor_side: right
      attach_side: left
      corner_radius: 60
      corner_radius_mode: forced
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 4
```

::: details More about corner size
- **Stroke width counts:** a corner's radius is limited by how close the nearest edge of a neighbouring line is, not its centre line, so a thick line gets a smaller radius next to others than a thin one. To get the wider corner back, increase the lane spacing (`trunk_line_spacing` or a channel's `line_spacing`) rather than thinning the line.
- **The straight run at each end:** every routed line keeps a short straight run at each end before it turns. Unset, it is one grid cell (`grid_resolution` times `min_stub_length_factor`, and never less than one cell in `auto` mode), or twice `corner_radius` in `forced` mode. A line's `stub_length` overrides it; going below about one grid cell can make very short lines misbehave, so check what the router chose first with the [debugger](#debugging).
- **Bundled lines turn sooner:** where lines step onto their lanes before a channel or trunk, that small S-bend is limited by the lane spacing, not by `corner_radius`, so the router keeps only as much lead-in as it can use (never more than twice `corner_radius`). A large `corner_radius` for the big bends elsewhere doesn't push every lane change further out.
- **Lane changes keep the full radius:** when bundle members start far apart and converge on tight lanes, each one's lane change is drawn as a real S-curve of two arcs with the full `corner_radius`; a member with less distance to cover sweeps less of the same curve. Members start bending at about the same point, unless one would cut through a neighbour's approach, in which case it starts only as far out as it must.
- **Recovering squeezed corners:** `corner_room_weight` (on by default, `4`) lets the refinement pass of `smart` and `auto` lines move a bend a little to give a squeezed corner its full radius, when the extra distance is small. Unlike `forced`, it is a real cost comparison and never forces a long detour. Set `0` card-wide or on one line to turn it off.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `corner_radius_mode` | string | `auto` | On a line: `auto` (the radius is a target) or `forced` (room for it is reserved) |
| `stub_length` | number | the router's | On a line: the straight run at each end, viewBox units |
| `corner_room_weight` | number | `4` | On a line or in `routing`: how hard the refinement pass works to give a squeezed corner its full radius. `0` turns it off |
| `routing.min_stub_length_factor` | number | `1` | Multiplier on `grid_resolution` for the shortest straight run at each end |

## routing

**`msd.routing` holds the card-wide routing settings; a line's own setting wins where both exist.** Most cards need none of them.

- The settings people change most are in [Bundling](#bundling), [Crossing Avoidance](#crossing-avoidance) and [Corner Size](#corner-size-target-vs-forced). The table below has the rest, and [Advanced Routing Settings](#advanced-routing-settings) the deep internals.
- In MSD Studio the same settings are on the Routing tab: Common Routing Options, Trace Bundling & Crossings, and Advanced Routing Configuration.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 240]
  routing:
    turn_penalty: 6
    clearance: 12
  overlays:
    - id: cargo
      type: control
      position: [300, 120]
      size: [120, 100]
      obstacle: true
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: panel-dark
        interactive: false
        text:
          label:
            content: CARGO
    - id: bridge
      type: control
      position: [70, 40]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: BRIDGE
            show: true
    - id: engineering
      type: control
      position: [530, 200]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: ENGINEERING
            show: true
    - id: route_line
      type: line
      anchor: bridge
      attach_to: engineering
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 4
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `routing.default_mode` | string | `auto` | What `auto` means on this card; see [Routing Modes](#routing-modes) |
| `routing.clearance` | number | `0` | Space kept round obstacles, viewBox units |
| `routing.grid_resolution` | number | scaled to the card | The pathfinding grid's cell size, viewBox units. Unset, it is the shorter side of `view_box` divided by 12, kept between `16` and `64`. Values below 5 become `32` |
| `routing.turn_penalty` | number | `2` | The cost of each change of direction: higher gives straighter paths |
| `routing.corner_room_weight` | number | `4` | See [Corner Size](#corner-size-target-vs-forced) |
| `routing.min_stub_length_factor` | number | `1` | See [Corner Size](#corner-size-target-vs-forced) |
| [Bundling](#bundling), [crossing](#crossing-avoidance) settings | | | `trunk_*` and `crossing_*` |

### Advanced Routing Settings

**Deep internals of the router, rarely needed.** They are under Advanced Routing Configuration on the Studio's Routing tab.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 240]
  routing:
    smoothing_mode: chaikin
    smoothing_iterations: 3
    clearance: 12
  overlays:
    - id: cargo
      type: control
      position: [300, 120]
      size: [120, 100]
      obstacle: true
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: panel-dark
        interactive: false
        text:
          label:
            content: CARGO
    - id: bridge
      type: control
      position: [70, 40]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: BRIDGE
            show: true
    - id: engineering
      type: control
      position: [530, 200]
      size: [100, 34]
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-button
        preset: lozenge
        interactive: false
        text:
          name:
            content: ENGINEERING
            show: true
    - id: smooth_line
      type: line
      anchor: bridge
      attach_to: engineering
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 4
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `routing.route_hint_penalty` | number | `6` | The cost of a first or last step that goes against `route_hint` |
| `routing.smoothing_mode` | string | `none` | `chaikin` softens every line into curves (a line's own setting wins) |
| `routing.smoothing_iterations` | number | `0` | Smoothing passes, `1` to `5`; `chaikin` does nothing without at least `1` |
| `routing.smoothing_max_points` | number | `160` | Most points a smoothed path keeps |
| `routing.smart_proximity` | number | `0` | How close to an obstacle a bend must be for the refinement pass to move it, viewBox units. `0` turns this off (`corner_room_weight` still runs) |
| `routing.smart_detour_span` | number | `48` | Refinement pass: how far a bend may move, viewBox units |
| `routing.smart_max_extra_bends` | number | `3` | Refinement pass: most bends it may add |
| `routing.smart_min_improvement` | number | `4` | Refinement pass: how much better a change must be to keep it |
| `routing.smart_max_detours_per_elbow` | number | `4` | Refinement pass: tries per bend |
| `routing.channel_force_penalty` | number | `800` | The cost of a route that misses a `force` channel |
| `routing.channel_avoid_multiplier` | number | `1` | Multiplier on every `avoid` channel's cost |
| `routing.channel_prefer_bias` | number | `0.9` | Per-cell discount inside a `prefer` channel, scaled by its `weight` |
| `routing.channel_avoid_bias` | number | `3` | Per-cell cost inside an `avoid` channel, scaled by its `weight` |
| `routing.trunk_min_length` | number | `60` | Shortest straight run that becomes a trunk others can join, viewBox units |
| `routing.trunk_min_overlap` | number | `60` | Shortest shared stretch that makes joining worthwhile, viewBox units |
| `routing.trunk_max_join_candidates` | number | `2` | Most trunks one line considers chaining through |
| `routing.trunk_bundle_discount_cap` | number | `150` | The most distance credited when a line rides a trunk another line made, viewBox units, so a long ride can't pay for extra bends elsewhere. Never applies to your own channels |
| `routing.trunk_discovery_max_passes` | number | `4` | Most routing passes before drawing (a safety limit for the order-independence) |
| `routing.cost_defaults.bend` | number | `10` | Route cost of each bend |
| `routing.cost_defaults.proximity` | number | `4` | Route cost of running close to an obstacle |

## Debugging

**The browser console and MSD Studio both show what the router decided.**

- In MSD Studio's canvas toolbar, **Routing Grid** (amber) draws the router's own pathfinding grid, which differs from the drag-snap grid, and **Discovered Trunks** (cyan) draws every bundle in effect with its member count. Both are off by default.
- For the internals (how bundling, lanes and the pre-render passes work) see [Routing Engine Architecture](../../architecture/msd/routing).

```js
// the line's routed points, straight from the route cache (read-only);
// .meta.debug shows what the router resolved for it:
// { stubLength, gridResolution, cornerRadiusMode, cornerRadius }
window.lcards.debug.msd.routing.inspect('line_id')

// router state: cache size, obstacle count, trunk and crossing registry counts
window.lcards.debug.msd.routing.stats()

// every trunk on this card: id, direction, creator, member lines and bounds,
// the data the Studio's Discovered Trunks overlay draws
window.lcards.debug.msd.routing.trunks('card_id')
```

## Known Limitations

**Two rough edges are known and left as they are on purpose: each fix that was tried made other, correct layouts worse.**

- **Joining a trunk is all or nothing.** A line within `trunk_proximity` of a trunk can join it; one just outside can't. Right at that distance, a move of one unit can switch bundling on or off. Widening the distance to soften this changed bundling in layouts that were already right, so it was undone. If a line snaps in and out of a bundle, change `trunk_proximity` itself.
- **A line through several trunks that alternate horizontal and vertical** can now and then pick an order that isn't the shortest, which shows as a small backtrack where two trunks meet. It needs several such trunks in a row, which ordinary diagrams rarely have; so far it has only shown up in stress tests with many lines.
