# Shape Overlay

`type: shape`

**Shapes draw your own geometry on the MSD canvas: a room, a zone round a system, a wall, a conduit.** They use the same style keys as [lines](./line-overlay#styling) (dashes, markers, colours that follow an entity) and add a fill.

- Lines can attach to a shape's corners and points, the same way they attach to a control.
- Shapes are drawn under lines and controls (`z_index` `50`), over the background.

## Kinds

**`kind` picks the shape: `rect` for a box, `circle` for a round or oval area, `polyline` for a path through points.**

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 240]
  overlays:
    # a room
    - id: reactor_room
      type: shape
      kind: rect
      position: [40, 40]
      size: [180, 120]
      corner_style: round
      corner_radius: 12
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 3
        fill: var(--lcars-orange)
        fill_opacity: 0.15
    # a field
    - id: containment_field
      type: shape
      kind: circle
      position: [260, 50]
      size: [140, 140]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 3
    # a conduit
    - id: power_conduit
      type: shape
      kind: polyline
      points:
        - [440, 40]
        - [560, 40]
        - [560, 200]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-yellow)
        width: 4
        dash_array: "12,6"
```

| `kind` | Placed with | Drawn as |
|---|---|---|
| `rect` | `position`, `size` | A rectangle |
| `circle` | `position`, `size` | An ellipse inside the box: equal width and height give a circle |
| `polyline` | `points`, `closed` | A path through the points, open or closed |

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | required | Unique id, for lines, rules and the Studio |
| `type` | string | required | `shape` |
| `kind` | string | required | `rect`, `circle` or `polyline` |
| `tags` | list | - | Tags for rules: the selector `tag:<name>` matches every overlay with that tag |
| `z_index` | number | `50` | Stacking order among overlays; higher is in front. Lines default to `100`, controls to `200` |
| `locked` | boolean | `false` | MSD Studio only: the shape can't be dragged, resized or have its points moved on the canvas. No effect on the dashboard |
| `animations` | list | - | Animations on the shape; see [Animations and Rules](./animations) |

## rect and circle

**A `rect` or `circle` fills a box: `position` is its top-left corner and `size` its width and height.** This differs from a control, whose `position` is its centre unless you set `attachment`.

- `position` takes `[x, y]` in viewBox units or the name of an anchor.
- A `rect` gets rounded corners with `corner_style: round` and a `corner_radius`; without both its corners are square. A `circle` has no corners.
- `obstacle: true` makes routed lines go round the box, as on a [control](./control-overlay#obstacle).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 220]
  anchors:
    west: [20, 110]
    east: [580, 110]
  overlays:
    # rounded corners
    - id: bay
      type: shape
      kind: rect
      position: [220, 50]
      size: [160, 120]
      corner_style: round
      corner_radius: 20
      obstacle: true
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 3
        fill: var(--lcars-orange)
        fill_opacity: 0.2
    # a line routed round the bay
    - id: corridor
      type: line
      anchor: west
      attach_to: east
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 3
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `position` | `[x, y]` / string | required | Top-left corner: `[x, y]` in viewBox units or an anchor name |
| `size` | `[width, height]` | required | Width and height, viewBox units |
| `corner_style` | string | square corners | `rect` only: `round` rounds the corners. `miter` and `bevel` leave them square |
| `corner_radius` | number | `0` | `rect` with `corner_style: round`: the corner radius, viewBox units |
| `obstacle` | boolean | `false` | Lines routed `auto`, `smart` or `grid` go round the box |

## polyline

**A `polyline` draws a path through a list of points: a wall, a conduit, an outline.** `closed: true` joins the last point back to the first, so the shape can be filled.

- Each point is `[x, y]` in viewBox units or an anchor name. At least two points are needed.
- Bends are rounded by default with a radius of `34`, like a line's; a bend between two short runs gets a smaller one. `corner_style: miter` keeps them sharp.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 240]
  overlays:
    # an open conduit with cut-off corners
    - id: conduit
      type: shape
      kind: polyline
      corner_style: bevel
      corner_radius: 24
      points:
        - [40, 40]
        - [260, 40]
        - [260, 200]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 6
    # a closed, filled outline with square corners
    - id: deck
      type: shape
      kind: polyline
      closed: true
      corner_style: miter
      points:
        - [340, 40]
        - [560, 40]
        - [560, 200]
        - [420, 200]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 3
        fill: var(--lcars-orange)
        fill_opacity: 0.2
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `points` | list | required | The points in order, each `[x, y]` or an anchor name. At least two |
| `closed` | boolean | `false` | Join the last point back to the first, so `style.fill` shows |
| `corner_style` | string | `round` | `round`, `miter` (sharp) or `bevel` (cut off) |
| `corner_radius` | number | `34` | Arc radius (`round`) or size of the cut (`bevel`), viewBox units |
| `corner_angle` | number | `45` | `bevel` only: angle of the cut, `0` to `90` degrees |
| `smoothing_mode` | string | `none` | `chaikin` softens the path into curves |
| `smoothing_iterations` | number | `0` | Smoothing passes, `0` to `5`. `chaikin` needs at least `1` |

## Attachment Points

**Lines attach to a shape like they attach to a control: name the shape in `anchor` or `attach_to` and a point in `anchor_side` or `attach_side`.**

- A `rect` or `circle` has the nine points of its box: `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, `center` and the four corners (`top-left` ...). On a circle the corners are the box's corners, outside the circle.
- A `polyline` has one point per entry in `points`: `vertex0`, `vertex1` and so on, in order.
- In MSD Studio's Connect mode these show as green dots on the canvas (controls are orange, anchors cyan); drag a line's end near one to snap it on.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 260]
  overlays:
    - id: wall
      type: shape
      kind: polyline
      corner_style: miter
      points:
        - [40, 40]
        - [240, 40]
        - [240, 220]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 4
    - id: room
      type: shape
      kind: rect
      position: [380, 60]
      size: [180, 120]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 3
    # from the wall's middle point to the room's top-left corner
    - id: connector
      type: line
      anchor: wall
      anchor_side: vertex1
      attach_to: room
      attach_side: top-left
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-yellow)
        width: 3
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`anchor_side`, `attach_side`](./line-overlay#attachment-points) | | | Set on the line: a box point, or `vertex<N>` on a polyline |

## Styling

**A shape takes the same `style` keys as a line, plus a fill that counts.** See [Line Overlay: Styling](./line-overlay#styling) for every key.

- `style.fill` shows on every `rect` and `circle` and on a `closed` polyline. Without a `style.color` the outline is `var(--lcars-orange)`.
- Markers (`marker_start`, `marker_mid`, `marker_end`) only work on a polyline; a box has no ends.
- `line_cap` shapes each dash of a dashed outline, so `dash_array: "0,10"` with `line_cap: round` draws a ring of dots. `line_join` and `miter_limit` have no effect on a circle.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 220]
  overlays:
    # a dotted ring
    - id: sensor_ring
      type: shape
      kind: circle
      position: [60, 30]
      size: [160, 160]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 8
        dash_array: "0,16"
        line_cap: round
    # a polyline with an arrow
    - id: flow
      type: shape
      kind: polyline
      points:
        - [300, 180]
        - [300, 50]
        - [560, 50]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        width: 4
        marker_end:
          type: arrow
          size: 20
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style.color` | colour / state map | `var(--lcars-orange)` | Outline colour |
| `style.fill` | colour / state map | `none` | Fill colour |
| `style.fill_opacity` | number | `1` | `0` to `1` |
| [Line style keys](./line-overlay#styling) | | | `width`, `opacity`, `line_cap`, `line_join`, `dash_array`, `gradient`, `pattern`, markers and `animatable`, as on a line |

## Dynamic Styling

**A shape's outline and fill can follow an entity: a room that lights up, a field that turns red on a breach.** Give the shape its own `entity` and make `style.color` or `style.fill` a map of states.

- The keys are the same as on a line or button: `active`, `inactive`, a state name, a range such as `above:90`. `state_attribute` and `ranges_attribute` work as on a [line](./line-overlay#dynamic-styling).
- Both colours update on their own when the entity changes. Rules can restyle shapes too; see [Animations and Rules](./animations).
- Change the toggle under the card to see the field follow.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 220]
  overlays:
    - id: containment_field
      type: shape
      kind: circle
      position: [220, 30]
      size: [160, 160]
      entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_doors
      style:
        width: 4
        color:
          active: var(--lcars-alert-red)
          inactive: var(--lcars-green)
        fill:
          active: alpha(var(--lcars-alert-red), 0.4)
          inactive: alpha(var(--lcars-green), 0.15)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | string | - | The entity a state map in `style.color` or `style.fill` follows |
| `state_attribute` | string | - | Match this attribute's value against the state keys instead of the state |
| `ranges_attribute` | string | - | Compare this attribute against `above:`, `below:` and `between:` keys |

## Drawing & Editing in MSD Studio

**The Shapes tab and the canvas toolbar have three draw tools: Polyline, Rectangle and Circle.**

- **Polyline:** click to place each point; double-click (or turn the tool off) to finish. Points snap to the grid, with a live preview as you go.
- **Rectangle and circle:** drag from one corner to the opposite one, with a live preview.
- **Editing:** select a shape to drag its points (polyline) or its resize handles (rectangle, circle) on the canvas.
- The Bounding Boxes and Attachment Points toggles at the top right of the Shapes tab show the same aids as on the Controls tab.

# Select Menu Card

`custom:lcards-select-menu`

**A grid of LCARS buttons, one per option of an `input_select` or `select` entity: tap one to select it.** The selected option lights up, and the card follows the entity when something else changes it.

- Each option is a real [button card](../button/) underneath, so every button preset and the button's `style` keys work here.
- Without an entity, the card is a manual menu: list the buttons in `options` and give each one its own action.

::: tip Try it
- The card editor has tabs for the config, the grid, the style, the options and the actions, with a live preview.
- The [Playground](./playground) lets you edit select menu YAML here in the docs and see the result.
:::

| Page | Covers |
|------|--------|
| [Options and Actions](./options) | Which options show, their labels and icons, and what a tap does |
| [Grid and Sizing](./layout) | Columns, gaps and row height, and how the card sizes itself in a dashboard |
| [Styles](./styles) | Colours, text and borders for every option, the button template, rules |
| [Playground](./playground) | Edit YAML and see the select menu live |

---

## Quick Start

**Three menus to start from: an entity's options as they are, the same options with your own labels, and a manual menu of navigation buttons.** Tap an option in the first two to select it.

- `grid.columns` sets how many buttons sit side by side; the card adds rows for the rest.
- Keys under `options` must match the entity's option values exactly, including case.

```yaml live
# The entity's options, one column
type: custom:lcards-select-menu
entity: input_select.demo_mode
preset: lozenge
```

```yaml live
# Four columns with your own labels
type: custom:lcards-select-menu
entity: input_select.demo_mode
preset: capped
grid:
  columns: 4
  gap: 6px
options:
  Auto:
    label: AUTO
  Cool:
    label: CHILL
  Heat:
    label: WARM
  "Off":
    label: STANDBY
```

```yaml live
# A manual menu: no entity, each option navigates
type: custom:lcards-select-menu
preset: lozenge
grid:
  columns: 2
  gap: 4px
options:
  - value: bridge
    label: BRIDGE
    tap_action:
      action: navigate
      navigation_path: /lovelace/bridge
  - value: engineering
    label: ENGINEERING
    tap_action:
      action: navigate
      navigation_path: /lovelace/engineering
```

## Layouts and Presets

**`preset` picks the button look for every option, and `grid` arranges them.** A few layouts and presets against a sample `input_select` (tap an option to select it):

## Card Options

**The select menu's own top-level keys.** Each block has its own page; this table links to it.

- The card also takes the keys every LCARdS card takes (`height`, `width`, `overflow`, `z_index`, `grid_options`, `id`, `tags`, `data_sources` ...): see [Common card properties](../common).
- In a sections view the card asks for enough rows to show every option ([Grid and Sizing](./layout#sizing-in-a-dashboard)).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-select-menu
entity: input_select.lcards_test_mode
preset: bullet
grid:
  columns: 3
hold_action:
  action: more-info
```

::: details More about the entity
- **Domains:** `input_select.*` options are set with `input_select.select_option`, and `select.*` options with `select.select_option`.
- **Loading:** while the configured entity is not in Home Assistant, the card shows "Loading…" instead of buttons.
- **No entity:** the card cannot list options or show which one is selected, so it needs array-form `options`, and a tap does nothing unless the option or the card sets a `tap_action`.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `type` | string | required | `custom:lcards-select-menu` |
| `entity` | string | - | The `input_select` or `select` entity whose options become buttons and whose state marks the selected one |
| `preset` | string | - | The [button preset](../button/#presets) every option button uses (`lozenge`, `bullet`, `capped`, `outline`, `toggle-tab` ...) |
| `grid` | object | one column | How the buttons are arranged: see [grid](./layout#grid) |
| `options` | object / list | the entity's options | Labels, icons, styles and actions per option, and which options show: see [options](./options#options) |
| `style` | object | from the preset | Colours, text and borders for every option: see [style](./styles#style) |
| `button_template` | object | - | Any other button card keys for every option: see [button_template](./styles#button-template) |
| `tap_action` | object | select the option | Replaces the tap of every option: see [Actions](./options#actions) |
| `hold_action` | object | `action: none` | Hold action for every option |
| `double_tap_action` | object | `action: none` | Double-tap action for every option |

# Grid and Sizing

How the option buttons are arranged, and how tall the card is in a dashboard or inside a layout.

## grid

**`grid` arranges the option buttons as a CSS grid: how many columns, the gaps between buttons and the height of each row.** Most menus need only `columns` and `gap`.

- `columns` takes a number for equal columns, or any CSS `grid-template-columns` value for columns of different widths (`100px 1fr 2fr`).
- Each row is `56px` high unless you set `grid-auto-rows`, and the buttons fill their cells. To place smaller buttons in their cells, give them a size in `button_template` (`width`, `height`) and set `justify-items` or `align-items`.
- `rows` sets a number of rows (each `grid-auto-rows` high) or a CSS `grid-template-rows` track list. With the default row flow, options beyond those rows add more.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-select-menu
entity: input_select.demo_mode
preset: lozenge
grid:
  columns: 2
  gap: 6px
  grid-auto-rows: 44px
```

::: details More about grid
- **Column flow:** with `grid-auto-flow: column` the options fill each column top to bottom, so set `rows`: without it every option goes in one row.
- **Gap aliases:** `row_gap` and `column_gap` are accepted as other spellings of `row-gap` and `column-gap`; the dashed key wins when both are set.
- **Other CSS grid keys:** the card builds the grid from the keys in this table only; other CSS grid properties under `grid` have no effect.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `grid.columns` | number / string | `1` | Number of equal-width columns (1 to 24), or a CSS `grid-template-columns` value |
| `grid.grid-template-columns` | string | - | A CSS `grid-template-columns` value; wins over `columns` |
| `grid.gap` | string | `4px` | Gap between rows and between columns |
| `grid.row-gap` | string | `gap` | Gap between rows; `row_gap` is an alias |
| `grid.column-gap` | string | `gap` | Gap between columns; `column_gap` is an alias |
| `grid.grid-auto-rows` | string | `56px` | Row height, such as `48px`, `minmax(40px, 56px)` or `auto` |
| `grid.grid-auto-flow` | string | `row` | `row`, `column`, `dense`, `row dense` or `column dense` |
| `grid.rows` | number / string | - | A number of rows, each `grid-auto-rows` high, or a CSS `grid-template-rows` value |
| `grid.justify-items` | string | `stretch` | Each button's place across its cell: `stretch`, `start`, `end` or `center`. Places buttons with a `button_template.width`; without one they fill the cell across |
| `grid.align-items` | string | `stretch` | Each button's place down its cell: `stretch`, `start`, `end` or `center`. Places buttons with a `button_template.height`; without one they fill the cell down |
| `grid.height` | string | natural | `fit` or `100%`: see [Height modes](#height-modes) |

## Sizing in a Dashboard

**In a sections view the card asks Home Assistant for enough grid rows to show every option.** It works the rows out from the number of options, the columns, `grid.rows`, the row height and the row gap.

- The row height it counts is `grid-auto-rows` in pixels (the larger value of `minmax(Apx, Bpx)`), or `56px` for anything else. A pixel track in `grid.rows` counts as given.
- A pixel `height` on the card sizes it instead, and your own `grid_options.rows` always wins.
- The card asks for 4 grid columns unless `grid_options.columns` says otherwise. In a masonry view it reports one unit per row of options (or its pixel `height` in 50 px units).

```yaml live
# 8 options in 4 columns: 2 rows, so a 2-row cell
type: custom:lcards-select-menu
entity: input_select.deck
preset: capped
grid:
  columns: 4
  gap: 4px
options:
  - value: bridge
    label: BRIDGE
  - value: engineering
    label: ENGINEERING
  - value: sickbay
    label: SICKBAY
  - value: tactical
    label: TACTICAL
  - value: science
    label: SCIENCE
  - value: cargo
    label: CARGO
  - value: shuttle
    label: SHUTTLE BAY
  - value: holodeck
    label: HOLODECK
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `height` | number / string | - | A fixed card height; a pixel value also sets the rows the card asks for. See [Sizing](../common#sizing) |
| `grid_options.rows` | number | enough for every option | Rows in a sections view; wins over the card's own count |
| `grid_options.columns` | number | `4` | Columns in a sections view; the card can't be resized below 2 |

## Height modes

**`grid.height` lets a menu inside a layout size its parent's row, or fill a row the parent sizes.** Leave it out and the option grid is as tall as its rows, and the card flows like normal content.

- `fit` gives the card a fixed pixel height worked out from the config (rows × row height + gaps, the same count as [Sizing in a Dashboard](#sizing-in-a-dashboard)), so a parent row sized to its content (`auto` or `minmax(0, max-content)`) can follow it exactly. Measuring the menu through Home Assistant's card wrapper is unreliable; a definite height always works. It needs a pixel `grid-auto-rows` (`Npx` or `minmax(Apx, Bpx)`, which counts the larger value).
- `100%` makes the option grid fill the height its container gives it. With a pixel `grid-auto-rows`, the card measures the container and shares it between the rows (not the options: 4 options in 2 columns are 2 rows), within the bounds; with a flexible maximum such as `minmax(40px, 1fr)`, CSS shares the height out.
- For a fixed card height with scrolling, use the card's own `height` and `overflow_y` instead.

This sidebar is the pattern the shell strategy uses: the menu's row hugs the menu, and a filler panel takes the rest.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
height: 300
layout:
  grid-template-columns: 1fr
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, max-content)
  grid-auto-rows: minmax(40px, 1fr)
  grid-gap: 5px
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-select-menu
    entity: input_select.demo_mode
    preset: lozenge
    grid:
      columns: 1
      gap: 5px
      grid-auto-rows: minmax(40px, 56px)
      height: fit
    view_layout:
      # scrolls inside the menu if the container is too short
      overflow-y: auto
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-dark
    # lets the filler shrink with its row
    min_height: 1
```

::: details More about height modes
- **The parent row:** `minmax(0, max-content)` tracks the menu's published height exactly, capped by the container; the filler row (`minmax(40px, 1fr)`) takes the rest.
- **Buttons in rows that shrink:** set a small `min_height` on them. Without one, the button preset's minimum height (56 px from the theme) keeps them painting at full size even in a collapsed row.
- **100% when even the minimum does not fit:** the buttons stay at the minimum row height and the option grid scrolls inside the card instead of spilling into the layout. Until the container has been measured (the first frame), the grid clips.
- **Other values:** `grid.height` takes only `fit` and `100%`; anything else is ignored.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `grid.height` | string | - | Unset: as tall as the rows. `fit`: a fixed pixel height from the config. `100%`: fill the container |
| `grid.grid-auto-rows` | string | `56px` | Must be `Npx` or `minmax(Apx, Bpx)` for `fit`, and for `100%` to pick the row height itself |

# Options and Actions

Which buttons the menu shows, what each one says, and what happens when you tap, hold or double-tap one. Colours and text for every option are on [Styles](./styles).

## options

**`options` changes the buttons: their labels, icons, styles and actions, and which options show.** Leave it out and the card shows every option of the entity, labelled with its value, in the entity's order.

- `options` takes two forms. As a map keyed by option value ([object form](#object-form)) it changes some options and keeps the entity's list. As a list ([array form](#array-form)) it is the list: only those options show, in that order.
- Option values are case-sensitive: `Off` and `off` are different options. Quote values YAML would read as something else, such as `"Off"` or `"On"`.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-select-menu
entity: input_select.demo_mode
preset: lozenge
grid:
  columns: 2
  gap: 6px
options:
  Auto:
    label: AUTOMATIC
  Heat:
    label: WARM
    style:
      card:
        color:
          background:
            active: var(--lcars-red)
            inactive: var(--lcars-dark-red)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `options` | object / list | the entity's options | Object form: changes per option, entity order kept. List: the options to show, in order |
| [Per-option fields](#per-option-fields) | | | `value`, `label`, `icon`, `style`, `tap_action`, `hold_action`, `double_tap_action` |

### Object form

**A map keyed by option value changes just the options you name; every other option still shows with its defaults.** The buttons stay in the entity's order.

- A key that is not one of the entity's options is ignored, so the object form cannot add buttons. Use the [array form](#array-form) for that.
- The object form needs an entity: without one there is no option list to change, and the card shows nothing.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-select-menu
entity: input_select.lcards_test_mode
preset: capped
grid:
  columns: 3
  gap: 4px
options:
  alpha:
    label: ALPHA SHIFT
  gamma:
    label: GAMMA SHIFT
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `options.<value>` | object | - | Changes for the option with this value: the [per-option fields](#per-option-fields) except `value` |

### Array form

**A list of options sets exactly which buttons show and in what order.** Options of the entity you leave out are hidden, and an entry the entity does not have still shows.

- Every entry needs `value`. With an entity, the button whose `value` matches the entity's state is the selected one.
- Use the array form for a manual menu without an entity: give each entry its own `tap_action` (or set one for the whole card), because without an entity a tap does nothing by default.

```yaml live
# Reordered, and Off left out
type: custom:lcards-select-menu
entity: input_select.demo_mode
preset: bullet
grid:
  columns: 3
  gap: 4px
options:
  - value: Heat
    label: HEAT
  - value: Cool
    label: COOL
  - value: Auto
    label: AUTO
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `options[].value` | string | required | The option this button stands for |
| [Per-option fields](#per-option-fields) | | | `label`, `icon`, `style` and the actions |

### Per-option fields

**The keys one option takes, in either form.** A per-option key wins over the same key set for the whole card.

- `icon` adds an icon area to that button only; options without an icon keep the whole button for their label.
- A per-option `style` has the same shape as the card's [style](./styles#style) and merges over it key by key.
- The card-level keys `rules`, `sounds`, `variables`, `zones` and `debug_zones` go to that option's button, so its label can use its own `variables`.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-select-menu
entity: input_select.demo_mode
preset: lozenge
grid:
  columns: 2
  gap: 6px
options:
  - value: Auto
    label: AUTO
    icon: mdi:thermostat-auto
  - value: Cool
    label: COOL
    icon: mdi:snowflake
    style:
      card:
        color:
          background:
            inactive: var(--lcars-blue)
  - value: Heat
    label: "{variables.mode}"
    icon: mdi:fire
    variables:
      mode: WARM
  - value: "Off"
    label: STANDBY
    hold_action:
      action: more-info
```

::: details More about per-option fields
- **Per-option style merges:** an option's `style` changes only the keys it sets; the card's other colours, text and border settings stay.
- **Card-level keys:** an option's `variables`, `zones` and `sounds` merge over the same keys in [`button_template`](./styles#button-template), and its `rules` load after the template's. Rules are global: an option's rule can target any card by its `id` or `tags`.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | string | required in a list | The option value. In object form the key is the value |
| `label` | string | the value | Text on the button |
| `icon` | string | - | An icon such as `mdi:home` (or `si:github`); sets `show_icon: true` for this button |
| `style` | object | the card's `style` | Style for this button: same keys as [style](./styles#style) |
| `tap_action` | object | the card's | Tap action for this button: see [Actions](#actions) |
| `hold_action` | object | the card's | Hold action for this button |
| `double_tap_action` | object | the card's | Double-tap action for this button |
| `variables` | object | - | Your own values for this button's templates (`{variables.<name>}`): see [Variables](../common#variables) |
| `rules` | list | - | Rules this button loads: see [Rules Engine](../../core/rules/) |
| `sounds` | object | - | Sound overrides for this button: see [Card Sounds](../../core/sounds.md) |
| `zones` | object | - | Named areas on this button that text fields and animations can target |
| `debug_zones` | boolean | `false` | Outline this button's zones |

## Actions

**A tap selects the option; you can replace that for one option, for the whole card, or in the button template.** Hold and double-tap do nothing unless you set them.

- For each of the three actions, the first one set in this order wins: the option's own, the card's, the [button template](./styles#button-template)'s, then the built-in default.
- The built-in tap calls `input_select.select_option` (or `select.select_option` for a `select.*` entity) with the option's value. Without an entity there is no built-in tap.
- Hold and double-tap default to `action: none`, so a hold never falls through to the tap and selects an option by accident.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-select-menu
entity: input_select.lcards_test_mode
preset: capped
grid:
  columns: 3
  gap: 4px
# every option: hold for more information
hold_action:
  action: more-info
options:
  - value: alpha
    label: ALPHA
  - value: beta
    label: BETA
  # this option navigates instead of selecting
  - value: gamma
    label: SETTINGS
    tap_action:
      action: navigate
      navigation_path: /config
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `tap_action` | object | select the option | Any [action](../../core/actions.md); on the card it replaces the tap of every option without its own |
| `hold_action` | object | `action: none` | Any [action](../../core/actions.md) |
| `double_tap_action` | object | `action: none` | Any [action](../../core/actions.md) |

# Select Menu Playground

Edit the YAML and the card redraws as you type. Pick a starting point (options from an input_select, or custom labels), then change the preset or the grid.

**You don't need to know the YAML to start:**

- **Quick settings** above the editor change the most common options for you.
- **Type in the editor** and it suggests the options that fit where your cursor is, with a short description. Press **Ctrl+Space** to see suggestions anywhere, and hover over a key to read what it does.
- **Options here** (under the editor) lists everything you can add at the cursor. **Insert** adds it at the right indent, and **Docs** opens its section in a new tab.

<ClientOnly>

</ClientOnly>

## How the preview works

The preview is the real select menu card, the same code your dashboard runs. The docs site has no Home Assistant, so:

- **Entities get sample values.** The entities listed under the preview are always there, and any other entity id in your YAML gets a plausible value for its domain (lights and switches are on, sensors get a number with a unit).
- **Taps that toggle** switch the sample entity, so state colours change as on a dashboard. **More info**, **navigate** and other actions say what they would do instead.
- **Jinja2 templates** (`{{ ... }}`) need Home Assistant and render empty here; `{entity.state}` tokens and `[[[ JavaScript ]]]` templates work.
- **Icons** aren't drawn (Home Assistant provides them), and sounds are off.

Messages under the card show schema warnings for your YAML.

When it looks right, **Copy YAML** and paste it into your card's YAML editor, then swap in your own entities.

# Styles

How the option buttons look: colours for the selected and the other options, text and borders, and any other button card key through the button template.

## style

**`style` sets the colours, text and borders of every option button, on top of the preset.** It has the same shape as the [button card's style](../button/styles), so a colour can be a state map.

- In a state map, `active` is the selected option and `inactive` the others. `hover` and `pressed` apply while the pointer is over a button or pressing it, `unavailable` when the entity is unavailable, and `default` on a menu without an entity.
- Each layer wins over the one before, key by key: the preset, then `button_template.style`, then the card's `style`, then the option's own [`style`](./options#per-option-fields), then [rules](#rules-engine).
- `opacity` dims every option but the selected one, so the selection stands out.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-select-menu
entity: input_select.demo_mode
preset: lozenge
grid:
  columns: 4
  gap: 6px
style:
  card:
    color:
      background:
        active: var(--lcars-orange)
        inactive: var(--lcars-dark-gray)
  text:
    default:
      color:
        active: var(--lcars-black)
        inactive: var(--lcards-moonlight)
      font_size: 18
      font_weight: 700
  border:
    radius: 6
  opacity: 0.6
```

::: details More about style
- **Layers merge key by key:** a later layer changes only the keys it sets. A card `style.card.color.background.active` keeps the template's `inactive` colour, and an option's `style.border.width` keeps the card's colours.
- **One value or a state map:** a colour given as one value in one layer and as a state map in a later one is replaced by the map, so the states the map leaves out fall back to the theme.
- **Per-side borders:** a per-side `border.width` or per-corner `border.radius` object in a later layer keeps the earlier layer's single value on the sides it leaves out.
- **Opacity:** `opacity` applies to the whole option button. Without an `entity` no option is selected, so it applies to none.
- **Rules:** a rule patches the card's style through its `id` or `tags`, over every other layer: see [Rules Engine](#rules-engine).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.card.color.background` | colour / state map | from the preset | Button fill |
| `style.text.default.color` | colour / state map | from the preset | Label colour |
| `style.text.default.font_size` | number / string | from the preset | Label size, px or a CSS size |
| `style.text.default.font_weight` | number / string | from the preset | CSS font weight |
| `style.text.default.text_transform` | string | from the preset | `uppercase`, `lowercase`, `capitalize` or `none` |
| `style.text.default.letter_spacing` | string | - | CSS letter spacing, such as `0.1em` or `2px` |
| `style.border.radius` | number / string | from the preset | Corner radius, px or a CSS value |
| `style.border.radius.top_left` | number | from the preset | One corner, px; likewise `top_right`, `bottom_right` and `bottom_left` |
| `style.border.width` | number / string | from the preset | Border width, px |
| `style.border.color` | colour / state map | from the preset | Border colour |
| `style.opacity` | number | `1` | Opacity of every option but the selected one, 0 to 1 |

## Text Layer Visibility

**Each button shows the option's label and nothing else: the card hides the button's `name` and `state` text fields.** The label is the button's `text.label` field, centred.

- To show `name` or `state` as well, turn them on in `button_template.text`. By default `name` is the entity's friendly name and `state` its state (the selected option); the template's `content` sets other text, templates included.
- Any other text setting in the template (`font_size`, `position`, `color` ...) applies too. The label's text is always the option's `label`, whatever the template says.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-select-menu
entity: input_select.demo_mode
preset: lozenge
grid:
  columns: 2
  gap: 6px
  grid-auto-rows: 64px
button_template:
  text:
    label:
      font_size: 20
    name:
      show: true
      content: MODE
    state:
      show: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `button_template.text.label.show` | boolean | `true` | The option's label; its text is always the option's `label` |
| `button_template.text.name.show` | boolean | `false` | The button's name field |
| `button_template.text.state.show` | boolean | `false` | The button's state field |
| `button_template.text.label.font_size` | number / string | from the preset | The label's size; the label's other text settings work the same way |

## button_template

**`button_template` is a [button card](../button/) config that every option starts from.** Use it for button keys the select menu does not have itself: textures, sounds, animations, padding, more text fields.

- The card, the option and the card's own keys are applied over it, so `type`, `entity`, `preset`, `state_classification` and the label's text always come from the select menu. `id` and `tags` in the template are dropped: the menu's own go to the rules engine.
- An `icon` in the template shows on every option without its own `icon`.
- The editor's Style tab opens the button editor on this template.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-select-menu
entity: input_select.demo_mode
preset: outline
grid:
  columns: 2
  gap: 6px
button_template:
  shape_texture:
    preset: scanlines
    opacity: 0.25
    config:
      line_spacing: 4
      color: var(--lcars-orange)
```

::: details More about button_template
- **Actions in the template:** `tap_action`, `hold_action` and `double_tap_action` in the template are the last choice before the built-in default: see [Actions](./options#actions).
- **Style in the template:** `button_template.style` is the first layer of [style](#style), under the card's and the option's.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `button_template` | object | - | Any [button card](../button/#card-options) keys for every option |
| `button_template.style` | object | - | Style under the card's `style` |
| `button_template.text` | object | - | Text fields; `name` and `state` are hidden unless shown here |
| `button_template.icon` | string | - | Icon for every option without its own |

## Rules Engine

**The card registers with the rules engine as type `select-menu`, so a rule can target it by its `id`, its `tags` or its type.** Rules are written in any card's `rules` list: see the [Rules Engine](../../core/rules/) page.

- The card's tags for rules are `select-menu` plus its own `tags`; without an `id` it gets a generated one.
- A rule's `style` patch applies to every option button, over the card's and the options' own style. When the rule stops matching, the buttons go back to their style.
- An option can carry its own `rules` list too: see [Per-option fields](./options#per-option-fields).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-select-menu
entity: input_select.demo_mode
preset: lozenge
id: deck-nav
tags:
  - nav
grid:
  columns: 2
  gap: 6px
rules:
  - id: away-recolours-nav
    when:
      entity: binary_sensor.away_mode
      state: "on"
    apply:
      overlays:
        tag:nav:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background:
                  active: var(--lcars-red)
                  inactive: var(--lcars-gray)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | generated | The card's id for rule selectors |
| `tags` | list | - | Tags for `tag:` selectors |
| `rules` | list | - | Rules this card loads: see [Rules Engine](../../core/rules/) |

## Full Example

**A six-deck navigation menu: three columns of fixed-height lozenges with icons, wide-spaced labels and one style for the card.** The array form lists the decks in the order you want.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-select-menu
entity: input_select.deck_view
preset: lozenge
id: deck-nav
tags:
  - nav
grid:
  columns: 3
  gap: 6px
  grid-auto-rows: 52px
style:
  border:
    radius: 14
  text:
    default:
      font_size: 14
      letter_spacing: 0.08em
      text_transform: uppercase
options:
  - value: bridge
    label: BRIDGE
    icon: mdi:bridge
  - value: engineering
    label: ENGINEERING
    icon: mdi:engine
  - value: sickbay
    label: SICKBAY
    icon: mdi:medical-bag
  - value: tactical
    label: TACTICAL
    icon: mdi:radar
  - value: holodecks
    label: HOLODECKS
    icon: mdi:virtual-reality
  - value: science
    label: SCIENCE
    icon: mdi:flask
```

# Slider Card

`custom:lcards-slider`

**A slider you drag to set a light, cover, fan, thermostat or volume, or a read-only gauge for a sensor.** It comes in four looks: pill bars, ruler gauges, shaped fills and ring gauges.

- Most sliders need only `entity` and `preset`. The card works out from the entity what to control and over what range.
- In a sections view each look asks for a cell that fits it (a pill bar 1 row, a ring 4, Picard 7); `grid_options` changes it.

::: tip Try it
- The card editor's tabs cover the options on these pages, with a live preview.
- The [Playground](./playground) lets you edit slider YAML here in the docs and see the result.
:::

| Page | Covers |
|------|--------|
| [Pills and Gauges](./styles) | The pill bar and ruler gauge: track, ticks, labels, indicator, borders, text |
| [Ring, Shaped and Picard](./components) | The ring gauge, shaped fills and the Picard gauge |
| [Ranges and Markers](./ranges) | Coloured value bands and live markers on the track |
| [Control and Motion](./control) | What it controls, min and max, value easing, the drag badge |
| [Playground](./playground) | Edit YAML and see the slider live |

---

## Quick start

**Two examples to start from: a light you drag, and a sensor shown as a gauge.**

- `style.track.display` sets the scale a gauge shows. What a slider can set is `control.min` and `control.max`, which come from the entity unless you change them ([Control and Motion](./control#control-options)).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: light.bedroom
preset: pills-left-border
```

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: sensor.temperature
preset: gauge-basic
style:
  track:
    display:
      min: -10
      max: 40
      unit: "°C"
```

## Presets

**`preset` picks the look.** Every preset is shown here against a sample light; drag one to set its brightness.

- A preset is a starting point: any `style` key you set overrides it.
- Without a preset, lights, covers, fans, climate and the other draggable domains draw pills, and everything else (sensors) draws a gauge.

| Preset | Look |
|--------|------|
| `pills-basic` | Segmented pill bar |
| `pills-left-border` | Pill bar with an LCARS cap on the left |
| `pills-left-border-rounded` | Pill bar with a left cap and a rounded right end |
| `gauge-basic` | Ruler gauge: tick marks, labels and a fill bar |
| `gauge-left-border` | Ruler gauge with a left cap |
| `gauge-left-border-rounded` | Ruler gauge with a left cap and a rounded right end |
| `shaped-vertical` | Upright lozenge fill with text above and below ([shaped](./components#shaped-component)) |
| `shaped-horizontal` | Flat lozenge fill with text left and right ([shaped](./components#shaped-component)) |
| `ring` | Three-quarter ring, name above a large value ([ring](./components#ring-gauge)) |
| `picard-ring` | Near-full thick ring with flat ends ([ring](./components#ring-gauge)) |
| `picard-gauge-vertical` | Picard-style upright gauge ([Picard](./components#picard-component)) |
| `picard-gauge-column` | Picard-era column gauge: number caps at both ends, a thin value bar and a small oval thumb ([gauge](./styles#style-gauge)) |

## Card options

**The slider's own top-level keys.** Each block has its own page; this table links to it.

- The slider also takes the keys every LCARdS card takes (`height`, `grid_options`, `id`, `tags`, `tap_action`, `animations`, `sounds`, `data_sources` ...): see [Common card properties](../common).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: light.bedroom
preset: gauge-left-border
control:
  min: 10 # never dimmer than 10 %
drag_badge:
  enabled: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `entity` | string | - | The entity to show and control. Its domain sets what the slider controls and its range: see [Control and Motion](./control#automatic-domain-behaviour) |
| `preset` | string | pills or gauge, by domain | The look: see [Presets](#presets) |
| `control` | object | by domain | The range, the step, read-only, inverted: see [Control options](./control#control-options) |
| `text` | object | from the preset | Text on the card: the name, the value, your own labels. See [Text labels](./styles#text-labels) |
| `style` | object | from the preset | Overrides for the preset: the [track and gauge](./styles), [ranges](./ranges), [ring, shaped and Picard](./components), [borders](./styles#style-border) |
| `component` | string | from the preset | `shaped`, `ring` or `picard` without a preset that sets it |
| `value_tween` | object | on | Eases the fill and markers to a new value when the entity changes: see [Value tween](./control#value-tween). Off when the device asks for reduced motion |
| `drag_badge` | object | off | A badge with the live value while you drag: see [Drag value badge](./control#drag-value-badge) |
| `ranges_attribute` | string | - | The attribute that [range colours](/core/colours/attributes#ranges-attribute) compare, for entities whose state is not a number |
| `state_attribute` | string | - | The attribute whose value picks [exact-match colours](/core/colours/attributes#state-attribute) |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/slider-card/components.html -->

# Ring, Shaped and Picard

**Three looks that draw their own shape instead of a [pill bar or ruler](./styles).** Use them when a plain bar is not the look you want: a round dial, a filled lozenge or a framed Picard-era gauge.

- Pick one with a preset, or set `component` yourself to combine it with another preset.
- They draw to the card's cell. In a sections view each asks for a cell that fits it: a ring 4 rows, Picard 7 rows by 6 columns, an upright slider 4 rows by 3 columns. `grid_options` changes it.

| `component` | Presets | Looks like |
|---|---|---|
| `ring` | `ring`, `picard-ring` | A thick arc round a large value: [Ring gauge](#ring-gauge) |
| `shaped` | `shaped-vertical`, `shaped-horizontal` | A solid fill inside a shape: [Shaped component](#shaped-component) |
| `picard` | `picard-gauge-vertical` | A framed upright gauge with scanning lights: [Picard component](#picard-component) |

---

## Ring gauge

**A round dial: drag round the ring, or tap a point on it, to set the value.** Use it for a light, a thermostat or any number you want to read at a glance.

- Angles are in degrees, with `0` at the top, counted clockwise. The default runs from `-135` to `135`, which leaves the gap at the bottom.
- Set `-90` to `90` for a half ring, or the same angle twice for a full ring.
- The ring is read-only for sensors, or when `control.locked: true` is set.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: light.bedroom
preset: ring
style:
  ring:
    thickness: 16%
    fill:
      color: var(--lcards-blue)
```

::: details More about the ring
- **Keyboard:** the arrow keys change the value by one `control.step` while the ring has focus (Page Up and Page Down by ten, Home and End to the ends). A press on the centre text does nothing.
- **Size:** the ring stays round and is as large as its arc allows. A full ring fills the card's smaller side; a half ring fills a card twice as wide as it is tall. The centre text stays inside the arc (above the cut on a half ring).
- **Wrapping:** an end angle at or before the start wraps round.
- **Ranges:** [range](./ranges) bands draw as arcs over the track, under the value arc, at full opacity unless the range sets `opacity`.
- **Other track keys:** `style.track.invert_fill` grows the value from the end angle back to the start. The [drag badge](./control#drag-value-badge) sits in the centre. Borders and track margins don't apply.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style.ring.start_angle` | number | `-135` | Where the minimum sits, degrees (0 = top, clockwise) |
| `style.ring.end_angle` | number | `135` | Where the maximum sits; equal to `start_angle` draws a full ring |
| `style.ring.thickness` | number / string | `12%` | Band thickness: a percentage of the diameter (`12%`) or px (`14`, `14px`) |
| `style.ring.cap` | string | `round` | Arc ends: `round` or `flat` |
| `style.ring.fill.color` | colour / state map | theme | Value arc colour; a [state map](/core/colours) works |
| `style.ring.track.color` | colour / state map | theme | Unfilled ring colour; a state map works |
| `style.ring.padding` | number | auto | Room outside the ring for the scale, markers and their labels, px. Worked out from them when unset |
| `style.ring.focus_ring` | boolean | `false` | Outline the ring while it has keyboard focus; the keys work either way |
| `style.ring.scale` | object | - | Ticks and labels outside the ring: see [Scale](#scale) |

### The picard-ring preset

**The Picard-era ring: a near-full thick ring with flat ends, a small label over a large number.** Use it for zone and level readouts in the Protostar style.

- It is still `component: ring`, so every ring key, [Scale](#scale) and [value marker](#value-markers) works on it.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: input_number.target_level
preset: picard-ring
text:
  name:
    content: Zone N
style:
  ring:
    scale:
      tick_marks:
        major:
          interval: 20
        minor:
          interval: 5
      labels:
        show_unit: false
  # a red band at the top of the range
  ranges:
    - min: 80
      max: 100
      color: theme:colors.status.error
```

Ring variants (drag any of them):

::: details More about picard-ring
- **What it sets:** `start_angle: -165`, `end_angle: 165`, `thickness: 20%` and `cap: flat`, with a half-transparent track. The name is upper case, in the fill colour, over a large state.
- **The `ring` preset** sets `-135` to `135`, `thickness: 12%` and round caps, with the name small above a large state.
:::

### Scale

**Ticks and value labels round the outside of the ring, so you can read a value off the dial.** They work like the gauge's [`scale`](./styles#style-gauge) and take the same keys.

- A plain ring has no scale. Each part shows once its block is set: the major ticks, the minor ticks or the labels.
- The labels sit at the major tick interval. Minor ticks are left out where a major tick falls, and the end of a full ring gets no tick, since it is the same point as the start.
- The ring shrinks to make room for the scale. Set `style.ring.padding` to choose that room yourself, for example to line up several rings.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: light.bedroom
preset: ring
style:
  ring:
    start_angle: -120
    end_angle: 120
    scale:
      tick_marks:
        major:
          interval: 25
          height: 10
          color: var(--lcards-orange)
        minor:
          interval: 5
      labels:
        show_unit: false
        font_size: 13
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style.ring.scale.tick_marks.major.interval` | number | `10` | Value units between major ticks, counted from the minimum |
| `style.ring.scale.tick_marks.major.height` | number | `8` | Tick length, px, outward from the ring |
| `style.ring.scale.tick_marks.major.width` | number | `2` | Tick line width, px |
| `style.ring.scale.tick_marks.major.color` | colour / state map | theme | Major tick colour |
| `style.ring.scale.tick_marks.major.enabled` | boolean | `true` | `false` hides the major ticks while keeping the block |
| `style.ring.scale.tick_marks.minor.interval` | number | `2` | Value units between minor ticks |
| `style.ring.scale.tick_marks.minor.height` | number | `4` | Tick length, px |
| `style.ring.scale.tick_marks.minor.width` | number | `1` | Tick line width, px |
| `style.ring.scale.tick_marks.minor.color` | colour / state map | theme | Minor tick colour |
| `style.ring.scale.tick_marks.minor.enabled` | boolean | `true` | `false` hides the minor ticks while keeping the block |
| `style.ring.scale.labels.show_unit` | boolean | `true` | Add the unit to each label |
| `style.ring.scale.labels.unit` | string | entity unit | Unit to add; wins over the entity's unit |
| `style.ring.scale.labels.color` | colour / state map | theme | Label colour |
| `style.ring.scale.labels.font_size` | number | `12` | Label size, px |
| `style.ring.scale.labels.padding` | number | `3` | Gap between the ticks and the labels, px |
| `style.ring.scale.labels.enabled` | boolean | `true` | `false` hides the labels while keeping the block |

### Value markers

**A [range](./ranges) with a `value` instead of `min` and `max` draws a marker at that value on the ring.** Use it to show a second number on the dial, such as the current temperature against the target.

- A marker takes its colour from the range's `color`, or `indicator.color` when set.
- A marker and its label move with [value tweens](./control#value-tween).
- The label sits outside the ring, past the marker and past the scale, so it never lands on a scale label.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: climate.living_room
preset: ring
control:
  min: 10
  max: 30
  step: 0.5
text:
  state:
    content: "{entity.attributes.temperature}°"
style:
  ring:
    scale:
      tick_marks:
        major:
          interval: 5
      labels:
        show_unit: false
  ranges:
    # the room's current temperature, the dial shows the target
    - value: "{entity.attributes.current_temperature}"
      indicator:
        type: triangle
        color: theme:colors.status.success
      label:
        text: NOW
```

::: details More about value markers
- **Placement:** `indicator.align` anchors a marker at the inner edge of the band (`start`), its middle (`center`) or its outer edge (`end`). A triangle at `start` sits inside the ring and points out; elsewhere it points in.
- **Size:** `size.width` runs round the ring and `size.height` along the radius. A `round` dot uses `width` for both.
- **Ignored here:** `indicator.rotation` and `indicator.offset.x` don't apply on a ring; the marker always turns with the ring.
- **All range keys:** the [ranges page](./ranges#value-marker-fields) lists every marker key; the rows below are how the ring reads them.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style.ranges[].value` | number / string | required | The value to mark: a number or a template such as `{entity.attributes.current_temperature}` |
| `indicator.type` | string | `line` | `line`: a line across the band. `triangle`: outside the ring, pointing in. `round`: a dot on the band |
| `indicator.align` | string | by type | `start`, `center` or `end`. A line starts at `start`, a triangle at `end`, a dot at `center` |
| `indicator.color` | colour / state map | the range's `color` | Marker colour. Without either, `style.gauge.marker_indicator.color`, then the theme |
| `indicator.size.width` | number | by type | Size round the ring, px. Line: about a fifth of the band (at least 2). Triangle: `12`. Dot: half the band (at least 6) |
| `indicator.size.height` | number | by type | Size along the radius, px. Line: the band plus 6. Triangle: `10`. Not used by a dot |
| `indicator.offset.y` | number | `0` | Move the marker outward, px; negative moves it inward |
| `indicator.border.enabled` | boolean | `false` | Outline a triangle or dot |
| `indicator.border.color` | colour / state map | theme | Outline colour |
| `indicator.border.width` | number | `1` | Outline width, px |
| `label.text` | string | - | Caption outside the ring; templates work |
| `label.color` | colour / state map | theme | Caption colour |
| `label.font_size` | number | `12` | Caption size, px |
| `label.offset.x` | number | `0` | Move the caption sideways, px |
| `label.offset.y` | number | `0` | Move the caption down, px; negative moves it up |

### Centre text

**Four text zones inside the ring hold the name, the value and anything else you add.** Use them to move a field, for example to put the name under a half ring.

- The zones are `label` (above the value), `value` (the middle), `sublabel` (below) and `center` (the whole inner area).
- The presets put `name` in `label` and `state` in `value`. Size text with `font_size_percent` (see [zones](/core/text-fields-style#filling-a-zone)), so it grows and shrinks with the ring.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: light.bedroom
preset: ring
style:
  ring:
    start_angle: -90
    end_angle: 90
    thickness: 20%
    cap: flat          # round caps would poke below the half ring
text:
  # the name under the half ring
  name:
    zone: sublabel
    position: top
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text.<field>.zone` | string | preset | `label`, `value`, `sublabel` or `center`. The ring presets use `label` for `name` and `value` for `state` |
| `text.<field>.position` | string | preset | Where the text sits inside its zone, such as `top`, `center` or `bottom` |
| `text.<field>.font_size_percent` | number | preset | Text height as a percentage of the zone's height (1–100). The `ring` preset uses 60 for the name and 85 for the state |

## Shaped component

**A solid fill inside a shape: a lozenge, hexagon, diamond or your own outline.** Use it for a level, a volume or a brightness that should read as a filled container.

- Pick it with the `shaped-vertical` or `shaped-horizontal` preset. They set the orientation, the text bands and where the name and state go; with `component: shaped` alone, also set `style.track.orientation`.
- The text sits in bands outside the shape: top and bottom when upright, left and right when flat. Send a text field to one with `zone: top`, `bottom`, `left` or `right`.
- [Range](./ranges) bands draw inside the shape, under the fill, at full opacity unless the range sets `opacity`. Value markers are not drawn.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: light.bedroom
preset: shaped-horizontal
style:
  shaped:
    type: hexagon
    fill:
      color: var(--lcards-blue)
    track:
      background: var(--lcards-gray-darkest)
    text_bands:
      left:
        size: 110
      right:
        size: 70
```

::: details More about shaped
- **Your own shape:** `type: polygon` takes its corners in `polygon.points`, each `[x, y]` a fraction (0–1) of the shape's width and height, for example `[[0, 0], [1, 0.5], [0, 1]]` for a triangle. `type: path` takes an SVG path in `path.d`.
- **Empty bands:** a band set to `0` is not a text zone, so a field sent there has nowhere to go.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style.shaped.type` | string | `lozenge` | `lozenge`, `rect`, `rounded`, `diamond`, `hexagon`, `polygon` or `path` |
| `style.shaped.radius` | number | auto | Corner radius, px, for `lozenge` (half the shorter side) and `rounded` (`8`) |
| `style.shaped.fill.color` | colour / state map | theme | The filled part; a [state map](/core/colours) works. Falls back to `style.gauge.fill.color.active` |
| `style.shaped.track.background` | colour / state map | theme | The empty part; a state map works. Falls back to `style.track.background` |
| `style.shaped.text_bands.top.size` | number | `36` | Top text band height, px (upright) |
| `style.shaped.text_bands.bottom.size` | number | `36` | Bottom text band height, px (upright) |
| `style.shaped.text_bands.left.size` | number | `60` | Left text band width, px (flat) |
| `style.shaped.text_bands.right.size` | number | `60` | Right text band width, px (flat) |
| `style.shaped.polygon.points` | list | - | For `polygon`: the corners as `[x, y]` pairs, fractions (0–1) of the shape |
| `style.shaped.path.d` | string | - | For `path`: an SVG path `d` in absolute coordinates |
| `style.shaped.path.translate` | boolean | `false` | Measure the path from the shape's top-left corner instead of the card's |

## Picard component

**The Picard-era upright gauge: a framed range column, a solid value bar and three scanning lights.** Use it for a tall readout with a ruler, such as a temperature or a power level.

- Pick it with the `picard-gauge-vertical` preset, which sets `component: picard` and an upright track. The ruler on the right is the gauge's [`scale`](./styles#style-gauge).
- The frame and the value bar take the top border's colour unless you set their own.
- With [ranges](./ranges), the frame becomes a notched outline and the ranges fill the column inside it. Without ranges, the frame is a solid bar.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: sensor.temperature
preset: picard-gauge-vertical
style:
  range:
    frame:
      color:
        active: var(--lcards-blue-light)
        inactive: var(--lcards-gray-dark)
  solid_bar:
    color:
      active: var(--lcards-green)
      inactive: var(--lcards-gray)
  animation:
    indicator:
      color: lighten(var(--lcards-orange), 0.2)
  # bands in the framed range column
  ranges:
    - min: 0
      max: 60
      color: var(--lcards-blue)
      opacity: 0.7
    - min: 60
      max: 100
      color: var(--lcards-orange)
      opacity: 0.7
```

::: details More about Picard
- **Scanning lights:** the three lights at the top left pulse one after another, every `animation_speed` seconds. They stand still when the device asks for reduced motion, and `show_animation: false` removes them.
- **Range opacity:** like any gauge band, a range in the column is drawn at `0.3` opacity unless it sets `opacity`.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style.range.frame.color` | colour / state map | `style.border.top.color` | The frame round the range column |
| `style.range.border.color` | colour / state map | theme | The lines between the ranges in the column |
| `style.range.border.gap` | number | `2` | Width of those lines, px |
| `style.solid_bar.color` | colour / state map | `style.border.top.color` | The solid value bar |
| `style.animation.indicator.color` | colour / state map | theme | The scanning lights |
| `show_animation` | boolean | `true` | Show the scanning lights |
| `animation_speed` | number | `2` | Seconds for one pulse of the lights, `0.1` to `10` |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/slider-card/control.html -->

# Control and Motion

What the slider sets and how it moves: the `control` block, what each kind of entity controls, the glide to a new value, and the badge you see while dragging.

## Control options

**`control` changes what the slider can set: its range, its step, or whether it can be dragged at all.** The slider works all of this out from the entity, so you only need `control` to change something, such as a cover that should never close below 20 %.

- `control.min` and `control.max` limit what the slider can set. The scale the track shows can be different: set it with [`style.track.display`](./styles#style-track).
- A light's brightness is set in percent (0 to 100), and a media player's volume too, whatever the entity stores.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: cover.living_room_blinds
preset: pills-left-border
control:
  min: 20 # never close the blinds fully
  max: 100
  step: 5
```

::: details More about control
- **Another attribute:** `attribute` picks what the slider shows and sets, such as a light's colour temperature or a cover's tilt. The attributes it can set are in [Automatic domain behaviour](#automatic-domain-behaviour); any other attribute is shown read-only. It also takes a token or a `[[[JavaScript]]]` template that returns an attribute name.
- **Read-only sliders:** a slider with nothing to set (a sensor, or an attribute no action sets) stays read-only even with `locked: false`.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `min` | number | by domain | Lowest value the slider can set |
| `max` | number | by domain | Highest value the slider can set |
| `step` | number | by domain | Smallest change, at least 0.01 |
| `attribute` | string | by domain | The attribute the slider shows and sets |
| `locked` | boolean | `false` when it can set its attribute, else `true` | `true`: only show the value |
| `invert_value` | boolean | `false` | Swap the ends: the minimum at the right (or top), so dragging right lowers the value. To only draw the fill from the other end, use [`style.track.invert_fill`](./styles#style-track) |

### Automatic domain behaviour

**The entity's domain decides what a slider controls and its range.** These are the defaults that the `control` keys above change.

- Without a [preset](./#presets), the draggable domains draw a pill bar and every other domain draws a gauge.
- A climate entity or water heater without `min_temp` and `max_temp` falls back to 15 to 30 (15 to 60 for a water heater), in steps of `target_temp_step` or 0.5.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: climate.living_room # the range comes from its min_temp and max_temp
preset: pills-left-border-rounded
```

| Domain | Draggable | Controls | Range |
|--------|-----------|----------|-------|
| `light` | Yes | `brightness` | 0–100 (%) |
| `cover` | Yes | `current_position` | 0–100 |
| `fan` | Yes | `percentage` | 0–100 |
| `climate` | Yes | `temperature` | the entity's `min_temp`–`max_temp` |
| `water_heater` | Yes | `temperature` | the entity's `min_temp`–`max_temp` |
| `media_player` | Yes | `volume_level` | 0–100 (%) |
| `humidifier` | Yes | `humidity` | the entity's `min_humidity`–`max_humidity` |
| `valve` | Yes | `current_valve_position` | 0–100 |
| `input_number` | Yes | its state | the entity's `min`, `max`, `step` |
| `number` | Yes | its state | the entity's `min`, `max`, `step` |
| `sensor` | No | its state | 0–100, or the entity's `min` and `max` |

Every other domain is read-only, like a sensor.

**Other attributes it can set** with `control.attribute`:

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: light.living_room
preset: pills-left-border
control:
  attribute: color_temp_kelvin # warm to cool, instead of brightness
```

| Domain | `attribute` | Range |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| `light` | `color_temp_kelvin` | the light's `min_color_temp_kelvin`–`max_color_temp_kelvin` (K), steps of 50 |
| `cover` | `current_tilt_position` | 0–100 (%) |
| `climate` | `target_temp_low`, `target_temp_high` | the entity's `min_temp`–`max_temp`; the other target is sent with it, so it works in heat/cool mode |
| `climate` | `humidity` | the entity's `min_humidity`–`max_humidity` |

## Value tween

**The fill and markers glide to a new value instead of jumping.** It is on by default, and it only runs when the value changes from outside the slider: an automation, another card or the device itself.

- Dragging stays instant: the fill follows your finger. Only positions glide; text and colours change at once.
- The glide is off when the device asks for reduced motion, whatever `enabled` says.

In this example the fill follows your drag at once, and the marker follows the number's state. Drag and let go: when the entity reports its new value, the marker glides there over 1.5 seconds, as the fill would for a change from outside.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: input_number.demo_level
preset: gauge-basic
value_tween:
  duration: 1500
  ease: outBack
style:
  ranges:
    # follows the entity's state, so it glides after a drag
    - value: "{entity.state}"
      indicator:
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
```

::: details More about value tween
- **`spring`:** a springy glide that overshoots and bounces back. Its speed follows `duration`, but the last small bounces take longer to settle: about three times `duration`.
- **A shaped slider** has no markers, so `targets.markers` does nothing there.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Glide to new values |
| `duration` | number | `500` | Milliseconds, 0 to 5000 |
| `ease` | string | `outQuad` | `linear`, `spring`, `in`, `out`, `inOut`, `outIn`, or those joined to `Quad`, `Cubic`, `Quart`, `Quint`, `Sine`, `Expo`, `Circ`, `Back`, `Elastic` or `Bounce` (`inQuad`, `outCubic`, `inOutSine` ...) |
| `targets.track` | boolean | `true` | Glide the fill and indicator (gauge, shaped, ring) or the lit pills (pills) |
| `targets.markers` | boolean | `true` | Glide [value markers](./ranges#value-marker-fields) and their captions |

## Drag value badge

**A small badge shows the value you are dragging to, like Home Assistant's own sliders.** It is off by default; turn it on with `drag_badge.enabled: true`.

- The badge sits below a flat track, beside an upright one (to the left on the Picard gauge), and in the centre of a ring. It draws outside the track, so leave room below or beside the card.
- It shows only while you drag, never for changes from elsewhere, and only on a slider you can drag.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: light.bedroom
preset: pills-left-border
drag_badge:
  enabled: true
  format:
    decimals: 0
  background:
    color:
      default: var(--lcars-blue)
```

::: details More about the drag badge
- **Unit:** the badge uses the unit the track shows: `style.track.display.unit`, else the entity's unit, else `%` for lights, covers, fans, media players, humidifiers and valves.
- **Release:** the badge appears at once when a drag starts. On release it fades out over `release.duration`, or hides at once with `behavior: instant` or when the device asks for reduced motion.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Show the badge while dragging |
| `format.decimals` | number | locale default | Decimal places, 0 to 4 |
| `format.show_unit` | boolean | `true` | Show the unit |
| `format.unit` | string | the track's unit | Unit to show instead |
| `font_size` | number | `14` | Text size, px (8 to 48) |
| `offset.x` | number | `0` | Nudge right, px |
| `offset.y` | number | `0` | Nudge down, px. Write `"y"` in quotes: Home Assistant's editor reads a bare `y` as `true` |
| `color` | colour / object | `var(--lcars-text-light)` | Text colour; a [state map](/core/colours) works |
| `background.enabled` | boolean | `true` | A chip behind the text |
| `background.color` | colour / object | see-through surface | Chip colour |
| `border.enabled` | boolean | `true` | A border round the chip |
| `border.width` | number | `1` | Border width, px (0 to 10) |
| `border.color` | colour / object | theme border | Border colour |
| `release.behavior` | string | `fade` | On release: `fade` fades the badge out, `instant` hides it at once |
| `release.duration` | number | `500` | Fade time, ms, 0 to 2000 (`fade` only) |

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/slider-card/playground.html -->

# Slider Playground

Edit the YAML and the card redraws as you type. Pick a starting point (a brightness pill bar, a temperature gauge or a number level), then change the preset or the entity.

**You don't need to know the YAML to start:**

- **Quick settings** above the editor change the most common options for you.
- **Type in the editor** and it suggests the options that fit where your cursor is, with a short description. Press **Ctrl+Space** to see suggestions anywhere, and hover over a key to read what it does.
- **Options here** (under the editor) lists everything you can add at the cursor. **Insert** adds it at the right indent, and **Docs** opens its section in a new tab.

<ClientOnly>

</ClientOnly>

## How the preview works

The preview is the real slider card, the same code your dashboard runs. The docs site has no Home Assistant, so:

- **Entities get sample values.** The entities listed under the preview are always there, and any other entity id in your YAML gets a plausible value for its domain (lights and switches are on, sensors get a number with a unit).
- **Taps that toggle** switch the sample entity, so state colours change as on a dashboard. **More info**, **navigate** and other actions say what they would do instead.
- **Jinja2 templates** (`{{ ... }}`) need Home Assistant and render empty here; `{entity.state}` tokens and `[[[ JavaScript ]]]` templates work.
- **Icons** aren't drawn (Home Assistant provides them), and sounds are off.

Messages under the card show schema warnings for your YAML.

When it looks right, **Copy YAML** and paste it into your card's YAML editor, then swap in your own entities.
