# Ranges and Markers

**`style.ranges` is a list of coloured bands and live markers drawn on the track.** Use a band to show a comfort zone or a danger zone, and a marker to show a second value, such as the room temperature next to the thermostat setting. An item with `min` and `max` is a band; an item with `value` is a marker.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: climate.living_room
preset: gauge-basic
control:
  min: 10
  max: 30
style:
  gauge:
    progress_bar:
      height: 8 # a thin fill, so the bands show
      align: end
  ranges:
    # three bands: cold, comfortable, hot
    - min: 10
      max: 17
      color: var(--lcards-blue)
      opacity: 0.5
    - min: 17
      max: 24
      color: theme:colors.status.success
      opacity: 0.5
    - min: 24
      max: 30
      color: theme:colors.status.error
      opacity: 0.5
    # a marker at the room temperature, with a caption
    - value: "{entity.attributes.current_temperature}"
      color: var(--lcars-orange)
      label:
        text: NOW
```

## Range band fields

**A band colours the stretch of the track between `min` and `max`.** On a gauge it is a coloured block behind the scale; on pills it recolours the pills inside it; on a [ring](./components#ring-gauge) it colours that part of the ring, and on a [shaped](./components#shaped-component) slider that part of the shape.

- Bands sit under the fill, so a full-height fill hides them. Use a thin fill (`style.gauge.progress_bar.height`) or a low `opacity` to keep them visible.
- `min` and `max` can follow other entities, so a band can show a range that changes, such as a target set elsewhere.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: sensor.temperature
preset: gauge-basic
style:
  track:
    display:
      min: -10
      max: 40
      unit: "°C"
  gauge:
    progress_bar:
      height: 8
      align: end
  ranges:
    - min: -10
      max: 0
      color: var(--lcards-blue)
    - min: 30
      max: 40
      color: theme:colors.status.error
      opacity: 0.6
```

::: details More about bands
- **Templates:** `min` and `max` take only the quick template kinds: tokens such as `{entity.state}`, `{entity.attributes.x}`, `{states.domain.object_id.state}`, `{datasource:name}`, `{config.x}`, `{variables.x}`, and `[[[JavaScript]]]`. Jinja2 is not supported there, because positions are worked out again on every state change.
- **Scale:** `min` and `max` are measured on the scale the track shows (`style.track.display`), not on the range the slider sets.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `min` | number / string | required | Where the band starts: a number or a quick [template](/core/templates/) |
| `max` | number / string | required | Where the band ends, as `min` |
| `color` | colour / object | - | Band colour; a [state map](/core/colours) works |
| `opacity` | number | `0.3` on a gauge, `1` on a ring or shaped slider | Band opacity, 0 to 1. On pills it sets the pills' opacity inside the band; without it they keep their usual opacity |

## Value marker fields

**A marker points at one value on the track and moves when that value changes.** On a gauge it is a triangle at the value; on pills the pill at the value is filled and outlined; on a [ring](./components#value-markers) it sits on the band. A [shaped](./components#shaped-component) slider draws bands only, no markers.

- A marker's `color` colours it on every look: the marked pill, or the gauge or ring marker. `indicator.color` wins over it when both are set.
- Defaults for every marker on the card go in [`style.gauge.marker_indicator`](./styles#style-gauge); a marker's own `indicator` keys win.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: light.bedroom
preset: pills-left-border
style:
  ranges:
    # pills: the pill at 75 is filled with this colour and outlined
    - value: 75
      color: var(--lcars-orange)
      pill_style:
        stroke_color: var(--lcars-yellow)
        stroke_width: 3
```

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: sensor.temperature
preset: gauge-basic
style:
  track:
    display:
      min: -10
      max: 40
      unit: "°C"
  ranges:
    # gauge: a round marker at 20 and a line marker at 30
    - value: 20
      color: var(--lcars-yellow)
      indicator:
        type: round
        size:
          width: 12
    - value: 30
      color: theme:colors.status.error
      indicator:
        type: line
        size:
          width: 3
          height: 24
```

::: details More about markers
- **Templates:** `value` takes the same quick template kinds as a band's `min`, so a marker can follow another entity's state or attribute.
- **On a ring:** markers size themselves by type (`round` uses `width` only), `rotation` is not used, and `offset` takes `y` only, which moves the marker outward.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | number / string | required | Where the marker sits: a number or a quick [template](/core/templates/), as a band's `min` |
| `color` | colour / object | pills: `var(--lcars-text-light)`, gauge and ring: `marker_indicator.color`, else the theme | The marker's colour; a [state map](/core/colours) works |
| `indicator.type` | string | `triangle` (`line` on a ring) | `line`, `round` or `triangle` |
| `indicator.align` | string | `start` | Where across the track: `start`, `center` or `end`. On a ring: `start` for `line`, `end` for `triangle`, `center` for `round` |
| `indicator.color` | colour / object | the marker's `color` | Wins over `color` |
| `indicator.size.width` | number | `20` | Width, px |
| `indicator.size.height` | number | `20` | Height, px |
| `indicator.rotation` | number | `180` | Turn, degrees (not on a ring) |
| `indicator.offset.x` | number | `0` (`20` on `picard-gauge-vertical`) | Nudge right, px |
| `indicator.offset.y` | number | `10` on a flat gauge (`20` with the left-border gauge presets), else `0` | Nudge down, px (on a ring: outward) |
| `indicator.border.enabled` | boolean | `false` | Outline the marker |
| `indicator.border.color` | colour / object | theme | Outline colour |
| `indicator.border.width` | number | `1` | Outline width, px |
| `pill_style.stroke` | boolean | `true` | Pills: outline the marked pill |
| `pill_style.stroke_width` | number | `2` | Pills: outline width, px |
| `pill_style.stroke_color` | colour / object | the marker's `color` | Pills: outline colour |

## Label fields

**A label is a caption on a marker, such as NOW or TARGET, or the value itself.** It sits beside the marker on a gauge, beside the marked pill on pills, and outside the scale on a ring. Nothing shows unless `label.text` is set.

- On a flat track the caption sits above the marker, or below it when the card has no room above (a flat gauge's marker is at the top of the track). On an upright track it sits beside the marker.
- Captions don't move out of the way of tick labels, the value text or each other: use `offset` to place one exactly.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: sensor.temperature
preset: gauge-basic
style:
  track:
    display:
      min: -10
      max: 40
      unit: "°C"
  ranges:
    - value: 25
      color: var(--lcars-orange)
      label:
        text: TARGET 25
        color: var(--lcars-orange)
        font_size: 16
        offset:
          x: 50 # right of the marker
          "y": 16 # level with the marker
```

::: details More about labels
- **Templates:** `label.text` takes every [template](/core/templates/) kind, Jinja2 and data sources included, unlike a marker's `value`.
- **Offsets replace the default spot:** setting `offset.y` on a flat track (or `offset.x` on an upright one) replaces the default distance from the marker, so the number you give is measured from the marker itself.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `label.text` | string | - | The caption: any [template](/core/templates/), Jinja2 and data sources included |
| `label.color` | colour / object | theme | Caption colour; a [state map](/core/colours) works |
| `label.font_size` | number | `14` (`12` on a ring) | Size, px |
| `label.offset.x` | number | beside the marker | Nudge sideways, px |
| `label.offset.y` | number | above the marker (below when there is no room) | Nudge down, px |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/slider-card/styles.html -->

# Pills and Gauges

**The two flat looks of the slider card: a row of pills that light up to the value, or a ruler gauge with a fill bar.** Pick one with a `pills-*` or `gauge-*` preset, or set `style.track.type`.

- Both looks lie flat by default. Set `style.track.orientation: vertical` to stand one upright; the fill then rises from the bottom.
- Every colour key on this page takes a colour, a CSS variable, a theme token or a state map (`default`, `active`, `inactive` ...), as described on the [Colours](/core/colours) page.

The [ring, shaped and Picard](./components) looks have their own page.

---

## `style.track`

**The track is the bar both looks are drawn in: its size, the scale it shows and, for pills, the pills themselves.**

- Leave `segments.count` out and the card fits as many pills of `segments.size.width` as the width allows. Set it and that many pills stretch to share the space.
- `display` changes only the scale the card shows. What the slider sets on the entity is [`control.min` and `max`](./control#control-options).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: light.bedroom
preset: pills-basic
style:
  track:
    segments:
      count: 10
      gap: 6
      gradient:
        start: var(--lcars-orange)
        end: var(--lcards-moonlight)
```

::: details More about style.track
- **Upright pills:** with no `count`, an upright track fits as many pills of `segments.size.height` as the height allows, then stretches them a little so they fill it exactly. A flat track keeps the pill width you set and leaves any spare room at the end.
- **Inverted fill:** with `invert_fill: true` the pill gradient swaps ends too, so the `start` colour stays where the fill starts.
- **Border caps and margin:** the track starts inside any [border caps](#style-border); `margin` adds space inside them.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `type` | string | preset | `pills` or `gauge`. `shaped` is set for you by the [shaped component](./components#shaped-component) |
| `orientation` | string | `horizontal` | `horizontal` or `vertical` |
| `height` | number / string | theme | Track height: px, a `px` or `rem` string, or a theme token |
| `invert_fill` | boolean | `false` | Fill from the other end (right, or top when upright) |
| `margin` | number | `0` | Space on every side of the track, px. Or set each side with the keys below |
| `margin.top` | number | `0` (pills presets: `5`) | Space above the track, px |
| `margin.right` | number | `0` | Space right of the track, px |
| `margin.bottom` | number | `0` | Space below the track, px |
| `margin.left` | number | `0` (pills presets: `5`) | Space left of the track, px |
| `display.min` | number | `control.min` | Lowest value on the scale |
| `display.max` | number | `control.max` | Highest value on the scale |
| `display.unit` | string | entity unit | Unit shown, instead of the entity's `unit_of_measurement` |
| `segments.count` | number | as many as fit | Number of pills, 2 to 200. Unset, as many `size`-wide pills as fit; set, the pills stretch to fill |
| `segments.gap` | number / string | `4` | Gap between pills, px |
| `segments.shape.radius` | number | `0` (pills presets) | Pill corner radius, px |
| `segments.size.width` | number | `10` (pills presets) | Pill width, px. Flat tracks, and only when `count` is unset |
| `segments.size.height` | number | `12` | Pill height, px. Upright tracks, and only when `count` is unset |
| `segments.gradient.start` | colour | theme | Colour of the first pill; a [state map](/core/colours) works |
| `segments.gradient.end` | colour | theme | Colour of the last pill |
| `segments.appearance.filled.opacity` | number | `1` | Opacity of lit pills, 0–1 |
| `segments.appearance.unfilled.opacity` | number | `0.2` | Opacity of unlit pills, 0–1 |

## `style.gauge`

**The gauge's fill bar, its ruler of ticks and labels, the value indicator, and the defaults for value markers.** `progress_bar` is the fill, `scale` the ruler, `indicator` the mark at the current value.

- The value indicator is off until you set `indicator.type`, `color` or `size`, or `enabled: true`. A triangle points down; `rotation: 180` points it up at the ruler.
- [Value markers](./ranges#value-marker-fields) (ranges with a `value`) take their shape from `marker_indicator`, and a marker's own `indicator` keys win over it. A marker's colour is its range's `color` (or its `indicator.color`); `marker_indicator.color` is the default when it sets neither.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: sensor.temperature
preset: gauge-basic
style:
  track:
    height: 48
    display:
      min: -20
      max: 45
      unit: "°C"
  gauge:
    progress_bar:
      color: var(--lcards-blue)
      radius: 4
      background:
        color: var(--lcards-gray-darkest)
    scale:
      tick_marks:
        major:
          interval: 10
          color: var(--lcards-moonlight)
          height: 12
        minor:
          interval: 5
          color: var(--lcards-gray)
          height: 6
      labels:
        color: var(--lcards-moonlight)
    indicator:
      type: triangle
      rotation: 180 # point up at the ruler
      size:
        width: 18
        height: 16
      color: var(--lcars-orange)
```

::: details More about style.gauge
- **Per-end radius:** `progress_bar.radius` and `progress_bar.background.radius` take a number for both ends, or `start` and `end` keys. `start` is the left end (bottom when upright), `end` the right end (top when upright).
- **Turning the indicator on with a template:** `indicator.enabled` takes a [template](/core/templates/) that gives true or false, for example `"{{ not is_state('sensor.x', 'unavailable') }}"`.
- **Marker defaults on a ring:** a [ring](./components#ring-gauge) takes only `marker_indicator.color` from this block.
- **Marker offset on bordered gauges:** the `gauge-left-border` presets set `marker_indicator.offset.y: 20`, so the marker clears the top cap and its tip meets the minor ticks.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `progress_bar.color` | colour | theme | Fill colour; a [state map](/core/colours) works |
| `progress_bar.height` | number | the track | Fill thickness, px |
| `progress_bar.layer` | string | `background` | `background` (behind the ticks) or `foreground` (in front) |
| `progress_bar.align` | string | `middle` | Where the fill sits across the track: `start`, `middle` or `end` |
| `progress_bar.padding.top` | number | `0` | Nudge from the aligned place, px |
| `progress_bar.padding.right` | number | `0` | Nudge from the aligned place, px |
| `progress_bar.padding.bottom` | number | `0` | Nudge from the aligned place, px |
| `progress_bar.padding.left` | number | `0` | Nudge from the aligned place, px |
| `progress_bar.radius` | number | `2` | Corner radius, px |
| `progress_bar.radius.start` | number | `2` | Radius at the start end only, px |
| `progress_bar.radius.end` | number | `2` | Radius at the far end only, px |
| `progress_bar.background.color` | colour | - | The empty track behind the fill. Unset, there is none |
| `progress_bar.background.height` | number | as the bar | Empty track thickness, px |
| `progress_bar.background.radius` | number | as the bar | Empty track corner radius, px. Takes `start` and `end` as the bar does |
| `progress_bar.background.min` | number | `control.min` | Value where the empty track starts |
| `progress_bar.background.max` | number | `control.max` | Value where the empty track ends |
| `scale.tick_marks.major.enabled` | boolean | `true` | Show major ticks |
| `scale.tick_marks.major.interval` | number | `10` | A major tick every this many value units; a fraction (`0.5`) suits a small range, and the labels show its decimals |
| `scale.tick_marks.major.color` | colour | theme | Major tick colour |
| `scale.tick_marks.major.height` | number | the track | Major tick length, px |
| `scale.tick_marks.major.width` | number | `2` | Major tick width, px |
| `scale.tick_marks.minor.enabled` | boolean | `true` | Show the minor ticks between the major ones |
| `scale.tick_marks.minor.interval` | number | `2` | A minor tick every this many value units; fractions work |
| `scale.tick_marks.minor.color` | colour | theme | Minor tick colour |
| `scale.tick_marks.minor.height` | number | `10` | Minor tick length, px |
| `scale.tick_marks.minor.width` | number | `1` | Minor tick width, px |
| `scale.labels.enabled` | boolean | `true` | Show the value labels |
| `scale.labels.show_unit` | boolean | `true` | Add the unit to each label |
| `scale.labels.unit` | string | entity unit | Unit on the labels |
| `scale.labels.color` | colour | theme | Label colour |
| `scale.labels.font_size` | number | `14` | Label size, px |
| `scale.labels.padding` | number | `3` | Space round the labels, px |
| `indicator.enabled` | boolean / string | off | Show the value indicator. Setting `type`, `color` or `size` also turns it on |
| `indicator.type` | string | `line` | `line`, `round` or `triangle` |
| `indicator.color` | colour | theme | Indicator colour; a [state map](/core/colours) works |
| `indicator.size.width` | number | `4` | Indicator width, px |
| `indicator.size.height` | number | `25` | Indicator height, px |
| `indicator.rotation` | number | `0` | Turn, degrees, -180 to 180. `180` points a triangle up |
| `indicator.offset.x` | number | `0` | Nudge sideways, px |
| `indicator.offset.y` | number | `0` | Nudge up or down, px |
| `indicator.border.enabled` | boolean | `true` | An outline round the indicator; `false` removes it |
| `indicator.border.width` | number | `1` | Outline width, px |
| `indicator.border.color` | colour | theme | Outline colour |
| `marker_indicator.type` | string | `triangle` | Marker shape: `line`, `round` or `triangle` |
| `marker_indicator.align` | string | `start` | Where the marker sits across the track: `start`, `center` or `end` |
| `marker_indicator.size.width` | number | `20` | Marker width, px |
| `marker_indicator.size.height` | number | `20` | Marker height, px |
| `marker_indicator.rotation` | number | `180` | Turn, degrees; `180` points a triangle at the ticks |
| `marker_indicator.offset.x` | number | `0` | Nudge from the aligned place, px (used on upright gauges) |
| `marker_indicator.offset.y` | number | `10` (flat), `0` (upright) | Nudge from the aligned place, px (used on flat gauges) |
| `marker_indicator.color` | colour | theme | Marker colour |
| `marker_indicator.border.enabled` | boolean | `false` | An outline round each marker |
| `marker_indicator.border.width` | number | `1` | Outline width, px |
| `marker_indicator.border.color` | colour | theme | Outline colour |

## `style.border`

**LCARS caps on the ends and sides of the track, with an optional rounded card outline.** A left cap alone is the classic LCARS end.

- A cap is drawn only when its side has `enabled: true` and a `size` above 0. The track then starts inside it.
- Text fields without a `zone` go into the first cap that is on, in the order `left`, `right`, `top`, `bottom`. See [Text labels](#text-labels).
- `radius` rounds the corners of the whole card, caps and track together.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: light.bedroom
preset: pills-basic
style:
  border:
    radius: 8
    left:
      enabled: true
      size: 20
      color:
        default: var(--lcards-gray)
        active: var(--lcars-orange)
```

::: details More about style.border
- **Rounding one end:** set the corner keys instead of one number, for example `top_right: 12` and `bottom_right: 12` with the left corners at `0`. The `*-left-border-rounded` presets do this, so the capped end stays square.
- **Large radii:** a corner's radius is capped at half the card's shorter side.
- **Hover and press:** a cap's state map also takes `hover` and `pressed` colours.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `radius` | number / string | - | Corner radius of the card: px, a `px` or `rem` string, or a CSS variable such as `var(--ha-card-border-radius, var(--ha-border-radius-lg))` (a theme variable: give it a fallback). Unset, the corners are square |
| `radius.top_left` | number / string | `0` | One corner only, px or a CSS variable |
| `radius.top_right` | number / string | `0` | One corner only |
| `radius.bottom_right` | number / string | `0` | One corner only |
| `radius.bottom_left` | number / string | `0` | One corner only |
| `left.enabled` | boolean | `false` | Draw the left cap |
| `left.size` | number | `0` | Left cap width, px |
| `left.color` | colour | theme | Left cap colour; a [state map](/core/colours) works |
| `right.enabled` | boolean | `false` | Draw the right cap |
| `right.size` | number | `0` | Right cap width, px |
| `right.color` | colour | theme | Right cap colour |
| `top.enabled` | boolean | `false` | Draw the top cap |
| `top.size` | number | `0` | Top cap height, px |
| `top.color` | colour | theme | Top cap colour |
| `bottom.enabled` | boolean | `false` | Draw the bottom cap |
| `bottom.size` | number | `0` | Bottom cap height, px |
| `bottom.color` | colour | theme | Bottom cap colour |

## Text labels

**Text fields of your own, such as a label and a read-out of the value.** The pills and gauge presets show no text until you add some.

- A field without a `zone` goes into the first [border cap](#style-border) that is on. Set `zone: track` to put it over the track instead.
- The presets already hold a `name` field (the entity's name) and a `state` field (the value) that are hidden. Turn one on with `show: true`; the ring and shaped presets already show both.
- Every [text field](/core/text-fields) key works here, including templates in `content`.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: light.bedroom
preset: pills-left-border
text:
  default:
    color: var(--lcards-moonlight)
  label:
    content: Brightness
    zone: track
    position: top-left
    font_size: 11
  value:
    content: "[[[return Math.round(entity.attributes.brightness / 255 * 100) + '%']]]"
    zone: track
    position: top-right
    font_size: 11
```

::: details More about text labels
- **Missing zones:** a `zone` that does not exist on the card, such as a cap that is off, puts the field over the track.
- **Preset text style:** the presets set `text.default` to the theme's LCARS font in upper case.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `text.<name>` | object | - | A text field of your own; any name except `default` |
| `text.<name>.content` | string | - | The text; [templates](/core/templates/) work |
| `text.<name>.zone` | string | first cap | `left`, `right`, `top` or `bottom` (a cap that is on), or `track`. With no cap on, `track` |
| `text.<name>.position` | string | from `default` | Where in the zone: `top-left`, `center`, `bottom-right` ... (see [Placing text](/core/text-fields-placement#position)) |
| `text.<name>.show` | boolean | `true` | Show or hide the field |
| `text.default` | object | theme font, upper case | Style every field inherits. It is not drawn itself |
| `text.name.show` | boolean | `false` | Show the entity's name |
| `text.state.show` | boolean | `false` | Show the value: a light's brightness as a percentage, otherwise the entity's state |
| [Text field keys](/core/text-fields) | | | `font_size`, `color`, `font_weight`, `text_transform` and the rest |

## Putting it together

**A thermostat: a gauge with its own scale, coloured comfort bands, a state-coloured fill and a left cap.**

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: climate.living_room
preset: gauge-basic
control:
  attribute: temperature
  min: 15
  max: 30
  step: 0.5
text:
  label:
    content: Living Room
    zone: track # over the track, not in the left cap
    position: top-left
    font_size: 11
    text_transform: uppercase
  value:
    content: "[[[return entity.attributes.current_temperature + '°C']]]"
    zone: track
    position: top-right
    font_size: 11
style:
  track:
    height: 52
    display:
      unit: "°C"
  gauge:
    progress_bar:
      color:
        default: var(--lcards-blue)
        heat: var(--lcars-alert-red)
        cool: var(--lcards-blue)
      radius: 3
    scale:
      tick_marks:
        major:
          interval: 5
        minor:
          interval: 1
    indicator:
      type: triangle
      rotation: 180
      size:
        width: 18
        height: 16
      color: var(--lcars-orange)
  ranges:
    - min: 15
      max: 19
      color: var(--lcards-blue)
      opacity: 0.25
    - min: 19
      max: 24
      color: theme:colors.status.success
      opacity: 0.25
    - min: 24
      max: 30
      color: theme:colors.status.error
      opacity: 0.25
  border:
    radius: 8
    left:
      enabled: true
      size: 20
      color:
        default: var(--lcards-gray)
        active: var(--lcars-orange)
tap_action:
  action: more-info
```

# Features

Every LCARdS card shares two things: options you set on each card (actions, colours, text) and services that work across all cards at once (themes, rules, data sources). This section covers both. New here? [How LCARdS works](../getting-started/what-is-lcards#how-it-works) shows how they fit together.

## On Every Card

Options you set on each card:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| [Actions](actions.md) | Tap, hold, and double-tap actions wired to any Home Assistant service call |
| [Colours](colours.md) | Accepted colour formats and state-based colour maps |
| [Presets](presets.md) | Named style collections: apply a full card appearance in one line |
| [Sounds](sounds.md) | Event-driven audio feedback via the Sound Manager |
| [Styles](styles.md) | The `style:` block: card background, border, icon, and dimension overrides |
| [Text Fields](text-fields.md) | Label and value field templating reference |

## Shared Services

Services every card on the screen shares, so they work across cards at once:

| Service | Description |
|---|---|
| [Alert Mode](alert-mode.md) | Coordinated dashboard-wide red/yellow alert states with full UI and audio transformation |
| [Data Sources](datasources/) | Live entity subscriptions, polling, history buffers, and transformations |
| [Rules Engine](rules/) | Conditional styling engine: change colours, icons, labels, and trigger animations based on entity state |
| [Templates](templates/) | Four template types: JavaScript, token, data source, and Jinja2, evaluated uniformly across all properties |
| [Themes](themes/) | Token-based colour palette shared across all cards |

## Effects

| Effect | Description |
|---|---|
| [Animations](animations.md) | anime.js-powered animations triggered by interactions or entity changes |
| [Background Animations](effects/background-animations.md) | Canvas2D animated backgrounds behind card content |
| [Filters](effects/filters.md) | Stackable CSS and SVG visual filters: blur, brightness, colour shift, displacement |

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/actions.html -->

# Actions

**What a card does when you tap it, hold it or double-tap it: toggle a light, run any Home Assistant action, open a dashboard, a page or a dialog.** Actions follow Home Assistant's own action model, so YAML from Home Assistant's cards works here too.

- A card takes up to three actions: `tap_action`, `hold_action` and `double_tap_action`. Each is an object whose `action` key picks what happens.
- The button, elbow, slider, select menu, data grid and astrometrics cards take actions; each card's page says where on the card they apply.

## Quick start

**A button that raises a red alert when tapped and clears it when held.** Try it here: the alert recolours this page.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: lozenge
text:
  label:
    content: RED ALERT
    show: true
# tap: raise a red alert
tap_action:
  action: perform-action
  perform_action: lcards.red_alert
# hold: back to normal
hold_action:
  action: perform-action
  perform_action: lcards.clear_alert
```

## Action types

**The `action` key picks what happens: toggle the entity, run an action, open a dashboard, a page or a dialog, or nothing.**

- `toggle` picks its service as Home Assistant's own cards do: from `off`, `closed` or `locked` it turns the entity on, from any other state off.
- `none` is how to stop a card's default: a button toggles its entity on a tap until its `tap_action` says otherwise.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_lights
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
tap_action:
  action: toggle
```

| `action` | What it does |
|----------|--------------|
| `toggle` | Toggle the entity. Locks unlock and lock, covers and valves open and close, buttons are pressed, scenes are turned on |
| `perform-action` | Run a Home Assistant action: name it in `perform_action` and give its data in `data` |
| `call-service` | The older name for `perform-action` |
| `more-info` | Open Home Assistant's more-info dialog for the entity |
| `navigate` | Go to another dashboard or view (`navigation_path`) |
| `url` | Open an address in a new browser tab (`url_path`) |
| `assist` | Open Home Assistant's Assist dialog |
| `fire-dom-event` | Fire Home Assistant's `ll-custom` event with the action, for integrations that listen for it such as [browser_mod](/configuration/browser-mod) |
| `fly-to`, `set-clock`, `set-model-scale` | Move the camera, the scene date or the model size of an astrometrics card: see [Scene actions](/cards/astrometrics/points#scene-actions) |
| `none` | Do nothing, in place of the card's default |

::: details More about toggle
- **Groups** toggle through Home Assistant's `homeassistant` domain (`homeassistant.turn_on`, `homeassistant.turn_off`).
- **An entity with no state yet** gets its domain's own `toggle` action (`light.toggle`).
:::

## Action keys

**The keys of an action object, besides `action`: which entity it acts on, what to run, and where to go.**

- `target` goes to Home Assistant as the action's target, separate from `data`, as Home Assistant's own cards send it.
- The older names `call-service`, `service` and `service_data` still work, and the [config checker](/getting-started/config-checker) suggests the current one. When an action sets both an old and a new name, the new one wins, as in Home Assistant.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_doors
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
# tap: turn the doors on
tap_action:
  action: perform-action
  perform_action: input_boolean.turn_on
  target:
    entity_id: input_boolean.lcards_test_doors
# hold: turn them off
hold_action:
  action: perform-action
  perform_action: input_boolean.turn_off
  target:
    entity_id: input_boolean.lcards_test_doors
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | string | required | What happens: see [Action types](#action-types) |
| `entity` | string | the card's entity | The entity `toggle` and `more-info` act on |
| `perform_action` | string | - | `perform-action`: the action to run, as `domain.action` (`light.turn_on`) |
| `service` | string | - | The older name for `perform_action` |
| `data` | object | - | `perform-action`: the action's data (`brightness_pct: 50`) |
| `service_data` | object | - | The older name for `data` |
| `target` | object | - | `perform-action`: what the action acts on |
| `target.entity_id` | string / list | - | Entity ids to act on |
| `target.device_id` | string / list | - | Device ids to act on |
| `target.area_id` | string / list | - | Area ids to act on |
| `browser_mod` | object | - | `fire-dom-event`: what browser_mod runs, in its own grammar (`service` and `data`): see [browser_mod](/configuration/browser-mod) |
| `navigation_path` | string | - | `navigate`: the dashboard path, starting with `/` (`/lovelace/bridge`). Required |
| `url_path` | string | - | `url`: the address to open. Required |
| `pipeline_id` | string | `preferred` | `assist`: the Assist pipeline to use |
| `start_listening` | boolean | `true` | `assist`: start listening as soon as the dialog opens |
| [Scene action keys](/cards/astrometrics/points#scene-actions) | | | `card`, `view`, `point`, `duration`, `warp`, `date`, `rate` and `model_scale` for the astrometrics actions |

## Tap, hold and double-tap

**When each of the three actions runs.** A hold is a press of half a second; a double tap is two taps close together.

- A hold runs `hold_action` after 500 ms, and the tap that would follow when you let go is skipped.
- When a card has a `double_tap_action`, a single tap waits 300 ms for a second tap before it runs `tap_action`. A card without one runs its tap at once.
- Each action can name its own `entity`, so one card can control several things.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_lights
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
# tap: the lights
tap_action:
  action: toggle
# double tap: the doors
double_tap_action:
  action: toggle
  entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_doors
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tap_action` | object | `toggle` on a button, none on an elbow or slider | What a tap does. The select menu, data grid and astrometrics pages give their own defaults |
| `hold_action` | object | - | What a press held for 500 ms does |
| `double_tap_action` | object | - | What two taps within 300 ms do |

## Hover and cursor

**The button and elbow cards change colour and can animate when the mouse pointer is over them, and show a hand cursor.** Two card-level keys (not keys of an action) turn that off or change the cursor.

### interactive

**`interactive: false` makes a button or elbow decorative: no hover colour, no hover animations and the arrow cursor.** Use it for a label or panel that should not look clickable.

- A button or elbow with no action and no entity a tap can toggle is decorative already (a title, a sweep, a filler, a sensor readout); set `interactive: true` to give it hover effects anyway.
- Tap, hold and double-tap actions still run on a card with `interactive: false`.
- The hover sound (`card_hover`, see [Card Sounds](/core/sounds)) does not play either.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_lights
preset: lozenge
# decorative: no hand cursor or hover effects
interactive: false
text:
  name:
    show: true
# still runs on a tap
tap_action:
  action: toggle
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `interactive` | boolean | `true` with an action or a switchable entity, else `false` | `false`: no hover colour, hover animations or hover sound, and the arrow cursor. Actions still run |

### style.cursor

**The mouse cursor over a button or elbow, whatever `interactive` says.** Use it for hover effects with another cursor shape, or for the hand cursor on a decorative card.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: lozenge
text:
  label:
    content: TARGET
    show: true
style:
  cursor: crosshair
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style.cursor` | string | `pointer`, or `default` with `interactive: false` | Any CSS cursor: `pointer`, `default`, `none`, `not-allowed`, `crosshair`, `grab`, `zoom-in`, `help`, `wait`, `progress`, `move`, `copy`, `text` |
