# Rule-based Animations

A rule's `apply.animations` plays animations on any number of cards while the rule matches. Use it instead of a card's own [`on_entity_change`](/core/animations/entity-change-triggers) animations when one condition should animate several cards, or the condition involves several entities. Rules themselves are covered in the [Rules Engine](/core/rules/).

## Basic structure

**Add an `animations` list to a rule's `apply` block; each entry names its targets and a preset.** The animations start when the rule matches and looping ones stop when it no longer does.

- A rule sits in the `rules` list of any LCARdS card, but every card's rules run in one engine for the whole page, so a rule on one card can animate others. Give each rule an `id` no other card uses.
- The animations start when the rule changes from not matching to matching, including when the page loads with the condition already true. They don't start again while it stays matched.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-anim-rule-basic-btn
entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
preset: lozenge
tags:
  - docs-anim-temperature
text:
  name:
    content: Temperature
    show: true
tap_action:
  action: toggle
# while the toggle is on, every card tagged docs-anim-temperature pulses
rules:
  - id: docs-anim-rule-basic
    when:
      entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
      state: "on"
    apply:
      animations:
        - tag: docs-anim-temperature
          preset: pulse
          loop: true
          duration: 1000
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `apply.animations` | list | - | Animations to play while the rule matches. Each entry has one [target](#targeting) and the [animation keys](#animation-parameters) |

## Targeting

**Each entry names its targets with one of `overlay`, `tag`, `type` or `pattern`.** Tags are the usual way to animate a group: give the cards the same entry in `tags` and target that.

- `overlay` is a card's `id` (or an MSD overlay's, or an astrometrics point's or object's). `tag` matches a card's `tags`. Buttons and elbows also carry their card type, their preset name and, when they have an entity, `entity-based` as tags.
- `type` is the kind of card or overlay: `button`, `elbow`, `slider`, `select-menu`, `chart`, `data-grid` or `astrometrics`, an MSD's `line`, `shape` or `control`, or `astrometrics-point` and `astrometrics-object`. It reaches every one on the page.
- `pattern` is a regular expression matched against the ids.
- Only one is used, in the order `overlay`, `tag`, `type`, `pattern`: an entry with both `overlay` and `tag` targets the overlay only.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 120px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr
  grid-template-rows: 1fr 1fr
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: lozenge
    entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
    tap_action:
      action: toggle
    text:
      name:
        content: ALERT
        show: true
    view_layout:
      grid-column: 1 / 4
    rules:
      - id: docs-anim-rule-targets
        when:
          entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
          state: "on"
        apply:
          animations:
            # one card, by id
            - overlay: docs-anim-deck-sensors
              preset: blink
              loop: true
            # every card with the tag
            - tag: docs-anim-deck-engines
              preset: pulse
              loop: true
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    id: docs-anim-deck-sensors
    preset: filled
    text:
      name:
        content: SENSORS
        show: true
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: filled
    tags:
      - docs-anim-deck-engines
    text:
      name:
        content: WARP
        show: true
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: filled
    tags:
      - docs-anim-deck-engines
    text:
      name:
        content: IMPULSE
        show: true
```

`type` and `pattern` written out:

```yaml alternatives
# every button on the page
- type: button
  preset: pulse
  loop: true

# every card whose id starts with temp_
- pattern: "^temp_"
  preset: shimmer
  loop: true
```

::: details More about targeting
- **Not the same as style selectors:** `apply.overlays` names its groups in the map key (`tag:alert-buttons:`), while an animation entry has a key of its own (`- tag: alert-buttons`).
- **Cards that load later:** when a rule matches before its target has loaded (an MSD's overlays still being built), it keeps looking for about a second and a half, then skips that entry.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `overlay` | string | - | One card or overlay, by `id` |
| `tag` | string | - | Every card and overlay with this tag |
| `type` | string | - | Every card or overlay of this kind |
| `pattern` | string | - | Every card and overlay whose id matches this regular expression |

## Animation parameters

**An entry takes the preset, its `params` and the timing keys of a card's own animations.** `map_range` works here too, in `duration`, `delay` and any `params` value.

- An entry has no `trigger`: the rule matching is what plays it.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-anim-rule-params-btn
entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_doors
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: Doors
    show: true
tap_action:
  action: toggle
rules:
  - id: docs-anim-rule-params
    when:
      entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_doors
      state: "on"
    apply:
      animations:
        - overlay: docs-anim-rule-params-btn
          preset: glow
          loop: true
          duration: 800
          delay: 0
          ease: inOutQuad
          params:
            color: var(--lcars-orange)
            blur_max: 12
            # the glow grows with the shields
            blur_min:
              map_range:
                entity: input_number.lcards_test_shields
                input: [0, 100]
                output: [0, 8]
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `preset` | string | required | What the animation does: see the [Preset Reference](/core/animations/preset-reference) |
| `params` | object | the preset's defaults | The preset's own settings. Each value may be a [`map_range`](/core/animations/timing-and-easing#map-range-descriptors) |
| `duration` | number / object | the preset's | Length of one play, ms, or a `map_range` |
| `delay` | number / object | `0` | Wait before it starts, ms, or a `map_range` |
| `loop` | boolean / number | `false` | `true` repeats until the rule stops matching, a number repeats that many more times |
| `ease` | string | the preset's | An [easing](/core/animations/timing-and-easing#easing-functions) name or a curve with numbers as a string |

## Lifecycle: automatic stop on unmatch

**When the rule stops matching, the looping animations it started stop and the cards go back to how they looked.** Animations that play once run to the end, even if the rule stops matching while they play.

- An entry with `loop` set to `true` or a number counts as looping, and is stopped.
- Nothing needs cleaning up: start and stop both follow the rule.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-anim-rule-life-btn
entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_lights
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: Lights
    show: true
tap_action:
  action: toggle
rules:
  - id: docs-anim-rule-life
    when:
      entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_lights
      state: "on"
    apply:
      animations:
        # strobes until the lights go off
        - overlay: docs-anim-rule-life-btn
          preset: strobe
          loop: true
        # one fade-in when they come on; it finishes even if they go off at once
        - overlay: docs-anim-rule-life-btn
          preset: fade
```

::: details More about stopping
- **Several rules on one card:** when a rule stops matching, only the looping animations it started stop; another rule's loop on the same card keeps running.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `loop` | boolean / number | `false` | Any value but `false` makes the entry stop when the rule stops matching |

## Multi-card coordination example

**One rule for a red alert: recolour a group of cards, pulse them, blink one and shimmer the elbow.** Switch the toggle under the cards on and off.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 160px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr
  grid-template-rows: 1fr 1fr
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow:
      type: header-left
    view_layout:
      grid-column: 1 / 4
    rules:
      - id: docs-anim-rule-red-alert
        when:
          entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
          state: "on"
        apply:
          overlays:
            tag:docs-anim-action-buttons:
              style:
                card:
                  color:
                    background: var(--lcars-alert-red)
          animations:
            - tag: docs-anim-action-buttons
              preset: pulse
              loop: true
              params:
                max_scale: 1.08
            - overlay: docs-anim-main-alert
              preset: strobe
              loop: true
            - type: elbow
              preset: shimmer
              loop: true
              params:
                color_to: var(--lcars-alert-red)
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    id: docs-anim-main-alert
    preset: filled
    text:
      name:
        content: RED ALERT
        show: true
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: filled
    tags:
      - docs-anim-action-buttons
    text:
      name:
        content: SHIELDS
        show: true
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: filled
    tags:
      - docs-anim-action-buttons
    text:
      name:
        content: PHASERS
        show: true
```

## Combining with style patches

**One `apply` block can restyle cards and animate them at the same time.** Both take effect when the rule matches and end when it no longer does.

- `apply.overlays` changes the style of the cards it names; `apply.animations` animates them. See the [Rules Engine](/core/rules/) for `apply.overlays`.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-anim-alert-badge
entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_visible
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: Warning
    show: true
tap_action:
  action: toggle
rules:
  - id: docs-anim-rule-warning
    when:
      entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_visible
      state: "on"
    apply:
      # yellow and blinking while the switch is on
      overlays:
        docs-anim-alert-badge:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-alert-yellow)
      animations:
        - overlay: docs-anim-alert-badge
          preset: blink
          loop: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `apply.overlays.<id>` | object | - | The card's new `style` while the rule matches: see the [Rules Engine](/core/rules/) |
| `apply.animations` | list | - | Animations played while the rule matches |

# Timing and Easing

How long an animation takes, how often it repeats, how it speeds up and slows down, and what happens when the device asks for less motion. The other animation keys are on the [Card Animations](/core/animations#animation-options) page.

## Timing

**`duration`, `delay`, `loop` and `alternate` set how long one play takes, when it starts and how many times it repeats.** Leave them out and the preset's own timing applies.

- Each preset has its own defaults: `pulse` takes 1200 ms and loops for ever, `fade` takes 1000 ms and plays once. The [Preset Reference](/core/animations/preset-reference) lists them.
- `loop` counts repeats after the first play: `loop: 1` plays twice. With `alternate: true` every other play runs backwards, so `loop: 1` with `alternate: true` goes there and back once.
- The same keys inside `params` work too; the entry's own key wins when both are set.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: Tap me
    show: true
animations:
  # dims to 30 % and comes back, twice, after a short wait
  - trigger: on_tap
    preset: fade
    duration: 250
    delay: 100
    loop: 3
    alternate: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `duration` | number / object | the preset's | Length of one play, ms, or a [`map_range`](#map-range-descriptors). No upper limit |
| `delay` | number / object | `0` | Wait before the first play, ms, or a `map_range` |
| `loop` | boolean / number | the preset's | `true` repeats for ever, `false` plays once, a number repeats that many more times |
| `alternate` | boolean | the preset's | Play every other repeat backwards |

## `map_range` descriptors

**A number that follows an entity: a spin that speeds up with the wind, a pulse that slows as the battery drains.** Write `map_range` in place of the number, with the entity and the two ranges to map between.

- It maps the entity's value from `input` to `output` in a straight line. With `output: [2000, 400]` a higher value gives a shorter duration, so the animation runs faster.
- It works in `duration`, `delay` and any value in `params`, on a card's own animations and in a rule's `apply.animations`.
- On a looping animation, a `map_range` in `duration` keeps following the entity while the animation runs: the speed changes as the value does. Every other value is read once, when the animation starts.
- `output` can also be two colours, for a colour param: the colour is blended between them, transparency too. Each can be any colour LCARdS accepts (a hex of any length, a named colour, `rgb()` or `hsl()`, a CSS variable, a `theme:` token or a computed colour such as `alpha()`).

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.workbench
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
tap_action:
  action: toggle
animations:
  # pulses while the light is on, faster the brighter it is
  - trigger: on_entity_change
    entity: light.workbench
    preset: pulse
    loop: true
    while:
      state: "on"
    duration:
      map_range:
        entity: light.workbench
        attribute: brightness_pct
        input: [0, 100]
        output: [2000, 400]
```

::: details More about map_range
- **A value it can't use:** an entity that doesn't exist, a missing attribute or a state that isn't a number (`unavailable`) leaves the value out, so the preset's default applies.
- **The same words elsewhere:** button textures, astrometrics objects and the rules' `map_range_cond` use the same `entity`, `attribute`, `input`, `output` and `clamp`.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `map_range.entity` | string | required | The entity to follow |
| `map_range.attribute` | string | the state | An attribute to read instead. `brightness_pct` gives a light's brightness as 0–100 |
| `map_range.input` | list | required | `[min, max]` of the entity's value |
| `map_range.output` | list | required | `[min, max]` of the result: two numbers, or two colours in any form |
| `map_range.clamp` | boolean | `true` | Keep the result inside `output` when the value goes past `input` |

## Easing functions

**`ease` sets how the animation speeds up and slows down: a gentle start, a bounce at the end, a spring.** LCARdS runs anime.js v4, so ease names have no `ease` prefix: `inOutQuad`, `outElastic`, `inOutSine`.

- An anime.js v3 name such as `easeInOutQuad` is not a v4 name: it plays as `linear`. Write `inOutQuad`.
- A curve with numbers is written as a string, as in the [anime.js easing editor](https://animejs.com/easing-editor), whose output you can paste in: `steps(4)`, `cubicBezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)`, `spring({ bounce: 0.4, duration: 500 })`. The animation editor offers these too, with a field for each number.
- The object form takes `type` and `params`; a spring sets its own length, so `duration` has no effect with it.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: Spring
    show: true
animations:
  # springs out and back on each tap
  - trigger: on_tap
    preset: scale
    loop: 1
    alternate: true
    ease:
      type: spring
      params:
        stiffness: 150
        damping: 20
```

Every form `ease` takes, one per line:

```yaml alternatives
ease: inOutQuad                     # a named curve
ease: outElastic                    # elastic bounce at the end
ease: linear                        # constant speed
ease: steps(4)                      # four jumps instead of a smooth curve
ease: cubicBezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)   # a custom curve, as in CSS
ease: spring({ bounce: 0.4, duration: 500 })  # pasted from the anime.js easing editor
ease:                               # spring physics
  type: spring
  params:
    stiffness: 150
    damping: 20
```

| Curve | Names |
|-------|-------|
| Power | `in`, `out`, `inOut`, `outIn` |
| Quad, Cubic, Quart, Quint | `inQuad`, `outQuad`, `inOutQuad`, `outInQuad` (and the same for `Cubic`, `Quart`, `Quint`) |
| Sine, Circ, Expo | `inSine`, `outSine`, `inOutSine`, `outInSine` (and the same for `Circ`, `Expo`) |
| Back | `inBack`, `outBack`, `inOutBack`, `outInBack` |
| Elastic | `inElastic`, `outElastic`, `inOutElastic`, `outInElastic` |
| Bounce | `inBounce`, `outBounce`, `inOutBounce`, `outInBounce` |
| Other | `linear`, `steps(N)`, `cubicBezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)`, `irregular(steps, randomness)`, `spring({ bounce, duration })` |

::: details More about easing
- **Object `params` by `type`:** `in`, `out`, `inOut`, `outIn` take `power` (`1.675`); the `Back` curves `overshoot` (`1.70158`); the `Elastic` curves `amplitude` (`1`) and `period` (`0.3`); `cubicBezier` takes `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2` (`0.25`, `0.1`, `0.25`, `1`); `spring` takes `mass` (`1`), `stiffness` (`100`), `damping` (`10`) and `velocity` (`0`); `steps` takes `steps` (`10`) and `fromStart` (`false`); `irregular` takes `steps` (`10`) and `randomness` (`1`); `custom` takes `customString`, any of the string forms above.
- **`ease_params`:** a string `ease` with `params.ease_params` is read as the object form: `ease: outBack` with `ease_params: { overshoot: 3 }` is a stronger overshoot.
- **`easing`:** the anime.js v3 key is still read when `ease` is missing, but the config checker flags it as unknown. Write `ease`.
- **A bad curve:** a string with numbers that can't be read, or an unknown `type`, plays as `linear`.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `ease` | string / object | the preset's | A curve name, a curve with numbers as a string, or `type` with `params` |
| `ease.type` | string | - | Object form: the curve (`spring`, `cubicBezier`, `steps`, `irregular`, `linear`, `custom`, `inBack` ...) |
| `ease.params` | object | that curve's defaults | Object form: the curve's numbers (see above) |
| `params.ease_params` | object | - | Numbers for a string `ease`, as in the object form |

## Reduced motion

**When the device asks for less motion (the Reduce motion accessibility setting, `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`), LCARdS does not play animations.** An animation that runs once jumps straight to where it would end, so entrance and `on_show` animations still leave the card visible.

- A looping animation (pulse, glow, blink, cascades) does not run, and canvas background and screen effects show a still frame. Turning the setting back off lets the next trigger play.
- Some motion carries meaning: an alert flash that should catch the eye even when everything else stays still. Mark that animation with `essential_motion: true` and it plays anyway. Use it sparingly; people turn the setting on because motion bothers them.
- The animation editor has the same switch (**Essential motion**).

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_doors
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: Front door
    show: true
animations:
  # blinks when the door opens, even with Reduce motion on
  - trigger: on_entity_change
    entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_doors
    to_state: "on"
    preset: blink
    essential_motion: true
    duration: 400
    loop: 6
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `essential_motion` | boolean | `false` | Keep playing when the device asks for reduced motion. Only for motion that carries meaning |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/animations/triggers.html -->

# Triggers

`trigger` on an animation entry says when it plays. This page covers every trigger except `on_entity_change`, which has its own page: [Entity Change Triggers](/core/animations/entity-change-triggers).

## trigger

**One trigger per entry; give a card several entries to react to several things.** Leave `trigger` out and the entry plays when the card loads.

- `on_state_change`, `on_redraw` and `on_exit` are not triggers (the config checker rejects them, and they never fire). For state changes use `on_entity_change`.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: Triggers
    show: true
animations:
  # once when the card loads
  - trigger: on_load
    preset: fade
    params:
      from: 0
      to: 1
  # on every tap
  - trigger: on_tap
    preset: bounce
  # on a long press
  - trigger: on_hold
    preset: shake
```

| Trigger | Plays |
|---------|-------|
| `on_load` | Once, when the card first renders |
| `on_show` | Each time the card appears: when its view opens, when a visibility condition shows it, or when you come back from another view |
| `on_tap` | When the card is tapped or clicked |
| `on_double_tap` | When the card is double-tapped |
| `on_hold` | On a long press |
| `on_hover` | While the mouse is over the card |
| `on_leave` | When the mouse leaves the card |
| `on_entity_change` | When a watched entity changes: see [Entity Change Triggers](/core/animations/entity-change-triggers) |
| `on_datasource_change` | When a [data source](/core/datasources/) updates: see [on_datasource_change](#on-datasource-change) |

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `trigger` | string | `on_load` | When the entry plays: one of the triggers above |

## Taps and holds

**`on_tap`, `on_double_tap` and `on_hold` play when you touch the card, alongside its tap, double-tap and hold actions.** Use them for feedback that the press landed.

- The animation and the action both happen: a tap that toggles a light also plays the `on_tap` animation.
- On a slider, tap and hold animations sit on its border caps, where the actions are. On a data grid a tap anywhere on the grid plays them, and [`tap-ripple`](/core/animations/preset-reference#tap-ripple) starts from the tap point.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.workbench
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
tap_action:
  action: toggle
hold_action:
  action: more-info
animations:
  # grows and shrinks back once
  - trigger: on_tap
    preset: pulse
    loop: 1
    duration: 200
  - trigger: on_hold
    preset: shake
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `trigger` | string | `on_load` | `on_tap`, `on_double_tap` or `on_hold` |

## Hover

**`on_hover` plays while the mouse is over the card, and `on_leave` when it moves off.** A looping hover animation, such as a glow, stops as soon as the mouse leaves.

- Hover only works with a mouse or trackpad: on a touch screen these triggers never fire.
- Leaving the card first stops the `on_hover` animations, then plays the `on_leave` ones.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: Hover me
    show: true
animations:
  # glows while the mouse is over the card
  - trigger: on_hover
    preset: glow
    params:
      color: var(--lcars-orange)
      blur_max: 12
  # a short fade when it leaves
  - trigger: on_leave
    preset: fade
    duration: 300
    loop: 1
    alternate: true
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `trigger` | string | `on_load` | `on_hover` or `on_leave` |

## Entrance animations with `on_show`

**`on_show` plays each time the card is put on the page: when its view opens, when a visibility condition shows it, or when you come back from another view.** Use it, not `on_load`, for entrance animations.

- `on_load` plays once per card. Home Assistant builds a card hidden by a `visibility` condition and only attaches it when the condition is met, so an `on_load` animation has already run, out of sight, by the time it appears.
- `on_show` does not play again while the card stays on the page: state changes and re-renders don't replay it.
- Give several cards the same `on_show` animation with rising `delay` values to build a view up piece by piece when it opens.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: filled
text:
  name:
    content: Perimeter Armed
    show: true
animations:
  # slides in from the left and fades in, each time the card appears
  - trigger: on_show
    preset: slide
    params:
      from: left
      distance: 120
      duration: 600
  - trigger: on_show
    preset: fade
    params:
      from: 0
      to: 1
      duration: 600
```

::: details More about on_show
- **With a visibility condition:** add a `visibility` list to the card (here, a condition on `alarm_control_panel.home` with `state: armed_away`) and the entrance plays every time the alarm is armed. The docs show the card without one.
- **A re-render while it plays:** a card that re-renders just after it appears plays its entrance again from the start, so it is not cut short.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `trigger` | string | `on_load` | `on_show` plays each time the card appears; `on_load` once, when it first renders |

## on_datasource_change

**`on_datasource_change` plays each time a [data source](/core/datasources/) on the card gets a new value.** Use it to flash a reading when it updates.

- `datasource` names the source from the card's `data_sources`. The animation plays on every update, whatever the value.
- The data source must exist when the card loads; one that doesn't is skipped with a warning in the browser console.
- Shown as the animation entry only: it needs a data source defined on the card.

```yaml
animations:
  - trigger: on_datasource_change
    datasource: outdoor_temp
    preset: blink
    loop: 1
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `datasource` | string | required | The data source to watch, by name. A name with a dot (`outdoor_temp.rolling_avg`) still watches the whole source |

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/animations.html -->

# Card Animations

**Animations make a card move: a pulse when you tap it, a glow while a light is on, a slide-in when a view opens.** Every LCARdS card takes an `animations` list. Each entry names a `preset` (what moves) and a `trigger` (when it plays).

- A card can have as many entries as you like, each with its own trigger. An entry without `trigger` plays when the card loads.
- Each preset has its own duration, easing and looping; set `duration`, `loop` or `ease` on the entry to change them.
- When the device asks for less motion, animations jump to their end or stay still: see [Reduced motion](/core/animations/timing-and-easing#reduced-motion).

::: tip Try it
- The button and elbow editors have an animation editor on the **Effects** tab, with a field for every option on these pages; the data grid and MSD studios have one too.
- Every example here is live: tap the cards.
:::

| Page | Covers |
|------|--------|

## Quick start

**Two entries to start from: a bounce on every tap, and a pulse that runs while the light is on.** Tap the card to switch the light and watch the pulse start and stop.

- `params` holds the preset's own settings, here how far the pulse grows. The [Preset Reference](/core/animations/preset-reference) lists them for each preset.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.workbench
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
tap_action:
  action: toggle
animations:
  # a quick bounce on every tap
  - trigger: on_tap
    preset: bounce
    duration: 400
    params:
      scale_max: 1.08
      bounces: 2
  # a pulse while the light is on
  - trigger: on_entity_change
    entity: light.workbench
    preset: pulse
    loop: true
    while:
      state: "on"
    params:
      max_scale: 1.05
```

## Available presets

**`preset` picks what the animation does.** Each name links to its parameters and defaults in the [Preset Reference](/core/animations/preset-reference).

| Category | Presets |
|----------|---------|
| Motion | [`bounce`](/core/animations/preset-reference#bounce), [`blink`](/core/animations/preset-reference#blink), [`fade`](/core/animations/preset-reference#fade), [`glow`](/core/animations/preset-reference#glow), [`pulse`](/core/animations/preset-reference#pulse), [`rotate`](/core/animations/preset-reference#rotate), [`scale`](/core/animations/preset-reference#scale), [`scale-reset`](/core/animations/preset-reference#scale-reset), [`shake`](/core/animations/preset-reference#shake), [`skew`](/core/animations/preset-reference#skew), [`slide`](/core/animations/preset-reference#slide), [`strobe`](/core/animations/preset-reference#strobe) |
| Colour | [`cascade-color`](/core/animations/preset-reference#cascade-color), [`color-shift`](/core/animations/preset-reference#color-shift), [`shimmer`](/core/animations/preset-reference#shimmer) |
| Text | [`text-glitch`](/core/animations/preset-reference#text-glitch), [`text-reveal`](/core/animations/preset-reference#text-reveal), [`text-decode`](/core/animations/preset-reference#text-decode), [`text-scramble`](/core/animations/preset-reference#text-scramble), [`text-typewriter`](/core/animations/preset-reference#text-typewriter) |
| Visual effects | [`cascade`](/core/animations/preset-reference#cascade), [`flicker`](/core/animations/preset-reference#flicker), [`glitch`](/core/animations/preset-reference#glitch), [`ripple`](/core/animations/preset-reference#ripple) |
| SVG | [`draw`](/core/animations/preset-reference#draw), [`march`](/core/animations/preset-reference#march), [`morph`](/core/animations/preset-reference#morph) |
| Stagger | [`stagger-grid`](/core/animations/preset-reference#stagger-grid), [`stagger-wave`](/core/animations/preset-reference#stagger-wave), [`stagger-radial`](/core/animations/preset-reference#stagger-radial), [`stagger-flash`](/core/animations/preset-reference#stagger-flash), [`tap-ripple`](/core/animations/preset-reference#tap-ripple) |
| Effects | [`boot-sequence`](/core/animations/preset-reference#boot-sequence), [`sensor-sweep`](/core/animations/preset-reference#sensor-sweep) |
| Timeline | [`timeline-cascade`](/core/animations/preset-reference#timeline-cascade), [`timeline-attention`](/core/animations/preset-reference#timeline-attention), [`sequence`](/core/animations/preset-reference#sequence) |
| Advanced | [`chaos`](/core/animations/preset-reference#chaos), [`physics-spring`](/core/animations/preset-reference#physics-spring) |
| Utility | [`motionpath`](/core/animations/preset-reference#motionpath), [`set`](/core/animations/preset-reference#set), [`custom`](/core/animations/preset-reference#custom) |

## Targets

**Without a target an animation moves the whole card; `target` or `targets` picks parts of it, such as one text field.** Use it to scramble just the label, or blink just the state.

- The selector is a CSS selector looked for inside the card. Text fields carry `data-field-id` with their name, so `[data-field-id='name']` is the name text.
- `target` animates every element the selector matches; `targets` takes a list of selectors and animates the first match of each.
- `target: background` animates the card's [background animations](/core/effects/background-animations/binding-and-animation#animating-the-background) instead of its elements; `effect` picks one of them.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.workbench
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
  state:
    show: true
    content: "{entity.state}"
    position: center
tap_action:
  action: toggle
animations:
  # only the state text blinks when you tap
  - trigger: on_tap
    preset: blink
    target: "[data-field-id='state']"
    loop: 3
    duration: 200
```

::: details More about targets
- **A selector that matches nothing:** the animation still plays, on the whole card, with a warning in the browser console.
- **SVG elements with their own transform:** an element with its own `transform` (common in SVGs exported from Inkscape, such as MSD base images) keeps it, so it stays exactly where it was drawn. A `scale`, `rotate` or `pulse` animation on a rotated or scaled group then turns about a point slightly off the group's centre. Colour, opacity, stroke and draw animations are not affected.
- **MSD overlays:** on an MSD, a line or shape picks its drawn part by itself; see [MSD Animations and Rules](/cards/msd/animations).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `target` | string | the whole card | CSS selector for the elements to animate, or `background` for the card's background animations |
| `targets` | string / list | - | One or more CSS selectors; the first element each one matches is animated |
| `effect` | number | every effect | With `target: background`: the index of the `background_animation` entry to animate (`0` is the first, the bottom layer) |

## Putting it together

**One button with an entrance, tap feedback, a hover glow and two entity animations.** Hover over it with a mouse, tap it, and watch the light switch on and off.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.workbench
preset: lozenge
text:
  label:
    show: true
    content: Workbench
    position: top-left
  state:
    show: true
    content: "{entity.state}"
    position: center
tap_action:
  action: toggle
animations:
  # entrance: fades in once when the card loads
  - trigger: on_load
    preset: fade
    duration: 800
    params:
      from: 0
      to: 1
  # tap feedback: a quick bounce
  - trigger: on_tap
    preset: bounce
    duration: 400
    params:
      scale_max: 1.08
      bounces: 2
  # hover: glows while the mouse is over the card
  - trigger: on_hover
    preset: glow
    params:
      color: var(--lcars-orange)
      blur_max: 12
  # pulses while the light is on
  - trigger: on_entity_change
    entity: light.workbench
    preset: pulse
    loop: true
    while:
      state: "on"
    params:
      max_scale: 1.05
  # dims and comes back once when the light turns off
  - trigger: on_entity_change
    entity: light.workbench
    to_state: "off"
    preset: fade
    duration: 300
    loop: 1
    alternate: true
    params:
      from: 1
      to: 0.7
```

## Animation options

**Every key an animation entry takes, on every LCARdS card.** The same entries go in an MSD's `animations` lists; a rule's `apply.animations` takes a smaller set ([Rule-based Animations](/core/animations/rule-based-animations#animation-parameters)).

- `duration`, `delay`, `loop`, `alternate` and `ease` can also sit inside `params`; the entry's own key wins when both are set.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: Options
    show: true
animations:
  - id: tap-glow
    trigger: on_tap
    preset: glow
    duration: 600
    delay: 100
    loop: 2
    alternate: true
    ease: inOutSine
    params:
      color: var(--lcars-yellow)
```

::: details More about animation options
- **Unrecognised keys warn, they don't block.** A key the animation or its `params` doesn't know (a leftover from switching `preset`, say) gives a console warning but never stops the card loading. Only a wrong type on a key it does know (`duration: fast`) is an error. Clear leftovers anyway: some presets read `params` differently depending on what else is there.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `preset` | string | required | What the animation does: see [Available presets](#available-presets) |
| `trigger` | string | `on_load` | When it plays: see [Triggers](/core/animations/triggers) |
| `params` | object | the preset's defaults | The preset's own settings: see the [Preset Reference](/core/animations/preset-reference). Each value may be a [`map_range`](/core/animations/timing-and-easing#map-range-descriptors) |
| `id` | string | - | A name for the entry, for debugging: letters, digits, `-` and `_` |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | `false` keeps the entry but never plays it |
| `duration` | number / object | the preset's | Length of one play, ms, or a `map_range`: see [Timing](/core/animations/timing-and-easing#timing) |
| `delay` | number / object | `0` | Wait before it starts, ms, or a `map_range` |
| `loop` | boolean / number | the preset's | `true` repeats for ever, `false` plays once, a number repeats that many more times |
| `alternate` | boolean | the preset's | Play every other repeat backwards |
| `ease` | string / object | the preset's | The easing curve: see [Easing](/core/animations/timing-and-easing#easing-functions) |
| `essential_motion` | boolean | `false` | Keep playing when the device asks for reduced motion: see [Reduced motion](/core/animations/timing-and-easing#reduced-motion) |
| `target` | string | the whole card | What to animate: see [Targets](#targets) |
| `targets` | string / list | - | Several things to animate: see [Targets](#targets) |
| `effect` | number | every effect | With `target: background`: which background animation |
| `entity` | string | - | `on_entity_change`: the entity to watch: see [Entity Change Triggers](/core/animations/entity-change-triggers#watching-an-entity) |
| `attribute` | string | the state | `on_entity_change`: an attribute to watch instead of the state; `brightness_pct` gives a light's brightness as 0–100 |
| `from_state` | string | - | `on_entity_change`: play only when the value changes from this |
| `to_state` | string | - | `on_entity_change`: play only when the value changes to this |
| `while` | object | - | `on_entity_change`: play while this holds and stop when it no longer does: see [while](/core/animations/entity-change-triggers#lifecycle-conditions-while) |
| `check_on_load` | boolean | `true` | `on_entity_change`: also check the entity when the card loads |
| `datasource` | string | - | `on_datasource_change`: the data source to watch: see [on_datasource_change](/core/animations/triggers#on-datasource-change) |

# Borg Actions

**The `lcards.borg_assimilate` and `lcards.borg_deassimilate` actions start and end the [Borg assimilation](/core/borg) from automations, scripts, dashboard buttons and the Developer Tools Actions panel.** Without targeting they reach every connected browser.

- The assimilation runs in each browser that is connected when the action fires. It is not stored: a reload, or a browser opened later, shows the normal dashboard, so a reload also ends it.
- [Borg Assimilation](/core/borg) explains what happens and the layers format; the [console API](/core/borg#console-api) takes the same options in camelCase.

## lcards.borg_assimilate

**`lcards.borg_assimilate` starts the assimilation; its fields tune the intro, the transition, the font, the sound and the effects left after the intro.** With no fields, the intro waits for a click and the default effects follow it.

- The flat intro fields (`site_count` to `overrun`) are shortcuts for `intro_layers.canvas`. When both are given, the keys in `intro_layers.canvas` win and the flat fields fill the rest.
- `intro_layers.canvas` takes the [intro.canvas](/core/borg#intro-canvas) keys in camelCase or snake_case (`site_count`, `tendrils_per_site`, `tendril_length`, `particle_count`, `glow_color`, `cube_style`). There `cube` is `true` or `false`, and `cubeStyle` picks the style.
- `intro_layers` and `persistent_layers` are maps, not lists; [Layers format](/core/borg#layers-format) describes them.

```yaml live
# On this page: the classic cube, auto-dismissed after 8 seconds
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: ASSIMILATE
    show: true
tap_action:
  action: perform-action
  perform_action: lcards.borg_assimilate
  data:
    intro_duration: 8000
    cube: classic
```

The examples below run from an automation or a script:

```yaml
# Every browser; the intro waits for a click
action: lcards.borg_assimilate
```

```yaml
# Auto-dismiss after 12 seconds, with a gentle fade
action: lcards.borg_assimilate
data:
  intro_duration: 12000
  transition_style: fade_only
```

```yaml
# More injection sites, denser tendrils, longer reach
action: lcards.borg_assimilate
data:
  site_count: 12
  tendrils_per_site: 14
  tendril_length: 900
  particle_count: 3
```

```yaml
# No cube, gentler corruption, the dashboard still visible behind the front
action: lcards.borg_assimilate
data:
  cube: none
  corruption: 0.2
  overrun: 0.3
```

```yaml
# Flat shortcuts plus a blurred backdrop for the intro
action: lcards.borg_assimilate
data:
  intro_duration: 10000
  site_count: 12
  intro_layers:
    backdrop:
      preset: blur
      amount: 6px
```

```yaml
# Only the colours and the font: no effects after the intro
action: lcards.borg_assimilate
data:
  suppress_persistent: true
```

```yaml
# A colour tint only after the intro
action: lcards.borg_assimilate
data:
  persistent_layers:
    color:
      preset: color-tint
      color: alpha(var(--lcars-green), 0.2)
```

::: details More about lcards.borg_assimilate
- **No effects after the intro:** `persistent_layers: {}` does the same as `suppress_persistent: true`.
- **Palette hue:** the action has no hue field; the console's `paletteHue` and the Config Panel's Connectivity tab set one.
- **Ranges:** values outside a field's range are refused by Home Assistant with an error, before anything reaches a browser.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `intro_duration` | number | - | Ends the intro after this many ms, 1000 to 60000. Without it the intro waits for a click; a click still ends it earlier |
| `site_count` | number | `8` | Injection sites on the screen, 1 to 20 |
| `tendrils_per_site` | number | `5` | Tendrils per injection site, 1 to 20 |
| `tendril_length` | number | `600` | Longest tendril reach in pixels, 100 to 1200 |
| `particle_count` | number | `2` | Nano-probe particles per tendril, 0 to 6; `0` turns them off |
| `renderer` | string | `auto` | `auto` or `webgl`: the WebGL intro where the browser supports it; `canvas`: the [classic intro](/core/borg#classic-intro) |
| `cube` | string | `detailed` | WebGL intro: `detailed` (solid cube with machinery, lattice, glows and halo), `classic` (wireframe) or `none` (no cube) |
| `corruption` | number | `0.5` | WebGL intro: signal corruption strength, 0 to 1; `0` turns it off |
| `overrun` | number | `0.65` | WebGL intro: darkness behind the assimilation front, 0 to 1 |
| `transition_style` | string | `blur_fade` | Palette transition: `blur_fade`, `flash`, `fade_only` or `off` |
| `palette_hue` | number | `110` | The hue (0 to 359) the palette shifts toward: `110` is Borg yellow-green, `240` blue, `0` red |
| `font_swap` | boolean | `true` | `false` keeps the dashboard font; everything else still runs |
| `sound` | string | the `borg_assimilate` [sound event](/core/borg#sounds) | A sound for this call: a file URL (`/local/sounds/borg.mp3`), a media library id or a sound asset key; `none` for silence |
| `suppress_persistent` | boolean | `false` | `true` leaves no effects after the intro. Ignored when `persistent_layers` is set |
| `intro_layers` | map | - | Layers for the intro, merged slot by slot with the defaults; see [Layers format](/core/borg#layers-format) |
| `persistent_layers` | map | - | Layers kept after the intro, replacing the defaults; wins over `suppress_persistent` |
| [Targeting](#targeting) | | | `target_device_ids`, `target_device_names`, `target_user_ids`, `target_user_names` |

## lcards.borg_deassimilate

**`lcards.borg_deassimilate` restores the dashboard: a short glitch outro, then the colours of the alert mode from before the assimilation, the normal font and screen.** A browser that is not assimilated ignores it.

```yaml
# Every browser, with the default glitch outro
action: lcards.borg_deassimilate
```

```yaml
# At once, with no outro
action: lcards.borg_deassimilate
data:
  with_outro: false
```

```yaml
# A shorter, stronger glitch
action: lcards.borg_deassimilate
data:
  outro_layers:
    canvas:
      preset: glitch
      duration: 800
      intensity: 0.6
  revert_transition_style: fade_only
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `with_outro` | boolean | `true` | `false` restores at once, with no outro and no wait |
| `outro_layers` | map | glitch on `canvas` for 1200 ms | Outro layers, replacing the default. The longest `duration` in them sets the wait, at least 1200 ms. See [glitch](/core/effects/screen-effects#glitch) |
| `revert_transition_style` | string | `fade_only` | Palette transition back to normal: `fade_only`, `flash`, `blur_fade` or `off` |
| `sound` | string | the `borg_deassimilate` [sound event](/core/borg#sounds) | A sound for this call, as for `lcards.borg_assimilate` |
| [Targeting](#targeting) | | | `target_device_ids`, `target_device_names`, `target_user_ids`, `target_user_names` |

## Targeting

**The targeting fields limit either action to some devices or users; without them every connected browser runs it.** They work as on every other `lcards.*` action.

- A browser runs the action when its device or its user is in the lists.
- The Borg never writes `input_select.lcards_alert_mode`, targeted or not, so other browsers keep their alert mode.
- If the targets match no device or user at all (a typo in a name, say), the action fails with an error rather than reaching every browser.
- [Users & Devices](/configuration/users-devices) shows each browser's device name and id; `window.lcards.targeting.getMyIds()` in the browser console returns them too.

```yaml
# Only the living room TV
action: lcards.borg_assimilate
data:
  intro_duration: 10000
  target_device_names:
    - Living Room TV
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `target_device_ids` | list | all devices | Browser device ids (the `lcards_device_id` each browser stores) |
| `target_device_names` | list | all devices | Device display names, set in the LCARdS Config Panel or with `?lcards_device=`, any case. A name shared by several devices matches all of them |
| `target_user_ids` | list | all users | Home Assistant user ids |
| `target_user_names` | list | all users | Home Assistant user display names, any case |

## In an automation

**An automation can assimilate on a schedule and restore after a delay.** This one assimilates every browser at 20:00 on Halloween night and restores them 30 minutes later.

```yaml
alias: Halloween Borg mode
triggers:
  - trigger: time
    at: "20:00:00"
conditions:
  - condition: template
    value_template: "{{ now().month == 10 and now().day == 31 }}"
actions:
  - action: lcards.borg_assimilate
    data:
      intro_duration: 10000
  - delay:
      minutes: 30
  - action: lcards.borg_deassimilate
```

# Borg Assimilation

**Borg assimilation is an LCARdS Easter egg that takes over the whole dashboard: Borg colours, a Borg font, a full-screen assimilation and lingering screen effects, until you restore it.** Start it from an automation, a dashboard button or the browser console.

- **Colours:** the palette shifts toward Borg yellow-green (hue 110°), slightly desaturated and darker. `paletteHue` picks another hue.
- **Font:** LCARS text switches to the `lcards_borg` typeface.
- **Intro:** injection sites appear with a breathing glow and grow tendrils, an assimilation front spreads out and overruns the screen with Borg circuitry, a Borg cube emerges at the centre and bursts of signal corruption tear the picture. It stays until someone clicks the screen, or until a timeout.
- **After the intro:** screen effects stay on (by default a light glitch, a green tint and a saturation boost) until the dashboard is restored. Restoring plays a short glitch, then puts the colours, font and screen back.

::: tip Try it
The buttons in the [Quick start](#quick-start) assimilate this page and restore it. In the LCARdS Config Panel, the **Connectivity** tab's **Resistance is Futile** display style runs the assimilation when the connection to Home Assistant is lost; **Simulate Disconnect** shows it.
:::

| Page | Covers |
|------|--------|
| [Borg Actions](/core/borg-actions) | `lcards.borg_assimilate` and `lcards.borg_deassimilate`: every field, examples and targeting |
| [Screen Effects](/core/effects/screen-effects#preset-reference) | The presets the intro, persistent and outro layers can use |

## Quick start

**The `lcards.borg_assimilate` action assimilates every connected browser, and `lcards.borg_deassimilate` restores them.** On this page the two buttons below run it here only.

- Clicking anywhere on the screen ends the intro; the screen effects after it stay until you restore.
- The assimilation is not stored: a page reload, or a browser opened later, shows the normal dashboard.

```yaml live
# Assimilates this page; the intro ends after 10 seconds or on a click
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: ASSIMILATE
    show: true
style:
  card:
    color:
      background:
        default: var(--lcars-green)
tap_action:
  action: perform-action
  perform_action: lcards.borg_assimilate
  data:
    intro_duration: 10000
```

```yaml live
# Restores this page
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: RESTORE
    show: true
tap_action:
  action: perform-action
  perform_action: lcards.borg_deassimilate
```

From an automation or a script (not live here):

```yaml
action: lcards.borg_assimilate
```

From the browser console:

```js
window.lcards.borg.assimilate()     // window.lcards.alert.borg() does the same
window.lcards.borg.status           // true while assimilated
window.lcards.borg.deassimilate()
```

## Sequence of events

**Assimilation changes the colours and the font first, plays the intro until it is dismissed, then applies the persistent layers.** Restoring plays the outro, then reverts everything.

When assimilation starts:

1. The `borg_assimilate` sound plays (or the `sound` option's sound), and the palette starts shifting to Borg colours with the `transitionStyle` transition.
2. The `lcards_borg` font loads and replaces the LCARS font, at the same time (skipped with `fontSwap: false`).
3. The intro layers show: the `borg-assimilation` effect on the canvas slot, with the intro's `backdrop` and `color` layers behind and over it.
4. The intro stays until someone clicks anywhere on the screen, or until `duration` ms have passed.
5. All intro layers are cleared, and the persistent layers are applied. They stay until the dashboard is restored.

When it is restored:

1. If the intro is still showing, it ends at once, without a click.
2. The `borg_deassimilate` sound plays (or the `sound` option's sound), and the outro layers show (skipped with `withOutro: false`).
3. After the longest `duration` in the outro layers, and at least 1200 ms, the palette goes back to the alert mode that was active before the assimilation, with the `revertTransitionStyle` transition.
4. The Borg font is removed (if it was swapped in) and every screen effect is cleared.

::: details More about the sequence
- **Twice in a row:** starting an assimilation while one is running, or restoring when nothing is assimilated, does nothing (a warning is logged). The alert mode to go back to is the one from before the first start.
- **The alert mode afterwards:** restoring returns the colours to the alert mode that was active when the assimilation started (red alert stays red alert). It is `green_alert` when that mode is unknown or was itself a Borg alert. The `input_select.lcards_alert_mode` helper is never changed by the Borg.
- **Clicks during the intro:** the intro takes every click until it is dismissed; after it, the dashboard works normally under the persistent layers.
- **All screen effects:** restoring clears every screen effect, including one started separately with `lcards.trigger_effect`.
- **The font:** the Borg typeface replaces `--lcars-font` and `--lcars-fallback-font`, so text in another font keeps it.
- **Palette hue:** a custom `paletteHue` lasts for that assimilation only; restoring resets it.
:::

## intro.canvas

**`intro.canvas` sets up the assimilation intro itself: how many injection sites, how many tendrils, their colours, the cube and the signal corruption.** The canvas slot always plays the `borg-assimilation` effect during the intro; a `preset` given here is ignored.

- The WebGL intro (the default) runs on the graphics card in a worker, so the dashboard stays responsive. Browsers without WebGL2 play the [classic intro](#classic-intro).
- With the WebGL intro, `particleCount` sets the light pulses travelling along each tendril.
- In the [actions](/core/borg-actions#lcards-borg-assimilate) these keys are flat fields in snake_case (`site_count`, `tendrils_per_site`, ...), or go under `intro_layers.canvas` in either spelling.
- On a slow wall tablet, lower `corruption`, use the classic cube or none, or play the classic intro.

```yaml
# From an automation: a denser intro, no cube
action: lcards.borg_assimilate
data:
  intro_layers:
    canvas:
      siteCount: 12
      tendrilsPerSite: 10
      tendrilLength: 800
      particleCount: 3
      cube: false
      seed: 7
```

```js
// The same from the browser console
window.lcards.borg.assimilate({
  intro: {
    canvas: {
      siteCount: 12,
      tendrilsPerSite: 10,
      tendrilLength: 800,
      particleCount: 3,
      cube: false,
      seed: 7,
    },
  },
})
```

::: details More about the intro
- **Reduced motion:** with reduced motion set on the device, the intro draws its finished picture once, with no flicker, tearing or movement.
- **No OffscreenCanvas:** in a browser without OffscreenCanvas and Web Workers the intro canvas draws nothing; the intro's backdrop and colour layers still show and the screen still waits for a click or the `duration`.
- **On its own:** the `borg-assimilation` effect can also run without the rest of the assimilation, through `lcards.trigger_effect`; see [Screen Effects](/core/effects/screen-effects#borg-assimilation). Played that way it starts from its own defaults (7 sites, 8 tendrils per site, green colours).
- **Frame rate:** with the console at debug level (`window.lcards.setGlobalLogLevel('debug')`) the WebGL intro logs its frame rate.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `siteCount` | number | `8` | Injection sites on the screen, 1 to 20 |
| `tendrilsPerSite` | number | `5` | Tendrils grown from each injection site, 1 to 24 (1 to 20 as the actions' flat `tendrils_per_site`) |
| `tendrilLength` | number | `600` | Longest tendril reach in pixels, 100 to 1200 |
| `particleCount` | number | `2` | Nano-probe particles (WebGL: light pulses) travelling each tendril, 0 to 6; `0` turns them off |
| `color` | string | `var(--lcars-martian)` | Tendril and injection site colour: any CSS colour, variable or LCARdS colour expression |
| `glowColor` | string | `var(--lcards-yellow)` | Glow at each injection site and around the particles |
| `renderer` | string | `auto` | `auto` and `webgl` play the WebGL intro where the browser supports WebGL2; `canvas` plays the classic intro |
| `cube` | boolean | `true` | WebGL intro: a rotating Borg cube emerges at the centre; `false` leaves it out |
| `cubeStyle` | string | `detailed` | WebGL intro: `detailed` is a solid cube, corner first, covered in machinery with a rail lattice, pulsing glows and a soft halo; `classic` is the lighter glowing wireframe cube |
| `corruption` | number | `0.5` | WebGL intro: strength of the signal corruption bursts (block displacement, scanline tearing, colour fringing), 0 to 1; `0` turns them off |
| `overrun` | number | `0.65` | WebGL intro: how dark the screen gets behind the assimilation front, 0 to 1; `0` draws only the circuitry over the dashboard |
| `seed` | number | - | WebGL intro: a number gives the same layout every time |

### Classic intro

**The classic intro is the original Canvas2D animation: signal flicker, injection sites, Bézier tendrils with nano-probe particles and bridges between them.** Set `renderer: canvas` to play it; every `intro.canvas` key above except the WebGL ones applies.

- In the Config Panel, pick **Classic (Canvas2D)** under Renderer in the Borg canvas effect.

```yaml
# From an automation
action: lcards.borg_assimilate
data:
  renderer: canvas
```

```js
// From the browser console
window.lcards.borg.assimilate({ intro: { canvas: { renderer: 'canvas' } } })
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `renderer` | string | `auto` | `canvas` plays the classic intro; `auto` and `webgl` play the WebGL intro where the browser supports WebGL2 |

## Layers format

**The intro, the persistent layers and the outro each take a layers map: one entry per screen effect slot, each with a `preset` and that preset's settings.** It is the same format as `lcards.trigger_effect`.

- The slots are `canvas`, `backdrop` and `color`; other names are ignored, and so is a slot without a `preset` (except `intro.canvas`, which never takes one).
- `intro` is merged with the defaults slot by slot: give `backdrop` and you replace the default intro backdrop, while the default `color` layer stays. A slot with no `preset` (for example `backdrop: {}`) turns that default layer off.
- `persistentLayers` and `outroLayers` replace their defaults entirely. An empty map (`persistentLayers: {}`) leaves no effects after the intro.
- [Screen Effects](/core/effects/screen-effects#preset-reference) lists every preset and its settings. The ones most used here are `scanlines`, `glitch` and `static` (canvas), `color-tint` and `vignette` (color) and `blur` and `saturate` (backdrop).

```yaml
# From an automation: blurred intro, then scanlines and a green tint
action: lcards.borg_assimilate
data:
  intro_layers:
    backdrop:
      preset: blur
      amount: 6px
  persistent_layers:
    canvas:
      preset: scanlines
      lineHeight: 3
      opacity: 0.2
      scroll: 2
    color:
      preset: color-tint
      color: alpha(var(--lcars-green), 0.12)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `intro.canvas` | map | see [intro.canvas](#intro-canvas) | The `borg-assimilation` effect's settings; no `preset` |
| `intro.backdrop` | map | `saturate`, `amount: 200%` | A layer behind the intro; cleared when the intro ends |
| `intro.color` | map | `color-tint`, `color: rgba(0,60,0,0.25)` | A colour layer over the intro; cleared when the intro ends |
| `persistentLayers.canvas` | map | `glitch`, `intensity: 0.08`, `maxShift: 400`, `bandHeight: 3`, `fps: 20` | Canvas layer kept after the intro |
| `persistentLayers.color` | map | `color-tint`, `color: rgba(0, 60, 0, 0.10)` | Colour layer kept after the intro |
| `persistentLayers.backdrop` | map | `saturate`, `amount: 200%` | Backdrop layer kept after the intro |
| `outroLayers.canvas` | map | `glitch`, `duration: 1200`, `intensity: 0.4`, `opacity: 0.7` | The outro; any outro layer's `duration` sets how long the outro plays, at least 1200 ms |

## Console API

**`window.lcards.borg.assimilate(opts)` and `window.lcards.borg.deassimilate(opts)` run the Borg from the browser console, with the same options as the actions in camelCase.** Open the developer tools (F12) on any LCARdS dashboard.

- `window.lcards.borg.status` is `true` while assimilated.
- The console calls affect this browser only.

```js
// Blue instead of Borg green, auto-dismiss after 10 seconds, keep the font
window.lcards.borg.assimilate({
  duration: 10000,
  paletteHue: 240,
  fontSwap: false,
  transitionStyle: 'fade_only',
})

// Restore at once, with no outro
window.lcards.borg.deassimilate({ withOutro: false })
```

### assimilate(opts?) options

**The options of `assimilate()`: the intro's timeout and transition, the layers, the hue, the font and the sound.** As an action, the same options have snake_case names; [Borg Actions](/core/borg-actions#lcards-borg-assimilate) has them all.

```yaml
# The action equivalent of the console call above
action: lcards.borg_assimilate
data:
  intro_duration: 10000
  font_swap: false
  transition_style: fade_only
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `duration` | number | `0` | Ends the intro after this many ms; `0` waits for a click. A click still ends it earlier |
| `transitionStyle` | string | `blur_fade` | Palette transition: `blur_fade`, `flash`, `fade_only` or `off` |
| `intro` | map | see [Layers format](#layers-format) | Intro layers, merged slot by slot with the defaults |
| `persistentLayers` | map | see [Layers format](#layers-format) | Layers kept after the intro; `{}` for none |
| `paletteHue` | number | `110` | The hue (0 to 359) the palette shifts toward: `110` is Borg yellow-green, `240` blue, `0` red. As an action: `palette_hue` |
| `fontSwap` | boolean | `true` | `false` keeps the dashboard font; everything else still runs |
| `sound` | string | the `borg_assimilate` [sound event](#sounds) | A sound for this call: a file URL (`/local/sounds/borg.mp3`), a media library id (`media-source://...`) or a sound asset key; `none` plays nothing |

### deassimilate(opts?) options

**The options of `deassimilate()`: whether to play the outro, its layers, the transition back and the sound.**

```yaml
# From an automation: a shorter, stronger outro
action: lcards.borg_deassimilate
data:
  outro_layers:
    canvas:
      preset: glitch
      duration: 800
      intensity: 0.6
  revert_transition_style: fade_only
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `withOutro` | boolean | `true` | `false` restores at once, with no outro and no wait |
| `outroLayers` | map | see [Layers format](#layers-format) | Outro layers, replacing the default glitch; the longest `duration` in them sets the wait, at least 1200 ms. See [glitch](/core/effects/screen-effects#glitch) |
| `revertTransitionStyle` | string | `fade_only` | Palette transition back to normal: `fade_only`, `flash`, `blur_fade` or `off` |
| `sound` | string | the `borg_deassimilate` [sound event](#sounds) | A sound for this call, as for `assimilate()` |

## Sounds

**Assimilation and restoring each fire a sound event, Borg assimilation (`borg_assimilate`) and Borg deassimilation (`borg_deassimilate`), in the Alerts category.** LCARdS ships no Borg audio, so both are silent until you give them a sound.

- **Config Panel:** in the **Sounds** tab's overrides, pick a file for the two Borg rows from the Home Assistant media library.
- **Your own sound scheme** (saved from the Config Panel, or a pack's `sound_schemes`): map the events to a sound asset key, a media library id or a URL. A file in the `www` folder of your Home Assistant configuration is served under `/local/`.
- **One call:** the `sound` option (console) or field (action) plays a sound for that call only; `none` keeps it silent.
- The Alerts switch and the master sound switch apply to all three.

```yaml
# In a sound scheme
borg_assimilate: /local/sounds/borg.mp3
borg_deassimilate: /local/sounds/borg-restore.mp3
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `borg_assimilate` | sound | silent | Plays as assimilation starts |
| `borg_deassimilate` | sound | silent | Plays as restoring starts |
