# Background Animations

**`background_animation` draws moving layers behind a card's content: grids, starfields, nebulae, an LCARS data cascade, a warp field, a rotating planet.** It works on the button, elbow, slider, MSD and astrometrics cards.

- The value is a list of effects. Each entry names a `preset` and gives that preset's keys in `config`; the first entry is the bottom layer.
- The background sits behind the card's own fill, so it shows best on a card with a transparent fill, such as the button's `outline` preset, or inside an elbow's arms.
- On the MSD card it goes under `msd:` (`msd.background_animation`); on every other card it is a top-level key.

::: tip Try it
- The button and elbow editors have a Background Animation section on the Effects tab, with every preset's keys and a live preview. The MSD and Astrometrics Studios have one too.
:::

| Page | Covers |
|------|--------|
| [Preset Reference](./background-animations/preset-reference) | Every preset and its `config` keys |
| [Stacking and Zoom](./background-animations/stacking-and-zoom) | Layering several effects, the zoom wrapper, example backgrounds |
| [Binding and Animation](./background-animations/binding-and-animation) | Keys that follow an entity, animating the background from triggers and rules, the animatable keys |

---

## Quick start

**Two backgrounds to start from: a scrolling grid behind a button, and a data cascade inside an elbow's arms.**

- Give the card some height (`grid_options.rows` in a sections view) so there is room to see the effect.
- On an elbow, `inset: auto` keeps the background inside the bars; see [Canvas options](#canvas-options).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: outline
text:
  name:
    content: SENSOR GRID
    show: true
grid_options:
  rows: 3
background_animation:
  - preset: grid
    config:
      line_spacing: 30
      color: alpha(var(--lcars-orange), 0.4)
      scroll_speed_x: 15
      scroll_speed_y: 15
```

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-elbow
grid_options:
  rows: 4
elbow:
  type: header-left
  segment:
    bar_width: 90
    bar_height: 20
    color: var(--lcars-orange)
background_animation:
  inset: auto # inside the bars
  effects:
    - preset: cascade
```

## Available presets

**`preset` picks the effect; the [Preset Reference](./background-animations/preset-reference) lists each one's `config` keys.** There are seventeen.

- `config` is optional for most presets: a key you leave out takes the preset's default. `image` needs a `source`.
- The presets marked WebGL draw on the GPU where the browser has WebGL and fall back to a Canvas2D version where it does not; see [WebGL presets](#webgl-presets).

| Preset | Draws |
|--------|-------|
| [`grid`](./background-animations/preset-reference#grid) | A grid with optional major and minor lines; polar rings and spokes (`pattern: polar`); on WebGL also a perspective floor (`view: floor`) or a cylinder, dome, sphere or funnel (`surface`) |
| [`grid-diagonal`](./background-animations/preset-reference#grid-diagonal) | Diagonal hatching (WebGL) |
| [`grid-hexagonal`](./background-animations/preset-reference#grid-hexagonal) | A honeycomb (WebGL) |
| [`starfield`](./background-animations/preset-reference#starfield) | Scrolling stars in parallax depth layers |
| [`nebula`](./background-animations/preset-reference#nebula) | Soft nebula clouds; `volumetric: true` shades them with noise on WebGL |
| [`contour-field`](./background-animations/preset-reference#contour-field) | Banded contours like a star chart (WebGL) |
| [`cascade`](./background-animations/preset-reference#cascade) | The LCARS data waterfall: rows of numbers cycling colour |
| [`level`](./background-animations/preset-reference#level) | A fill bar with waves and sloshing, for a tank or gauge |
| [`fluid`](./background-animations/preset-reference#fluid) | A swirling colour wash (WebGL) |
| [`plasma`](./background-animations/preset-reference#plasma) | Two-colour plasma bands (WebGL) |
| [`flow`](./background-animations/preset-reference#flow) | Streaks streaming in one direction |
| [`shimmer`](./background-animations/preset-reference#shimmer) | A highlight band sweeping across |
| [`scanlines`](./background-animations/preset-reference#scanlines) | CRT-style scanlines |
| [`image`](./background-animations/preset-reference#image) | An image, fixed or from an entity |
| [`solid`](./background-animations/preset-reference#solid) | A flat colour |
| [`warp-starfield`](./background-animations/preset-reference#warp-starfield) | Stars flying at you in 3D, streaking at speed (WebGL; `starfield` without it) |
| [`holo-sphere`](./background-animations/preset-reference#holo-sphere) | A rotating wireframe planet with a scan band (WebGL; the same look on Canvas2D) |

## WebGL presets

**Some presets draw on the GPU with three.js where the browser has WebGL, and fall back to Canvas2D where it does not, so the background never goes blank.** `renderer` on the entry chooses.

- `warp-starfield` and `holo-sphere` are three.js scenes. Without WebGL, `warp-starfield` draws a `starfield` and `holo-sphere` the same sphere on Canvas2D.
- `grid`, `grid-diagonal` and `grid-hexagonal` draw the same pixels as their Canvas2D versions in the flat view. On WebGL they also do a perspective floor with a camera ([grid views](./background-animations/preset-reference#grid-views-and-camera)), cylinders, domes and spheres seen from outside or inside ([grid surfaces](./background-animations/preset-reference#grid-surfaces)), and funnels that can morph and ripple ([grid wells](./background-animations/preset-reference#grid-wells)).
- `contour-field`, `plasma` and `fluid` draw the same field on the GPU, with the same keys. On WebGL their noise keys become [animatable](./background-animations/binding-and-animation#animatable-keys).
- `nebula` uses WebGL only with `volumetric: true` (opt-in, because it changes the look); without WebGL it draws the plain clouds.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: outline
text:
  name:
    content: WARP
    show: true
grid_options:
  rows: 3
background_animation:
  - preset: warp-starfield
    config:
      count: 400
```

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: outline
text:
  name:
    content: CANVAS2D
    show: true
grid_options:
  rows: 3
background_animation:
  # always the Canvas2D version: for warp-starfield, a starfield
  - preset: warp-starfield
    renderer: canvas
    config:
      count: 400
```

::: details More about WebGL presets
- **One context:** a WebGL preset loads only when a card uses it, and all of them share one WebGL context across the dashboard. Each sits in the stack like any other entry.
- **Why the GPU helps the noise presets:** on the CPU, `contour-field`, `plasma` and `fluid` work out their whole field when they first draw, resize or change alert colours, which can pause the page for a moment on a large background. On the GPU they don't.
- **A lost context:** if a three.js scene fails to start or loses its context, that entry switches to its Canvas2D version for good.
- **Off-screen:** a three.js scene gives the shared context back while its card is off the page.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `renderer` | string | `auto` | `auto`: WebGL when the browser has it, Canvas2D otherwise. `webgl`: the same, stated outright. `canvas`: always the Canvas2D version (no GPU use). Presets that are Canvas2D only ignore it |

## Effect options

**The keys of one entry in the list: which preset, its settings, and how it is drawn.** Any number of entries can be stacked; see [Stacking and Zoom](./background-animations/stacking-and-zoom).

- Colours in `config` take every LCARdS colour form: CSS variables, `theme:` tokens, `alpha()` and the other computed colours, rgba and hex. See [Colours](../colours).
- Any `config` value can follow an entity with `map_range` or a template; see [Binding and Animation](./background-animations/binding-and-animation).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: outline
text:
  name:
    content: DEFLECTOR
    show: true
grid_options:
  rows: 3
background_animation:
  - preset: starfield
    config:
      count: 150
      speed: 0.5 # half speed
  # kept in the list, drawn only once enabled
  - preset: grid
    enabled: false
    config:
      color: alpha(var(--lcars-orange), 0.3)
```

::: details More about effect options
- **`speed` and the zoom wrapper:** `speed` also runs the [zoom](./background-animations/stacking-and-zoom#zoom-wrapper) cycle faster, whether it is fixed in `config`, bound to an entity or animated.
- **Disabled entries keep their place:** an entry with `enabled: false` still counts when an animation picks an entry by number (`effect:`).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `preset` | string | required | The effect: see [Available presets](#available-presets) |
| `config` | object | the preset's defaults | The preset's own keys: see the [Preset Reference](./background-animations/preset-reference) |
| `config.speed` | number | `1` | Time multiplier for every preset that moves (all but `image` and `solid`): `2` is twice as fast, `0` freezes it. On `shimmer` it is the sweep speed in px per second (default `6`) |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | `false` keeps the entry in the list but draws nothing |
| `renderer` | string | `auto` | For presets with a WebGL version: see [WebGL presets](#webgl-presets) |
| `transition` | number | `500` | Milliseconds an [entity-bound](./background-animations/binding-and-animation#entity-binding) value takes to glide to a new value. `0` snaps |
| `zoom` | object | - | Draws the effect as layers zooming outward: see [Zoom wrapper](./background-animations/stacking-and-zoom#zoom-wrapper) |

## Canvas options

**To set where the background is drawn, or its frame rate, write `background_animation` as an object with the list under `effects`.** `inset` keeps the canvas off the card's edges, for a sidebar or footer bar that should stay clear.

- `inset: auto` works on elbow cards: it fits the canvas inside the elbow's arms and follows the bars when they change. The [elbow's appearance page](/cards/elbow/appearance#background-animation-inset) covers how it treats each elbow type. On every other card `auto` means no inset.
- A side you leave out of an `inset` object is `0`.
- `fps` caps how often the background redraws. It is read only in the object form.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: outline
text:
  name:
    content: CANVAS INSET
    show: true
grid_options:
  rows: 3
background_animation:
  inset:
    left: 60 # keep the left 60 px clear
    bottom: 20
  effects:
    - preset: grid-hexagonal
      config:
        hex_radius: 20
        color: alpha(var(--lcars-ice), 0.4)
```

::: details More about canvas options
- **Frame rate:** the default cap of 30 frames per second is plenty for ambient motion and spares low-end devices such as wall tablets. Set `60` for a smoother look on a desktop or high-refresh screen; `0` removes the cap. The editor's Canvas Settings section sets it.
- **Size:** the canvas follows the card's size as it changes (a sections grid settling, the sidebar opening), less the inset, and is never smaller than 1 px.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `background_animation` | list / object | - | A list of effects, or an object with `effects`, `inset` and `fps` |
| `effects` | list | required in the object form | The effects, bottom layer first: see [Effect options](#effect-options) |
| `inset` | string / object | none | `auto`: inside an elbow's arms (no inset on other cards). An object: px per side |
| `inset.top` | number | `0` | Space kept clear at the top, px |
| `inset.right` | number | `0` | Space kept clear on the right, px |
| `inset.bottom` | number | `0` | Space kept clear at the bottom, px |
| `inset.left` | number | `0` | Space kept clear on the left, px |
| `fps` | number | `30` | Most frames per second the background draws. `0`: no cap |

## Troubleshooting

**When a background doesn't show, looks wrong or slows a device down, check these first.**

- **Nothing shows:** the card's own fill may cover it (try the button's `outline` preset), the colour may be fully transparent, or the card may have no height to draw in. A preset name the card doesn't know is logged in the browser console and that entry is skipped.
- **A colour doesn't resolve:** check that a `theme:` token path exists in the active theme ([Themes](../themes/)). Quote hex colours (`"#ff9966"`): unquoted, YAML reads everything after `#` as a comment.
- **A device slows down:** use fewer stacked effects and fewer zoom layers, wider `line_spacing`, and set scroll speeds to `0` where you don't need the motion.

::: details More about how a background runs
- **Pauses on its own:** the background stops drawing while its card is scrolled off the page or the browser tab is hidden, and carries on where it left off.
- **Reduced motion:** when the device asks for reduced motion, the background draws one frame and holds it.
- **A struggling device:** if the frame rate falls very low, the background pauses itself and tries again later.
- **Patterns that line up:** stacked grids line up best with the same `line_spacing` (or multiples of it), and major line intervals that divide the card's size evenly.
- **A different system:** [Animations](../animations) animate a card's own parts; background animations are drawn on a canvas behind them. An animation can still [target the background](./background-animations/binding-and-animation#animating-the-background). [Filters](./filters) are SVG filter effects on the card.
:::

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/effects/filters.html -->

# Filters

**Filters change how a whole card looks: blur it, brighten it, take the colour out, tint it, give it a shadow or warp it.** Stack several in a list to combine them.

- `filters` works on the [button](../../cards/button/) and [elbow](../../cards/elbow/) cards, and on the [data grid](../../cards/data-grid/) with CSS filters only. The MSD card has the same filters for its blueprint as `base_svg.filters` ([Base SVG Filters](../../cards/msd/base-svg-filters)).
- There are two kinds: the browser's CSS filters, which most looks need, and SVG filter primitives for what CSS can't do, such as a real colour tint or a distortion.

## filters

**`filters` is a list of filters applied to the card, one after another.** Each entry names a `type` and gives its `value`; SVG filters also need `mode: svg`.

- The CSS filters run first, in list order, then the SVG filters, chained in list order. Where you put an SVG entry among the CSS ones makes no difference.
- On the button and elbow the filters apply to the card's drawing (its SVG), so the shape, its text and its icon change together.
- An SVG type written without `mode: svg` is read as a CSS filter, which doesn't exist, so it is skipped (with a warning in the browser console).

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
# softened and brighter
filters:
  - type: blur
    value: 1px
  - type: brightness
    value: 1.3
```

::: details More about filters
- **Live values:** filter values are fixed; templates and entity bindings don't work in them.
- **Data grid:** the grid takes CSS filters only. SVG filters need an SVG to attach to, so the grid skips them and logs a warning.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `filters` | list | - | The filters, applied in order |
| `filters[].type` | string | required | The filter: one of the [CSS filters](#css-filters) or [SVG filters](#svg-filters) |
| `filters[].value` | number / string / object | per type | A number or string for a CSS filter, an object of [value keys](#svg-value-keys) for an SVG filter |
| `filters[].mode` | string | `css` | `css` or `svg`. Set `svg` for the SVG filters |

## CSS Filters

**The browser's own CSS filters: blur, brighten, change the contrast or saturation, shift the hues, fade or turn the card grey.** Leave out `mode` (or write `mode: css`); most take one number as `value`.

- `blur` takes a length and `hue-rotate` an angle, as strings with their unit (`"4px"`, `"90deg"`).
- Every CSS entry needs a valid `value`. One without a `value`, or a `blur` without `px`, makes the browser drop the CSS filters of the whole list, not just that entry.
- Each filter has a playground under the example: move the sliders to see it on a sample shape, and copy the YAML it prints.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
# faded colours, a little darker, slightly soft
filters:
  - type: saturate
    value: 0.4
  - type: brightness
    value: 0.85
  - type: blur
    value: 1px
```

::: details Try each CSS filter
The playgrounds run the real filter code on a sample shape.

**`blur`**

**`brightness`**

**`contrast`**

**`saturate`**

**`hue-rotate`**

**`grayscale`**

**`sepia`**

**`invert`**

**`opacity`**

**`drop-shadow`**

:::

| `type` | `value` | Example | Effect |
|--------|---------|---------|--------|
| `blur` | string, `px` | `"4px"` | Gaussian blur; `"0px"` is none |
| `brightness` | number | `1.4` | `0` is black, `1` unchanged, above `1` brighter |
| `contrast` | number | `1.2` | `0` is grey, `1` unchanged, above `1` more contrast |
| `saturate` | number | `0.5` | `0` is grey, `1` unchanged, above `1` stronger colour |
| `hue-rotate` | string, `deg` | `"90deg"` | Turns every hue round the colour wheel; `"0deg"` is none |
| `grayscale` | number, 0 to 1 | `1` | `1` is fully grey, `0` none |
| `sepia` | number, 0 to 1 | `0.6` | `1` is full sepia, `0` none |
| `invert` | number, 0 to 1 | `1` | `1` inverts the colours fully, `0` none |
| `opacity` | number, 0 to 1 | `0.5` | How see-through the card is; `1` is solid. For a see-through background only, use the background colour's alpha (`style.card.color.background`) |
| `drop-shadow` | object | see [below](#drop-shadow) | A shadow outside the shape |

### drop-shadow

**A shadow behind the card's shape, for depth or a glow.** The shadow follows the drawn shape, not the card's box.

- `x` and `y` are numbers in px; `blur` is a length string such as `"6px"`.
- The colour goes straight into CSS, so `var(--lcars-*)` variables and CSS colours work, but `theme:` tokens and `alpha()` don't.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
filters:
  - type: drop-shadow
    value:
      x: 2
      "y": 2
      blur: 6px
      color: var(--lcars-orange)
```

::: details More about drop-shadow
- **Short form:** `value` can also be the CSS shadow as one string, such as `"2px 2px 6px black"`. The card reads it, but the config checker and the editor expect the object.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value.x` | number | `0` | Offset to the right, px (negative is left) |
| `value.y` | number | `0` | Offset down, px (negative is up) |
| `value.blur` | string | `0px` | Blur radius, such as `"6px"` |
| `value.color` | colour | black | Shadow colour: a CSS colour or `var(--lcars-*)` |

## SVG Filters

**SVG filter primitives, for effects the CSS filters can't give: a real colour tint, colour matrices, glows, outlines and distortion.** Each entry needs `mode: svg`, and its `value` is an object of [value keys](#svg-value-keys).

- They chain: each primitive works on the result of the one before it in the list, so a blur followed by a blend makes a glow.
- `tint` is the friendly one: a single entry for a colour wash. The others are the browser's SVG primitives, named as in SVG (`feGaussianBlur` ...).
- The filter area reaches half the card's size past each edge, so a glow, shadow or warp has room outside the shape.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
# a soft glow: blur the card, then blend the blur back over it
filters:
  - mode: svg
    type: feGaussianBlur
    value:
      stdDeviation: 4
  - mode: svg
    type: feBlend
    value:
      mode: screen
```

::: details Try each SVG filter
The playgrounds run the real filter code on a sample shape.

**`feGaussianBlur`**

**`feColorMatrix`**

**`feOffset`**

**`feBlend`**

**`feComposite`**

**`feMorphology`**

**`feTurbulence`**

**`feDisplacementMap`**

On its own `feDisplacementMap` has nothing to warp by, so this playground may look unchanged. Chain it after `feTurbulence` in a real config to see the distortion.

**`tint`**

:::

| `type` | Value keys | Effect |
|--------|------------|--------|
| `feGaussianBlur` | `stdDeviation` | Gaussian blur that chains with the other SVG filters; smoother than the CSS blur |
| `feColorMatrix` | `type`, `values` | Colour changes: saturation, hue turn, luminance to alpha or a custom matrix |
| `feOffset` | `dx`, `dy` | Shifts the result; with a blur, makes a shadow |
| `feBlend` | `mode`, `in2` | Blends the result with the card (or another input) in a CSS blend mode |
| `feComposite` | `operator`, `k1` to `k4`, `in2` | Combines the result with the card (or another input) |
| `feMorphology` | `operator`, `radius` | Thins (`erode`) or thickens (`dilate`) the shapes |
| `feTurbulence` | `type`, `baseFrequency`, `numOctaves`, `seed` | Makes a noise texture, usually for `feDisplacementMap` |
| `feDisplacementMap` | `scale`, `xChannelSelector`, `yChannelSelector`, `in`, `in2` | Warps the card by the colours of the result before it |
| `tint` | `color` | A flat colour wash over the card, such as an alert tint |

### SVG Value Keys

**The keys each SVG filter takes in its `value`; a key you leave out takes the default in the table.** Inputs name what a primitive works on: `SourceGraphic` (the card as drawn), `SourceAlpha` (its shape only), or the result of the primitive before.

- `feBlend` and `feComposite` combine the previous result (on top) with `in2`, which is the card itself unless you set it.
- `feDisplacementMap` warps `in` (the card) by `in2` (the previous result, such as `feTurbulence` noise). `feTurbulence` makes new content and ignores what came before it.
- `tint` starts from a flat colour and lays it over the card, so SVG filters listed before a `tint` have no effect. Its wash covers the whole filter area, background included, not only the shape.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
# noise, then warp the card by it
filters:
  - mode: svg
    type: feTurbulence
    value:
      baseFrequency: 0.04
      numOctaves: 2
      seed: 5
  - mode: svg
    type: feDisplacementMap
    value:
      scale: 8
      xChannelSelector: R
      yChannelSelector: G
```

::: details More about the SVG value keys
- **Colour matrix values:** with `type: saturate`, `values` is a multiplier (`0` grey, `1` unchanged); with `type: hueRotate`, an angle in degrees; with `type: matrix`, 20 numbers (a 4x5 matrix) as a list or a space-separated string. `luminanceToAlpha` takes no `values`.
- **Arithmetic composite:** with `operator: arithmetic`, the result is `k1*i1*i2 + k2*i1 + k3*i2 + k4`, where `i1` is the previous result and `i2` is `in2`.
- **Tint colour:** `tint`'s `color` takes any LCARdS colour, `theme:` tokens and `alpha()` included; its alpha sets how much of the card shows through.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stdDeviation` | number | `0` | `feGaussianBlur`: amount of blur |
| `type` | string | `saturate` | `feColorMatrix`: `saturate`, `hueRotate`, `luminanceToAlpha` or `matrix` |
| `values` | number / string / list | `1` saturate, `0` hueRotate | `feColorMatrix`: meaning depends on `type`; see the details above |
| `dx` | number | `0` | `feOffset`: shift right, px (negative is left) |
| `dy` | number | `0` | `feOffset`: shift down, px (negative is up) |
| `mode` | string | `normal` | `feBlend`: `normal`, `multiply`, `screen`, `darken`, `lighten`, `overlay`, `color-dodge`, `color-burn`, `hard-light`, `soft-light`, `difference`, `exclusion`, `hue`, `saturation`, `color` or `luminosity` |
| `operator` | string | `over` | `feComposite`: `over`, `in`, `out`, `atop`, `xor` or `arithmetic` |
| `k1` | number | `0` | `feComposite`: arithmetic coefficient, only with `operator: arithmetic` |
| `k2` | number | `0` | `feComposite`: arithmetic coefficient, only with `operator: arithmetic` |
| `k3` | number | `0` | `feComposite`: arithmetic coefficient, only with `operator: arithmetic` |
| `k4` | number | `0` | `feComposite`: arithmetic coefficient, only with `operator: arithmetic` |
| `in2` | string | `SourceGraphic` | `feBlend`, `feComposite`: the second input |
| `operator` | string | `erode` | `feMorphology`: `erode` (thinner) or `dilate` (thicker) |
| `radius` | number | `1` | `feMorphology`: how far to thin or thicken |
| `type` | string | `turbulence` | `feTurbulence`: `turbulence` (cloudy) or `fractalNoise` (softer) |
| `baseFrequency` | number | `0.05` | `feTurbulence`: `0` to `1`; lower is larger features |
| `numOctaves` | integer | `1` | `feTurbulence`: `1` to `10` layers of detail |
| `seed` | number | `0` | `feTurbulence`: change it for a different pattern |
| `scale` | number | `10` | `feDisplacementMap`: how strong the distortion is |
| `xChannelSelector` | string | `R` | `feDisplacementMap`: the channel that moves pixels across: `R`, `G`, `B` or `A` |
| `yChannelSelector` | string | `G` | `feDisplacementMap`: the channel that moves pixels up and down |
| `in` | string | `SourceGraphic` | `feDisplacementMap`: the image it warps |
| `in2` | string | the previous result | `feDisplacementMap`: the map it warps by |
| `color` | colour | `rgba(0,0,0,0.5)` | `tint`: the wash colour, with its alpha |

## Mixing CSS and SVG Filters

**CSS and SVG filters can share one list.** The CSS filters are applied first, in their order, then the SVG filters as one chain, whatever order the entries are in.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
filters:
  # CSS
  - type: brightness
    value: 1.2
  # SVG
  - mode: svg
    type: feColorMatrix
    value:
      type: saturate
      values: 0.6
```

- [Styles](../styles.md): card background and border styles

# Screen Effects

**Screen effects cover the whole browser window, above Home Assistant and every LCARdS card: blur, colour tints, TV static, pixelation, glitches, CRT scanlines and more.** Use them for alert states, dramatic transitions and feedback from an automation.

- They are fired by the `lcards.trigger_effect` action (from an automation, a script or **Developer tools > Actions**) or from the browser console, so the examples on this page are action data and console code rather than live cards.
- The [alert overlay card](../../cards/alert-overlay/overlay#layers) uses the same presets in its `layers`; its page shows them live on the Alert Studio's mock screen.
- Effects never catch clicks or taps: the dashboard under them keeps working.

## Quick Start

**Fire an effect with the `lcards.trigger_effect` action, or try one from the browser console.** Each effect goes in one of three slots (`backdrop`, `color`, `canvas`), with a `preset` and its settings.

- Run the action from an automation or script, or from **Developer tools > Actions** to try it.
- Without `duration` an effect stays until `lcards.clear_effect` (or the next `lcards.trigger_effect`) removes it.

```yaml
# In an automation or script: glitch every LCARdS browser for 1.5 seconds
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  layers:
    canvas:
      preset: glitch
  duration: 1500
```

```js
// In the browser console: TV static for 2 seconds, then gone
window.lcards.screenEffect.play('static', { duration: 2000 })

// Effects that stay until cleared
window.lcards.screenEffect.applySlot('backdrop', 'blur', { amount: '12px' })
window.lcards.screenEffect.applySlot('color', 'color-tint', { color: 'alpha(var(--lcars-alert-red), 0.35)' })
window.lcards.screenEffect.clear()
```

## Preset Reference

**Every preset belongs to one of three slots, and each slot shows one preset at a time.** The slots stack: the backdrop filter changes the dashboard itself, the canvas animation is drawn over it, and the colour layer goes on top.

- Put each preset in its own slot (`blur` in `backdrop`, `static` in `canvas` ...); the [Slots](#slots) table lists which goes where.
- Settings you leave out take the defaults in each preset's table. Setting names are written as in the tables (`tintStrength`, `pixelSize`).
- The alert overlay below uses all three slots; its own page has the [layers](../../cards/alert-overlay/overlay#layers) in full.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-alert-overlay
layers:
  # blur the dashboard
  backdrop:
    preset: blur
    amount: 12px
  # CRT lines over it
  canvas:
    preset: scanlines
    opacity: 0.3
  # a red tint on top
  color:
    preset: color-tint
    color: alpha(var(--lcars-alert-red), 0.3)
```

::: details More about presets
- **Colours:** colour settings (`color-tint`'s `color`, `color` on `static` and `pixelate`, `color` and `glowColor` on `borg-assimilation`) take any LCARdS colour: CSS colours, `var(--lcars-*)` and `var(--lcards-*)` variables, `theme:` tokens and computed colours such as `alpha(var(--lcars-alert-red), 0.4)`. They are read when the effect starts, so a running effect keeps its colour if the alert mode changes.
- **Reduced motion:** with reduced motion on, `static`, `pixelate` and `glitch` hold a single frame, `scanlines` stop scrolling, and `borg-assimilation` shows its finished picture without flicker or corruption.
- **Your own presets:** the console API can add presets at runtime; see [Console API](#console-api).
:::

### Backdrop presets

**Backdrop presets filter the dashboard behind the effect layer with a CSS `backdrop-filter`: the dashboard still shows through, changed.** They work best on dashboards with plenty on them.

#### `blur`

**Blurs everything behind the effect layer.**

```yaml
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  layers:
    backdrop:
      preset: blur
      amount: 12px
  duration: 3000
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | string | `8px` | CSS blur radius: `4px` subtle, `20px` heavy |

#### `saturate`

**Makes the colours behind the effect layer stronger.**

```yaml
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  layers:
    backdrop:
      preset: saturate
      amount: 300%
  duration: 3000
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | string | `200%` | CSS saturation, such as `150%` or `400%` |

#### `grayscale`

**Takes the colour out of the screen behind the effect layer.**

```yaml
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  layers:
    backdrop:
      preset: grayscale
      amount: 50%
  duration: 3000
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | string | `100%` | CSS grayscale amount: `100%` is black and white, `50%` partly grey |

#### `contrast`

**Raises (or lowers) the contrast of the screen behind the effect layer.**

```yaml
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  layers:
    backdrop:
      preset: contrast
      amount: 150%
  duration: 3000
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | string | `200%` | CSS contrast amount, such as `150%` or `300%` |

#### `hue-rotate`

**Turns every hue on screen round the colour wheel.**

```yaml
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  layers:
    backdrop:
      preset: hue-rotate
      angle: 90deg
  duration: 3000
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `angle` | string | `180deg` | CSS hue rotation, such as `90deg` or `-45deg` |

### Color tint presets

**Colour presets lay a colour over the whole screen, above the canvas animation.** The colour layer is a plain element with a CSS background.

#### `color-tint`

**A see-through colour over the entire screen.** Its alpha sets how much of the dashboard shows through.

```yaml
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  layers:
    color:
      preset: color-tint
      color: alpha(var(--lcars-alert-red), 0.4)
  duration: 2000
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | colour | `rgba(0,0,0,0.5)` | The tint, any LCARdS colour; use one with alpha |

#### `vignette`

**Darkens the edges of the screen with a radial fade, like a film vignette.** The middle stays clear.

```yaml
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  layers:
    color:
      preset: vignette
      opacity: 0.8
  duration: 3000
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `opacity` | number | `0.7` | How dark the edges get, 0 to 1 |

### Canvas presets

**Canvas presets draw an animation over the whole screen.** `static`, `pixelate` and `glitch` blend into the dashboard with a CSS blend mode, so the content shows through; `scanlines` draws see-through dark lines.

::: info Canvas and screen content
For browser security reasons, canvas effects can't read the dashboard's pixels; they draw their own textures over it. The result is an obscuring or distorting layer over the real content, not a filter of it.
:::

#### `static`

**TV static: chunky random noise over the screen.** The noise is drawn small and scaled up with hard pixel edges, and blends in with `mix-blend-mode: overlay`.

```yaml
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  layers:
    canvas:
      preset: static
      scale: 6
      opacity: 0.7
  duration: 800
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `opacity` | number | `0.55` | Strength of the whole effect, 0 to 1 |
| `scale` | number | `4` | Grain size: `2` is fine, `8` very coarse |
| `color` | colour | `#ffffff` | Colour blended into the noise, by `tintStrength` |
| `tintStrength` | number | `0` | 0 to 1 blend toward `color`: `0` is pure noise, `1` solid colour |

#### `pixelate`

**A mosaic of small dark blocks with slight differences in lightness, like a low-resolution, degraded signal.** It blends with `mix-blend-mode: multiply`, so the blocks darken the content, and redraws about 8 times a second.

```yaml
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  layers:
    canvas:
      preset: pixelate
      pixelSize: 12
      opacity: 0.6
  duration: 2000
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pixelSize` | number | `8` | Block size in px; larger is chunkier |
| `opacity` | number | `0.75` | Strength of the whole effect, 0 to 1 |
| `variance` | number | `0.35` | Lightness difference between blocks, 0 to 1: `0` is even, `1` the most contrast |
| `baseLight` | number | `80` | Base grey of the blocks, 0 (black) to 255 (white); lower is darker |
| `color` | colour | `#8c9aa6` | Colour blended into each block, by `tintStrength` |
| `tintStrength` | number | `0` | 0 to 1 blend toward `color`: `0` is a neutral grey mosaic, `1` solid colour blocks |

#### `glitch`

**Thin horizontal bands shifted sideways, with red and cyan fringes at their edges: data corruption.** Only a small share of the rows glitch in each frame; it blends with `mix-blend-mode: overlay`.

```yaml
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  layers:
    canvas:
      preset: glitch
      intensity: 0.12
      maxShift: 60
  duration: 1000
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `intensity` | number | `0.08` | Share of the bands glitched in each frame, 0 to 1. Keep it low (0.05–0.15) for a subtle effect |
| `maxShift` | number | `40` | Largest sideways shift, px |
| `bandHeight` | number | `4` | Height of each band, px |
| `opacity` | number | `0.85` | Strength of the whole effect, 0 to 1 |
| `fps` | number | `20` | Frames per second |

#### `scanlines`

**CRT-style horizontal lines across the screen, still or scrolling down.**

```yaml
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  layers:
    canvas:
      preset: scanlines
      lineHeight: 3
      opacity: 0.35
      scroll: 40
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lineHeight` | number | `4` | Height of each line, px; the gap between lines is the same |
| `opacity` | number | `0.25` | Darkness of the lines, 0 to 1 |
| `scroll` | number | `0` | Scroll speed in px per second: `0` is still, more scrolls down |

#### `borg-assimilation`

**Green tendrils grow across the screen from several injection sites while an assimilation front spreads from them and overruns the screen with Borg circuitry; a Borg cube emerges in the middle and bursts of signal corruption tear the picture.** This is the effect behind [Borg Assimilation](../borg.md), and it can be fired on its own.

- It runs on WebGL in a background worker. `renderer: canvas` plays the classic intro instead (tendrils with nano-probe particles, drawn with Canvas2D), and browsers without WebGL2 get the classic one whatever `renderer` says.
- Fired on its own it stays until it is cleared, or until `duration` runs out.

```yaml
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  layers:
    canvas:
      preset: borg-assimilation
      siteCount: 5
      color: var(--lcars-martian)
```

::: details More about borg-assimilation
- **Browser support:** the effect needs a browser with OffscreenCanvas and web workers; elsewhere it is skipped and nothing shows.
- **Limits:** on WebGL, `siteCount`, `tendrilsPerSite`, `tendrilLength` and `particleCount` are held to the ranges in the table.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `siteCount` | number | `7` | Number of injection sites, 1 to 20 |
| `tendrilsPerSite` | number | `8` | Tendrils grown from each site, 1 to 24 |
| `tendrilLength` | number | `600` | Longest tendril reach in px, 100 to 1200 |
| `particleCount` | number | `2` | Particles travelling each tendril, 0 to 6; `0` turns them off |
| `color` | colour | `#00cc44` | Tendril, branch and site colour |
| `glowColor` | colour | `#00ff66` | Glow at each site and round the particles |
| `renderer` | string | `auto` | `auto` or `webgl`: the WebGL intro where the browser supports it; `canvas`: the classic intro |
| `cube` | boolean | `true` | WebGL: the Borg cube in the middle |
| `cubeStyle` | string | `detailed` | WebGL: `detailed` (solid cube with machinery, rail lattice, pulsing glows and a halo) or `classic` (wireframe) |
| `corruption` | number | `0.5` | WebGL: signal corruption strength, 0 to 1; `0` turns it off |
| `overrun` | number | `0.65` | WebGL: how dark the screen gets behind the assimilation front, 0 to 1 |
| `seed` | number | - | WebGL: the same layout every time |

## Home Assistant Service

**Two actions fire and clear screen effects from automations and scripts, on every LCARdS browser or only some.** They need the LCARdS integration, and they reach the browsers that have Home Assistant open.

### `lcards.trigger_effect`

**Plays one or more screen effects, one per slot.** Give each slot you want a `preset` and its settings.

- A slot you leave out keeps what it shows, so a blur stays while a later call adds static. Set a slot to `null` to clear it.
- `duration` clears the slots that call set after that many milliseconds; each slot keeps its own timer, so a later effect is never cut short. Without it the effects stay until `lcards.clear_effect` or a later call replaces them.
- Without a target the effects play on every browser. With targets, a browser plays them when it matches any of the device or user targets; a target that matches nobody fails the action. See [Targeting](../../configuration/ha-actions#targeting).
- Find this browser's device and user ids in the browser console with `window.lcards.targeting.getMyIds()`.

```yaml
# Full red alert: blur, red tint and TV static, cleared after 5 seconds
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  layers:
    backdrop:
      preset: blur
      amount: 12px
    color:
      preset: color-tint
      color: alpha(var(--lcars-alert-red), 0.35)
    canvas:
      preset: static
      opacity: 0.3
  duration: 5000
```

::: details More examples
```yaml
# A blur on one user's browsers, until lcards.clear_effect
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  layers:
    backdrop:
      preset: blur
      amount: 16px
  target_user_ids:
    - a1b2c3d4e5f6
```

```yaml
# A vignette on one browser, by its device id
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  layers:
    color:
      preset: vignette
      opacity: 0.8
  duration: 3000
  target_device_ids:
    - abc123def456
```

```yaml
# The kitchen tablet, by the device name set in the LCARdS config panel
action: lcards.trigger_effect
data:
  layers:
    canvas:
      preset: glitch
      intensity: 0.15
  duration: 1200
  target_device_names:
    - Kitchen tablet
```
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `layers` | object | required | The effects, one entry per slot |
| `layers.backdrop` | object | - | A [backdrop preset](#backdrop-presets) and its settings |
| `layers.color` | object | - | A [colour preset](#color-tint-presets) and its settings |
| `layers.canvas` | object | - | A [canvas preset](#canvas-presets) and its settings |
| `layers.<slot>.preset` | string | required | The preset for that slot |
| `duration` | number | - | Clear every slot after this many ms, at least `100`. Without it the effects stay |
| `target_device_ids` | list | - | Only these browsers, by LCARdS device id |
| `target_device_names` | list | - | Only these browsers, by the device name set in LCARdS (any case; a name shared by several devices reaches all of them) |
| `target_user_ids` | list | - | Only these Home Assistant users, by user id |
| `target_user_names` | list | - | Only these Home Assistant users, by name (any case) |

#### Slots

| Slot | Presets | Drawn with |
|------|---------|------------|
| `backdrop` | `blur`, `grayscale`, `saturate`, `contrast`, `hue-rotate` | CSS `backdrop-filter` on the dashboard behind |
| `canvas` | `static`, `pixelate`, `glitch`, `scanlines`, `borg-assimilation` | An animated canvas (Canvas2D; WebGL for `borg-assimilation`) |
| `color` | `color-tint`, `vignette` | A see-through element with a CSS background, on top |

### `lcards.clear_effect`

**Clears screen effects: every slot, or only the one in `slot`.** Use `slot` to take off one layer and keep the others.

```yaml
# In an automation or script: take off the canvas effect, keep the blur and tint
action: lcards.clear_effect
data:
  slot: canvas
```

::: details More examples
```yaml
# Everything, on every browser
action: lcards.clear_effect
```

```yaml
# Everything, on one browser only
action: lcards.clear_effect
data:
  target_device_ids:
    - abc123def456
```
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slot` | string | every slot | `backdrop`, `canvas` or `color`: clear only that slot |
| `target_device_ids` | list | - | Only these browsers, by LCARdS device id |
| `target_device_names` | list | - | Only these browsers, by device name |
| `target_user_ids` | list | - | Only these Home Assistant users, by user id |
| `target_user_names` | list | - | Only these Home Assistant users, by name |

## Console API

**`window.lcards.screenEffect` runs the same effects from the browser console, on this browser only.** Handy for trying presets and settings before you put them in an automation.

- `applySlot()` and `apply()` show an effect until it is cleared; `play()` takes it off again after `duration` ms (default `1000`) and returns a promise that settles then.
- A new effect in a slot replaces the one there; the other slots are left alone (unlike `lcards.trigger_effect`).
- `registerPreset()` adds a preset: `slot`, `defaults`, and an `enter(el, params)` function that starts the effect on the slot's element and returns a function that stops it.

```js
// An effect in a slot, until cleared
window.lcards.screenEffect.applySlot('backdrop', 'blur', { amount: '12px' })
window.lcards.screenEffect.applySlot('color', 'color-tint', { color: 'alpha(var(--lcars-alert-red), 0.35)' })
window.lcards.screenEffect.applySlot('canvas', 'static', { opacity: 0.3 })

// apply(): the same, in the preset's own slot
window.lcards.screenEffect.apply('blur', { amount: '12px' })

// play(): gone again after duration ms
window.lcards.screenEffect.play('static', { duration: 2000, scale: 6 })

// Take effects off
window.lcards.screenEffect.clearSlot('backdrop')   // one slot
window.lcards.screenEffect.clear()                  // every slot

// What is there
window.lcards.screenEffect.list()                   // preset names
window.lcards.screenEffect.catalog()                // name, label, slot, settings and defaults of each
window.lcards.screenEffect.getPreset('glitch')      // one preset's definition

// Your own preset
window.lcards.screenEffect.registerPreset('my-green', {
  slot: 'color',
  defaults: { color: 'alpha(var(--lcars-green), 0.3)' },
  params_schema: [{ key: 'color', type: 'color-text' }],  // marks color as a colour to resolve
  enter(el, params) {
    el.style.background = params.color;
    return () => { el.style.background = ''; };
  },
})
window.lcards.screenEffect.apply('my-green')
```

# Presets

**A preset is a named look for a card: one `preset:` key sets its shape, colours, text, border and how it shows each state.** Pick the nearest preset, then override only what you want to change.

- Buttons, elbows and select menus take the [button presets](#button-lcards-button); sliders take the [slider presets](#slider-lcards-slider).
- Your own config always wins over the preset, and [rules](rules/) win over both while the dashboard runs.

## Applying a Preset

**Set `preset:` to a preset's name, then add your own keys on top.** Anything you set replaces the preset's value for that key; everything else stays as the preset has it.

- Many button presets hide the entity's name; `text.name.show: true` brings it back.
- A preset can set more than `style:`: the button presets also set `min_height` and the icon and text layout, and `icon` and the `bar-label-*` presets set a fixed `height`.

```yaml live
# The lozenge preset as it is (tap to toggle the light)
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
tap_action:
  action: toggle
```

```yaml live
# The same preset with a grey fill while the light is off
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
style:
  card:
    color:
      background:
        inactive: var(--lcards-gray-dark)
tap_action:
  action: toggle
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `preset` | string | - | The preset's name. A button, elbow or select menu takes a button preset; a slider takes a slider preset. Without one a slider draws pills or a gauge, by the entity's domain |

## Built-in Presets

**Every preset in the built-in packs, with a picture of each.** A `-right` variant mirrors its preset (rounded or capped end on the other side). A test (`tests/core/presets-doc.test.js`) keeps these tables in sync with the packs.

### Button (`lcards-button`)

`base` is the foundation the others build on; the editor's preset list leaves it out.

| Preset | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `base` | Foundation every other button preset builds on: minimal styles only |
| `lozenge` | Classic LCARS lozenge: rounded ends, primary colour fill |
| `lozenge-right` | Lozenge mirrored, with the icon shown on the right |
| `bullet` | Lozenge rounded on the right only, flat on the left: navigation bullets |
| `bullet-right` | Bullet mirrored: rounded on the left |
| `capped` | Lozenge with one capped end, rounded on the left: row labels |
| `capped-right` | Capped mirrored: rounded on the right |
| `barrel` | Square-cornered block |
| `barrel-right` | Barrel mirrored |
| `filled` | Solid filled button with its name shown |
| `filled-right` | Filled mirrored |
| `outline` | Transparent fill with a border outline |
| `outline-right` | Outline mirrored |
| `icon` | Icon-only button |
| `text-only` | Pure text label with no background or border |
| `bar-label-base` | Base bar label: a filled bar with a text "break" in it |
| `bar-label-left` | Bar label with left-aligned text |
| `bar-label-center` | Bar label with centred text |
| `bar-label-right` | Bar label with right-aligned text |
| `bar-label-square` | Bar label with square corners, for large indicators |
| `bar-label-lozenge` | Bar label with rounded ends (pill shape) |
| `bar-label-bullet-left` | Bar label rounded on the right, flat on the left |
| `bar-label-bullet-right` | Bar label flat on the right, rounded on the left |
| `bar-label-capped-left` | Bar label rounded on the left, flat on the right |
| `bar-label-capped-right` | Bar label rounded on the right, flat on the left |
| `panel-light` | Square-cornered panel with a random LCARS label (light); with an entity, the theme accent when on and the dark structure tone when off. No hover effects |
| `toggle-tab` | Dark square tab with a centred name; a coloured line along the top shows the state |
| `panel-flagged` | Dark code panel with a thin accent flag on its left edge. No hover effects |
| `panel-dark` | Square-cornered panel with a random LCARS label (dark); with an entity, the theme accent when on and the dark structure tone when off. No hover effects |

### Slider (`lcards-slider`)

`base` is the foundation the others build on; the editor's preset list leaves it out.

| Preset | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `base` | Foundation every other slider preset builds on |
| `pills-basic` | Segmented pill slider |
| `pills-left-border` | Pills slider with a left border |
| `pills-left-border-rounded` | Pills with a left border and a rounded free end |
| `gauge-basic` | Ruler-style gauge for displays and controls |
| `gauge-left-border` | Gauge slider with a left border |
| `gauge-left-border-rounded` | Gauge with a left border and a rounded free end |
| `shaped-vertical` | Vertical shaped slider with exterior text labels (`style.shaped.type` picks the shape) |
| `shaped-horizontal` | Horizontal shaped slider with exterior text labels |
| `ring` | Ring gauge: a 270 degree value arc around a large value, the name above it (`component: ring`) |
| `picard-ring` | Picard-era ring: near-full thick ring with flat ends, small label over a large value |
| `picard-gauge-vertical` | Picard-style vertical gauge (`component: picard`) |
| `picard-gauge-column` | Picard-era column gauge: number caps at both ends, a thin value bar, short ticks and a small oval thumb |

Rendered:

### Elbow and select menu

**The select menu takes the button presets above; the elbow has no presets.** An elbow's shape comes from `elbow.type` (`header-left`, `footer-right`, `frame` and more: see [Elbow](../cards/elbow/index.md)) and its look from `style`.

- The select menu's `preset:` is a button preset applied to every option button. Its `button_template.style`, its `style` and each option's own `style` go on top, in that order.
- Charts and data grids have no style presets (their `preset` keys are animation presets).

## How Presets Compose

**When a card loads, its config is built in layers, and each layer wins over the one before it.**

```
System defaults
    ↓
Preset values
    ↓
Card config (your YAML)  ← wins on conflict
    ↓
Rule patches (runtime)   ← wins over everything
```

- You only need to specify what differs from the preset. Anything you don't set falls through to the preset, and anything the preset doesn't set falls through to the system default.
- Objects merge key by key: a `style.border.radius` with only `top_left` keeps the preset's other three corners.
- On a button with a `component`, `preset` names one of the component's own presets instead (see [Button components](/cards/button/components)).
- The card editor's [Main Engineering](../cards/main-engineering.md#provenance) tab shows which layer set each value.

## Browsing Available Presets

**The card editor and the LCARdS config panel both list the presets you can use.**

- **Config tab** → the preset dropdown: shows the presets for the current card type.
- **Config panel** → **Pack Explorer**: lists every preset from every loaded pack, grouped by card type. The Theme panel of the card editor's [Main Engineering](../cards/main-engineering.md#theme) tab has a button that opens it.

## Packs and Custom Presets

**Presets come from content packs.** The built-in `lcards_buttons` and `lcards_sliders` packs provide the presets listed above, and LCARdS loads them when it starts.

- A pack registered with `window.lcards.core.packManager.registerPack()` adds its presets to the editor's lists. There is no way yet to install a pack from YAML or the editor.
- A preset can build on another with `extends` (`extends: button.lozenge`): it starts from that preset and changes only what it sets.

See [Pack System](../architecture/subsystems/pack-system.md) for how to create packs with custom presets.

## Related

- [Styles](styles.md): the `style:` block reference for overriding visual properties
- [Rules Engine](rules/): rules can patch style properties at runtime, overriding both preset and card config
- [Common Card Properties](../cards/common.md): shared card keys
