# Rules Engine

**A rule changes cards while a condition holds: when an entity, the time or a template says so, it patches the cards it targets, and takes the patch off again when the condition stops holding.** One rule can restyle a single card, every card with a tag, or the lines on an MSD.

- A rule has three parts: `when` (the condition), `apply` (what changes) and an `id`. It can sit in any card's `rules` list and still change other cards on the page.
- A patch is a piece of card config (`style`, `text` ...) merged over the card's own while the rule matches. Rules can also start animations and tint an MSD's blueprint.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    E[Entity state changes] --> R[Rule evaluates its condition]
    R -- matches --> P[Patch applied to targets]
    R -- no longer matches --> C[Patch taken off the targets]
    P --> T1[Card tagged 'nav']
    P --> T2[Card tagged 'nav']
    P --> T3[Card with id 'header']
```

::: tip Try it
- Every card editor has a **Rules** tab: it lists the rules on the page, adds and edits them with a condition builder, and turns them on and off.
- The Rules view of the [Live Demo](/getting-started/live-demo) shows rules recolouring and blinking cards as you drag sliders.
:::

| Page | Covers |
|------|--------|
| [Conditions](./conditions) | `when`: entity states and attributes, numbers, time, sun, chance, `all`/`any`/`not`, JavaScript and Jinja2 |
| [Targets and Changes](./changes) | `apply`: naming cards with `id` and `tags`, selectors, patches, animations, MSD blueprint filters |
| [Priority and Debugging](./priority) | Which rule wins, `stop`, `enabled`, and seeing which rules apply now |
| [Examples](./examples) | Whole rule sets to copy: a temperature alert, day and night, a multi-condition alert |

---

## Quick start

**A rule on one card can restyle a group of others: here the toggle turns the three panels red.** The panels carry the tag `docs-rules-deck`, and the rule's `tag:docs-rules-deck` selector finds them.

- Tap TOGGLE (or use the control under the card) to switch `input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle`; the rule matches while it is `"on"`.
- The rule lives on the toggle button, but it would work from any card on the page: rules are not tied to the card that holds them.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 150px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr
  grid-template-rows: 1fr 1fr
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: lozenge
    entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
    tap_action:
      action: toggle
    text:
      name:
        content: TOGGLE
        show: true
    view_layout:
      grid-column: 1 / 4
    rules:
      - id: docs-rules-quick-start
        when:
          entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
          state: "on"
        apply:
          overlays:
            tag:docs-rules-deck:
              style:
                card:
                  color:
                    background: var(--lcars-alert-red)
  # three panels in one group
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: filled
    tags:
      - docs-rules-deck
    text:
      name:
        content: REACTOR
        show: true
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: filled
    tags:
      - docs-rules-deck
    text:
      name:
        content: INJECTORS
        show: true
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: filled
    tags:
      - docs-rules-deck
    text:
      name:
        content: CONDUITS
        show: true
```

## Where rules live

**Rules go in the `rules` list of any LCARdS card, or in a content pack.** All of them run in one engine for the whole page, keyed by rule `id`.

- Give every rule an `id` no other card on the page uses: cards listing the same `id` share one rule (the one loaded last is used), and a card rule with the `id` of a pack rule is skipped.
- A rule with no `id` is skipped too, with a warning in the browser console.

::: tip Rule changes apply when you save
Adding, changing or removing a rule takes effect when you save the card (the card editor's preview shows it straight away), with no page refresh. A card taken off the dashboard takes its rules with it a few seconds later.
:::

## Rule structure

**Every rule needs `id`, `when` and `apply`; the other keys are optional.** This rule recolours its own card while the power level is above 80.

- Drag the power control under the card above or below 80 to see the rule match and let go.
- `priority`, `stop` and `enabled` decide what happens when several rules patch the same card: see [Priority and Debugging](./priority).

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-rules-structure-btn
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: POWER
    show: true
rules:
  - id: docs-rules-structure
    name: Power high
    priority: 10
    when:
      entity: input_number.lcards_test_power
      above: 80
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-rules-structure-btn:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-alert-red)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | required | The rule's name, unique on the page. Shown in the Rules tab and in traces |
| `name` | string | - | A readable label for the editor |
| `when` | object / list | required | The condition: see [Conditions](./conditions). A list means all of its items |
| `apply` | object | required | What changes while the rule matches: see [Targets and Changes](./changes) |
| `priority` | number | `0` | Higher runs first and wins where two rules patch the same key: see [priority](./priority#priority) |
| `stop` | boolean | `false` | While this rule matches, lower-priority rules' patches on the same cards are dropped: see [stop](./priority#stop) |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | `false` turns the rule off without deleting it: see [enabled](./priority#enabled) |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/rules/changes.html -->

# Targets and Changes

**A rule's `apply` block says what changes while the rule matches: patches for the cards it targets, animations to play, and filters on an MSD's blueprint.** The condition that drives it is on the [Conditions](./conditions) page.

## Targets

**A rule finds cards by their `id`, by a tag in their `tags`, or by their type.** Give a card an `id` to target that one card, and the same tag to several cards to target them together.

- `id` and `tags` are [card-level options](/cards/common#id-and-tags) every LCARdS card takes. A card without an `id` gets a generated one, so only a card with an `id` can be named.
- On an MSD, lines, shapes and controls take `id` and `tags` too. A control's card takes the control's `id` and `tags`, so a rule names the control to change the card inside it.
- Astrometrics points and objects are targets in the same way: see [Astrometrics rules](/cards/astrometrics/data#rules).

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 150px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr
  grid-template-rows: 1fr 1fr
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: lozenge
    entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
    tap_action:
      action: toggle
    text:
      name:
        content: TOGGLE
        show: true
    view_layout:
      grid-column: 1 / 3
    rules:
      - id: docs-rules-targets
        when:
          entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
          state: "on"
        apply:
          overlays:
            # one card, by its id
            docs-rules-target-bridge:
              style:
                card:
                  color:
                    background: var(--lcars-alert-yellow)
            # every card with this tag
            tag:docs-rules-engineering:
              style:
                card:
                  color:
                    background: var(--lcars-alert-red)
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    id: docs-rules-target-bridge
    preset: filled
    text:
      name:
        content: BRIDGE
        show: true
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: filled
    tags:
      - docs-rules-engineering
    text:
      name:
        content: ENGINEERING
        show: true
```

::: details More about targets
- **Automatic tags:** a button or elbow also carries its type (`button`, `elbow`), its preset's name and, when it has an entity, `entity-based`; a select menu carries `select-menu` and a slider `slider`. MSD lines, shapes and controls carry `msd-overlay` and their type.
- **Types:** `type:` matches `button`, `elbow`, `slider`, `select-menu`, `chart`, `data-grid` and `astrometrics` cards, and the MSD overlay types `line`, `shape` and `control`.
- **The whole page:** rules see every card on the page, not only the cards in one section or view, so pick ids and tags no other card uses by accident.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` (on a card) | string | generated | The card's name, for `apply.overlays.<id>` and `overlay:` |
| `tags` (on a card) | list | - | Group names, for `tag:<name>` selectors, such as `[nav, lights]` |

## apply.overlays

**`apply.overlays` maps selectors to patches: each key picks cards, and its value is config merged over theirs while the rule matches.** A patch can change any of the card's options, not only `style`: here the third card's name changes too.

- A selector is a card's `id`, or `tag:<name>`, `type:<type>`, `pattern:<regex>` or `all`. `exclude` leaves cards out of every selector in the rule.
- The card's own config comes back when the rule stops matching.
- On an MSD, a line or shape takes its own `style` keys (`color`, `width`, `opacity` ...): see [Rules on an MSD](/cards/msd/animations#rules).

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 150px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr
  grid-template-rows: 1fr 1fr
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: lozenge
    entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
    tap_action:
      action: toggle
    text:
      name:
        content: TOGGLE
        show: true
    view_layout:
      grid-column: 1 / 4
    rules:
      - id: docs-rules-selectors
        when:
          entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
          state: "on"
        apply:
          overlays:
            # every card whose id starts with docs-sel-, but not docs-sel-2
            "pattern:^docs-sel-":
              style:
                card:
                  color:
                    background: var(--lcars-alert-red)
            exclude: [docs-sel-2]
            # a patch can change any option: here the name
            docs-sel-3:
              text:
                name:
                  content: ALERT
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    id: docs-sel-1
    preset: filled
    text:
      name:
        content: ONE
        show: true
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    id: docs-sel-2
    preset: filled
    text:
      name:
        content: TWO
        show: true
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    id: docs-sel-3
    preset: filled
    text:
      name:
        content: THREE
        show: true
```

::: details More about apply.overlays
- **Several selectors on one card:** their patches merge in the order written. Under `style`, a later selector's keys replace the earlier one's at the first level (a later `style.card` replaces an earlier `style.card` whole); other keys are replaced whole.
- **Several rules on one card:** their patches merge deeply, the highest `priority` on top: see [Priority and Debugging](./priority#priority).
- **Quoting:** quote a `pattern:` selector whose regex holds YAML characters (`"pattern:^temp_.*$"`).
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `apply.overlays.<id>` | object | - | The patch for the card or overlay with this `id` |
| `apply.overlays.tag:<name>` | object | - | The patch for every card or overlay with this tag |
| `apply.overlays.type:<type>` | object | - | The patch for every card or overlay of this type, such as `type:slider` or `type:line` |
| `apply.overlays.pattern:<regex>` | object | - | The patch for every card or overlay whose `id` matches this JavaScript regular expression. An invalid regex is skipped |
| `apply.overlays.all` | object | - | The patch for every card and overlay on the page |
| `apply.overlays.exclude` | list / string | - | Ids left out of every selector in this rule |

## Templates in patches

**A patch value can be a template, so one rule sets a value that follows an entity.** Here the line is red above 80 and yellow below; drag the power control to see it change.

- The rules engine works out JavaScript (`[[[ ]]]`) and Jinja2 (`{{ }}`) in values directly under `style` and at the top level of a patch. Deeper values, such as a button's `text.name.content`, reach the card as written, and the card works out its own templates.
- A patch belongs to no one card, so `{entity.state}` and the `entity` variable have no entity here: read `states['...']` by id.
- The template is worked out when the rule is checked, which happens when an entity in its `when` changes. Name the entity the template reads in `when` too, as this rule does.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
msd:
  view_box: [0, 0, 600, 120]
  overlays:
    - id: docs_tpl_line
      type: line
      anchor: [40, 60]
      attach_to: [560, 60]
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-blue)
        width: 6
rules:
  - id: docs-rules-template
    when:
      entity: input_number.lcards_test_power
      above: 0
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs_tpl_line:
          style:
            color: "[[[return Number(states['input_number.lcards_test_power'].state) > 80 ? 'var(--lcars-alert-red)' : 'var(--lcars-alert-yellow)']]]"
            width: 10
```

::: details More about templates in patches
- **Shape textures:** a `map_range` value in a patch's `shape_texture.config` (such as `fill_pct`) is worked out from its entity, as in [animations](/core/animations).
:::

## apply.animations

**`apply.animations` plays animations on cards while the rule matches, such as a blink on alert.** Each item names its target (`overlay`, `tag`, `type` or `pattern`) and a `preset`.

- An animation starts when the rule begins to match, not again while it keeps matching. A looping one stops when the rule stops matching; a one-shot plays to its end.
- Targets are list items here (`- tag: alert`), not map keys as in `apply.overlays` (`tag:alert:`).
- The animation keys and presets are on [Rule-based Animations](/core/animations/rule-based-animations) and [Animations](/core/animations).

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-rules-anim-btn
preset: lozenge
entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
tap_action:
  action: toggle
text:
  name:
    content: TOGGLE
    show: true
rules:
  - id: docs-rules-animation
    when:
      entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
      state: "on"
    apply:
      animations:
        - overlay: docs-rules-anim-btn
          preset: blink
          loop: true
          duration: 1000
```

::: details More about apply.animations
- **One target per item:** with more than one target key, the first of `overlay`, `tag`, `type`, `pattern` wins. `exclude` does not apply to animations.
- **Cards still loading:** a target that is not on the page yet is looked for again for about a second and a half, so a rule that matches as an MSD loads still finds its lines.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `overlay` | string | - | Target one card or overlay by its `id` |
| `tag` | string | - | Target every card or overlay with this tag |
| `type` | string | - | Target every card or overlay of this type, such as `button` or `line` |
| `pattern` | string | - | Target every card or overlay whose `id` matches this regular expression |
| `preset` | string | required | The animation preset, such as `pulse`, `blink` or `glow` |
| `loop` | boolean / number | `false` | `true` loops until the rule stops matching; a number repeats that many more times |
| `duration` | number / object | the preset's | Length, ms. Or a `map_range` that follows an entity |
| `delay` | number / object | the preset's | Wait before starting, ms. Or a `map_range` |
| `ease` | string | the preset's | anime.js easing name, such as `inOutQuad` |
| `params` | object | - | The preset's own settings; values may be `map_range` |

## apply.base_svg

**`apply.base_svg` crossfades an MSD's blueprint to other filters while the rule matches: dimmer, grey, or a red tint on alert.** Here the toggle tints the ship red.

- It works on MSD cards only, and on the MSD whose `rules` holds the rule.
- When no rule's `base_svg` holds any more, the blueprint goes back to its own `base_svg.filters`. `filters: []` (or `{}`) clears every filter while the rule matches.
- Each filter type and ready-made recipes (dimmed, backdrop, red wash, monochrome) are on [Base SVG Filters](/cards/msd/base-svg-filters).

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-msd-card
grid_options:
  columns: full
  rows: 4
msd:
  base_svg:
    source: builtin:ncc-1701-a-blue
  view_box: [180, 270, 1600, 720]
rules:
  - id: docs-rules-base-svg
    when:
      entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
      state: "on"
    apply:
      base_svg:
        filters:
          - mode: svg
            type: tint
            value:
              color: alpha(var(--lcars-alert-red), 0.35)
        transition: 1500
```

::: details More about apply.base_svg
- **Two rules:** the highest-priority matching rule's `base_svg` wins. A rule from a content pack belongs to no card, so it reaches every MSD that has no rule of its own holding.
- **Older configs** wrote `filters` as one map of CSS filters (`opacity: 0.3`, `brightness: 0.7`, `blur: "2px"`, `grayscale`, `hue_rotate: "90deg"`, `sepia`, `saturate`, `contrast`, `invert`). It still works; the list form above also takes the SVG filters, such as `tint`.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `apply.base_svg.filters` | list / object | - | The blueprint's [filters](/cards/msd/base-svg-filters) while the rule matches. `[]` clears them |
| `apply.base_svg.transition` | number | `1000` | Crossfade time, ms |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/rules/conditions.html -->

# Rule Conditions

**A rule's `when` block is its condition: while it is true the rule's `apply` block holds, and when it turns false the patch comes off.** It can test an entity, the time, the sun, a template, or several of these combined. The rest of a rule is on the [Rules Engine](./) page.

- A rule is checked again when an entity it names changes: the `entity` of a condition, or an entity a template reads. A rule with a `time_between`, `weekday_in` or `random_chance` condition is also checked at the start of every minute.
- The examples on this page each hold one rule on one button. Use the controls under a card to change the entity and watch the rule match.

## All conditions at a glance

**One key picks the kind of condition; the table links to each.**

| Condition | Key | What it checks |
|-----------|-----|----------------|
| [Entity state](#entity) | `entity` | The entity's state against a [comparison](#comparison-operators) |
| [Entity attribute](#entity-attr) | `entity_attr` | One attribute of an entity against a comparison |
| [Map range](#map-range-cond) | `map_range_cond` | The state mapped onto a new scale, then compared |
| [All, any, not](#all-any-and-not) | `all`, `any`, `not` | Every, at least one, or none of the conditions inside |
| [Time range](#time-between) | `time_between` | The time is inside a `"HH:MM-HH:MM"` window |
| [Day of week](#weekday-in) | `weekday_in` | Today is in a list of days |
| [Sun elevation](#sun-elevation) | `sun_elevation` | The sun is above or below an angle |
| [Random chance](#random-chance) | `random_chance` | True with a probability from `0` to `1` |
| [JavaScript](#javascript) | `condition`, `javascript`, `js` | A JavaScript expression returns a truthy value |
| [Jinja2](#jinja2) | `condition`, `jinja2` | A Home Assistant Jinja2 template renders true |

## entity

**`entity` tests an entity's state: on its own, or with a comparison such as `state: "on"` or `above: 25`.** This is the condition most rules use.

- `state` means exactly the same as `equals`. Quote `"on"` and `"off"`, or YAML may read them as true and false.
- With no comparison at all, the condition is true while the entity has a state.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-cond-entity-btn
preset: lozenge
entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
tap_action:
  action: toggle
text:
  name:
    content: TOGGLE
    show: true
rules:
  - id: docs-cond-entity
    when:
      entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
      state: "on"
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-cond-entity-btn:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-alert-red)
```

::: details More about entity
- **Missing entities:** a condition on an entity that does not exist (a typo, a deleted helper) is false.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `entity` | string | required | The entity whose state is tested |
| [Comparison operators](#comparison-operators) | | | `state`, `equals`, `not_equals`, `above`, `at_least`, `below`, `at_most`, `in`, `not_in`, `regex` |

### Comparison operators

**The comparison keys test a value: an entity's state, an attribute or a mapped value.** They work the same in `entity`, `entity_attr` and `map_range_cond` conditions.

- The four numeric operators combine: every one you give must hold, so `above: 18` with `below: 26` is a range. `at_least` and `at_most` include the bound itself.
- A condition uses one of the other operators at most, the first it finds in the order of the table, and then ignores any numeric ones next to it. Write a second condition in an `all` list to test two things.
- The editor's operator list also offers "between" (`at_least` plus `at_most`) and "between (exclusive)" (`above` plus `below`), and fills in both bounds.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-cond-range-btn
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: POWER 40 TO 80
    show: true
rules:
  # an inclusive range: 40 <= power <= 80
  - id: docs-cond-range
    when:
      entity: input_number.lcards_test_power
      at_least: 40
      at_most: 80
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-cond-range-btn:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-alert-yellow)
```

::: details More about comparison operators
- **Numbers and text:** `equals` and `not_equals` compare loosely, so `equals: 25` matches the state `"25"`. `in` and `not_in` compare exactly, and states are text: write `in: ["1", "2"]`, not `in: [1, 2]`.
- **Not a number:** a numeric operator on a state that is not a number (`unavailable`, `unknown`) is false.
- **Regular expressions:** `regex` is a JavaScript regular expression tested against the state; one that does not compile is false.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `state` | string / number | - | Equal to this. The same as `equals` |
| `equals` | string / number | - | Equal to this (`==`) |
| `not_equals` | string / number | - | Not equal to this (`!=`) |
| `above` | number | - | Greater than this (`>`) |
| `at_least` | number | - | Greater than or equal to this (`>=`) |
| `below` | number | - | Less than this (`<`) |
| `at_most` | number | - | Less than or equal to this (`<=`) |
| `in` | list | - | One of these values, such as `["on", "idle"]` |
| `not_in` | list | - | None of these values, such as `["off", "unavailable"]` |
| `regex` | string | - | Matches this regular expression, such as `"^heat"` |

## entity_attr

**`entity_attr` tests one attribute of an entity instead of its state, such as a light's `brightness`.** Name the entity in `entity_attr` and the attribute in `attribute`, then add a [comparison](#comparison-operators).

- The condition editor writes the same test as `entity` plus `attribute`; both forms work.
- The sample light here has a brightness of 200, so the rule matches.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-cond-attr-btn
preset: lozenge
entity: light.demo
text:
  name:
    content: BRIGHT
    show: true
rules:
  - id: docs-cond-attr
    when:
      entity_attr: light.demo
      attribute: brightness
      above: 128
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-cond-attr-btn:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-alert-yellow)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `entity_attr` | string | required | The entity whose attribute is tested |
| `attribute` | string | required | The attribute's name. Without it the condition is false |
| [Comparison operators](#comparison-operators) | | | Applied to the attribute's value |

## map_range_cond

**`map_range_cond` maps an entity's numeric state from one scale onto another, then compares the mapped value.** Use it when the threshold you think in is on a different scale from the raw value: a percentage of a power range, say.

- `input` is the range the raw value moves over, `output` the range it is mapped onto, and the comparison keys sit inside `map_range_cond` next to them.
- Here power (0 to 100) is mapped onto 0 to 5000 W, and the rule matches above 4000 W.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-cond-map-btn
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: OVER 4000 W
    show: true
rules:
  - id: docs-cond-map
    when:
      map_range_cond:
        entity: input_number.lcards_test_power
        input: [0, 100]
        output: [0, 5000]
        above: 4000
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-cond-map-btn:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-alert-red)
```

::: details More about map_range_cond
- **Not a number:** a state that is not a number, or an `input` or `output` that is not two numbers, makes the condition false.
- **`state` is not an alias here:** write `equals` to test for one mapped value.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `entity` | string | required | The entity whose state is mapped |
| `input` | `[min, max]` | required | The range of the raw value |
| `output` | `[min, max]` | required | The range it is mapped onto |
| `clamp` | boolean | `true` | Keep the mapped value inside `output` when the raw value leaves `input` |
| [Comparison operators](#comparison-operators) | | | Applied to the **mapped** value; give at least one |

## all, any and not

**`all`, `any` and `not` combine conditions: every one, at least one, or the opposite.** They nest to any depth, so a rule can say "this, and one of those, but not that".

- A bare list under `when` means `all`.
- `not` takes one condition. Given a list, it is true unless every item in the list is true.
- Here the button turns red while power is above 50, the doors are not open, and the lights are on or the mode is `gamma`.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-cond-logic-btn
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: COMBINED
    show: true
rules:
  - id: docs-cond-logic
    when:
      all:
        # power above 50
        - entity: input_number.lcards_test_power
          above: 50
        # doors not open
        - not:
            entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_doors
            state: "on"
        # lights on, or the mode is gamma
        - any:
            - entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_lights
              state: "on"
            - entity: input_select.lcards_test_mode
              state: gamma
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-cond-logic-btn:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-alert-red)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `all` | list | - | True when every condition in the list is true (AND) |
| `any` | list | - | True when at least one condition in the list is true (OR) |
| `not` | condition | - | True when the condition inside is false (NOT) |

## time_between

**`time_between` is true inside a time window each day, such as `"22:00-06:00"` for the night.** A window that ends before it starts runs past midnight.

- The rule is checked at the start of every minute, so it turns on and off on time with no entity to watch.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-cond-time-btn
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: DAY SHIFT
    show: true
rules:
  - id: docs-cond-time
    when:
      time_between: "08:00-20:00"
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-cond-time-btn:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-blue)
```

::: details More about time_between
- **Format:** two-digit hours and minutes, 24-hour (`"08:00-20:00"`, not `"8:00-20:00"`); any other text is false.
- **Edges:** both ends count, to the minute: `"08:00-20:00"` is true from 08:00 through 20:00. The time is the browser's local time.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `time_between` | string | - | `"HH:MM-HH:MM"`, start then end. Wraps past midnight when the end is earlier |

## weekday_in

**`weekday_in` is true on the days you list, such as weekdays only.** Pair it with `time_between` in an `all` list for "weekday mornings".

- Like `time_between`, the rule is checked at the start of every minute, so it follows the day as it changes.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-cond-weekday-btn
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: WEEKDAY
    show: true
rules:
  - id: docs-cond-weekday
    when:
      weekday_in: [mon, tue, wed, thu, fri]
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-cond-weekday-btn:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-blue)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `weekday_in` | list | - | Days from `mon`, `tue`, `wed`, `thu`, `fri`, `sat`, `sun` (any case). The browser's local day |

## sun_elevation

**`sun_elevation` compares the sun's height above the horizon, in degrees, for rules that follow daylight.** Below `0` the sun has set; a few degrees above it is the golden hour.

- It takes the four numeric operators, which combine as on an entity: `above: 0` with `below: 8` is a band.
- The elevation comes from Home Assistant's `sun.sun` entity (its `elevation` attribute).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-cond-sun-btn
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: DAYLIGHT
    show: true
rules:
  - id: docs-cond-sun
    when:
      sun_elevation:
        above: 0
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-cond-sun-btn:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-yellow)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `sun_elevation.above` | number | - | The sun is higher than this, degrees |
| `sun_elevation.at_least` | number | - | The sun is at this height or higher, degrees |
| `sun_elevation.below` | number | - | The sun is lower than this, degrees (`0` is the horizon) |
| `sun_elevation.at_most` | number | - | The sun is at this height or lower, degrees |

## random_chance

**`random_chance` is true with the probability you give, drawn again each time the rule is checked.** Use it for alerts or accents that come and go at random.

- `0.25` is true about one time in four; `0` is never and `1` is always.
- The rule is checked at the start of every minute (and when an entity it names changes), and each check is a new draw.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-cond-chance-btn
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: ONE IN TWO
    show: true
rules:
  - id: docs-cond-chance
    when:
      random_chance: 0.5
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-cond-chance-btn:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-alert-red)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `random_chance` | number | - | The probability of being true, `0.0` to `1.0` |

## Template conditions

**For logic no built-in condition covers, write the condition as JavaScript or a Jinja2 template.** `condition` tells the two apart by their brackets: `[[[ ]]]` is JavaScript, `{{ }}` is Jinja2.

- A `condition` with neither (`condition: light.desk is on`) never matches, and a warning is logged in the browser console.
- [Templates](/core/templates/) covers the template syntax used elsewhere in LCARdS.

### JavaScript

**`condition: "[[[ ... ]]]"` runs JavaScript in the browser; the rule matches when it returns a truthy value.** The code must `return` its result.

- The rule is checked again when an entity read as `states['domain.object']` (or `hass.states['domain.object']`) changes. Entities read any other way, such as a computed id, do not trigger it.
- A YAML block (`condition: |`) holds longer code. `javascript:` (or `js:`) takes the same code without the brackets.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-cond-js-btn
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: POWER ABOVE 80
    show: true
rules:
  - id: docs-cond-js
    when:
      condition: |
        [[[
          const power = Number(states['input_number.lcards_test_power'].state);
          return power > 80;
        ]]]
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-cond-js-btn:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-alert-red)
```

::: details More about JavaScript conditions
- **Errors:** code that throws makes the condition false; the error is logged in the browser console.
- **`entity`:** rules are shared by every card on the page, and `entity` is the entity of the card that happens to check the rule, which may not be the card holding it. Read `states['...']` by id instead.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `condition` | string | - | JavaScript inside `[[[ ]]]` |
| `javascript` | string | - | The same code without `[[[ ]]]`. `js` is a short name for it |
| `entity` (in the code) | object | - | The bound entity of a card on the page, or `null` |
| `hass` (in the code) | object | - | The full Home Assistant object |
| `states` (in the code) | object | - | `hass.states`: every entity's state object by id |

### Jinja2

**`condition: "{{ ... }}"` is a Home Assistant template, rendered by Home Assistant; the rule matches when it renders true.** It can use Home Assistant's own functions and filters (`is_state`, `state_attr`, `float` ...).

- The rule is checked again when an entity the template reads (`states('...')`, `is_state('...')`) changes.
- `True`, `true`, `1`, `yes` and `on` count as true; `False`, `false`, `0`, `no`, `off`, `none` and an empty result as false. Any other number is true unless it is `0`, and any other text is true.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-cond-jinja-btn
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: MODE GAMMA
    show: true
rules:
  - id: docs-cond-jinja
    when:
      condition: "{{ is_state('input_select.lcards_test_mode', 'gamma') }}"
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-cond-jinja-btn:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-alert-red)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `condition` | string | - | A template inside `{{ }}` |
| `jinja2` | string | - | A template, named as Jinja2 explicitly |

### Choosing between JS and Jinja2

**JavaScript is instant and runs in the browser; Jinja2 runs on Home Assistant and has its functions.**

| | JavaScript | Jinja2 |
|---|---|---|
| Evaluated by | Browser | Home Assistant server |
| Latency | Synchronous, instant | Async round-trip |
| Access to Home Assistant functions | No (use `states` directly) | Yes (`is_state`, `state_attr`, filters ...) |
| Best for | Fast logic, math, multi-entity | Home Assistant native functions, formatted values |

## Invalid conditions

**A condition LCARdS does not recognise never matches, so a typo turns the rule off rather than on everywhere.**

- **Unknown key** (a typo such as `entitty:`): the condition never matches.
- **Plain-string `condition:`** (no `[[[ ]]]` or `{{ }}`, such as `condition: light.desk is on`): a warning is logged in the browser console and the condition never matches. Wrap it as JavaScript or Jinja2 instead.

# Rule Examples

**Whole rule sets to copy and change.** Each shows several rule keys working together; the keys are explained on the [Rules Engine](./), [Conditions](./conditions), [Targets and Changes](./changes) and [Priority and Debugging](./priority) pages.

## Temperature alert

**Three rules colour one card by temperature: red above 30, yellow above 25, blue below.** Drag the temperature control to move between them.

- The critical rule has the highest priority and `stop: true`, so above 30 nothing else changes the card.
- Between 25 and 30 only the warning rule matches; below 25 only the normal one.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-rules-temp-display
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: TEMPERATURE
    show: true
rules:
  - id: docs-rules-temp-critical
    priority: 100
    stop: true
    when:
      entity: input_number.lcards_test_temperature
      above: 30
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-rules-temp-display:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-alert-red)
  - id: docs-rules-temp-warning
    priority: 50
    when:
      entity: input_number.lcards_test_temperature
      above: 25
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-rules-temp-display:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-alert-yellow)
  - id: docs-rules-temp-normal
    priority: 10
    when:
      entity: input_number.lcards_test_temperature
      below: 25
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-rules-temp-display:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-blue)
```

## Day and night mode

**Two time-based rules on an MSD: at night the blueprint dims and the lines tagged `nav` fade; by day both come back.** They go in the MSD card's `rules`.

- Time rules are checked at the start of every minute, so the switch happens on time.
- `filters: []` clears the blueprint's filters for the day.
- It is the `rules` of an MSD of your own (with lines tagged `nav`), so it is shown as YAML only.

```yaml
rules:
  - id: night-mode
    priority: 100
    when:
      time_between: "22:00-06:00"
    apply:
      base_svg:
        filters:
          - type: opacity
            value: 0.5
          - type: brightness
            value: 0.8
        transition: 2000
      overlays:
        tag:nav:
          style:
            opacity: 0.5

  - id: day-mode
    priority: 90
    when:
      time_between: "06:00-22:00"
    apply:
      base_svg:
        filters: []
        transition: 2000
      overlays:
        tag:nav:
          style:
            opacity: 1
```

## Multi-condition with animations

**One rule with three conditions: hot, humid and the air conditioning off.** While all three hold, the cards tagged `status` turn red and pulse, and the MSD's blueprint takes a red tint.

- `not` turns "the air conditioning is on" into "it is not on".
- `stop: true` with the high priority keeps other rules off the `status` cards while this one holds.
- The entities are your own (a temperature and humidity sensor, a climate entity), so this example is shown as YAML only. Put it in the MSD card's `rules`.

```yaml
rules:
  - id: climate-critical
    priority: 100
    stop: true
    when:
      all:
        - entity: sensor.temperature
          above: 28
        - entity: sensor.humidity
          above: 70
        - not:
            entity: climate.ac
            state: "on"
    apply:
      overlays:
        tag:status:
          style:
            color: var(--lcars-red)
      animations:
        - tag: status
          preset: pulse
          loop: true
      base_svg:
        filters:
          - mode: svg
            type: tint
            value:
              color: alpha(var(--lcars-alert-red), 0.35)
        transition: 500
```

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/rules/priority.html -->

# Priority and Debugging

**When several rules match at once, `priority` decides which one wins and `stop` can silence the rest.** This page also shows how to see which rules apply now. The rule keys themselves are on the [Rules Engine](./#rule-structure) page.

## priority

**The higher `priority` wins where two matching rules patch the same key of the same card.** Rules are also checked in descending priority order.

- Patches from several rules merge, highest priority on top: a key only one rule sets still applies, whatever its priority.
- Here power is 82, so both rules match and the red one (priority 100) wins. Drag power under 80 for yellow, and under 50 for neither.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-rules-priority-btn
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: POWER
    show: true
rules:
  - id: docs-rules-priority-high
    priority: 100
    when:
      entity: input_number.lcards_test_power
      above: 80
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-rules-priority-btn:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-alert-red)
  - id: docs-rules-priority-mid
    priority: 50
    when:
      entity: input_number.lcards_test_power
      above: 50
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-rules-priority-btn:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-alert-yellow)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `priority` | number | `0` | Higher wins. Rules with the same priority have no set order |

## stop

**`stop: true` makes a matching rule the only one that patches its cards: lower-priority rules' patches on those cards are dropped while it matches.** Use it for an alert that must override every other style.

- It works card by card: a lower-priority rule still patches cards the stopping rule does not touch, and its animations and blueprint filters still run.
- The whole lower patch is dropped, not only the keys that clash. Here, above 80 the button turns red and the lower rule's name change is dropped too; between 50 and 80 the name reads HIGH.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-rules-stop-btn
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: POWER
    show: true
rules:
  - id: docs-rules-stop-critical
    priority: 100
    stop: true
    when:
      entity: input_number.lcards_test_power
      above: 80
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-rules-stop-btn:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-alert-red)
  - id: docs-rules-stop-high
    priority: 10
    when:
      entity: input_number.lcards_test_power
      above: 50
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-rules-stop-btn:
          text:
            name:
              content: HIGH
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `stop` | boolean | `false` | While this rule matches, drop lower-priority rules' patches on the cards it patches |

## enabled

**`enabled: false` turns a rule off without deleting it.** The Rules tab's toggle in the card editor sets it.

- A rule that is off never matches, so it patches nothing and starts no animations.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
id: docs-rules-enabled-btn
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    content: RULE OFF
    show: true
rules:
  - id: docs-rules-enabled
    enabled: false
    when:
      entity: input_number.lcards_test_power
      above: 0
    apply:
      overlays:
        docs-rules-enabled-btn:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-alert-red)
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | `false` turns the rule off |

## Viewing active rules

**The card editor's Rules and Provenance tabs show which rules there are and what they change now; the browser console shows the engine's trace.**

- The **Rules** tab lists the rules that target this card and every rule on the page, with each rule's priority, `stop`, on or off, source card, targets, condition and number of changes. It adds, edits, reorders, turns off and deletes the rules in this card's config, and marks a rule that applies when you save the card.
- The **Provenance** tab's "Set by rules now" filter lists the values of this card that a rule is setting right now, and which rule.

From the browser console:

```javascript
const rm = window.lcards.core.rulesManager;
rm.getAllRules()                     // all registered rules
rm.getTrace()                        // detailed evaluation trace
rm.getRecentMatches(30000)           // matches in the last 30 s (default 60 s)
rm.getRuleTrace('my-rule-id', 20)    // history for one rule (default the last 20)
```

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/sounds.html -->

# Card Sounds

**LCARdS cards can play a sound when you tap, hold, double-tap or hover over them, toggle an entity or drag a slider.** The sounds come from the active sound scheme; a card's own `sounds` block mutes the card or changes the sound of one event, for that card only.

- Sounds are off until you turn them on: [Sound Configuration](../configuration/sounds.md) covers the helpers, schemes and the per-user and per-device settings.
- Without a `sounds` block a card plays the scheme's sounds. [Which cards fire which events](#which-cards-fire-which-events) lists the cards that play them.

## How card sounds work

**Each card event looks for its sound in a fixed order, and the first answer wins.**

1. **The master switch and the Cards switch.** With either one off, no card sound plays, whatever the card says.
2. **The card's `sounds` block.** `enabled: false` silences the card; an event key plays that sound, or nothing for `null`.
3. **Per-event overrides** from the Sound tab of the LCARdS Config Panel: a device's override beats a user's, which beats the global one.
4. **The active sound scheme's sound** for that event.
5. **Silence**, when none of these gives a sound.

## Muting a card

**`enabled: false` silences every sound this card plays.** Use it on a card you tap often, or one that should stay quiet while the rest of the dashboard plays sounds.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_lights
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
sounds:
  enabled: false
```

::: details More about muting
- **Dialogs:** a `more-info` or `assist` action opens a Home Assistant dialog, and the dialog's own sound (More info open, Dialog open) still plays.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sounds.enabled` | boolean | `true` | `false`: this card plays no sounds |

## Event sounds

**An event key in `sounds` plays another sound for that event on this card, or none for `null`.** The other events keep the scheme's sounds.

- A sound is an asset key (the name a sound pack gives a sound, such as `lcards_default_nav` or `computer_activate`), a `media-source://` id picked from the Home Assistant media library, or a URL (`/local/sounds/beep.mp3`). `schema/registries.json` on this site lists every built-in key under `sound_assets`.
- `toggle_on` and `toggle_off` play in place of the tap, hold or double-tap sound when that action is a `toggle`: `toggle_on` when the entity is `off`, `closed` or `locked`, `toggle_off` from any other state.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_lights
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
# not a toggle action, so a tap plays card_tap (a toggle plays toggle_on or toggle_off)
tap_action:
  action: perform-action
  perform_action: input_boolean.toggle
  target:
    entity_id: input_boolean.lcards_test_lights
sounds:
  # another sound on a tap
  card_tap: lcards_default_nav
  # no sound on a hold
  card_hold: null
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sounds.card_tap` | string / `null` | the scheme's | A tap |
| `sounds.card_hold` | string / `null` | the scheme's | A hold (a press of half a second) |
| `sounds.card_double_tap` | string / `null` | the scheme's | A double tap |
| `sounds.card_hover` | string / `null` | the scheme's | The mouse pointer moving onto the card. Not on touch screens |
| `sounds.toggle_on` | string / `null` | the scheme's | A `toggle` action turning the entity on |
| `sounds.toggle_off` | string / `null` | the scheme's | A `toggle` action turning the entity off |
| [Slider events](#slider-events) | | | `slider_drag_start`, `slider_change` and `slider_drag_end` |

### Slider events

**Three more events on the slider card: grabbing the slider, each change of value, and letting go.** They take the same values as the other event keys.

- `slider_change` is silent in the built-in `lcards_default` scheme, so the slider does not click on every step; give it a sound to hear each change.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-slider
entity: input_number.lcards_test_value
sounds:
  slider_drag_start: lcards_default_slider_grab
  slider_drag_end: lcards_default_slider_release
  # null keeps it silent under any scheme
  slider_change: null
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sounds.slider_drag_start` | string / `null` | the scheme's | Grabbing the slider |
| `sounds.slider_change` | string / `null` | the scheme's (silent in `lcards_default`) | Each change of value |
| `sounds.slider_drag_end` | string / `null` | the scheme's | Letting go of the slider |

## Which cards fire which events

**Card sounds come with actions: a card plays the tap, hold and double-tap sounds where it runs those actions.** The slider events are the slider card's alone.

| Event | Cards |
|-------|-------|
| `card_tap` | Button, elbow, select menu options, data grid cells with actions, a slider with a `tap_action`, astrometrics points and on-card buttons |
| `card_hold` | Button, elbow, select menu options, data grid cells with actions, a slider with a `hold_action`, astrometrics points |
| `card_double_tap` | Button, elbow, select menu options, data grid cells with actions, a slider with a `double_tap_action` |
| `card_hover` | Button, elbow and select menu options (not with `interactive: false`), a slider with actions |
| `toggle_on`, `toggle_off` | Any of these whose action is a `toggle` |
| `slider_drag_start`, `slider_change`, `slider_drag_end` | Slider |

On a select menu, each option is a button: give `sounds` to an option, as on the [Select Menu options](../cards/select-menu/options.md) page.

## See also

- [Sound Configuration](../configuration/sounds.md): turning sounds on, schemes, and per-user and per-device overrides
- [Home Assistant Actions: `lcards.play_sound`](../configuration/ha-actions.md#lcards-play-sound): play a sound from an automation
- [Actions](actions.md): tap, hold and double-tap actions

# Card Styles

**The `style:` block sets how a button looks: its background, its border and its corners.** Start from a [preset](presets.md) for the shape, then set only what you want to change.

- These keys are the button's. The [select menu](/cards/select-menu/styles) takes the same keys for its option buttons; the slider, elbow and other cards have their own style keys on their pages.
- Every colour takes one colour or a [state map](colours.md) with one colour per state (`default`, `active`, `inactive`, `unavailable`, `hover`, `pressed`, exact states and ranges).
- [Rules](rules/) can change any style value while the dashboard runs.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
style:
  card:
    color:
      background:
        default: var(--lcards-orange)
        inactive: var(--lcards-gray-dark)
  border:
    color: var(--lcards-blue)
    width: 2
    radius: 8
tap_action:
  action: toggle
```

## style.card

**`style.card.color.background` is the card's fill colour, one colour or one per state.** Use it to light a button when its entity is on and dim it when off.

- A single colour (`background: var(--lcards-orange)`) is used in every state.
- In a state map, `active` is used while the entity is on, `inactive` while it is off and `unavailable` when Home Assistant cannot reach it; `default` is the fallback when no other key matches.
- `hover` and `pressed` colour the button while the pointer is over it or it is pressed. They have no effect when [`interactive`](/cards/button/styles#interactive) is `false`.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge
text:
  name:
    show: true
style:
  card:
    color:
      background:
        default: var(--lcards-orange)
        active: var(--lcards-orange)
        inactive: var(--lcards-gray-dark)
        unavailable: var(--lcards-gray-darkest)
        hover: var(--lcards-orange-light)
        pressed: var(--lcards-orange-dark)
tap_action:
  action: toggle
```

::: details More about style.card
- **Colour formats:** CSS variables, `theme:` token paths, colour functions, hex and the other formats on the [Colours](colours.md) page all work, on their own or as values in a state map.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.card.color.background` | colour / state map | from the preset (theme button colours) | The card's fill |

## style.border

**The border's colour, width and corner radius.** Rounded presets set the radius for you; set it yourself for a custom shape.

- `width` and `radius` take one number for every side or corner, or an object with one key per side (`top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left`) or corner (`top_left`, `top_right`, `bottom_right`, `bottom_left`). The sides or corners an object leaves out keep the preset's value.
- The border colour takes a state map like the background, so a border can light up when the entity is on.
- A radius larger than half the button's height (or width) is made smaller to fit, so a tall button keeps its shape.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: outline
text:
  name:
    show: true
style:
  border:
    width: 3
    color:
      default: var(--lcards-gray)
      active: var(--lcards-orange)
      inactive: var(--lcards-gray-dark)
    radius:
      top_left: 12
      top_right: 12
      bottom_right: 4
      bottom_left: 4
tap_action:
  action: toggle
```

::: details More about style.border
- **Without a preset:** a button with no `preset` draws a `2` px border with `20` px corners unless you set them.
- **Theme values:** `width` and `radius` also take a CSS variable, such as `var(--ha-border-radius-lg)`.
:::

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.border.color` | colour / state map | the button's own colour (theme button colours) | Border colour. It matches the fill by default, so on a filled preset set a different colour to see the border |
| `style.border.width` | number / string / object | from the preset: `0` on most | Border width in px, a token, or one per side |
| `style.border.width.top` | number / string | from the preset | Top border width |
| `style.border.width.right` | number / string | from the preset | Right border width |
| `style.border.width.bottom` | number / string | from the preset | Bottom border width |
| `style.border.width.left` | number / string | from the preset | Left border width |
| `style.border.radius` | number / string / object | from the preset | Corner radius in px (0 to 100), a CSS variable, or one per corner |
| `style.border.radius.top_left` | number / string | from the preset | Top-left corner radius |
| `style.border.radius.top_right` | number / string | from the preset | Top-right corner radius |
| `style.border.radius.bottom_right` | number / string | from the preset | Bottom-right corner radius |
| `style.border.radius.bottom_left` | number / string | from the preset | Bottom-left corner radius |

## icon_style

**The icon's colour and size are set in `icon_style`, at the top level of the card, not inside `style:`.** The icon shows when `show_icon` is `true`, and its colour can follow the entity's state like the background.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge
show_icon: true
icon: mdi:lightbulb
text:
  name:
    show: true
icon_style:
  size: 28
  color:
    active: var(--lcards-yellow)
    inactive: var(--lcards-gray)
tap_action:
  action: toggle
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `icon_style.color` | colour / state map | the preset's icon colour | Icon colour |
| `icon_style.size` | number | `24` | Icon size, 8 to 200 px |
| [All icon keys](/cards/button/icons#icon-style) | | | Position, rotation, padding and spacing, on the button's Icons page |

## Dimensions

**The card's size is set at the top level of the card, not inside `style:`.** By default a card is as big as its cell; set a size for a fixed card or for one outside a sections grid.

- A number is pixels (`200` is `200px`); a string takes any CSS length, such as `50%` or `10vh`.
- `min_height` is a floor for a card that sizes itself. When `height` is set too, the card is exactly `height` tall and `min_height` is ignored.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.living_room
preset: lozenge
width: 200
height: 48
text:
  name:
    show: true
tap_action:
  action: toggle
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `width` | number / string | the cell's width | Card width: a number is px, or any CSS length |
| `height` | number / string | the cell's height | Card height: a number is px, or any CSS length |
| `min_height` | number / string | the button's preset: the theme's button height | Smallest height (a number is px). Ignored when `height` is set |
| [More sizing keys](/cards/common#sizing) | | | `min_width`, `max_height`, `max_width` and how sizes work in a sections grid |

## Interaction with Presets and Rules

**A card's look is built in layers, and each layer wins over the one before it.** You only set the values that differ from the preset; anything you leave out comes from the layer below.

- The layers, lowest first: LCARdS and theme defaults, the [preset](presets.md), your `style:` block, then [rule](rules/) patches while the dashboard runs.
- To see which layer set each value, open the card editor's [Main Engineering](../cards/main-engineering.md#provenance) tab and its **Provenance** panel.

```yaml live controls
# The preset gives the shape and colours, the style block makes it blue,
# and a rule turns it red while the kitchen light is on (tap to toggle)
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.kitchen
preset: lozenge
id: layered-btn
text:
  name:
    content: LAYERS
    show: true
style:
  card:
    color:
      background: var(--lcards-blue)
rules:
  - id: layered-red
    when:
      entity: light.kitchen
      state: "on"
    apply:
      overlays:
        layered-btn:
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background: var(--lcars-red)
tap_action:
  action: toggle
```

- [Button styles](/cards/button/styles): text fields, hover, the cursor and filters on a button

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/templates/ -->

# Templates

**Templates put live values into a card's settings: an entity's state in a label, a word or colour worked out in JavaScript, a Home Assistant Jinja2 template, or a processed [data source](../datasources/) value.** There are four kinds, and one string can mix them.

- **Tokens** `{entity.state}` are the quickest: they fill in a value without asking Home Assistant.
- **JavaScript** `[[[ ]]]` is for logic and calculations, **Jinja2** `{{ }}` is Home Assistant's own template language, and **data sources** `{ds:name}` show values that LCARdS has smoothed, converted or otherwise processed.
- A card works out its templates again when an entity it follows changes; see [Entity Tracking](#entity-tracking-reactivity) for which ones it follows.

::: tip Try it
A card editor's **Main Engineering > Templates** tab lists every template on the card with its live result, and opens any of them in a sandbox that completes entities, data sources and theme tokens. See [Main Engineering](../../cards/main-engineering#templates).
:::

## Token Templates

**A token in single braces fills in one value: the card's entity state, an attribute, another entity, a config value, a variable or a theme token.** It is worked out at once, in the browser, with no round trip to Home Assistant.

- `{entity.state}` is the state as Home Assistant shows it: translated, and with its unit (`21.5 °C`, `Open`). A text field's [`display_format`](../text-fields-content#display-format) picks the raw state or the unit only.
- The card does not follow an entity named in a `{states.…}` token by itself: list it in [`triggers_update`](#manual-tracking-with-triggers-update), as below.
- Anything in single braces is read as a token, so one that names nothing (a typo, an attribute the entity doesn't have) shows as nothing. On a text field, `template: false` shows braces as written.
- Tokens are an LCARdS shorthand, not Jinja2. If you know Home Assistant's templates, [Jinja2](#jinja2-templates) gives you all of it; use tokens where the value must be ready at once.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: sensor.demo_temperature
preset: lozenge
variables:
  deck: DECK 7
triggers_update:
  - light.demo
text:
  default:
    color: var(--lcars-black)
  reading:
    content: "{entity.state}"
    position: top-left
  deck:
    content: "{variables.deck}"
    position: top-right
  light:
    content: "LIGHT {states.light.demo.state}"
    position: bottom-left
grid_options:
  rows: 2
```

| Token | Value |
|-------|-------|
| `{entity.state}` | The card entity's state, as Home Assistant shows it |
| `{entity.attributes.NAME}` | One of its attributes, as Home Assistant shows it |
| `{states.domain.object_id.state}` | The state of another entity, named by its full entity ID |
| `{states.domain.object_id.attributes.NAME}` | An attribute of another entity |
| `{config.NAME}` | A value from this card's own config |
| `{variables.NAME}` | One of the card's [`variables`](../../cards/common#variables) |
| `{hass.user.name}` | The name of the Home Assistant user looking at the dashboard |
| `{theme:token.path}` | A theme token's value: see [Themes](../themes/) |

## JavaScript Templates

**`[[[ ]]]` runs JavaScript in the browser and puts in what it returns: use it for any logic or calculation.** Write `return` with the value; a template that returns nothing shows as nothing.

- JavaScript gets the raw entity: `entity.state` is `on`, not `On`, and a number in a state is a string, so use `Number(entity.state)` to calculate with it.
- A template with an error is shown as written, and the browser console logs a warning.
- The card does not follow entities a template reads from `states` or `hass.states`: list them in [`triggers_update`](#manual-tracking-with-triggers-update).

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.demo
preset: lozenge
text:
  default:
    color: var(--lcars-black)
  status:
    content: "[[[ return entity.state === 'on' ? 'ACTIVE' : 'STANDBY' ]]]"
    position: top-left
  level:
    content: >-
      [[[
        const b = entity.attributes.brightness;
        return entity.state === 'on' && b ? Math.round(b / 255 * 100) + '%' : '-';
      ]]]
    position: top-right
grid_options:
  rows: 2
```

| Variable | Type | Contents |
|----------|------|----------|
| `entity` | object | The card's entity: `entity.state`, `entity.attributes`, `entity.entity_id`, `entity.last_changed` |
| `states` | object | Every entity's state object by ID, as `states['sensor.outdoor_temp'].state` |
| `hass` | object | The whole Home Assistant object: `hass.states`, `hass.user`, `hass.formatEntityState(entity)` ... |
| `user` | object | The current Home Assistant user (`hass.user`) |
| `config` | object | This card's whole config |
| `variables` | object | The card's `variables` |
| `theme` | object | The active theme, with its tokens: `theme.colors.ui.primary` |

## Jinja2 Templates

**`{{ }}` and `{% %}` are Home Assistant's own templates, rendered by Home Assistant: every function and filter you know from automations works.** Use them when you already know Home Assistant's templating, or need something only the server knows.

- The value arrives a moment after the card draws, since Home Assistant renders it. On an error, or with no answer in 5 seconds, the template is shown as written.
- Entities named in `states('…')`, `is_state`, `state_attr`, `is_state_attr` and `has_value` are [followed automatically](#automatic-tracking).
- The card's `config` and `variables`, and `user` (the user's name), are passed in: `{{ variables.room }}` works.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.demo
preset: lozenge
text:
  default:
    color: var(--lcars-black)
  temperature:
    content: "{{ states('sensor.demo_temperature') | float(0) | round(1) }} °C"
    position: top-left
  status:
    content: "{% if is_state('light.demo', 'on') %}LIGHT ON{% else %}LIGHT OFF{% endif %}"
    position: bottom-left
grid_options:
  rows: 2
```

::: details More about Jinja2 templates
- **When it renders:** each time the card works out its templates, not continuously. `now()` moves on only when the card refreshes, which is when an entity it follows changes.
- **The whole string goes to Home Assistant:** text around the template and any tokens already filled in are sent with it and come back unchanged.
:::

## Data Source Templates

**`{ds:name}` puts in the current value of a [data source](../datasources/), a live value LCARdS keeps and processes in the browser; `{datasource:name}` is the same.** Declare the data source in the card's `data_sources`, and the card updates whenever it does.

- Without a format, the value is shown as Home Assistant shows numbers, with the entity's unit: `21.4 °C`.
- With a format, you own the output: the number is formatted to it and **no unit is added**, so write your own after it.
- A dot picks a [processor](../datasources/#processors)'s value: `{ds:name.processor}`, and one statistic of a `statistics` processor with `{ds:name.processor.max}`. A processor's value has no unit, and without a format shows as a plain number.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: lozenge
data_sources:
  outdoor_temp:
    entity: sensor.demo_outdoor_temperature
    processing:
      fahrenheit:
        type: convert_unit
        from: c
        to: f
text:
  default:
    color: var(--lcars-black)
  native:
    content: "{ds:outdoor_temp}" # Home Assistant's number format, with the unit
    position: top-left
  precise:
    content: "{ds:outdoor_temp:.2f} °C" # your precision, your unit
    position: top-right
  converted:
    content: "{ds:outdoor_temp.fahrenheit:.0f} °F" # a processor's value
    position: bottom-left
grid_options:
  rows: 2
```

| Format | Example | Result |
|--------|---------|--------|
| (none) | `{ds:temp}` | `21.4 °C`: Home Assistant's number format, with the entity's unit |
| `:.Nf` | `{ds:temp:.1f}` | `21.4`: N decimal places, no unit |
| `:int` | `{ds:temp:int}` | `21`: rounded to a whole number, no unit |
| `:.N%` | `{ds:level:.0%}` | `75%`: a percentage. A value whose unit is already `%` is not multiplied by 100 |
| `:str` | `{ds:mode:str}` | The value as plain text |
| `:bool` | `{ds:flag:bool}` | `true` or `false` |

The number format follows your Home Assistant language settings, so `{ds:temp}` reads `21,4 °C` where a comma is the decimal mark. An unknown format shows the plain number.

## Where Templates Work

**Text takes all four kinds of template; colour and other style settings take JavaScript and Jinja2.** For a theme colour in a style setting, use [`theme:`](../themes/#using-theme-tokens) instead of a token.

| Setting | Template kinds |
|---------|----------------|
| `text.<field>.content` on the button, elbow and slider ([Text Fields](../text-fields-content#content)) | All four |
| Data grid cells ([Data Grid](../../cards/data-grid/data)) | All four |
| Astrometrics label `content` ([Live Data](../../cards/astrometrics/data#templates)) | All four |
| Slider `style.ranges[].label.text` ([Ranges](../../cards/slider-card/ranges)) | All four |
| Slider `style.ranges[].value`, `.min` and `.max` | Tokens, JavaScript and data sources: no Jinja2, since positions are worked out again on every state change |
| Style values: `style`, `icon_style` (`icon_style.icon` included) and a text field's `color` on the button, elbow and slider; the elbow's `elbow` settings; `style` on the chart; MSD overlay styles | JavaScript and Jinja2 |
| Rule `condition` ([Rule Conditions](../rules/conditions#template-conditions)) | JavaScript and Jinja2 |

## Template Evaluation Order

**When one string mixes kinds, they are worked out in a fixed order: JavaScript, then tokens, then data sources, then Jinja2.** Each step works on the text the one before left.

1. `[[[ ]]]`: JavaScript
2. `{token}`: tokens
3. `{ds:…}` / `{datasource:…}`: data sources
4. `{{ }}`: Jinja2, last because it waits for Home Assistant

Settings that must have a value at once, such as a slider marker's position, stop after step 3.

## Entity Tracking & Reactivity

**A card works out its templates again when an entity it follows changes: its own `entity`, the entities its Jinja2 templates name, and the entities in `triggers_update`.** A data source in the card's own `data_sources` updates it too, whenever the data source changes.

### Automatic tracking

**Entities named in a Jinja2 template are found and followed with no extra config.** The card reads the entity IDs written in `states()`, `state_attr()`, `is_state()`, `is_state_attr()` and `has_value()`.

- Only IDs written out in quotes are found. An ID built from variables, or the `states.sensor.x.state` form, isn't: add those to `triggers_update`.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.demo
preset: lozenge
text:
  default:
    color: var(--lcars-black)
  toggle:
    content: "{% if is_state('input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle', 'on') %}TOGGLE ON{% else %}TOGGLE OFF{% endif %}" # followed: is_state()
    position: top-left
grid_options:
  rows: 2
```

### Manual tracking with `triggers_update`

**`triggers_update` lists more entities whose changes make the card work out its templates again.** Use it for the entities LCARdS can't find for itself: those a JavaScript template reads, those in `{states.…}` tokens, and IDs a Jinja2 template builds.

- It adds to what the card follows; its own `entity` is always followed.

```yaml live controls
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.demo
preset: lozenge
triggers_update:
  - input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
  - sensor.demo_temperature
text:
  default:
    color: var(--lcars-black)
  status:
    content: |
      [[[
        const toggle = states['input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle']?.state;
        const temp = states['sensor.demo_temperature']?.state;
        return toggle === 'on' ? `ON (${Number(temp).toFixed(1)}°)` : 'OFF';
      ]]]
    position: top-left
grid_options:
  rows: 2
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `triggers_update` | list | - | Entity IDs to follow as well as the card's own: when one changes, the card works out all its templates again |
